# Prismatic cohomology: δ-rings, relative and absolute comparisons, and crystalline lattices

Part PR.0 of `PrismaticCohomology`, covering PR.0–PR.7. The logarithmic stage PR.8 belongs to the second part. This document specifies proposed declarations; every implementation status is unchecked. [The packet](../packets/PrismaticCohomology--PR.0.json) records the dependency graph and [the suggested Lean file](../suggested/PrismaticCohomology--PR.0.lean) gives prototype forms. Neither compilation nor a planned stage certifies a proof.

## Library, conventions and construction order

The baseline is Mathlib `082e2d37e8b0463410cdb532e111cd43d5a66174` and Tau Ceti `f790474821cf4256814db967cb154e7af3d0c369`. The 140 cited declaration statements were read at the pin. Existing rings, Witt vectors, divided powers, adic completion, homological complexes, derived categories and general module/stack descent are reused. No prismatic comparison is imported as an implemented Tau Ceti theorem. The δ-ring prefix has lemma-level proof outlines; the remaining targets have declaration-level statements and key proof steps, with smaller calculations kept in those outlines.

Fix a prime p. All rings are commutative and unital, including the zero ring. Elementary integral-polynomial δ-identities hold without a p-local assumption; prismatic statements impose the p-local and completeness hypotheses listed with each declaration. A prism consists of a δ-ring, an invertible Cartier ideal I, derived (p,I)-completeness and p∈I+φ(I)A. Boundedness means bounded p-power torsion in A/I. Orientations are chosen generators, and distinguished elements need not be p times a unit.

Complexes use cohomological indexing. Completion and tensor products are derived unless the statement explicitly specifies classical completion. Mathlib derived categories give the prototypes their ordinary categorical carriers; animated rings, stable derived ∞-categories and E∞ structures need the named suppliers. The Hodge–Tate object is Δ⊗^L_AA/I; crystalline and de Rham comparisons retain scalar extension along φ_A. The Breuil–Kisin line has A{1}/I≃I/I²; Frobenius on A{n} has target I^(−n)⊗A{n} for every integer n. Absolute Nygaard steps are integer-indexed and constant for filtration index ≤0. Syntomic fibres use the completed Nygaard datum.

The construction order is PR.0 → PR.1 → PR.2 → PR.3, followed by PR.5 and PR.6, then PR.4 and PR.7. PR.4 imports PR.6 for its BMS2/AΩ applications. PR.5 owns absolute Nygaard theory, PR.3 owns prism twists and relative Nygaard theory, and PR.4 owns syntomic complexes. Trace interpretations are exported to RefinedTraceMethods; they do not enter PR.0–PR.6 as prerequisites. The list below groups declarations by mathematical layer, and orders each layer by its internal prerequisites. The current RS-01 revision has a pending independent review, so this pass keeps the current stage structure; its unaccepted ownership extensions remain proposals.

## PR.0. Delta-rings, prisms and envelopes

Begin with the integral polynomial C_p(x,y), evaluated without dividing in the target ring. The δ-operation is data even when Frobenius is already specified: p-torsion destroys the reconstruction from φ. Length-two Witt vectors, square-zero examples, localization and classical completion give the elementary library its tests. The target-level extension constructs free and cofree δ-rings, distinguishes Witt-coordinate operations from δ-iterates, and introduces the three prism axioms. The four standard examples then support boundedness, rigidity, perfection and envelopes. Derived completion and integral perfectoid algebra come from their existing owners; neither a Witt carrier nor ordinary adic completion supplies those theories by itself.

**Inputs.** `CrystallineCohomology:CR.0`; `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.0`; `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`; `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E1`; `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E5:animation/animated-commutative-rings`; `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E5:animation/nonabelian-derived-category`; `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E5:animation/universal-property-of-animation`; `PerfectoidQuotients:Q0:integral-algebra`; `PerfectoidQuotients:Q0:integral-algebra/semiperfectoid-quasisyntomic-and-qrsp-rings`; `PerfectoidQuotients:Q0:integral-algebra/theta-naturality`.

**Planets.** [δ-rings](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-delta-frobenius-dictionary); [Free δ-rings](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-free-delta-ring); [Distinguished elements](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-distinguished-element); [Prisms](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-prism); [Perfect prisms and perfectoid rings](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-perfect-prisms-perfectoid-rings); [Prismatic envelopes](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-regular-prismatic-envelopes).

**Proof refinement and acceptance boundary.** Refine the target-level prism and envelope proofs to the density of the retained lemma-level δ-ring prefix; the specified cofree Witt proof and étale algebraization inputs remain explicit gaps. Formalize the explicit monomial module model and uniform filtration estimate in the corrected square-zero unbounded-torsion example; its mathematical regularity argument is now supplied in the proof sketch. The complete derived-Frobenius classification of Remark 2.5 and perfectoid covers of regular local rings of Remark 3.11 have no consumer among these targets; the W₂ pullback square used by PR.2 is already included.

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-0-delta-addition-correction"></a>

### Integral addition correction

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-addition-correction` · definition. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Delta` in `TauCeti/RingTheory/Delta/Basic`.

Define C_p(x,y) as minus the sum over 1<=i<=p-1 of (binomial(p,i)/p) x^i y^(p-i). The quotient is an exact natural/integer coefficient, then cast to R. Never divide by p in R.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** p is prime; R is a commutative unital ring, possibly zero or with p-torsion.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Use the pinned prime-binomial divisibility theorem to justify each integral coefficient.
2. Evaluate this fixed integer polynomial in the existing ring. Finite sums, powers and the index involution i->p-i give the API.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`mathlib:Nat.Prime.dvd_choose_self`](#mathlib-nat-prime-dvd-choose-self).

**Consumers.** PR.0 delta axioms and Witt-coordinate comparison: Pins the sign and retains the addition law in p-torsion rings..

**Planning API.**

- `TauCeti.Delta.addCorrection_map` (functoriality): Every ring map carries C_p(x,y) to C_p of the images.
- `TauCeti.Delta.addCorrection_zero` (simp): C_p(x,0)=0.
- `TauCeti.Delta.addCorrection_symm` (relation): C_p(x,y)=C_p(y,x).

**Unit tests.**

- `correction_dyadic` (computation): Over Z, C_2(x,y)=-xy.
- `correction_cubic` (computation): Over Z, C_3(x,y)=-xy(x+y).
- `correction_zero_argument` (degenerate): C_p(x,0)=0 in every ring.

**Acceptance.** C_2=-xy and C_3=-xy(x+y). The formula evaluates when p is zero or a zero divisor in R.

**Sources.** [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Definition 2.1. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 13. Makes the integral polynomial underlying the displayed addition axiom explicit..

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-0-ordinary-frobenius-lift"></a>

### Ordinary Frobenius lift

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/ordinary-frobenius-lift` · definition. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Delta` in `TauCeti/RingTheory/Delta/Basic`.

A FrobeniusLift is a unital endomorphism f of R such that for each x there exists y with f(x)=x^p+p y. Equivalently its reduction modulo (p) is Frobenius. The witnesses form a proposition, not a chosen delta operation or a derived homotopy.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** p is prime; R is a commutative unital ring.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Use the subtype of the existing RingHom R R cut out by the pointwise divisibility property.
2. The kernel description of the quotient by (p) gives the quotient characterization. Equality of lifts is equality of their ring maps.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`mathlib:Ideal.Quotient.mk`](#mathlib-ideal-quotient-mk); [`mathlib:Ideal.span`](#mathlib-ideal-span).

**Consumers.** torsionfree-frobenius-equivalence: Records exactly the ordinary data from which cancellation can recover a unique delta..

**Planning API.**

- `TauCeti.Delta.FrobeniusLift.ext` (extensionality): Equality of underlying maps gives equality of lifts.
- `TauCeti.Delta.FrobeniusLift.mod_p` (compatibility): f(x) and x^p have equal images modulo (p).
- `TauCeti.Delta.FrobeniusLift.congruence_iff` (characterisation): The witness condition is equivalent to the quotient equality for all x.

**Unit tests.**

- `lift_on_integers` (computation): The identity on Z is a lift.
- `lift_in_characteristic_p` (compatibility): The identity on F_p is a lift.
- `power_not_ring_map` (non-example): No lift on Z at p=2 has underlying function x->x^2.

**Acceptance.** The identity on F_p is a lift although F_p has no delta structure. A map of sets such as x->x^p on Z is not substituted for a ring map.

**Sources.** [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Remarks 2.2 and 2.5. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed pages 13, 14. Names the ordinary congruence datum and explicitly does not replace the derived datum..

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-0-witt2-mul-coordinate"></a>

### Second coordinate of length-two Witt multiplication

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/witt2-mul-coordinate` · lemma. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Delta` in `TauCeti/RingTheory/Delta/Basic`.

On TruncatedWittVector p 2 R, (xy)_1=x_0^p*y_1+y_0^p*x_1+p*x_1*y_1.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** p is prime; R is arbitrary commutative and unital.

**Construction or proof.**

1. In the universal integer polynomial ring expand (x_0^p+p*x_1)(y_0^p+p*y_1), subtract (x_0*y_0)^p, and cancel p there.
2. Transport using coefficientwise Witt maps and truncation to R. The zeroth product coordinate follows from constantCoeff as a ring map. No cancellation in R is used.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`mathlib:WittVector.ghostComponent`](#mathlib-wittvector-ghostcomponent); [`mathlib:WittVector.ghostComponent_apply`](#mathlib-wittvector-ghostcomponent-apply); [`mathlib:wittPolynomial_one`](#mathlib-wittpolynomial-one); [`mathlib:WittVector.constantCoeff`](#mathlib-wittvector-constantcoeff); [`mathlib:WittVector.map_coeff`](#mathlib-wittvector-map-coeff); [`mathlib:WittVector.truncate`](#mathlib-wittvector-truncate); [`mathlib:WittVector.truncate_surjective`](#mathlib-wittvector-truncate-surjective); [`mathlib:WittVector.coeff_truncate`](#mathlib-wittvector-coeff-truncate); [`mathlib:WittVector.map`](#mathlib-wittvector-map).

**Acceptance.** Keep p*x_1*y_1 before specializing to characteristic p.

**Sources.** [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Remark 2.4. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 13. The multiplication coordinate calculation is its own declaration..

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-0-complete-regular-sequence"></a>

### Completely regular sequences relative to a base

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/complete-regular-sequence` · definition. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/Envelope`.

Let A be an animated commutative ring and I = (f_1,…,f_n) ⊂ π_0(A) a finitely generated ideal. Let B be a derived I-complete animated A-algebra. A sequence x_1,…,x_r ∈ π_0(B) is I-completely regular relative to A if the map Kos(A; f_1,…,f_n) → Kos(B; f_1,…,f_n, x_1,…,x_r) is a flat map of animated rings. For discrete A and B and I = 0 this says that (x_1,…,x_r) is Koszul-regular on B and B/(x) is flat over A.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** A animated; I finitely generated; B derived I-complete. Kos(A; f) is the derived quotient A ⊗^L_{Z[t_1..t_n]} Z; flatness of a map of animated rings is the notion of EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E5:animation / DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1. The definition does not depend on the choice of generators of I.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Definition (BS22 Definition 2.42).
2. Independence of the generators of I: Kos(B; f, x) ≃ Kos(B; x) ⊗^L_A Kos(A; f) and π_0(Kos(A; f)) = π_0(A)/I, so flatness of Kos(A; f) → Kos(B; f, x) says exactly that Kos(B; x) ⊗^L_A π_0(A)/I is discrete and flat over π_0(A)/I (that is, Kos(B; x) is I-completely flat over A); this does not mention the generators. The source uses this independence without comment.

**Direct prerequisites.** `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`; `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E5:animation/animated-commutative-rings`; [`mathlib:RingTheory.Sequence.IsRegular`](#mathlib-ringtheory-sequence-isregular); [`mathlib:Module.Flat`](#mathlib-module-flat).

**Consumers.** BS22 Lemma 2.43, Corollary 2.44: the hypothesis under which PD envelopes and δ-envelopes are completely flat. BS22 Proposition 3.13 and Example 3.14: the ideals J admitting prismatic envelopes are those locally generated by I and a sequence (p,I)-completely regular relative to A; kernels of surjections from completely smooth algebras onto completely smooth R are of this form. Anschütz–Le Bras Remark 3.1.8: the crystalline comparison extends to syntomic algebras because the Čech–Alexander kernels are generated by such sequences.

**Planning API.**

- `TauCeti.Prismatic.IsRelativelyRegular` (data): For discrete rings: A → B, an ideal I of A and a sequence x_1,…,x_r in B; the predicate that x is weakly regular on B/IB and that B/(IB + (x_1,…,x_k)) is flat over A/I for every k ≤ r. This discrete condition implies the definition whenever the chosen generators of I form a regular sequence on A and on B; it is the form in which the definition is tested.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.IsRelativelyRegular.nil` (example): The empty sequence is relatively regular exactly when B/IB is flat over A/I.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.IsRelativelyRegular.polynomial` (example): The variables x_1,…,x_r of A[x_1,…,x_r] are relatively regular for every ideal I.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.IsRelativelyRegular.baseChange` (functoriality): Relative regularity is preserved by base change along A → A′.

**Unit tests.**

- `relatively_regular_variable` (computation): In Z[x] over Z with I = (p), the sequence [x] is relatively regular.
- `relatively_regular_empty_self` (degenerate): For B = A the empty sequence is relatively regular for every I.
- `relatively_regular_p_fails` (non-example): In Z over Z with I = (p), the sequence [p] is not relatively regular: it is zero on Z/p, hence not regular there.
- `relatively_regular_non_flat_quotient` (non-example): In Z[x] over Z with I = (0), the sequence [p·x] is regular but not relatively regular: Z[x]/(p·x) is not flat over Z.

**Acceptance.** For A = Z_p, I = (p), B = Z_p⟨x⟩: the sequence (x) is p-completely regular relative to A. For A = Z_p, I = (p), B = Z_p: the sequence (p) is not p-completely regular relative to A, since Kos(Z_p; p) → Kos(Z_p; p, p) is not flat.

**Sources.** [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Definition 2.42. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 26. Definition as printed..

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-0-correction-identity"></a>

### Cleared-denominator correction identity

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/correction-identity` · lemma. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Delta` in `TauCeti/RingTheory/Delta/Basic`.

In every commutative ring, p C_p(x,y)=x^p+y^p-(x+y)^p.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** p is prime. Multiplication by p need not be injective in R.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Multiply the finite sum by p and use exact integer divisibility of its coefficients.
2. Apply the pinned binomial theorem and separate its i=0 and i=p terms. No cancellation in R is used.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-addition-correction`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-delta-addition-correction); [`mathlib:add_pow`](#mathlib-add-pow); [`mathlib:Nat.Prime.dvd_choose_self`](#mathlib-nat-prime-dvd-choose-self).

**Acceptance.** The identity holds in characteristic p, although it cannot recover C_p there.

**Sources.** [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Definition 2.1. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 13. Explicit polynomial justification of the correction, not division in the target..

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-0-delta-frobenius-dictionary"></a>

### Delta structure on a ring

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-frobenius-dictionary` · definition. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Delta` in `TauCeti/RingTheory/Delta/Basic`.

On the existing ring R, a delta structure is a function delta:R->R with delta(0)=delta(1)=0, delta(x+y)=delta(x)+delta(y)+C_p(x,y), and delta(xy)=x^p delta(y)+y^p delta(x)+p delta(x)delta(y). Morphisms are unital ring maps commuting with delta. Retain the integrated dictionary ID for this definition; its two equivalences are separate construction nodes.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** p is prime; R is a commutative unital ring. The elementary polynomial prefix is generalized to rings; subsequent prismatic consumers retain the source Z_(p)-algebra hypotheses.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Package precisely the four polynomial axioms as data on R, not an assumed comparison theorem. Delta is not an additive map.
2. Prove extensionality from equality of the functions. Apply the addition law to x+(-x) and to 1+1 for the elementary API.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-addition-correction`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-delta-addition-correction).

**Consumers.** PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/distinguished-factor-rigidity: The product identity controls delta of a product.. HabiroRings:HR.1 and PerfectoidQuotients:Q0: Import one-prime delta data, not a second construction or all-prime commuting lifts..

**Planning API.**

- `TauCeti.Delta.Structure.ext` (extensionality): Pointwise equality of delta gives equality of structures.
- `TauCeti.Delta.Structure.delta_neg` (relation): delta(-x)=-delta(x)-C_p(x,-x).
- `TauCeti.Delta.Structure.delta_two` (simp): delta(1+1)=C_p(1,1).

**Unit tests.**

- `delta_two_forced` (computation): Every 2-delta structure on Z sends 2 to -1.
- `delta_zero_operation_rejected` (non-example): No 2-delta structure on Z has identically zero delta.
- `delta_zero_ring` (degenerate): The zero ring admits a delta structure.
- `delta_product_rule_integers` (computation): Every 2-δ-structure on Z has δ(4) = −6 = 2²·δ(2) + 2²·δ(2) + 2·δ(2)² with δ(2) = −1: the product rule with its term p·δ(x)·δ(y).

**Acceptance.** The zero operation on Z is not a delta structure. A delta structure alone is not a prism: no ideal or completion is supplied.

**Sources.** [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Definition 2.1; opening p-local convention. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 13. Preserves the actual axioms and distinguishes the elementary generalization from the source's prismatic scope..

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-0-correction-map-naturality"></a>

### Naturality of the integral correction

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/correction-map-naturality` · lemma. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Delta` in `TauCeti/RingTheory/Delta/Localization`.

For a unital ring map f:R->T, f(C_p(x,y))=C_p(f(x),f(y)). This promotes the existing addCorrection_map API without introducing a second declaration.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** p is prime; R and T are commutative rings, including rings with p-torsion.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Apply the ring map to the finite sum defining C_p. Each integer coefficient, power and product is preserved. The division was performed in the integers before evaluation.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-addition-correction`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-delta-addition-correction).

**Acceptance.** Reduction to characteristic p retains the correction polynomial.

**Sources.** [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Definition 2.1: integral addition polynomial; existing addCorrection_map API. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 13. Explicit API promotion needed by the new coefficientwise Witt map..

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-0-witt2-unit-criterion"></a>

### Units in length-two Witt vectors

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/witt2-unit-criterion` · lemma. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Delta` in `TauCeti/RingTheory/Delta/Localization`.

For z=(a,b) in W_2(R), z is a unit if and only if both a and a^p+p*b are units of R.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** p is prime; R is an arbitrary commutative ring, possibly zero.

**Construction or proof.**

1. An inverse z*(c,d)=1 gives ac=1. Expanding the first ghost polynomial of the product gives (a^p+p*b)(c^p+p*d)=1. Hence both factors specified in the statement are units.
2. Conversely, put g=a^p+p*b and use the actual inverses of the units a and g. The Witt vector (a^(-1),-b*a^(-p)*g^(-1)) has product with z equal to (1,0): its second coordinate is g*(-b*a^(-p)*g^(-1))+a^(-p)*b=0. Commutativity gives a two-sided inverse.
3. Zeroth-coordinate and one-coordinate rules are obtained from constantCoeff and surjective truncation. No p-cancellation or ghost injectivity over R is used.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/witt2-mul-coordinate`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-witt2-mul-coordinate); [`mathlib:WittVector.constantCoeff`](#mathlib-wittvector-constantcoeff); [`mathlib:WittVector.truncate_surjective`](#mathlib-wittvector-truncate-surjective); [`mathlib:WittVector.coeff_truncate`](#mathlib-wittvector-coeff-truncate); [`mathlib:TruncatedWittVector.ext`](#mathlib-truncatedwittvector-ext).

**Acceptance.** For p=2 over Z, (1,1) is not a unit although its first coordinate is. Over F_p the criterion reduces to invertibility of a. The unique vector over the zero ring is a unit.

**Sources.** [BS22-LOCALIZATION](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Lemma 2.15 and proof. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 16. An explicit refinement of the localization argument; the sharper unit criterion and Witt proof are authored deductions, not a claim about the printed proof..

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-0-delta-adic-correction"></a>

### Ideal membership of the addition correction

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-adic-correction` · lemma. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Delta` in `TauCeti/RingTheory/Delta/AdicCompletion`.

For any ideal J of A, if y is in J then C_p(x,y) is in J, for arbitrary x.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** p is prime; A is a commutative ring. The ideal need not contain p.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Every term in the fixed correction polynomial has a positive exponent of y. Each monomial therefore belongs to J, and finite sums and negation preserve membership. The calculation uses no division in A.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-addition-correction`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-delta-addition-correction).

**Acceptance.** The assertion applies to J=I^m and supplies the correction in a congruence calculation.

**Sources.** [BS22-COMPLETION](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Lemma 2.17, full statement and proof, printed. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 17. An explicit refinement of the classical completion proof. The shifted quotient maps and one-power estimate are derived here, not attributed as separately numbered source results..

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-0-associated-frobenius"></a>

### Associated Frobenius endomorphism

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/associated-frobenius` · construction. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Delta` in `TauCeti/RingTheory/Delta/Basic`.

Construct the ordinary lift phi_delta(x)=x^p+p delta(x) from a delta structure, for arbitrary commutative rings including p-torsion.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** p is prime; use the given delta structure on R.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Zero and unit follow from the corresponding delta axioms.
2. For addition expand the delta law and use correction-identity. For multiplication expand the delta product law and factor as phi(x)phi(y).
3. Delta(x) supplies the congruence witness. A delta-compatible ring map commutes with phi by the same expansion.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-frobenius-dictionary`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-delta-frobenius-dictionary); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/ordinary-frobenius-lift`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-ordinary-frobenius-lift); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/correction-identity`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-correction-identity).

**Consumers.** PR.0 prism condition p in I+phi(I)R: Supplies an actual ring endomorphism before imposing the prism condition..

**Planning API.**

- `TauCeti.Delta.toFrobenius_apply` (simp): Evaluation is x^p+p delta(x).
- `TauCeti.Delta.toFrobenius_rank_one` (relation): delta(x)=0 implies phi(x)=x^p.
- `TauCeti.Delta.toFrobenius_map` (functoriality): Delta-compatible ring maps commute with associated Frobenius.

**Unit tests.**

- `phi_rank_one` (computation): A delta-zero element has phi(x)=x^p.
- `phi_integer_two` (computation): For the canonical operation on Z at p=2, phi(2)=2, not 4.
- `phi_zero_ring` (degenerate): Any two structures on the zero ring give the same lift.

**Acceptance.** No converse without a cancellation hypothesis is asserted.

**Sources.** [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Remark 2.2. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 13. Builds the ring-map laws rather than assuming the associated endomorphism..

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-0-delta-stable-quotient"></a>

### Descent to a delta-stable quotient

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-stable-quotient` · theorem. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Delta` in `TauCeti/RingTheory/Delta/Basic`.

For a delta structure on R and an ideal I, delta(I) contained in I is equivalent to existence of a unique delta structure on R/I compatible with the quotient map.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** p is prime; use the actual ideal and quotient ring.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Replacing a representative a by a+i changes delta(a) by delta(i)+C_p(a,i). Stability puts the first term in I; every monomial of the correction has a positive power of i, so the second lies in I.
2. Descend the four polynomial axioms. Surjectivity of the quotient gives uniqueness. Conversely, compatibility on an element of I puts its delta in the kernel.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-frobenius-dictionary`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-delta-frobenius-dictionary); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-addition-correction`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-delta-addition-correction).

**Acceptance.** I=0 returns the original operation and I=R gives the zero ring. The ideal (p) in canonical Z is Frobenius-stable but not delta-stable, since delta(p)=1-p^(p-1).

**Sources.** [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Lemma 2.9. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 15. The quotient construction with its necessary stability and uniqueness conditions..

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-0-square-zero-correction"></a>

### Correction polynomial on a square-zero extension

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/square-zero-correction` · lemma. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Delta` in `TauCeti/RingTheory/Delta/Basic`.

Let B map to F_p and use its central action. In the existing square-zero extension B plus F_p, the second coordinate of C_p((a,b),(c,d)) is (abar^(p-1)-(abar+cbar)^(p-1))*b+(cbar^(p-1)-(abar+cbar)^(p-1))*d.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** p is prime; B is commutative; the left action comes from the unital B->F_p map and the opposite action is central.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Expand powers with snd_pow and products with snd_mul. Termwise, a finite polynomial has second coordinate its first partial derivative times b plus its second partial derivative times d.
2. Differentiate the integral polynomial identity p C_p(X,Y)=X^p+Y^p-(X+Y)^p termwise, then cancel p in Z[X,Y]. This gives partial_X C_p=X^(p-1)-(X+Y)^(p-1) and the Y analogue.
3. Evaluate these already-integral identities in F_p. No division or cancellation occurs there.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/correction-identity`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-correction-identity); [`mathlib:TrivSqZeroExt.snd_mul`](#mathlib-trivsqzeroext-snd-mul); [`mathlib:TrivSqZeroExt.snd_pow`](#mathlib-trivsqzeroext-snd-pow); [`mathlib:add_pow`](#mathlib-add-pow).

**Acceptance.** At p=2 the result is -cbar*b-abar*d, the second coordinate of -xy.

**Sources.** [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Definition 2.1; authored square-zero acceptance calculation. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 13. The existing square-zero coordinate arithmetic..

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-0-witt2-add-coordinate"></a>

### Second coordinate of length-two Witt addition

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/witt2-add-coordinate` · lemma. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Delta` in `TauCeti/RingTheory/Delta/Basic`.

On TruncatedWittVector p 2 R, (x+y)_1=x_1+y_1+C_p(x_0,y_0), for arbitrary commutative R.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** p is prime; use the existing Witt ring operations, not pointwise operations.

**Construction or proof.**

1. First work over the integer polynomial ring in four input coordinates. Use ghost components 0 and 1 as ring maps and the first two Witt polynomials. Subtract the zeroth-coordinate pth powers and cancel p only in this universal ring. correction-identity identifies the correction.
2. Evaluate the variables in R using WittVector.map and map_coeff, then truncate the infinite universal vectors. Surjectivity and unchanged coordinates give the formula for every truncated vector. Zero-padding is only a lift of sets, not a ring map.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/correction-identity`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-correction-identity); [`mathlib:WittVector.ghostComponent`](#mathlib-wittvector-ghostcomponent); [`mathlib:WittVector.ghostComponent_apply`](#mathlib-wittvector-ghostcomponent-apply); [`mathlib:wittPolynomial_zero`](#mathlib-wittpolynomial-zero); [`mathlib:wittPolynomial_one`](#mathlib-wittpolynomial-one); [`mathlib:WittVector.map`](#mathlib-wittvector-map); [`mathlib:WittVector.map_coeff`](#mathlib-wittvector-map-coeff); [`mathlib:WittVector.truncate`](#mathlib-wittvector-truncate); [`mathlib:WittVector.truncate_surjective`](#mathlib-wittvector-truncate-surjective); [`mathlib:WittVector.coeff_truncate`](#mathlib-wittvector-coeff-truncate); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/correction-map-naturality`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-correction-map-naturality).

**Acceptance.** Over F_2, (1,0)+(1,0)=(0,1), rejecting pointwise addition.

**Sources.** [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Remark 2.4. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 13. Constructs the coordinate formula on the existing carrier by universal polynomial descent, not ghost injectivity in R..

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-0-delta-adic-power-loss"></a>

### One-power loss on an ideal containing p

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-adic-power-loss` · lemma. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Delta` in `TauCeti/RingTheory/Delta/AdicCompletion`.

If p is in the ideal I of the delta ring A, then delta(x) is in I^n whenever x is in I^(n+1), for every n>=0. No finite-generation or Noetherian hypothesis.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** p is prime; I is an actual ideal in the given commutative delta ring; p means the integer cast.

**Construction or proof.**

1. For n=0 the target ideal is the whole ring. Induct on n, writing I^(n+2)=I^(n+1)*I and using the existing dependent product-membership induction, retaining membership of the intermediate summands.
2. For a in I^(n+1) and b in I, the product formula has terms a^p*delta(b), b^p*delta(a) and p*delta(a)*delta(b). By the induction hypothesis these lie respectively in I^(p*(n+1)), I^(p+n) and I^(n+1), hence all in I^(n+1).
3. For a sum of elements of I^(n+2), the two delta values are already in I^(n+1). Its addition correction lies in I^(n+2) by delta-adic-correction, hence in I^(n+1). This closes the dependent product induction; no assertion that delta is additive is used.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-frobenius-dictionary`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-delta-frobenius-dictionary); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-adic-correction`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-delta-adic-correction); [`mathlib:Submodule.mul_induction_on'`](#mathlib-submodule-mul-induction-on-).

**Acceptance.** For canonical delta on Z and I=(p), delta(p^(n+1))=p^n*(1-p^((n+1)*(p-1))) has exactly order n, so the loss is sharp. The hypothesis p in I matters: on Z_(p)[X] with phi(X)=X^p+p, delta(X^m) has nonzero constant term p^(m-1), so it is not (X)-adically continuous.

**Sources.** [BS22-COMPLETION](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Lemma 2.17, full statement and proof, printed. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 17. An explicit refinement of the classical completion proof. The shifted quotient maps and one-power estimate are derived here, not attributed as separately numbered source results..

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-0-witt2-unit-jacobson"></a>

### Witt units over a radical base

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/witt2-unit-jacobson` · lemma. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Delta` in `TauCeti/RingTheory/Delta/Localization`.

If p belongs to jacobson(0_B), a vector z in the existing W_2(B) is a unit exactly when its zeroth Witt coordinate is a unit.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** B is a commutative ring and p_B is in its Jacobson radical.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Use witt2-unit-criterion: the two necessary and sufficient units are a=z_0 and g=a^p+p*z_1.
2. When a is a unit, factor g=a^p*(1+p*z_1*a^(-p)). The second factor is a unit by the pinned Jacobson criterion. The converse is the first condition of the exact Witt criterion.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/witt2-unit-criterion`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-witt2-unit-criterion); [`mathlib:Ideal.mem_jacobson_bot`](#mathlib-ideal-mem-jacobson-bot).

**Consumers.** PR.0 coefficient and localization inputs to local distinguished generators: Supplies the actual p-local delta structure or its target unit condition without p-cancellation..

**Acceptance.** Over F_p this recovers the first-coordinate criterion without ghost injectivity. Over Z at p=2 the vector (1,1) is a counterexample when the radical hypothesis is removed, since its first ghost expression is 3.

**Sources.** [BS22-FRESH-LOCAL](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Remark 2.4; Remark 2.16. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed pages 13, 17. Authored specialization of the already planned exact Witt unit criterion, motivated by the source radical argument..

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-0-delta-span-stability"></a>

### Delta stability from ideal generators

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-span-stability` · lemma. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Delta` in `TauCeti/RingTheory/Delta/Ideal`.

For a subset S of A, the ordinary ideal J generated by S is delta-stable if and only if delta(s) belongs to J for every s in S.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** p is prime; A is a commutative ring with the specified delta structure d. No p-torsionfreeness, finite generation or p-locality is assumed.

**Construction or proof.**

1. The forward implication is restriction along the inclusion of S in its ideal span.
2. For the converse apply span induction to the predicate delta(x) belongs to J, keeping x in J as the induction membership. Zero follows from delta(0)=0.
3. For a sum, use the delta addition identity and delta-adic-correction with J: the correction term is in J because the second summand is in J.
4. For a scalar multiple ax, use delta(ax)=a^p delta(x)+x^p delta(a)+p delta(a)delta(x). The first and third terms lie in J by the inductive hypothesis, and the second because x lies in J and p is positive. This argument never assumes delta is additive.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-frobenius-dictionary`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-delta-frobenius-dictionary); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-adic-correction`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-delta-adic-correction); [`mathlib:Ideal.subset_span`](#mathlib-ideal-subset-span); [`mathlib:Submodule.span_induction`](#mathlib-submodule-span-induction).

**Acceptance.** The empty generating set gives the stable zero ideal. For p=2 on the integers, the generator 2 fails the criterion because delta(2)=-1 is not in (2).

**Sources.** [BS22-DELTA-QUOTIENT](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Section 2 opening convention and Definition 2.1; Lemma 2.9 and Example 2.10. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed pages 13, 15. Declaration-sized refinement of the source universal delta quotient. The source uses p-local rings; the displayed proof uses only the integral delta identities and establishes this explicitly broader elementary statement..

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-0-torsionfree-frobenius-equivalence"></a>

### Torsion-free Frobenius reconstruction

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/torsionfree-frobenius-equivalence` · construction. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Delta` in `TauCeti/RingTheory/Delta/Basic`.

If multiplication by p on R is injective, construct an equivalence between delta structures and ordinary Frobenius lifts, with forward map associated-frobenius. CharZero alone is not sufficient.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** p is prime. Multiplication by the cast of p on R is injective; the zero ring is permitted.

**Construction or proof.**

1. The congruence gives a solution delta(x) of p delta(x)=f(x)-x^p, unique by injectivity. Choose it pointwise.
2. Multiply each proposed delta axiom by p. Addition uses correction-identity; multiplication expands (x^p+p delta(x))(y^p+p delta(y)). The differences are the additivity and multiplicativity errors of f, hence zero. Cancel only the remaining factor p.
3. Both composites are identities by the same uniqueness and ring-map extensionality. The public equivalence does not depend on witness choices.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/associated-frobenius`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-associated-frobenius); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/correction-identity`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-correction-identity).

**Consumers.** PR.0 crystalline and Breuil-Kisin examples: Converts a constructed lift into delta only after checking p-torsionfreeness..

**Planning API.**

- `TauCeti.Delta.frobeniusEquiv_apply` (compatibility): The forward map is toFrobenius.
- `TauCeti.Delta.frobeniusEquiv_symm_spec` (characterisation): The inverse satisfies p delta(x)=f(x)-x^p.
- `TauCeti.Delta.frobeniusEquiv_symm_toFrobenius` (relation): Reconstruction from the associated lift returns the original structure.

**Unit tests.**

- `reconstruction_integer_value` (computation): At p=2 the identity on Z reconstructs delta(2)=-1.
- `reconstruction_rejects_characteristic_p` (non-example): Multiplication by p is not injective on F_p.
- `reconstruction_zero_ring` (degenerate): Multiplication by p is injective on the zero ring.

**Acceptance.** The zero ring meets the injectivity condition vacuously. A characteristic-zero ring with a p-torsion ideal need not meet it.

**Sources.** [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Remark 2.2. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 13. Retains exactly the p-torsionfree reconstruction hypothesis and constructs both inverses..

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-0-square-zero-delta-family"></a>

### Delta structures on a square-zero extension

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/square-zero-delta-family` · construction. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Delta` in `TauCeti/RingTheory/Delta/Basic`.

For a delta ring B mapping to F_p and lambda in F_p, define delta_lambda(a,b)=(delta_B(a),(lambda-abar^(p-1))*b) on the existing central square-zero extension B plus F_p. This is a delta structure with associated Frobenius (a,b)->(phi_B(a),0).

1. The first coordinates of the four axioms are those for B; zero and unit in the second coordinate are immediate.
2. For addition insert square-zero-correction. The second coordinate simplifies to (lambda-(abar+cbar)^(p-1))*(b+d).
3. For multiplication the second coordinates of x^p and y^p vanish, and so does that of p delta(x)delta(y). Use abar^p=abar and cbar^p=cbar to get (lambda-(abar*cbar)^(p-1))*(abar*d+cbar*b).

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-0-delta-witt-section-equivalence"></a>

### Delta structures as Witt-vector sections

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-witt-section-equivalence` · construction. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Delta` in `TauCeti/RingTheory/Delta/Basic`.

For arbitrary R, construct an equivalence between delta structures and unital ring maps s:R->TruncatedWittVector p 2 R whose first coordinate is s(x)_0=x. Send delta to s(x)=(x,delta(x)); recover delta from coordinate one. This is a first-coordinate section, not a ghost-map section.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** p is prime; no p-torsionfreeness hypothesis on R.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Given delta, construct the two-coordinate vector. The two preceding Witt formulas and delta axioms give preservation of addition and multiplication. Zero and one have coordinates (0,0) and (1,0).
2. Given a ring-map section, take its second coordinate. The ring-map laws and coordinate formulas give all four delta axioms.
3. Coefficient extensionality and the first-coordinate condition prove both inverse identities. The first ghost expression x^p+p delta(x) identifies the composite with associated Frobenius, without cancellation in R.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-frobenius-dictionary`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-delta-frobenius-dictionary); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/associated-frobenius`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-associated-frobenius); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/witt2-add-coordinate`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-witt2-add-coordinate); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/witt2-mul-coordinate`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-witt2-mul-coordinate); [`mathlib:TruncatedWittVector`](#mathlib-truncatedwittvector); [`mathlib:TruncatedWittVector.ext`](#mathlib-truncatedwittvector-ext); [`mathlib:WittVector.constantCoeff`](#mathlib-wittvector-constantcoeff); [`mathlib:WittVector.truncate_surjective`](#mathlib-wittvector-truncate-surjective); [`mathlib:WittVector.coeff_truncate`](#mathlib-wittvector-coeff-truncate).

**Consumers.** PR.0 free delta-algebra, localization and Witt-adjunction work: Supplies torsion-safe underived data before the full adjunction or derived comparison is constructed..

**Planning API.**

- `TauCeti.Delta.wittSectionEquiv_apply` (constructor): The section has coordinates (x,delta(x)).
- `TauCeti.Delta.wittSectionEquiv_symm_apply` (projection): The inverse recovers coordinate one.
- `TauCeti.Delta.wittSectionEquiv_ghost_one` (compatibility): s(x)_0^p+p*s(x)_1 equals phi_delta(x).

**Unit tests.**

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-0-witt2-coefficient-map"></a>

### Coefficient map on length-two Witt vectors

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/witt2-coefficient-map` · construction. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Delta` in `TauCeti/RingTheory/Delta/Localization`.

For a ring map f:R->T construct witt2Map(f):W_2(R)->W_2(T) with both Witt coordinates mapped by f, using the existing TruncatedWittVector p 2 carrier.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** p is prime; R,T are commutative rings. No torsion-freeness or condition on the Jacobson radical.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Apply f coordinatewise. The zeroth-coordinate, zero and unit rules follow from the pinned infinite Witt map and surjective coordinate-preserving truncation.
2. The second addition-coordinate formula and correction-map-naturality give additivity. The second multiplication-coordinate formula gives multiplicativity by applying f to each factor and integer coefficient. Package the resulting map as a RingHom.
3. Prove identity and composition by equality of both coordinates. This is a length-two adapter; it does not rebuild truncated Witt rings.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/correction-map-naturality`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-correction-map-naturality); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/witt2-add-coordinate`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-witt2-add-coordinate); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/witt2-mul-coordinate`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-witt2-mul-coordinate); [`mathlib:WittVector.map`](#mathlib-wittvector-map); [`mathlib:WittVector.map_coeff`](#mathlib-wittvector-map-coeff); [`mathlib:WittVector.truncate_surjective`](#mathlib-wittvector-truncate-surjective); [`mathlib:WittVector.coeff_truncate`](#mathlib-wittvector-coeff-truncate); [`mathlib:TruncatedWittVector.ext`](#mathlib-truncatedwittvector-ext).

**Consumers.** PR.0/delta-localization and delta-localization-universal: Carries the actual Witt section to the localized coefficient ring and compares sections under a delta morphism..

**Planning API.**

- `TauCeti.Delta.witt2Map_coeff` (projection): The jth coordinate of witt2Map(f)(z) equals f(z_j); the separate lemma node supplies this API.
- `TauCeti.Delta.witt2Map_id` (functoriality): The identity ring map induces the identity Witt map.
- `TauCeti.Delta.witt2Map_comp` (functoriality): witt2Map(g composed with f)=witt2Map(g) composed with witt2Map(f).
- `TauCeti.Delta.witt2Map_truncate` (compatibility): For a ring map f:R→S and x∈W(R), witt2Map(f)(truncate₂(x)) = truncate₂(WittVector.map(f)(x)).

**Unit tests.**

- `witt2_map_identity` (compatibility): witt2Map(id)(z)=z.
- `witt2_map_torsion_coordinate` (computation): The image of (0,1) in W_2(Z) under reduction to W_2(F_2) has coordinates (0,1), although both target ghost coordinates vanish.
- `witt2_map_zero_target` (degenerate): Any coefficient map to the zero ring sends every length-two Witt vector to zero.

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-0-delta-adic-congruence"></a>

### Uniform ideal-adic congruence bound

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-adic-congruence` · lemma. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Delta` in `TauCeti/RingTheory/Delta/AdicCompletion`.

If p is in I and x-y is in I^(n+1), then delta(x)-delta(y) is in I^n. Thus the modulus of ideal-adic uniform continuity may be chosen as n+1.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** p is prime; I need not be finitely generated and A need not be separated.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Put h=x-y. The addition law gives delta(y+h)-delta(y)=delta(h)+C_p(y,h).
2. Apply delta-adic-power-loss to the first term. Apply delta-adic-correction to place the second in I^(n+1), then in I^n.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-adic-power-loss`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-delta-adic-power-loss); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-adic-correction`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-delta-adic-correction); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-frobenius-dictionary`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-delta-frobenius-dictionary).

**Acceptance.** At p=2, 0 and 2 are equal modulo 2 but their deltas are 0 and -1 modulo 2. An unshifted congruence is false.

**Sources.** [BS22-COMPLETION](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Lemma 2.17, full statement and proof, printed. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 17. An explicit refinement of the classical completion proof. The shifted quotient maps and one-power estimate are derived here, not attributed as separately numbered source results..

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-0-frobenius-image-unit-jacobson"></a>

### Frobenius image units in radical targets

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/frobenius-image-unit-jacobson` · lemma. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Delta` in `TauCeti/RingTheory/Delta/Localization`.

Let d be a delta structure on A and f:A→B any unital ring map. If p lies in the Jacobson radical of B, then f(phi_d(x)) is a unit exactly when f(x) is a unit, for every x in A. No delta structure on B or delta compatibility of f is assumed.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** p is prime; A and B are commutative unital rings, including zero rings; p_B belongs to jacobson(0_B).

**Construction or proof.**

1. Expand f(phi_d(x))=f(x)^p+p_B*f(delta_A(x)). The second term lies in the radical.
2. For a unit u and radical element r, u+r=u*(1+u^(-1)*r) is a unit by Ideal.mem_jacobson_bot. Apply this first with u=f(x)^p. For the converse apply it with u=f(phi_d(x)) and radical element -p_B*f(delta_A(x)).
3. A positive power is a unit if and only if its base is a unit: an inverse to a^p gives an inverse a^(p-1)*(a^p)^(-1). This proves the reverse implication without any Frobenius on B.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/associated-frobenius`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-associated-frobenius); [`mathlib:Ideal.jacobson`](#mathlib-ideal-jacobson); [`mathlib:Ideal.mem_jacobson_bot`](#mathlib-ideal-mem-jacobson-bot).

**Consumers.** PR.0 coefficient and localization inputs to local distinguished generators: Supplies the actual p-local delta structure or its target unit condition without p-cancellation..

**Acceptance.** With f the identity on a delta ring having p in its radical, Frobenius reflects units. The proof never replaces delta compatibility by Frobenius compatibility in a torsion target.

**Sources.** [BS22-FRESH-LOCAL](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Remark 2.16, printed; associated Frobenius formula of Remark 2.2. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed pages 13, 17. The needed image version is an explicit deduction of the radical-unit argument; it is stronger than the stated one-direction observation and does not require a target delta structure..

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-0-p-torsion-freeness-criteria"></a>

### p-torsion in δ-rings

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/p-torsion-freeness-criteria` · lemma. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Delta` in `TauCeti/RingTheory/Delta/Perfect`.

A δ-ring A is p-torsion-free if its Frobenius φ is injective (for instance if A is perfect), and also if A is reduced. Neither hypothesis implies the other: A = Z_p[x]/(x^p − 1) with φ(x) = x^p is reduced and φ(x − 1) = 0; B = Z_p[x]/(x^2) with φ(x) = p·x is not reduced and φ is injective.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** A is any δ-ring. (The source assumes Z_(p)-algebras and uses that δ(p) = 1 − p^{p−1} is a unit; this is not needed, because p·x = 0 gives p^{p−1}φ(x) = φ(p^{p−1}x) = 0 and δ(p)φ(x) = 0, hence φ(x) = 0.)

**Construction or proof.**

1. Stronger claim: if p·x=0 then φ(x)=0. The formula p^p·δ(x)=p^(p−1)·(φ(x)−x^p)=φ(p^(p−1)·x)−p^(p−1)·x^p gives p^p·δ(x)=0 because p≥2. Applying δ to p·x=0 then gives δ(p)·φ(x)=0. Also p^(p−1)·φ(x)=φ(p^(p−1)·x)=0. Integer-cast-delta gives δ(p)+p^(p−1)=1, so adding these annihilation equations gives φ(x)=0 without any unit hypothesis. Injectivity of φ now forces x=0.
2. If A is reduced and p x = 0: p^p δ(x) = 0 gives p δ(x) = 0 by reducedness; φ(x) = 0 gives x^p = −p δ(x) = 0, so x = 0 (BS22 proof of Lemma 2.28).

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-frobenius-dictionary`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-delta-frobenius-dictionary); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/associated-frobenius`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-associated-frobenius); [`mathlib:IsReduced`](#mathlib-isreduced); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/integer-cast-delta`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-integer-cast-delta).

**Acceptance.** Z ⊕ F_2·ε with the λ = 1 structure of square-zero-delta-family has 2-torsion and is neither reduced nor has injective Frobenius. The two examples of Remark 2.29.

**Sources.** [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Lemma 2.28 (p-torsion in δ-rings) with proof; Remark 2.29. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 20. Lemma and the two examples showing the criteria are not comparable..

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-0-integer-delta"></a>

### Canonical delta operation on the integers

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/integer-delta` · construction. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Delta` in `TauCeti/RingTheory/Delta/Basic`.

Construct the canonical delta structure on Z with D_p(a)=(a-a^p)/p, using exact integer division. Its associated Frobenius is the identity. This is the integral elementary prefix of the source p-local example.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** p is prime. Negative integers and p=2 are included.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Apply FiniteField.pow_card in F_p to show that p divides a-a^p for every integer a.
2. The identity map on Z is an ordinary lift. Multiplication by the nonzero integer p is injective, so apply the established reconstruction.
3. The inverse equation gives the quotient formula and, at a=p, D_p(p)=1-p^(p-1).

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/torsionfree-frobenius-equivalence`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-torsionfree-frobenius-equivalence); [`mathlib:FiniteField.pow_card`](#mathlib-finitefield-pow-card).

**Consumers.** integer-cast-delta and square-zero-delta-family: Pins scalar, negative-integer and dyadic conventions..

**Planning API.**

- `TauCeti.Delta.intDelta_apply` (simp): delta(a)=(a-a^p)/p in Z.
- `TauCeti.Delta.intDelta_frobenius` (compatibility): Associated Frobenius is RingHom.id Z.
- `TauCeti.Delta.intDelta_prime` (example): delta(p)=1-p^(p-1).

**Unit tests.**

- `integer_negative_dyadic` (computation): D_2(-1)=-1.
- `integer_cubic_value` (computation): D_3(2)=-2.
- `integer_zero` (degenerate): D_p(0)=0.

**Acceptance.** D_2(-1)=-1, whereas at odd p it is zero.

**Sources.** [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Example 2.6. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 14. Restricts the source formula to Z and proves its integrality; it does not identify Z with Z_(p)..

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-0-frobenius-forgetful-not-injective"></a>

### Distinct delta structures with the same Frobenius

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/frobenius-forgetful-not-injective` · theorem. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Delta` in `TauCeti/RingTheory/Delta/Basic`.

For lambda different from mu in F_p, the square-zero structures on B plus F_p differ but have the same associated lift. With B=Z the ring has characteristic zero; with B=Z_(p) it is p-local. Ordinary Frobenius data need not determine delta.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** The base and scalar actions are those of square-zero-delta-family; lambda and mu are distinct.

**Construction or proof.**

1. At epsilon=(0,1) the values are inr(lambda) and inr(mu), distinct by injectivity of inr.
2. Both associated maps send (a,b) to inl(phi_B(a)); ring-map extensionality proves equality.
3. For the p-local example, (a-a^p)/p lies in Z_(p) by reduction to F_p, and multiplication by p is injective. Reconstruct its canonical base structure, then apply the general family. The integer ring is not silently treated as p-local.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/square-zero-delta-family`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-square-zero-delta-family); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/torsionfree-frobenius-equivalence`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-torsionfree-frobenius-equivalence); [`mathlib:TrivSqZeroExt.inr_injective`](#mathlib-trivsqzeroext-inr-injective).

**Acceptance.** The identity between the two structures is Frobenius-compatible but not delta-compatible. For lambda=1, phi(epsilon)=epsilon^p=0 while delta(epsilon)=epsilon is nonzero, rejecting the rank-one converse.

**Sources.** [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Remarks 2.2-2.3 and Example 2.6; authored witness. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed pages 13, 14. A concrete failure of strengthened hypotheses, not an allegation of an error in the source..

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-0-delta-shifted-quotient"></a>

### Shifted quotient delta operation

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-shifted-quotient` · construction. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Delta` in `TauCeti/RingTheory/Delta/AdicCompletion`.

For each n, construct the function q_n:A/I^(n+1) -> A/I^n sending the class of a to the class of delta(a). This is a function, not a ring homomorphism, additive map or delta structure on either finite quotient.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** p is prime and lies in I; A carries the given delta structure.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Two representatives of a class differ by I^(n+1). The congruence bound makes their delta values equal modulo I^n, so quotient recursion defines q_n.
2. This constructs only a one-step-shifted map. It imposes no delta-stability on I or its powers and no false delta structure on a nonzero p-nilpotent ring.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-adic-congruence`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-delta-adic-congruence).

**Consumers.** delta-classical-completion: Defines the nth completed delta coordinate from one higher precision of the input..

**Planning API.**

- `TauCeti.Delta.shiftedQuotient_mk` (simp): q_n([a]_(n+1))=[delta(a)]_n; the separate lemma node supplies this evaluation.
- `TauCeti.Delta.shiftedQuotient_transition` (functoriality): For m<=n, reduction from n to m after q_n equals q_m after reduction from n+1 to m+1.
- `TauCeti.Delta.shiftedQuotient_zero` (simp): q_n(0)=0, including the zero target A/I^0.

**Unit tests.**

- `shifted_quotient_zero_level` (degenerate): The map q_0 has target A/I^0=0 and sends every input to zero.

**Acceptance.** The map q_1 sends 2 mod 4 to -1 mod 2 at p=2 and is not additive.

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-0-free-delta-ring"></a>

### Free δ-rings

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/free-delta-ring` · construction. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Delta` in `TauCeti/RingTheory/Delta/Free`.

For a set S, the free δ-ring Z{S} on S is the polynomial ring Z[x_{s,n} : s ∈ S, n ≥ 0] with the unique δ-structure such that δ(x_{s,n}) = x_{s,n+1}; its Frobenius is φ(x_{s,n}) = x_{s,n}^p + p·x_{s,n+1}. For every δ-ring R and every family (f_s) in R there is a unique map of δ-rings Z{S} → R with x_{s,0} ↦ f_s; it sends x_{s,n} to δ^n(f_s). The Frobenius endomorphism of Z{S} is faithfully flat. After inverting p, Z{S}[1/p] is also the polynomial ring on the elements φ^n(x_{s,0}). The source works over Z_(p); Z_(p){S} = Z{S} ⊗_Z Z_(p), and all statements base-change.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** p is prime; S is any set. The source states the one-generator case over Z_(p) (all rings there are Z_(p)-algebras); the statement over Z has the same proof, since Z[x_{s,n}] is p-torsion-free and the displayed φ lifts Frobenius, and it base-changes to the source statement.

**Construction or proof.**

1. On A = Z[x_{s,n}] define the ring endomorphism φ(x_{s,n}) = x_{s,n}^p + p·x_{s,n+1}. It lifts Frobenius modulo p, and A is p-torsion-free, so torsionfree-frobenius-equivalence gives the unique δ-structure with φ as its Frobenius; it satisfies δ(x_{s,n}) = x_{s,n+1}.
2. Universal property: the ring map η with η(x_{s,n}) = δ^n(f_s) exists and is unique by the universal property of the polynomial ring; it commutes with δ on the generators, hence everywhere because the two δ-identities determine δ on the subring generated by the x_{s,n} (BS22, proof of Lemma 2.11).
3. Faithful flatness: write φ as the filtered colimit of the maps Z[x_{s,j} : j ≤ i] → Z[x_{s,j} : j ≤ i+1]. By the fibrewise criterion it suffices to treat [1/p], where the map shifts the polynomial generators φ^j(x), and the reduction modulo p, where it is Frobenius followed by a polynomial inclusion; both are faithfully flat.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/torsionfree-frobenius-equivalence`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-torsionfree-frobenius-equivalence); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-frobenius-dictionary`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-delta-frobenius-dictionary); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/associated-frobenius`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-associated-frobenius); [`mathlib:MvPolynomial`](#mathlib-mvpolynomial); [`mathlib:MvPolynomial.X`](#mathlib-mvpolynomial-x); [`mathlib:Module.FaithfullyFlat`](#mathlib-module-faithfullyflat).

**Consumers.** BS22 Lemma 2.15, proof: a δ-ring is a quotient of a free δ-ring, which is p-torsion-free; this reduces localization to the torsion-free case. BS22 Corollary 2.12 and Construction 4.17: faithful flatness of φ gives fpqc-local surjectivity of Frobenius; free δ-A-algebras surjecting onto R are the weakly initial objects of the prismatic site (PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/cech-alexander-complex). BS22 Lemma 2.36, Corollary 2.39, Proposition 3.13: the pushouts defining A{φ(f)/p} and prismatic envelopes are taken along maps out of free δ-rings.

**Planning API.**

- `TauCeti.Delta.Free` (data): The carrier Z[x_{s,n}] of the free δ-ring on S, a polynomial ring on S × N.
- `TauCeti.Delta.freeDelta` (structure): The δ-structure on Free S.
- `TauCeti.Delta.freeDelta_X` (simp): δ(x_{s,n}) = x_{s,n+1}.
- `TauCeti.Delta.Free.lift` (universal-property): For a δ-ring R and f : S → R, the ring map Free S → R with x_{s,n} ↦ δ^n(f s).
- `TauCeti.Delta.Free.lift_isDeltaHom` (universal-property): lift f commutes with δ, and it is the unique δ-map sending x_{s,0} to f s.
- `TauCeti.Delta.Free.frobenius_faithfullyFlat` (other): Free S is faithfully flat over itself along its Frobenius.

**Unit tests.**

- `free_delta_frobenius_X` (computation): φ(x_{s,0}) = x_{s,0}^p + p·x_{s,1} in Free S.
- `free_delta_lift_int_two` (computation): For p = 2 the δ-map Free(point) → Z with x_0 ↦ 2 sends x_1 to −1.
- `free_delta_empty` (degenerate): The free δ-ring on the empty set is Z with its canonical δ-structure: the structure map Z → Free(∅) is bijective.
- `free_delta_not_free_ring` (non-example): The ring map Z[x] → Free(point), x ↦ x_0, is not surjective: x_1 = δ(x_0) is not in its image, so the free δ-ring is strictly bigger than the free ring.

**Acceptance.** For S a point and p = 2: δ(x_0) = x_1 and δ(x_0^2) = 2 x_0^2 x_1 + 2 x_1^2, computed from the product rule. The universal map to (Z, canonical δ) sending x_0 to 2 for p = 2 sends x_1 to δ(2) = −1.

**Sources.** [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Lemma 2.11 (Free δ-rings) and its proof; Corollary 2.12. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed pages 15, 16. The node states the lemma for an arbitrary set of generators and over Z; the source proves one generator over Z_(p) by the same argument..

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-0-witt2-derived-pullback-square"></a>

### The pullback square for W_2 of a simplicial commutative ring

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/witt2-derived-pullback-square` · lemma. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Delta` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/Delta/WittTwoPullback`.

(1) For a p-torsion-free ring R the square of rings formed by the restriction W_2(R) → R, (x, y) ↦ x, the Witt vector Frobenius F : W_2(R) → R, (x, y) ↦ x^p + p·y, the projection R → R/p and the composite R → R/p → R/p of the projection with the Frobenius of R/p is a pullback square: W_2(R) ≅ {(a, b) ∈ R × R : b ≡ a^p modulo p}. (2) For every simplicial commutative ring B there is a pullback square of simplicial commutative rings, functorial in B, with the same two maps out of W_2(B) (W_2 applied levelwise) and with R/p replaced by B ⊗^L_Z F_p. In particular, for a cosimplicial simplicial ring B^• with discrete colim lim, colim_{Δ^op} lim_Δ W_2(B^•) is W_2 of colim_{Δ^op} lim_Δ B^•.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** p is prime. In (1) R is p-torsion-free; in (2) B is any simplicial commutative ring (an animated ring, EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E5:animation). W_2 is the ring of length-two p-typical Witt vectors with the addition and multiplication of PR.0/witt2-add-coordinate and PR.0/witt2-mul-coordinate. Only the square is planned here. The reformulation of δ-structures as derived Frobenius lifts (the rest of BS22 Remark 2.5) is not: no target needs it.

**Construction or proof.**

1. (1) The map W_2(R) → R × R, (x, y) ↦ (x, x^p + p·y), is a ring homomorphism by the coordinate formulas (PR.0/witt2-add-coordinate, PR.0/witt2-mul-coordinate); it is injective because p is a nonzerodivisor of R, and its image is the set of pairs (a, b) with b ≡ a^p modulo p.
2. (2) Both W_2 (whose underlying set-valued functor is R ↦ R × R) and R ↦ R ×_{R/p} R, restricted to polynomial rings over Z, extend to sifted-colimit-preserving functors on animated rings; a finitely generated polynomial ring is p-torsion-free, so (1) identifies the two functors there, and the identification extends (EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E5:animation/universal-property-of-animation). The extension of R ↦ R/p is B ↦ B ⊗^L_Z F_p (BS22 Remark 2.5: "Passing to simplicial resolutions").
3. The last sentence: regard the square as a pullback square of E_∞-rings; on underlying spectra a pullback square is preserved by limits and by colimits, and the totalisation and the realisation are computed levelwise in the three other corners. Discreteness of colim lim B^• is what identifies the result with W_2 of a ring.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/witt2-add-coordinate`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-witt2-add-coordinate); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/witt2-mul-coordinate`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-witt2-mul-coordinate); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-witt-section-equivalence`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-delta-witt-section-equivalence); `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E5:animation/animated-commutative-rings`; `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E5:animation/universal-property-of-animation`; [`mathlib:TruncatedWittVector`](#mathlib-truncatedwittvector).

**Acceptance.** R = Z: W_2(Z) ≅ {(a, b) ∈ Z × Z : b ≡ a^p mod p}; the pair (p, 0) is the image of the Witt vector (p, −p^{p−1}), and (1, 0) is not in the image. R = F_p (not p-torsion-free): the underived square fails, W_2(F_p) = Z/p² is not F_p ×_{F_p} F_p = F_p; the derived square holds with F_p ⊗^L_Z F_p in the corner.

**Sources.** [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Remark 2.5 (the two squares) and the proof of Lemma 7.7 (1). Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed pages 14, 57. The node states the two squares of the remark; the proof of Lemma 7.7 (1) uses the second..

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-0-integer-cast-delta"></a>

### Delta on integer scalars

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/integer-cast-delta` · lemma. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Delta` in `TauCeti/RingTheory/Delta/Basic`.

For every delta structure on R and integer a, delta(a*1_R) is the cast of the integer (a-a^p)/p. Consequently a nonzero ring of characteristic p has no delta structure.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** p is prime. Do not assume p-torsionfreeness of R.

**Construction or proof.**

1. In Z, verify D(n+1)=D(n)+C_p(n,1) by multiplying by p and cancelling in Z.
2. The addition axiom gives the same recurrence after casting to R. Start at zero, induct upwards for nonnegative integers and run the recurrence backwards for negative integers. Only additive cancellation is used in R.
3. Evaluate at a=p: if p=0 in R then 0=delta(0)=1-p^(p-1)=1 because p>=2.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/integer-delta`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-integer-delta); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-frobenius-dictionary`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-delta-frobenius-dictionary); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/correction-identity`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-correction-identity); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/correction-map-naturality`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-correction-map-naturality).

**Acceptance.** This does not rule out some p-torsion in a mixed-characteristic ring. Retain the dyadic negative-scalar value.

**Sources.** [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Example 2.6. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 14. Direct scalar proof for arbitrary targets, without assuming initiality of an unconstructed category..

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-0-delta-localization"></a>

### Localization of a delta structure

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-localization` · construction. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Delta` in `TauCeti/RingTheory/Delta/Localization`.

Let B be an A-algebra carrying IsLocalization S B and let i:A->B be its algebra map. Given a delta structure on A and units i(phi(s)) for every s in S, construct a delta structure localize on B compatible with i. No injectivity of i or multiplication by p is required.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** p is prime; A,B are commutative rings; S is a submonoid of A. The image-unit condition is in B; it is not an assertion that phi(S) is literally contained in S.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Compose the actual Witt section A->W_2(A) with witt2Map(i). It sends a to (i(a),i(delta(a))). For s in S its first coordinate is a unit by localization and its first ghost expression is i(phi(s)), a unit by hypothesis. The Witt unit criterion makes this section image a unit.
2. Apply the existing ring IsLocalization.lift to obtain a map s_B:B->W_2(B). The first-coordinate projection is a ring map, as verified using constantCoeff and surjective truncation.
3. The composite of that projection with s_B agrees with id_B on i(A), by lift_eq. Localization ringHom_ext proves equality on B, so s_B is a first-coordinate section.
4. Apply the existing inverse Witt-section equivalence to s_B. Its inverse identities and the coefficient formula give the resulting operation on B. Fraction representatives are not used to define it.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-witt-section-equivalence`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-delta-witt-section-equivalence); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/witt-section-coordinates`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-witt-section-coordinates); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/witt2-coefficient-map-coeff`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-witt2-coefficient-map-coeff); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/witt2-unit-criterion`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-witt2-unit-criterion); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/associated-frobenius`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-associated-frobenius); [`mathlib:IsLocalization`](#mathlib-islocalization); [`mathlib:IsLocalization.map_units`](#mathlib-islocalization-map-units); [`mathlib:IsLocalization.lift`](#mathlib-islocalization-lift); [`mathlib:IsLocalization.lift_eq`](#mathlib-islocalization-lift-eq); [`mathlib:IsLocalization.ringHom_ext`](#mathlib-islocalization-ringhom-ext); [`mathlib:WittVector.constantCoeff`](#mathlib-wittvector-constantcoeff); [`mathlib:WittVector.truncate_surjective`](#mathlib-wittvector-truncate-surjective); [`mathlib:WittVector.coeff_truncate`](#mathlib-wittvector-coeff-truncate).

**Consumers.** Bhatt-Scholze Lemma 2.15 and subsequent localized delta constructions: Supplies the ordinary localized delta structure with a precise saturation condition before completion or prism conditions are considered..

**Planning API.**

- `TauCeti.Delta.localize_algebraMap` (compatibility): delta_B(i(a))=i(delta_A(a)); supplied by localized-delta-on-base.
- `TauCeti.Delta.localize_unique` (characterisation): Every delta structure on B compatible with i equals localize; supplied by delta-localization-unique.
- `TauCeti.Delta.localize_fraction` (simp): For z=a/s, i(s)^p*i(phi(s))*delta_B(z)=i(s)^p*i(delta(a))-i(a)^p*i(delta(s)); supplied by delta-localization-fraction.

**Unit tests.**

- `delta_localization_identity` (compatibility): The identity localization recovers the original delta structure.
- `delta_localization_zero` (degenerate): A zero localization has the unique zero delta operation.
- `delta_localization_rational_value` (computation): Localizing the canonical 2-delta structure on Z in Q gives delta(1/3)=1/9.
- `delta_localization_torsion_survives` (non-example): In the localization of Z plus F_2*epsilon at powers of (3,1), the lambda=1 operation extends, epsilon remains nonzero, and delta(epsilon)=epsilon. A p-torsionfree-quotient substitute fails.

**Acceptance.** The result is a delta structure on the given B, not a new localization ring or a p-torsionfree quotient.

**Sources.** [BS22-LOCALIZATION](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Lemma 2.15 and proof. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 16. An explicit refinement of the localization argument; the sharper unit criterion and Witt proof are authored deductions, not a claim about the printed proof..

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-0-delta-localization-universal"></a>

### Universal property in delta rings

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-localization-universal` · theorem. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Delta` in `TauCeti/RingTheory/Delta/Localization`.

Let e be any compatible extension of d from A to the localization B. For a delta-compatible ring map f:A->C sending S to units, there is a unique ring map g:B->C extending f and commuting with delta. Its underlying map is the existing IsLocalization.lift.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** p is prime; C is a commutative ring with a specified delta structure; no p-torsionfreeness of C.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Take g to be the existing ring localization lift; lift_eq gives its base values.
2. Compare the maps witt2Map(g) composed with the Witt section of e, and the Witt section of C composed with g. On i(a), their two coordinates agree by the compatibility of e and f and the base values of g.
3. Use truncated Witt extensionality and localization ringHom_ext. Equality of second coordinates gives delta compatibility on all B. Any other candidate agrees with g on i(A), hence equals it as a ring map.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/witt2-coefficient-map-coeff`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-witt2-coefficient-map-coeff); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/witt-section-coordinates`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-witt-section-coordinates); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-witt-section-equivalence`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-delta-witt-section-equivalence); [`mathlib:IsLocalization.lift`](#mathlib-islocalization-lift); [`mathlib:IsLocalization.lift_eq`](#mathlib-islocalization-lift-eq); [`mathlib:IsLocalization.ringHom_ext`](#mathlib-islocalization-ringhom-ext); [`mathlib:TruncatedWittVector.ext`](#mathlib-truncatedwittvector-ext).

**Acceptance.** Identity and composite maps are compatible by the unique extension property. This proof works even when different delta structures can have the same Frobenius.

**Sources.** [BS22-LOCALIZATION](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Lemma 2.15 and proof. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 16. An explicit refinement of the localization argument; the sharper unit criterion and Witt proof are authored deductions, not a claim about the printed proof..

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-0-delta-ring-category"></a>

### Limits, colimits and Witt vectors of δ-rings

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-ring-category` · construction. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Delta` in `TauCeti/RingTheory/Delta/Witt`.

The category of δ-rings (objects: commutative rings with a δ-structure; morphisms: ring maps commuting with δ) has all limits and colimits, and the forgetful functor to commutative rings preserves both. In particular products, equalizers, tensor products A ⊗_C B along δ-maps and filtered colimits of δ-rings carry unique δ-structures making the structure maps δ-maps. The forgetful functor has a left adjoint (free δ-rings) and a right adjoint, the p-typical Witt vector functor W: for a ring R, W(R) carries the δ-structure whose Frobenius is the Witt vector Frobenius, and for a δ-ring A there is a natural δ-map w_A : A → W(A), the unit, whose first two Witt coordinates are (x, δ(x)).

**Hypotheses and conventions.** p is prime; rings are commutative. The δ-structure on W(R) for R with p-torsion is defined by cofreeness, not by dividing F(x) − x^p by p.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Limits: δ is defined coordinatewise on a product and restricts to an equalizer of δ-maps, since the axioms are equational.
2. Colimits: by delta-witt-section-equivalence a δ-structure on R is a ring section of W_2(R) → R; the natural map colim_i W_2(R_i) → W_2(colim_i R_i) turns the sections of the R_i into a section for the colimit of underlying rings (BS22 Remark 2.7).
3. Adjoints: the forgetful functor commutes with limits and colimits and the categories are presentable, giving both adjoints; the right adjoint is W by Joyal's theorem (cited in Remark 2.7). Concretely the Witt vector Frobenius F on W(R) satisfies F(x) ≡ x^p mod p and W(R) is the universal δ-ring over R; when R is p-torsion-free so is W(R) and the structure is δ(x) = (F(x) − x^p)/p.
4. The unit w_A is determined by the ghost identities φ^n(x) = δ_0(x)^{p^n} + p δ_1(x)^{p^{n−1}} + … + p^n δ_n(x) (Remark 2.13); its truncation to W_2 is the section of delta-witt-section-equivalence.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-witt-section-equivalence`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-delta-witt-section-equivalence); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/witt-section-coordinates`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-witt-section-coordinates); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-frobenius-dictionary`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-delta-frobenius-dictionary); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/free-delta-ring`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-free-delta-ring); [`mathlib:WittVector`](#mathlib-wittvector); [`mathlib:WittVector.frobenius`](#mathlib-wittvector-frobenius); [`mathlib:WittVector.ghostComponent`](#mathlib-wittvector-ghostcomponent); [`mathlib:TensorProduct`](#mathlib-tensorproduct).

**Consumers.** BS22 Corollary 2.12, Lemma 2.15, Lemma 2.36, Proposition 3.13: pushouts of δ-rings are computed on underlying rings, which is what makes A{J/I} computable. BS22 Remark 2.22, p.19: The composite can∘w_A∘φ_A:A→W(A/d) carries d to p times a unit; the Frobenius at the start is essential.. PrismaticCohomology:PR.5/cartier-witt-divisor: Cartier–Witt divisors live on W(R) with its δ-structure.

**Planning API.**

- `TauCeti.Prismatic.IsDeltaHom` (characterisation): For δ-structures d on A and e on B, a ring map f : A → B is a map of δ-rings when f(d(x)) = e(f(x)) for all x; the identity is one, composites of such maps are such maps, and such a map commutes with the associated Frobenius endomorphisms.
- `TauCeti.Delta.Structure.prod` (constructor): The coordinatewise δ-structure on A × B.
- `TauCeti.Delta.Structure.tensorProduct` (constructor): For δ-maps C → A and C → B, the unique δ-structure on A ⊗_C B for which both inclusions are δ-maps.
- `TauCeti.Delta.witt` (structure): The δ-structure on W(R) whose Frobenius is the Witt vector Frobenius.
- `TauCeti.Delta.witt_frobenius` (compatibility): The Frobenius of the δ-structure on W(R) equals WittVector.frobenius.
- `TauCeti.Delta.wittUnit` (universal-property): For a δ-ring A, the δ-map w_A : A → W(A).
- `TauCeti.Delta.wittUnit_coeff_zero` (simp): The 0-th Witt coordinate of w_A(x) is x.
- `TauCeti.Delta.wittUnit_coeff_one` (simp): The first Witt coordinate of w_A(x) is δ(x).
- `TauCeti.Delta.wittUnit_ghost` (characterisation): The n-th ghost component of w_A(x) is φ^n(x).
- `TauCeti.Delta.wittUnit_isDeltaHom` (compatibility): The unit w_A:A→W(A) commutes with δ, including when A has p-torsion.
- `TauCeti.Delta.wittLift` (universal-property): For a δ-ring A and a ring map f:A→R, W(f)∘w_A is the unique δ-map A→W(R) whose zeroth Witt coordinate is f. This natural bijection Hom_δ(A,W(R)) ≃ Hom_Ring(A,R) is the right-adjoint universal property.

**Unit tests.**

- `witt_unit_int_ghost` (computation): For A = Z with its canonical δ-structure, every ghost component of w_Z(n) equals n.
- `delta_prod_fst` (compatibility): The first projection A × B → A commutes with δ for the product structure.
- `witt_delta_torsionfree` (compatibility): On W(Z) the δ-structure satisfies p·δ(x) = F(x) − x^p.
- `witt_unit_not_teichmuller` (non-example): For A = Z and p = 2, w_Z(2) is not the Teichmüller representative [2]: its first Witt coordinate is δ(2) = −1, not 0.

**Acceptance.** For A = Z with its canonical δ-structure, w_Z : Z → W(Z) has ghost components (n, n, n, …). The pushout of Z{t} → Z{s} (t ↦ φ(s)) and Z{t} → A (t ↦ x) is A ⊗_{Z{t}} Z{s} as a ring.

**Sources.** [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Remark 2.7 (Limits and colimits of δ-rings, and Witt vectors); Remark 2.13.
