<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-0-distinguished-element"></a>

### Distinguished elements

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/distinguished-element` · definition. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/Prism`.

An element d of a δ-ring A is distinguished if δ(d) is a unit of A. Every map of δ-rings preserves distinguished elements. Examples: p ∈ Z_p (δ(p) = 1 − p^{p−1}); [p]_q = (q^p − 1)/(q − 1) ∈ Z_p[[q−1]] with φ(q) = q^p; any generator ξ of the kernel of θ : A_inf(O_C) → O_C; any generator of the kernel of W[[u]] → O_K, u ↦ π, with φ(u) = u^p.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** A is a δ-ring for the prime p.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Definition. Preservation under δ-maps: f(δ(d)) = δ(f(d)) and ring maps preserve units.
2. δ(p) = (p − p^p)/p = 1 − p^{p−1} is a unit of Z_(p). For [p]_q: δ([p]_q) ≡ δ(p) modulo (q − 1), and (q − 1)-adic completeness lifts units. For ξ and for the Breuil–Kisin generator: specialise along the δ-maps A_inf → W(k) and W[[u]] → W, u ↦ 0, under which the element maps to p times a unit (BS22 Example 2.20).

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-frobenius-dictionary`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-delta-frobenius-dictionary); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/integer-delta`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-integer-delta).

**Consumers.** BS22 Lemma 2.25 and Lemma 3.1: a locally principal ideal I with p, I in the radical satisfies p ∈ I + φ(I)A exactly when it is locally generated by a distinguished element. BS22 Definition 3.2 and Lemma 3.8: the ideal of an orientable prism is generated by a distinguished nonzerodivisor. PrismaticCohomology:PR.5/cartier-witt-divisor: the condition on δ of a generator is the Cartier–Witt condition on W(R).

**Planning API.**

- `TauCeti.Prismatic.IsDistinguished` (data): The predicate: δ(d) is a unit.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.IsDistinguished.map` (functoriality): A δ-map sends distinguished elements to distinguished elements.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.isDistinguished_p_int` (example): p is distinguished in Z_(p) with its canonical δ-structure.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.IsDistinguished.p_mem_span` (relation): If d is distinguished then p ∈ (d, φ(d)): indeed p·δ(d) = φ(d) − d^p.

**Unit tests.**

- `distinguished_p_value` (computation): In Z_(p) with its canonical δ-structure, δ(p) = 1 − p^{p−1}.
- `distinguished_p_squared_fails` (non-example): p^2 is not distinguished in Z_(p).
- `distinguished_zero_ring` (degenerate): In the zero ring every element is distinguished.
- `distinguished_unit_times_p` (compatibility): For a unit u of Z_(p), u·p is distinguished (distinguished-factor-rigidity applied to Z_(p)).
- `distinguished_universal_not_p_multiple` (non-example): In the universal δ-Z_(p)-algebra with δ(d) inverted, d is distinguished but d∉pA: modulo p it remains a nonzero polynomial variable. Thus distinguished does not mean p times a unit.

**Acceptance.** δ(p) = 1 − p^{p−1} in Z_(p); for p = 2 this is −1. p^2 is not distinguished in Z_p: δ(p^2) = p − p^{2p−1} is divisible by p. In the free δ-ring on d, the generator d is not distinguished; it becomes distinguished after inverting δ(d) and its Frobenius iterates (BS22 Example 2.21).

**Sources.** [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Definition 2.19 and Example 2.20. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 18. Definition and the four examples..

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-0-rank-one-elements"></a>

### Perfect elements have rank one

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/rank-one-elements` · lemma. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Delta` in `TauCeti/RingTheory/Delta/Perfect`.

Let A be a δ-ring and x ∈ A. Then δ(x^{p^n}) ∈ p^n A for all n ≥ 0. In particular, if A is p-adically separated and y ∈ A admits a p^n-th root for every n, then δ(y) = 0 (y has rank 1); in particular φ(y) = y^p (the converse needs A p-torsion-free).

**Hypotheses and conventions.** A is a δ-ring; for the second statement A is p-adically separated.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Reduce to the universal case x = x_0 in the free δ-ring (free-delta-ring), which is p-torsion-free. There δ(x^{p^n}) ∈ p^n A is equivalent to φ(x^{p^n}) ≡ x^{p^{n+1}} modulo p^{n+1}. For n = 0 this is the definition of φ; inductively, a ≡ b modulo p^k implies a^p ≡ b^p modulo p^{k+1} by the binomial theorem, applied to φ(x) ≡ x^p modulo p (BS22 proof of Lemma 2.32).
2. If y = z_n^{p^n} for every n then δ(y) ∈ ∩_n p^n A = 0. The separatedness hypothesis is needed: on Q[x^{1/p^∞}] the identity is a Frobenius lift and δ(x) = (x − x^p)/p ≠ 0.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-frobenius-dictionary`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-delta-frobenius-dictionary); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/free-delta-ring`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-free-delta-ring).

**Acceptance.** In W(R) for R perfect, the Teichmüller representatives [a] have rank 1: φ([a]) = [a]^p. q ∈ Z_p[[q − 1]] with δ(q) = 0 has rank 1 without having p-power roots: the converse of the lemma fails.

**Sources.** [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Lemma 2.32 (Perfect elements have rank 1) with proof. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 21. Statement and proof..

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-shifted-quotient-transition` · lemma. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Delta` in `TauCeti/RingTheory/Delta/AdicCompletion`.

For m<=n, factorPow(I,m<=n) composed with q_n equals q_m composed with factorPow(I,m+1<=n+1), as functions.

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-0-delta-ideal-closure"></a>

### Delta-stabilization of an ideal

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-ideal-closure` · definition. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Delta` in `TauCeti/RingTheory/Delta/Ideal`.

For an ideal I of A, define its delta-stabilization C_d(I) to be the ordinary ideal generated by all delta^n(a), for n a nonnegative integer and a in I. The exponent means iteration of delta, with delta^0 the identity; it is not a ring power or a Witt-coordinate operation.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** p is prime; A is a commutative ring with the specified delta structure d. No p-torsionfreeness, finite generation or p-locality is assumed.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Use the existing ideal span of the set of all iterated delta images. The index n=0 includes the original ideal.
2. Stability and the least-stable-ideal characterization are separate lemma nodes. Idempotence and monotonicity follow from those lemmas, giving the usual closure-operator laws without introducing another ideal type.
3. For the prime-ideal acceptance test, use integer-cast-delta: delta(p)=1-p^(p-1). The zeroth and first iterates place p and delta(p) in the closure; p is at least two, so their ideal combination is 1.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-frobenius-dictionary`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-delta-frobenius-dictionary); [`mathlib:Ideal.span`](#mathlib-ideal-span); [`mathlib:Function.iterate_zero_apply`](#mathlib-function-iterate-zero-apply); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/integer-cast-delta`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-integer-cast-delta).

**Consumers.** Bhatt–Scholze Example 2.10 and Notation 2.8; PrismaticCohomology:PR.0: Supplies the concrete universal quotient that kills prescribed relations and all their delta iterates. It is an algebraic ingredient for delta-algebra presentations; no derived or prism-envelope universal property is asserted..

**Planning API.**

- `TauCeti.Delta.idealClosure_eq_span` (characterisation): C_d(I) is exactly the ideal span of the set of all delta^n(a) with n nonnegative and a in I.
- `TauCeti.Delta.le_idealClosure` (constructor): I is contained in C_d(I), by the zeroth iterate.
- `TauCeti.Delta.idealClosure_stable` (structure): For x in C_d(I), delta(x) is in C_d(I); the separate stability lemma supplies this API.
- `TauCeti.Delta.idealClosure_le` (universal-property): For a delta-stable ideal J, C_d(I) is contained in J if and only if I is contained in J; the separate minimality lemma supplies this API.
- `TauCeti.Delta.idealClosure_idem` (simp): C_d(C_d(I))=C_d(I).
- `TauCeti.Delta.idealClosure_mono` (functoriality): If I is contained in J, then C_d(I) is contained in C_d(J).

**Unit tests.**

- `ideal_closure_zero` (degenerate): The delta-stabilization of the zero ideal is the zero ideal.
- `ideal_closure_stable_fixed` (characterisation): If I is already delta-stable, then C_d(I)=I.
- `ideal_closure_prime_is_top` (computation): In every delta ring A, C_d((p)) is the unit ideal: both p and delta(p)=1-p^(p-1) belong to it, so 1 does too.
- `ideal_closure_not_ordinary_span` (non-example): For the canonical 2-delta structure on the integers, C_d((2)) differs from the ordinary ideal (2), since delta(2)=-1.

**Acceptance.** Check the zero ideal and the ideal generated by p; delta-stabilization of the latter is the unit ideal.

**Sources.** [BS22-DELTA-QUOTIENT](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Section 2 opening convention and Definition 2.1; Lemma 2.9 and Example 2.10. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed pages 13, 15. Declaration-sized refinement of the source universal delta quotient. The source uses p-local rings; the displayed proof uses only the integral delta identities and establishes this explicitly broader elementary statement..

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-0-distinguished-factor-rigidity"></a>

### Factors of distinguished elements

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/distinguished-factor-rigidity` · lemma. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/Prism`.

Let A be a δ-ring. (1) If d ∈ A is distinguished, u ∈ A is a unit and d, p ∈ rad(A), then u·d is distinguished. (2) If d = f·h is distinguished with f, p ∈ rad(A), then f is distinguished and h is a unit.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** A is a δ-ring; rad(A) is the Jacobson radical. For (1): d, p ∈ rad(A). For (2): f, p ∈ rad(A).

**Construction or proof.**

1. (1) δ(u d) = u^p δ(d) + d^p δ(u) + p δ(u) δ(d); the first term is a unit and the other two lie in rad(A).
2. (2) δ(f h) = f^p δ(h) + h^p δ(f) + p δ(f) δ(h) is a unit and the first and third terms lie in rad(A), so h^p δ(f) is a unit; hence h and δ(f) are units.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-frobenius-dictionary`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-delta-frobenius-dictionary); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/distinguished-element`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-distinguished-element); [`mathlib:Ideal.jacobson`](#mathlib-ideal-jacobson); [`mathlib:Ideal.mem_jacobson_bot`](#mathlib-ideal-mem-jacobson-bot).

**Acceptance.** In Z_(p): p = p·1 and (−p) = (−1)·p are distinguished. The hypothesis f ∈ rad(A) in (2) is needed: in Z_(p), p = 1·p with f = 1 ∉ rad; f is not distinguished (δ(1) = 0) and h = p is not a unit.

**Sources.** [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Lemmas 2.23 and 2.24 with proofs. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 19. Statement and proof as in the source; the integrated decomposition id is kept..

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-0-perfect-delta-rings"></a>

### Perfect δ-rings and Witt vectors of perfect rings

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/perfect-delta-rings` · theorem. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Delta` in `TauCeti/RingTheory/Delta/Perfect`.

A δ-ring A is perfect if φ is an isomorphism. The following categories are equivalent: (1) perfect p-complete δ-rings; (2) p-adically complete, p-torsion-free rings A with A/p perfect; (3) perfect F_p-algebras. The functor (1) → (2) forgets δ; in particular every ring map between perfect p-complete δ-rings is a δ-map. The functors between (2) and (3) are A ↦ A/p and R ↦ W(R); in particular W(R) has exactly one δ-structure for R perfect of characteristic p. The inclusion of perfect δ-rings into δ-rings has the left adjoint A ↦ colim_φ A and the right adjoint A ↦ lim_φ A.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** p is prime. "p-complete" in (1) and (2) is classical p-adic completeness; for perfect δ-rings it agrees with derived p-completeness because they are p-torsion-free.

**Construction or proof.**

1. A perfect δ-ring is p-torsion-free by p-torsion-freeness-criteria, and φ reduces to the Frobenius of A/p, which is therefore bijective; this gives (1) → (2), fully faithful by torsionfree-frobenius-equivalence once ring maps are shown to commute with the unique Frobenius lifts.
2. (2) ≃ (3): for R perfect, W(R) is p-torsion-free and p-adically complete with W(R)/p = R (Mathlib: WittVector.isAdicCompleteIdealSpanP and the p-torsion-freeness in the same file); conversely a p-complete p-torsion-free A with A/p perfect is W(A/p) by the uniqueness of deformations of perfect F_p-algebras (vanishing cotangent complex, BS22 proof of Corollary 2.31).
3. On W(R) the Witt vector Frobenius is bijective for R perfect (WittVector.frobenius_bijective) and is the unique lift of Frobenius, giving (2) → (1).
4. The adjoints: colim_φ A and lim_φ A are computed on underlying rings by delta-ring-category and φ becomes bijective on them (Remark 2.27).

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/p-torsion-freeness-criteria`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-p-torsion-freeness-criteria); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/torsionfree-frobenius-equivalence`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-torsionfree-frobenius-equivalence); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-ring-category`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-delta-ring-category); [`mathlib:PerfectRing`](#mathlib-perfectring); [`mathlib:WittVector.frobenius_bijective`](#mathlib-wittvector-frobenius-bijective); [`mathlib:WittVector.isAdicCompleteIdealSpanP`](#mathlib-wittvector-isadiccompleteidealspanp); [`mathlib:WittVector`](#mathlib-wittvector); `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.0`.

**Acceptance.** W(F_p) = Z_p with φ = id is perfect; Z_p[x] with φ(x) = x^p is not (x is not in the image of φ). For R = F_p[x^{1/p^∞}], W(R) is the p-completion of Z_p[x^{1/p^∞}] with φ(x^{1/p^n}) = x^{1/p^{n−1}}.

**Sources.** [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Definition 2.26, Remark 2.27, Corollary 2.31 with proof. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 20. Definition, the two adjoints and the three-way equivalence..

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-0-prism"></a>

### Prisms

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/prism` · definition. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/Prism`.

A prism is a δ-ring A with an ideal I satisfying three conditions: I is an invertible A-module, A is derived (p,I)-complete, and p∈I+φ(I)A. A generator is not part of the structure. Derived completeness puts p and I in the Jacobson radical. The stronger statements about distinguished local generators and the principal ideal φ(I)A are proved by the subsequent nodes local-distinguished-prism-generators and prism-frobenius-ideal-principal.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** p is prime; A is a δ-ring. Derived (p, I)-completeness is the notion of DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1; it implies p, I ⊂ rad(A). A prism is not a δ-ring alone, and no generator of I is part of the data.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Definition (BS22 Definition 3.2(1)).
2. p, I ⊂ rad(A): for f in an ideal along which A is derived complete, 1 + f·a is a unit (DD.1).

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-frobenius-dictionary`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-delta-frobenius-dictionary); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/associated-frobenius`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-associated-frobenius); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/distinguished-element`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-distinguished-element); `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`; [`mathlib:Module.Invertible`](#mathlib-module-invertible); [`mathlib:Ideal.jacobson`](#mathlib-ideal-jacobson).

**Consumers.** BS22 Lemma 3.5: maps of prisms are rigid: the ideal of the target is generated by the ideal of the source. BS22 Definition 4.1 and PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/relative-prismatic-site: objects of the prismatic site are prisms over a base prism with a map to the formal scheme. BS22 Theorem 3.10: perfect prisms are equivalent to perfectoid rings. Bhatt–Lurie Definition 3.1.4 and PrismaticCohomology:PR.5/cartier-witt-divisor: a prism gives a point of the Cartier–Witt stack through A → W(A).

**Planning API.**

- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Prism` (structure): A δ-structure, an invertible ideal I, derived (p,I)-completeness, and p∈I+φ(I)A. In Lean the completeness predicate is RHom(A[1/f],A)=0 for f∈(p,I), expressed by vanishing of morphisms in every shift of Mathlib’s derived category; DD.1 supplies its equivalence with derived completion.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Prism.φ` (projection): The Frobenius lift φ(x) = x^p + p·δ(x) of the prism.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Prism.bar` (projection): The reduction A/I.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Prism.p_mem_pow` (characterisation): p ∈ I^p + φ(I)A.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Prism.ext` (extensionality): Two prisms on the same ring with equal δ and equal ideals are equal.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Prism.ofDistinguished` (constructor): If d is a distinguished nonzerodivisor in a δ-ring A and A is derived (p,d)-complete, (A,(d)) is a prism. The identity pδ(d)=φ(d)−d^p proves the prism relation; no boundedness assumption is needed.

**Unit tests.**

- `prism_ideal_ne_bot` (characterisation): If A is nonzero then the ideal of a prism on A is nonzero.
- `prism_p_squared_fails` (non-example): There is no prism structure on the ring Z_p with ideal (p^2).
- `prism_zero_ring` (degenerate): On the zero ring there is exactly one prism.
- `prism_ideal_p_implies_torsionfree` (characterisation): If the ideal of a prism is (p) then p is a nonzerodivisor of A.

**Acceptance.** (Z_p, (p)), (Z_p[[q−1]], ([p]_q)), (A_inf, ker θ) and (W(k)[[u]], (E(u))) are prisms. (Z_p, (p^2)) is not a prism: p ∉ (p^2) + φ(p^2)Z_p. (Z_p[[q−1]], (q−1)) is not a prism: p ∉ (q−1, q^p−1). (Z, (p)) is not a prism: Z is not derived p-complete.

**Sources.** [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Definition 3.2 (1); Definition 1.1. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed pages 2, 28. Definition as printed, with the Cartier divisor condition spelled out as invertibility of I..

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-0-frobenius-fpqc-local-surjectivity"></a>

### Fpqc local surjectivity of Frobenius

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/frobenius-fpqc-local-surjectivity` · lemma. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/PR0`.

For a δ-ring A and x∈A there is a faithfully flat δ-map A→B and y∈B with φ_B(y)=x. The ring B is the pushout of Z{t}→A, t↦x, and Z{t}→Z{s}, t↦φ(s).

**Hypotheses and conventions.** p is prime; no p-torsion-freeness or completion of A is assumed.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Use the free δ-ring universal property to define both maps.
2. Compute the pushout on underlying rings using delta-ring-category.
3. The second map is faithfully flat: it is the Frobenius of the free one-generator δ-ring followed by a renaming of generators. Faithful flatness survives base change. The image of s gives y.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/free-delta-ring`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-free-delta-ring); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-ring-category`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-delta-ring-category); [`mathlib:RingHom.FaithfullyFlat`](#mathlib-ringhom-faithfullyflat).

**Acceptance.** For x=p in Z_(p), the construction adjoins a Frobenius preimage without requiring one in Z_(p). This is a local surjectivity assertion, not surjectivity of φ on every δ-ring.

**Sources.** [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Corollary 2.12, §2. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 16. The pushout proof uses the faithful flatness of free Frobenius..

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-0-joyal-delta-operations"></a>

### Joyal operations and Witt-coordinate identities

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/joyal-delta-operations` · definition. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/PR0`.

For a δ-ring A, define δ_n(x) as the n-th Witt coordinate of the canonical δ-map w_A:A→W(A). Then δ_0(x)=x, δ_1(x)=δ(x), and φ^n(x)=∑_(i=0)^n p^iδ_i(x)^(p^(n−i)). In the free δ-ring δ_n(x) equals δ^n(x) plus a polynomial in the previous iterates. Thus the free δ-ring is also the polynomial ring on the δ_n(x).

**Hypotheses and conventions.** The cofree Witt δ-ring and its canonical unit are those of delta-ring-category; its unresolved proof is inherited explicitly. The identity is polynomial and therefore valid with p-torsion; division by p^n is used only in the universal torsion-free ring.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Take the coordinates of w_A and compute its n-th ghost component. Since w_A is a δ-map, that component is φ^n(x).
2. In the universal torsion-free free δ-ring, recursively solve the ghost identities to obtain δ_n=δ^n plus lower iterates. The leading coefficient is one.
3. Evaluate the resulting integral universal polynomials in any δ-ring; triangularity gives the alternative algebraically independent generators.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-ring-category`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-delta-ring-category); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/free-delta-ring`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-free-delta-ring).

**Consumers.** PR.6/ainf-omega-comparison-map: Controls higher δ operations of the envelope generators through Witt coordinates..

**Planning API.**

- `TauCeti.Delta.joyalDelta` (constructor): Define δ_n(x)=(w_A(x))_n, with δ_0=id and δ_1=δ.
- `TauCeti.Delta.joyalDelta_ghost` (relation): φ^n(x)=∑_(i=0)^n p^iδ_i(x)^(p^(n−i)), naturally under δ-ring maps.
- `TauCeti.Delta.joyalDelta_free_generators` (characterisation): The δ_n(x) freely generate the underlying polynomial algebra of the free δ-ring; the change from iterated δ is integral and triangular.

**Unit tests.**

- `pr0_joyal_zero` (degenerate): δ_0(0)=0 and δ_1(0)=0.
- `pr0_joyal_first` (computation): δ_0(x)=x and δ_1(x)=δ(x).
- `pr0_joyal_second_not_iterate` (non-example): At p=2 in Z_(2), δ(2)=−1, δ²(2)=−1, whereas δ_2(2)=−4 from 2=2⁴+2(−1)²+4δ_2(2). Higher Witt coordinates are not iterated δ.

**Acceptance.** The n=0 and n=1 identities recover x and δ(x). At p=2,n=2, φ²(x)=x⁴+2δ(x)²+4δ_2(x); δ_2 need not equal δ∘δ.

**Sources.** [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Remarks 2.13–2.14, §2.1. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 16. Witt coordinates supply the higher operations and the triangular change of generators..

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-0-delta-localization-unique"></a>

### Uniqueness of localized delta data

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-localization-unique` · lemma. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Delta` in `TauCeti/RingTheory/Delta/Localization`.

Under the localization construction hypotheses, every delta structure e on B compatible with i:A->B equals localize. In particular the construction is independent of proofs of the image-unit condition.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** B carries the actual IsLocalization S B instance. Compatibility means equality of delta operations on the image of A, not merely compatibility of Frobenius.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Take the Witt sections of e and localize. Their first coordinates on i(a) coincide, and their second coordinates coincide by compatibility and localized-delta-on-base.
2. Truncated Witt extensionality gives equality of the two sections after precomposition with i. Localization ringHom_ext gives equality on all B; injectivity of the Witt-section equivalence gives equality of structures.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/localized-delta-on-base`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-localized-delta-on-base); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/witt-section-coordinates`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-witt-section-coordinates); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-witt-section-equivalence`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-delta-witt-section-equivalence); [`mathlib:TruncatedWittVector.ext`](#mathlib-truncatedwittvector-ext); [`mathlib:IsLocalization.ringHom_ext`](#mathlib-islocalization-ringhom-ext).

**Acceptance.** Coincidence of associated Frobenius alone is not used; it would be insufficient on p-torsion.

**Sources.** [BS22-LOCALIZATION](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Lemma 2.15 and proof. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 16. An explicit refinement of the localization argument; the sharper unit criterion and Witt proof are authored deductions, not a claim about the printed proof..

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-0-delta-localization-fraction"></a>

### Delta of a fraction

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-localization-fraction` · lemma. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Delta` in `TauCeti/RingTheory/Delta/Localization`.

For z=mk'(B,a,s), the constructed delta satisfies i(s)^p*i(phi(s))*delta_B(z)=i(s)^p*i(delta(a))-i(a)^p*i(delta(s)). The coefficient of delta_B(z) is a unit, so this determines the value without dividing by p.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** The data and unit condition are those of delta-localization; a is in A and s is in S.

**Construction or proof.**

1. The existing mk'_spec' gives i(s)*z=i(a). Apply the product axiom and localized-delta-on-base to obtain i(delta(a))=i(phi(s))*delta_B(z)+z^p*i(delta(s)).
2. Multiply by i(s)^p and use (i(s)*z)^p=i(a)^p. The image-unit condition and map_units show the coefficient is a unit. This calculation also proves independence of the chosen expression for z.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/localized-delta-on-base`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-localized-delta-on-base); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-frobenius-dictionary`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-delta-frobenius-dictionary); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/associated-frobenius`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-associated-frobenius); [`mathlib:IsLocalization.mk'`](#mathlib-islocalization-mk-); [`mathlib:IsLocalization.mk'_spec'`](#mathlib-islocalization-mk--spec-); [`mathlib:IsLocalization.map_units`](#mathlib-islocalization-map-units).

**Acceptance.** For the canonical integer structure at p=2, delta(1/3)=1/9. For phi(X)=X^p+p in the rational function field, delta(X^-1)=-1/(X^p*(X^p+p)); replacing the second denominator by X^p is false.

**Sources.** [BS22-LOCALIZATION](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Lemma 2.15 and proof. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 16. An explicit refinement of the localization argument; the sharper unit criterion and Witt proof are authored deductions, not a claim about the printed proof..

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-0-delta-classical-completion"></a>

### Canonical delta structure on the inverse-limit completion

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-classical-completion` · construction. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Delta` in `TauCeti/RingTheory/Delta/AdicCompletion`.

Let I contain p. On the existing ring B=AdicCompletion I A construct a delta structure D whose normalized nth coordinate is q_n applied to the (n+1)st coordinate of the input. The construction works without finite generation. Calling B complete for its extended-ideal topology, and uniqueness among all compatible delta structures, use the separate finite-generation theorem.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** p is prime; A is a commutative delta ring; I is an ideal with p in I. Use the actual inverse-limit carrier, coordinate maps and ring structure from the pinned library; do not introduce a replacement completed ring.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Write rho_n for the existing normalized evaluation B->A/I^n. Choose a_n in A lifting rho_(n+1)(x). Coherence of x gives a_m-a_n in I^(m+1) for m<=n, so the sequence delta(a_n) is I-adic Cauchy by delta-adic-congruence.
2. Use the existing AdicCompletion.mk on this Cauchy sequence. Its normalized evaluation is [delta(a_n)]_n=q_n(rho_(n+1)(x)). The shifted-quotient transition theorem verifies compatibility. Independence of all choices follows from the displayed coordinate formula and ext_evalₐ.
3. To verify zero, one, addition and multiplication, evaluate at level n and choose representatives of x and y at the SAME level n+1. The representatives a+b and ab represent x+y and xy there. The given delta axioms in A and shiftedQuotient_mk give the desired equations modulo I^n; evaluation is a ring map and carries the fixed correction polynomial to its evaluation. ext_evalₐ gives the axioms in B.
4. No linear or ring inverse-limit lifting theorem is applied to delta: it is nonlinear. Only the existing Cauchy-sequence constructor and coordinatewise verification are used.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-shifted-quotient-mk`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-delta-shifted-quotient-mk); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-shifted-quotient-transition`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-delta-shifted-quotient-transition); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-adic-congruence`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-delta-adic-congruence); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/correction-map-naturality`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-correction-map-naturality); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-frobenius-dictionary`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-delta-frobenius-dictionary); [`mathlib:AdicCompletion`](#mathlib-adiccompletion); [`mathlib:AdicCompletion.AdicCauchySequence`](#mathlib-adiccompletion-adiccauchysequence); [`mathlib:AdicCompletion.mk`](#mathlib-adiccompletion-mk); [`mathlib:AdicCompletion.evalₐ`](#mathlib-adiccompletion-eval-); [`mathlib:AdicCompletion.evalₐ_mk`](#mathlib-adiccompletion-eval--mk); [`mathlib:AdicCompletion.ext_evalₐ`](#mathlib-adiccompletion-ext-eval-); [`mathlib:AdicCompletion.transitionMap_comp_eval_apply`](#mathlib-adiccompletion-transitionmap-comp-eval-apply).

**Consumers.** Bhatt-Scholze Lemma 2.17 and completed delta/prism examples: Supplies the actual classical completed delta operation before imposing prism or derived-completion conditions..

**Planning API.**

- `TauCeti.Delta.completion_eval` (projection): rho_n(D(x))=q_n(rho_(n+1)(x)); supplied by delta-completion-coordinate.
- `TauCeti.Delta.completion_algebraMap` (compatibility): D(i(a))=i(delta(a)); supplied by delta-completion-base.
- `TauCeti.Delta.completion_congr` (relation): Equal (n+1)st input coordinates give equal nth delta coordinates; supplied by delta-completion-congruence.

**Unit tests.**

- `completion_dyadic_scalar` (computation): For A=Z and I=(2), rho_1(D(i(2))) is the nonzero class of -1 modulo 2.
- `completion_unit_ideal` (degenerate): For I=A the inverse-limit ring is zero and D sends every element to zero.
- `completion_complete_base` (compatibility): Under the existing ofAlgEquiv for a complete base, D agrees with the given delta operation.
- `completion_torsion_survives` (non-example): For A=Z plus F_2*epsilon, I=(2), and the lambda=1 delta operation, epsilon remains nonzero in the completion and D(epsilon)=epsilon.

**Acceptance.** The constructor supplies a delta operation on the inverse-limit ring even if the finite quotients do not admit delta structures. It does not assert derived completeness or that an infinitely generated ideal is an ideal of definition of the inverse-limit topology.

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-0-p-local-integer-delta"></a>

### The canonical p-local integer delta structure

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/p-local-integer-delta` · construction. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Delta` in `TauCeti/RingTheory/Delta/Localization`.

On the existing Localization.AtPrime of the prime ideal (p) in Z, construct the canonical delta structure. Its Frobenius is the identity and p*delta(x)=x-x^p; the equation specifies division by p inside this domain, not a field division operation.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** p is prime. Use the prime-ideal instance from Nat.prime_iff_prime_int and Ideal.isPrime_span_singleton_of_prime.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Take S to be the complement of (p) and use Mathlib Localization.AtPrime (p). Integer Frobenius is the identity, so every phi(s) has the same unit image as s. Apply localize to intDelta.
2. The base formula gives the cast API. The associated Frobenius agrees with the identity on the image of Z, using the base formula and integer Frobenius identity. IsLocalization.ringHom_ext proves equality on the localization.
3. Expand the associated Frobenius formula to obtain p*delta(x)=x-x^p. This is the source operation and it lies in the existing ring because it was constructed by localization, with no integrality assumption hidden in a quotient notation.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/integer-frobenius-identity`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-integer-frobenius-identity); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-localization`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-delta-localization); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/localized-delta-on-base`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-localized-delta-on-base); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/associated-frobenius`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-associated-frobenius); [`mathlib:Nat.prime_iff_prime_int`](#mathlib-nat-prime-iff-prime-int); [`mathlib:Ideal.isPrime_span_singleton_of_prime`](#mathlib-ideal-isprime-span-singleton-of-prime); [`mathlib:Localization.AtPrime`](#mathlib-localization-atprime); [`mathlib:IsLocalization.AtPrime.isLocalRing`](#mathlib-islocalization-atprime-islocalring); [`mathlib:IsLocalization.map_units`](#mathlib-islocalization-map-units); [`mathlib:IsLocalization.ringHom_ext`](#mathlib-islocalization-ringhom-ext).

**Consumers.** PR.0 coefficient and localization inputs to local distinguished generators: Supplies the actual p-local delta structure or its target unit condition without p-cancellation..

**Planning API.**

- `TauCeti.Delta.intAtPrime_algebraMap` (compatibility): Delta of the image of a in Z equals the image of intDelta(a).
- `TauCeti.Delta.intAtPrime_frobenius` (compatibility): The associated ring endomorphism is the identity.
- `TauCeti.Delta.intAtPrime_spec` (characterisation): For every x, p*delta(x)=x-x^p.
- `TauCeti.Delta.intAtPrime_unique` (extensionality): Every δ-structure on Z_(p) agrees with intAtPrime; equality follows on integers and then on inverses of integers prime to p.

**Unit tests.**

- `p_local_integer_prime` (computation): Delta(p)=1-p^(p-1).
- `p_local_integer_negative_dyadic` (computation): At p=2, delta(-1)=-1.
- `p_local_integer_third` (computation): At p=2, if z is the localization fraction 1/3 then 9*delta(z)=1, hence delta(z)=1/9.
- `p_local_integer_zero` (degenerate): Delta(0)=0.

**Acceptance.** This ring is Z_(p), not the p-adic completion Z_p. No p-cancellation in a target ring is used to establish its universal property.

**Sources.** [BS22-FRESH-LOCAL](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Example 2.6; Lemma 2.15. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed pages 14, 16. Instantiates the source coefficient ring on the actual pinned localization carrier..

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-0-delta-ideal-closure-stable"></a>

### Stability of delta-stabilization

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-ideal-closure-stable` · lemma. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Delta` in `TauCeti/RingTheory/Delta/Ideal`.

For every ideal I, delta carries C_d(I) into C_d(I).

**Hypotheses and conventions.** p is prime; A is a commutative ring with the specified delta structure d. No p-torsionfreeness, finite generation or p-locality is assumed.

**Construction or proof.**

1. For a generating element delta^n(a), its delta is delta^(n+1)(a), another generator.
2. Apply delta-span-stability to these generators. Their ideal span is C_d(I) by definition; no assumption that I itself is stable is used.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-ideal-closure`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-delta-ideal-closure); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-span-stability`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-delta-span-stability); [`mathlib:Ideal.subset_span`](#mathlib-ideal-subset-span); [`mathlib:Function.iterate_succ_apply'`](#mathlib-function-iterate-succ-apply-).

**Acceptance.** At p=2 on the integers, stabilization of (2) contains -1 and hence is the stable unit ideal, not the original ideal.

**Sources.** [BS22-DELTA-QUOTIENT](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Section 2 opening convention and Definition 2.1; Lemma 2.9 and Example 2.10. The source uses p-local rings; the displayed proof uses only the integral delta identities and establishes this explicitly broader elementary statement..

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-0-delta-ideal-closure-minimal"></a>

### Minimality of delta-stabilization

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-ideal-closure-minimal` · lemma. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Delta` in `TauCeti/RingTheory/Delta/Ideal`.

For any delta-stable ideal J, C_d(I) is contained in J if and only if I is contained in J.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** p is prime; A is a commutative ring with the specified delta structure d. No p-torsionfreeness, finite generation or p-locality is assumed.

**Construction or proof.**

1. The forward direction uses the zeroth iterate in the generating set.
2. Conversely, if I is contained in J, induction on n shows delta^n(a) belongs to J for every a in I. Use stability of J in the successor step, then the universal property of ideal span.

**Acceptance.** If I is already delta-stable, use J=I to obtain C_d(I)=I; with J=C_d(I), the same criterion gives idempotence.

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-0-distinguished-in-perfect-delta-rings"></a>

### Distinguished elements of perfect δ-rings

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/distinguished-in-perfect-delta-rings` · lemma. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Delta` in `TauCeti/RingTheory/Delta/Perfect`.

Let A be a perfect p-complete δ-ring, so A = W(R) with R = A/p perfect, and let d = Σ_{i≥0} [a_i] p^i be the Teichmüller expansion of d ∈ A. Then d is distinguished if and only if a_1 is a unit of R. Moreover (Lemma 2.34) if A is a p-torsion-free, p-adically separated δ-ring with A/p reduced and d ∈ A is distinguished, then d is a nonzerodivisor and R = A/d satisfies R[p^∞] = R[p].

**Hypotheses and conventions.** First statement: A perfect and p-complete. Second statement: A p-torsion-free, p-adically separated, A/p reduced (for example A perfect and p-complete); d distinguished.

**Construction or proof.**

1. With A = W(R) by perfect-delta-rings, δ(d) = (1/p)(Σ [a_i^p] p^i − (Σ [a_i] p^i)^p), so δ(d) ≡ a_1^p modulo p; by p-completeness d is distinguished exactly when a_1 is a unit of R (BS22 proof of Lemma 2.33).
2. For regularity, a nonzero annihilator f of d can be chosen outside pA, using p-torsion-freeness and separatedness. The δ-product identity then reads f^p δ(d) + δ(f) φ(d) = 0. Because φ(f)φ(d)=0, multiplication by φ(f) removes the second summand; invertibility of δ(d) forces f^p φ(f)=0. Modulo p this becomes f^(2p)=0, contradicting reducedness of A/p and the choice of f (BS22 Lemma 2.34(1)).
3. Bounded torsion: it suffices that R[p] = R[p^2]. If p^2 f = g d then δ(d) g^p + δ(g) φ(d) ∈ pA; multiplying by φ(g) and using φ(d g) ∈ pA gives δ(d) g^p φ(g) ∈ pA, so g^{2p} ∈ pA and g ∈ pA; hence p f ∈ dA (proof of Lemma 2.34(2)).

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/perfect-delta-rings`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-perfect-delta-rings); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/rank-one-elements`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-rank-one-elements); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/distinguished-element`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-distinguished-element); [`mathlib:WittVector.teichmuller`](#mathlib-wittvector-teichmuller); [`mathlib:IsReduced`](#mathlib-isreduced); [`mathlib:nonZeroDivisors`](#mathlib-nonzerodivisors).

**Acceptance.** In W(F_p) = Z_p: d = p has a_0 = 0, a_1 = 1; d = p^2 has a_1 = 0 and is not distinguished. ξ = p − [p^♭] ∈ A_inf(O_C) has unit coefficient of p in its Teichmüller expansion and is distinguished; A_inf/ξ = O_C is p-torsion-free.

**Sources.** [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Lemma 2.33 (Distinguished elements in perfect δ-rings) and Lemma 2.34, with proofs. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 21. Both lemmas, stated together because the perfect-prism lemma uses them together..

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-0-prism-category"></a>

### Maps of prisms; perfect, bounded, orientable and crystalline prisms

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/prism-category` · definition. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/Prism`.

A map of prisms (A, I) → (B, J) is a map of δ-rings A → B carrying I into J; prisms form a full subcategory of δ-pairs. A prism (A, I) is perfect if φ is an isomorphism; bounded if A/I has bounded p^∞-torsion, that is, (A/I)[p^∞] = (A/I)[p^n] for some n; orientable if I is principal, an orientation being a choice of generator; crystalline if I = (p). A crystalline prism is bounded and orientable. A map of prisms (A, I) → (B, J) is (faithfully) flat if A → B is (p, I)-completely (faithfully) flat.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** (A, I), (B, J) prisms. (p, I)-complete (faithful) flatness is the notion of DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Definitions (BS22 Definition 3.2).
2. Crystalline ⇒ bounded and orientable: A is p-torsion-free because I = (p) is invertible, and A/p is killed by p.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/prism`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-prism); `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`; [`mathlib:Submodule.IsPrincipal`](#mathlib-submodule-isprincipal); [`mathlib:Module.FaithfullyFlat`](#mathlib-module-faithfullyflat).

**Consumers.** BS22 Lemma 3.7 and Corollary 3.12: bounded prisms with faithfully flat maps form the site on which the structure sheaves are sheaves. BS22 Theorem 1.8 and PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/relative-prismatic-site: the comparison theorems are stated over a bounded base prism. BS22 Theorem 5.2: the crystalline comparison is stated for crystalline prisms. PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/etale-comparison: the étale comparison is stated over a perfect prism.

**Planning API.**

- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Prism.Hom` (structure): A map of prisms: a ring map commuting with δ and carrying I into J.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Prism.Hom.id` (constructor): The identity map of a prism.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Prism.Hom.comp` (functoriality): Composition of maps of prisms.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Prism.IsBounded` (data): A/I has bounded p^∞-torsion.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Prism.IsPerfect` (data): φ is bijective.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Prism.IsOrientable` (data): I is principal.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Prism.IsCrystalline` (data): I = (p).
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Prism.IsCrystalline.isBounded` (relation): A crystalline prism is bounded.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Prism.IsCrystalline.isOrientable` (relation): A crystalline prism is orientable.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Prism.Hom.ext` (extensionality): Maps between fixed prisms are equal when their underlying ring homomorphisms are equal; δ-compatibility and ideal containment are propositions.

**Unit tests.**

- `prism_hom_id_toRingHom` (degenerate): The underlying ring map of the identity map of a prism is the identity.
- `prism_hom_map_phi` (compatibility): A map of prisms commutes with the Frobenius lifts.
- `prism_bounded_of_torsionfree_quotient` (characterisation): If p is a nonzerodivisor on A/I then the prism is bounded.
- `prism_perfect_frobenius_injective` (characterisation): A perfect prism has injective Frobenius; a prism with non-injective Frobenius is not perfect.

**Acceptance.** (Z_p, (p)) is perfect, bounded, oriented by p and crystalline; (Z_p[[q−1]], ([p]_q)) is bounded and orientable, not perfect, not crystalline. A δ-map is a map of prisms only if it carries I into J: the map Z_p[[q−1]] → Z_p, q ↦ 1, is a map of prisms ([p]_q) → (p), and there is no map of prisms in the other direction because p is not sent into ([p]_q) by the structure map Z_p → Z_p[[q−1]].

**Sources.** [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Definition 3.2 (2)–(3); Definition 1.4. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed pages 3, 28. Definitions as printed..

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-0-transversal-prism-regular-sequences"></a>

### Regular sequences in a transversal prism

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/transversal-prism-regular-sequences` · lemma. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/Prism`.

Let (A, I) be a prism and d ∈ I a distinguished element. If (p, d) is a regular sequence in A, then for all r, s ≥ 0 with r ≠ s the sequences (p, φ^r(d)) and (φ^r(d), φ^s(d)) are regular.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** (A, I) prism; d ∈ I distinguished; (p, d) regular (the prism is transversal: A/I is p-torsion-free). The proof uses that p lies in the Jacobson radical and that A is p-adically separated, both consequences of derived (p, I)-completeness with p-torsion-freeness.

**Construction or proof.**

1. (p, φ^r(d)): modulo p, φ^r(d) ≡ d^{p^r}, and a power of a nonzerodivisor of A/p is a nonzerodivisor.
2. (φ^r(d), φ^s(d)): replacing d by φ^{min(r,s)}(d), which is again distinguished with (p, φ^{min(r,s)}(d)) regular, one may assume min(r, s) = 0 (this reduction is the source's). For e distinguished, φ(e) = e^p + p·δ(e) gives φ^m(e) ≡ p·u_m modulo e with u_m a unit, by induction on m. So regularity of (e, φ^m(e)) is regularity of (e, p), and (e, p) is regular because (p, e) is regular and both are nonzerodivisors of A (A is p-torsion-free and p-adically separated): vanishing of the first Koszul homology is symmetric in the two elements. The same symmetry gives the other order (φ^m(e), e).
3. The source proves the statement by this reduction and by citing Lemmas 3.3 and 3.6 of Anschütz–Le Bras, The cyclotomic trace in degree 2; the argument above is the direct proof and uses only the listed prerequisites.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/prism`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-prism); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/distinguished-element`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-distinguished-element); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/associated-frobenius`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-associated-frobenius); [`mathlib:RingTheory.Sequence.IsRegular`](#mathlib-ringtheory-sequence-isregular).

**Acceptance.** q-de Rham prism: ([p]_q, [p]_{q^p}) is a regular sequence in Z_p[[q−1]]; so is (p, [p]_{q^{p^r}}). In a crystalline prism d = p and (p, d) is not regular: the hypothesis excludes it.

**Sources.** [ALB23](https://arxiv.org/abs/1907.10525v4), Lemma 2.1.7 (arXiv numbering; Lemma 2.7 in the published version) with proof. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 13. Statement as printed (routed item PAPER-ANSCHUTZ-LEBRAS-23/11)..

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-0-delta-localization-criterion"></a>

### Criterion for extension across a localization

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-localization-criterion` · theorem. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Delta` in `TauCeti/RingTheory/Delta/Localization`.

A delta structure on A extends compatibly to B=S^(-1)A if and only if each i(phi(s)) is a unit in B. When it extends it is unique. Equivalently each phi(s) divides some element of S.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** p is prime; A and B are commutative rings; IsLocalization S B specifies i.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Sufficiency is delta-localization and localized-delta-on-base; uniqueness is delta-localization-unique.
2. For necessity, a compatible extension has associated ring endomorphism phi_B. Expanding x^p+p*delta(x) gives phi_B(i(s))=i(phi_A(s)). Ring homomorphisms carry the unit i(s) to a unit.
3. The pinned algebraMap_isUnit_iff expresses the image-unit condition as the stated divisibility/saturation condition. It needs no domain hypothesis.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-localization`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-delta-localization); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/localized-delta-on-base`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-localized-delta-on-base); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-localization-unique`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-delta-localization-unique); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/associated-frobenius`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-associated-frobenius); [`mathlib:IsLocalization.map_units`](#mathlib-islocalization-map-units); [`mathlib:IsLocalization.algebraMap_isUnit_iff`](#mathlib-islocalization-algebramap-isunit-iff).

**Acceptance.** In A=Z_(p)[X] with phi(X)=X^p+p, the localization A[X^-1] has no compatible delta structure: X^p+p is not a Laurent unit. For p=2 on Z plus F_2*epsilon and s=(3,1), phi(s)=(3,0) divides s^2 but is not a power of s. Literal stability is not necessary.

**Sources.** [BS22-LOCALIZATION](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Lemma 2.15 and proof. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 16. An explicit refinement of the localization argument; the sharper unit criterion and Witt proof are authored deductions, not a claim about the printed proof..

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-0-delta-localization-jacobson"></a>

### Localization with a radical target

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-localization-jacobson` · construction. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Delta` in `TauCeti/RingTheory/Delta/Localization`.

Given a delta structure d on A and an existing localization B of A at S, construct the unique compatible delta structure on B whenever p_B lies in jacobson(0_B). No literal Frobenius stability of S and no p-torsionfreeness are imposed.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** A and B are commutative rings; B has Algebra A B and IsLocalization S B; p_B is in the Jacobson radical.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Every i(s) is a unit by IsLocalization.map_units. The Frobenius image-unit lemma makes i(phi_d(s)) a unit.
2. Supply these actual unit proofs to the existing localize construction. Its base formula and uniqueness immediately give the new API; its universal property supplies delta compatibility of all induced localization maps.
3. Equality with any instance of localize follows by uniqueness, so the convenience constructor adds no ring carrier or independent localization theory.

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-0-delta-universal-quotient"></a>

### Universal delta quotient by an ideal

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-universal-quotient` · construction. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Delta` in `TauCeti/RingTheory/Delta/Ideal`.

On the existing quotient ring Q=A/C_d(I), construct the unique delta structure for which the ordinary quotient map q:A to Q commutes with delta. This is the universal delta A-algebra annihilating I, as proved by the separate universal-property theorem.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** p is prime; A is a commutative ring with the specified delta structure d. No p-torsionfreeness, finite generation or p-locality is assumed.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Apply delta-stable-quotient to the ideal C_d(I), using delta-ideal-closure-stable. Select the unique compatible delta structure on the existing quotient carrier.
2. Its evaluation on q(a) is q(delta(a)). The map kills I since I is contained in its closure. The universal mapping property is proved separately through the existing ring quotient lift.

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-0-delta-etale-extension"></a>

### δ-structures on completely étale algebras and derived completions

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-etale-extension` · theorem. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Delta` in `TauCeti/RingTheory/Delta/Etale`.

Let A be a δ-ring and I ⊂ A a finitely generated ideal containing p. For an A-algebra B which is derived complete and completely étale for I, exactly one δ-operation on B makes the structure map A→B a δ-map. In particular the δ-structure of A extends uniquely to the derived I-completion of A, for every finitely generated ideal I containing a power of p.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** A is a δ-ring; I is finitely generated and contains p (for the last sentence: a power of p). Derived I-completeness and I-complete étaleness are the notions of DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1; the classical completion statement is delta-classical-completion, which this node does not replace.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Use delta-witt-section-equivalence: a compatible δ-structure on B is a ring map w_B : B → W_2(B) over w_A lifting the identity of B.
2. By Elkik's algebraization theorem (DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1) B is the derived I-completion of an étale A-algebra B′. By van der Kallen's theorem W_2(A) → W_2(B′) is étale; from 0 → φ_*B′ → W_2(B′) → B′ → 0 and the equality of derived I- and φ(I)-completion (p ∈ I), W_2(B) is the derived I-completion of W_2(B′).
3. Since A → B′ is étale and W_2(B) → B is a pro-infinitesimal thickening, there is a unique lift B′ → W_2(B) of B′ → B over A → W_2(B); it extends uniquely to B because W_2(B) is derived I-complete.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-witt-section-equivalence`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-delta-witt-section-equivalence); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-classical-completion`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-delta-classical-completion); `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`; [`mathlib:Algebra.Etale`](#mathlib-algebra-etale); [`mathlib:TruncatedWittVector`](#mathlib-truncatedwittvector).

**Acceptance.** For A = Z_(p) and I = (p): the derived p-completion Z_p carries the unique δ-structure with φ = id. For A = Z_p[x] with φ(x) = x^p and B the p-completion of A[1/x]: the δ-structure extends with φ(1/x) = 1/x^p.

**Sources.** [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Lemma 2.18 (Étale maps) and its proof. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 17. The node is the lemma with the consequence stated after it; the proof imports Elkik algebraization and van der Kallen's theorem..

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-0-crystalline-prism"></a>

### Crystalline prisms

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/crystalline-prism` · construction. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/Examples`.

For every p-torsion-free, p-adically complete δ-ring A, the pair (A, (p)) is a crystalline prism, and every crystalline prism is of this form. Examples: (Z_p, (p)) with φ = id; (W(k), (p)) for a perfect field (or perfect F_p-algebra) k with the Witt vector Frobenius; (Z_p⟨x⟩, (p)) with φ(x) = x^p.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** A is a δ-ring, p-torsion-free and classically p-adically complete.

**Construction or proof.**

1. (p) is invertible because p is a nonzerodivisor; A is derived p-complete because it is classically complete and p-torsion-free (DD.1); p ∈ (p).
2. Conversely if (A, (p)) is a prism then (p) invertible forces p to be a nonzerodivisor, and derived p-completeness with p-torsion-freeness gives classical completeness.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/prism`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-prism); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/prism-category`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-prism-category); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/integer-delta`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-integer-delta); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/perfect-delta-rings`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-perfect-delta-rings); `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`; [`mathlib:PadicInt`](#mathlib-padicint); [`mathlib:WittVector`](#mathlib-wittvector); [`mathlib:WittVector.isAdicCompleteIdealSpanP`](#mathlib-wittvector-isadiccompleteidealspanp).

**Consumers.** BS22 Theorem 5.2 and PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/crystalline-comparison: the base of the crystalline comparison. BS22 Construction 6.1: the universal oriented prism maps to a crystalline prism, reducing the Hodge–Tate comparison to characteristic p. BS22 Theorem 3.10 for R of characteristic p: perfect crystalline prisms (W(R), (p)) correspond to perfect F_p-algebras R.

**Planning API.**

- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Prism.crystalline` (constructor): The prism (A, (p)) of a δ-ring A in which p is a nonzerodivisor (and which is p-adically complete).
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Prism.crystalline_I` (simp): Its ideal is (p).
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Prism.crystalline_isCrystalline` (characterisation): It is crystalline.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Prism.padicInt` (example): The prism (Z_p, (p)).
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Prism.witt` (example): The prism (W(k), (p)) of a perfect ring k of characteristic p.

### Initiality of the p-local integer delta ring

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/p-local-integer-initial` · theorem. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Delta` in `TauCeti/RingTheory/Delta/Localization`.

For every commutative delta ring B in which the image of every integer not divisible by p is a unit, there exists exactly one unital ring map Z_(p)→B commuting with delta. B may have nonzero p-torsion or be the zero ring.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** p is prime; the coefficient condition is explicit: for every integer n with p not dividing n, the cast of n is a unit of B.

**Construction or proof.**

1. The integer-cast-delta lemma shows that Int.castRingHom B commutes with delta. This uses the integer recurrence, not cancellation of p in B.
2. Membership outside the principal ideal (p) is precisely nondivisibility by p. The coefficient condition therefore supplies unit images of all denominators.
3. Use the existing delta-localization-universal theorem with the actual intAtPrime operation, whose compatibility on Z is supplied by p-local-integer-delta-base.
4. Any unital ring map Z_(p)→B restricts to the integer cast. Localization ringHom_ext therefore proves uniqueness even before imposing delta compatibility.

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-0-animated-delta-rings"></a>

### Simplicial commutative δ-rings

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/animated-delta-rings` · construction. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Delta` in `TauCeti/RingTheory/Delta/Animated`.

A simplicial commutative δ-ring is a simplicial object in the category of δ-rings; the ∞-category of animated δ-rings is obtained from these by inverting weak equivalences of underlying simplicial sets, equivalently it is the animation (sifted-colimit completion) of the category of free δ-rings on finite sets. The forgetful functor to animated commutative rings preserves all limits and colimits; in particular a derived pushout of animated δ-rings is computed as the derived pushout of the underlying animated rings. Free adjunction: for an animated δ-ring A and x ∈ π_0(A), the animated δ-A-algebra A{x/p} is the derived pushout of A ← Z{t} → Z{s} (t ↦ x, t ↦ p·s); similarly A{J/I} for I = (d) and J = (d, x_1,…,x_r) is the derived pushout of A ← A{t_1,…,t_r} → A{s_1,…,s_r} (free δ-A-algebras) along t_i ↦ x_i and t_i ↦ d·s_i. For a finitely generated ideal I containing a power of p the derived I-complete animated δ-rings form a full subcategory, with derived I-completion left adjoint to the inclusion.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** p is prime. Animated commutative rings, sifted left Kan extension and derived pushouts are supplied by EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E5:animation; derived completion by DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1. The source uses this ∞-category without defining it (Corollary 2.39, Corollary 2.44, the proof of Proposition 3.13, Construction 6.1); the node supplies the definition those uses need.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Define the 1-category of simplicial δ-rings levelwise. Because the free δ-ring functor is a polynomial ring functor on underlying rings (free-delta-ring), free δ-rings on finite sets are compact projective generators and the category of δ-rings is the category of product-preserving presheaves on them; apply animation (EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E5:animation).
2. The forgetful functor is induced by the functor on compact projective generators sending Z{S} to the polynomial ring Z[S × N], a filtered colimit of finitely generated polynomial rings, so it preserves sifted colimits; with preservation of finite coproducts (delta-ring-category: coproducts of δ-rings are tensor products of underlying rings) it preserves all colimits. Limits are computed levelwise.
3. Define A{x/p} and A{J/I} by the displayed pushouts; by the previous step their underlying animated rings are the corresponding derived tensor products, which is how Lemma 2.38 enters the proof of Corollary 2.39.
4. Derived completion of an animated δ-ring along a finitely generated ideal containing p carries a unique compatible δ-structure: apply delta-etale-extension's argument levelwise in the W_2-description, since W_2 commutes with the relevant limits.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-ring-category`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-delta-ring-category); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/free-delta-ring`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-free-delta-ring); `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E5:animation/nonabelian-derived-category`; `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E5:animation/universal-property-of-animation`; `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E5:animation/animated-commutative-rings`; `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`; [`mathlib:CategoryTheory.SimplicialObject`](#mathlib-categorytheory-simplicialobject); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-etale-extension`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-delta-etale-extension).

**Consumers.** BS22 Corollary 2.39: δ-pushouts must be pushouts of simplicial commutative rings in order to apply Lemma 2.38. BS22 Proposition 3.13, proof: the prismatic envelope is first built as a derived (p,I)-complete animated δ-ring and then shown to be discrete. BS22 Construction 6.1 and PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/derived-prismatic-cohomology: the universal oriented prism maps to a crystalline one through an animated δ-ring; derived prismatic cohomology is valued in animated objects.

**Planning API.**

- `TauCeti.Delta.SimplicialDeltaRing` (structure): A simplicial commutative ring with a δ-structure in each degree, compatible with all simplicial operators.
- `TauCeti.Delta.SimplicialDeltaRing.const` (constructor): The constant simplicial δ-ring on a δ-ring.
- `TauCeti.Delta.SimplicialDeltaRing.frobenius` (data): The levelwise Frobenius φ, an endomorphism of the underlying simplicial ring.
- `TauCeti.Delta.SimplicialDeltaRing.frobenius_app` (simp): In each degree n the Frobenius is x ↦ x^p + p·δ_n(x).

**Unit tests.**

- `simplicial_delta_const_obj` (degenerate): The constant simplicial δ-ring on A has the ring A in every degree.
- `simplicial_delta_const_frobenius` (compatibility): The levelwise Frobenius of the constant simplicial δ-ring on A is the Frobenius of A in every degree.
- `simplicial_delta_face_commutes` (characterisation): Every simplicial operator of a simplicial δ-ring commutes with the levelwise Frobenius.
- `simplicial_delta_frobenius_mod_p` (characterisation): In each degree the Frobenius of a simplicial δ-ring is congruent to the p-th power map modulo p; a simplicial ring with an arbitrary levelwise endomorphism is not a simplicial δ-ring.

**Acceptance.** A discrete δ-ring, viewed as a constant simplicial δ-ring, has π_0 the original δ-ring and no higher homotopy. For A = Z_(p){x}, the animated δ-ring obtained by freely adjoining φ(x)/p is discrete (BS22 Remark 2.37); and A{x/p} is Z_(p){s} with x = p·s, a pushout along an isomorphism.

**Sources.** [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Corollary 2.39 (statement: the derived pushout square in simplicial commutative δ-rings); Remark 2.37; Corollary 2.44; proof of Proposition 3.13.
