<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-0-breuil-kisin-prism"></a>

### The Breuil–Kisin prism

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/breuil-kisin-prism` · construction. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/Examples`.

Let K be a complete discretely valued field of characteristic 0 with perfect residue field k of characteristic p, W = W(k), π a uniformizer of O_K and E(u) ∈ W[u] its Eisenstein minimal polynomial over W[1/p]. Then A = W[[u]] with the δ-structure extending the canonical one on W and satisfying φ(u) = u^p, and I = (E(u)), is a bounded, oriented, non-perfect prism with A/I ≅ O_K via u ↦ π. Every generator of the kernel of A → O_K is distinguished.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** k perfect of characteristic p; K finite totally ramified over W[1/p]; E Eisenstein of degree e = [K : W[1/p]]. The perfect residue-field hypothesis identifies the unramified coefficient ring with W(k); the source’s shorter description omits that hypothesis (register entry PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22/E8).

**Construction or proof.**

1. A is p-torsion-free and the displayed φ lifts Frobenius, so torsionfree-frobenius-equivalence gives δ. A is (p, u)-adically complete, hence (p, E)-adically complete since E ≡ u^e modulo p.
2. E is a nonzerodivisor of the domain A. Under the δ-map A → W, u ↦ 0, E maps to E(0) = p·(unit), which is distinguished in W; since units and δ are detected modulo u in the u-complete ring A, δ(E) is a unit.
3. A/E ≅ O_K is p-torsion-free, so the prism is bounded; φ is not surjective (u is not in its image).

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/prism`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-prism); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/prism-category`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-prism-category); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/torsionfree-frobenius-equivalence`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-torsionfree-frobenius-equivalence); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/distinguished-element`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-distinguished-element); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/crystalline-prism`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-crystalline-prism); [`mathlib:PowerSeries`](#mathlib-powerseries); [`mathlib:WittVector`](#mathlib-wittvector); [`mathlib:Polynomial.IsEisensteinAt`](#mathlib-polynomial-iseisensteinat).

**Consumers.** PrismaticCohomology:PR.7/breuil-kisin-evaluation: evaluating a prismatic F-crystal on this prism gives a Breuil–Kisin module. BS22 §15.2 and AInfCohomology:AI.7: Breuil–Kisin cohomology is prismatic cohomology over this prism. BS22 Remark 3.11: the analogous prism structure on W[[x_1,…,x_d]] gives perfectoid covers of regular local rings.

**Planning API.**

- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Prism.breuilKisin` (constructor): For a power-series δ-ring W[[u]] with φ(u) = u^p over a crystalline base and E ∈ W[u] Eisenstein at p: the prism (W[[u]], (E)). Require E to be monic with positive degree; Mathlib’s IsEisensteinAt alone permits E=1 and is insufficient.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Prism.breuilKisin_I` (simp): Its ideal is generated by E(u).
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Prism.breuilKisin_phi_X` (simp): φ(u) = u^p.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Prism.breuilKisin_isBounded` (characterisation): It is a bounded, orientable prism.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Prism.breuilKisin_bar` (equivalence): For E the positive-degree monic Eisenstein minimal polynomial of the uniformizer π, W(k)[[u]]/(E) ≃ O_K via u↦π, respecting W(k). This map supplies the structure map of the Breuil–Kisin object in the absolute site.

**Unit tests.**

- `breuil_kisin_not_perfect` (non-example): The Breuil–Kisin prism is not perfect: u is not in the image of φ.
- `breuil_kisin_not_crystalline` (non-example): For E = u − p over Z_p the ideal (E) is not (p).
- `breuil_kisin_linear_reduction` (computation): For E = u − p over Z_p, the quotient Z_p[[u]]/(u − p) is Z_p via u ↦ p.

**Acceptance.** K = Q_p, π = p: A = Z_p[[u]], E = u − p, δ(u − p) = δ(−p) + (correction) is a unit congruent to δ(−p) modulo u. K = Q_p(p^{1/2}), p odd: E = u^2 − p.

**Prototype boundary.** `TauCeti.Prismatic.Prism.breuilKisin_bar` needs its supplier carrier: R06 and DD.1 must supply complete DVR geometry, the coefficient embedding W(k)→O_K and continuous evaluation u↦π. The typed Eisenstein prism above does not identify its quotient with an arbitrary target ring.

**Sources.** [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Example 2.20 (4). Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 18. The example as printed, with the residue field hypothesis made explicit..

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-0-delta-completion-unique-fg"></a>

### Unique classical completion for a finitely generated ideal

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-completion-unique-fg` · theorem. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Delta` in `TauCeti/RingTheory/Delta/AdicCompletion`.

If I is finitely generated and contains p, the classical completion AdicCompletion I A has a unique delta structure for which its canonical algebra map from A is delta-compatible. The constructed operation has the one-step ideal-adic continuity bound. No Noetherianity, p-torsionfreeness, reducedness or separation hypothesis on A is imposed.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** p is prime; I.FG is retained for the kernel-power equality and hence uniqueness among ALL compatible structures, not just those already known continuous.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Existence and base compatibility are delta-classical-completion and delta-completion-base. The pinned isAdicComplete theorem identifies the inverse-limit ring as a complete module for I when I is finite.
2. Put J=I.map(i) in B. It contains p_B. The exact pow_smul_top_eq_ker_eval theorem, transported through normalized evalₐ, identifies J^r with ker(rho_r). The normalization uses (I^r times top)=I^r on A and the elementary scalar-extension identity (I^r).map(i)=J^r; no closure is silently inserted.
3. Let e be ANY compatible delta structure on B. For x and n, choose a in A representing rho_(n+1)(x). Then x-i(a) is in J^(n+1). Apply delta-adic-congruence to e on B with ideal J. Thus rho_n(e(x))=rho_n(e(i(a)))=[delta_A(a)]_n by compatibility.
4. The last expression is q_n(rho_(n+1)(x)), hence rho_n(D(x)). Equality of every coordinate makes e=D. This derives continuity of a competing structure from the algebraic estimate and kernel equality rather than assuming it.
5. For the constructed D, completion_congr and the same kernel equality give ideal-adic continuity with one-step modulus. This is the full classical conclusion of Lemma 2.17; no comparison with derived completion or Lemma 2.18 is asserted.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-completion-base`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-delta-completion-base); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-completion-coordinate`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-delta-completion-coordinate); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-completion-congruence`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-delta-completion-congruence); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-adic-congruence`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-delta-adic-congruence); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-frobenius-dictionary`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-delta-frobenius-dictionary); [`mathlib:AdicCompletion.pow_smul_top_eq_ker_eval`](#mathlib-adiccompletion-pow-smul-top-eq-ker-eval); [`mathlib:AdicCompletion.factor_evalₐ_eq_eval`](#mathlib-adiccompletion-factor-eval--eq-eval); [`mathlib:AdicCompletion.isAdicComplete`](#mathlib-adiccompletion-isadiccomplete); [`mathlib:AdicCompletion.ext_evalₐ`](#mathlib-adiccompletion-ext-eval-); [`mathlib:AdicCompletion.evalₐ_of`](#mathlib-adiccompletion-eval--of); [`mathlib:Ideal.smul_top_eq_map`](#mathlib-ideal-smul-top-eq-map); [`mathlib:Ideal.map_pow`](#mathlib-ideal-map-pow).

**Acceptance.** Finite generation is not used in the initial ideal-power bound or canonical coordinate construction; it is used here. No delta structure on A/I^n is presumed. Such a claim would already fail for Z/p^n. With I=A the statement correctly gives the unique structure on the zero completion.

**Sources.** [BS22-COMPLETION](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Lemma 2.17, full statement and proof, printed. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 17. An explicit refinement of the classical completion proof. The shifted quotient maps and one-power estimate are derived here, not attributed as separately numbered source results.. [PIN-adic-complete](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/082e2d37e8b0463410cdb532e111cd43d5a66174/Mathlib/RingTheory/AdicCompletion/Completeness.lean), pow_smul_top_eq_ker_eval and isAdicComplete.  The already implemented finite-generation kernel comparison is used directly, not replanned..

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-0-delta-universal-quotient-lift"></a>

### Universal property of the delta quotient

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-universal-quotient-lift` · theorem. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Delta` in `TauCeti/RingTheory/Delta/Ideal`.

Let B be a delta ring and f:A to B a unital ring map commuting with delta and annihilating I. There exists a unique ring map g:A/C_d(I) to B extending f and commuting with the quotient delta operation. Its underlying map is the existing ordinary quotient lift.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** p is prime; A is a commutative ring with the specified delta structure d. No p-torsionfreeness, finite generation or p-locality is assumed.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Delta-kernel-stability makes the ordinary kernel of f delta-stable. Minimality of C_d(I), with I contained in that kernel, shows f annihilates the closure.
2. Construct g by the existing Ideal.Quotient.lift and use its evaluation theorem to prove g(q(a))=f(a).
3. For an arbitrary quotient element choose a representative using surjectivity of q. Evaluate the quotient delta via delta-universal-quotient-projection and use compatibility of f to prove compatibility of g.
4. Any competing map agrees after precomposition with the surjective q, hence agrees everywhere. This proves initiality among the stated delta-compatible maps, without building an unrelated category or assuming an adjunction.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-kernel-stability`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-delta-kernel-stability); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-ideal-closure-minimal`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-delta-ideal-closure-minimal); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-universal-quotient-projection`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-delta-universal-quotient-projection); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-universal-quotient`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-delta-universal-quotient); [`mathlib:RingHom.mem_ker`](#mathlib-ringhom-mem-ker); [`mathlib:Ideal.Quotient.lift`](#mathlib-ideal-quotient-lift); [`mathlib:Ideal.Quotient.lift_mk`](#mathlib-ideal-quotient-lift-mk); [`mathlib:Ideal.Quotient.mk_surjective`](#mathlib-ideal-quotient-mk-surjective); [`mathlib:Ideal.Quotient.ringHom_ext`](#mathlib-ideal-quotient-ringhom-ext).

**Acceptance.** With target Q=A/C_d(I) and f=q, the unique factor is the identity. With the zero target, the unique zero-ring map is allowed and delta-compatible.

**Sources.** [BS22-DELTA-QUOTIENT](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Section 2 opening convention and Definition 2.1; Lemma 2.9 and Example 2.10. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed pages 13, 15. Declaration-sized refinement of the source universal delta quotient. The source uses p-local rings; the displayed proof uses only the integral delta identities and establishes this explicitly broader elementary statement..

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-0-delta-radical-localization"></a>

### p-local localization of a δ-ring

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-radical-localization` · construction. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Delta` in `TauCeti/RingTheory/Delta/Localization`.

Let A be a δ-ring and S ⊂ A a multiplicative subset. Let T be the multiplicative subset generated by S, φ(S), φ^2(S), …. Then (S^{-1}A)_(p) := the localization of S^{-1}A along V(p) (inverting 1 + p·a for all a) coincides with (T^{-1}A)_(p); it carries a unique δ-structure compatible with the one on A, has p in its Jacobson radical, and A → (S^{-1}A)_(p) is the initial δ-A-algebra B with p ∈ rad(B) in which every element of S is invertible. The same holds for the localization along V(p, I) for an ideal I, which is the form used for prisms.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** p is prime; A is a δ-ring; S is a submonoid of A. An arbitrary localization S^{-1}A need not carry a compatible δ-structure; the statement concerns its p-localization.

**Construction or proof.**

1. If p ∈ rad(B) and f ∈ B is a unit then φ(f) = f^p + p·δ(f) is a unit (frobenius-image-unit-jacobson). Hence in any δ-A-algebra B with p ∈ rad(B) where S is invertible, all of T is invertible.
2. T is φ-stable, so delta-localization-phi-stable gives the unique compatible δ-structure on T^{-1}A, initial among δ-A-algebras inverting T.
3. The submonoid 1 + p·T^{-1}A is φ-stable because φ is a ring map: φ(1 + p·a) = 1 + p·φ(a); localize again by delta-localization-phi-stable. The result has p in its radical and, by step 1, the stated initial property; the comparison with (S^{-1}A)_(p) follows because both are initial for the same property among rings with p in the radical (BS22 Remark 2.16).

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-localization-phi-stable`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-delta-localization-phi-stable); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-localization-universal`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-delta-localization-universal); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/frobenius-image-unit-jacobson`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-frobenius-image-unit-jacobson); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-localization-jacobson`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-delta-localization-jacobson); [`mathlib:IsLocalization`](#mathlib-islocalization); [`mathlib:Ideal.jacobson`](#mathlib-ideal-jacobson).

**Consumers.** BS22 Lemma 3.1, proof: the localizations A[1/g_i] along V(p, I) carry unique δ-structures; their product is the ind-Zariski cover on which I is generated by a distinguished element. BS22 Example 2.21 and Example 3.4: the universal distinguished element lives in the localization of Z_(p){d} at δ(d) and its Frobenius iterates. BS22 Lemma 3.7(4): bounded prisms are locally orientable through the completion of such a localization.

**Planning API.**

- `TauCeti.Delta.frobeniusSaturation` (data): The submonoid T generated by all φ^n(s), s ∈ S, n ≥ 0.
- `TauCeti.Delta.frobeniusSaturation_stable` (characterisation): φ maps T into T, and S ≤ T.
- `TauCeti.Delta.radicalSaturation` (data): The submonoid of elements of A that become units modulo p in T^{-1}A; the localization of A at it is (S^{-1}A)_(p).
- `TauCeti.Delta.localizeRadical_p_mem_jacobson` (characterisation): In the localization B of A at the radical saturation, p lies in the Jacobson radical and every element of S is a unit.
- `TauCeti.Delta.localizeRadical` (constructor): The unique δ-structure on the localization B of A at the radical saturation that is compatible with A → B.
- `TauCeti.Delta.localizeRadical_unique` (universal-property): Any δ-A-algebra C with p ∈ rad(C) in which S is invertible receives a unique δ-A-algebra map from B.

**Unit tests.**

- `frobenius_saturation_phi_stable_already` (degenerate): If φ(S) ⊂ S then the Frobenius saturation of S is S.
- `frobenius_saturation_int` (computation): For A = Z with its canonical δ-structure (φ = id) the Frobenius saturation of any submonoid is itself.
- `frobenius_saturation_free_strict` (non-example): In the free δ-ring on one generator x_0, the Frobenius saturation of the powers of x_0 contains x_0^p + p·x_1, which is not a power of x_0.

**Acceptance.** For A = Z and S generated by 3 with p = 2: the result is Z_(2) with its canonical δ-structure. For A = Z{x} and S = {x^n}: T contains φ(x) = x^p + p δ(x), which is not a unit of Z{x}[1/x] but is a unit of its p-localization.

**Sources.** [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Remark 2.16 (Localizations in the p-local world). Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 17. The node states the remark with the Frobenius-saturated monoid T written out..

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-0-free-delta-pd-envelope"></a>

### The PD envelope of the free δ-ring as a δ-pushout

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/free-delta-pd-envelope` · theorem. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Delta` in `TauCeti/RingTheory/Delta/DividedPowers`.

(1) (Lemma 2.35) Let A be a p-torsion-free δ-Z_(p)-algebra and z ∈ A with γ_p(z) = z^p/p! ∈ A. Then γ_n(z) = z^n/n! ∈ A for all n ≥ 0. (2) (Lemma 2.36) The δ-ring C = Z_(p){x, φ(x)/p}, defined as the pushout of Z_(p){z} ← Z_(p){y} → Z_(p){x} along y ↦ p·z and y ↦ φ(x), is identified with the PD envelope D = D_(x)(Z_(p){x}); both are the smallest δ-subring of Z_(p){x}[1/p] containing Z_(p){x} and x^p/p. (3) (Remark 2.37) The same square is a pushout of simplicial commutative rings: the animated ring obtained by freely adjoining φ(x)/p to Z_(p){x} is discrete.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** p is prime; A is a p-torsion-free Z_(p)-algebra with a δ-structure. The inverse of every prime-to-p integer is available, so γ_n(z)=z^n/n! is defined in A[1/p]. The printed Remark 2.37 writes D_(x)(Z_(p)) for D_(x)(Z_(p){x}); the corrected form is used (register entry PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22/E3).

**Construction or proof.**

1. (1) First γ_{p^2}(z) ∈ A: δ(z^p/p) = (z^p + pδ(z))^p/p^2 − z^{p^2}/p^{p+1} ∈ A, and the first term equals p^{p−2}((z^p + pδ(z))/p)^p ∈ A. Then induct on n using γ_{kp} = u·γ_k∘γ_p with u a unit of Z_(p): γ_p(z) is again admissible.
2. (2) The left vertical map of the pushout square is φ on Z_(p){x}, faithfully flat by free-delta-ring, so C is p-torsion-free and embeds in Z_(p){x}[1/p]. D ⊂ C by (1). For C ⊂ D show that φ preserves D and reduces to Frobenius modulo p: φ(x^n/n!) expands with coefficients ((pi)!/i!)·(p^{n−i}/(n−i)!) ∈ Z_(p), divisible by p for 0 < i or i < n, and (x^n/n!)^p = p!·γ_p(x^n/n!) ≡ 0 modulo p.
3. (3) The pushout of animated rings is computed by the derived tensor product; flatness of φ (free-delta-ring) makes it discrete.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/free-delta-ring`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-free-delta-ring); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-ring-category`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-delta-ring-category); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/animated-delta-rings`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-animated-delta-rings); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/torsionfree-frobenius-equivalence`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-torsionfree-frobenius-equivalence); `CrystallineCohomology:CR.0`; [`mathlib:DividedPowers`](#mathlib-dividedpowers).

**Acceptance.** For p = 2 and z = x: δ(x^2/2) = x^4/8 + x^2·δ(x) + δ(x)^2, which exhibits x^4/8 = 3·γ_4(x) as an element of C. C ≠ Z_(p){x}[1/p]: 1/p ∉ C.

**Sources.** [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Lemmas 2.35 and 2.36 with proofs; Remark 2.37. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed pages 22, 23, 24. The three statements are the inputs to Corollary 2.39 and are stated together..

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-0-delta-prime-power-valuation"></a>

### δ and prime power nilpotence

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-prime-power-valuation` · lemma. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/PR0`.

On Z_(p), if v_p(a)=n>0 then v_p(δ(a))=n−1. In particular δ^n(p^n) is a unit. No nonzero δ-ring has p^n=0 for any n>0.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** p is prime; the valuation formula concerns Z_(p), while the nilpotence conclusion concerns all δ-rings.

**Construction or proof.**

1. For a=p^n u with u a p-adic unit, δ(a)=(a−a^p)/p = p^(n−1)u(1−a^(p−1)); the last two factors are units.
2. Iterate the valuation formula to reach a unit in n steps.
3. The canonical δ-map Z_(p)→A exists because every integer prime to p becomes a unit if p is nilpotent. It sends δ^n(p^n) to δ^n(0)=0, forcing the zero ring.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/integer-delta`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-integer-delta); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/p-local-integer-delta`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-p-local-integer-delta); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-localization-phi-stable`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-delta-localization-phi-stable); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/integer-cast-delta`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-integer-cast-delta).

**Acceptance.** For p=2, δ(4)=−6 has valuation one and δ²(4)=−21 is odd. The assertion rules out nonzero rings Z/p^n, including n>1.

**Sources.** [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Example 2.6, §2. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 14. The integral formula gives the valuation drop and the non-nilpotence consequence..

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-0-local-distinguished-prism-generators"></a>

### Local distinguished generators of a prism ideal

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/local-distinguished-prism-generators` · lemma. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/Prism`.

Let A be a δ-ring. (a) (Lemma 2.25) If d, p ∈ rad(A), then d is distinguished if and only if p ∈ (d, φ(d)); in particular distinguishedness depends only on the ideal (d). (b) (Lemma 3.1) Let I ⊂ A be a locally principal ideal with p, I ⊂ rad(A). The following are equivalent: (1) p ∈ I^p + φ(I)A; (2) p ∈ I + φ(I)A; (3) one can choose a δ-map A→A′, obtained as an ind-Zariski localization and faithfully flat, for which IA′=(d), δ(d) is a unit, and both d and p lie in rad(A′).

**Hypotheses and conventions.** A is a δ-ring; in (a) d, p ∈ rad(A); in (b) I is locally principal and p, I ⊂ rad(A). No global generator of I is assumed in (b).

**Construction or proof.**

1. (a) If δ(d) is a unit then p·δ(d) = φ(d) − d^p shows p ∈ (d, φ(d)). Conversely let p = a d + b φ(d). As d, p ∈ rad(A) it suffices to show A/(p, d, δ(d)) = 0; after a suitable ind-Zariski localization one may assume p, d, δ(d) ∈ rad(A). Substituting φ(d) = d^p + p δ(d) gives p(1 − b δ(d)) = c d; the left side is distinguished by distinguished-factor-rigidity (1), so d is distinguished by distinguished-factor-rigidity (2), and then δ(d) is a unit lying in the radical, forcing the localized ring to vanish (BS22 proof of Lemma 2.25).
2. (b) (1) ⇒ (2) is clear. (2) ⇒ (3): choose g_1,…,g_n generating the unit ideal with IA[1/g_i] principal; localize each A[1/g_i] along V(p, I) using delta-radical-localization, and let A′ be the product; on each factor apply (a).
3. (3) ⇒ (1): on A′, p·δ(d) = φ(d) − d^p gives p ∈ I^p A′ + φ(I)A′; descend the containment along the faithfully flat map A → A′.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/distinguished-factor-rigidity`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-distinguished-factor-rigidity); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/distinguished-element`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-distinguished-element); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-radical-localization`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-delta-radical-localization); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/associated-frobenius`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-associated-frobenius); [`mathlib:Module.FaithfullyFlat`](#mathlib-module-faithfullyflat); [`mathlib:Ideal.jacobson`](#mathlib-ideal-jacobson).

**Acceptance.** For A = Z_p[[q − 1]] and I = ([p]_q): p ∈ (I, φ(I)) because φ([p]_q) = [p]_{q^p} ≡ p modulo [p]_q. For I = (p^2) ⊂ Z_p: p ∉ I + φ(I)A, consistent with p^2 not being distinguished.

**Sources.** [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Lemma 2.25 and Lemma 3.1 with proofs. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed pages 19, 28. The two lemmas are stated together as in the integrated decomposition, whose id is kept..

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-0-pd-envelope-as-delta-envelope"></a>

### PD envelopes of regular sequences are δ-envelopes

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/pd-envelope-as-delta-envelope` · theorem. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Delta` in `TauCeti/RingTheory/Delta/DividedPowers`.

(1) (Lemma 2.38) Let B be a p-torsion-free Z_(p)-algebra and f_1,…,f_r ∈ B a Koszul-regular sequence on B/p. The derived pushout D′ of D_(x)(Z_(p)[x_1,…,x_r]) ← Z_(p)[x_1,…,x_r] → B (x_i ↦ f_i) in animated rings is discrete, p-torsion-free and equal to the PD envelope D_(f_1,…,f_r)(B); its formation commutes with base change B → B′ to p-torsion-free Z_(p)-algebras in which the f_i stay Koszul-regular modulo p. (2) (Corollary 2.39) Let A be a p-torsion-free δ-Z_(p)-algebra and f_1,…,f_r ∈ A a regular sequence in A/p. The animated δ-ring A{φ(f_1)/p,…,φ(f_r)/p} (animated-delta-rings) is discrete, p-torsion-free and equal to D_I(A), I = (f_1,…,f_r); so D_I(A) is a δ-ring, finitely presented as a δ-A-algebra. (3) (Remark 2.40) D_I(A) is the φ-pullback of A{f_1/p,…,f_r/p}, which depends only on I and is the universal p-torsion-free δ-A-algebra in which p divides I. (4) (Warning 2.41) The Frobenius twist cannot be removed: for A = Z_(p)[x], f = x, the subrings A{x/p} ⊂ A[1/p] for the δ-structures with φ(x) = x^p and φ(x) = x^p + p are not comparable.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** B and A are p-torsion-free Z_(p)-algebras; the f_i are Koszul-regular on B/p (respectively regular in A/p). The specified structure maps make the polynomial pushout a Z_(p)-algebra construction. PD envelopes and their universal property are supplied by CrystallineCohomology:CR.0. The misprints in the printed proofs (register entry PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22/E9) do not affect the statements.

**Construction or proof.**

1. (1) Modulo p, F_p[x] → D_(x)(F_p[x]) is free over F_p[x]/(x_i^p) = Kos(F_p[x]; x_i^p); so D′ ⊗^L F_p is free over Kos(B/p; f_i^p), which is discrete because Kos(B/p; f_i^{n_i}) is discrete for all n_i by induction. Hence D′ is discrete and p-torsion-free. The maps a : D_(f)(B) → D′ (universal property) and b : D′ → D_(f)(B) (pushout) are mutually inverse: check after inverting p and on PD generators.
2. (2) Factor the pushout square as two squares; by free-delta-pd-envelope the middle row is Z_(p){x_i} → D_(x)(Z_(p){x_i}); apply (1) with flat base change Z_(p)[x] → Z_(p){x}.
3. (3), (4) as in the source: A{f_i/p} is characterised by its universal property; the explicit elements δ_1(x/p) and δ_2(x/p) differ by 1/p.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/free-delta-pd-envelope`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-free-delta-pd-envelope); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/animated-delta-rings`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-animated-delta-rings); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/free-delta-ring`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-free-delta-ring); `CrystallineCohomology:CR.0`; `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E5:animation/animated-commutative-rings`; [`mathlib:RingTheory.Sequence.IsRegular`](#mathlib-ringtheory-sequence-isregular); [`mathlib:DividedPowers`](#mathlib-dividedpowers); `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`.

**Acceptance.** A = Z_p[x] with φ(x) = x^p, f = x: A{x^p/p} is the divided power polynomial algebra on x over Z_p. Warning 2.41: δ_1(x/p) = (x^p/p^{p+1})(p^{p−1} − 1) and δ_2(x/p) = δ_1(x/p) + 1/p.

**Sources.** [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Lemma 2.38, Corollary 2.39 with proofs; Remark 2.40; Warning 2.41. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed pages 24, 25. Statements (1)–(4) are the lemma, the corollary, the remark and the warning..

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-0-pd-envelope-complete-flatness"></a>

### Complete flatness of PD envelopes and of p-adic δ-envelopes

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/pd-envelope-complete-flatness` · theorem. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/Envelope`.

(1) (Lemma 2.43) Let A be an animated ring and B a p-complete animated A-algebra with x_1,…,x_r ∈ π_0(B) such that x_1^p,…,x_r^p is p-completely regular relative to A. Let D be the pushout of D_(y)(Z_p[y_1,…,y_r])^∧ ← Z_p[y_1,…,y_r]^∧ → B (y_i ↦ x_i) in derived p-complete animated rings. Then A → D is p-completely flat. (2) (Corollary 2.44) Let A be a p-complete animated δ-ring, B a p-complete animated δ-A-algebra and x_1,…,x_r ∈ π_0(B) p-completely regular relative to A. Then C = B{x_1/p,…,x_r/p}^∧, the pushout of Z_p{z_i}^∧ ← Z_p{x_i}^∧ → B (x_i ↦ p·z_i), is p-completely flat over A.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** Derived p-completion and p-complete flatness are those of DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1. In (1) the hypothesis is on the p-th powers x_i^p; in (2) on the x_i themselves.

**Construction or proof.**

1. (1) Reduce modulo p: D_(y)(F_p[y]) is free over F_p[y]/(y_i^p), so D ⊗^L F_p is a free module over Kos(B ⊗^L F_p; x_i^p), which is flat over A ⊗^L F_p by hypothesis.
2. (2) Apply Frobenius: by pd-envelope-as-delta-envelope (Remark 2.40) the φ-pullback of B{x_i/p} is the PD envelope of (x_i), to which (1) applies after noting that φ(x_i) ≡ x_i^p; then descend complete flatness along the p-completely faithfully flat Frobenius of the free δ-ring (free-delta-ring), as in the source.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/complete-regular-sequence`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-complete-regular-sequence); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/pd-envelope-as-delta-envelope`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-pd-envelope-as-delta-envelope); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/free-delta-ring`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-free-delta-ring); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/animated-delta-rings`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-animated-delta-rings); `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`; `CrystallineCohomology:CR.0`.

**Acceptance.** A = Z_p, B = Z_p⟨x⟩: C = Z_p{x, x/p}^∧ is p-completely flat over Z_p. The hypothesis is not automatic: for B = A = Z_p the sequence (p) is not p-completely regular relative to A (complete-regular-sequence), and the corollary does not apply to B{p/p}^∧.

**Sources.** [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Lemma 2.43 and Corollary 2.44 with proofs. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed pages 26, 27. Lemma and corollary as printed..

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-0-ainf-prism"></a>

### The perfect prism of a perfectoid ring

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/ainf-prism` · construction. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/Examples`.

Let R be an integral perfectoid ring (in the sense of BMS1 §3, supplied by PerfectoidQuotients:Q0:integral-algebra), R^♭ = lim_{x↦x^p} R/p its tilt, A_inf(R) = W(R^♭) and θ : A_inf(R) → R Fontaine's map. Then A_inf(R) with the Witt vector Frobenius and I = ker θ is a perfect prism with A_inf(R)/I = R: ker θ is generated by a distinguished nonzerodivisor ξ, and A_inf(R) is classically (p, ξ)-complete. For R = O_C with C a perfectoid field of characteristic 0 containing a compatible system p^♭ of p-power roots of p (for instance C algebraically closed), one may take ξ = p − [p^♭].

**Hypotheses and conventions.** R is integral perfectoid: π-adically complete for some π with π^p dividing p (equivalently p-adically complete with π^p = p·unit for some π), Frobenius on R/p surjective and ker θ principal (BMS1 Definition 3.5; BMS2 Definition 4.18).

**Construction or proof.**

1. W(R^♭) is a perfect p-complete δ-ring by perfect-delta-rings. θ is surjective (Mathlib: surjective_fontaineTheta) and ker θ = (ξ) with ξ having unit first Teichmüller coefficient (BMS1 Remark 3.11, supplied by Q0:integral-algebra), so ξ is distinguished by distinguished-in-perfect-delta-rings and a nonzerodivisor by the same node.
2. Completeness: W(R^♭) is p-adically complete and R^♭ is complete for the image of ξ; this gives classical, hence derived, (p, ξ)-completeness. p ∈ (ξ, φ(ξ)) by local-distinguished-prism-generators (a).

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/prism`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-prism); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/prism-category`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-prism-category); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/perfect-delta-rings`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-perfect-delta-rings); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/distinguished-in-perfect-delta-rings`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-distinguished-in-perfect-delta-rings); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/local-distinguished-prism-generators`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-local-distinguished-prism-generators); `PerfectoidQuotients:Q0:integral-algebra/semiperfectoid-quasisyntomic-and-qrsp-rings`; `PerfectoidQuotients:Q0:integral-algebra/theta-naturality`; [`mathlib:WittVector.fontaineTheta`](#mathlib-wittvector-fontainetheta); [`mathlib:surjective_fontaineTheta`](#mathlib-surjective-fontainetheta); [`mathlib:PreTilt`](#mathlib-pretilt); [`mathlib:WittVector.frobenius_bijective`](#mathlib-wittvector-frobenius-bijective); `PerfectoidQuotients:Q0:integral-algebra`.

**Consumers.** BS22 Theorem 3.10: one of the two functors of the equivalence between perfectoid rings and perfect prisms. BS22 Theorem 17.2 and PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/ainf-omega-comparison: AΩ is compared with prismatic cohomology over (A_inf, ker θ). BS22 Theorem 9.1 and PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/etale-comparison: the base prism of the étale comparison.

**Planning API.**

- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Prism.ainf` (constructor): For a p-adically complete ring O with p not a unit, Frobenius surjective on O/p and ker θ generated by a distinguished nonzerodivisor: the prism (W(O^♭), ker θ).
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Prism.ainf_I` (simp): Its ideal is the kernel of Fontaine's θ.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Prism.ainf_phi` (compatibility): Its Frobenius is the Witt vector Frobenius of W(O^♭).
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Prism.ainf_isPerfect` (characterisation): It is a perfect prism.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Prism.ainf_bar_equiv` (equivalence): θ induces an isomorphism W(O^♭)/ker θ ≅ O.

**Unit tests.**

- `ainf_prism_theta_teichmuller` (computation): θ sends the Teichmüller lift [x] to the untilt of x (Mathlib: fontaineTheta_teichmuller).
- `ainf_prism_kernel_not_p` (non-example): If p ≠ 0 in O then ker θ ≠ (p): p is not in the kernel.
- `ainf_prism_perfect_bounded` (characterisation): The prism (W(O^♭), ker θ) is bounded.

**Acceptance.** R = Z_p^cycl-completion, ε = (1, ζ_p, ζ_{p^2}, …): ξ = [p]_q at q = [ε^{1/p}], that is ξ = 1 + [ε^{1/p}] + … + [ε^{(p−1)/p}], and θ(ξ) = 1 + ζ_p + … + ζ_p^{p−1} = 0. R perfect of characteristic p: A_inf(R) = W(R), ker θ = (p), and the prism is the crystalline prism (W(R), (p)).

**Sources.** [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Example 2.20 (3); Theorem 3.10 (the functor R ↦ (A_inf(R), ker θ)); Example 1.3. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed pages 2, 18, 32. The example for O_C, stated for every perfectoid ring as in Theorem 3.10..

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-0-q-de-rham-prism"></a>

### The q-de Rham prism

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/q-de-rham-prism` · construction. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/Examples`.

A = Z_p[[q − 1]] with the δ-structure determined by φ(q) = q^p (equivalently δ(q) = 0), and I = ([p]_q), where [p]_q = (q^p − 1)/(q − 1) = 1 + q + … + q^{p−1} is the p-th cyclotomic polynomial evaluated at q. Then (A, I) is a bounded, oriented, non-perfect prism with A/I = Z_p[ζ_p]. The ideal of the prism is ([p]_q), not (q − 1): (A, (q − 1)) is not a prism.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** p is prime.

**Construction or proof.**

1. A is p-torsion-free and φ(q) = q^p extends uniquely to a continuous ring endomorphism lifting Frobenius, so torsionfree-frobenius-equivalence gives δ with δ(q) = 0. A is (p, q − 1)-complete, hence (p, [p]_q)-complete because [p]_q ≡ (q − 1)^{p−1} modulo p.
2. [p]_q ≡ p modulo (q − 1), so δ([p]_q) ≡ δ(p) modulo (q − 1); δ(p) is a unit and A is (q − 1)-adically complete, so δ([p]_q) is a unit. [p]_q is a nonzerodivisor of the domain A.
3. A/[p]_q = Z_p[ζ_p] is p-torsion-free: bounded. For (q − 1): p ∉ (q − 1, q^p − 1) = (q − 1).

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/prism`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-prism); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/prism-category`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-prism-category); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/torsionfree-frobenius-equivalence`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-torsionfree-frobenius-equivalence); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/distinguished-element`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-distinguished-element); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/local-distinguished-prism-generators`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-local-distinguished-prism-generators); [`mathlib:PowerSeries`](#mathlib-powerseries); [`mathlib:PadicInt`](#mathlib-padicint); [`mathlib:Polynomial.cyclotomic`](#mathlib-polynomial-cyclotomic); [`mathlib:Polynomial.cyclotomic_prime`](#mathlib-polynomial-cyclotomic-prime); [`mathlib:Polynomial.eval_one_cyclotomic_prime`](#mathlib-polynomial-eval-one-cyclotomic-prime).

**Consumers.** BS22 §16 and PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/q-pd-pair: the base of q-crystalline and q-de Rham cohomology. BS22 §12.2: the key case of the Nygaard filtration is computed over this prism. HabiroRings:HR.1 and HabiroCohomologyFoundations:HQ.8: the p-adic chart of the Habiro ring; the identity q^p − 1 = (q − 1)[p]_q relates the two completion ideals.

**Planning API.**

- `TauCeti.Prismatic.qAnalog` (data): The q-analogue [n]_q = 1 + q + … + q^{n−1} in a ring with a chosen element q.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.qAnalog_mul_sub_one` (relation): (q − 1)·[n]_q = q^n − 1.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.qAnalog_one_eq` (simp): At q = 1, [n]_q = n.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Prism.qDeRham` (constructor): The prism (Z_p[[q − 1]], ([p]_q)).
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Prism.qDeRham_I` (simp): Its ideal is generated by [p]_q.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Prism.qDeRham_phi_q` (simp): φ(q) = q^p.

**Unit tests.**

- `q_analog_two` (computation): [2]_q = 1 + q.
- `q_analog_prime_cyclotomic` (compatibility): In Z[X] with q = X, [p]_q is the p-th cyclotomic polynomial.
- `q_de_rham_ideal_not_q_minus_one` (non-example): In Z_p[[q − 1]] the ideals ([p]_q) and (q − 1) are different.
- `q_de_rham_p_mem` (characterisation): p ∈ ([p]_q, [p]_{q^p}) in Z_p[[q − 1]].

**Acceptance.** [p]_q evaluated at q = 1 is p; φ([p]_q) = [p]_{q^p} ≡ p modulo [p]_q. p = 2: [2]_q = 1 + q, δ(1 + q) = δ(1) + δ(q) − q = −q, a unit.

**Sources.** [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Example 2.20 (2); Notation 16.1; Example 1.3. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed pages 2, 18, 106. The example as printed..

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-0-universal-oriented-prism"></a>

### The universal oriented prism

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/universal-oriented-prism` · construction. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/Examples`.

Let A_0 = Z_(p){d, δ(d)^{-1}} be the localization of the free δ-ring on d at the multiplicative set generated by δ(d), φ(δ(d)), φ^2(δ(d)), …; it is the initial δ-ring over Z_(p) with a distinguished element, and d is a nonzerodivisor modulo p. Let A be the (p, d)-completion of A_0 and I = (d). Then (A, I) is a bounded prism oriented by d, and it is the universal oriented prism: for every prism (B, J) with a chosen generator e of J there is a unique map of prisms A → B with d ↦ e. In A the sequence (p, d) is regular and the Frobenius of A/p is d-completely flat.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** p is prime. It is universal among oriented prisms, not among orientable ones. The flatness of Frobenius asserted here is weaker than the faithful flatness that Construction 6.1 assumes; register entry PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22/E13 records that gap, and PrismaticCohomology:PR.1 handles it.

**Construction or proof.**

1. A_0 exists and has the stated universal property by free-delta-ring and delta-localization-phi-stable; it is a localization of a polynomial ring, and d is a variable, so d is a nonzerodivisor modulo p and (p, d) is regular.
2. Completion: delta-classical-completion gives the δ-structure on the (p, d)-completion; regularity of (p, d) persists, A/d is p-torsion-free, so (A, (d)) is a bounded prism with d distinguished.
3. Universal property: a generator e of J is distinguished (prism, local-distinguished-prism-generators (a)); the δ-map Z_(p){d} → B, d ↦ e, inverts δ(d) and its Frobenius iterates since units are preserved by φ when p ∈ rad(B), and extends to the completion because B is derived (p, J)-complete.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/free-delta-ring`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-free-delta-ring); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-localization-phi-stable`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-delta-localization-phi-stable); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-radical-localization`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-delta-radical-localization); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-classical-completion`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-delta-classical-completion); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/prism`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-prism); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/prism-category`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-prism-category); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/local-distinguished-prism-generators`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-local-distinguished-prism-generators).

**Consumers.** BS22 Construction 6.1 and Proposition 6.2: the Hodge–Tate comparison for an oriented prism is reduced to this universal case and then to a crystalline prism. BS22 Proposition 3.13, proof: the flatness of prismatic envelopes is proved by base change from the universal oriented prism. Bhatt–Lurie §3.2: the formal spectrum of this prism is an atlas-type chart of the Cartier–Witt stack (PrismaticCohomology:PR.5/cartier-witt-stack).

**Planning API.**

- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Prism.Oriented` (structure): An oriented prism: a prism with a chosen generator of its ideal.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Prism.Oriented.isDistinguished` (characterisation): The chosen generator is distinguished.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Prism.Oriented.generator_mem_nonZeroDivisors` (characterisation): The chosen generator is a nonzerodivisor.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Prism.Oriented.isOrientable` (relation): The underlying prism is orientable.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Prism.universalOriented` (constructor): The derived (p,d)-completion of the free δ-Z_(p)-algebra on d with all Frobenius iterates of δ(d) inverted is an oriented bounded prism; regularity makes this completion classical as well.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Prism.universalOriented_lift` (universal-property): For an oriented prism (B,J,e), there is exactly one prism map from the universal oriented prism sending d to e. Its δ-ring restriction is the free lift; completeness extends it uniquely.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Prism.universalOriented_lift_generator` (simp): The universal lift carries its chosen orientation d to the target orientation e; replacing e by a unit multiple changes the lift accordingly.

**Unit tests.**

- `oriented_padic` (computation): The prism (Z_p, (p)) is oriented by p, and δ(p) = 1 − p^{p−1}.
- `oriented_generator_unique_up_to_unit` (characterisation): Two orientations of the same prism differ by a unit.
- `oriented_not_unit` (non-example): If A is nonzero, the generator of an oriented prism is not a unit.

**Acceptance.** The map to (Z_p, (p)) with d ↦ p, and the map to (Z_p[[q−1]], ([p]_q)) with d ↦ [p]_q. There is no map from the universal oriented prism to (Z_p, (p)) sending d to p^2.

**Sources.** [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Example 2.21; Example 3.4. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed pages 18, 29. The two examples as printed..

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-0-rigidity-prism-ideal"></a>

### Rigidity of maps of prisms

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/rigidity-prism-ideal` · theorem. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/Prism`.

If (A, I) → (B, J) is a map of prisms, the natural map I ⊗_A B → J is an isomorphism; in particular J = IB. Conversely, if (A, I) is a prism and A → B is a map of δ-rings with B derived (p, I)-complete, then (B, IB) is a prism if and only if B[I] = 0, that is, I ⊗_A B → B is injective.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** (A, I) is a prism; in the converse B is a δ-A-algebra that is derived (p, I)-complete.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Both I ⊗_A B and J are invertible B-modules and the map between them can be checked to be an isomorphism after faithfully flat base change; by local-distinguished-prism-generators choose compatible ind-Zariski covers on which I = (d) and J = (e) with d, e distinguished.
2. Then d = e·f for some f; by distinguished-factor-rigidity (2) f is a unit, so (d) = (e).
3. Converse: B[I] = 0 says that IB ≅ I ⊗_A B is invertible; derived completeness is assumed and p ∈ IB + φ(IB)B is inherited from A.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/prism`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-prism); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/prism-category`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-prism-category); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/local-distinguished-prism-generators`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-local-distinguished-prism-generators); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/distinguished-factor-rigidity`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-distinguished-factor-rigidity); `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`; [`mathlib:Module.Invertible`](#mathlib-module-invertible).

**Acceptance.** Every map of prisms out of a crystalline prism lands in a crystalline prism. The unique δ-map Z_p[[q−1]] → Z_p (with φ = id on Z_p) sends q to 1 and [p]_q to p; it is a map of prisms to (Z_p, (p)), and indeed J = IB = (p).

**Sources.** [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Lemma 3.5 (Rigidity of maps) with proof; Proposition 1.5. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed pages 3, 29. Statement and proof; the integrated decomposition id is kept..

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-0-prism-frobenius-ideal-principal"></a>

### The Frobenius pullback of a prism ideal is principal

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/prism-frobenius-ideal-principal` · lemma. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/Prism`.

Let (A, I) be a prism. Then φ(I)A is a principal ideal and each of its generators is a distinguished element. Both φ^*I=I⊗_{A,φ}A and the ideal I^p are free A-modules of rank one.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** (A, I) is a prism.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Write p = a + b with a ∈ I^p, b ∈ φ(I)A (prism: p ∈ I^p + φ(I)A). On a cover A → B with IB = (d), d distinguished, write a = x d^p, b = y φ(d); if y were not a unit, after localizing so that d, p, y ∈ rad(B), the identity p(1 − y δ(d)) = d·(d^{p−1}(x + y)) and distinguished-factor-rigidity would make d a unit, contradicting d ∈ rad(B). So b generates φ(I)A and is distinguished (source: proof of Lemma 3.6, which cites the criterion as "Proposition 3.1"; it is Lemma 3.1).
2. φ^*I ≅ I^p modulo p, hence globally since p ∈ rad(A); and A → φ^*I, 1 ↦ f for f lifting a generator of φ(I)A, is an isomorphism, checked after base change to the p-completed perfection where distinguished elements are nonzerodivisors (distinguished-in-perfect-delta-rings).

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/prism`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-prism); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/local-distinguished-prism-generators`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-local-distinguished-prism-generators); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/distinguished-factor-rigidity`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-distinguished-factor-rigidity); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/distinguished-in-perfect-delta-rings`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-distinguished-in-perfect-delta-rings); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/perfect-delta-rings`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-perfect-delta-rings).

**Planning API.**

- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Prism.exists_distinguished_generator_map` (characterisation): For a prism (A,I), there exists a distinguished d∈A with φ(I)A=(d). The stronger assertion about every generator is part of the node theorem.

**Acceptance.** For (Z_p[[q−1]], ([p]_q)): φ(I)A = ([p]_{q^p}). For a perfect prism the lemma gives that I itself is principal.

**Sources.** [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Lemma 3.6 with proof. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 29. Statement and proof..

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-0-bounded-prism-complete-flatness"></a>

### Properties of bounded prisms

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/bounded-prism-complete-flatness` · theorem. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/Bounded`.

Let (A, I) be a bounded prism. (1) A is classically (p, I)-complete. (2) If M ∈ D(A) is derived (p, I)-complete and (p, I)-completely flat, then M is discrete and classically (p, I)-complete; for every n ≥ 0, M[I^n] = 0 and M/I^n M has bounded p^∞-torsion. (3) The functor B ↦ (B, IB) is an equivalence from (p, I)-completely (faithfully) flat, derived (p, I)-complete δ-A-algebras to (faithfully) flat maps of prisms (A, I) → (B, J). (4) There is a (p, I)-completely faithfully flat map A → B of δ-rings, the derived (p, I)-completion of an ind-Zariski localization, with IB = (d) for a distinguished nonzerodivisor d; so (A, I) → (B, (d)) is a faithfully flat map of bounded prisms.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** (A, I) is bounded: A/I has bounded p^∞-torsion. In (2) and (3) derived (p, I)-completeness of M and of B is a hypothesis: the printed statement of Lemma 3.7(2)–(3) omits it, its proof uses it, and without it the statement is false (register entry PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22/E10).

**Construction or proof.**

1. Write derived (p, I)-completion as R lim_n R lim_m of Koszul-type quotients by I^n and p^m; since I is invertible, reduce the I-direction to A/I^n, which has bounded p^∞-torsion by dévissage from A/I.
2. Apply the bounded-torsion criterion for p-complete flatness (BMS2 Lemma 4.7, supplied by DD.1) to M ⊗^L_A A/I^n: it is discrete with bounded p^∞-torsion, giving M[I^n] = 0; pass to the limit over n.
3. (3) follows from (2) and rigidity-prism-ideal: B[I] = 0. (4): complete the ind-Zariski cover of local-distinguished-prism-generators (b) and apply (3).

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/prism`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-prism); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/prism-category`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-prism-category); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/rigidity-prism-ideal`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-rigidity-prism-ideal); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/local-distinguished-prism-generators`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-local-distinguished-prism-generators); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-etale-extension`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-delta-etale-extension); `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`.

**Acceptance.** M = A: recovers (1). For the q-de Rham prism, A/[p]_q^n is p-torsion-free for all n. For a (p,f)-complete ring R with f a nonzerodivisor, bounded p^∞-torsion of R/f does not give bounded p^∞-torsion of R (unbounded-torsion-example; that ring is not claimed to be a prism).

**Sources.** [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Lemma 3.7 (Properties of bounded prisms) with proof. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 30. Statement with the derived completeness hypothesis restored; the integrated decomposition id is kept..

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-0-perfect-prism-properties"></a>

### Properties of perfect prisms

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/perfect-prism-properties` · lemma. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/Perfect`.

Let (A, I) be a perfect prism. (1) I is principal and every generator is a distinguished nonzerodivisor. (2) (A, I) is bounded, with (A/I)[p^∞] = (A/I)[p]; in particular A is classically (p, I)-complete.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** (A, I) is a prism with φ bijective.

**Construction or proof.**

1. (1) By prism-frobenius-ideal-principal, φ(I)A = φ(I) = (b) with b distinguished; φ^{-1} is an automorphism commuting with δ, so I = (φ^{-1}(b)) and φ^{-1}(b) is distinguished. A generator is a nonzerodivisor because I is invertible; any other generator is a unit multiple, distinguished by distinguished-factor-rigidity (1).
2. Before applying BS22 Lemma 2.34, derive classical p-completeness and p-adic separatedness from derived p-completeness and p-torsion-freeness via DD.1. Reducedness of A/p alone does not supply separatedness.
3. (2) A is p-torsion-free (p-torsion-freeness-criteria) and A/p is perfect, hence reduced; apply distinguished-in-perfect-delta-rings (Lemma 2.34) to a generator d, then bounded-prism-complete-flatness (1).

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/prism-frobenius-ideal-principal`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-prism-frobenius-ideal-principal); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/p-torsion-freeness-criteria`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-p-torsion-freeness-criteria); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/distinguished-in-perfect-delta-rings`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-distinguished-in-perfect-delta-rings); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/bounded-prism-complete-flatness`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-bounded-prism-complete-flatness); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/prism-category`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-prism-category); `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`.

**Acceptance.** (A_inf(O_C), (ξ)): A_inf/ξ = O_C is p-torsion-free. (W(R), (p)) for R perfect.

**Sources.** [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Lemma 3.8 (Properties of perfect prisms) with proof. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 31. Statement and proof..

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-0-regular-prismatic-envelopes"></a>

### Prismatic envelopes of regular ideals

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/regular-prismatic-envelopes` · construction. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/Envelope`.

Let (A, I) be a bounded prism, B a (p, I)-completely flat δ-A-algebra (derived (p, I)-complete), and J ⊂ B an ideal containing IB such that, Zariski locally on Spf(B), J = (I, x_1,…,x_r) with (x_1,…,x_r) (p, I)-completely regular relative to A (complete-regular-sequence). Then there is a universal map of δ-pairs (B, J) → (C, IC) to a prism over (A, I); write C = B{J/I}^∧. Moreover: (1) C is (p, I)-completely flat over A; (2) the formation of C commutes with base change along every map of bounded prisms (A, I) → (A′, IA′); (3) for a (p, I)-completely flat map of δ-A-algebras B → B′, C ⊗̂^L_B B′ ≅ B′{JB′/I}^∧. When I = (d) and J = (d, x_1,…,x_r), C is the derived (p, d)-completion of the animated δ-ring B{x_1/d,…,x_r/d}, which is discrete and d-torsion-free.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** (A, I) bounded; B a (p, I)-completely flat, derived (p, I)-complete δ-A-algebra; J as stated. C is in general not (p, I)-completely flat over B. The typical case (BS22 Example 3.14): R p-completely smooth over A/I, B_0 → R a surjection from a (p, I)-completely smooth A-algebra, B_0 → B (p, I)-completely flat with B a δ-A-algebra, J the kernel of B → R ⊗̂^L_{B_0} B.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Reduce to I = (d) oriented and J = (d, x_1,…,x_r) globally using bounded-prism-complete-flatness (4), faithfully flat descent of derived complete modules (DD.1) and property (3), which makes the construction a sheaf in B.
2. Define C′ = B{x_i/d}^∧ in derived (p, d)-complete animated δ-rings (animated-delta-rings). Show C′ is (p, d)-completely flat over A: push out along ψ: Z_p{z}^∧ → Z_p{y}^∧, z ↦ φ(y), where Z_p{z}^∧ → A is z ↦ d; ψ is the Frobenius of the completed free δ-ring, (p,z)-completely faithfully flat by free-delta-ring. On A' = A ⊗̂ Z_p{y}^∧ adjoin φ(y)/p to get D, where φ(y) = p·unit (distinguished-factor-rigidity), so C'' = B''{x_i/p}^∧ is flat over D by pd-envelope-complete-flatness (Corollary 2.44); D is the PD envelope of (y) in A' (pd-envelope-as-delta-envelope), which maps to Kos(A'; p, y), so flatness over A' is detected after base change to D.
3. By bounded-prism-complete-flatness (2) C′ is discrete, classically complete and d-torsion-free, so (C′, dC′) is a prism by rigidity-prism-ideal; the universal property is that of the pushout, since a map to a prism (C″, dC″) makes x_i uniquely divisible by d.
4. (2) and (3) follow from the pushout description and completed base change.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/prism`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-prism); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/prism-category`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-prism-category); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/bounded-prism-complete-flatness`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-bounded-prism-complete-flatness); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/rigidity-prism-ideal`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-rigidity-prism-ideal); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/complete-regular-sequence`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-complete-regular-sequence); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/pd-envelope-complete-flatness`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-pd-envelope-complete-flatness); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/pd-envelope-as-delta-envelope`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-pd-envelope-as-delta-envelope); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/animated-delta-rings`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-animated-delta-rings); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/universal-oriented-prism`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-universal-oriented-prism); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/free-delta-ring`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-free-delta-ring); `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`; `CrystallineCohomology:CR.0`.

**Consumers.** BS22 Construction 4.17–4.18 and PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/cech-alexander-complex: the terms of the Čech–Alexander complex are prismatic envelopes of the kernels of B^{⊗n} → R. BS22 Theorem 5.2: for a crystalline prism the envelope is the Frobenius descent of the PD envelope, which gives the crystalline comparison. BS22 Lemma 16.10 and PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/q-pd-envelope: q-PD envelopes are prismatic envelopes over the q-de Rham prism. BS22 Proposition 7.10: the prism of a regular semiperfectoid quotient is an envelope.

**Planning API.**

- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Envelope` (structure): For an oriented prism (A, (d)) and elements x_1,…,x_r of a δ-A-algebra B: a δ-B-algebra C with elements z_i satisfying d·z_i = x_i, d a nonzerodivisor on C, initial among δ-B-algebras C″ in which d is a nonzerodivisor and divides every x_i. (Derived completeness of C and C″ is the condition supplied by DD.1.)
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Envelope.lift` (universal-property): The unique δ-B-algebra map from the envelope to such a C″.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Envelope.lift_z` (simp): lift sends z_i to the unique element w_i with d·w_i = x_i.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Envelope.hom_ext` (extensionality): Two δ-B-algebra maps out of an envelope into a ring where d is a nonzerodivisor agree.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Envelope.unique` (universal-property): Two envelopes of the same data are isomorphic as B-algebras by an isomorphism matching the z_i.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Envelope.exists` (constructor): For every δ-ring B, element d and family x there is an envelope (before completion). Its relation to B{J/I}^∧ is not asserted: under the hypotheses of the node, B{J/I}^∧ receives a unique δ-B-algebra map from it, and whether this is the derived (p,d)-completion is left open.

**Unit tests.**

- `envelope_trivial` (degenerate): For the empty family of elements, B itself (if d is a nonzerodivisor on B) is an envelope.
- `envelope_divisible_element` (compatibility): If x = d·y in B and d is a nonzerodivisor on B then B is an envelope of the single element x, with z = y.
- `envelope_z_unique` (characterisation): In an envelope the elements z_i are determined by d·z_i = x_i.
- `envelope_delta_z` (characterisation): In an envelope, φ(d)·δ(z_i) = δ(x_i) − z_i^p·δ(d): the element δ(z_i) is forced, so the envelope is not the ring B[z]/(d·z − x), which has no such element in general.
- `envelope_not_localization` (non-example): For a δ-structure with φ(x) = x^p on a polynomial ring in x, the subring generated by x and x/p is not stable under δ: δ(x/p) = (x^p/p^{p+1})·(p^{p−1} − 1) does not lie in it; for p = 2, δ(x/2) = x^2/8 is not in Z[x, x/2].

**Acceptance.** (A, I) = (Z_p, (p)), B = Z_p⟨x⟩ with φ(x) = x^p, J = (p, x): C = Z_p{x/p}^∧, whose Frobenius pullback is the p-completed PD polynomial algebra. Over the q-de Rham prism with B = A⟨x⟩, δ(x) = 0 and J = ([p]_q, x): C = B{x/[p]_q}^∧; its base change along the A-linear δ-map B → B, x ↦ x^p, is B{φ(x)/[p]_q}^∧ = B{x^p/[p]_q}^∧, the q-PD envelope of (B, (q − 1, x)) (BS22 Lemma 16.10); this is not the Frobenius twist of C, which is B{x^p/[p]_{q^p}}^∧. For J = IB the envelope is B itself.

**Sources.** [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Proposition 3.13 (Existence of prismatic envelopes for regular ideals) with proof; Example 3.14. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed pages 33, 35. Statement and proof; the integrated decomposition id is kept..

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-0-unbounded-torsion-example"></a>

### A (p,f)-complete ring with bounded torsion modulo f and unbounded torsion

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/unbounded-torsion-example` · construction. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/Examples`.

Let R be the (p, f)-adic completion of Z[f, x_{i,j} : i ≥ 0, 0 ≤ j ≤ i]/J_0, where J_0 is generated by the elements p·x_{i,j} − f·x_{i,j+1} (with x_{i,i+1} := 0) and by all products x_{i,j}·x_{k,l}. (The source omits the products; without them f·x_{1,1}^2 = 0 and x_{1,1}^2 ≠ 0, so f is a zero divisor and x_{1,1}^2 is (p,f)-torsion. With them R/f is the p-adic completion of Z ⊕ ⊕ (Z/p)·x_{i,j}.) Then R is classically (p, f)-complete (it is a completion), f is a nonzerodivisor of R (use the module model and the uniform filtration estimate in the proof below), all p^∞-torsion of R/f is killed by p, yet p^i·x_{i,0} = p^{i−1}·f·x_{i,1} = … = f^i·x_{i,i} ≠ 0 and p^{i+1}·x_{i,0} = f^i·p·x_{i,i} = 0, so R has unbounded p^∞-torsion. The (p, f)^∞-torsion of R is zero.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** The displayed chain is the corrected one: the source prints p^i·f·x_{i,1} for its second term (register entry PAPER-ANSCHUTZ-LEBRAS-23/E3).

**Construction or proof.**

1. The relations give p·x_{i,j} = f·x_{i,j+1}, hence p^k·x_{i,0} = f^k·x_{i,k} for k ≤ i by induction on k, and p·x_{i,i} = f·x_{i,i+1} = 0, hence p^{i+1}·x_{i,0} = 0.
2. R/f is the p-adic completion of Z ⊕ ⊕_{i,j} (Z/p)·x_{i,j} (square-zero), whose p-power torsion is killed by p.
3. Nonvanishing: the ring map from R to the square-zero extension T ⊕ ε·T, T = (Z/p^{i+1})[f]/(f^{i+1}), sending x_{i,j} to ε·p^j·f^{i−j} and every other x_{k,l} to 0, respects the relations (p·p^j f^{i−j} = f·p^{j+1} f^{i−j−1}, and p·p^i = 0 in T) and is defined on the completion because T is (p, f)-adically discrete; it sends f^i·x_{i,i} to ε·p^i·f^i ≠ 0. This verification is supplied here; the source asserts the nonvanishing without proof.
4. Put A = Z[f] and K = (p,f). The square-zero module with generators x_{i,0},…,x_{i,i} identifies with M_i = (K^i + (p^{i+1}))/(p^{i+1}) ⊂ A/(p^{i+1}), by x_{i,j} ↦ p^j f^{i−j}. To verify the presentation, reduce a relation modulo p: its first coefficient is divisible by p; subtract a multiple of p x_{i,0} − f x_{i,1}, divide by p, and induct on i. Its K-adic completion is the corresponding monomial ideal in (Z/p^{i+1})[[f]], where f is injective. The completed direct sum of the M_i injects into their product: at each finite K-adic level an element has finite support and is detected by its coordinates. Thus f remains injective in R. In each M_i the monomial description gives (K^n M_i : f) ⊂ K^{n−1} M_i for n ≥ 1, uniformly in i. Division by f therefore preserves the restricted-product convergence condition; the quotient of the completed direct sum by f is ⊕ M_i/fM_i, a direct sum of F_p-vector spaces. Together with the base summand Z_p, this proves the description of R/f and its bounded p-torsion. Since f is injective, no nonzero element is killed by a power of K.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/bounded-prism-complete-flatness`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-bounded-prism-complete-flatness); [`mathlib:MvPolynomial`](#mathlib-mvpolynomial); [`mathlib:AdicCompletion`](#mathlib-adiccompletion).

**Consumers.** Anschütz–Le Bras Appendix A: shows that Lemma A.1 and the descent statements must assume bounded p^∞-torsion of the reduction, not of the ring. PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/bounded-prism-complete-flatness: the non-example behind the form of the boundedness hypothesis: A/I bounded does not give A bounded. PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/quasisyntomic-descent: the descent statements for finite projective modules assume boundedness of the reduction.

**Planning API.**

- `TauCeti.Prismatic.UnboundedTorsion.Rel` (data): In the polynomial ring Z[f, x_{i,j}], the ideal generated by the elements p·x_{i,j} − f·x_{i,j+1} (with x_{i,j} = 0 for j > i) and by all products x_{i,j}·x_{k,l}.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.UnboundedTorsion.Ring` (data): The quotient of Z[f, x_{i,j}] by Rel: the uncompleted model of R.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.UnboundedTorsion.p_pow_mul_x` (relation): p^k·x_{i,0} = f^k·x_{i,k} for k ≤ i.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.UnboundedTorsion.p_pow_succ_mul_x` (relation): p^{i+1}·x_{i,0} = 0.

- `TauCeti.Prismatic.UnboundedTorsion.Completion` (data): The (p,f)-adic completion of Ring, the corrected square-zero ring R.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.UnboundedTorsion.f_nonzerodivisor` (relation): Multiplication by the image of f in Completion is injective.

**Unit tests.**

- `unbounded_torsion_order_two` (computation): p^2·x_{1,0} = 0 in the uncompleted model.
- `unbounded_torsion_nonzero` (non-example): p·x_{1,0} ≠ 0 in the uncompleted model: the torsion is not killed by p.
- `unbounded_torsion_no_bound` (characterisation): For every n there is an element killed by a power of p and not by p^n.

**Acceptance.** i = 1: p·x_{1,0} = f·x_{1,1} ≠ 0 and p^2·x_{1,0} = f·p·x_{1,1} = 0: an element of exact p-torsion order 2. For (p,f)-complete rings, bounded p^∞-torsion of R/f is not inherited by R; R is not claimed to carry a δ-structure.

**Sources.** [ALB23](https://arxiv.org/abs/1907.10525v4), Appendix A, Example A.4. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 95. The example with its misprinted chain corrected (routed item PAPER-ANSCHUTZ-LEBRAS-23/155)..

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-0-prism-perfection"></a>

### Perfection of a prism

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/prism-perfection` · construction. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/Perfect`.

Let (A, I) be a prism and A_perf = colim_φ A the perfection of the δ-ring A. Then I·A_perf = (d) for a distinguished element d; p is a nonzerodivisor of A_perf; d is a nonzerodivisor of the p-adic completion of A_perf and of A_perf/N, N = ∩_n p^n A_perf, but in general not of A_perf itself; (A_perf/d)[p^∞] = (A_perf/d)[p]. The derived (p, I)-completion A_∞ of A_perf agrees with its classical (p, I)-adic completion, and (A, I)_perf := (A_∞, I·A_∞) is a perfect prism with a map from (A, I) that is initial among maps from (A, I) to perfect prisms.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** (A, I) is a prism. In the printed proof "A/d[p^∞] = A/d[p]" stands for A_perf/d (register entry PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22/E11).

**Construction or proof.**

1. A → A_perf factors through φ : A → A, so I·A_perf is generated by a distinguished element by prism-frobenius-ideal-principal.
2. A_perf is a perfect δ-ring: p-torsion-free by p-torsion-freeness-criteria. A_perf need not be p-adically separated; let N = ∩ p^n A_perf (a δ-stable ideal, a Q_p-vector space). A' = A_perf/N is p-torsion-free, p-adically separated, perfect, with A'/p = A_perf/p reduced, so distinguished-in-perfect-delta-rings applies to A' and to the p-adic completion of A_perf: d is a nonzerodivisor there and (A'/d)[p^∞] = (A'/d)[p]. Since N ∩ dA_perf = dN and N/dN is p-torsion-free, (A_perf/d)[p^∞] = (A_perf/d)[p].
3. Complete p-adically first (derived = classical by torsion-freeness), then d-adically (each A_perf/d^n has bounded p^∞-torsion). The universal property follows from perfect-delta-rings (left adjoint colim_φ) and completeness of perfect prisms.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/prism`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-prism); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/prism-category`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-prism-category); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/prism-frobenius-ideal-principal`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-prism-frobenius-ideal-principal); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/perfect-delta-rings`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-perfect-delta-rings); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/p-torsion-freeness-criteria`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-p-torsion-freeness-criteria); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/distinguished-in-perfect-delta-rings`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-distinguished-in-perfect-delta-rings); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/perfect-prism-properties`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-perfect-prism-properties); `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`.

**Consumers.** BS22 Theorem 3.10 and Corollary 7.3: composing with A ↦ A/I gives the perfectoidization of A/I for prisms. BS22 Definition 8.2 and PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/perfection-of-prismatic-cohomology: perfection of prismatic cohomology is the completed colimit along Frobenius. Bhatt–Scholze F-crystals and PrismaticCohomology:PR.7/laurent-f-crystal: Laurent F-crystals are computed on perfections of prisms.

**Planning API.**

- `TauCeti.Delta.Perfection` (structure): For a δ-ring A and a ring B: a ring map ι : A → B and a ring automorphism ψ of B with ψ∘ι = ι∘φ, initial among such triples. It presents B as A_perf = colim(A → A → …) along φ.
- `TauCeti.Delta.Perfection.exists` (constructor): Every δ-ring has a perfection.
- `TauCeti.Delta.Perfection.lift` (universal-property): A ring map g from A to a ring C with an automorphism χ such that χ∘g = g∘φ factors uniquely through ι by a map intertwining ψ and χ.
- `TauCeti.Delta.Perfection.lift_comp` (simp): lift g composed with ι is g.
- `TauCeti.Delta.Perfection.p_mem_nonZeroDivisors` (characterisation): If p lies in the Jacobson radical of A then p is a nonzerodivisor of A_perf.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Prism.perfection_generator` (characterisation): For a prism with p and I in the Jacobson radical, I·A_perf is generated by one element.

**Unit tests.**

- `perfection_of_perfect_prism` (degenerate): If φ is bijective then ι : A → A_perf is bijective.
- `perfection_padic` (computation): For the prism (Z_p, (p)), ι : Z_p → A_perf is bijective.
- `perfection_kills_frobenius_kernel` (non-example): ι need not be injective: every a with φ(a) = 0 maps to 0 in A_perf (for instance x − 1 in Z_p[x]/(x^p − 1) with φ(x) = 1).
- `prism_perfection_raw_generator_zero_divisor` (non-example): For the bounded square-zero extension A=Z_p[[u]]⊕∏_(i≥0) Z_p[[u]]/(u^(p^(i+1))−p), d=u−p, the image of d in colim_φ A can kill a nonzero element. This is compatible with regularity of d after p-completion and prevents applying Lemma 2.34 before separatedness.

**Acceptance.** (Z_p[[q−1]], ([p]_q))_perf = (Z_p[q^{1/p^∞}]^∧_{(p,q−1)}, ([p]_q)), whose reduction is Z_p[ζ_{p^∞}]^∧. The perfection of the Breuil–Kisin prism is (A_inf(O_{K_∞}^∧), ker θ) with K_∞ = K(π^{1/p^∞}).

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-0-perfect-prisms-perfectoid-rings"></a>

### Perfect prisms and perfectoid rings

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/perfect-prisms-perfectoid-rings` · theorem. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/Perfect`.

The functors R ↦ (A_inf(R), ker θ) and (A, I) ↦ A/I are mutually inverse equivalences between the category of integral perfectoid rings (BMS1 §3) and the category of perfect prisms. This is a theorem: neither category is defined through the other.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** Perfectoid rings are those of PerfectoidQuotients:Q0:integral-algebra; perfect prisms those of prism-category.

**Construction or proof.**

1. R ↦ (A_inf(R), ker θ) lands in perfect prisms by ainf-prism.
2. For a perfect prism (A, I): by perfect-prism-properties I = (d) with d distinguished; A = W(S) for S = A/p perfect (perfect-delta-rings) and d = [a_0] + p·u with u a unit (distinguished-in-perfect-delta-rings). R = A/d is classically p-complete, its Frobenius modulo p is surjective and π = image of [a_0^{1/p}] satisfies π^p = p·unit. The kernel of θ_R is principal: R/p = S/a_0, so R^♭ = lim_φ S/a_0 is the a_0-adic completion of S, which is S; hence A_inf(R) = W(S) = A, θ_R is the quotient map A → A/d by uniqueness of lifts of S → S/a_0, and ker θ_R = (d). So R is perfectoid, and this already identifies (A_inf(A/I), ker θ) with (A, I).
3. A_inf(A/I) ≅ A compatibly with the maps to A/I by the previous step (R^♭ ≅ S); it is a δ-map by perfect-delta-rings, and it carries ker θ onto I. The other composite is ainf-prism's A_inf(R)/ker θ = R.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/ainf-prism`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-ainf-prism); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/perfect-prism-properties`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-perfect-prism-properties); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/perfect-delta-rings`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-perfect-delta-rings); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/distinguished-in-perfect-delta-rings`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-distinguished-in-perfect-delta-rings); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/rigidity-prism-ideal`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-rigidity-prism-ideal); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/prism-category`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-prism-category); `PerfectoidQuotients:Q0:integral-algebra/semiperfectoid-quasisyntomic-and-qrsp-rings`; [`mathlib:WittVector.fontaineTheta`](#mathlib-wittvector-fontainetheta); `PerfectoidQuotients:Q0:integral-algebra`.

**Acceptance.** O_C ↔ (A_inf, (ξ)); a perfect F_p-algebra R ↔ (W(R), (p)); Z_p^cycl ↔ (Z_p[q^{1/p^∞}]^∧, ([p]_q)). Z_p is not perfectoid, and correspondingly there is no perfect prism with A/I = Z_p.

**Sources.** [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Theorem 3.10 (Perfectoid rings = perfect prisms) with proof; Lemma 3.8. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed pages 31, 32. Statement and proof; the integrated decomposition id is kept..

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-0-prismatic-envelope-rank-one-presentation"></a>

### Presentation of a prismatic envelope for a rank-one element

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/prismatic-envelope-rank-one-presentation` · theorem. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/Envelope`.

Let (A, I) be a bounded prism, d ∈ A a distinguished element and x ∈ A an element of rank 1 (δ(x) = 0). Then for every n ≥ 0 there are elements z_n ∈ A{x/d}^{∧(p,d)}, natural in (A, x), with φ^n(d)·φ^{n−1}(d)^p ⋯ d^{p^n}·z_n = x^{p^n}; and δ^n(x/d) lies in the subring A[z_0,…,z_n] of A{x/d}^{∧(p,d)}.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** (A, I) bounded prism; d distinguished; δ(x) = 0. A{x/d}^{∧(p,d)} is the derived (p, d)-completed δ-A-algebra obtained by freely adjoining x/d.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Argue in the universal case A = Z_p[x]{d, δ(d)^{-1}}^{∧(p,d)} with δ(x) = 0, which is transversal ((p, d) regular) and in which (x, d) is regular; by transversal-prism-regular-sequences the sequences (φ^r(d), φ^{r−1}(d)) are regular.
2. Set z_n = x^{p^n}/(φ^n(d)·φ^{n−1}(d)^p ⋯ d^{p^n}); z_0 = x/d. Since φ(x) = x^p, φ(z_n) = x^{p^{n+1}}/s with s = φ^{n+1}(d) ⋯ φ(d)^{p^n}. The numerator is divisible by d^{p^{n+1}} in A{x/d}, and (d^{p^{n+1}}, s) is a regular sequence in A{x/d}^{∧(p,d)}: φ^m(d) ≡ p·u_m modulo d with u_m a unit, so s ≡ u·p^k modulo d, and (d, p) is regular there because the universal oriented prism T = Z_p{d, δ(d)^{-1}}^{∧(p,d)} is transversal (universal-oriented-prism) and T → A{x/d}^{∧(p,d)} is (p, d)-completely flat (regular-prismatic-envelopes (1) with base (T, (d)), B = T⟨x⟩ = A and J = (d, x)); A → A{x/d}^{∧(p,d)} itself is not completely flat. Hence d^{p^{n+1}} divides φ(z_n), which gives z_{n+1}.
3. δ^n(x/d) ∈ A[z_0,…,z_n] by induction, from δ(z_n) = (φ(z_n) − z_n^p)/p and the relation between φ(z_n) and z_{n+1} (Anschütz–Le Bras, proof of Lemma 4.9.4). The source expects, and does not prove, that the natural surjection from A[y_1, y_2, …]/(x − d y_1, y_1^p − φ(d) y_2, …) is an isomorphism after completion; that is not part of this node.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/regular-prismatic-envelopes`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-regular-prismatic-envelopes); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/transversal-prism-regular-sequences`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-transversal-prism-regular-sequences); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/rank-one-elements`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-rank-one-elements); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/distinguished-element`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-distinguished-element); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/bounded-prism-complete-flatness`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-bounded-prism-complete-flatness); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/universal-oriented-prism`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-universal-oriented-prism).

**Acceptance.** n = 0: d·z_0 = x. n = 1: φ(d)·d^p·z_1 = x^p. For d = p (so φ(d) = p) and x of rank one: z_1 = x^p/p^{p+1} and δ(x/p) = (φ(x/p) − (x/p)^p)/p = p^{p−1}·z_1 − z_1 ∈ A[z_0, z_1].

**Sources.** [ALB23](https://arxiv.org/abs/1907.10525v4), Lemma 4.9.4 (arXiv numbering; Lemma 4.89 in the published version) with proof, and the sentence before the proof. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 72. Statement as printed (routed item PAPER-ANSCHUTZ-LEBRAS-23/127); the quoted sentence is the expectation the source records after the statement..

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-0-perfectoid-tor-independence"></a>

### Tor-independence of perfectoid rings

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/perfectoid-tor-independence` · theorem. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/Prism`.

Let S ← R → T be maps of perfectoid rings, with corresponding perfect prisms (B, IB) ← (A, I) → (C, IC). Then D = B ⊗̂^L_A C (derived (p, I)-completed) is concentrated in degree 0 and is a perfect δ-ring, (D, ID) is a perfect prism, and S ⊗̂^L_R T = D/ID is concentrated in degree 0 and perfectoid. In particular pushouts exist in the category of perfectoid rings and are computed by p-completed derived tensor products.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** R, S, T integral perfectoid; completions are derived p-completions (resp. (p, I)-completions) in the sense of DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Check discreteness and perfectness of D after derived reduction modulo p: B/p ⊗^L_{A/p} C/p is discrete and perfect by Tor-independence of perfect F_p-algebras (Bhatt–Scholze, Projectivity of the Witt vector affine Grassmannian, Lemma 3.16; routed to EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E1 by the extraction of that paper).
2. D is then a perfect p-complete δ-ring (delta-ring-category, perfect-delta-rings); ID is generated by a distinguished element, a nonzerodivisor by distinguished-in-perfect-delta-rings, so (D, ID) is a perfect prism and D/ID = S ⊗̂^L_R T; conclude by perfect-prisms-perfectoid-rings.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/perfect-prisms-perfectoid-rings`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-perfect-prisms-perfectoid-rings); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/perfect-delta-rings`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-perfect-delta-rings); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/distinguished-in-perfect-delta-rings`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-distinguished-in-perfect-delta-rings); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-ring-category`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-delta-ring-category); `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E1`; `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`.

**Acceptance.** O_C⟨x^{1/p^∞}⟩ ⊗̂_{O_C} O_C⟨y^{1/p^∞}⟩ = O_C⟨x^{1/p^∞}, y^{1/p^∞}⟩. For non-perfectoid rings the completed tensor product can have higher Tor: Z_p ⊗^L_{Z_p[x]} Z_p along x ↦ 0 twice.

**Sources.** [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Proof of Lemma 10.3 (the paragraph beginning with the reduction to maps of perfectoid rings). Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 78. The statement is proved inside the proof of Lemma 10.3 and used implicitly in Proposition 8.10; it is stated here as its own theorem (routed item PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22/111)..

## PR.1. Relative sites and the basic comparisons

For a bounded base prism (A,I), the relative affine site consists of bounded prisms over it with a map R→B/J, with the arrows reversed for the site. The topology is generated by finite families whose product is completely faithfully flat; its complete-flat condition includes Tor vanishing. The empty family covers the zero prism. The structure sheaf, its Frobenius and its completed base change lead to the smooth crystalline and Hodge–Tate comparisons. Hyperdescent is a separate theorem. The de Rham comparison here retains the p-torsion-freeness of W(A/I); PR.3 proves the general version through the Frobenius factorization.
