<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-1-prismatic-structure-sheaf"></a>

### The site of all bounded prisms and its structure sheaves

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/prismatic-structure-sheaf` · construction. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.Site` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/Site/Basic`.

Let Prism_bdd be the category of bounded prisms (B,J) and maps of prisms. A map (B,J) → (C,JC) is a flat cover when C is (p,J)-completely faithfully flat over B. (1) The opposite category Prism_bdd^op, with the flat topology: the Grothendieck topology generated by the finite families {(B,J) -> (C_s,JC_s)}_{s in S} of maps of bounded prisms for which B -> prod_s C_s is (p,J)-completely faithfully flat (Bhatt-Lurie Remarks 4.1.2 and 4.4.28; S may be empty, covering the zero prism; one flat cover is the case |S|=1), is a site: isomorphisms are covers, covers compose, and a cover (A,I) → (B,IB) has a pushout along every map (A,I) → (C,IC) of bounded prisms, namely (D,ID) with D the derived (p,I)-completion of B ⊗^L_A C, and (C,IC) → (D,ID) is again a flat cover. (2) The presheaves O : (B,J) ↦ B and Ō : (B,J) ↦ B/J are sheaves. (3) For a flat cover (A,I) → (B,IB) with Čech nerve (B^•,IB^•) in bounded prisms (B^n is the derived (p,I)-completion of the (n+1)-fold derived tensor power of B over A, and is discrete), the augmented cosimplicial objects A → B^• and A/I → B^•/IB^• are limit diagrams in D(A); so the Čech complex of O (and of Ō) for every flat cover is exact in positive degrees, and H^i((A,I),O) = H^i((A,I),Ō) = 0 for i > 0 on every object.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** Every object is a bounded prism: A/I has bounded p^∞-torsion. Without boundedness the completed pushout need not be discrete, and the statement is not made. Complete (faithful) flatness is taken in the sense of Bhatt–Scholze §1.2: M ⊗^L_A N is concentrated in degree 0 for every (p,I)-torsion module N (and M ⊗^L_A A/(p,I) is faithfully flat over A/(p,I)). Covers are in addition derived (p,I)-complete, which is automatic for prisms (register entry PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22/E10 adds the word 'complete' to Lemma 3.7). Variance: morphisms of the site go opposite to ring maps; the final object of a slice (∗/A)_Δ is (A,I). Set theory: the category of all bounded prisms is large; a cut-off cardinal κ is fixed as in Anschütz–Le Bras Remark 3.1.2, and no statement depends on κ.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Site axioms (Corollary 3.12, first paragraph). Isomorphisms and composites are immediate. For the pushout, rigidity (PR.0/rigidity-prism-ideal) reduces to a diagram (C,IC) ← (A,I) → (B,IB) with A → B a cover; put D = (B ⊗^L_A C)^∧. Complete faithful flatness is stable under completed base change (requested from DD.1; the source leaves this stability argument implicit), so D is (p,I)-completely faithfully flat over C.
2. By PR.0/bounded-prism-complete-flatness (Lemma 3.7 (2),(3)), D is discrete, classically (p,I)-complete and I-torsion-free with D/ID of bounded p^∞-torsion; its δ-structure is the one of the completed pushout of δ-rings (PR.0/delta-ring-category, PR.0/animated-delta-rings). So (D,ID) is a bounded prism and one checks the universal property of the pushout in bounded prisms.
3. Sheaf axiom and acyclicity (second paragraph). The Čech nerve B^• in bounded prisms is the termwise derived (p,I)-completion of the derived Čech nerve of A → B. For each n, Kos(A;p^n,I^n) → Kos(B^•;p^n,I^n) is a limit diagram in D(A) by faithfully flat descent for maps of animated rings (the source cites it without proof; requested from DD.1 as completed faithfully flat descent). Passing to the limit over n gives A ≃ lim B^• in D(A).
4. Tensoring A ≃ lim B^• with the perfect complex A/I (I is invertible) gives A/I ≃ lim B^•/IB^•, hence the statements for Ō.
5. A presheaf of modules whose Čech complex is exact for every cover of every object has vanishing higher cohomology on every object (Cartan's criterion; requested from E2 in the form needed for a site with fibre products).

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/prism`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-prism); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/prism-category`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-prism-category); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/rigidity-prism-ideal`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-rigidity-prism-ideal); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/bounded-prism-complete-flatness`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-bounded-prism-complete-flatness); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-ring-category`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-delta-ring-category); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/animated-delta-rings`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-animated-delta-rings); `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`; `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E2`; [`mathlib:CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology`](#mathlib-categorytheory-grothendiecktopology); [`mathlib:CategoryTheory.Presheaf.IsSheaf`](#mathlib-categorytheory-presheaf-issheaf).

**Consumers.** Bhatt–Scholze Definition 4.1: the relative site (X/A)_Δ is a slice of this site and inherits the site axioms and the two sheaves. Bhatt–Scholze Construction 4.18: the vanishing of higher cohomology on every object makes the Čech–Alexander complex compute Δ_{R/A}. Bhatt–Scholze Proposition 3.13, proof: descent of completely flat modules along the cover of Lemma 3.7 (4) reduces envelopes to orientable prisms. PrismaticCohomology:PR.5 (absolute prismatic site): the absolute site X_Δ is the slice of this site over the sheaf h_X. PrismaticCohomology:PR.7 (prismatic crystals): crystals are defined on this site and descend along flat covers.

- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Site.BoundedPrism` (structure): The type of bounded prisms (B,J), a category in which a morphism (C,K) → (B,J) is a map of prisms (B,J) → (C,K); so it is the site category Prism_bdd^op.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Site.IsFlatCover` (characterisation): A map of prisms f : (B,J) → (C,JC) is a flat cover iff C is (p,J)-completely faithfully flat over B; in particular B/(p,J) → C/(p,J) is faithfully flat.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Site.BoundedPrism.flatTopology` (structure): The Grothendieck topology on Prism_bdd^op generated by the finite families {(B,J) → (C_s,JC_s)} with B → ∏_s C_s (p,J)-completely faithfully flat; every flat cover generates a covering sieve, the projections of a finite product of bounded prisms generate a covering sieve, and the empty sieve covers the zero prism.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Site.BoundedPrism.pushout` (constructor): For a flat cover (A,I) → (B,IB) and a map (A,I) → (C,IC), the bounded prism (D,ID), D = (B ⊗^L_A C)^∧, the pushout in bounded prisms; (C,IC) → (D,ID) is a flat cover.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Site.BoundedPrism.structurePresheaf` (data): O : (B,J) ↦ B, a presheaf of commutative rings on the site.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Site.BoundedPrism.reducedStructurePresheaf` (data): Ō : (B,J) ↦ B/J, a presheaf of commutative rings on the site, with the reduction map O → Ō.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Site.BoundedPrism.structurePresheaf_isSheaf` (characterisation): O and Ō are sheaves for the flat topology.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Site.BoundedPrism.cechComplex` (data): For a map f : (A,I) → (B,IB) of bounded prisms, the Čech complex B → B^1 → B^2 → … of A-modules, B^n the completed (n+1)-fold tensor power.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Site.BoundedPrism.cechComplex_exact` (other): If f is a flat cover the Čech complex is exact in positive degrees and its H^0 is A; the same holds after − ⊗_A A/I.

**Unit tests.**

- `pr1_structure_presheaf_obj` (computation): O(B,J) = B and Ō(B,J) = B/J for every bounded prism (B,J).
- `pr1_flat_cover_id` (degenerate): The identity of a bounded prism is a flat cover, and the Čech complex of the identity cover has H^0 = B and no higher cohomology.
- `pr1_flat_cover_base_change` (characterisation): For a flat cover (A,I) → (B,IB) and any map (A,I) → (C,IC) of bounded prisms, the projection from the pushout (C,IC) → (D,ID) is a flat cover.
- `pr1_non_flat_not_cover` (non-example): The map of crystalline prisms (Z_p⟨x⟩,(p)) → (Z_p,(p)), x ↦ 0 (with φ(x) = x^p), is not a flat cover, because F_p[x] → F_p is not flat; in general a map of bounded prisms whose reduction modulo (p,J) is not flat is not a cover.
- `pr1_product_projection_family_covers` (non-example): For two nonzero bounded prisms, the two projection maps from their product are jointly completely faithfully flat, so their arrows generate a covering sieve. Neither projection by itself is faithfully flat; a topology defined by a single cover in each covering sieve fails this test.
- `pr1_empty_cover_zero_prism` (degenerate): The empty family covers the zero prism, hence its empty sieve is covering. Every sheaf of rings takes the zero prism to the one-element ring.

**Acceptance.** For (A,I) = (Z_p,(p)) and the cover Z_p → W(F̄_p), the Čech complex W(F̄_p) → W(F̄_p ⊗ F̄_p) → … is exact in positive degrees with H^0 = Z_p. The variance of the opposite category and the explicit structure maps of O and Ō are checked on a composite of two covers. Ordinary site cohomology of a singular X is not identified here with the derived theory of PR.2.

**Sources.** [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Corollary 3.12 and its proof. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 33. <a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-1-relative-frobenius-cosimplicial-lemma"></a>

### The relative Frobenius of a polynomial Čech nerve is a cosimplicial quasi-isomorphism on modules

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/relative-frobenius-cosimplicial-lemma` · lemma. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.Crystalline` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/Crystalline/Comparison`.

Let k be a commutative ring of characteristic p, B a polynomial k-algebra (in any set of variables), B^• the Čech nerve of k → B (B^n = B^{⊗_k (n+1)}), and B^{•,(1)} := B^• ⊗_{k,Frob} k its Frobenius twist, with the relative Frobenius B^{•,(1)} → B^•, a map of cosimplicial k-algebras. For every cosimplicial B^{•,(1)}-module N the natural map N → N ⊗_{B^{•,(1)}} B^• induces a quasi-isomorphism on the associated unnormalised cochain complexes of k-modules.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** k is a ring with p = 0; B is a polynomial k-algebra; no finiteness on the number of variables. N is a cosimplicial module over the cosimplicial ring B^{•,(1)}; the tensor product is termwise. In the proof the displayed decomposition of the monoid M = N^r reads ⊔_{s ∈ S} (pM + s) = M with S = {0,…,p−1}^r; the printed index set is M (source issue PrismaticCohomology/E11).

**Construction or proof.**

1. Filtered colimits reduce to finitely many variables: B = k[M], M = N^r. The Čech nerve is k[EM] for the cosimplicial monoid EM, [n] ↦ M^{[n]}, and B^{•,(1)} → B^• is k[E(pM)] → k[EM].
2. With S = {0,…,p−1}^r, the subsets S^{[n]} ⊂ M^{[n]} are preserved by the coface maps (they only insert 0), so ES ⊂ EM is a semi-cosimplicial subset and k[E(pM)] ⊗_k k[ES] ≅ k[EM] as semi-cosimplicial k[E(pM)]-modules; the unit corresponds to id ⊗ η with η : k → k[ES] induced by 0 ∈ S.
3. The unnormalised complex depends only on the semi-cosimplicial structure, so it suffices that id_N ⊗ η : N → N ⊗_k k[ES] is a quasi-isomorphism.
4. k[ES] is the semi-cosimplicial module underlying the Čech nerve C^• of k → k[M^{grp}/pM^{grp}], and η underlies its unit, which is a cosimplicial homotopy equivalence because the algebra map has a section; homotopy equivalences of cosimplicial k-modules are preserved by N ⊗_k −.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`mathlib:AlgebraicTopology.alternatingCofaceMapComplex`](#mathlib-algebraictopology-alternatingcofacemapcomplex); [`mathlib:MvPolynomial`](#mathlib-mvpolynomial).

**Acceptance.** For B = k (no variables) the map is the identity. For B = k[x] and N = B^{•,(1)} the lemma says that k[x^p]-type Čech complex and the Čech complex of k → k[x] are quasi-isomorphic; both are resolutions of k. The decomposition k[E(pM)] ⊗_k k[ES] ≅ k[EM] is an isomorphism of semi-cosimplicial modules only: codegeneracies do not preserve S (p = 2, r = 1: (1,1) ↦ 2 ∉ S).

**Sources.** [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Lemma 5.4 and its proof. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 48. The node is Lemma 5.4..

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-1-perfect-prism-initial"></a>

### A perfect prism is initial among prisms over its reduction

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/perfect-prism-initial` · lemma. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.Site` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/Site/Basic`.

Let (A,I) be a perfect prism with associated perfectoid ring R = A/I. For every prism (B,J), every ring map A/I → B/J lifts uniquely to a map of prisms (A,I) → (B,J). Equivalently, the category of prisms (B,J) with a map R → B/J is the category of prisms under (A,I): (R)_Δ = (R/A)_Δ, with (A,I) as initial object in the algebraic language. The converse fails: for a prism (A,I) and a perfect prism (B,J) there may be several maps (A,I) → (B,J) inducing the same map A/I → B/J.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** (A,I) is a perfect prism, so A = W(A/p) with A/p perfect, and A/I is a perfectoid ring (PR.0/perfect-prisms-perfectoid-rings). (B,J) is an arbitrary prism, not necessarily bounded; B may have p-torsion, so compatibility with Frobenius lifts does not by itself give a δ-map. The absolute prismatic site (R)_Δ as a site is defined in PrismaticCohomology:PR.5; the statement here is about maps of prisms only.

**Construction or proof.**

1. The p-completed cotangent complex of A over Z_p vanishes because A = W(perfect ring) (DD.0), and B is derived (p,J)-complete (it is a prism) while B/J is derived p-complete; by deformation theory along the (p,J)-adic tower Hom(A,B) ≃ Hom(A,B/J) ≃ Hom(A,B/(J,p)). So A → A/I → B/J lifts uniquely to a ring map α : A → B, compatible with the Frobenius lifts, and α(I) ⊂ J.
2. α is a δ-map: since φ_A is bijective, α factors uniquely through B^{perf} := lim_φ B; B^{perf} is a perfect δ-ring, hence p-torsion-free (PR.0/perfect-delta-rings, Lemma 2.28), so the φ-equivariant map A → B^{perf} is a δ-map, and B^{perf} → B is a δ-map.
3. Uniqueness as a map of prisms follows from uniqueness as a ring map.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/perfect-prisms-perfectoid-rings`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-perfect-prisms-perfectoid-rings); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/perfect-delta-rings`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-perfect-delta-rings); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/prism-category`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-prism-category); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-ring-category`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-delta-ring-category); `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.0`; `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`.

**Acceptance.** (A,I) = (Z_p,(p)): every prism (B,J) with p ∈ J, that is every crystalline prism, receives exactly one map from (Z_p,(p)). (A,I) = (A_inf, ker θ): a ring map O_C → B/J determines the map A_inf → B. Failure of the converse: for the Breuil–Kisin prism (Z_p[[u]],(u − p)) and the perfect prism (A_inf(O_C), ker θ), the maps u ↦ [p^♭] attached to the different compatible systems p^♭ of p-power roots of p are distinct maps of prisms inducing the same map Z_p → O_C.

**Sources.** [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Lemma 4.8 (in Remark 4.7) and its proof. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 38. The node is Lemma 4.8 with the remark following its proof..

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-1-relative-prismatic-site"></a>

### The relative prismatic site (X/A)_Δ

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/relative-prismatic-site` · definition. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.Site` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/Site/Basic`.

Fix a bounded prism (A,I) and a p-adic formal scheme X over Spf(A/I). The prismatic site (X/A)_Δ has as objects the triples (B, g, f): a bounded prism (B,IB) with a map of prisms g : (A,I) → (B,IB), and a map f : Spf(B/IB) → X over Spf(A/I). A morphism (C,g',f') → (B,g,f) is a map of prisms (B,IB) → (C,IC) under (A,I) whose reduction Spf(C/IC) → Spf(B/IB) commutes with the maps to X. It is a flat cover when (B,IB) → (C,IC) is a faithfully flat map of prisms. The topology is the flat topology generated by the finite families {(B,g,f) ← (C_s,g_s,f_s)} with B → ∏_s C_s (p,I)-completely faithfully flat (Bhatt–Lurie, Remark 4.1.2). The structure sheaf O_Δ : (B,g,f) ↦ B is a sheaf of δ-A-algebras; the reduced structure sheaf Ō_Δ : (B,g,f) ↦ B/IB is a sheaf of O(X)-algebras, and Ō_Δ = O_Δ ⊗_A A/I. For X = Spf(R) one writes (R/A)_Δ, with objects (B → B/IB ← R). Equivalently, with (∗/A)_Δ the slice of the site of all bounded prisms over (A,I) and h_X the presheaf (B,IB) ↦ Hom_{A/I}(Spf(B/IB), X) on it, h_X is a sheaf and (X/A)_Δ is the category of pairs ((B,IB), η ∈ h_X(B,IB)) with the induced topology, so Shv((X/A)_Δ) = Shv((∗/A)_Δ)_{/h_X}. A map X → Y of p-adic formal schemes over A/I induces h_X → h_Y and hence a morphism of topoi Shv((X/A)_Δ) → Shv((Y/A)_Δ).

**Hypotheses and conventions.** (A,I) is a bounded prism; formal schemes over A/I carry the p-adic topology. The definition is made for every p-adic formal scheme X over A/I; the comparison theorems of this stage assume X smooth over A/I (Remark 4.2), and for general X the cohomology of this site is not the derived theory of PR.2. By rigidity (PR.0/rigidity-prism-ideal) the prism ideal of every object is IB, so only B, g and f are data. In the affine case the algebraic language of Notation 4.16 is used: an object mapping to every other object of (R/A)_Δ, viewed as rings, is called weakly initial (it is weakly final in the site). The text of Notation 4.16 is read with the corrections of register entry PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22/E12 (R = A/I; Spf in place of Spec).

**Construction or proof.**

1. Definition 4.1: the objects, morphisms and covers are as stated; the site axioms and the sheaf property of O_Δ and Ō_Δ are inherited from the site of all bounded prisms (PR.1/prismatic-structure-sheaf), because pushouts of objects of (X/A)_Δ along covers are computed on underlying prisms and carry the induced map to X.
2. Remark 4.3: h_X is a sheaf on (∗/A)_Δ. For a flat cover (B,IB) → (C,IC) with Čech nerve C^•, B/IB → C^•/IC^• is a limit diagram of p-complete rings by the reduced form of Corollary 3.12, and maps of formal schemes Spf(−) → X glue along p-completely faithfully flat covers (fpqc descent for morphisms, on the reductions modulo p^n; requested from SF.4).
3. The identification of (X/A)_Δ with the category of elements of h_X is a direct unwinding; Shv of a category of elements of a sheaf is the slice topos (requested from E2 with the localisation of a topos at an object).
4. Functoriality: X → Y gives h_X → h_Y and the morphism of slice topoi; for X = Spf(R), Y = Spf(R') and R' → R the functor (R/A)_Δ → (R'/A)_Δ composes the structure map with R' → R.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/prismatic-structure-sheaf`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-prismatic-structure-sheaf); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/prism-category`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-prism-category); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/rigidity-prism-ideal`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-rigidity-prism-ideal); `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.4`; `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E2`; [`mathlib:CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.over`](#mathlib-categorytheory-grothendiecktopology-over); [`mathlib:CategoryTheory.Presheaf.IsSheaf`](#mathlib-categorytheory-presheaf-issheaf).

**Consumers.** Bhatt–Scholze Construction 4.4 and 4.9: Δ_{X/A} and Δ̄_{X/A} are the derived pushforwards of O_Δ and Ō_Δ to X_ét. Bhatt–Scholze Constructions 4.17–4.18: weakly initial objects and their Čech nerves in (R/A)_Δ compute the cohomology. Bhatt–Scholze Lemma 4.21: the functor (R/A)_Δ → (S/A)_Δ for a p-completely étale R → S and its right adjoint restriction of scalars. PerfectoidQuotients:Q1: imports the site and its comparison theorems as its compatibility export. PrismaticCohomology:PR.2 (Lemma 7.7, Proposition 7.10): for a quasiregular semiperfectoid S the site (S/A)_Δ has an initial object, the prism Δ_S. PrismaticCohomology:PR.5: the absolute site of X and its comparison with the relative sites over a base prism.

**Planning API.**

- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Site.RelativePrism` (structure): An object of (R/A)_Δ: a bounded prism (B,J), a map of prisms g : (A,I) → (B,J) and a ring map R → B/J compatible with A/I → B/J; morphisms are taken in the site direction (ring maps go backwards).
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Site.RelativePrism.ideal_eq_map` (compatibility): For every object, J = IB (rigidity of the prism ideal).
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Site.RelativePrism.flatTopology` (structure): The Grothendieck topology on (R/A)_Δ generated by flat covers; a morphism whose underlying map of prisms is a flat cover generates a covering sieve.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Site.RelativePrism.structureSheaf` (data): O_Δ : (B,g,f) ↦ B as a presheaf of commutative rings, with O_Δ(B) an A-algebra through g.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Site.RelativePrism.reducedStructureSheaf` (data): Ō_Δ : (B,g,f) ↦ B/IB as a presheaf of commutative rings, with Ō_Δ(B) an R-algebra through f.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Site.RelativePrism.structureSheaf_isSheaf` (characterisation): O_Δ and Ō_Δ are sheaves for the flat topology.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Site.RelativePrism.forget` (functoriality): The category-of-elements projection (R/A)_Δ→(∗/A)_Δ forgets only the map f:R→B/IB and retains the base-prism map g:(A,I)→(B,IB). Its composite with (∗/A)_Δ→Prism_bdd^op also forgets g. Both preserve covering families.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Site.RelativePrism.restrict` (functoriality): For an A/I-algebra map R → S, the functor (S/A)_Δ → (R/A)_Δ, (B, S → B/IB) ↦ (B, R → S → B/IB); it preserves covers and commutes with O_Δ and Ō_Δ.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Site.RelativePrism.base` (example): For R = A/I, the object (A, id, id) of ((A/I)/A)_Δ; it is final in the site (initial in the algebraic language).

**Unit tests.**

- `pr1_relative_site_base_terminal` (degenerate): For R = A/I the object (A, id, id) is a final object of the site ((A/I)/A)_Δ.
- `pr1_relative_site_sheaf_obj` (computation): O_Δ(B,g,f) = B and Ō_Δ(B,g,f) = B/IB.
- `pr1_relative_site_ideal_rigid` (non-example): A δ-A-algebra B with an ideal J strictly containing IB such that (B,J) is a prism receiving a map of prisms from (A,I) does not exist: for every map of prisms (A,I) → (B,J) one has J = IB.
- `pr1_relative_site_restrict_id` (compatibility): Restriction along the identity R → R is the identity functor of (R/A)_Δ, and restriction is compatible with the forgetful functors to Prism_bdd^op.

**Acceptance.** For X = Spf(A/I) the site is the slice (∗/A)_Δ of all bounded prisms over (A,I), with final object (A,I). For a perfect prism (A,I) and X = Spf(A/I⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩) the object given by the perfect prism of the perfectoid ring A/I⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ lies in the site. A triple with prism ideal J ≠ IB does not occur, by rigidity.

**Sources.** [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Definition 4.1. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 36. The node is Definition 4.1 with morphisms and variance written out.. [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Remark 4.3. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 37. The slice description and the functoriality in X are Remark 4.3.. [ALB23](https://arxiv.org/abs/1907.10525v4), Definition 3.1.1. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 16.
