<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-1-prismatic-to-etale-morphism"></a>

### The morphism from the prismatic topos to the étale topos

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/prismatic-to-etale-morphism` · comparison. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.Site` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/Site/Basic`.

Let X be a smooth p-adic formal scheme over A/I and let fSch_{/X} be the category of p-adic formal schemes with an adic map to X, with the étale topology. The functor μ : (X/A)_Δ → fSch_{/X}, (B,g,f) ↦ (Spf(B/IB) → X), is cocontinuous. It therefore induces a morphism of topoi μ_X : Shv((X/A)_Δ) → Shv(fSch_{/X}); composing with the restriction Shv(fSch_{/X}) → Shv(X_ét) gives ν_X : Shv((X/A)_Δ) → Shv(X_ét). For an étale map U → X the site (U/A)_Δ is the slice of (X/A)_Δ over U, restriction to it preserves sheaves, and for every sheaf F on (X/A)_Δ one has (ν_* F)(U → X) = H^0((U/A)_Δ, F|_{(U/A)_Δ}); for a sheaf of abelian groups, R^iν_*F is the sheafification of U ↦ H^i((U/A)_Δ, F).

**Hypotheses and conventions.** X is a smooth p-adic formal scheme over A/I (the construction only uses that X is a p-adic formal scheme; smoothness is the standing hypothesis of §4.1). The étale site of a p-adic formal scheme is that of its reduction modulo p; it is requested from SF.2. μ is cocontinuous, not continuous: only the pushforward ν_* and its derived functors are used.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Cocontinuity (Construction 4.4). Given an object (B,g,f) and an étale cover of Spf(B/IB), refine it to a p-completely étale cover B/IB → C̄. By Bhatt–Scholze Lemma 2.18 (étale extension of δ-structures, with Elkik algebraization; stage PR.0 and DD.1) there is a unique (p,I)-completely étale δ-B-algebra C with C/IC = C̄; each (C_i,IC_i) is a bounded prism by PR.0/bounded-prism-complete-flatness, and the finite family {(B,IB) → (C_i,IC_i)} is a covering family of the flat topology (B → ∏ C_i is completely faithfully flat) lying in the pulled-back sieve.
2. A cocontinuous functor of sites induces a morphism of topoi whose pushforward is the right Kan extension (Stacks, Tag 00XO; in Mathlib the pushforward of a cocontinuous functor).
3. For étale U → X the objects of (X/A)_Δ whose map to X factors through U form the slice over the sheaf h_U, which is (U/A)_Δ; the formula for ν_* is the right Kan extension formula evaluated on U, and the description of R^iν_* follows by sheafifying.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/relative-prismatic-site`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-relative-prismatic-site); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/bounded-prism-complete-flatness`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-bounded-prism-complete-flatness); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-etale-extension`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-delta-etale-extension); `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`; `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2`; `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.4`; [`mathlib:CategoryTheory.Functor.IsCocontinuous`](#mathlib-categorytheory-functor-iscocontinuous); [`mathlib:CategoryTheory.Functor.sheafPushforwardCocontinuous`](#mathlib-categorytheory-functor-sheafpushforwardcocontinuous); [`mathlib:Algebra.Etale`](#mathlib-algebra-etale).

**Consumers.** Bhatt–Scholze Construction 4.9: Δ_{X/A} = Rν_*O_Δ and Δ̄_{X/A} = Rν_*Ō_Δ. Bhatt–Scholze Theorems 6.3 and 6.4: the comparison theorems are statements about sheaves on X_ét and are proved on affines. PrismaticCohomology:PR.4 (Theorem 9.1): the étale comparison is formulated on X_ét through ν.

**Acceptance.** For X = Spf(R) and a p-completely étale R → S, (ν_*O_Δ)(Spf S) = H^0((S/A)_Δ, O_Δ). For U = X the formula gives ν_*F(X) = H^0((X/A)_Δ, F), the global sections. The lift of a Zariski cover Spf(R_f) of Spf(B/IB) is the (p,I)-completed localisation of B at a lift of f, with its unique δ-structure.

**Sources.** [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Construction 4.4. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 37. The node is Construction 4.4.. [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Construction 4.4. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 37. Cocontinuity is deduced there from Lemma 2.18..

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-1-change-of-topology"></a>

### Flat, étale, Nisnevich and Zariski topologies compute the same cohomology

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/change-of-topology` · comparison. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.Site` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/Site/Basic`.

On the category underlying (X/A)_Δ consider the topologies whose covers are the maps of prisms (B,IB) → (C,IC) that are (p,I)-completely étale covers, Nisnevich covers or Zariski covers. There are morphisms of topoi Shv((X/A)_Δ) → Shv((X/A)_{Δ,ét}) → Shv((X/A)_{Δ,Nis}) → Shv((X/A)_{Δ,Zar}), and the derived pushforward along each of them carries O_Δ to O_Δ and Ō_Δ to Ō_Δ. Hence RΓ((X/A)_Δ, O_Δ) and RΓ((X/A)_Δ, Ō_Δ) may be computed in any of the four topologies. The same holds for coefficients in a crystal in (p,I)-complete complexes, that is an assignment (B,g,f) ↦ M(B) ∈ D_{(p,I)-comp}(B) compatible with completed base change.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** (A,I) is bounded and X is a p-adic formal scheme over A/I. Zariski, Nisnevich and étale covers of Spf(B) lift uniquely to (p,I)-completely étale δ-B-algebras, so each of these topologies is coarser than the flat topology. Only the two structure sheaves and crystals are compared; arbitrary sheaves on the four sites have different cohomology.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Each of the coarser topologies has covers that are flat covers, so the identity functor is a continuous morphism of sites and induces the displayed morphisms of topoi (Remark 4.5).
2. For the derived pushforward ε_* from the flat to a coarser topology, R^iε_*O_Δ is the sheafification of (B,g,f) ↦ H^i((B,g,f), O_Δ) in the flat topology of the slice, and this slice is a slice of the site of all bounded prisms; by PR.1/prismatic-structure-sheaf (3) these groups vanish for i > 0 and equal B for i = 0. The same argument applies to Ō_Δ.
3. For crystals one uses (p,I)-completely faithfully flat descent for D_{(p,I)-comp}(−) (requested from DD.1) in place of Corollary 3.12.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/prismatic-structure-sheaf`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-prismatic-structure-sheaf); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/relative-prismatic-site`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-relative-prismatic-site); `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`; `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E2`.

**Consumers.** Bhatt–Scholze Remark 4.5: justifies the choice of the flat topology while keeping étale-local computations. PrismaticCohomology:PR.7: crystals do not depend on the topology.

**Acceptance.** For R = A/I the cohomology of O_Δ in the Zariski topology of ((A/I)/A)_Δ is A in degree 0. The étale-topology version is the one used when a statement is checked on an étale chart of X.

**Sources.** [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Remark 4.5. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 37. The node is Remark 4.5..

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-1-cech-alexander-complex"></a>

### Weakly initial objects and Čech–Alexander complexes

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/cech-alexander-complex` · construction. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.Site` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/Site/Basic`.

Let (A,I) be a bounded prism and R a p-completely smooth A/I-algebra. A presentation is a surjection B_0 → R of A-algebras with B_0 the (p,I)-completion of a polynomial A-algebra A[x_s : s ∈ S]. Put B := Free_{δ,A}(B_0)^∧, the (p,I)-completed free δ-A-algebra on B_0; J_0 := ker(B_0 → R); R′ := (B/J_0B)^∧ (p-adic completion), a p-completely ind-smooth A/I-algebra; and C := B{J/I}^∧, the prismatic envelope over (A,I) of the δ-pair (B, J), J = ker(B → R′). Then (C → C/IC ← R) is an object of (R/A)_Δ, C is (p,I)-completely flat over A, and the object is weakly initial: it admits a map to every object of (R/A)_Δ (in the algebraic language). The construction is functorial in the presentation and carries completed tensor products of presentations over A to coproducts in (R/A)_Δ (algebraic language; products in the site). The Čech–Alexander cosimplicial object of the presentation is (C^• → C^•/IC^• ← R), obtained by applying the construction to the (p,I)-completed Čech nerve B_0^• of A → B_0 with its surjections B_0^n → R; it is the Čech nerve of (C^0 → C^0/IC^0 ← R), and C^n is the envelope of the completed (n+1)-fold tensor power of B over A along the kernel of the map to R′-type quotients. Taking B_0 = A[x_r : r ∈ R]^∧ with x_r ↦ r gives a strictly functorial cosimplicial δ-A-algebra C^•_R and cochain complex C^•((R/A)_Δ, O_Δ); this functorial choice does not commute with base change in the prism. For R = A/I⟨X_1,…,X_n⟩ the choice B_0 = A⟨X_1,…,X_n⟩ gives a cosimplicial δ-A-algebra that commutes with base change along every map of bounded prisms.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** (A,I) is a bounded prism; R is p-completely smooth over A/I. The same construction applies verbatim to a p-completely syntomic A/I-algebra, because the hypothesis of the envelope theorem still holds (Anschütz–Le Bras Remark 3.1.8). Proposition 3.13 is stated for an ideal that is Zariski-locally (I, x_1,…,x_r) with a finite sequence completely regular relative to A. For a presentation with finitely many variables this is Example 3.14. For infinitely many variables (in particular the functorial choice S = R) the ideal J is a filtered union of such ideals, and the envelope exists and is completely flat as the completed filtered colimit of the envelopes; this step is not in the printed text and is recorded as source issue PrismaticCohomology/E12. Derived and classical (p,I)-completions of B_0, B and of the tensor powers agree because A is bounded (Lemma 3.7).

**Construction or proof.**

1. Envelope. For a finite set S' ⊂ S with A[x_s : s ∈ S']^∧ → R surjective, choose lifts f_s of the images of x_s for s ∉ S'. Then J_0 is generated by ker(A[x_{S'}]^∧ → R), which is Zariski-locally (I, a regular sequence relative to A) since R is p-completely smooth, and by the elements x_s − f_s. For finite S'' ⊃ S' the ideal J_{S''} ⊂ B generated by the first kernel and the x_s − f_s, s ∈ S'' \ S', satisfies the hypothesis of PR.0/regular-prismatic-envelopes (B is completely flat over A[x_{S''}]^∧). The envelope of (B,J) is the (p,I)-completed colimit of the envelopes B{J_{S''}/I}^∧; it has the universal property and is (p,I)-completely flat over A.
2. Object of the site: C/IC receives R′, hence R; (C,IC) is a bounded prism over (A,I) by PR.0/regular-prismatic-envelopes and PR.0/bounded-prism-complete-flatness.
3. Weak initiality (Construction 4.17). Given (D → D/ID ← R), lift R → D/ID to an A-algebra map B_0 → D, possible since B_0 is a completed polynomial algebra and D is (p,I)-complete; extend uniquely to a δ-A-algebra map B → D by the universal property of free δ-rings (PR.0/free-delta-ring); it carries J into ID, so it factors uniquely through C by the universal property of the envelope; the induced map on reductions is compatible with the maps from R.
4. Coproducts and Čech nerve: the universal properties of Free_δ and of the envelope show that the construction sends B_0 ⊗̂_A B_0' (with the induced surjection to R) to the coproduct; hence applying it to the Čech nerve of A → B_0 gives the Čech nerve of the object C^0.
5. Functorial choice and Remark 4.19: for S = R the assignment R ↦ (B_0 → R) is functorial; for the completed polynomial ring the presentation A⟨X⟩ → A/I⟨X⟩ is compatible with base change, and so is the envelope by PR.0/regular-prismatic-envelopes (2).

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/relative-prismatic-site`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-relative-prismatic-site); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/regular-prismatic-envelopes`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-regular-prismatic-envelopes); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/free-delta-ring`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-free-delta-ring); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/bounded-prism-complete-flatness`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-bounded-prism-complete-flatness); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-ring-category`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-delta-ring-category); `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`; [`mathlib:MvPolynomial`](#mathlib-mvpolynomial); [`mathlib:AlgebraicTopology.alternatingCofaceMapComplex`](#mathlib-algebraictopology-alternatingcofacemapcomplex).

**Consumers.** Bhatt–Scholze Lemma 4.20: termwise base change of the complex computes Δ of the base-changed algebra. Bhatt–Scholze Lemma 4.21: the image of the complex under the étale-lifting functor computes Δ̄ of an étale algebra. Bhatt–Scholze Theorem 5.2, proof: φ_A^*C^• is compared with the cosimplicial PD envelope D^• computing crystalline cohomology. Bhatt–Scholze Proposition 6.2, proof: the base-change-compatible complex of the affine line reduces the Hodge–Tate comparison to Z_p. Anschütz–Le Bras Lemma 5.1.6: H^0 of the site is a subring of the p-torsion-free ring C^0. PrismaticCohomology:PR.6 (Theorem 16.18): q-crystalline cohomology is computed by the analogous q-PD Čech–Alexander complex.

**Planning API.**

- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Site.weaklyInitial` (constructor): For a family g : S → R whose associated map A[x_s]^∧ → R is surjective, the object (C → C/IC ← R) of (R/A)_Δ with C the prismatic envelope described above.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Site.weaklyInitial_hom_nonempty` (characterisation): Every object of (R/A)_Δ receives a map from the weakly initial object in the algebraic language: for every object X there is a morphism X → weaklyInitial in the site.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Site.weaklyInitial_flat` (compatibility): The ring C is (p,I)-completely flat over A; in particular C/(p,I) is flat over A/(p,I).
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Site.cechAlexander` (data): The cosimplicial commutative ring C^• of a presentation; C^0 is the ring of the weakly initial object and C^n the ring of its (n+1)-fold self-coproduct.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Site.cechAlexander_obj_zero` (simp): C^0 is the ring underlying weaklyInitial.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Site.cechAlexanderComplex` (data): The cochain complex of A-modules associated with C^• (alternating sums of cofaces), concentrated in degrees ≥ 0.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Site.cechAlexander_baseChange` (compatibility): For a map of bounded prisms (A,I) → (A′,IA′) and the base-changed presentation of R′ = R ⊗̂_A A′, the comparison map of cosimplicial rings C^• → C′^•; its termwise (p,I)-completed linearisation C^• ⊗̂_A A′ → C′^• is an isomorphism.

**Unit tests.**

- `pr1_cech_alexander_base` (degenerate): For R = A/I and the empty family of variables the weakly initial object is the final object (A, id, id) of the site, and C^• is constant with value A.
- `pr1_cech_alexander_affine_line` (computation): For R = A/I⟨X⟩ with the presentation A⟨X⟩ → R: C^0 = A{X}^∧ is the completed free δ-A-algebra on one generator, so maps of prisms over (A,I) from (C^0,IC^0) to a bounded prism (B,IB) over (A,I) correspond bijectively to elements of B; and C^1 = A{X,Y}{(X−Y)/I}^∧.
- `pr1_weakly_initial_not_initial` (non-example): If Ω^1_{R/(A/I)} ≠ 0 the two coface maps C^0 ⇉ C^1 are different; so the weakly initial object is not initial and Δ_{R/A} ≠ C^0.

**Acceptance.** For R = A/I and the empty set of variables, C^• is the constant cosimplicial ring A. For R = A/I⟨X⟩ and B_0 = A⟨X⟩: C^0 = A{X}^∧ and C^1 = A{X,Y}{(X−Y)/I}^∧. For a crystalline prism the same recipe with PD envelopes in place of prismatic envelopes computes crystalline cohomology, and the two are related by PR.0/pd-envelope-as-delta-envelope.

**Sources.** [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Construction 4.17. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 41. The weakly initial object and its functoriality are Construction 4.17.. [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Construction 4.18 and Remark 4.19. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed pages 42, 43. The cosimplicial object and the functorial choice are Construction 4.18; the base-change-compatible model for the affine line is Remark 4.19.. [ALB23](https://arxiv.org/abs/1907.10525v4), Remark 3.1.8 (2). Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 17. The kernel is an inductive limit of ideals to which Proposition 3.13 applies; this is the colimit step used for infinitely many variables..

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-1-prismatic-hyperdescent"></a>

### Prismatic hyperdescent

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/prismatic-hyperdescent` · theorem. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/PR1`.

On the flat site of bounded prisms, the assignments (B,J)↦B and (B,J)↦B/J, valued in the respective derived categories, satisfy hyperdescent. A flat hypercover of an object computes its derived sections by totalisation. The same holds on a relative prismatic site and after derived pushforward to the small étale site.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** Bounded prisms; finite jointly completely faithfully flat covering families; a universe cut-off is fixed. The statement uses derived totalisations, not an ordinary equalizer of rings.

**Construction or proof.**

1. The structure sheaves are acyclic on every object by prismatic-structure-sheaf; their derived-section values are therefore the indicated degree-zero rings.
2. The hyperdescent theorem for derived sections of a sheaf identifies the value on an object with totalisation over any hypercover. Equivalently, the nonnegative cohomological t-structure makes these derived-section sheaves hypercomplete.
3. Apply the same argument on the category of elements defining the relative site; derived pushforward preserves the relevant limits.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/prismatic-structure-sheaf`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-prismatic-structure-sheaf); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/relative-prismatic-site`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-relative-prismatic-site); `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E2`.

**Acceptance.** The Čech hypercover of a flat cover recovers Corollary 3.12. The zero prism has the empty covering family and zero derived module of sections.

**Sources.** [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Corollary 3.12 and Definition 4.1, §3–4. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed pages 33, 36. Acyclicity and passage to the relative site supply the input to derived hyperdescent..

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-1-relative-prismatic-cohomology"></a>

### Relative prismatic cohomology Δ_{X/A}

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/relative-prismatic-cohomology` · construction. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.Site` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/Site/Basic`.

For a bounded prism (A,I) and a smooth p-adic formal scheme X over A/I put Δ_{X/A} := Rν_*O_Δ ∈ D(X_ét, A) and RΓ_Δ(X/A) := RΓ((X/A)_Δ, O_Δ) = RΓ(X_ét, Δ_{X/A}) ∈ D(A). For a p-completely smooth A/I-algebra R put Δ_{R/A} := RΓ((R/A)_Δ, O_Δ) = RΓ(Spf(R), Δ_{Spf(R)/A}) ∈ D(A). These are commutative algebra objects (E_∞-A-algebras), derived (p,I)-complete, concentrated in cohomological degrees ≥ 0, and equipped with a φ_A-semilinear endomorphism (PR.1/frobenius-on-prismatic-cohomology). Functoriality: a map X → Y over A/I gives Δ_{Y/A} → Rf_*Δ_{X/A}; a map of bounded prisms (A,I) → (B,IB) with a compatible map of formal schemes gives a map from Δ_{X/A} to the restriction of scalars of Δ_{X'/B}; every object (B,g,f) of (R/A)_Δ gives an evaluation map Δ_{R/A} → B of E_∞-A-algebras, and Δ_{R/A} is the limit of O_Δ over a Čech–Alexander cosimplicial object (PR.1/cech-alexander-computes-cohomology).

**Hypotheses and conventions.** (A,I) is a bounded prism. X is a smooth p-adic formal scheme over A/I; R is a p-completely smooth A/I-algebra: R is derived p-complete and R ⊗^L_{A/I} (A/I)/p is a smooth (A/I)/p-algebra in degree 0. For other X the same formula defines site cohomology, which this stage uses only for p-completely syntomic algebras (PR.1/crystalline-comparison-syntomic, PR.1/p-torsion-free-h0-syntomic). The commutative algebra structure is in the derived ∞-category; in a 1-categorical derived category only the commutative ring structure on cohomology and the cosimplicial ring models are visible. Derived (p,I)-completeness follows because Δ_{R/A} is a limit of the (p,I)-complete rings B.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Definition: Construction 4.9 (first displayed formula) and Notation 4.16. O_Δ is a sheaf of rings on (X/A)_Δ (PR.1/relative-prismatic-site), so Rν_*O_Δ and RΓ are defined and are commutative algebra objects; RΓ(X_ét, Rν_*O_Δ) = RΓ((X/A)_Δ, O_Δ) by the Leray composition for the morphism of topoi ν (PR.1/prismatic-to-etale-morphism).
2. Coconnectivity is automatic for the cohomology of a sheaf of modules. Completeness: for f ∈ (p,I), RHom_A(A[1/f], RΓ(O_Δ)) = RΓ of the presheaf B ↦ RHom_A(A[1/f], RΓ(B,O)) = RHom_A(A[1/f], B) = 0, using the acyclicity of O on objects (PR.1/prismatic-structure-sheaf (3)) and derived completeness of each B (DD.1). The Frobenius is added by PR.1/frobenius-on-prismatic-cohomology.
3. Functoriality in X is the functoriality of the slice topoi (Remark 4.3); functoriality in the prism sends (C,g',f') over (B,IB) to itself viewed over (A,I); evaluation at an object is restriction of global sections.
4. The Frobenius comes from the endomorphism φ of the sheaf O_Δ (PR.1/frobenius-on-prismatic-cohomology).

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/relative-prismatic-site`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-relative-prismatic-site); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/prismatic-to-etale-morphism`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-prismatic-to-etale-morphism); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/prismatic-structure-sheaf`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-prismatic-structure-sheaf); `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`; `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E2`; `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2`; [`mathlib:DerivedCategory`](#mathlib-derivedcategory).

**Consumers.** Bhatt–Scholze Theorem 1.8: the object all comparison theorems are about. PrismaticCohomology:PR.2 (Construction 7.6): derived prismatic cohomology is the left Kan extension of R ↦ Δ_{R/A} from p-completely smooth (polynomial) algebras. PrismaticCohomology:PR.3 (§15): the relative Nygaard filtration lives on φ_A^*Δ_{R/A}. PrismaticCohomology:PR.6 (Theorems 16.18, 17.2): q-crystalline cohomology and AΩ are compared with Δ_{R/A} over the q-de Rham and A_inf prisms. AInfCohomology:AI.7: Breuil–Kisin cohomology is Δ_{X/A} over the Breuil–Kisin prism. RefinedTraceMethods:RT.6: the graded pieces of the motivic filtration are compared with Nygaard-completed Δ.

**Planning API.**

- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Site.cohomologyEval` (projection): For an object (B,g,f) of (R/A)_Δ, the evaluation map Δ_{R/A} → B in D(A) (B viewed as an A-module through g); it is natural in the object.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Site.cohomologyUnit` (data): The unit A → Δ_{R/A} of the algebra structure, as a map A[0] → Δ_{R/A} in D(A).
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Site.cohomologyMap` (functoriality): For a map R → S of A/I-algebras, the map Δ_{R/A} → Δ_{S/A} in D(A); cohomologyMap_id and cohomologyMap_comp express functoriality.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Site.cohomologyMap_id` (simp): The map induced by the identity of R is the identity of Δ_{R/A}.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Site.cohomologyMap_comp` (simp): The map induced by a composite R → S → T is the composite of the induced maps.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Site.cohomologyBaseChangeMap` (functoriality): For a map of bounded prisms f : (A,I) → (B,IB), a B/IB-algebra R′ and a compatible ring map R → R′, the map Δ_{R/A} → f_*Δ_{R′/B} in D(A).
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Site.cohomology_isZero_of_neg` (characterisation): H^i(Δ_{R/A}) = 0 for i < 0 when R is p-completely smooth over A/I.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Site.cohomologyCup` (structure): The derived tensor product Δ_(R/A)⊗^L_AΔ_(R/A)→Δ_(R/A), with the unit A→Δ_(R/A), gives a commutative algebra object; evaluation and maps in R respect multiplication and the unit. Hodge–Tate reduction carries this to its cup product.

**Unit tests.**

- `pr1_cohomology_base` (degenerate): For R = A/I the unit A → Δ_{(A/I)/A} is an isomorphism.
- `pr1_cohomology_unit_natural` (compatibility): For a map R → S of A/I-algebras, the composite of the unit A → Δ_{R/A} with Δ_{R/A} → Δ_{S/A} is the unit of Δ_{S/A}.
- `pr1_cohomology_base_degrees` (computation): For R = A/I, H^i(Δ_{(A/I)/A}) = 0 for every i ≠ 0.
- `pr1_cohomology_not_discrete` (non-example): If the p-completed module Ω̂^1_{R/(A/I)} ≠ 0 for a p-completely smooth R (for instance R = A/I⟨X⟩), then Δ_{R/A} is not concentrated in degree 0: H^1(Δ_{R/A} ⊗^L_A A/I) ≠ 0. So Δ_{R/A} is not the value of O_Δ on any single object.

**Acceptance.** Δ_{(A/I)/A} = A, with the identity Frobenius-semilinear structure φ_A. For R = A/I⟨X⟩ the complex Δ_{R/A} is not concentrated in degree 0: H^1(Δ_{R/A} ⊗^L_A A/I) ≅ Ω^1_{R/(A/I)}{−1} ≠ 0. For a crystalline prism (A,(p)) and R smooth over A/p, φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} ≅ RΓ_crys(R/A) (PR.1/crystalline-comparison).

**Sources.** [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Construction 4.9, first paragraph, and Notation 4.16. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed pages 39, 41. The node is the definition of Δ_{X/A} and Δ_{R/A} given there, with the functorialities of Remark 4.3 and Theorem 1.8.. [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Theorem 1.8, opening. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 4. The global object RΓ_Δ(X/A) and its Frobenius are introduced there.. [ALB23](https://arxiv.org/abs/1907.10525v4), Definition 3.1.5. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 16. Anschütz–Le Bras define Δ_{R/A} the same way and record (p,I)-completeness..

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-1-hodge-tate-cohomology"></a>

### Hodge–Tate cohomology Δ̄_{X/A} and Breuil–Kisin twists of A/I-modules

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/hodge-tate-cohomology` · construction. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.HodgeTate` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/HodgeTate/Basic`.

For (A,I) bounded and X smooth over A/I put Δ̄_{X/A} := Rν_*Ō_Δ ∈ D(X_ét, O_X), a commutative algebra object with structure map O_X → Δ̄_{X/A}, and for a p-completely smooth A/I-algebra R put Δ̄_{R/A} := RΓ((R/A)_Δ, Ō_Δ) ∈ D(R). Then Δ̄_{X/A} ≃ Δ_{X/A} ⊗^L_A A/I and Δ̄_{R/A} ≃ Δ_{R/A} ⊗^L_A A/I. For an A/I-module M and i ∈ Z put M{i} := M ⊗_{A/I} (I/I²)^{⊗i}, where I/I² is an invertible A/I-module and negative powers are powers of the dual; for i ≥ 0, M{i} = M ⊗_{A/I} I^i/I^{i+1}. A generator d of I identifies M{i} with M through d^i. For every i ≥ 0 there is a distinguished triangle Δ̄_{X/A}{i+1} → Δ_{X/A} ⊗^L_A I^i/I^{i+2} → Δ̄_{X/A}{i}.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** (A,I) is a bounded prism, X a smooth p-adic formal scheme over A/I, R a p-completely smooth A/I-algebra. The twist M{i} of this stage is the twist of A/I-modules of Bhatt–Scholze Construction 4.9. The Breuil–Kisin twists A{n} of the prism itself, with A{1}/I = I/I², belong to PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/breuil-kisin-twist and are not used here. The Hodge–Tate comparison carries the twist {−i} on Ω^i and no Frobenius twist.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Definition: Construction 4.9. Ō_Δ is a sheaf of O(X)-algebras, so Rν_*Ō_Δ is a commutative algebra object of D(X_ét, O_X).
2. The formula Δ̄ ≃ Δ ⊗^L_A A/I: on each object B/IB = B ⊗^L_A A/I because I ⊗_A B → B is injective with image IB (PR.0/rigidity-prism-ideal). Since A/I is a perfect A-complex (I is invertible), − ⊗^L_A A/I commutes with Rν_* and with RΓ.
3. The triangle is Δ_{X/A} ⊗^L_A applied to the exact sequence 0 → I^{i+1}/I^{i+2} → I^i/I^{i+2} → I^i/I^{i+1} → 0 of A-modules, using I^j/I^{j+1} = (I/I²)^{⊗j} and Δ ⊗^L_A I^j/I^{j+1} = Δ̄{j}.
4. Twists: I is an invertible A-module (PR.0/prism), so I/I² = I ⊗_A A/I is invertible over A/I and the tensor powers are defined for all integers.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/relative-prismatic-cohomology`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-relative-prismatic-cohomology); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/relative-prismatic-site`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-relative-prismatic-site); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/prism`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-prism); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/rigidity-prism-ideal`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-rigidity-prism-ideal); [`mathlib:Ideal.Cotangent`](#mathlib-ideal-cotangent); [`mathlib:TensorPower`](#mathlib-tensorpower); [`mathlib:DerivedCategory`](#mathlib-derivedcategory).

**Consumers.** Bhatt–Scholze Theorem 4.11: its cohomology sheaves are the twisted differential forms. Bhatt–Scholze Corollary 4.12: base change is proved for Δ̄ and lifted to Δ by derived Nakayama. PrismaticCohomology:PR.2 (Construction 7.6): the conjugate filtration is the left Kan extension of the canonical filtration of Δ̄. PrismaticCohomology:PR.3 (Theorems 12.2, 15.2): graded pieces of the Nygaard filtration are truncations of Δ̄ with twists.

**Planning API.**

- `TauCeti.Prismatic.HodgeTate.Twist` (data): For i ≥ 0 the invertible R-module R{i} = R ⊗_{A/I} (I/I²)^{⊗i}; M{i} = M ⊗_R R{i} and M{−i} = M ⊗_R Hom_R(R{i}, R).
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.HodgeTate.twistZero` (simp): R{0} ≅ R.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.HodgeTate.twistAdd` (simp): R{i+j} ≅ R{i} ⊗_R R{j}.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.HodgeTate.twistOfOrientation` (compatibility): A generator d of I gives an isomorphism R{i} ≅ R, the class of d^{⊗i} going to 1.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.HodgeTate.reduction` (projection): The reduction map Δ_{R/A} → Δ̄_{R/A} in D(A) (Δ̄ viewed as an A-complex through A → A/I → R).
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.HodgeTate.structureMap` (data): The structure map R → Δ̄_{R/A}, as a map R[0] → Δ̄_{R/A} in D(R).
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.HodgeTate.cohomologyMap` (functoriality): For a map R → S of A/I-algebras, the map Δ̄_{R/A} → Δ̄_{S/A} over R (the target restricted to R).

**Unit tests.**

- `pr1_twist_zero` (degenerate): R{0} = R.
- `pr1_twist_oriented` (computation): If I = (d) then R{i} is free of rank one over R for every i ≥ 0, with basis the class of d^{⊗i}.
- `pr1_hodge_tate_base` (degenerate): For R = A/I the structure map A/I → Δ̄_{(A/I)/A} is an isomorphism.
- `pr1_hodge_tate_not_discrete` (non-example): If the p-completed module Ω̂^1_{R/(A/I)} ≠ 0 for a p-completely smooth R then H^1(Δ̄_{R/A}) ≠ 0; so Δ̄_{R/A} is not R[0], the reduction of the structure sheaf of a lift.

**Acceptance.** Δ̄_{(A/I)/A} = A/I. For an oriented prism (A,(d)) every twist M{i} is identified with M by d^i, and the triangle for i = 0 is the reduction of Δ →d Δ modulo d². For the q-de Rham prism (Z_p[[q−1]],([p]_q)), I/I² is free on the class of [p]_q.

**Sources.** [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Construction 4.9, first paragraph. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 39. The node is the definition of Δ̄_{X/A}, of the twists M{i} and of the triangle given there.. [ALB23](https://arxiv.org/abs/1907.10525v4), Definition 3.1.5. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 16. The same definition in the affine case, with the twist M{n} := M ⊗ (I/I²)^{⊗n} recalled before Theorem 3.1.6..

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-1-cech-alexander-computes-cohomology"></a>

### Čech–Alexander complexes compute prismatic cohomology; independence of the presentation

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/cech-alexander-computes-cohomology` · theorem. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.Site` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/Site/Basic`.

Let (A,I) be a bounded prism, R a p-completely smooth A/I-algebra and C^• the Čech–Alexander cosimplicial ring of a presentation B_0 → R. Then the natural maps Δ_{R/A} → lim_Δ C^• and Δ̄_{R/A} → lim_Δ C^•/IC^• are isomorphisms in D(A) (of E_∞-A-algebras), so Δ_{R/A} is computed by the cochain complex of C^• and Δ̄_{R/A} by that of C^•/IC^•. For two presentations B_0 → R and B_0′ → R the presentation B_0 ⊗̂_A B_0′ → R receives maps from both, and the induced maps of cosimplicial rings are compatible with the identifications with Δ_{R/A}; hence the isomorphism class and the comparison isomorphisms do not depend on the presentation (the category of presentations is sifted). In particular the strictly functorial complex C^•((R/A)_Δ, O_Δ) represents the functor R ↦ Δ_{R/A}.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** (A,I) bounded; R p-completely smooth over A/I (or p-completely syntomic, with the same proof). The statement uses the general fact: for a topos 𝒳, an abelian sheaf F and a weakly final object X_0 with Čech nerve X_0^•, RΓ(𝒳,F) ≃ R lim RΓ(X_0^•,F); if F is acyclic on each X_0^n this is the complex F(X_0^•) (Bhatt–Scholze, footnote to Construction 4.18).

**Construction or proof.**

1. Čech descent: the map from the weakly final object X_0 to the final object of the topos is an epimorphism, so RΓ(𝒳,F) ≃ R lim_Δ RΓ(X_0^•,F) by cohomological descent along its Čech nerve (requested from E2; the source adapts Stacks, Tag 07JM).
2. Acyclicity: each (C^n, IC^n) is an object of the site of bounded prisms and O, Ō have no higher cohomology on any object (PR.1/prismatic-structure-sheaf (3)), so RΓ(X_0^n, O_Δ) = C^n and RΓ(X_0^n, Ō_Δ) = C^n/IC^n.
3. Independence: products of presentations exist, so the category of presentations is sifted (non-empty with binary coproducts); a map of presentations induces a map of Čech nerves of weakly final objects over the final object, hence the identity on RΓ.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/cech-alexander-complex`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-cech-alexander-complex); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/prismatic-structure-sheaf`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-prismatic-structure-sheaf); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/relative-prismatic-cohomology`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-relative-prismatic-cohomology); `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E2`.

**Acceptance.** For R = A/I the theorem gives Δ_{R/A} = A. Two presentations of A/I⟨X⟩, by A⟨X⟩ and by A⟨X,Y⟩ with Y ↦ 0, give quasi-isomorphic complexes through the presentation A⟨X,Y,X′⟩. H^0(Δ_{R/A}) is the equaliser of the two coface maps C^0 ⇉ C^1.

**Sources.** [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Construction 4.18 and its footnote. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 42. The theorem is the conclusion of Construction 4.18, with the topos-theoretic lemma of the footnote.. [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Theorem 5.2, proof (the same argument on the crystalline side). Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 45. Independence of the presentation by siftedness is stated there for the parallel crystalline construction..

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-1-frobenius-on-prismatic-cohomology"></a>

### The Frobenius of prismatic cohomology

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/frobenius-on-prismatic-cohomology` · construction. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.Site` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/Site/Basic`.

The structure sheaf O_Δ of (X/A)_Δ is a sheaf of δ-A-algebras: on each object (B,g,f) the ring B carries its δ-structure, with Frobenius lift φ_B(x) = x^p + pδ(x), and maps of prisms commute with δ. Hence φ : O_Δ → O_Δ is an endomorphism of sheaves of rings which is φ_A-semilinear, that is A-linear as a map O_Δ → φ_{A,*}O_Δ. It induces φ_X : Δ_{X/A} → φ_{A,*}Δ_{X/A} in D(X_ét, A) and φ_R : Δ_{R/A} → φ_{A,*}Δ_{R/A} in D(A), maps of commutative algebra objects, natural in X (or R) and compatible with base change of the prism. By adjunction φ_R is the same as its linearisation φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} → Δ_{R/A}, where φ_A^* = − ⊗^L_{A,φ_A} A (derived (p,I)-completed where stated). On a Čech–Alexander model, φ_R is induced by the termwise Frobenius lifts of the cosimplicial δ-ring C^•.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** (A,I) bounded prism, X a p-adic formal scheme over A/I (smooth where comparison theorems are used). φ_A need not be flat or an isomorphism; φ_A^* is a derived functor and is not assumed to commute with totalisations unless proved (Theorem 5.2, proof). φ carries I into φ(I)A, which is contained in I only for crystalline prisms; so in general Ō_Δ has no induced endomorphism (for I = (p) it has the Frobenius); reduction modulo I after φ gives the maps used in the de Rham comparison.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Maps of prisms are maps of δ-rings (PR.0/prism-category), so the Frobenius lifts φ_B are natural in the object: φ is an endomorphism of the presheaf O_Δ, semilinear over φ_A because g is a δ-map.
2. Apply Rν_* and RΓ: restriction of scalars along φ_A is exact, so R ν_*(φ_{A,*}O_Δ) = φ_{A,*}Rν_*O_Δ, giving φ_X and φ_R as maps of commutative algebra objects.
3. The linearisation is the adjoint map under the adjunction between derived extension of scalars along φ_A and restriction of scalars (requested from DD.1 with its completed form).
4. On C^•: each C^n is a δ-A-algebra and cofaces and codegeneracies are δ-maps, so φ is a map of cosimplicial rings over φ_A; under PR.1/cech-alexander-computes-cohomology it induces φ_R.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/relative-prismatic-cohomology`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-relative-prismatic-cohomology); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/relative-prismatic-site`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-relative-prismatic-site); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/cech-alexander-computes-cohomology`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-cech-alexander-computes-cohomology); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/prism-category`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-prism-category); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-frobenius-dictionary`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-delta-frobenius-dictionary); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/associated-frobenius`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-associated-frobenius); `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`.

**Consumers.** Bhatt–Scholze Theorem 5.2: the crystalline comparison is Frobenius-equivariant. Bhatt–Scholze Theorem 6.4: the de Rham comparison is the reduction of the Frobenius twist φ_A^*Δ modulo I. PrismaticCohomology:PR.3 (Theorem 15.3, Corollary 15.5): the linearised Frobenius factors through Lη_I and is an isogeny. PrismaticCohomology:PR.4 (Theorem 9.1): étale cohomology is the fibre of φ − 1 after inverting I.

**Planning API.**

- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Site.RelativePrism.sheafFrobenius` (data): The endomorphism φ of the presheaf of rings O_Δ, with component φ_B on the object (B,g,f).
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Site.RelativePrism.sheafFrobenius_structureMap` (compatibility): φ_B(g(a)) = g(φ_A(a)) for a ∈ A: the Frobenius of O_Δ is φ_A-semilinear.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Site.frobenius_naturality` (functoriality): For a map R → S of A/I-algebras the square formed by φ_R, φ_S and the induced maps Δ_{R/A} → Δ_{S/A} commutes.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Site.frobeniusLinearization` (data): The linearisation φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} → Δ_{R/A}, the adjoint of φ_R under φ_A^* ⊣ φ_{A,*}.

**Unit tests.**

- `pr1_frobenius_sheaf_component` (computation): On an object (B,g,f) the Frobenius of O_Δ is x ↦ x^p + pδ(x).
- `pr1_frobenius_trivial_base` (degenerate): If φ_A is the identity (for instance A = Z_p) then φ_{A,*} is isomorphic to the identity functor of D(A), so φ_R is an A-linear endomorphism of Δ_{R/A}.
- `pr1_frobenius_not_linear` (non-example): If φ_A(a) ≠ a and g : A → B is injective then φ_B(g(a)) ≠ g(a): the Frobenius is not A-linear, so it is not an endomorphism of Δ_{R/A} in D(A).

**Acceptance.** On Δ_{(A/I)/A} = A the Frobenius is φ_A. For (A,I) = (Z_p,(p)) the Frobenius of Δ_{R/Z_p} is Z_p-linear. For a crystalline prism, φ corresponds under the crystalline comparison to the Frobenius of crystalline cohomology (PR.1/crystalline-comparison).

**Sources.** [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Theorem 1.8, opening. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 4. The φ_A-linear endomorphism φ of RΓ_Δ(X/A) is introduced there.. [ALB23](https://arxiv.org/abs/1907.10525v4), Definition 3.1.5. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 16. The Frobenius of Δ_{R/A} is induced by the Frobenius of the structure sheaf..

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-1-base-change-finite-tor-amplitude"></a>

### Base change along maps of finite complete Tor amplitude

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/base-change-finite-tor-amplitude` · theorem. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.Site` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/Site/Basic`.

Let (A,I) → (A′,IA′) be a map of bounded prisms such that A → A′ has finite (p,I)-complete Tor amplitude, let R be a p-completely smooth A/I-algebra and R′ := R ⊗̂_A A′ its p-completed base change (a p-completely smooth A′/IA′-algebra). Then the natural maps Δ_{R/A} ⊗̂^L_A A′ → Δ_{R′/A′} and Δ̄_{R/A} ⊗̂^L_{A/I} A′/IA′ → Δ̄_{R′/A′} are isomorphisms, the completions being derived (p,I)-adic and p-adic. More precisely, for every map of bounded prisms the termwise completed base change C^• ⊗̂_A A′ of the functorial Čech–Alexander cosimplicial ring of R computes Δ_{R′/A′}, and the Tor amplitude hypothesis is used only to commute the completed base change with the totalisation.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** Both prisms are bounded; A → A′ has finite (p,I)-complete Tor amplitude: A′ ⊗^L_A A/(p,I) has finite Tor amplitude over A/(p,I). R is p-completely smooth over A/I. The Tor amplitude hypothesis is removed by PR.1/prismatic-base-change, which uses the Hodge–Tate comparison; the present statement is an input of that comparison and cannot be replaced by it.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Termwise statement (Lemma 4.20, proof): C^n is the prismatic envelope of a completed free δ-A-algebra; by PR.0/regular-prismatic-envelopes (2) envelopes commute with base change along every map of bounded prisms, and the base change of a weakly initial object and of its Čech nerve is again one for R′. So C^• ⊗̂_A A′ computes Δ_{R′/A′} by PR.1/cech-alexander-computes-cohomology.
2. Lemma 4.22: for a ring C with a finitely generated ideal J and a map C → C′ of finite J-complete Tor amplitude, the J-completed base change commutes with totalisations of cosimplicial objects of D^{≥0}. Proof in the source: finite skeleta commute, and the functor K ↦ (K ⊗^L_C C′) ⊗^L Kos(C′;x_1^m,…,x_r^m) lowers the degree of coconnectivity by a constant independent of m. Requested from DD.1.
3. Apply Lemma 4.22 to C^• over (A,(p,I)), and reduce modulo I for Δ̄.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/cech-alexander-complex`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-cech-alexander-complex); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/cech-alexander-computes-cohomology`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-cech-alexander-computes-cohomology); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/regular-prismatic-envelopes`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-regular-prismatic-envelopes); `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`.

**Acceptance.** A completely flat map of bounded prisms satisfies the hypothesis with amplitude 0. The map α of PR.1/crystallization-of-oriented-prism satisfies the hypothesis. For A → A′ with infinite complete Tor dimension the statement is not available at this point of the theory.

**Sources.** [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Lemma 4.20, Lemma 4.22 and their proofs. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed pages 43, 44. The node is Lemma 4.20 together with the algebraic Lemma 4.22 used in its proof..

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-1-etale-localization"></a>

### Étale localisation of Hodge–Tate cohomology

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/etale-localization` · theorem. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.Site` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/Site/Basic`.

Let (A,I) be a bounded prism and R → S a p-completely étale map of p-completely smooth A/I-algebras. Then the natural map Δ̄_{R/A} ⊗̂^L_R S → Δ̄_{S/A} is an isomorphism (derived p-completed tensor product). The restriction functor (S/A)_Δ → (R/A)_Δ has, in the algebraic language, a left adjoint F : (R/A)_Δ → (S/A)_Δ sending (B → B/IB ← R) to (B_S → B_S/IB_S ← S), where B_S is the unique (p,I)-completely étale δ-B-algebra with B_S/IB_S = B/IB ⊗̂^L_R S; F preserves coproducts and weakly initial objects.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** (A,I) is bounded; R and S are p-completely smooth over A/I and R → S is p-completely étale: S is derived p-complete and S ⊗^L_R R/p is étale over R/p. The statement is for Δ̄; the corresponding statement for Δ follows only after completion along I and is not an S-linear statement, since Δ_{R/A} is not an R-module.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Construction of F (Lemma 4.21, proof): for an object (B → B/IB ← R) the map B/IB → B/IB ⊗̂^L_R S is p-completely étale; by Bhatt–Scholze Lemma 2.18 with Elkik algebraization (stage PR.0, DD.1) it deforms uniquely to a (p,I)-completely étale δ-B-algebra B_S, and (B_S, IB_S) is a bounded prism by PR.0/bounded-prism-complete-flatness. Adjointness follows from the uniqueness of étale lifts.
2. As a left adjoint F preserves coproducts and weakly initial objects. Apply it to the Čech–Alexander cosimplicial object C^• of R: D^• := F(C^•) is the Čech nerve of a weakly initial object of (S/A)_Δ, so D^•/ID^• computes Δ̄_{S/A} (PR.1/cech-alexander-computes-cohomology, whose proof only needs a weakly initial object and its Čech nerve).
3. Termwise C^n/IC^n ⊗̂^L_R S ≅ D^n/ID^n by the definition of F; the p-completed base change along the p-completely flat map R → S commutes with the totalisation by Lemma 4.22 (DD.1).

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/cech-alexander-complex`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-cech-alexander-complex); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/cech-alexander-computes-cohomology`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-cech-alexander-computes-cohomology); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/hodge-tate-cohomology`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-hodge-tate-cohomology); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/bounded-prism-complete-flatness`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-bounded-prism-complete-flatness); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-etale-extension`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-delta-etale-extension); `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`; [`mathlib:Algebra.Etale`](#mathlib-algebra-etale).

**Acceptance.** For a p-completed localisation S = R⟨1/f⟩: Δ̄_{S/A} = Δ̄_{R/A} ⊗̂^L_R R⟨1/f⟩. Étale chart: for a p-completely étale map A/I⟨X_1,…,X_n⟩ → S, Δ̄_{S/A} = Δ̄_{A/I⟨X⟩/A} ⊗̂^L S; with the Hodge–Tate comparison for the polynomial ring this gives H^i(Δ̄_{S/A}) = Ω^i_{S/(A/I)}{−i}. For R = S the functor F is the identity.

**Sources.** [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Lemma 4.21 and its proof. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 43. The node is Lemma 4.21 with the adjoint functor of its proof..

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-1-bockstein-differential"></a>

### The Bockstein differential on twisted Hodge–Tate cohomology

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/bockstein-differential` · construction. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.HodgeTate` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/HodgeTate/Comparison`.

Let (A,I) be a bounded prism and R a p-completely smooth A/I-algebra (or X smooth over A/I, with sheaves on X_ét). For i ≥ 0 the connecting map of the triangle Δ̄_{R/A}{i+1} → Δ_{R/A} ⊗^L_A I^i/I^{i+2} → Δ̄_{R/A}{i} is the Bockstein differential β_I : H^i(Δ̄_{R/A}){i} → H^{i+1}(Δ̄_{R/A}){i+1}. With the cup product of the commutative algebra object Δ̄_{R/A}, the graded group H^*(Δ̄_{R/A}){∗} = ⊕_i H^i(Δ̄_{R/A}){i} is a graded-commutative differential graded A/I-algebra: β_I is A/I-linear, β_I ∘ β_I = 0 and β_I(xy) = β_I(x)y + (−1)^{deg x} x β_I(y). Its degree-0 part is an R-algebra through η^0_R : R → H^0(Δ̄_{R/A}), and β_I ∘ η^0_R : R → H^1(Δ̄_{R/A}){1} is an A/I-linear derivation into a derived p-complete R-module. It therefore induces the R-linear map η^1_R : Ω^1_{R/(A/I)} → H^1(Δ̄_{R/A}){1}, f dg ↦ f·β_I(η^0_R(g)), where Ω^1_{R/(A/I)} is the p-completed module of differentials, finite projective over R.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** (A,I) is a bounded prism; R is p-completely smooth over A/I. β_I is A/I-linear but not R-linear. Graded commutativity is xy = (−1)^{deg x · deg y} yx. The vanishing of squares of odd elements is not part of this node; for elements β_I(f), f ∈ R, it is Lemma 4.10 and is proved in PR.1/hodge-tate-affine-line. When I = (d) the twists are trivialised by d and β_I is the Bockstein of the triangle Δ → Δ → Δ̄ given by multiplication by d (the convention of the source for d = p).

**Construction or proof.**

1. Construction 4.9: the triangle is that of PR.1/hodge-tate-cohomology; its connecting map Δ̄{i} → Δ̄{i+1}[1] induces β_I on cohomology.
2. β_I ∘ β_I = 0: the two triangles for i and i+1 come from the filtration of Δ ⊗^L_A I^i/I^{i+3} by powers of I, and a composite of consecutive connecting maps of a three-step filtration vanishes on cohomology.
3. Leibniz rule: the I-adic filtration of the commutative algebra object Δ_{R/A} is multiplicative, so the connecting maps of its graded pieces form a derivation on ⊕_i H^*(gr^i) (the standard multiplicativity of the Bockstein spectral sequence of a filtered commutative algebra object; requested from DD.1 as the multiplicative I-adic filtration).
4. η^0 is H^0 of the structure map R → Δ̄_{R/A}. The derivation β_I η^0 factors through the completed differentials because its target is derived p-complete (universal property of Ω^1, completed form requested from DD.2).

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/hodge-tate-cohomology`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-hodge-tate-cohomology); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/relative-prismatic-cohomology`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-relative-prismatic-cohomology); `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`; `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.2`; [`mathlib:KaehlerDifferential`](#mathlib-kaehlerdifferential); [`mathlib:KaehlerDifferential.D`](#mathlib-kaehlerdifferential-d).

**Consumers.** Bhatt–Scholze Construction 4.9: the target of the Hodge–Tate comparison map is this dg algebra. Bhatt–Scholze Proposition 6.2: η^0 and η^1 are proved to be isomorphisms for the affine line before η^* is available in general. Bhatt–Scholze Proposition 4.15: the extension class of τ^{≤1}Δ̄ is the Bockstein; it is the cotangent complex L_{X/A}. PrismaticCohomology:PR.3 (Theorem 15.3): Lη_I of Δ has terms H^i(Δ̄){i} and differential β_I.

**Planning API.**

- `TauCeti.Prismatic.HodgeTate.twistedCohomology` (data): The R-module H^i(Δ̄_{R/A}){i} = H^i(Δ̄_{R/A}) ⊗_R R{i}, for i ≥ 0.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.HodgeTate.bockstein` (data): The additive map β_I : H^i(Δ̄_{R/A}){i} → H^{i+1}(Δ̄_{R/A}){i+1}; it is A/I-linear.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.HodgeTate.bockstein_comp_bockstein` (relation): β_I ∘ β_I = 0.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.HodgeTate.cup` (structure): The cup product H^i{i} × H^j{j} → H^{i+j}{i+j}, R-bilinear, associative, unital and graded-commutative.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.HodgeTate.bockstein_cup` (relation): β_I(x ∪ y) = β_I(x) ∪ y + (−1)^i x ∪ β_I(y) for x of degree i.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.HodgeTate.eta0` (data): The R-linear map η^0_R : R → H^0(Δ̄_{R/A}){0}, a ring map for the cup product.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.HodgeTate.eta1` (universal-property): The R-linear map η^1_R : Ω^1_{R/(A/I)} → H^1(Δ̄_{R/A}){1} with η^1_R(dg) = β_I(η^0_R(g)).

**Unit tests.**

- `pr1_bockstein_eta1_d` (computation): η^1_R(dg) = β_I(η^0_R(g)) for every g ∈ R; hence η^1_R(f dg) = f·β_I(η^0_R(g)).
- `pr1_bockstein_base_zero` (degenerate): For R = A/I, β_I vanishes on H^0(Δ̄_{(A/I)/A}) = A/I.
- `pr1_bockstein_not_linear` (non-example): If dg ≠ 0 in Ω^1_{R/(A/I)} for a p-completely smooth R, then β_I(η^0_R(g)) ≠ 0 although β_I(η^0_R(1)) = 0: β_I is not R-linear.

**Acceptance.** For R = A/I the cohomology is A/I in degree 0 and β_I = 0. For R = A/I⟨X⟩, β_I(X) is a generator of H^1(Δ̄_{R/A}){1} ≅ Ω^1_{R/(A/I)} (PR.1/hodge-tate-affine-line). For a crystalline prism and I = (p), β_p is the Bockstein of crystalline cohomology modulo p², which on the de Rham complex of a lift sends the class of x^p to the class of x^{p−1}dx.

**Sources.** [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Construction 4.9. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 39. The node is the Bockstein differential, the dg-algebra structure and the maps η^0, η^1 of Construction 4.9..

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-1-p-torsion-free-h0-syntomic"></a>

### p-torsion-freeness of H^0 for p-completely syntomic algebras

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/p-torsion-free-h0-syntomic` · theorem. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.Site` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/Site/Basic`.

Let (A,I) be a bounded prism with A p-torsion-free, and let S be a p-completely syntomic A/I-algebra: S is p-complete with bounded p^∞-torsion, S/p ≅ S ⊗^L_{A/I} (A/I)/p, and (A/I)/p → S/p is syntomic. Then H^0((S/A)_Δ, O_Δ) is p-torsion-free. Under the identification of site cohomology with derived prismatic cohomology for such S (PrismaticCohomology:PR.2), this is the statement that H^0(Δ_{S/A}) is p-torsion-free.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** (A,I) is a bounded prism and A is p-torsion-free. S is p-completely syntomic over A/I in the sense of Anschütz–Le Bras, footnote to Lemma 5.1.6. The proof planned here is complete when the pro-system ((A/I^n)[p])_n is pro-zero, which holds whenever A/p has bounded I^∞-torsion ((A/d^n)[p] ≅ (A/p)[d^n] with transition maps multiplication by d): every crystalline prism, every prism with (p,d) regular (Breuil–Kisin, q-de Rham), every perfect prism (A/p is reduced; this is the case A = A_inf(R), R any perfectoid ring, used by the source) and every noetherian A. For an arbitrary p-torsion-free bounded prism the step 'a derived (p,I)-complete, (p,I)-completely flat A-module is p-torsion-free' is asserted in the source by calling the module p-completely flat over A; this is recorded as a gap of the packet and as source issue PrismaticCohomology/E14. The identification with derived prismatic cohomology uses descent from quasiregular semiperfectoid rings and belongs to PR.2; this node is about the site.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Čech–Alexander complex: since S is p-completely syntomic, the kernel of a presentation is (ind-)Zariski-locally generated by I and a sequence completely regular relative to A, so PR.1/cech-alexander-complex applies and gives a weakly initial object C^0 of (S/A)_Δ with C^0 derived (p,I)-complete and (p,I)-completely flat over A (PR.0/regular-prismatic-envelopes (1)).
2. H^0((S/A)_Δ, O_Δ) is the equaliser of C^0 ⇉ C^1 (PR.1/cech-alexander-computes-cohomology), a subring of C^0; so it suffices that C^0 is p-torsion-free.
3. For a derived (p,I)-complete, (p,I)-completely flat A-module B over the p-torsion-free bounded prism A: B is discrete (PR.0/bounded-prism-complete-flatness), B[p] = H^{−1}(B ⊗^L_A A/p), and by derived I-completeness and complete flatness B[p] ≅ lim_n B ⊗_A (A/I^n)[p], with transition maps induced by A/I^{n+1} → A/I^n. If the pro-system ((A/I^n)[p])_n is pro-zero the limit vanishes. For I = (p) this is the source's argument: B is p-completely flat over Z_p, hence p-torsion-free.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/cech-alexander-complex`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-cech-alexander-complex); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/cech-alexander-computes-cohomology`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-cech-alexander-computes-cohomology); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/regular-prismatic-envelopes`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-regular-prismatic-envelopes); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/bounded-prism-complete-flatness`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-bounded-prism-complete-flatness); `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`.

**Acceptance.** A = A_inf, S = O_C⟨x⟩/(x^n − p)-type syntomic algebras, and the application of the source: S the ring of a finite locally free group scheme over a quasisyntomic base. A = Z_p, S = F_p: H^0 = Z_p is p-torsion-free while H^0 of Ō_Δ is F_p; the statement is about O_Δ. If A has p-torsion the statement fails already for S = A/I, where H^0 = A.

**Sources.** [ALB23](https://arxiv.org/abs/1907.10525v4), Lemma 5.1.6 and its proof. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 76. The node is Lemma 5.1.6 (routed item PAPER-ANSCHUTZ-LEBRAS-23/134) for the cohomology of the site, with the step of its proof that is asserted there made explicit.. [ALB23](https://arxiv.org/abs/1907.10525v4), Lemma 5.1.6, proof. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 76. The first term of the Čech–Alexander complex is where the torsion-freeness is checked..

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-1-crystalline-comparison"></a>

### The crystalline comparison

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/crystalline-comparison` · theorem. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.Crystalline` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/Crystalline/Comparison`.

Let (A,(p)) be a crystalline prism (A is a p-torsion-free, p-complete δ-ring) and let I ⊂ A be an ideal with divided powers and p ∈ I. The Frobenius of A/p kills I/pA, so it induces ψ : A/I → A/p. Let R be a smooth A/I-algebra and R^{(1)} := R ⊗_{A/I,ψ} A/p, a smooth A/p-algebra. Let RΓ_crys(R/A) be the crystalline cohomology of Spec(R) relative to the PD thickening Spec(A/I) ⊂ Spf(A) (p-adically: the derived limit over n of the crystalline cohomology over A/p^n). Then there is a canonical isomorphism Δ_{R^{(1)}/A} ≃ RΓ_crys(R/A) of E_∞-A-algebras, compatible with the Frobenius endomorphisms (the Frobenius of prismatic cohomology on the left, the Frobenius of crystalline cohomology induced by the Frobenius of Spec(R) and φ_A on the right). In the case I = (p), with C^• the Čech–Alexander cosimplicial ring of a presentation B_0 → R and D^• the cosimplicial p-completed PD envelope of the same presentation, the isomorphism is induced by a map of cosimplicial δ-A-algebras φ_A^*C^• → D^•, where φ_A^*C^• (termwise base change along φ_A) computes Δ_{R^{(1)}/A}.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** (A,(p)) is a crystalline prism, hence bounded; I is a PD ideal containing p (its divided powers are unique since A is p-torsion-free, and they are compatible with the canonical ones on (p)). R is a smooth A/I-algebra in the usual sense (A/I has characteristic p). The Frobenius twist is on the prismatic side: it is R^{(1)}, not R, whose prismatic cohomology is the crystalline cohomology of R. For I = (p) and with base change (PR.1/prismatic-base-change) this reads φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} ≃ RΓ_crys(R/A); the untwisted statement Δ_{R/A} ≃ RΓ_crys(R/A) is false in general. The statement φ_A^*C^• computes Δ_{R^{(1)}/A} is termwise; it is not claimed here that φ_A^* commutes with the totalisation of C^•.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Crystalline side, I = (p) (requested from CR.1 and CR.2). For a presentation B_0 → R with kernel J_0, B := Free_δ(B_0)^∧ and R′ := B/J_0B, let D_0, D be the p-completed PD envelopes of J_0 ⊂ B_0 and J_0B ⊂ B; they are p-torsion-free (PR.0/pd-envelope-as-delta-envelope, Lemma 2.38), and the pro-object {(D/p^n → R′ ← R)}_n of the big crystalline site is weakly initial and compatible with coproducts. Hence RΓ_crys(R/A) ≃ lim D^•, D^• the envelope of the Čech nerve, independently of the presentation; big and small sites agree (Berthelot, III.4.1.4).
2. Prismatic side. C^• = B^•{J_0^•B^•/p}^∧ computes Δ_{R/A} (PR.1/cech-alexander-computes-cohomology), and its termwise base change φ_A^*C^• computes Δ_{R^{(1)}/A} (PR.1/base-change-finite-tor-amplitude, termwise part). By PR.0/pd-envelope-as-delta-envelope (Corollary 2.39), D^• = B^•{φ(J_0^•)B^•/p}^∧. The relative Frobenius of A → B^• therefore induces η : φ_A^*C^• → D^•, and D^• is the pullback of the cosimplicial B^{•,(1)}-module φ_A^*C^• along the flat relative Frobenius B^{•,(1)} → B^•.
3. Both sides of η are p-torsion-free. By PR.1/relative-frobenius-cosimplicial-lemma applied to N = φ_A^*C^•/p, η is a quasi-isomorphism modulo p, hence a quasi-isomorphism by derived Nakayama (DD.1).
4. Frobenius. η is a map of cosimplicial δ-A-algebras; the Frobenius of crystalline cohomology corresponds to the δ-Frobenius of D^• under RΓ_crys ≃ lim D^•, by functoriality of crystalline cohomology for the Frobenius endomorphism of the simplicial PD thickening (requested from CR.3).
5. General I. The map A/p → A/I is surjective with locally nilpotent kernel, so R lifts to a smooth A/p-algebra R̃, and R̃ ⊗_{A/p,Frob} A/p = R^{(1)}; the case I = (p) for R̃ and the invariance of crystalline cohomology under enlarging the PD ideal of the base give the isomorphism. It is canonical: for a presentation B_0 → R with B_0 a δ-A-algebra, the PD envelope D^• of the Čech nerve has φ_{D^•}(ker(D^• → R)) ⊂ pD^•, giving a cosimplicial object (D^• → D^•/p ← R^{(1)}) of (R^{(1)}/A)_Δ and hence a map Δ_{R^{(1)}/A} → lim D^• independent of choices; it agrees with the previous map because η is a morphism of cosimplicial objects of the site (R^{(1)}/A)_Δ (the source leaves this compatibility to the reader).

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/cech-alexander-complex`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-cech-alexander-complex); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/cech-alexander-computes-cohomology`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-cech-alexander-computes-cohomology); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/relative-frobenius-cosimplicial-lemma`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-relative-frobenius-cosimplicial-lemma); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/base-change-finite-tor-amplitude`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-base-change-finite-tor-amplitude); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/frobenius-on-prismatic-cohomology`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-frobenius-on-prismatic-cohomology); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/crystalline-prism`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-crystalline-prism); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/pd-envelope-as-delta-envelope`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-pd-envelope-as-delta-envelope); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/regular-prismatic-envelopes`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-regular-prismatic-envelopes); `CrystallineCohomology:CR.0`; `CrystallineCohomology:CR.1`; `CrystallineCohomology:CR.2`; `CrystallineCohomology:CR.3`; `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`; [`mathlib:DividedPowers`](#mathlib-dividedpowers); `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.4`.

**Acceptance.** A = Z_p, I = (p), R = F_p[x]: Δ_{F_p[x]/Z_p} ≃ RΓ_crys(F_p[x]/Z_p), the de Rham complex of Z_p⟨x⟩; here R^{(1)} = R. A = W(k) with k perfect and R̃ smooth over k: Δ_{R̃^{(1)}/W(k)} ≃ RΓ_crys(R̃/W(k)); the twist is by the Frobenius of k. A = A_crys(O_C/p) and I = ker(A_crys → O_C/p), a PD ideal strictly containing (p): for R smooth over O_C/p, Δ_{R^{(1)}/A_crys} ≃ RΓ_crys(R/A_crys), with ψ : O_C/p → A_crys/p induced by the Frobenius.

**Sources.** [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Notation 5.1, Theorem 5.2 and its proof. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 45. The node is Theorem 5.2 with the cosimplicial map of its proof.. [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Theorem 1.8 (1) and Example 1.9 (1). Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed pages 4, 5. The φ_A-twisted global form and its interpretation as a Frobenius descent.. <a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-1-crystallization-of-oriented-prism"></a>

### Mapping an oriented prism to a crystalline one

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/crystallization-of-oriented-prism` · construction. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.Crystalline` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/Crystalline/Comparison`.

Let (A,(d)) be an oriented prism such that A/(d) is p-torsion-free and the Frobenius A/(p,d) → A/(p,d^p), x ↦ x^p, is flat (for example the universal oriented prism, the (p,d)-completion of Z_(p){d, δ(d)^{−1}}). Let B := A{φ(d)/p}^∧ be the p-complete animated δ-A-algebra obtained by freely adjoining φ(d)/p. Then: (a) B is discrete and p-torsion-free, it is the p-completed PD envelope of (d) ⊂ A, and φ(d) = p·u in B with u a unit; B is (p,d)-complete. (b) The composite α : A → B of φ_A : A → A with the canonical map A → B satisfies α(d) ∈ pB, so α is a map of prisms (A,(d)) → (B,(p)) and (B,(p)) is a bounded crystalline prism. (c) Modulo p, α factors as A/p → A/(p,d) → A/(p,d^p) → B/p = D_{(d)}(A/p), where the first map has finite Tor amplitude, the second is the Frobenius and is faithfully flat, and the third is free. (d) The completed base change functor α̂^* : D_{comp}(A) → D_{comp}(B) on derived (p,d)-complete objects is conservative and has finite (p,d)-complete Tor amplitude. (e) For every p-completely smooth A/(d)-algebra R with p-completed base change R_B, α̂^*Δ_{R/A} ≃ Δ_{R_B/B} and α̂^*Δ̄_{R/A} ≃ Δ̄_{R_B/B}.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** (A,(d)) is an oriented prism with A/(d) p-torsion-free; then p is a nonzerodivisor on A and (p,d) is a regular sequence. The Frobenius hypothesis is the corrected one of register entry PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22/E13: only the flatness of A/(p,d) → A/(p,d^p) is used, and this is what Example 3.4 provides for the universal oriented prism; the printed hypothesis 'the Frobenius on A/p is flat' is stronger than what is proved there. α is the Frobenius-twisted canonical map; the canonical map A → B itself is not a map of prisms to (B,(p)), since the image of d is not divisible by p.

**Construction or proof.**

1. (a): by PR.0/pd-envelope-as-delta-envelope (Corollary 2.39 with the regular element d of A/p), A{φ(d)/p}^∧ is the p-completed PD envelope of (d), discrete and p-torsion-free; φ(d) = p·u with u a unit by PR.0/distinguished-factor-rigidity (Lemma 2.24), because φ(d) is distinguished and divisible by p. Since d^p ∈ (p, φ(d)), p-completeness implies (p,d)-completeness.
2. (b): α(d) = φ(d) = pu ∈ pB; α is a δ-map as a composite of δ-maps; (B,(p)) is a crystalline prism by PR.0/crystalline-prism.
3. (c): B/p is the PD envelope of (d) in A/p, free over A/(p,d^p) with basis the divided powers γ_{kp}(d) (CR.0); the composite A/p → B/p is induced by φ, which factors through A/(p,d) → A/(p,d^p).
4. (d): by derived Nakayama conservativity and Tor amplitude are checked modulo p for d-completed base change along the three maps of (c): the first is a quotient by a regular element, the others are faithfully flat (DD.1).
5. (e): PR.1/base-change-finite-tor-amplitude applied to α, using (d).

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/base-change-finite-tor-amplitude`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-base-change-finite-tor-amplitude); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/pd-envelope-as-delta-envelope`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-pd-envelope-as-delta-envelope); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/distinguished-factor-rigidity`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-distinguished-factor-rigidity); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/crystalline-prism`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-crystalline-prism); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/animated-delta-rings`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-animated-delta-rings); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/prism-category`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-prism-category); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/universal-oriented-prism`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-universal-oriented-prism); `CrystallineCohomology:CR.0`; `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`.

**Consumers.** Bhatt–Scholze Proposition 6.2 and Theorem 6.3: the Hodge–Tate comparison over the universal oriented prism is reduced to the crystalline prism (D_0,(p)) by conservativity of α̂^*. Bhatt–Scholze Proposition 6.2, proof: for a general oriented prism the pushout E = A ⊗̂_{A_0} D_0 and the base change of α are used. PrismaticCohomology:PR.3 (§15): the same reduction to the crystalline case is used for the Nygaard filtration and Lη.

**Planning API.**

- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Crystalline.crystallization` (constructor): The bounded crystalline prism (B,(p)), B = A{φ(d)/p}^∧, attached to an oriented prism (A,(d)).
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Crystalline.crystallizationCan` (data): The canonical δ-map A → B.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Crystalline.crystallizationMap` (data): The map of prisms α : (A,(d)) → (B,(p)).
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Crystalline.crystallizationMap_apply` (simp): α(a) = can(φ_A(a)) for a ∈ A.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Crystalline.crystallization_isCrystalline` (characterisation): The prism ideal of B is (p).
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Crystalline.crystallization_frobenius_unit` (relation): can(φ_A(d)) = p·u for a unit u of B.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Crystalline.crystallization_cohomology` (compatibility): For R p-completely smooth over A/(d) and R_B its base change, the base change map Δ_{R/A} → α_*Δ_{R_B/B} induces α̂^*Δ_{R/A} ≃ Δ_{R_B/B}.

**Unit tests.**

- `pr1_crystallization_alpha_d` (computation): α(d) lies in pB.
- `pr1_crystallization_alpha_eq` (compatibility): α = can ∘ φ_A; in particular α(d) = can(d)^p + p·can(δ(d)).
- `pr1_crystallization_can_not_prism_map` (non-example): If A/(p,d) ≠ 0 then can(d) ∉ pB: the untwisted canonical map A → B does not carry (d) into (p), so it is not a map of prisms (A,(d)) → (B,(p)).

**Acceptance.** For the universal oriented prism A_0 the ring D_0 = A_0{φ(d)/p}^∧ receives Z_p, and (Z_p,(p)) → (D_0,(p)) is a map of crystalline prisms. For the Breuil–Kisin prism (W(k)[[u]],(E(u))) the construction gives the p-completed PD envelope of (E(u)), a ring of Breuil type, with α induced by φ. α(d) = φ(d) is p times a unit; the canonical image of d is not in pB.

**Sources.** [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Construction 6.1. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 51. The node is Construction 6.1 with its properties (1)–(3), under the hypothesis as corrected in the register..

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-1-crystalline-comparison-syntomic"></a>

### The crystalline comparison for syntomic algebras

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/crystalline-comparison-syntomic` · theorem. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.Crystalline` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/Crystalline/Comparison`.

Let (A,(p)) be a crystalline prism, J ⊂ A a PD ideal with p ∈ J, and R a syntomic A/J-algebra (flat, of finite presentation, with local complete intersection fibres). Put R^{(1)} := R ⊗_{A/J,ψ} A/p. Then there is a canonical Frobenius-compatible isomorphism of E_∞-A-algebras RΓ((R^{(1)}/A)_Δ, O_Δ) ≃ RΓ_crys(R/A), where the left side is the cohomology of the prismatic site of R^{(1)} and the right side is crystalline cohomology relative to the PD thickening Spec(A/J) ⊂ Spf(A). For R smooth this is PR.1/crystalline-comparison.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** (A,(p)) crystalline; J a PD ideal containing p; R syntomic over A/J. The left side is site cohomology. Its identification with derived prismatic cohomology of R^{(1)}, and the extension of the comparison from quasiregular semiperfect F_p-algebras to all quasisyntomic F_p-algebras by descent, belong to PrismaticCohomology:PR.2 (nodes derived-agrees-with-site, qrsp-prism and quasisyntomic-descent) and consume this node; they are not asserted here. For J ≠ (p) the reduction to J = (p) uses a syntomic lift of R to A/p, which exists Zariski-locally (a relative global complete intersection lifts by lifting its equations, and flatness is checked on the unchanged fibres); the canonical map of the smooth case glues the local isomorphisms.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Presentation: choose B_0 → R̃ with B_0 a p-completed polynomial A-algebra and R̃ a (local) syntomic lift over A/p. In each cosimplicial degree the kernel of B^n → R̃ is the filtered union of ideals (p, x_1,…,x_r) with (x_1,…,x_r) p-completely regular relative to A (Anschütz–Le Bras Remark 3.1.8). Hence PR.0/regular-prismatic-envelopes applies along the colimit: the envelopes C^n exist, are p-completely flat over A and form a weakly initial Čech nerve, exactly as in PR.1/cech-alexander-complex.
2. The cohomology of the site (R̃/A)_Δ is lim C^• by the argument of PR.1/cech-alexander-computes-cohomology, which only uses a weakly initial object and the acyclicity of O_Δ on objects; termwise base change gives φ_A^*C^• for R^{(1)}.
3. The crystalline side is computed by the cosimplicial PD envelope D^• for any R (CR.2), and D^• = B^•{φ(J^•)/p}^∧ by PR.0/pd-envelope-as-delta-envelope, since the kernels are ind-regular modulo p.
4. The comparison map φ_A^*C^• → D^• and the proof that it is a quasi-isomorphism (PR.1/relative-frobenius-cosimplicial-lemma, which concerns only the polynomial Čech nerve, then derived Nakayama) and Frobenius-compatible are those of PR.1/crystalline-comparison.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/crystalline-comparison`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-crystalline-comparison); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/cech-alexander-complex`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-cech-alexander-complex); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/cech-alexander-computes-cohomology`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-cech-alexander-computes-cohomology); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/relative-frobenius-cosimplicial-lemma`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-relative-frobenius-cosimplicial-lemma); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/regular-prismatic-envelopes`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-regular-prismatic-envelopes); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/pd-envelope-as-delta-envelope`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-pd-envelope-as-delta-envelope); `CrystallineCohomology:CR.2`; `CrystallineCohomology:CR.0`.

**Acceptance.** R = F_p[x]/(x^n) over (Z_p,(p)): the prismatic site cohomology of R^{(1)} = R is RΓ_crys(R/Z_p), computed by the PD envelope of (x^n) in Z_p⟨x⟩ with its de Rham complex. R = k[x,y]/(xy) over W(k): a syntomic, non-smooth example. For R smooth the statement and the map coincide with PR.1/crystalline-comparison.

**Sources.** [ALB23](https://arxiv.org/abs/1907.10525v4), Remark 3.1.8 (2). Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 17. The node is the first assertion of Remark 3.1.8 (2) (routed item PAPER-ANSCHUTZ-LEBRAS-23/25).. [ALB23](https://arxiv.org/abs/1907.10525v4), Remark 3.1.8 (2), last sentence. <a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-1-hodge-tate-comparison-char-p"></a>

### The Hodge–Tate comparison in characteristic p

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/hodge-tate-comparison-char-p` · theorem. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.HodgeTate` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/HodgeTate/Comparison`.

Let (A,(p)) be a crystalline prism and S a smooth A/p-algebra. (1) For every f ∈ S the class β_p(f) ∈ H^1(Δ̄_{S/A}) has square zero, so the maps η^0_S, η^1_S of PR.1/bockstein-differential extend uniquely to a map of commutative differential graded A/p-algebras η^*_S : (Ω^*_{S/(A/p)}, d) → (H^*(Δ̄_{S/A}), β_p), the twists being trivialised by the generator p of I. (2) η^*_S is an isomorphism: H^i(Δ̄_{S/A}) ≅ Ω^i_{S/(A/p)}{−i} for all i. (3) The functor S ↦ Δ_{S/A} commutes with p-completed base change along every map of crystalline prisms (A,(p)) → (A′,(p)): Δ_{S/A} ⊗̂^L_A A′ ≃ Δ_{S ⊗_A A′/A′}.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** (A,(p)) is a crystalline prism; S is smooth over A/p. The source states (2) for 'the comparison map from Theorem 4.11', whose construction for p = 2 rests on Lemma 4.10, itself deduced from Proposition 6.2, whose proof uses this corollary. The order adopted here removes the circle: (1) is proved together with (2) from the Cartier isomorphism, and Proposition 6.2 then only uses the statement for η^0 and η^1 of the affine line. The Cartier isomorphism is imported from DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.3/polynomial-cartier-map (red-team finding RT-AREA-padic-2/26).

**Construction or proof.**

1. Reductions. By PR.1/etale-localization and the local structure of smooth algebras (Zariski-locally étale over a polynomial algebra) both sides localise, so S = A/p[X_1,…,X_n]. A is p-torsion-free, so Z_p → A is p-completely flat and PR.1/base-change-finite-tor-amplitude reduces to A = Z_p, S = F_p[X_1,…,X_n].
2. S = R^{(1)} for R = F_p[X_1,…,X_n], and PR.1/crystalline-comparison gives Δ_{S/Z_p} ≃ RΓ_crys(R/Z_p), hence Δ̄_{S/Z_p} ≃ RΓ_crys(R/Z_p) ⊗^L F_p ≃ Ω^•_{R/F_p}, the de Rham complex of R (crystalline cohomology of R is the de Rham complex of the lift Z_p⟨X⟩; requested from CR.2). The S-algebra structure of H^0 corresponds to the relative Frobenius S = R^{(1)} → H^0(Ω^•_{R/F_p}).
3. Cartier isomorphism (DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.3/polynomial-cartier-map): C^{−1} : Ω^i_{R^{(1)}/F_p} ≅ H^i(Ω^•_{R/F_p}) is an isomorphism of graded R^{(1)}-algebras. So H^*(Δ̄_{S/Z_p}) ≅ Ω^*_S as graded S-algebras; this algebra is strictly graded-commutative, which gives (1).
4. Identification with η^*. On the lift Z_p⟨X⟩ with φ(X_j) = X_j^p, the Bockstein of the class of x^p is the class of d(φ(x̃))/p = x^{p−1}dx + dδ(x̃), which is C^{−1}(dx). So η^1_S = C^{−1} on generators, and η^*_S = C^{−1} by multiplicativity; this proves (2).
5. (3): by derived Nakayama it suffices to compare modulo p, where both sides have cohomology Ω^i, which commutes with base change.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/crystalline-comparison`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-crystalline-comparison); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/etale-localization`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-etale-localization); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/base-change-finite-tor-amplitude`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-base-change-finite-tor-amplitude); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/bockstein-differential`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-bockstein-differential); `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.3/polynomial-cartier-map`; `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.2/ordinary-de-rham-complex`; `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.2`; `CrystallineCohomology:CR.2`; `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`; [`mathlib:Algebra.Smooth`](#mathlib-algebra-smooth); `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.4`; `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.3`.

**Acceptance.** S = F_p[X] over Z_p: H^0(Δ̄) = F_p[X], H^1(Δ̄) = F_p[X]·β_p(X), H^i = 0 for i ≥ 2; under the crystalline comparison β_p(X) is the class of X^{p−1}dX. S = F_2[X] (p = 2): β_2(X)² = 0. Base change: for a map of crystalline prisms Z_p → W(k), Δ_{F_p[X]/Z_p} ⊗̂ W(k) ≃ Δ_{k[X]/W(k)}.
