### The Hodge–Tate comparison for the affine line and the vanishing of β(f)²

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/hodge-tate-affine-line` · theorem. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.HodgeTate` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/HodgeTate/Comparison`.

Let (A,I) be a bounded prism and R = A/I⟨X⟩ the p-adic completion of the polynomial ring in one variable. Then η^0_R : R → H^0(Δ̄_{R/A}) and η^1_R : Ω^1_{R/(A/I)} → H^1(Δ̄_{R/A}){1} are isomorphisms and H^i(Δ̄_{R/A}) = 0 for i > 1. Consequently (Lemma 4.10): for every bounded prism (A,I), every smooth p-adic formal scheme X over A/I and every local section f of O_X, the element β_I(f) ∈ H^1(Δ̄_{X/A}){1} has square zero.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** (A,I) is an arbitrary bounded prism; no orientation and no torsion-freeness is assumed. Only the maps η^0 and η^1 of PR.1/bockstein-differential occur in the statement; the full map η^* is constructed afterwards (PR.1/hodge-tate-comparison-map). The printed proof refers to Ω^1_{R/(A/d)} for a general prism; it is Ω^1_{R/(A/I)}.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Choose η : R ⊕ Ω^1_{R/(A/I)}{−1}[−1] → Δ̄_{R/A} in D(R) inducing η^0 and η^1{−1} on cohomology, possible since both modules are finite free over R; it suffices that η is an isomorphism. The consequence follows by functoriality: f defines A/I⟨X⟩ → O_X(U), and β_I(X)² lies in H^2 = 0.
2. I = (p): this is PR.1/hodge-tate-comparison-char-p for S = A/p[X] in degrees 0 and 1.
3. Universal oriented prism (A_0,(d)): the base change α̂^* of PR.1/crystallization-of-oriented-prism is conservative and carries Δ̄_{R/A_0} to Δ̄_{R_{D_0}/D_0} and η to the corresponding map over the crystalline prism (D_0,(p)), which is an isomorphism by the previous step.
4. General oriented bounded prism (A,(d)): the orientation gives A_0 → A; with a : A_0 → D_0 the map α and E := A ⊗̂^L_{A_0} D_0, b : A → E, c : Z_p → E, the functor b̂^* is conservative on (p,d)-complete objects. Using the base-change-compatible Čech–Alexander complex of the affine line (PR.1/cech-alexander-complex, Remark 4.19) and Lemma 4.22 (b and c have finite complete Tor amplitude), b̂^*Δ̄_{R/A} ≃ ĉ^*Δ̄_{F_p[X]/Z_p}, compatibly with the maps η; the claim reduces to the case A = Z_p already treated.
5. General bounded prism: there is a faithfully flat map of bounded prisms (A,I) → (A′,(d)) with A′ oriented (PR.0/bounded-prism-complete-flatness, Lemma 3.7 (4)); flat base change (PR.1/base-change-finite-tor-amplitude) and faithful flatness reduce to the oriented case.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/bockstein-differential`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-bockstein-differential); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/hodge-tate-comparison-char-p`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-hodge-tate-comparison-char-p); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/crystallization-of-oriented-prism`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-crystallization-of-oriented-prism); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/base-change-finite-tor-amplitude`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-base-change-finite-tor-amplitude); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/cech-alexander-complex`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-cech-alexander-complex); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/cech-alexander-computes-cohomology`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-cech-alexander-computes-cohomology); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/bounded-prism-complete-flatness`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-bounded-prism-complete-flatness); `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`; [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/universal-oriented-prism`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-universal-oriented-prism).

**Acceptance.** A = Z_p: Δ̄_{F_p[X]/Z_p} has H^0 = F_p[X], H^1 = F_p[X]·β(X), nothing else. q-de Rham prism: for R = Z_p[ζ_p]⟨X⟩ over (Z_p[[q−1]],([p]_q)), H^1(Δ̄_{R/A}) is free of rank one over R. p = 2: β_I(f)² = 0 for every f, which graded commutativity alone does not give.

**Sources.** [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Proposition 6.2, the paragraph before it, and its proof. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 51. <a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-1-hodge-tate-comparison-map"></a>

### The Hodge–Tate comparison map η^*

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/hodge-tate-comparison-map` · construction. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.HodgeTate` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/HodgeTate/Comparison`.

Let (A,I) be a bounded prism and X a smooth p-adic formal scheme over A/I. There is a unique map η^*_X : (Ω^*_{X/(A/I)}, d) → (H^*(Δ̄_{X/A}){∗}, β_I) of sheaves of commutative differential graded A/I-algebras on X_ét which in degree 0 is the structure map η^0_X : O_X → H^0(Δ̄_{X/A}); in degree 1 it is η^1_X, f dg ↦ f β_I(g), and η^i(f_0 df_1 ∧ … ∧ df_i) = f_0 β_I(f_1) ⋯ β_I(f_i). It is O_X-linear in each degree, compatible with the O_X-module structures, functorial in X and compatible with maps of bounded prisms. Its construction depends functorially only on the commutative algebra object Δ_{X/A} ∈ D(X_ét, A) together with the O_X-algebra structure on Δ_{X/A} ⊗^L_A A/I. For X = Spf(R) one writes η^i_R : Ω^i_{R/(A/I)} → H^i(Δ̄_{R/A}){i}. Here Ω^i is the p-completed module of differential forms.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** (A,I) is a bounded prism and X is smooth over A/I. The existence of η^* uses Lemma 4.10: β_I(f)² = 0 for every local section f of O_X. For p odd this follows from graded commutativity; for p = 2 it is deduced from the affine line (PR.1/hodge-tate-affine-line), by functoriality along A/I⟨T⟩ → O_X(U), T ↦ f. The universal property used is that of the de Rham complex: Ω^*_{R/k} is initial among graded-commutative differential graded k-algebras E with a k-algebra map R → E^0 such that squares of the elements d(r) vanish (completed form for p-completely smooth R).

**Construction or proof.**

1. By PR.1/bockstein-differential the target is a graded-commutative dg A/I-algebra with O_X → H^0 and with η^0 ⊕ η^1 compatible with d and β_I.
2. Lemma 4.10 (from PR.1/hodge-tate-affine-line): β_I(f)² = 0. Hence the elements β_I(f) generate a strictly graded-commutative sub-dg-algebra, and the universal property of the de Rham complex (requested from DD.2, built on DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.2/ordinary-de-rham-complex) extends η^0 ⊕ η^1 uniquely to η^*.
3. Functoriality in X and in the prism follows from uniqueness; the sheaf version is obtained from the affine maps η^*_R by Zariski and étale gluing.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/bockstein-differential`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-bockstein-differential); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/hodge-tate-affine-line`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-hodge-tate-affine-line); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/hodge-tate-cohomology`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-hodge-tate-cohomology); `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.2/ordinary-de-rham-complex`; `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.2`; [`mathlib:KaehlerDifferential`](#mathlib-kaehlerdifferential).

**Consumers.** Bhatt–Scholze Theorems 4.11 and 6.3: the Hodge–Tate comparison is the statement that η^* is an isomorphism. Bhatt–Scholze Proposition 4.15: the maps H^i(μ), i = 0, 1, of the cotangent complex comparison are identified with η^0, η^1. PrismaticCohomology:PR.2 (Construction 7.6): the derived Hodge–Tate comparison is the left Kan extension of η^* on the canonical filtration. PerfectoidQuotients:Q1: exports the Hodge–Tate comparison for smooth algebras.

**Planning API.**

- `TauCeti.Prismatic.HodgeTate.comparisonMap` (data): The R-linear map η^i_R : Ω^i_{R/(A/I)} → H^i(Δ̄_{R/A}){i}, for every i ≥ 0.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.HodgeTate.comparisonMap_one` (simp): η^1_R(dg) = β_I(η^0_R(g)).
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.HodgeTate.comparisonMap_wedge` (relation): η^{i+j}_R(ω ∧ τ) = η^i_R(ω) ∪ η^j_R(τ).
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.HodgeTate.comparisonMap_d` (relation): η^{i+1}_R(dω) = β_I(η^i_R(ω)), for d the de Rham differential.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.HodgeTate.bockstein_eta0_cup_self` (relation): β_I(η^0_R(f)) ∪ β_I(η^0_R(f)) = 0 for every f ∈ R (Lemma 4.10).

**Unit tests.**

- `pr1_comparison_map_one_formula` (computation): η^1_R(f dg) = f·β_I(η^0_R(g)).
- `pr1_comparison_map_base` (degenerate): For R = A/I, η^0 : A/I → H^0(Δ̄_{(A/I)/A}) is bijective and Ω^i = 0 for i > 0.
- `pr1_comparison_map_square_zero` (characterisation): η^2_R(dg ∧ dg) = 0 = β_I(g) ∪ β_I(g), also for p = 2.

**Acceptance.** η^1_R(f dg) = f·β_I(g). For R = A/I the map is the identity of A/I in degree 0. For an étale map R → S the maps η^*_R and η^*_S are compatible with Ω^i_R ⊗_R S ≅ Ω^i_S and with PR.1/etale-localization.

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-1-hodge-tate-comparison"></a>

### The Hodge–Tate comparison theorem

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/hodge-tate-comparison` · theorem. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.HodgeTate` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/HodgeTate/Comparison`.

Let (A,I) be a bounded prism and X a smooth p-adic formal scheme over A/I. The Hodge–Tate comparison map η^*_X : (Ω^*_{X/(A/I)}, d) → (H^*(Δ̄_{X/A}){∗}, β_I) is an isomorphism of sheaves of differential graded A/I-algebras on X_ét. In particular Δ̄_{X/A} ∈ D(X_ét, O_X) is a perfect complex with H^i(Δ̄_{X/A}) ≅ Ω^i_{X/(A/I)}{−i}, zero for i larger than the relative dimension. For X = Spf(R) affine: Ω^i_{R/(A/I)}{−i} ≅ H^i(Δ_{R/A} ⊗^L_A A/I) as R-modules, for every i.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** (A,I) is a bounded prism; X is smooth over A/I (R p-completely smooth over A/I). Without smoothness the statement fails for site cohomology. The twist is {−i} = ⊗_{A/I} (I/I²)^{⊗ −i}; there is no Frobenius twist in this comparison. Ω^i denotes p-completed differential forms, a finite locally free O_X-module.

**Construction or proof.**

1. The map is globally defined (PR.1/hodge-tate-comparison-map), so the statement is local: it suffices to prove that η^i_R is an isomorphism for every p-completely smooth R.
2. Both sides localise for the étale topology: Ω^i_R ⊗_R S = Ω^i_S and PR.1/etale-localization. Since X is Zariski-locally étale over a completed affine space, one may take R = A/I⟨X_1,…,X_n⟩.
3. Choose η : ⊕_{i=0}^n Ω^i_{R/(A/I)}{−i}[−i] → Δ̄_{R/A} in D(R) lifting the maps η^i{−i} (the modules are finite free) and prove it is an isomorphism exactly as in PR.1/hodge-tate-affine-line: for I = (p) by PR.1/hodge-tate-comparison-char-p; for the universal oriented prism by PR.1/crystallization-of-oriented-prism; for an oriented prism by the pushout E and the base-change-compatible Čech–Alexander complex of A⟨X_1,…,X_n⟩; in general by faithfully flat base change to an oriented prism.
4. Perfectness: Δ̄_{X/A} has finitely many nonzero cohomology sheaves, each finite locally free.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/hodge-tate-comparison-map`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-hodge-tate-comparison-map); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/hodge-tate-affine-line`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-hodge-tate-affine-line); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/hodge-tate-comparison-char-p`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-hodge-tate-comparison-char-p); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/etale-localization`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-etale-localization); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/crystallization-of-oriented-prism`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-crystallization-of-oriented-prism); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/base-change-finite-tor-amplitude`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-base-change-finite-tor-amplitude); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/cech-alexander-complex`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-cech-alexander-complex); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/bounded-prism-complete-flatness`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-bounded-prism-complete-flatness); `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2`; `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.2`; `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.4`.

**Acceptance.** Smooth polynomial algebra: for R = A/I⟨X_1,…,X_n⟩, H^i(Δ̄_{R/A}) is free over R on the classes β_I(X_{j_1}) ⋯ β_I(X_{j_i}), j_1 < … < j_i, twisted by {−i}. Torus: R = A/I⟨X^{±1}⟩ gives H^1(Δ̄_{R/A}){1} free over R on η^1(dX/X) = X^{−1}β_I(X). A_inf prism and R = O_C⟨X⟩: H^1(Δ̄) ≅ Ω^1_{R/O_C}{−1}, the Breuil–Kisin–Fargues twist of BMS1.

**Sources.** [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Theorem 4.11. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 40. The node is Theorem 4.11.. ### Base change for prismatic cohomology

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/prismatic-base-change` · theorem. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.Site` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/Site/Basic`.

Let (A,I) → (B,IB) be a map of bounded prisms, X a smooth p-adic formal scheme over A/I, X_B := X ×_{Spf(A/I)} Spf(B/IB) and g : X_B → X the projection. Then (g^*Δ_{X/A})^∧ ≅ Δ_{X_B/B} in D(X_{B,ét}, B), the completion being derived (p,I)-adic, and (g^*Δ̄_{X/A})^∧ ≅ Δ̄_{X_B/B} with p-adic completion. For X = Spf(R): Δ_{R/A} ⊗̂^L_A B ≃ Δ_{R ⊗̂_A B/B}. If X is quasi-compact and quasi-separated then RΓ_Δ(X/A) ⊗̂^L_A B ≃ RΓ_Δ(X_B/B). Consequence (the φ_A-twisted crystalline comparison): for a crystalline prism (A,(p)) and R smooth over A/p, base change along the map of prisms φ_A : (A,(p)) → (A,(p)) gives φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} := Δ_{R/A} ⊗̂^L_{A,φ_A} A ≃ Δ_{R^{(1)}/A} ≃ RΓ_crys(R/A), compatibly with Frobenius; for X smooth, quasi-compact and quasi-separated over A/p, RΓ_crys(X/A) ≃ RΓ_Δ(X/A) ⊗̂^L_{A,φ_A} A.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** Both prisms are bounded; no flatness or Tor amplitude hypothesis on A → B. X is smooth over A/I. The statement for global sections requires X quasi-compact and quasi-separated: completed base change does not commute with infinite products. Theorem 1.8 (5) of the source omits this hypothesis (source issue PrismaticCohomology/E13); the sheaf statement, Corollary 4.12, needs no such hypothesis. φ_A : A → A is a map of prisms (A,(p)) → (A,(p)) only for crystalline prisms; for a general prism the Frobenius twist φ_A^*Δ_{X/A} is not the prismatic cohomology of a base change over (A,I).

**Construction or proof.**

1. By derived Nakayama (DD.1) it suffices to prove the statement modulo I: (g^*Δ̄_{X/A})^∧ ≅ Δ̄_{X_B/B}.
2. Both sides are perfect complexes with cohomology sheaves Ω^i{−i} by PR.1/hodge-tate-comparison, the base change map is compatible with the maps η^* (functoriality of PR.1/hodge-tate-comparison-map in the prism), and completed differential forms commute with base change (DD.2).
3. Global sections: use the projection formula and completed flat base change for quasi-coherent complexes on a quasi-compact quasi-separated formal scheme, requested from DD.5. Reduce through a finite affine cover and finite affine covers of its quasi-compact intersections; use quasi-coherent affine acyclicity to obtain a finite descent calculation. Completed scalar extension is exact and commutes with the finite limits in that calculation. A full unbounded Čech totalization does not commute with arbitrary scalar extension merely because the first cover is finite.
4. Consequence: apply the affine statement to φ_A : (A,(p)) → (A,(p)) and PR.1/crystalline-comparison with I = (p), noting R ⊗_{A/p,Frob} A/p = R^{(1)}.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/hodge-tate-comparison`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-hodge-tate-comparison); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/hodge-tate-comparison-map`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-hodge-tate-comparison-map); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/hodge-tate-cohomology`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-hodge-tate-cohomology); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/relative-prismatic-cohomology`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-relative-prismatic-cohomology); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/crystalline-comparison`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-crystalline-comparison); `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`; `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.2`; `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2`.

**Acceptance.** Crystalline base: for (Z_p,(p)) → (W(k),(p)), Δ_{F_p[X]/Z_p} ⊗̂ W(k) ≃ Δ_{k[X]/W(k)}. For the map of prisms α = can∘φ : (A_inf, ker θ) → (A_crys,(p)) (Construction 6.1 with d = ξ) and X smooth, quasi-compact and quasi-separated over O_C: RΓ_Δ(X/A_inf) ⊗̂^L_{A_inf,α} A_crys ≃ RΓ_Δ(Y/A_crys) with Y = X ×_{Spf O_C} Spf(A_crys/p) = (X_{O_C/p})^{(1)}; by PR.1/crystalline-comparison for the PD ideal ker(A_crys → O_C/p) the right side is RΓ_crys(X_{O_C/p}/A_crys), the A_crys-comparison of BMS1. Non-example: for X an infinite disjoint union of copies of Spf(F_p) over (Z_p,(p)) and B = Z_p⟨x⟩, the map (∏ Z_p) ⊗̂ Z_p⟨x⟩ → ∏ Z_p⟨x⟩ is not surjective.

### The de Rham comparison (W(A/I) p-torsion-free)

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/de-rham-comparison` · theorem. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.DeRham` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/DeRham/Comparison`.

Let (A,I) be a bounded prism such that the ring of p-typical Witt vectors W(A/I) is p-torsion-free, and let X be a smooth p-adic formal scheme over A/I. Then there is a natural isomorphism Δ_{X/A} ⊗̂^L_{A,φ_A} A/I ≃ Ω^*_{X/(A/I)} of commutative algebra objects of D(X_ét, A/I), where A/I is an A-algebra through A → A → A/I, the first map being φ_A, the completion is p-adic, and the right side is the p-completed de Rham complex. More precisely, for a p-completely smooth A/I-algebra R there is a functorial isomorphism Δ_{R/A} ⊗̂^L_{A,ψ} W(A/I) ≃ RΓ_crys((R/p)/W(A/I)) of commutative algebra objects of D(W(A/I)), where ψ : A → W(A/I) is the composite of the δ-map A → W(A/I) lifting A → A/I with the Witt vector Frobenius, and the crystalline cohomology is relative to the PD ideal ker(W(A/I) → A/(I,p)); reducing along W(A/I) → A/I gives the first isomorphism. If X is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, RΓ_dR(X/(A/I)) ≃ RΓ_Δ(X/A) ⊗̂^L_{A,φ_A} A/I.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** (A,I) is a bounded prism and W(A/I) is p-torsion-free. This holds if A/I is p-torsion-free, or if I = (p) and A/p is reduced. This is the hypothesis of Theorem 6.4 (red-team finding RT-AREA-padic-2/27). The statement for every bounded prism, without the hypothesis on W(A/I), is Corollary 15.4 of the source; it is deduced from the Lη_I factorisation of Frobenius and is the node PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/de-rham-comparison-general. It is not asserted here. The reduction is along the Frobenius-twisted map A → A/I. The untwisted reduction Δ_{X/A} ⊗^L_A A/I is Hodge–Tate cohomology, whose cohomology sheaves are Ω^i{−i} with the Bockstein as differential; the two are different objects. The proof of Theorem 6.4 is read with the correction of register entry PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22/E14: ψ carries I into FV W(A/I) = pW(A/I).

**Construction or proof.**

1. Reduce to the affine case by functoriality. The kernel J of W(A/I) → A/I → A/(I,p) is a PD ideal, and RΓ_crys((R/p)/W(A/I)) ⊗̂^L_{W(A/I)} A/I ≃ Ω^*_{R/(A/I)}, because R is a p-completely smooth lift of R/p over the PD thickening W(A/I) → A/I (crystalline cohomology is the de Rham cohomology of a smooth lift, with base change; requested from CR.2).
2. The map A → A/I lifts uniquely to a δ-map w : A → W(A/I) (PR.0/delta-ring-category: W is right adjoint to the forgetful functor). It carries I into V W(A/I), so ψ = F ∘ w carries I into FV W(A/I) = pW(A/I). As W(A/I) is p-torsion-free and p-complete, (W(A/I),(p)) is a bounded crystalline prism (PR.0/crystalline-prism) and ψ : (A,I) → (W(A/I),(p)) is a map of bounded prisms.
3. PR.1/prismatic-base-change along ψ: Δ_{R/A} ⊗̂^L_{A,ψ} W(A/I) ≃ Δ_{R′/W(A/I)} with R′ := R ⊗̂_{A/I,ψ} W(A/I)/p.
4. PR.1/crystalline-comparison for the crystalline prism W(A/I), the PD ideal J and the smooth W(A/I)/J = A/(I,p)-algebra R/p: its Frobenius twist (R/p)^{(1)} is R′, since A/(I,p) → W(A/I)/p is induced by the Witt vector Frobenius. Hence Δ_{R′/W(A/I)} ≃ RΓ_crys((R/p)/W(A/I)).
5. The composite A → W(A/I) → A/I of ψ with the projection is a ↦ φ_A(a) mod I (zeroth Witt component of F(w(a))), which gives the stated twist.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/prismatic-base-change`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-prismatic-base-change); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/crystalline-comparison`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-crystalline-comparison); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/relative-prismatic-cohomology`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-relative-prismatic-cohomology); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-ring-category`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-delta-ring-category); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/crystalline-prism`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-crystalline-prism); `CrystallineCohomology:CR.2`; `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.2`; `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.2/ordinary-de-rham-complex`; `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`; [`mathlib:WittVector`](#mathlib-wittvector); [`mathlib:WittVector.frobenius_verschiebung`](#mathlib-wittvector-frobenius-verschiebung).

**Acceptance.** A = Z_p[[u]], I = (E(u)), A/I = O_K p-torsion-free: Δ_{X/A} ⊗^L_{A,φ} O_K ≃ Ω^*_{X/O_K}. A = W(k), I = (p), k perfect: Δ_{R/W(k)} ⊗^L_{W(k),φ} k ≃ Ω^*_{R/k}; with the Cartier isomorphism this is consistent with Δ̄_{R/W(k)} having cohomology Ω^i_{R/k}. A hypothesis check: W(F_p[x]/(x²)) has p-torsion, and for A a p-torsion-free δ-lift of F_p[x]/(x²) the theorem does not apply; the statement is then PR.3/de-rham-comparison-general.

### Perfectness of prismatic cohomology of proper smooth formal schemes

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/proper-smooth-perfectness` · theorem. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.Site` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/Site/Basic`.

Let (A,I) be a bounded prism and X a proper smooth p-adic formal scheme over Spf(A/I). Then RΓ_Δ(X/A) is a perfect complex of A-modules, and RΓ(X_ét, Δ̄_{X/A}) = RΓ_Δ(X/A) ⊗^L_A A/I is a perfect complex of A/I-modules with a finite filtration whose graded pieces are RΓ(X, Ω^i_{X/(A/I)}){−i}[−i], 0 ≤ i ≤ dim(X/(A/I)). In particular RΓ_Δ(X/A) has Tor amplitude in [0, 2 dim], and its formation commutes with base change along every map of bounded prisms.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** (A,I) is a bounded prism; A/I need not be noetherian. X is proper and smooth over Spf(A/I): quasi-compact, separated, of finite relative dimension, with X ⊗ Z/p^n proper and smooth over A/(I,p^n) for all n. Perfectness is asserted for the complex of global sections, not for the individual cohomology modules H^i_Δ(X/A), which need not be finitely presented or flat.

**Construction or proof.**

1. By PR.1/hodge-tate-comparison, Δ̄_{X/A} ∈ D(X_ét, O_X) is perfect with cohomology sheaves Ω^i{−i}; the canonical filtration gives the filtration of RΓ(X, Δ̄_{X/A}) with the stated graded pieces.
2. For X proper and smooth over the p-complete ring A/I of bounded p^∞-torsion, RΓ(X, E) is a perfect complex of A/I-modules for every vector bundle E, and commutes with base change (finiteness for proper flat finitely presented morphisms without noetherian hypotheses, passed to the p-adic limit; requested from DD.5, with formal schemes from SF.4).
3. RΓ_Δ(X/A) is derived (p,I)-complete, A is classically (p,I)-complete (PR.0/bounded-prism-complete-flatness (1)) and RΓ_Δ(X/A) ⊗^L_A A/I is perfect over A/I; a derived I-complete complex over an I-adically complete ring whose reduction modulo I is perfect is perfect (requested from DD.1).
4. Base change: PR.1/prismatic-base-change for the quasi-compact and separated X; for perfect complexes the completed and the ordinary derived tensor product agree.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/hodge-tate-comparison`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-hodge-tate-comparison); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/prismatic-base-change`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-prismatic-base-change); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/hodge-tate-cohomology`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-hodge-tate-cohomology); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/bounded-prism-complete-flatness`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-bounded-prism-complete-flatness); `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.5`; `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`; `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.4`; `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2`.

**Acceptance.** X = P^1 over A/I: RΓ_Δ(X/A) ≃ A ⊕ A{−1}[−2] as a complex, of rank 2. X an abelian formal scheme of dimension g: RΓ_Δ(X/A) is perfect of amplitude [0,2g] with H^1 of rank 2g after base change to a field. For X affine of positive dimension (not proper), RΓ_Δ(X/A) is not perfect: H^0(Δ̄) = O(X) is not finitely generated over A/I.

**Sources.** [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Theorem 1.8, final sentence. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 4. ### Acceptance computations: polynomial algebra, étale chart, crystalline base, Frobenius twist

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/acceptance-computations` · application. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.Site` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/Site/Basic`.

(1) Smooth polynomial algebra. For a bounded prism (A,I) and R = A/I⟨X_1,…,X_n⟩, Δ_{R/A} is computed by the base-change-compatible Čech–Alexander complex of A⟨X_1,…,X_n⟩, and H^i(Δ̄_{R/A}){i} is the free R-module on the products β_I(X_{j_1}) ⋯ β_I(X_{j_i}), j_1 < … < j_i; so H^*(Δ̄_{R/A}){∗} is the exterior algebra over R on β_I(X_1),…,β_I(X_n) with differential determined by β_I(X_j^m) = m X_j^{m−1} β_I(X_j). (2) Étale chart. For a p-completely étale map A/I⟨X_1,…,X_n⟩ → S, H^i(Δ̄_{S/A}){i} ≅ Ω^i_{S/(A/I)} is free over S on the same classes, and Δ̄_{S/A} ≃ Δ̄_{A/I⟨X⟩/A} ⊗̂^L S. (3) Crystalline base. For (A,I) = (Z_p,(p)) and R = F_p[X], Δ_{R/Z_p} ≃ RΓ_crys(F_p[X]/Z_p) is the de Rham complex Z_p⟨X⟩ → Z_p⟨X⟩dX: H^0 = Z_p and H^1 is the cokernel of d, X^m ↦ mX^{m−1}dX; its reduction modulo p, which is Δ̄_{R/Z_p}, has cohomology F_p[X^p] in degree 0 and F_p[X^p]·X^{p−1}dX in degree 1, with β_p(X) the class of X^{p−1}dX. (4) Nontrivial Frobenius-twisted coefficient map. For A = W(k) with k = F_{p²} and R̃ = k[X,Y]/(Y² − X³ − aX − b) an affine elliptic curve whose j-invariant is not in F_p (p ≥ 5), the algebras R̃ and R̃^{(1)} = R̃ ⊗_{k,Frob} k are not isomorphic over k, and Δ_{R̃^{(1)}/W(k)} ≃ RΓ_crys(R̃/W(k)) while φ_A^*Δ_{R̃/W(k)} ≃ RΓ_crys(R̃/W(k)): the comparison holds only after the scalar extension along φ_A, which is not the identity on W(k). Likewise Δ_{R̃/W(k)} ⊗^L_{W(k),φ} k ≃ Ω^*_{R̃/k}, whereas the untwisted reduction Δ̄_{R̃/W(k)} = Δ_{R̃/W(k)} ⊗^L_{W(k)} k has cohomology modules Ω^i_{R̃/k} and is the de Rham complex of the Frobenius untwist R̃ ⊗_{k,Frob^{−1}} k, a curve not isomorphic to R̃.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** (1), (2): any bounded prism. (3): the crystalline prism (Z_p,(p)). (4): k = F_{p²}, p ≥ 5, a, b ∈ k with j-invariant outside F_p. In (3) the twist is invisible because F_p[X]^{(1)} = F_p[X] over F_p; (4) is chosen so that the twist changes the algebra. In (4) the two W(k)-module structures on RΓ_crys differ by φ; the complexes are abstractly isomorphic as complexes of abelian groups since φ is an automorphism of W(k).

**Construction or proof.**

1. (1): PR.1/hodge-tate-comparison for the polynomial ring, with the complex of PR.1/cech-alexander-complex (Remark 4.19) and the Leibniz rule of PR.1/bockstein-differential.
2. (2): PR.1/etale-localization and (1).
3. (3): PR.1/crystalline-comparison with A = Z_p, I = (p), R = F_p[X] = R^{(1)}, the de Rham computation of crystalline cohomology of the affine line (CR.2), and the identification of β_p in PR.1/hodge-tate-comparison-char-p.
4. (4): PR.1/crystalline-comparison for I = (p) over W(k), PR.1/prismatic-base-change along φ_A and PR.1/de-rham-comparison (W(k) is p-torsion-free and k is reduced); R̃^{(1)} is the curve with coefficients a^p, b^p, of j-invariant j^p ≠ j.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/hodge-tate-comparison`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-hodge-tate-comparison); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/etale-localization`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-etale-localization); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/crystalline-comparison`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-crystalline-comparison); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/prismatic-base-change`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-prismatic-base-change); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/de-rham-comparison`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-de-rham-comparison); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/cech-alexander-complex`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-cech-alexander-complex); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/bockstein-differential`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-bockstein-differential); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/hodge-tate-comparison-char-p`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-hodge-tate-comparison-char-p); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/crystalline-prism`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-crystalline-prism); `CrystallineCohomology:CR.2`.

**Acceptance.** Each of the four computations is a test of the corresponding comparison theorem with a wrong twist: (1) fails with the twist {i} in place of {−i} for a non-orientable prism, (3) fails if β is omitted, (4) fails without φ_A. The torus R = A/I⟨X^{±1}⟩ is an étale chart of the affine line and gives H^1(Δ̄_{R/A}){1} = R·η^1(dX/X).

**Sources.** [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Remark 4.19. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 43. Extend the smooth relative functor to animated A/I-algebras by a completed left Kan extension, so geometric realizations, the structure map to Hodge–Tate cohomology and the conjugate filtration are part of the interface. ### Derived prismatic cohomology

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/derived-prismatic-cohomology` · construction. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.Derived` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/Derived/Basic`.

Fix a bounded prism (A, I). Let Poly_{A/I} be the category of p-completed polynomial algebras (A/I)⟨x_1,…,x_n⟩, n ≥ 0, and Sm_{A/I} the category of p-completely smooth A/I-algebras. Let CAlg_φ(D_comp(A)) be the ∞-category of commutative algebra objects E of D_comp(A) equipped with a map of commutative algebras φ_E : E → φ_{A,*}E. PR.1 gives a functor Sm_{A/I} → CAlg_φ(D_comp(A)), R ↦ (Δ_{R/A}, φ_R). Derived prismatic cohomology is its left Kan extension Δ_{−/A} to the ∞-category of derived p-complete simplicial commutative A/I-algebras, with colimits in the target derived (p, I)-completed. Equivalently Δ_{−/A} is the unique functor on derived p-complete simplicial A/I-algebras that preserves sifted colimits and restricts to PR.1's functor on Poly_{A/I}; for a simplicial resolution P_• → R by objects of Poly_{A/I} (or by p-completely ind-smooth algebras) one has Δ_{R/A} ≃ (colim_{[n] ∈ Δ^op} Δ_{P_n/A})^∧, independently of the resolution. Derived Hodge–Tate cohomology is Δ̄_{R/A} := Δ_{R/A} ⊗^L_A A/I, a derived p-complete commutative algebra in D(R). The functor carries: (1) the unit A → Δ_{R/A}, with Δ_{(A/I)/A} = A; (2) the structure map R → Δ̄_{R/A}; (3) the φ_A-semilinear Frobenius φ_R : Δ_{R/A} → φ_{A,*}Δ_{R/A}, natural in R. For R in Sm_{A/I} the value is the site cohomology of PR.1 (node derived-agrees-with-site). Δ_{R/A} is an invariant of the animated ring R and not of π_0(R) alone (node derived-input-higher-homotopy).

**Hypotheses and conventions.** p is a fixed prime and (A, I) is a bounded prism (PR.0): A/I has bounded p^∞-torsion, and A is derived and classically (p, I)-complete. D(A) is the derived ∞-category of A-modules with cohomological indexing; D_comp(A) is the full subcategory of derived (p, I)-complete objects with its completed tensor product; "discrete" means concentrated in degree 0. A derived p-complete simplicial A/I-algebra is an animated commutative A/I-algebra (EnhancedDerivedSheaves E5:animation) whose underlying complex is derived p-complete (DD.1); tensor products of such algebras are derived and derived p-completed. PR.1's functor is used as a functor of ∞-categories; its coherence in R is supplied by the functorial Čech–Alexander complexes. The left Kan extension from Sm_{A/I} and the one from Poly_{A/I} agree; this is part of the statement and is proved through the Hodge–Tate comparison (BS22 Construction 7.6 (1)).

**Construction or proof.**

1. Coherent source functor: the functorial Čech–Alexander complex (PR.1) makes R ↦ (Δ_{R/A}, φ_R) a functor from Sm_{A/I} to cosimplicial derived (p, I)-complete δ-A-algebras, hence to CAlg_φ(D_comp(A)) after totalisation.
2. Animation: derived p-complete simplicial A/I-algebras are the derived p-complete objects (DD.1) of the animation of finitely generated polynomial A/I-algebras (E5:animation). By the universal property of animation (HTT 5.5.8.15) and the left Kan extension theorem of E3, the functor P ↦ Δ_{P^∧/A} on polynomial algebras extends uniquely to a sifted-colimit-preserving functor with values in D_comp(A); it inverts derived p-completion maps because its reduction modulo I has p-completed graded pieces, so it is defined on derived p-complete inputs.
3. Agreement of the two extensions: on Sm_{A/I} the complex Δ̄_{R/A} has the finite filtration τ^{≤i} with graded pieces Ω^i_{R/(A/I)}{−i}[−i] (PR.1, Hodge–Tate comparison), and R ↦ (Ω^i_{R/(A/I)})^∧ is left Kan extended from Poly_{A/I} (DD.0). By derived Nakayama for I (DD.1) the functor Δ_{−/A} on Sm_{A/I} is itself left Kan extended from Poly_{A/I}; hence the value on Sm_{A/I} is unchanged.
4. Structure maps: the unit, R → Δ̄_{R/A} and φ_R are the left Kan extensions of the corresponding natural transformations of PR.1; reduction modulo I commutes with the colimits because A/I is a perfect A-module (I is invertible).

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/relative-prismatic-cohomology`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-relative-prismatic-cohomology); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/cech-alexander-complex`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-cech-alexander-complex); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/frobenius-on-prismatic-cohomology`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-frobenius-on-prismatic-cohomology); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/hodge-tate-comparison`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-hodge-tate-comparison); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/hodge-tate-cohomology`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-hodge-tate-cohomology); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/prism`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-prism); `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E5:animation/animated-commutative-rings`; `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E5:animation/universal-property-of-animation`; `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E3/left-kan-extension-along-a-full-inclusion`; `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E5:abstract/algebra-objects`; `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.0`; `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`; [`mathlib:DerivedCategory`](#mathlib-derivedcategory); [`mathlib:CategoryTheory.SimplicialObject`](#mathlib-categorytheory-simplicialobject).

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-2-idempotent-retract-initial-object"></a>

### Initial objects as idempotent retracts

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/idempotent-retract-initial-object` · lemma. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.Semiperfectoid` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/Semiperfectoid/Discrete`.

Let C be an idempotent complete category and X an object of C. Let X/C be the category of objects Y of C equipped with a map X → Y. Assume that the identity functor of C factors through the projection X/C → C by a functor F : C → X/C. Then F(X) = (e : X → X) is an idempotent endomorphism of X, and the corresponding retract X′ of X is an initial object of C. In particular C has an initial object, and X is initial if and only if e is the identity.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** C is an ordinary category in which every idempotent splits. The factorisation may be given up to a natural isomorphism of the composite with the identity; this reduces to the strict case by transporting the structure maps along the isomorphism.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Write F(X) = (e : X → X). Applying F to the morphism e of C gives a morphism (X →e X) → (X →e X) in X/C with underlying map e, that is e ∘ e = e.
2. Split e as X → X′ → X. Then F(X′) = (X → X′) and this map is a (split) epimorphism.
3. F is faithful, so Hom_C(X′, Y) injects into Hom_{X/C}(X → X′, X → Y), which has at most one element because X → X′ is an epimorphism. There is at least one map X′ → X → Y. Hence X′ is initial.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`mathlib:CategoryTheory.IsIdempotentComplete`](#mathlib-categorytheory-isidempotentcomplete); [`mathlib:CategoryTheory.Under`](#mathlib-categorytheory-under); [`mathlib:CategoryTheory.Limits.IsTerminal`](#mathlib-categorytheory-limits-isterminal).

**Acceptance.** C the category of sets and X = ∅ with F(Y) = (∅ → Y): e is the identity and X is initial. C the category of pointed sets and X a two-point pointed set with F(Y) the constant map to the base point: e is the constant map and the retract is the one-point set. C = prisms over (A, I) with a map from R and X = (Δ_{R/A}, IΔ_{R/A}): BS22 Lemma 7.7 (3).

**Sources.** [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Lemma 7.8 and its proof. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 58. Exact statement..

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-2-finite-projective-modules-p-complete"></a>

### Finite projective modules over derived p-complete rings and their descent

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/finite-projective-modules-p-complete` · theorem. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.Semiperfectoid` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/Semiperfectoid/ModuleDescent`.

Let R be a derived p-complete ring with bounded p^∞-torsion. Then the natural functor from finite projective R-modules to the 2-limit over n of the categories of finite projective R/p^n-modules is an equivalence. Finite projective modules therefore have effective descent for p-completely faithfully flat covers between derived p-complete rings of bounded p-power torsion: for a p-completely faithfully flat map R → R′ of such rings, finite projective R-modules are equivalent to finite projective R′-modules with a descent datum over the p-completed tensor products R′ ⊗̂_R R′ and R′ ⊗̂_R R′ ⊗̂_R R′.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** p is a fixed prime; a derived p-complete ring with bounded p^∞-torsion is classically p-adically complete (DD.1). The completed tensor products are discrete with bounded p^∞-torsion (BMS2 Lemma 4.7 and Corollary 4.8).

**Construction or proof.**

1. R is classically p-complete, so finite projective modules lift uniquely along the tower R/p^n (Stacks Project, Tag 0D4B; requested from DD.1).
2. For a p-completely faithfully flat map R → R′ of p-complete rings with bounded p^∞-torsion, R/p^n → R′/p^n is faithfully flat for all n (BMS2 Corollary 4.8 (3); flatness from Lemma 4.7, surjectivity on spectra from n = 1).
3. Faithfully flat descent for finite projective modules along R/p^n → R′/p^n (SchemeAndStackFoundations SF.1), and a 2-limit of stacks is a stack.

**Direct prerequisites.** `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`; `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.1`; [`mathlib:Module.Projective`](#mathlib-module-projective); [`mathlib:Module.Finite`](#mathlib-module-finite); [`mathlib:Module.FaithfullyFlat`](#mathlib-module-faithfullyflat); [`mathlib:IsAdicComplete`](#mathlib-isadiccomplete).

**Acceptance.** R = Z_p: finite free Z_p-modules are compatible systems of finite free Z/p^n-modules. R → R′ = R⟨x^{1/p^∞}⟩: a finite projective R′-module with descent datum descends to R. The hypothesis of bounded p^∞-torsion is used to pass between derived and classical completeness and to make R/p^n → R′/p^n flat.

**Sources.** [ALB23](https://arxiv.org/abs/1907.10525v4), Appendix A, Lemma A.1 (published: Lemma A.1) and its proof. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 94. Exact statement and proof.. [BMS2](https://arxiv.org/abs/1802.03261v2), Corollary 4.8. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 20. The flatness of the reductions used in the proof..

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-2-conjugate-filtration"></a>

### Conjugate filtration on derived Hodge–Tate cohomology

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/conjugate-filtration` · construction. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.Derived` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/Derived/HodgeTate`.

For a bounded prism (A, I) and a derived p-complete simplicial A/I-algebra R, the conjugate filtration is the functorial increasing N-indexed filtration Fil_0^conj → Fil_1^conj → ⋯ → Δ̄_{R/A} by derived p-complete objects of D(R), defined as the derived p-completed left Kan extension, from p-completely smooth A/I-algebras, of the canonical filtration Fil_i^conj Δ̄_{R/A} := τ^{≤i} Δ̄_{R/A}. It is exhaustive (Δ̄_{R/A} is the derived p-completed colimit of the Fil_i^conj), multiplicative (there are maps Fil_i^conj ⊗^L_R Fil_j^conj → Fil_{i+j}^conj compatible with the product of Δ̄_{R/A}), natural in R (compatibility with base change of prisms is node derived-prismatic-base-change), and Fil_0^conj = R with Fil_0^conj → Δ̄_{R/A} the structure map. Its graded pieces gr_i^conj := cofib(Fil_{i−1}^conj → Fil_i^conj) are computed by node derived-hodge-tate-comparison. The filtration is not the Postnikov filtration of Δ̄_{R/A} outside the smooth case: for a nonzero regular quotient R = (A/I)/(f) with bounded p^∞-torsion, Δ̄_{R/A} is discrete while no Fil_i^conj → Δ̄_{R/A} is an isomorphism.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** p is a fixed prime and (A, I) is a bounded prism (PR.0): A/I has bounded p^∞-torsion, and A is derived and classically (p, I)-complete. A derived p-complete simplicial A/I-algebra is an animated commutative A/I-algebra (EnhancedDerivedSheaves E5:animation) whose underlying complex is derived p-complete (DD.1); tensor products of such algebras are derived and derived p-completed. Filtered objects are functors (N, ≤) → D(R); completed filtered tensor products and graded pieces are those of DD.1.

**Construction or proof.**

1. On Sm_{A/I} the canonical filtration τ^{≤i}Δ̄_{R/A} of the commutative algebra Δ̄_{R/A} ∈ D(R) is functorial and lax multiplicative, with gr_i = H^i(Δ̄_{R/A})[−i].
2. Left Kan extend the functor R ↦ (R, Fil_•^conj Δ̄_{R/A}) to derived p-complete simplicial A/I-algebras in filtered derived p-complete modules over the varying algebra (DD.1 for filtered objects; E3 and E5:animation for the extension).
3. Exhaustiveness: the extension commutes with colimits and colim_i τ^{≤i} is the identity on Sm_{A/I}. Fil_0: by PR.1, H^0(Δ̄_{R/A}) = R on Sm_{A/I}, and the left Kan extension of R ↦ R is the identity functor.
4. The non-example: for R = (A/I)/(f) the graded pieces are the free modules Γ^i_R(R·f̄){−i} of rank 1 (node derived-hodge-tate-comparison), so the cofibre of Fil_i^conj → Δ̄_{R/A} is a nonzero p-completely flat R-module.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/derived-prismatic-cohomology`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-derived-prismatic-cohomology); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/hodge-tate-comparison`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-hodge-tate-comparison); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/hodge-tate-cohomology`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-hodge-tate-cohomology); `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E3/left-kan-extension-along-a-full-inclusion`; `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E5:animation/universal-property-of-animation`; `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`.

**Consumers.** BS22 Example 7.9, Propositions 7.10 and 7.11: discreteness and flatness of Δ̄ are read off from the graded pieces. BS22 Theorem 12.2 (PR.3): the graded pieces of the Nygaard filtration are Fil_i^conj Δ̄_S{i}. ALB23 Propositions 3.2.1 and 3.5.1: Fil_1^conj is the cotangent complex over A; Künneth is checked on graded pieces.

**Planning API.**

- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Derived.conjFil` (constructor): The object Fil_i^conj Δ̄_{R/A} of D(R), for a discrete A/I-algebra R and i ∈ N.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Derived.conjFilMap_refl` (functoriality): The transition map for i ≤ i is the identity.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Derived.conjFilMap_trans` (functoriality): Transition maps compose: (i ≤ j) followed by (j ≤ k) is (i ≤ k).
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Derived.conjFilι` (projection): The map Fil_i^conj → Δ̄_{R/A}.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Derived.conjFilMap_ι` (compatibility): The transition map followed by Fil_j^conj → Δ̄_{R/A} is Fil_i^conj → Δ̄_{R/A}.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Derived.conjFilZeroIso` (characterisation): Fil_0^conj Δ̄_{R/A} is R in degree 0.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Derived.conjGr` (constructor): The graded piece gr_i^conj Δ̄_{R/A}, an object of D(R) with a map from Fil_i^conj.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Derived.conjFilMap` (functoriality): An A/I-algebra map R→S gives a filtered map Fil^conj_•Δ̄_R→Fil^conj_•Δ̄_S, after restriction of scalars to R; identity and composition hold. The graded maps are the corresponding maps on p-completed exterior powers of the cotangent complex.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Derived.conjFil_cofiber` (relation): For i≥0, Fil^conj_(i−1)→Fil^conj_i→gr^conj_i is a canonical cofibre sequence, with Fil^conj_(−1)=0.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Derived.conjFilCup` (structure): Pairings Fil^conj_i⊗^L_RFil^conj_j→Fil^conj_(i+j) respect transition maps, the degree-zero unit, and the cup product on Δ̄. The associated graded pairings are exterior products on the cotangent complex.

**Unit tests.**

- `pr2_conj_fil_zero` (degenerate): Fil_0^conj Δ̄_{R/A} ≃ R[0].
- `pr2_conj_fil_base` (degenerate): For R = A/I the map Fil_i^conj → Δ̄_{R/A} is an isomorphism for every i.
- `pr2_conj_fil_smooth_truncation` (compatibility): For R smooth over A/I, H^n(Fil_i^conj Δ̄_{R/A}) = 0 for n > i: the filtration is the canonical one.
- `pr2_conj_fil_not_postnikov` (non-example): For f a nonzerodivisor of A/I with (A/I)/(f) nonzero and of bounded p^∞-torsion, Fil_i^conj → Δ̄ is not an isomorphism for any i, although Δ̄ is discrete.

**Acceptance.** Fil_0^conj Δ̄_{R/A} = R for every R. For p-completely smooth R the filtration is τ^{≤i}Δ̄_{R/A}, so Fil_i^conj ∈ D^{≤i}. For R = A/I every Fil_i^conj → Δ̄_{R/A} = A/I is an isomorphism. For a nonzero regular quotient the filtration is strictly increasing although Δ̄ is discrete.

**Sources.** [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Construction 7.6. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 56. The filtration is asserted there; the node gives its construction by left Kan extension of the canonical filtration.. <a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-2-comparison-to-prisms"></a>

### The comparison map from derived prismatic cohomology to prisms and to site cohomology

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/comparison-to-prisms` · construction. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.Derived` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/Derived/Site`.

Let (A, I) be a bounded prism and R a derived p-complete simplicial A/I-algebra. For every prism (B, J) over (A, I), bounded or not, equipped with an A/I-algebra map π_0(R) → B/J, there is a map ev_{(B,J)} : Δ_{R/A} → B of commutative algebras in D_comp(A), natural in (B, J) and in R, commuting with Frobenius (φ_B ∘ ev = ev ∘ φ_R), whose reduction modulo I is a map Δ̄_{R/A} → B/J of R-algebras. These maps assemble to the comparison map c_R : Δ_{R/A} → lim_{(B,J)} B = RΓ((π_0(R)/A)_Δ, O_Δ) to the cohomology of the prismatic site of π_0(R). Construction: the functor R ↦ RΓ((π_0(R)/A)_Δ, O_Δ) restricts on p-completed polynomial algebras to PR.1's functor, and c is the unique natural transformation out of the left Kan extension extending the identity there; concretely, for a resolution R_• → R by p-completely ind-smooth algebras, Δ_{R/A} = colim_{Δ^op} lim_{C ∈ (R_•/A)_Δ} C and (B, J) defines compatible objects of all (R_n/A)_Δ, which gives Δ_{R/A} → colim_{Δ^op} B = B. The map c_R is an isomorphism for p-completely smooth R (node derived-agrees-with-site), for regular quotients (node regular-quotient-prismatic-envelope) and for quasiregular semiperfectoid R over a perfect prism (node qrsp-prism). It is not an isomorphism in general: the target depends only on π_0(R) and lies in D^{≥0}, whereas Δ_{R/A} does not (node derived-input-higher-homotopy).

**Hypotheses and conventions.** p is a fixed prime and (A, I) is a bounded prism (PR.0): A/I has bounded p^∞-torsion, and A is derived and classically (p, I)-complete. A derived p-complete simplicial A/I-algebra is an animated commutative A/I-algebra (EnhancedDerivedSheaves E5:animation) whose underlying complex is derived p-complete (DD.1); tensor products of such algebras are derived and derived p-completed. The cohomology of O_Δ on the site of bounded prisms is the limit over the category, because O_Δ is a sheaf with vanishing higher Čech cohomology (PR.1, BS22 Corollary 3.12 and Remark 4.5). When Δ_{R/A} is discrete, ev_{(B,J)} is a map of δ-rings (node derived-agrees-with-site).

**Construction or proof.**

1. Čech–Alexander theory (PR.1): for p-completely ind-smooth P, Δ_{P/A} = lim_{C ∈ (P/A)_Δ} C, also over the category of all prisms, since the weakly initial object and its Čech nerve are bounded and their universal property holds for all prisms.
2. Left Kan extension: the functor R ↦ lim over prisms under π_0(R) receives the canonical transformation from the left Kan extension of its restriction to polynomial algebras (E3); project to the factor indexed by (B, J).
3. Frobenius and multiplicativity: each projection lim_C C → B is a map of commutative algebras commuting with the Frobenius lifts of the prisms; reduction modulo I is compatible with the maps from R.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/derived-prismatic-cohomology`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-derived-prismatic-cohomology); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/cech-alexander-complex`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-cech-alexander-complex); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/prismatic-structure-sheaf`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-prismatic-structure-sheaf); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/relative-prismatic-site`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-relative-prismatic-site); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/prism-category`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-prism-category); `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E3/left-kan-extension-along-a-full-inclusion`; `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E5:animation/universal-property-of-animation`.

**Consumers.** BS22 Lemma 7.7 (3) and Proposition 7.10: weak initiality of Δ_{R/A} and the identification with the initial prism. BS22 Proposition 8.5 and Corollary 8.14: the map Δ_{S/A,perf} → RΓ((S/A)_Δ^perf, O_Δ) and the universal property of S_perfd. ALB23 Proposition 3.4.1: the canonical morphisms Δ_{R/A} → Δ^{init,unbdd}_{R/A} → Δ^init_{R/A}. PrismaticCohomology PR.4, PR.5: evaluation of derived prismatic cohomology on prisms of the absolute and perfect prismatic sites.

**Planning API.**

- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Derived.toPrism` (data): For a prism (B, J) over (A, I) and an A/I-algebra map R → B/J, the map ev : Δ_{R/A} → B in D(A).
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Derived.toPrism_frobenius` (compatibility): ev commutes with the Frobenius of Δ_{R/A} and of B.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Derived.toPrism_naturality` (functoriality): For a map of prisms (B, J) → (B′, J′) over (A, I) compatible with the maps from R, ev′ is ev followed by B → B′.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Derived.siteCohomology` (constructor): The object RΓ((R/A)_Δ, O_Δ) of D(A), the limit of B over all bounded prisms (B, J) over (A, I) with a map R → B/J.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Derived.toSite` (data): The comparison map c_R : Δ_{R/A} → RΓ((R/A)_Δ, O_Δ).
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Derived.toSite_isIso_of_smooth` (characterisation): For R smooth over A/I the map c_R is an isomorphism.

**Unit tests.**

- `pr2_to_prism_base` (degenerate): For R = A/I and (B, J) = (A, I), the map Δ_{(A/I)/A} → A is an isomorphism.
- `pr2_to_site_smooth` (compatibility): For R = A/I × A/I the comparison map c_R is an isomorphism.
- `pr2_to_prism_frobenius_base` (characterisation): For R = A/I and (B, J) = (A, I) the map ev commutes with φ_A.
- `pr2_evaluation_base_identity` (computation): For R=A/I and the base-prism object (A,I,id), evaluation ev:Δ_(R/A)→A is the identity under Δ_(R/A)=A; the site and all-prism limit comparison maps have this same base value.

**Acceptance.** R = A/I: Δ_{R/A} = A and ev_{(A,I)} is the identity. For p-completely smooth R the map c_R is an isomorphism. For R = A/I ⊗^L_{(A/I)⟨x⟩} A/I the map c_R : Δ_{R/A} → A is not an isomorphism. For a perfect prism and (B, J) perfect, ev_{(B,J)} factors through the perfection Δ_{R/A,perf}.

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-2-perfection-of-prismatic-cohomology"></a>

### Perfection of derived prismatic cohomology and perfectoidization

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/perfection-of-prismatic-cohomology` · construction. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.Perfection` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/Perfection/Basic`.

Fix a perfectoid ring R with perfect prism (A, I) = (A_inf(R), ker θ), I = (d), and a derived p-complete simplicial R-algebra S. (1) The perfection of Δ_{S/A} is Δ_{S/A,perf} := (colim(Δ_{S/A} → φ_*Δ_{S/A} → φ²_*Δ_{S/A} → ⋯))^∧ in D(A): the derived (p, I)-completed colimit of the transition maps φ_S, where φ^n_* is restriction of scalars along φ_A^n. It is a derived (p, I)-complete commutative algebra in D(A) with a φ_A-semilinear automorphism φ induced by φ_S and a canonical map can : Δ_{S/A} → Δ_{S/A,perf} of commutative algebras commuting with Frobenius. (2) The perfectoidization of S is S_perfd := Δ_{S/A,perf} ⊗^L_A A/I in D(R), a derived p-complete commutative algebra with a map S → Δ̄_{S/A} → S_perfd. Both constructions are functorial in S. They are objects distinct from Δ_{S/A} and Δ̄_{S/A}: can is an equivalence exactly when φ_S is one (node perfection-comparison). The definition is made relative to the base (A, I); see the hypotheses.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** (A, I) is a perfect prism: φ_A is bijective; then I = (d) for a distinguished nonzerodivisor d, R := A/I is an integral perfectoid ring and A = A_inf(R) (PR.0). S is a derived p-complete simplicial R-algebra, R = A/I; all tensor products are derived and completed. Independence of the perfect base prism, dependence on π_0(S) only, and the description through the perfect prismatic site are BS22 Proposition 8.5, which is not planned in this stage (recorded gap); every statement here is relative to the fixed perfect prism (A, I). The universal perfectoid ring of a semiperfectoid ring (BS22 Corollary 7.3) is a different construction, owned by PerfectoidQuotients Q2; the two agree whenever S_perfd is connective (node connective-perfectoidization-perfectoid).

**Construction or proof.**

1. The transition maps: φ_S : Δ_{S/A} → φ_{A,*}Δ_{S/A} is a map of commutative algebras in D(A) (node derived-prismatic-cohomology); apply φ^n_{A,*} and form the sequential colimit in D(A), then complete (DD.1).
2. Automorphism: the shift of the sequential diagram induces φ : Δ_{S/A,perf} → φ_{A,*}Δ_{S/A,perf}, an equivalence because the shifted diagram is cofinal; it is compatible with can by construction.
3. Reduction modulo I: A/I is a perfect A-module, so S_perfd is derived p-complete and receives Δ̄_{S/A}.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/derived-prismatic-cohomology`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-derived-prismatic-cohomology); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/prism-perfection`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-prism-perfection); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/perfect-prisms-perfectoid-rings`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-perfect-prisms-perfectoid-rings); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/ainf-prism`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-ainf-prism); `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`; `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E5:abstract/algebra-objects`; `PerfectoidQuotients:Q0:integral-algebra`; [`mathlib:DerivedCategory`](#mathlib-derivedcategory).

**Consumers.** BS22 Proposition 8.5, Corollaries 8.11–8.12 (proposed PerfectoidQuotientsPartIIIntegralPerfectoidization): S_perfd is identified with the limit of all perfectoid rings under S and with arc-cohomology of the structure sheaf. BS22 Theorems 9.1 and 9.4 (PR.4): the étale comparison is proved through the perfection: (Δ_{S/A}[1/d]/p^n)^{φ=1} depends only on Δ_{S/A,perf}. BS22 Theorem 10.9 and 10.11 (almost purity, proposed Part II of PerfectoidQuotients): perfectoidizations of finite covers. PerfectoidQuotients Q2–Q4: comparison with the universal perfectoid ring of a semiperfectoid ring.

**Planning API.**

- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Perfection.perfection` (constructor): The object Δ_{S/A,perf} of D(A) for an A/I-algebra S.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Perfection.perfectoidization` (constructor): The object S_perfd = Δ_{S/A,perf} ⊗^L_A A/I of D(A/I).
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Perfection.toPerfection` (data): The canonical map can : Δ_{S/A} → Δ_{S/A,perf}.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Perfection.perfectionFrobenius` (data): The Frobenius automorphism of the perfection, as an isomorphism Δ_{S/A,perf} ≃ φ_{A,*}Δ_{S/A,perf}.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Perfection.toPerfection_frobenius` (compatibility): can commutes with Frobenius: φ ∘ can = φ_{A,*}(can) ∘ φ_S.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Perfection.isIso_toPerfection` (characterisation): If φ_S : Δ_{S/A} → φ_{A,*}Δ_{S/A} is an isomorphism then can is an isomorphism.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Perfection.fromRing` (data): The map S → S_perfd in D(A/I).
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Perfection.perfectionMap` (functoriality): A map S→T of derived p-complete A/I-algebras over a fixed perfect prism induces a map of completed Frobenius perfections of Δ; identity and composition hold, and the maps commute with the original structure maps.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Perfection.perfectoidizationMap` (functoriality): A map S→T of derived p-complete A/I-algebras over a fixed perfect prism induces a map of perfectoidizations; identity and composition hold, and the maps commute with the original structure maps.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Perfection.perfectoidization_reduction` (compatibility): S_perfd ≃ Δ_(S/A),perf ⊗^L_A A/I, using the derived-completed perfection; the equivalence is natural in S as a commutative animated A/I-algebra equivalence.

**Unit tests.**

- `pr2_perfection_base` (degenerate): For a perfect prism and S = A/I the map can is an isomorphism.
- `pr2_perfectoidization_base` (degenerate): For a perfect prism, (A/I)_perfd is A/I in degree 0.
- `pr2_perfectoidization_char_p_discrete` (computation): For a perfect crystalline prism (A, (p)) and S = (A/p)[x], S_perfd has no cohomology outside degree 0; it is the perfection (A/p)[x^{1/p^∞}].
- `pr2_perfection_not_prismatic` (non-example): For a perfect crystalline prism (A, (p)) with A/p ≠ 0 and S = (A/p)[x], can : Δ_{S/A} → Δ_{S/A,perf} is not an isomorphism.

**Acceptance.** S = R: Δ_{R/A} = A, can is an isomorphism and R_perfd = R. S perfectoid: Δ_{S/A,perf} = A_inf(S) and S_perfd = S. (A, I) = (Z_p, (p)) and S = F_p[x]: S_perfd = F_p[x^{1/p^∞}], discrete, while Δ̄_{S/Z_p} has H^1 = Ω^1 ≠ 0. φ is an automorphism of Δ_{S/A,perf} for every S.

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-2-finite-projective-descent-prisms"></a>

### Descent of finite projective modules along faithfully flat maps of prisms

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/finite-projective-descent-prisms` · theorem. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.Semiperfectoid` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/Semiperfectoid/ModuleDescent`.

For bounded prisms, assigning to (A,I) the category of finite projective A-modules satisfies effective completely faithfully flat descent. Explicitly: for a map of bounded prisms (A, I) → (B, IB) with A → B (p, I)-completely faithfully flat, with Čech nerve B^• (B^n the (n+1)-fold derived (p, I)-completed tensor power of B over A, again a bounded prism), the category of finite projective A-modules is equivalent to the category of finite projective B-modules M equipped with an isomorphism of the two base changes of M to B^1 satisfying the cocycle condition over B^2.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** p is a fixed prime and (A, I) is a bounded prism (PR.0): A/I has bounded p^∞-torsion, and A is derived and classically (p, I)-complete. A map of prisms is faithfully flat when A → B is (p, I)-completely faithfully flat (PR.0); the appendix of ALB23 recalls this with the word "faithfully" omitted (recorded as a source issue).

**Construction or proof.**

1. A bounded prism is classically (p, I)-complete (PR.0), hence classically I-adically complete because I is finitely generated; so finite projective A-modules are compatible systems of finite projective A/I^n-modules (Stacks Project, Tag 0D4B).
2. A 2-limit of stacks is a stack, so it suffices that (A, I) ↦ {finite projective A/I^n-modules} is a stack for every n.
3. For a faithfully flat map of bounded prisms, A/I^n → B/I^nB = B ⊗^L_A A/I^n is a p-completely faithfully flat map of rings with bounded p^∞-torsion (A/I^n is a successive extension of the modules I^k/I^{k+1}, invertible over A/I); apply node finite-projective-modules-p-complete.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/finite-projective-modules-p-complete`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-finite-projective-modules-p-complete); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/bounded-prism-complete-flatness`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-bounded-prism-complete-flatness); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/prism-category`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-prism-category); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/rigidity-prism-ideal`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-rigidity-prism-ideal); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/prismatic-structure-sheaf`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-prismatic-structure-sheaf); `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`; [`mathlib:Module.Projective`](#mathlib-module-projective); [`mathlib:Module.Finite`](#mathlib-module-finite).

**Acceptance.** Finite projective modules over A_inf descend along the faithfully flat cover of prisms produced by node quasisyntomic-covers-lift-to-prisms. Rank one: invertible modules, in particular Breuil–Kisin twists, satisfy descent on the site of bounded prisms. Prismatic crystals in vector bundles on the absolute prismatic site form a stack (used by PR.7 and by ALB23 for prismatic Dieudonné crystals).

**Sources.** [ALB23](https://arxiv.org/abs/1907.10525v4), Appendix A, Proposition A.3 (published: Proposition A.3) and its proof. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 94. Exact statement and proof..

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-2-derived-hodge-tate-comparison"></a>

### Derived Hodge–Tate comparison

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/derived-hodge-tate-comparison` · theorem. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.Derived` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/Derived/HodgeTate`.

Let (A, I) be a bounded prism. For every derived p-complete simplicial A/I-algebra R and every i ≥ 0 there is an isomorphism in D(R), natural in R and multiplicative in i, gr_i^conj Δ̄_{R/A} ≃ (∧^i_R L_{R/(A/I)}){−i}[−i]^∧, where L_{R/(A/I)} is the cotangent complex, ∧^i the derived exterior power (DD.0), {−i} the Breuil–Kisin twist and ^∧ derived p-completion. For i = 0 it is Fil_0^conj = R; for p-completely smooth R it is the Hodge–Tate isomorphism Ω^i_{R/(A/I)}{−i} ≅ H^i(Δ̄_{R/A}) of PR.1. Consequences. (a) If R is discrete with bounded p^∞-torsion and L_{R/(A/I)} has p-complete Tor-amplitude in [−1, 0], then gr_i^conj ∈ D^{[0,i]}(R) and Δ̄_{R/A}, Δ_{R/A} ∈ D^{≥0}. (b) If R is discrete with bounded p^∞-torsion and L_{R/(A/I)}[−1] is p-completely flat over R, then gr_i^conj ≃ Γ^i_R(L_{R/(A/I)}[−1]){−i}^∧ is a p-completely flat R-module in degree 0, Δ̄_{R/A} is discrete, has bounded p^∞-torsion and R → Δ̄_{R/A} is p-completely faithfully flat, and Δ_{R/A} is discrete and I-torsion-free. (c) If the derived p-completion of L_{R/(A/I)} vanishes, then R ≃ Δ̄_{R/A}.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** p is a fixed prime and (A, I) is a bounded prism (PR.0): A/I has bounded p^∞-torsion, and A is derived and classically (p, I)-complete. A derived p-complete simplicial A/I-algebra is an animated commutative A/I-algebra (EnhancedDerivedSheaves E5:animation) whose underlying complex is derived p-complete (DD.1); tensor products of such algebras are derived and derived p-completed. M{n} := M ⊗_{A/I} (I/I²)^{⊗n} is the Breuil–Kisin twist of an A/I-module or complex M, for n ∈ Z; I/I² is an invertible A/I-module. Derived exterior and divided powers and the décalage isomorphism ∧^i(M[1]) ≃ Γ^i(M)[i] are those of DD.0; p-complete Tor-amplitude and p-complete flatness are those of BMS2 §4.1.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Smooth case: PR.1 gives gr_i = H^i(Δ̄_{R/A})[−i] ≅ Ω^i_{R/(A/I)}{−i}[−i], functorially in R ∈ Sm_{A/I} and compatibly with products.
2. Left Kan extension: graded pieces commute with colimits, so gr_i^conj is the left Kan extension of R ↦ (Ω^i_{R/(A/I)})^∧{−i}[−i]; by definition of the derived exterior powers of the cotangent complex (DD.0) and compatibility of derived completion with colimits (DD.1) this is (∧^i L_{R/(A/I)}){−i}[−i]^∧.
3. (a): ∧^i L has p-complete Tor-amplitude in [−i, 0], so its completion lies in D^{[−i,0]} (BMS2 Lemma 4.6, via DD.1); each Fil_i^conj has p-complete Tor-amplitude in [0, i] over R, so the colimit M has nonnegative p-complete Tor-amplitude; there is no uniform finite upper bound in i; as R has bounded p^∞-torsion, Δ̄ = M^∧ = Rlim_n (M ⊗^L_R R/p^n) is a limit of objects of D^{≥0} (proof of BMS2 Lemma 4.6), so Δ̄ ∈ D^{≥0}.
4. (b): décalage gives ∧^i(L)[−i] ≃ Γ^i(L[−1]); divided powers of a p-completely flat module are p-completely flat; BMS2 Lemma 4.7 gives discreteness and bounded torsion; R/p → Δ̄/p is injective with flat cokernel, hence faithfully flat. If Δ̄ = Δ ⊗^L_A A/I is discrete then, I being locally generated by a nonzerodivisor d and Δ being derived d-complete, multiplication by d is bijective on H^j(Δ) for j ≠ 0, 1, surjective on H^1 and injective on H^0; derived Nakayama gives H^j(Δ) = 0 for j ≠ 0.
5. (c): all gr_i^conj with i > 0 vanish.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/conjugate-filtration`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-conjugate-filtration); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/derived-prismatic-cohomology`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-derived-prismatic-cohomology); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/hodge-tate-comparison`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-hodge-tate-comparison); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/hodge-tate-comparison-map`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-hodge-tate-comparison-map); `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.0`; `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`.

**Acceptance.** Polynomial algebra: recovers Ω^i{−i} ≅ H^i(Δ̄). R = A/I: gr_i^conj = 0 for i > 0. R = (A/I)/(f), f a nonzerodivisor, R of bounded p^∞-torsion: gr_i^conj = Γ^i_R(R·f̄){−i}, free of rank 1. S perfectoid over a perfect prism: L^∧_{S/(A/I)} = 0, so Δ̄_{S/A} = S and Δ_{S/A} = A_inf(S). R = A/I ⊗^L_{(A/I)⟨x⟩} A/I: gr_i^conj ≃ R{−i} for all i (node derived-input-higher-homotopy).

**Sources.** [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Construction 7.6. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 56. Statement of the graded pieces as completed derived exterior powers, twisted and shifted.. [ALB23](https://arxiv.org/abs/1907.10525v4), Proposition 3.1.10 (published: Proposition 3.10). Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 18. Same statement with the multiplicativity made explicit.. [BMS2](https://arxiv.org/abs/1802.03261v2), Lemmas 4.6 and 4.7. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 19. The passage from p-complete Tor-amplitude to honest amplitude and flatness used in the consequences..

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-2-derived-prismatic-base-change"></a>

### Base change for derived prismatic cohomology

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/derived-prismatic-base-change` · theorem. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.Derived` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/Derived/Basic`.

Let (A, I) → (B, J) be a map of bounded prisms (so J = IB) and R a derived p-complete simplicial A/I-algebra. Let R_B := (R ⊗^L_A B)^∧ = (R ⊗^L_{A/I} B/J)^∧ be the derived p-completion. Then the natural map Δ_{R/A} ⊗̂^L_A B → Δ_{R_B/B} is an isomorphism of commutative algebras in D_comp(B), the completion on the left being the derived (p, J)-completion. It is compatible with Frobenius, and its reduction modulo J, Δ̄_{R/A} ⊗̂^L_{A/I} B/J ≃ Δ̄_{R_B/B}, is compatible with the conjugate filtrations and, through L_{R_B/(B/J)} ≃ L_{R/(A/I)} ⊗^L_R R_B, with the identifications of the graded pieces.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** p is a fixed prime and (A, I) is a bounded prism (PR.0): A/I has bounded p^∞-torsion, and A is derived and classically (p, I)-complete. A derived p-complete simplicial A/I-algebra is an animated commutative A/I-algebra (EnhancedDerivedSheaves E5:animation) whose underlying complex is derived p-complete (DD.1); tensor products of such algebras are derived and derived p-completed. No flatness of A → B is assumed; R ⊗^L_A B is computed in animated rings, and A/I ⊗^L_A B = B/J because I is invertible and B is I-torsion-free.

**Construction or proof.**

1. For p-completely smooth R this is base change for the site cohomology (PR.1).
2. Both sides commute with sifted colimits in R: the left side by construction and because − ⊗̂^L_A B commutes with completed colimits (DD.1), the right side because R ↦ R_B commutes with colimits. A natural transformation between sifted-colimit-preserving functors that is an isomorphism on Poly_{A/I} is an isomorphism.
3. The compatibility with filtrations follows from base change for the cotangent complex and its derived exterior powers (DD.0).

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/derived-prismatic-cohomology`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-derived-prismatic-cohomology); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/conjugate-filtration`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-conjugate-filtration); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/prismatic-base-change`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-prismatic-base-change); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/rigidity-prism-ideal`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-rigidity-prism-ideal); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/prism-category`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-prism-category); `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.0`; `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`; `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E5:animation/universal-property-of-animation`.

**Acceptance.** B = A: the identity. Base change to the perfection (A, I) → (A, I)_perf and to an orientable cover (A, I) → (B, (d)). For a map of perfect prisms A → A′ and S an A/I-algebra: Δ_{S/A} ⊗̂^L_A A′ ≃ Δ_{(S ⊗̂^L A′/I)/A′}, the formula used by PerfectoidQuotients Q2–Q4 to descend surjectivity of perfectoidization. The universal case of Example 7.9 is reached by base change from Z_p{d, f_1,…,f_r}[δ(d)^{−1}]^∧.

**Sources.** [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Construction 7.6 (4). Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 56. Exact statement; the node adds the compatibilities that the proof by left Kan extension gives..

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-2-derived-prismatic-etale-descent"></a>

### Étale descent and derived prismatic cohomology of formal schemes

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/derived-prismatic-etale-descent` · theorem. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.Derived` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/Derived/Descent`.

Let (A, I) be a bounded prism. (1) Étale base change: for a p-completely étale map R → R′ of derived p-complete simplicial A/I-algebras, Δ̄_{R/A} ⊗̂^L_R R′ ≃ Δ̄_{R′/A}, compatibly with conjugate filtrations. (2) Sheaf property: for a p-completely étale cover R → R′ with derived p-completed Čech nerve R′^•, the map Δ_{R/A} → lim_{[n] ∈ Δ} Δ_{R′^n/A} is an equivalence of commutative algebras with Frobenius in D_comp(A); so R ↦ Δ_{R/A} is a sheaf for the p-completely étale topology on derived p-complete A/I-algebras. (3) Globalisation: for a p-adic formal scheme X over Spf(A/I), locally the formal spectrum of a p-complete ring with bounded p^∞-torsion, there is a functorially defined derived (p, I)-complete commutative algebra Δ_{X/A} in D(X_ét, A) with a φ_A-semilinear Frobenius φ_X, such that RΓ(U, Δ_{X/A}) ≃ Δ_{R/A} for every affine object U = Spf(R) of X_ét, compatibly with Frobenius; Δ̄_{X/A} := Δ_{X/A} ⊗^L_A A/I is an object of D(X_ét, O_X) with an increasing exhaustive multiplicative filtration Fil_•^conj and gr_i^conj Δ̄_{X/A} ≃ (∧^i L_{X/(A/I)}){−i}[−i]^∧.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** p is a fixed prime and (A, I) is a bounded prism (PR.0): A/I has bounded p^∞-torsion, and A is derived and classically (p, I)-complete. A derived p-complete simplicial A/I-algebra is an animated commutative A/I-algebra (EnhancedDerivedSheaves E5:animation) whose underlying complex is derived p-complete (DD.1); tensor products of such algebras are derived and derived p-completed. The bounded-torsion hypothesis on X in (3) is the one of the arXiv v4 text of ALB23 Proposition 3.1.11; BS22 state the globalisation for every p-adic formal scheme.

**Construction or proof.**

1. (1): L_{R′/R} vanishes after derived p-completion, so the transitivity triangle gives (∧^i L_{R/(A/I)})^∧ ⊗̂^L_R R′ ≃ (∧^i L_{R′/(A/I)})^∧ (DD.0); the natural map of filtered objects is an isomorphism on graded pieces by the derived Hodge–Tate comparison, hence an isomorphism.
2. (2): by (1) the cosimplicial object Δ̄_{R′^•/A} is Δ̄_{R/A} ⊗̂^L_R R′^•, and M ≃ lim M ⊗̂^L_R R′^• for every derived p-complete M ∈ D(R) by p-completely faithfully flat descent (DD.1). Limits commute with − ⊗^L_A A/I, and a map of derived I-complete objects that is an isomorphism modulo I is an isomorphism.
3. (3): the sheaf on the affine objects of X_ét determines Δ_{X/A}; Frobenius, the filtration and its graded pieces are sheaves by the same argument (flat descent for the completed cotangent powers, DD.5).

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/derived-prismatic-cohomology`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-derived-prismatic-cohomology); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/conjugate-filtration`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-conjugate-filtration); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/derived-hodge-tate-comparison`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-derived-hodge-tate-comparison); `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.0`; `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`; `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.5`.

**Acceptance.** For X smooth the object Δ_{X/A} is the one of PR.1. For X = Spf(R) affine, RΓ(X, Δ_{X/A}) = Δ_{R/A}. For a finite disjoint union the value is the product: Δ_{(R_1 × R_2)/A} = Δ_{R_1/A} × Δ_{R_2/A}.

**Sources.** [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Construction 7.6 (2). Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 56.
