<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-2-kunneth-formula"></a>

### Colimit preservation and the Künneth formula

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/kunneth-formula` · theorem. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.Derived` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/Derived/Basic`.

Let (A, I) be a bounded prism. The functor R ↦ Δ_{R/A} from derived p-complete simplicial A/I-algebras to commutative algebras in D_comp(A) (derived (p, I)-complete E_∞-A-algebras) commutes with all colimits. In particular it is symmetric monoidal: Δ_{(A/I)/A} = A, and for every diagram R_1 ← R_3 → R_2 the canonical map Δ_{R_1/A} ⊗̂^L_{Δ_{R_3/A}} Δ_{R_2/A} → Δ_{(R_1 ⊗̂^L_{R_3} R_2)/A} is an equivalence of commutative algebras with Frobenius, where the completion on the left is derived (p, I)-adic and on the right derived p-adic.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** p is a fixed prime and (A, I) is a bounded prism (PR.0): A/I has bounded p^∞-torsion, and A is derived and classically (p, I)-complete. A derived p-complete simplicial A/I-algebra is an animated commutative A/I-algebra (EnhancedDerivedSheaves E5:animation) whose underlying complex is derived p-complete (DD.1); tensor products of such algebras are derived and derived p-completed. D(A) is the derived ∞-category of A-modules with cohomological indexing; D_comp(A) is the full subcategory of derived (p, I)-complete objects with its completed tensor product; "discrete" means concentrated in degree 0.

**Construction or proof.**

1. A left Kan extension from polynomial algebras preserves sifted colimits; it preserves all colimits as soon as its restriction to (completed) polynomial algebras preserves finite coproducts (HTT 5.5.8.15, E5:animation).
2. The initial object: Δ_{(A/I)/A} = A.
3. Binary coproducts: for p-completely smooth R and S the map Δ_{R/A} ⊗̂^L_A Δ_{S/A} → Δ_{(R ⊗̂ S)/A} is an isomorphism; by I-completeness it is checked on Δ̄, where it follows from the Hodge–Tate comparison of PR.1 and the Künneth decomposition of differential forms of a tensor product.
4. Pushouts are colimits of bar constructions, which gives the relative formula.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/derived-prismatic-cohomology`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-derived-prismatic-cohomology); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/derived-hodge-tate-comparison`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-derived-hodge-tate-comparison); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/hodge-tate-comparison`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-hodge-tate-comparison); `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E5:animation/universal-property-of-animation`; `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E5:abstract/symmetric-monoidal-infinity-category`; `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E5:abstract/algebra-objects`; `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`.

**Acceptance.** Δ_{(A/I)⟨x,y⟩/A} ≃ Δ_{(A/I)⟨x⟩/A} ⊗̂^L_A Δ_{(A/I)⟨y⟩/A}. R_1 = R_2 = A/I over R_3 = (A/I)⟨x⟩: Δ of the derived self-intersection is A ⊗̂^L_{Δ_{(A/I)⟨x⟩/A}} A (node derived-input-higher-homotopy). Filtered colimits: Δ of a completed filtered colimit is the completed filtered colimit, as used in BS22 Proposition 7.10. ALB23 apply the formula to the product of an abelian scheme with itself.

**Sources.** [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Construction 7.6 (5). Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 56. Colimit preservation and symmetric monoidality.. [ALB23](https://arxiv.org/abs/1907.10525v4), Proposition 3.5.1 (published: Proposition 3.30) and its proof. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 25. The relative Künneth formula with its proof; the proof says "final object" where the initial object A/I is meant (recorded as a source issue)..

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-2-derived-agrees-with-site"></a>

### Agreement with site cohomology: smooth algebras and the discrete case

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/derived-agrees-with-site` · theorem. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.Semiperfectoid` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/Semiperfectoid/Discrete`.

Let (A, I) be a bounded prism. (a) If R is a p-completely smooth A/I-algebra, the derived Δ_{R/A} is the site cohomology RΓ((R/A)_Δ, O_Δ) of PR.1, compatibly with Frobenius and with the Hodge–Tate comparison; the conjugate filtration is the canonical filtration. (b) Let R be a derived p-complete simplicial A/I-algebra such that Δ̄_{R/A} is concentrated in degree 0. Then: (1) Δ_{R/A} is discrete and I-torsion-free, and the Frobenius φ_R lifts naturally to a δ-A-algebra structure on the ring Δ_{R/A}; (2) (Δ_{R/A}, IΔ_{R/A}) is a prism over (A, I), equipped with a map R → Δ̄_{R/A} = Δ_{R/A}/IΔ_{R/A}; it is bounded exactly when Δ̄_{R/A} has bounded p^∞-torsion; (3) among prisms over (A,I) with a specified R→B/J there exists an initial prism; (Δ_{R/A}, IΔ_{R/A}) is weakly initial in it (the maps being those of node comparison-to-prisms, which are δ-maps), and the initial object is the image of an idempotent endomorphism of (Δ_{R/A}, IΔ_{R/A}). The statement does not assert that (Δ_{R/A}, IΔ_{R/A}) is initial; Bhatt and Scholze conjecture this. It is proved in the cases of nodes regular-quotient-prismatic-envelope and qrsp-prism, where consequently Δ_{R/A} computes the cohomology of the prismatic site of R.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** p is a fixed prime and (A, I) is a bounded prism (PR.0): A/I has bounded p^∞-torsion, and A is derived and classically (p, I)-complete. A derived p-complete simplicial A/I-algebra is an animated commutative A/I-algebra (EnhancedDerivedSheaves E5:animation) whose underlying complex is derived p-complete (DD.1); tensor products of such algebras are derived and derived p-completed. In (b) the category in (3) consists of all prisms over (A, I), bounded or not. A discrete Δ_{R/A} is not called "the initial object" here: the source proves weak initiality, and that the initial object is a retract.

**Construction or proof.**

1. (a) is the third step of the construction (node derived-prismatic-cohomology).
2. (b)(1): Čech–Alexander complexes and canonical simplicial resolutions give a functor R ↦ F_A(R) to simplicial cosimplicial derived (p, I)-complete δ-A-algebras with colim_{Δ^op} lim_Δ F_A(R) ≃ Δ_{R/A}. The δ-structure is a section F_A(R) → W_2(F_A(R)) of the restriction, lying over A → W_2(A) (PR.0). Using the functorial pullback square expressing W_2(B) as B ×_{B ⊗^L F_p} B (through the ghost map and φ) for simplicial commutative rings, and the discreteness of Δ_{R/A}, one identifies colim lim W_2(F_A(R)) with W_2(Δ_{R/A}); the section gives the δ-structure refining φ_R.
3. (b)(2): Δ_{R/A} is derived (p, I)-complete and Δ_{R/A} ⊗^L_A A/I is discrete, so Δ_{R/A} is discrete and I-torsion-free (node derived-hodge-tate-comparison, last step of (b)); IΔ_{R/A} is invertible and contains a distinguished element locally.
4. (b)(3): the maps of node comparison-to-prisms are δ-maps by the argument of (1). Apply node idempotent-retract-initial-object to the category of prisms over (A, I) with a map from R, which is idempotent complete, with X = (Δ_{R/A}, IΔ_{R/A}).

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/derived-prismatic-cohomology`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-derived-prismatic-cohomology); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/derived-hodge-tate-comparison`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-derived-hodge-tate-comparison); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/comparison-to-prisms`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-comparison-to-prisms); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/idempotent-retract-initial-object`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-idempotent-retract-initial-object); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/cech-alexander-complex`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-cech-alexander-complex); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/relative-prismatic-cohomology`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-relative-prismatic-cohomology); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-witt-section-equivalence`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-delta-witt-section-equivalence); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/prism`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-prism); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/prism-category`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-prism-category); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/animated-delta-rings`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-animated-delta-rings); `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`; [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/witt2-derived-pullback-square`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-witt2-derived-pullback-square).

**Acceptance.** R = A/I: the prism is (A, I), which is initial. R p-completely smooth of positive relative dimension: Δ̄_{R/A} is not discrete and (b) does not apply. R = (A/I)/(f): (b) applies and the idempotent is the identity (node regular-quotient-prismatic-envelope). R perfectoid over a perfect prism: Δ_{R/A} = A_inf(R) with its unique δ-structure.

**Sources.** [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Lemma 7.7 and its proof. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 57. <a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-2-derived-crystalline-comparison"></a>

### Derived crystalline comparison

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/derived-crystalline-comparison` · comparison. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.Semiperfectoid` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/Semiperfectoid/Crystalline`.

Let k be a perfect F_p-algebra and (A, I) = (W(k), (p)) the corresponding crystalline perfect prism. For a derived p-complete simplicial k-algebra S put S^{(1)} := S ⊗^L_{k,φ} k, and let RΓ_crys(S/A) be the derived crystalline cohomology of S over A: the p-completed left Kan extension of P ↦ RΓ_crys(P/A) from finitely generated polynomial k-algebras (for k = F_p the derived de Rham–Witt complex LWΩ_S of BMS2 §8.2); its reduction modulo p is the derived de Rham complex dR_{S/k} relative to k. It is not the p-completed derived de Rham cohomology of S over A: dR^∧_{k/W(k)} = (W(k)⟨x⟩/(x − p))^∧ ≠ W(k). Then there are natural isomorphisms of commutative algebras in D_comp(A), compatible with Frobenius, Δ_{S/A} ⊗̂^L_{A,φ_A} A ≃ Δ_{S^{(1)}/A} ≃ RΓ_crys(S/A), extending the crystalline comparison Δ_{P^{(1)}/A} ≃ RΓ_crys(P/A) of PR.1 for smooth k-algebras P. The Frobenius twist is part of the statement: Δ_{S/A} itself is not A-linearly isomorphic to RΓ_crys(S/A) in general.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** p is a fixed prime; k is perfect of characteristic p, so W(k) is a perfect p-torsion-free δ-ring and (W(k), (p)) is a bounded prism. A derived p-complete simplicial A/I-algebra is an animated commutative A/I-algebra (EnhancedDerivedSheaves E5:animation) whose underlying complex is derived p-complete (DD.1); tensor products of such algebras are derived and derived p-completed. The comparison of RΓ_crys(S/A) with site-theoretic crystalline cohomology of singular S is not part of this node; modulo p, RΓ_crys(S/A) is the derived de Rham complex dR_{S/k} of DD.2, by crystalline base change for polynomial algebras (CR.2).

**Construction or proof.**

1. First isomorphism: base change (node derived-prismatic-base-change) along the map of prisms φ_A : (A, (p)) → (A, (p)); the base change of S is S^{(1)}.
2. Second isomorphism on polynomial algebras: PR.1's crystalline comparison (BS22 Theorem 5.2 with the PD ideal J = (p)) gives Δ_{P^{(1)}/A} ≃ RΓ_crys(P/A), functorially in P and compatibly with Frobenius.
3. Left Kan extension: P ↦ Δ_{P^{(1)}/A} extends to S ↦ Δ_{S^{(1)}/A} because S ↦ S^{(1)} commutes with colimits; P ↦ RΓ_crys(P/A) ≃ (Ω^*_{P̃/A})^∧, for a p-complete smooth lift P̃, extends to RΓ_crys(S/A) by definition; the isomorphism of STEP2 is natural in P, hence extends.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/derived-prismatic-cohomology`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-derived-prismatic-cohomology); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/derived-prismatic-base-change`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-derived-prismatic-base-change); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/crystalline-comparison`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-crystalline-comparison); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/crystalline-prism`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-crystalline-prism); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/perfect-delta-rings`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-perfect-delta-rings); `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.2`; `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E5:animation/universal-property-of-animation`; [`mathlib:WittVector`](#mathlib-wittvector); [`mathlib:PerfectRing`](#mathlib-perfectring); `CrystallineCohomology:CR.2`; `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.4`.

**Acceptance.** S = k: Δ_{k/A} = W(k) = RΓ_crys(k/A); by contrast dR^∧_{k/W(k)} = (W(k)⟨x⟩/(x − p))^∧ is not W(k), so the derived de Rham complex over W(k) cannot replace derived crystalline cohomology. S = k[x]: the right side is the p-completed de Rham complex of W(k)⟨x⟩ and the left side is Δ_{k[x]/W(k)} twisted by φ. S quasiregular semiperfect: the right side is A_crys(S) (node qrsp-char-p-acrys). S = k/(x): Δ_{S/A} = A{[x]/p}^∧ and RΓ_crys(S/A) = A{[x]^p/p}^∧ are different subrings of A[1/p]-algebras; the twist cannot be removed.

**Sources.** [ALB23](https://arxiv.org/abs/1907.10525v4), Theorem 3.1.7 and Remark 3.1.8 (published: Theorem 3.7, Remark 3.8). Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 17. ALB23 extend the crystalline comparison by descent; the node proves the extension to all derived inputs by left Kan extension, from which the descent form follows (node qrsp-char-p-acrys (4)).. [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Theorem 5.2. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 45. The smooth case that is extended..

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-2-perfection-comparison"></a>

### Comparison of the perfected and the unperfected theory

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/perfection-comparison` · comparison. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.Perfection` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/Perfection/Basic`.

Let (A, I) be a perfect prism, R = A/I, and S a derived p-complete simplicial R-algebra. (1) can : Δ_{S/A} → Δ_{S/A,perf} is initial among maps of commutative algebras with Frobenius from Δ_{S/A} to objects E of D_comp(A) whose Frobenius φ_E is an equivalence; it is an equivalence if and only if φ_S is. (2) If S is a perfectoid R-algebra then L_{S/R} vanishes after derived p-completion, Δ̄_{S/A} = S, Δ_{S/A} = A_inf(S), can is an equivalence and S_perfd = S. (3) For every perfect prism (B, J) over (A, I) with a map π_0(S) → B/J, the map ev_{(B,J)} of node comparison-to-prisms factors uniquely through can; these factorisations assemble to Δ_{S/A,perf} → RΓ((S/A)_Δ^perf, O_Δ) = lim_{S → R′} A_inf(R′), the limit over all maps from S to perfectoid rings R′. (4) Characteristic p (BS22 Example 8.3): for a crystalline perfect prism (A, I) = (W(k), (p)), k a perfect F_p-algebra (in the source k = F_p), and a k-algebra S, the Frobenius of Δ_{S/A}/p preserves the conjugate filtration and acts on gr_i^conj = ∧^i L_{S/k}[−i] through the map induced by the Frobenius of S, which is zero for i ≠ 0; hence S_perf := colim_φ S ≃ S_perfd through the Frobenius-equivariant map S → Δ̄_{S/A}. (5) The two theories differ: for S = F_p[x] over (Z_p, (p)), H^0(Δ̄_{S/A}) = F_p[x] and H^1(Δ̄_{S/A}) = Ω^1_{F_p[x]/F_p} ≠ 0, while S_perfd = F_p[x^{1/p^∞}] is discrete. Neither theory is obtained from the other by a formal substitution: Δ_{S/A,perf} forgets the conjugate filtration in positive degrees, and Δ_{S/A} is not recovered from Δ_{S/A,perf}.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** (A, I) is a perfect prism: φ_A is bijective; then I = (d) for a distinguished nonzerodivisor d, R := A/I is an integral perfectoid ring and A = A_inf(R) (PR.0). S is a derived p-complete simplicial R-algebra, R = A/I; all tensor products are derived and completed. That the map in (3) is an equivalence is BS22 Proposition 8.5 (recorded gap); (3) only constructs it. In (4) the base is crystalline; for a perfect base of mixed characteristic and pS = 0 the source reduces to the base (Z_p, (p)) by independence of the base, which is the same gap.

**Construction or proof.**

1. (1): universal property of the sequential colimit along φ and of completion.
2. (2): the completed cotangent complexes of R and S over Z_p are R[1] and S[1] compatibly (BMS2 Proposition 4.19 and the proof of Lemma 4.25; from Q0:integral-algebra and DD.5), so L_{S/R}^∧ = 0; node derived-hodge-tate-comparison (c) gives Δ̄_{S/A} = S. The map ev to the prism (A_inf(S), I A_inf(S)) is an isomorphism modulo I, hence an isomorphism; A_inf(S) is perfect.
3. (3): φ_B is an automorphism, so ev extends over the colimit and the completion; for the identification of the perfect prismatic site with perfectoid rings under S use the equivalence of PR.0 and BS22 Lemma 4.8.
4. (4): reduce to S = F_p[x] by left Kan extension; there the Frobenius of Δ̄ on H^1 = Ω^1 is induced by x ↦ x^p, which kills dx. Reduction modulo p commutes with the colimit and the completion.
5. (5): PR.1's Hodge–Tate comparison for F_p[x] and (4).

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/perfection-of-prismatic-cohomology`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-perfection-of-prismatic-cohomology); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/derived-hodge-tate-comparison`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-derived-hodge-tate-comparison); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/comparison-to-prisms`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-comparison-to-prisms); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/conjugate-filtration`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-conjugate-filtration); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/perfect-prisms-perfectoid-rings`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-perfect-prisms-perfectoid-rings); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/perfect-delta-rings`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-perfect-delta-rings); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/hodge-tate-comparison`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-hodge-tate-comparison); `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.0`; `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.5`; `PerfectoidQuotients:Q0:integral-algebra`; [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/perfect-prism-initial`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-perfect-prism-initial); [`mathlib:PerfectRing`](#mathlib-perfectring).

**Acceptance.** S = R: both theories give A. S = R⟨x^{1/p^∞}⟩: perfectoid, so the two theories agree. S = F_p[x] over Z_p: they differ, as in (5). S = F_p[x]/(x²) over Z_p: S_perfd = (S)_perf = F_p.

**Sources.** [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Example 8.3. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 63. Part (4).. <a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-2-first-conjugate-piece-cotangent"></a>

### The first conjugate piece is the cotangent complex over the prism

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/first-conjugate-piece-cotangent` · theorem. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.Derived` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/Derived/HodgeTate`.

Let (A, I) be a bounded prism and R a derived p-complete simplicial A/I-algebra. There is a canonical isomorphism in D(R), natural in R, α_R : (L_{R/A}{−1}[−1])^∧ ≃ Fil_1^conj Δ̄_{R/A}, where L_{R/A} is the cotangent complex of R over A (not over A/I). It is an isomorphism of extensions: the transitivity triangle R ≃ (R ⊗^L_{A/I} L_{(A/I)/A}{−1}[−1])^∧ → (L_{R/A}{−1}[−1])^∧ → (L_{R/(A/I)}{−1}[−1])^∧, formed with L_{(A/I)/A} ≃ I/I²[1], is carried to Fil_0^conj → Fil_1^conj → gr_1^conj with the identifications gr_0^conj = R and gr_1^conj = (L_{R/(A/I)}{−1}[−1])^∧ of the derived Hodge–Tate comparison. For p-completely smooth R it reads L_{R/A}^∧ ≃ (τ^{≤1}Δ̄_{R/A}){1}[1]. For a p-adic formal scheme X over A/I that is locally the formal spectrum of a p-complete ring with bounded p^∞-torsion the isomorphisms glue to α_X : (L_{X/Spf(A)}{−1}[−1])^∧ ≃ Fil_1^conj Δ̄_{X/A} in D(X).

**Hypotheses and conventions.** p is a fixed prime and (A, I) is a bounded prism (PR.0): A/I has bounded p^∞-torsion, and A is derived and classically (p, I)-complete. A derived p-complete simplicial A/I-algebra is an animated commutative A/I-algebra (EnhancedDerivedSheaves E5:animation) whose underlying complex is derived p-complete (DD.1); tensor products of such algebras are derived and derived p-completed. M{n} := M ⊗_{A/I} (I/I²)^{⊗n} is the Breuil–Kisin twist of an A/I-module or complex M, for n ∈ Z; I/I² is an invertible A/I-module. All cotangent complexes are derived p-completed; the hypothesis on X is the one added in Proposition 3.1.11 of the arXiv v4 text of ALB23.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Both sides are left Kan extended from p-completely smooth A/I-algebras (DD.0 for the left side), so it suffices to construct α_R naturally for R in Sm_{A/I}.
2. For (B, J) in (R/A)_Δ pull back 0 → J/J² → B/J² → B/J → 0 along R → B/J. This is a square-zero extension of R by B/J{1} in A-algebras, classified by L_{R/A}^∧ → B/J{1}[1] (derivation description of the cotangent complex, DD.0). The limit over the site gives α_R : (L_{R/A}{−1}[−1])^∧ → Δ̄_{R/A}, which factors through τ^{≤1}.
3. For R = (A/I)⟨x⟩ one has L_{R/A}^∧ = R ⊗ I/I²[1] ⊕ R dx; on the first summand the map is the base extension of I/I² → J/J², on dx it is the Bockstein of the image of x. For the unshifted map L_{R/A}^∧ → Δ̄_{R/A}{1}[1], H^0 is the Hodge–Tate map Ω^1 ≅ H^1(Δ̄){1} and H^{−1} is the canonical map R ⊗ I/I² → H^0(Δ̄){1}. Equivalently, the displayed shifted map α_R has these maps in degrees 1 and 0, respectively.
4. By functoriality, and because Ω^1 is generated by the dr, α_R induces the canonical maps on cohomology for every R in Sm_{A/I}; hence it is an isomorphism, compatible with the two triangles.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/conjugate-filtration`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-conjugate-filtration); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/derived-hodge-tate-comparison`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-derived-hodge-tate-comparison); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/derived-prismatic-etale-descent`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-derived-prismatic-etale-descent); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/hodge-tate-comparison-map`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-hodge-tate-comparison-map); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/relative-prismatic-site`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-relative-prismatic-site); `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.0`; `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`.

**Acceptance.** R = A/I: both sides are A/I. R = (A/I)⟨x⟩: Fil_1^conj = τ^{≤1}Δ̄ = Δ̄ and the class of the extension of Ω^1{−1}[−1] by R vanishes, in accordance with the lift A⟨x⟩ over A/I². R = (A/I)/(f) with f a nonzerodivisor: Fil_1^conj is the discrete module (L_{R/A}{−1}[−1]) = J/J²{−1} for J = (I, f), an extension of R·f̄{−1} by R.

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-2-kunneth-formula-formal-schemes"></a>

### Künneth formula for smooth formal schemes

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/kunneth-formula-formal-schemes` · theorem. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.Derived` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/Derived/Descent`.

Fix a bounded (A,I). Require the formal schemes X and Y over Spf(A/I) to be quasi-compact, quasi-separated and p-completely smooth. Their prismatic complexes satisfy RΓ(X ×_{Spf(A/I)} Y, Δ_{X ×_{Spf(A/I)} Y/A}) ≃ RΓ(X, Δ_{X/A}) ⊗̂^L_A RΓ(Y, Δ_{Y/A}), an isomorphism of commutative algebras in D_comp(A) compatible with Frobenius, the completed tensor product being derived (p, I)-adic.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** p is a fixed prime and (A, I) is a bounded prism (PR.0): A/I has bounded p^∞-torsion, and A is derived and classically (p, I)-complete. The hypothesis quasi-compact quasi-separated is part of the statement in the arXiv v4 text of ALB23.

**Construction or proof.**

1. The external product map is defined by functoriality; on affine opens it is the isomorphism of node kunneth-formula.
2. Both sides are derived I-complete, so it suffices to compare after − ⊗^L_A A/I; for quasi-compact quasi-separated X this reduction commutes with RΓ.
3. On Δ̄ the conjugate filtration is finite (the canonical filtration), with graded pieces Ω^i{−i}[−i]; the claim follows from Ω^i_{X×Y} = ⊕_{a+b=i} Ω^a_X ⊠ Ω^b_Y and the projection formula and flat base change for quasi-coherent cohomology of quasi-compact quasi-separated formal schemes (requested from DD.5).

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/kunneth-formula`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-kunneth-formula); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/derived-prismatic-etale-descent`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-derived-prismatic-etale-descent); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/hodge-tate-comparison`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-hodge-tate-comparison); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/relative-prismatic-cohomology`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-relative-prismatic-cohomology); `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`; `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.5`.

**Acceptance.** X = Y = Spf(A/I)⟨x⟩ recovers the affine formula. For X, Y proper smooth both sides are perfect complexes of A-modules (PR.1) and the completed tensor product is the ordinary derived tensor product. X = Spf(A/I): the identity.

**Sources.** [ALB23](https://arxiv.org/abs/1907.10525v4), Corollary 3.5.2 (published: Corollary 3.31). Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 26. Exact statement and the indicated proof..

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-2-regular-quotient-prismatic-envelope"></a>

### Prismatic cohomology of a regular quotient is the prismatic envelope

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/regular-quotient-prismatic-envelope` · theorem. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.Semiperfectoid` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/Semiperfectoid/Regular`.

Fix a bounded prism (A, I). Let f_1,…,f_r ∈ A have images forming a Koszul-regular sequence on A/I, let J = (I, f_1,…,f_r), and assume that R := A/J has bounded p^∞-torsion. Then: (1) gr_i^conj Δ̄_{R/A} ≃ Γ^i_R(J/(J² + I)){−i}, a finite free R-module, for all i; Δ̄_{R/A} is discrete and p-completely faithfully flat over R, and Δ_{R/A} is discrete and I-torsion-free. (2) (Δ_{R/A}, IΔ_{R/A}) is a bounded prism and is the initial object of (R/A)_Δ; it is also initial among all prisms (B, IB) over (A, I) with a map R → B/IB, so the idempotent of node derived-agrees-with-site is the identity. (3) If I = (d), the natural map A{f_1/d,…,f_r/d}^∧ → Δ_{R/A}, from the derived (p, I)-complete simplicial δ-A-algebra obtained by freely adjoining the f_i/d, is an isomorphism; in particular the source is discrete, and it is the universal prism over (A, I) under the δ-pair (A, J); it is the prismatic envelope of PR.0/regular-prismatic-envelopes whenever A is flat over a bounded prism relative to which (f_i) is completely regular (the universal case of the proof; the rings of node regular-semiperfectoid-example).

**Hypotheses and conventions.** p is a fixed prime and (A, I) is a bounded prism (PR.0): A/I has bounded p^∞-torsion, and A is derived and classically (p, I)-complete. M{n} := M ⊗_{A/I} (I/I²)^{⊗n} is the Breuil–Kisin twist of an A/I-module or complex M, for n ∈ Z; I/I² is an invertible A/I-module. A regular sequence is Koszul-regular; the source assumes "bounded p-torsion", meaning bounded p^∞-torsion. In (3) the element f_i/d is adjoined in animated δ-A-algebras (PR.0, animated-delta-rings) and the result is derived (p, I)-completed.

**Construction or proof.**

1. L_{R/(A/I)} ≃ J/(J² + I)[1] with J/(J² + I) free on the f_i (DD.0), so gr_i^conj = Γ^i(J/(J² + I)){−i} by décalage; apply consequence (b) of node derived-hodge-tate-comparison and node derived-agrees-with-site.
2. The claims are local on Spf(A); assume I = (d). Since f_i = 0 in Δ̄_{R/A}, the universal property of free adjunction gives B := A{f_1/d,…,f_r/d}^∧ → Δ_{R/A}. If this is an isomorphism, the universal property of B shows that (B, IB) is initial.
3. Both sides commute with base change in (A, d, f) (node derived-prismatic-base-change), so pass to the universal case A = Z_p{d, f_1,…,f_r}[δ(d)^{−1}]^∧, where A/I and R are p-torsion-free and f is (p, I)-completely regular relative to A_0 = Z_p{d}[δ(d)^{−1}]^∧. There B is the prismatic envelope A{J/I}^∧ (PR.0), discrete, and (B, IB) is initial in (R/A)_Δ.
4. By weak initiality B → Δ_{R/A} has a retraction; so B/IB → Δ̄_{R/A} has a p-torsion-free cokernel and it suffices to show that B/IB[1/p] → Δ̄_{R/A}[1/p] is surjective. The target is generated as a Banach R[1/p]-algebra by gr_1^conj = J/(J² + I){−1}, and J/I maps onto gr_1^conj by the computation with a free resolution of R over A/I (the prismatic analogue of Bhatt, p-adic derived de Rham cohomology, Claim 3.30).

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/derived-hodge-tate-comparison`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-derived-hodge-tate-comparison); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/derived-agrees-with-site`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-derived-agrees-with-site); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/derived-prismatic-base-change`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-derived-prismatic-base-change); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/comparison-to-prisms`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-comparison-to-prisms); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/regular-prismatic-envelopes`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-regular-prismatic-envelopes); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/animated-delta-rings`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-animated-delta-rings); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/free-delta-ring`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-free-delta-ring); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/local-distinguished-prism-generators`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-local-distinguished-prism-generators); `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.0`; `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`; [`mathlib:RingTheory.Sequence.IsRegular`](#mathlib-ringtheory-sequence-isregular).

**Acceptance.** r = 0: R = A/I and Δ_{R/A} = A. (A, I) = (Z_p⟨x⟩, (p)) with δ(x) = 0 and f = x^p: R = F_p[x]/(x^p) and Δ_{R/A} = Z_p⟨x⟩{x^p/p}^∧ is the p-completed PD envelope of (x) in Z_p⟨x⟩ (PR.0, pd-envelope-as-delta-envelope). (A, I) = (A_inf(O_C), (ξ)) and f = p: R = O_C/p and Δ_{R/A} = A_inf{p/ξ}^∧ (node regular-semiperfectoid-example). The graded pieces gr_i^conj are free of rank binom(r+i−1, i).

**Sources.** [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Example 7.9. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 59. Exact statement and proof.. ### Acceptance example: a derived input with nonzero higher homotopy

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/derived-input-higher-homotopy` · application. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.Derived` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/Derived/Examples`.

Let (A, I) be a bounded prism with A/I ≠ 0 and R := A/I ⊗^L_{(A/I)⟨x⟩} A/I, both maps sending x to 0; R is the free derived p-complete simplicial A/I-algebra on one generator in degree 1, with π_0(R) = A/I and π_1(R) ≅ A/I. Then: (1) L_{R/(A/I)} ≃ R[1] and gr_i^conj Δ̄_{R/A} ≃ R{−i} for every i ≥ 0; (2) Δ̄_{R/A} ∈ D^{[−1,0]} and H^{−1}(Δ̄_{R/A}) contains π_1(R) = A/I, so it is nonzero; (3) Δ_{R/A} ≃ A ⊗̂^L_{Δ_{(A/I)⟨x⟩/A}} A; (4) the comparison map c_R : Δ_{R/A} → RΓ((π_0(R)/A)_Δ, O_Δ) = A is not an isomorphism, Δ_{R/A} is not discrete and is not determined by π_0(R); node derived-agrees-with-site (b) does not apply to R.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** p is a fixed prime and (A, I) is a bounded prism (PR.0): A/I has bounded p^∞-torsion, and A is derived and classically (p, I)-complete. A derived p-complete simplicial A/I-algebra is an animated commutative A/I-algebra (EnhancedDerivedSheaves E5:animation) whose underlying complex is derived p-complete (DD.1); tensor products of such algebras are derived and derived p-completed. M{n} := M ⊗_{A/I} (I/I²)^{⊗n} is the Breuil–Kisin twist of an A/I-module or complex M, for n ∈ Z; I/I² is an invertible A/I-module.

**Construction or proof.**

1. (1): the cotangent complex of a free animated algebra on M[1] is R ⊗ M[1]; ∧^i(R[1]) = Γ^i(R)[i] = R[i] (DD.0). Apply node derived-hodge-tate-comparison; no completion is needed since R is a perfect A/I-complex.
2. (2): each gr_i^conj ≃ R{−i} lies in D^{[−1,0]}, so do all Fil_i^conj and their completed colimit; since H^{−2}(gr_i^conj) = 0 the maps H^{−1}(Fil_{i−1}^conj) → H^{−1}(Fil_i^conj) are injective, and H^{−1}(Fil_0^conj) = π_1(R).
3. (3): node kunneth-formula applied to A/I ← (A/I)⟨x⟩ → A/I.
4. (4): the prismatic site of π_0(R) = A/I has the initial object (A, I), whose cohomology is A in degree 0; compare with (2) after reduction modulo I.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/derived-prismatic-cohomology`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-derived-prismatic-cohomology); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/derived-hodge-tate-comparison`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-derived-hodge-tate-comparison); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/kunneth-formula`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-kunneth-formula); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/comparison-to-prisms`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-comparison-to-prisms); `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E5:animation/animated-commutative-rings`; `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.0`; `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`.

**Acceptance.** The value differs from Δ_{π_0(R)/A} = A. Base change along a map of bounded prisms (A, I) → (B, J) carries the example for A to the example for B. For the crystalline prism (Z_p, (p)): R = F_p ⊗^L_{F_p[x]} F_p and Δ_{R/Z_p} = Z_p ⊗̂^L_{Δ_{F_p[x]/Z_p}} Z_p.

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-2-quasisyntomic-covers-lift-to-prisms"></a>

### Lifting quasisyntomic covers to the prismatic site

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/quasisyntomic-covers-lift-to-prisms` · theorem. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.Semiperfectoid` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/Semiperfectoid/Descent`.

Let (A, I) be a bounded prism and R a quasisyntomic A/I-algebra: R is p-complete with bounded p^∞-torsion and A/I → R is a quasisyntomic map (p-completely flat, with L_{R/(A/I)} of p-complete Tor-amplitude in [−1, 0]; BMS2 Definition 4.10). Then there is an object (B → B/IB ← R) of (R/A)_Δ such that R → B/IB is p-completely faithfully flat. One may take B = Δ_{S/A}, where S := (A/I)⟨x_j^{1/p^∞} : j ∈ J⟩ ⊗̂^L_{(A/I)⟨x_j : j ∈ J⟩} R for a surjection (A/I)⟨x_j : j ∈ J⟩ → R; then R → S is a quasisyntomic cover, S/p is relatively semiperfect over A/(I, p), (L_{S/(A/I)})^∧[−1] is a p-completely flat S-module, and S → Δ̄_{S/A} is p-completely faithfully flat. Consequently: (1) the map A→B is completely flat for (p,I), and is completely faithfully flat whenever A/I→R is so for p; (2) if A is perfect, (A, I) → (B, IB)_perf is flat, and faithfully flat if A/I → R is p-completely faithfully flat.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** p is a fixed prime and (A, I) is a bounded prism (PR.0): A/I has bounded p^∞-torsion, and A is derived and classically (p, I)-complete. Quasisyntomic maps are those of DD.0; in this statement "quasisyntomic A/I-algebra" is the relative notion, as the proof uses p-complete flatness of A/I → R. PerfectoidQuotients Q3 uses this statement for André's lemma; it is planned once, here.

**Construction or proof.**

1. R → S is the p-completed base change of the quasisyntomic cover (A/I)⟨x_j⟩ → (A/I)⟨x_j^{1/p^∞}⟩, hence a quasisyntomic cover (BMS2 Lemma 4.16); S is discrete with bounded p^∞-torsion.
2. S/p is a quotient of the flat A/(I, p)-algebra (A/(I, p))[x_j^{1/p^∞}], which has bijective relative Frobenius, so Ω^1_{S/(A/I)}/p = 0; together with Tor-amplitude in [−1, 0] this makes (L_{S/(A/I)})^∧[−1] p-completely flat.
3. Consequence (b) of node derived-hodge-tate-comparison: Δ̄_{S/A} is discrete and p-completely faithfully flat over S; node derived-agrees-with-site gives the δ-structure, so B = Δ_{S/A} is a bounded prism with R → S → B/IB p-completely faithfully flat.
4. (1): each map in A/I → R → S → B/IB is p-completely flat, so A → B is (p, I)-completely flat (PR.0, bounded prisms). (2): the perfection is the completed filtered colimit of B along φ; for perfect A each φ^n-twist of B is (p, I)-completely flat over A, and completed filtered colimits preserve complete (faithful) flatness.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/derived-hodge-tate-comparison`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-derived-hodge-tate-comparison); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/derived-agrees-with-site`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-derived-agrees-with-site); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/prism-category`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-prism-category); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/prism-perfection`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-prism-perfection); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/bounded-prism-complete-flatness`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-bounded-prism-complete-flatness); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/relative-prismatic-site`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-relative-prismatic-site); `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.0`; `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`; `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.5`.

**Acceptance.** R = A/I: B = A. R = (A/I)⟨x⟩: S = (A/I)⟨x^{1/p^∞}⟩ and B = Δ_{S/A} is the (p, I)-completed A[x^{1/p^∞}] with φ(x^{1/p^n}) = x^{1/p^{n−1}}, a relatively perfect δ-A-algebra with B/IB = S. For a quasisyntomic cover A/I → R of a perfect prism the resulting perfect prism over (A, I) is faithfully flat: the step used in André's lemma. For R = (A/I)⟨x⟩ the construction gives B = Δ_{S/A} with B/IB = S = (A/I)⟨x^{1/p^∞}⟩ ≠ R; the object Δ_{R/A} itself is not a prism (Δ̄_{R/A} has H^1 ≠ 0), although other objects with B/IB = R exist (A⟨x⟩ with δ(x) = 0).

**Sources.** [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Proposition 7.11 and its proof. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 60. Exact statement.. [ALB23](https://arxiv.org/abs/1907.10525v4), Proposition 3.3.8 (published: Proposition 3.20). Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 22. The same statement with the proof spelled out..

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-2-perfectoidization-coconnective"></a>

### Coconnectivity of perfectoidizations

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/perfectoidization-coconnective` · theorem. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.Perfection` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/Perfection/Basic`.

Let (A, I) be a perfect prism with R = A/I and d a generator of I. For every derived p-complete simplicial R-algebra S, both Δ_{S/A,perf} and S_perfd lie in D^{≥0}. Moreover H^0(Δ_{S/A,perf}) is a p-torsion-free, p-complete, perfect δ-ring on which φ is the unique Frobenius lift; A → H^0(Δ_{S/A,perf}) is a map of δ-rings; d is a nonzerodivisor of H^0(Δ_{S/A,perf}); and H^0(Δ_{S/A,perf})/p is a subring of H^0(Δ_{S/A,perf}/p).

**Hypotheses and conventions.** (A, I) is a perfect prism: φ_A is bijective; then I = (d) for a distinguished nonzerodivisor d, R := A/I is an integral perfectoid ring and A = A_inf(R) (PR.0). S is a derived p-complete simplicial R-algebra, R = A/I; all tensor products are derived and completed. The proof uses the operation P^0 on the homotopy groups of E_∞-F_p-algebras (Lurie, Rational and p-adic homotopy theory, §2.2); no atlas stage supplies it (recorded gap).

**Construction or proof.**

1. Δ_{S/A,perf}/p is the realisation of a simplicial cosimplicial F_p-algebra, the colimit along the levelwise Frobenius of the functorial model F_A(S)/p of node derived-agrees-with-site. The levelwise Frobenius of a simplicial cosimplicial F_p-algebra induces P^0 on its realisation, so P^0 acts invertibly on π_*(Δ_{S/A,perf}/p).
2. P^0 annihilates all homotopy classes of positive degree of an E_∞-F_p-algebra (Lurie, loc. cit., Remark 2.2.7). Hence Δ_{S/A,perf}/p ∈ D^{≥0}, and Δ_{S/A,perf} ∈ D^{≥0} by derived p-completeness.
3. H^0(Δ_{S/A,perf}) is p-torsion-free because Δ_{S/A,perf}/p ∈ D^{≥0}; φ lifts the Frobenius of H^0/p ⊂ H^0(Δ_{S/A,perf}/p) by the same argument. So H^0 is a perfect p-complete δ-ring with unique Frobenius lift (PR.0, perfect δ-rings), the map from A is a δ-map and d is carried to a distinguished element.
4. A distinguished element of a p-torsion-free, p-adically separated δ-ring with reduced reduction modulo p is a nonzerodivisor (BS22 Lemma 2.34, PR.0). Therefore S_perfd = cofib(d on Δ_{S/A,perf}) ∈ D^{≥0}.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/perfection-of-prismatic-cohomology`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-perfection-of-prismatic-cohomology); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/derived-agrees-with-site`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-derived-agrees-with-site); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/perfect-delta-rings`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-perfect-delta-rings); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/distinguished-element`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-distinguished-element); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/perfect-prisms-perfectoid-rings`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-perfect-prisms-perfectoid-rings); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/cech-alexander-complex`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-cech-alexander-complex); `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`; `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E5:abstract/algebra-objects`; [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/distinguished-in-perfect-delta-rings`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-distinguished-in-perfect-delta-rings).

**Acceptance.** S perfectoid: S_perfd = S in degree 0. S = F_p[x] over Z_p: S_perfd = F_p[x^{1/p^∞}] in degree 0. For S = O_C⟨x⟩ the object S_perfd is coconnective and not discrete (last example of node connective-perfectoidization-perfectoid): the theorem gives no bound from above. The unperfected Δ̄_{R/A} of node derived-input-higher-homotopy has H^{−1} ≠ 0; its perfection lies in D^{≥0}.

**Sources.** [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Lemma 8.4 and its proof. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 63. Exact statement; the additional assertions are established in the proof.. [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Proof of Lemma 8.4. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 63. The imported property of the operation..

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-2-perfectoidization-symmetric-monoidal"></a>

### Perfectoidization is symmetric monoidal

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/perfectoidization-symmetric-monoidal` · theorem. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.Perfection` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/Perfection/Basic`.

Let (A, I) be a perfect prism with R = A/I. The functors S ↦ Δ_{S/A,perf} and S ↦ S_perfd, from derived p-complete simplicial R-algebras to commutative algebras in D_comp(A), respectively to derived p-complete commutative algebras in D(R), are symmetric monoidal: for every diagram S_1 ← S_3 → S_2 the induced maps Δ_{S_1/A,perf} ⊗̂^L_{Δ_{S_3/A,perf}} Δ_{S_2/A,perf} → Δ_{(S_1 ⊗̂^L_{S_3} S_2)/A,perf} and S_{1,perfd} ⊗̂^L_{S_{3,perfd}} S_{2,perfd} → (S_1 ⊗̂^L_{S_3} S_2)_perfd are equivalences. In BS22 the source category is that of derived p-complete simplicial rings admitting a map from a perfectoid ring: given S_1 ← S_3 → S_2 one chooses a perfectoid ring mapping to S_3 and applies the statement above.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** (A, I) is a perfect prism: φ_A is bijective; then I = (d) for a distinguished nonzerodivisor d, R := A/I is an integral perfectoid ring and A = A_inf(R) (PR.0). S is a derived p-complete simplicial R-algebra, R = A/I; all tensor products are derived and completed. Independence of the perfect base prism, dependence on π_0(S) only, and the description through the perfect prismatic site are BS22 Proposition 8.5, which is not planned in this stage (recorded gap); every statement here is relative to the fixed perfect prism (A, I).

**Construction or proof.**

1. Δ_{−/A} is symmetric monoidal (node kunneth-formula).
2. Sequential colimits along Frobenius are sifted, so they commute with relative tensor products; derived (p, I)-completion is symmetric monoidal for the completed tensor product (DD.1). Hence the perfection is symmetric monoidal.
3. Reduction modulo I is the symmetric monoidal base change − ⊗^L_A A/I.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/kunneth-formula`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-kunneth-formula); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/perfection-of-prismatic-cohomology`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-perfection-of-prismatic-cohomology); `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`; `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E5:abstract/symmetric-monoidal-infinity-category`.

S_1, S_2, S_3 perfectoid: the completed derived tensor product of perfectoid rings is perfectoid and discrete (PR.0, perfectoid-tor-independence), in accordance with the formula. S_1 = S_2 = S_perfd over S when S_perfd is discrete: (S_perfd ⊗̂^L_S S_perfd)_perfd = S_perfd, the step used in node connective-perfectoidization-perfectoid. <a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-2-conjugate-splitting-and-lifting"></a>

### Splitting of the first conjugate piece and liftings modulo I²

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/conjugate-splitting-and-lifting` · theorem. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.Derived` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/Derived/HodgeTate`.

Let (A, I) be a bounded prism and X a p-completely flat p-adic formal scheme over A/I. The extension Fil_0^conj Δ̄_{X/A} = O_X → Fil_1^conj Δ̄_{X/A} → gr_1^conj Δ̄_{X/A} = (L_{X/(A/I)}{−1}[−1])^∧ has a splitting in D(X) exactly when a p-completely flat lift of X across A/I²→A/I exists. More precisely, the class of this extension in Ext^1_{O_X}(gr_1^conj, gr_0^conj) = Ext^2_{O_X}((L_{X/(A/I)})^∧{−1}, O_X) is, up to sign, the obstruction class to lifting X over A/I².

**Hypotheses and conventions.** p is a fixed prime and (A, I) is a bounded prism (PR.0): A/I has bounded p^∞-torsion, and A is derived and classically (p, I)-complete. M{n} := M ⊗_{A/I} (I/I²)^{⊗n} is the Breuil–Kisin twist of an A/I-module or complex M, for n ∈ Z; I/I² is an invertible A/I-module. X is locally the formal spectrum of a p-complete ring with bounded p^∞-torsion (automatic for p-completely flat X over the bounded A/I). ALB23 phrase the splitting as "isomorphic in D(X) to a complex with zero differentials"; the node uses the precise form from their proof, the vanishing of the extension class.

**Construction or proof.**

1. By node first-conjugate-piece-cotangent the extension class equals the class of the transitivity triangle O_X ⊗ I/I²[1] → L_{X/Spf(A)}^∧ → L_{X/(A/I)}^∧, twisted by {−1}.
2. Illusie, Complexe cotangent III.2.1.2.3 (ALB23 Proposition 3.2.2; requested from DD.0): for a ring S, an invertible ideal I and a flat S/I-scheme Y, the class of L_{Y/S} in Ext^2(L_{Y/(S/I)}, I/I² ⊗ O_Y) is, up to sign, the obstruction to lifting Y to a flat S/I²-scheme.
3. Reduce modulo p^n: since A/I is classically p-complete, a p-completely flat lift of X over A/I² is a compatible system of flat lifts of X ⊗ A/(I, p^n) over A/(I², p^n); derived p-completion does not change the derived reductions of the cotangent complex. A splitting of the completed triangle induces compatible splittings for all n, and a splitting (not only the vanishing of the class) determines the lift, so the lifts are compatible.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/first-conjugate-piece-cotangent`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-first-conjugate-piece-cotangent); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/conjugate-filtration`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-conjugate-filtration); `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.0`; `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`.

**Acceptance.** If X lifts to a (p, I)-completely flat δ-A-scheme, the Higgs specialisation of BS22 Remark 4.13 splits O_X → Δ̄_{X/A}, in particular Fil_1^conj. For (A, I) = (Z_p, (p)) the statement is the Deligne–Illusie criterion: Fil_1^conj splits exactly when X lifts to Z/p². X = Spf(A/I): the class lies in the zero group.

**Sources.** [ALB23](https://arxiv.org/abs/1907.10525v4), Corollary 3.2.3 (published: Corollary 3.14) and Proposition 3.2.2. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 20. Exact statement; the equality of classes is from the proof.. [ALB23](https://arxiv.org/abs/1907.10525v4), Proposition 3.2.2 (published: Proposition 3.13). <a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-2-qrsp-prism"></a>

### The prism of a quasiregular semiperfectoid ring

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/qrsp-prism` · theorem. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.Semiperfectoid` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/Semiperfectoid/Basic`.

Let S be a quasiregular semiperfectoid ring, R any perfectoid ring with a map R → S, and (A, I) = (A_inf(R), ker θ). Then: (1) gr_i^conj Δ̄_{S/A} ≃ Γ^i_S(L_{S/R}[−1]){−i}^∧ is a p-completely flat S-module; Δ̄_{S/A} is discrete with bounded p^∞-torsion, and the map S → Δ̄_{S/A} is p-completely faithfully flat. (2) Δ_{S/A} is discrete, carries a δ-A-algebra structure refining φ_S, and (Δ_{S/A}, IΔ_{S/A}) is a bounded, orientable prism. (3) (Δ_{S/A}, IΔ_{S/A}), with the map S → Δ_{S/A}/I, is the initial object of the category of all prisms (B, J) equipped with a ring map S → B/J: it is the initial prism Δ_S^init of S. Being bounded, it is also the initial object of the absolute prismatic site (S)_Δ and of (S/A)_Δ. (4) Hence Δ_{S/A}, with its δ-structure, Frobenius and map from S, does not depend on R; it is denoted Δ_S, and Δ̄_S := Δ_S/I. (5) If A/I → S is surjective and K = ker(A → S), the canonical maps Δ_{S/A} → Δ^{init,unbdd}_{S/A} := RΓ((S/A)_{Δ,unbdd}, O_Δ) → Δ^init_{S/A} := RΓ((S/A)_Δ, O_Δ) (evaluation on all prisms, then restriction to bounded prisms) are isomorphisms of δ-rings, and Δ^{init,unbdd}_{S/A} is the prismatic envelope A{K/I}^∧ of the δ-pair (A, K).

**Hypotheses and conventions.** Quasiregular semiperfectoid rings are those of BMS2 Definition 4.20, equivalently of BS22 Notation 7.1 (BMS2 Remarks 4.21–4.22, Lemma 4.25): S is p-complete with bounded p^∞-torsion, receives a surjection from a perfectoid ring, and L_{S/Z_p}[−1] is p-completely flat over S. The definition and these equivalences are supplied by DerivedDeRhamCohomology DD.0/DD.5 and are not restated as a node here. M{n} := M ⊗_{A/I} (I/I²)^{⊗n} is the Breuil–Kisin twist of an A/I-module or complex M, for n ∈ Z; I/I² is an invertible A/I-module. In (3) the category contains unbounded prisms; it is not the absolute prismatic site of BS22 Remark 4.7, whose objects are bounded (the registered correction PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22/E5). The existence of an initial prism for an arbitrary semiperfectoid ring (BS22 Proposition 7.2) belongs to PerfectoidQuotients Q2 and is not used: for quasiregular S existence follows from node derived-agrees-with-site. (S/A)_{Δ,unbdd} is the category of all prisms over (A, I) with a map S → B/J, with the chaotic topology (ALB23 §3.4).

**Construction or proof.**

1. L_{S/R}[−1] is p-completely flat over S for every perfectoid R → S (BMS2 Lemma 4.25, from DD.5). Consequence (b) of node derived-hodge-tate-comparison gives (1), and node derived-agrees-with-site gives (2) and a weakly initial prism whose initial retract is cut out by an idempotent e_S; it remains to show e_S = id.
2. Replace R by R⟨Y_i^{1/p^∞}⟩ for a set of variables: this does not change the completed cotangent complexes, hence not Δ_{S/R}; so R → S may be assumed surjective. Choose generators f_j of its kernel. The map S′ := R⟨X_j^{1/p^∞}⟩/(X_j − f_j)^∧ → S, X_j ↦ 0, is surjective and surjective on cotangent complexes, so Δ_{S′/A} → Δ_{S/A} is surjective by the Hodge–Tate comparison; by naturality of the idempotent it suffices to treat S′.
3. S′ is a completed filtered colimit of rings T = R⟨X_1^{1/p^∞},…,X_r^{1/p^∞}⟩/(X_1 − f_1,…,X_r − f_r), and Δ commutes with filtered colimits (node kunneth-formula). For T, Δ_{T/A} ≃ Δ_{T/A′} with A′ = A_inf(R⟨X_1^{1/p^∞},…,X_r^{1/p^∞}⟩), compatibly with idempotents, and node regular-quotient-prismatic-envelope gives e_T = id.
4. (3) and (4): by BS22 Lemma 4.8 (node PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/perfect-prism-initial) every ring map A/I → B/J to the reduction of a prism lifts uniquely to a map of prisms (A, I) → (B, J); so prisms over (A, I) with a map from S are the same as prisms with a ring map S → B/J.
5. (5): Δ^{init,unbdd}_{S/A} = A{K/I}^∧ by the universal property of the envelope; it is the initial object of the category in (3), hence equal to Δ_{S/A}, which is bounded and therefore also computes the cohomology of the site of bounded prisms.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/derived-hodge-tate-comparison`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-derived-hodge-tate-comparison); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/derived-agrees-with-site`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-derived-agrees-with-site); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/idempotent-retract-initial-object`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-idempotent-retract-initial-object); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/regular-quotient-prismatic-envelope`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-regular-quotient-prismatic-envelope); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/derived-prismatic-base-change`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-derived-prismatic-base-change); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/kunneth-formula`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-kunneth-formula); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/comparison-to-prisms`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-comparison-to-prisms); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/perfect-prisms-perfectoid-rings`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-perfect-prisms-perfectoid-rings); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/ainf-prism`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-ainf-prism); `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.5`; `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.0`; [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/perfect-prism-initial`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-perfect-prism-initial); `PerfectoidQuotients:Q0:integral-algebra`.

**Acceptance.** S = R perfectoid: Δ_S = A_inf(R). S = O_C/p: Δ_S = A_inf{p/ξ}^∧ (node regular-semiperfectoid-example). S = R⟨x^{1/p^∞}, y^{1/p^∞}⟩/(xy): node singular-qrsp-example. Independence: for S = O_C/p the perfect prisms A_inf(O_C) and A_inf(O_C⟨Y^{1/p^∞}⟩) with Y ↦ 0 give the same Δ_S. For pS = 0, Δ_S is A_crys(S) up to the Frobenius twist (node qrsp-char-p-acrys).

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-2-perfection-descendable"></a>

### Strong descent for the passage to the perfection

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/perfection-descendable` · theorem. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.Perfection` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/Perfection/Descent`.

Let R be a perfectoid ring with perfect prism (A, I), T = R[X_1,…,X_n]^∧ and T_∞ = R[X_1^{1/p^∞},…,X_n^{1/p^∞}]^∧, the p-adic completions. The natural maps Δ_{T/A} → Δ_{T_∞/A} and Δ_{T/A,perf} → Δ_{T_∞/A,perf} are descendable, in the sense of Mathew, as maps of commutative algebras in D_comp(A). Consequence used by the source: for a derived p-complete simplicial R-algebra S with a map T → S, with S̃ := (T_∞ ⊗^L_T S)^∧ and S̃^• the derived p-completed Čech nerve of S → S̃, one has Δ_{S/A} ≃ lim_{[m] ∈ Δ} Δ_{S̃^m/A} and Δ_{S/A,perf} ≃ lim_{[m] ∈ Δ} Δ_{S̃^m/A,perf}.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** (A, I) is a perfect prism: φ_A is bijective; then I = (d) for a distinguished nonzerodivisor d, R := A/I is an integral perfectoid ring and A = A_inf(R) (PR.0). Descendability, its stability under base change and tensor products, and the bound for colimits along compatible endomorphisms (Bhatt–Scholze, Projectivity of the Witt vector affine Grassmannian, Lemma 11.22) are requested from EnhancedDerivedSheaves E5:abstract. The reduced auxiliary ring A/(p, φ^{−1}(d)) ≅ R/p is semiperfect rather than necessarily perfect. The proof uses only its F_p-algebra structure; the stronger source description is recorded as a source issue.

**Construction or proof.**

1. The perfected statement follows from the unperfected one: if B → C is descendable of index ≤ n with compatible endomorphisms, then colim_φ B → colim_φ C is descendable of index ≤ 2n.
2. Δ_{−/A} commutes with coproducts (node kunneth-formula), and tensor products of descendable maps are descendable, so n = 1. Let F be the fibre of Δ_{T/A} → Δ_{T_∞/A}; it suffices that every map F^{⊗2} → Δ_{T/A} of Δ_{T/A}-modules is null, which follows from RHom_{Δ_{T/A}}(F^{⊗2}, Δ_{T/A}) ∈ D^{<0}.
3. By completeness this is checked after base change along A → A/(p, φ^{−1}(d)) =: k. There Δ_{T/A} ⊗^L_A k ≃ (φ_A^*Δ_{T/A} ⊗̂^L_A A/I) ⊗^L_{A/I} A/(I, p) is the de Rham complex of k[X] over k by the de Rham comparison of PR.1 (its hypothesis holds: A/I is perfectoid, hence reduced, and the ring of Witt vectors of a reduced ring is p-torsion-free), and by the Cartier isomorphism for a polynomial algebra this is the split square-zero extension Ω = T′ ⊕ Ω^1_{T′/k}[−1] with T′ = k[X]; likewise Δ_{T_∞/A} ⊗^L_A k ≃ T′_∞ := k[X^{1/p^∞}].
4. The fibre of Ω → T′ is T′[−1] as an Ω-module, and T′_∞ is a free T′-module with 1 in a basis, so the fibre of Ω → T′_∞ is a direct sum of copies of T′[−1]. The claim reduces to RHom_Ω((T′[−1])^{⊗2}, Ω) ∈ D^{<0}, computed with the resolution (⋯ → Ω[−3] → Ω[−2] → Ω[−1]) of T′[−1] whose maps are given by dX.
5. The consequence: descendability is stable under base change, and Δ_{S̃/A} = Δ_{S/A} ⊗̂^L_{Δ_{T/A}} Δ_{T_∞/A} by node kunneth-formula; a descendable map B → C satisfies B ≃ lim C^{⊗(•+1)}.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/kunneth-formula`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-kunneth-formula); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/perfection-of-prismatic-cohomology`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-perfection-of-prismatic-cohomology); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/derived-prismatic-cohomology`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-derived-prismatic-cohomology); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/derived-hodge-tate-comparison`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-derived-hodge-tate-comparison); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/de-rham-comparison`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-de-rham-comparison); `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.3/polynomial-cartier-map`; `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E5:abstract`; `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`; `PerfectoidQuotients:Q0:integral-algebra`; [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/perfectoidization-symmetric-monoidal`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-perfectoidization-symmetric-monoidal).

**Acceptance.** n = 0: both maps are identities. After perfection the target is Δ_{T_∞/A,perf} = A_inf(T_∞), the perfect prism of the perfectoid ring T_∞. In characteristic p, (A, I) = (Z_p, (p)): Δ_{F_p[X]/Z_p,perf} = Z_p⟨X^{1/p^∞}⟩ = Δ_{F_p[X^{1/p^∞}]/Z_p,perf}, and the second map is an isomorphism. The map T → T_∞ is a quasisyntomic cover, so the limit formula for Δ_{S/A} is also an instance of node quasisyntomic-descent when S is quasisyntomic; descendability gives it for every S.

**Sources.** [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Lemma 8.6 and its proof. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 66. Exact statement.. <a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-2-connective-perfectoidization-perfectoid"></a>

### Connective perfectoidizations are perfectoid and universal

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/connective-perfectoidization-perfectoid` · theorem. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.Perfection` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/Perfection/Basic`.

Let (A, I) be a perfect prism with R = A/I and S a derived p-complete simplicial R-algebra. Assume that S_perfd is connective; equivalently, by node perfectoidization-coconnective, that it is concentrated in degree 0. Then Δ_{S/A,perf} is discrete and is a perfect (p, I)-complete δ-A-algebra, (Δ_{S/A,perf}, IΔ_{S/A,perf}) is a perfect prism, S_perfd is a perfectoid ring, and S → S_perfd is the universal map from S to a perfectoid ring: every map from π_0(S) to a perfectoid ring S′ factors uniquely through S_perfd. In particular S_perfd is then independent of the perfect base, and for a semiperfectoid ring S whose S_perfd is connective it is the universal perfectoid ring of PerfectoidQuotients Q2 (BS22 Corollary 7.3).

**Hypotheses and conventions.** (A, I) is a perfect prism: φ_A is bijective; then I = (d) for a distinguished nonzerodivisor d, R := A/I is an integral perfectoid ring and A = A_inf(R) (PR.0). S is a derived p-complete simplicial R-algebra, R = A/I; all tensor products are derived and completed. Connectivity of S_perfd is a hypothesis: for S = O_C⟨x⟩ it fails (last acceptance example). That S_perfd is connective for every semiperfectoid S is part of BS22 Proposition 8.5 and Theorem 7.4, which belong to other roadmaps; it is not asserted here.

**Construction or proof.**

1. If S_perfd is discrete then Δ_{S/A,perf} is discrete by derived Nakayama (last step of node derived-hodge-tate-comparison (b)). By node perfectoidization-coconnective it is a perfect p-complete δ-A-algebra, and d is a distinguished nonzerodivisor in it; so (Δ_{S/A,perf}, (d)) is a perfect prism and S_perfd is perfectoid (PR.0).
2. Existence of factorisations: a map S → S′ to a perfectoid ring induces S_perfd → S′_perfd = S′ (node perfection-comparison (2)).
3. Uniqueness: two factorisations give a map η : S_perfd ⊗̂^L_S S_perfd → S′, which factors through (S_perfd ⊗̂^L_S S_perfd)_perfd because S′ = S′_perfd. By node perfectoidization-symmetric-monoidal and (S_perfd)_perfd = S_perfd this is S_perfd via the multiplication map, so η factors through the multiplication.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/perfectoidization-coconnective`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-perfectoidization-coconnective); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/perfectoidization-symmetric-monoidal`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-perfectoidization-symmetric-monoidal); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/perfection-comparison`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-perfection-comparison); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/perfection-of-prismatic-cohomology`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-perfection-of-prismatic-cohomology); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/perfect-prisms-perfectoid-rings`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-perfect-prisms-perfectoid-rings); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/perfect-delta-rings`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-perfect-delta-rings); `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`; `PerfectoidQuotients:Q0:integral-algebra`.

**Acceptance.** S perfectoid: S_perfd = S with the identity. S = F_p[x] over (Z_p, (p)): S_perfd = F_p[x^{1/p^∞}] is the universal perfect F_p[x]-algebra. S = F_p[x^{1/p^∞}]/(x) over (Z_p, (p)): S_perfd = F_p[x^{1/p^∞}]/(x^{1/p^n} : n ≥ 0) = F_p, the quotient by the radical. S = O_C⟨x⟩, C complete and algebraically closed over Q_p: there is no universal perfectoid S-algebra U. Indeed the automorphisms t^{1/p^n} ↦ ζ_{p^n} t^{1/p^n} of O_C⟨t^{1/p^∞}⟩ fix t, so the map U → O_C⟨t^{1/p^∞}⟩ classifying t would land in the invariants O_C⟨t⟩; but the image of x is a p-th power modulo p in U and t is not one in (O_C/p)[t]. Hence S_perfd is not connective.

**Sources.** [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Corollary 8.14 and its proof. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 70. Exact statement..

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-2-quasisyntomic-descent"></a>

### Quasisyntomic descent and unfolding

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/quasisyntomic-descent` · theorem. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.Semiperfectoid` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/Semiperfectoid/Descent`.

Let (A, I) be a bounded prism. Let C_{A/I} be the category of p-complete A/I-algebras B with bounded p^∞-torsion such that L_{B/(A/I)} has p-complete Tor-amplitude in [−1, 0], and call B → C in C_{A/I} a cover if it is a quasisyntomic cover (p-completely faithfully flat with L_{C/B} of p-complete Tor-amplitude in [−1, 0]). (1) For every cover B → C with p-completed Čech nerve C^• (each C^n is discrete, of bounded p^∞-torsion and in C_{A/I}), the maps Δ_{B/A} → lim_{[n] ∈ Δ} Δ_{C^n/A}, Δ̄_{B/A} → lim Δ̄_{C^n/A} and Fil_i^conj Δ̄_{B/A} → lim Fil_i^conj Δ̄_{C^n/A}, for every i, are equivalences. So B ↦ Δ_{B/A} is a sheaf on C_{A/I}^op with values in commutative algebras with Frobenius in D_comp(A). (2) If (A, I) is perfect, C_{A/I} contains the category QSyn_{A/I} of all maps A/I → B with B a quasisyntomic ring (BMS2 Variant 4.33 and Lemma 4.34), so B ↦ Δ_{B/A} is a sheaf for the quasisyntomic topology on QSyn_{A/I}. (3) Unfolding: for perfect (A, I) and B in QSyn_{A/I}, choose a quasisyntomic cover B → S with S quasiregular semiperfectoid. All terms S^n of its Čech nerve are quasiregular semiperfectoid and Δ_{B/A} ≃ lim_{[n] ∈ Δ} Δ_{S^n}, a limit of discrete δ-rings; thus Δ_{−/A} on QSyn_{A/I} is the unfolding (BMS2 Proposition 4.31) of S ↦ Δ_S on quasiregular semiperfectoid rings. In particular Δ_{B/A} ∈ D^{≥0}, and Δ_{B/A} with its Frobenius does not depend on the perfect prism (A, I) under B.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** p is a fixed prime and (A, I) is a bounded prism (PR.0): A/I has bounded p^∞-torsion, and A is derived and classically (p, I)-complete. A derived p-complete simplicial A/I-algebra is an animated commutative A/I-algebra (EnhancedDerivedSheaves E5:animation) whose underlying complex is derived p-complete (DD.1); tensor products of such algebras are derived and derived p-completed. BS22 state (2), for a perfect prism. Part (1) is the statement the same proof gives for a bounded prism under the cotangent hypothesis that BMS2 Lemma 4.34 supplies in the perfect case (its proof read with the registered correction PAPER-BHATT-MORROW-SCHOLZE-19/E2). The quasisyntomic site, covers by quasiregular semiperfectoid rings, unfolding and flat descent for completed cotangent powers are supplied by DD.5. Descent is asserted for the quasisyntomic topology only: for a p-completely faithfully flat map without control of the cotangent complex the graded pieces are not uniformly coconnective and the argument does not apply.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Reduce to Δ̄: limits commute with − ⊗^L_A A/I, and a map of derived I-complete objects that is an isomorphism modulo I is an isomorphism (DD.1).
2. Graded pieces: B ↦ (∧^i L_{B/(A/I)})^∧ satisfies descent along p-completely faithfully flat maps of p-complete rings with bounded p^∞-torsion (BMS2 Theorem 3.1 and Remark 4.9; DD.5); twisting and shifting preserve this. By induction each Fil_i^conj satisfies descent.
3. Passage to the colimit: on C_{A/I}, gr_i^conj ∈ D^{[0,i]} (node derived-hodge-tate-comparison (a)), so all Fil_i^conj lie in D^{≥0}. Totalisations of cosimplicial objects of D^{≥0} commute with filtered colimits, and with derived p-completion, so Δ̄ satisfies descent.
4. (2): BMS2 Lemma 4.34. (3): BMS2 Lemmas 4.28 and 4.30 give the cover and its Čech nerve (DD.5), node qrsp-prism gives discreteness and independence of the base, and BMS2 Proposition 4.31 identifies sheaves on the two sites.

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-2-qrsp-char-p-acrys"></a>

### In characteristic p the prism of a quasiregular semiperfect ring is A_crys

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/qrsp-char-p-acrys` · comparison. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.Semiperfectoid` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/Semiperfectoid/Crystalline`.

Let S be a quasiregular semiperfectoid ring with pS = 0 (a quasiregular semiperfect F_p-algebra), k := S^♭ the inverse-limit perfection of S, so that k → S is surjective, and A := W(k) with the crystalline perfect prism (A, (p)). Let A_crys(S) be the p-adic completion of the PD envelope of A → S (PD structure compatible with that of (p)), the universal p-complete PD thickening of S (CR.0). Then: (1) there is a canonical isomorphism of p-complete δ-A-algebras, compatible with Frobenius, Δ_{S/A} ⊗̂_{A,φ_A} A ≃ A_crys(S). (2) Since φ_A is bijective this gives a φ-equivariant isomorphism of δ-rings Δ_S ≃ A_crys(S); it is φ_A-semilinear over W(k) and not W(k)-linear. Under it the structure map S → Δ̄_S = Δ_S/p corresponds to the map S → A_crys(S)/p through which the Frobenius of A_crys(S)/p factors. (3) If S = k/(x) for a nonzerodivisor x ∈ k, then Δ_{S/W(k)} = W(k){[x]/p}^∧ and A_crys(S) = W(k){[x]^p/p}^∧. (4) For every quasisyntomic k-algebra B the isomorphism of node derived-crystalline-comparison, φ_A^*Δ_{B/A} ≃ RΓ_crys(B/A) (derived crystalline cohomology, node derived-crystalline-comparison), is the unfolding of the isomorphisms (1) over the Čech nerve of a quasisyntomic cover B → S by a quasiregular semiperfect ring: the crystalline comparison extends by descent from quasiregular semiperfect rings to all quasisyntomic F_p-algebras.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** Quasiregular semiperfectoid rings are those of BMS2 Definition 4.20, equivalently of BS22 Notation 7.1 (BMS2 Remarks 4.21–4.22, Lemma 4.25): S is p-complete with bounded p^∞-torsion, receives a surjection from a perfectoid ring, and L_{S/Z_p}[−1] is p-completely flat over S. The definition and these equivalences are supplied by DerivedDeRhamCohomology DD.0/DD.5 and are not restated as a node here. For every perfect prism (A′, I′) with a map A′/I′ → S one has Δ_{S/A′} = Δ_S (node qrsp-prism), so (2) holds for all such bases, as in ALB23 Lemma 3.4.2. ALB23 prove (2) using the map θ : Δ_S → S of BS22 Theorem 12.2 (PR.3). The route planned here does not use the Nygaard filtration.

**Construction or proof.**

1. By node derived-crystalline-comparison, Δ_{S/A} ⊗̂_{A,φ_A} A ≃ RΓ_crys(S/A), the derived crystalline cohomology of S over A (not the p-completed derived de Rham complex of S over A).
2. For quasiregular semiperfect S the derived crystalline cohomology of S over A (the p-completed left Kan extension of P ↦ RΓ_crys(P/A) from polynomial k-algebras; the derived de Rham–Witt complex LWΩ_S of BMS2 §8.2) is concentrated in degree 0, p-torsion-free and naturally isomorphic to A_crys(S) compatibly with Frobenius (BMS2 Proposition 8.13 and Theorem 8.14 (1), (3)); its reduction modulo p is LΩ_{S/F_p} ≅ A_crys(S)/p (BMS2 Proposition 8.12). The derived de Rham reduction modulo p is requested from DD.4; the crystalline discreteness, torsion-freeness and comparison are requested from CR.4; the identification of LWΩ_S with the left Kan extension used here is the recorded gap "Derived crystalline cohomology of quasiregular semiperfect rings". This gives (1); (2) is its untwisted form, and the description of S → A_crys(S)/p follows from semilinearity.
3. (3): node regular-quotient-prismatic-envelope gives Δ_{S/A} = A{[x]/p}^∧; base change along φ_A gives A{[x]^p/p}^∧, which is the p-completed PD envelope of ([x]) by PR.0 (pd-envelope-as-delta-envelope).
4. (4): both sides are quasisyntomic sheaves on quasisyntomic k-algebras (node quasisyntomic-descent; RΓ_crys(−/A) is a quasisyntomic sheaf because its reduction modulo p, dR_{−/k}, has a conjugate filtration with graded pieces ∧^i L_{−/k}[−i] (DD.3), which satisfy descent by DD.5), and the isomorphism is natural.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/qrsp-prism`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-qrsp-prism); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/derived-crystalline-comparison`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-derived-crystalline-comparison); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/regular-quotient-prismatic-envelope`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-regular-quotient-prismatic-envelope); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/quasisyntomic-descent`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-quasisyntomic-descent); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/pd-envelope-as-delta-envelope`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-pd-envelope-as-delta-envelope); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/crystalline-prism`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-crystalline-prism); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/perfect-delta-rings`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-perfect-delta-rings); `CrystallineCohomology:CR.0`; `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.4`; `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.5`; [`mathlib:WittVector`](#mathlib-wittvector); [`mathlib:PerfectRing`](#mathlib-perfectring).

**Acceptance.** S = k perfect: both sides are W(k) and the isomorphism of (2) is φ. S = F_p[x^{1/p^∞}]/(x): Δ_S is the p-completed PD envelope of (x^{1/p}) in Z_p[x^{1/p^∞}]^∧, and A_crys(S) that of (x). S = O_C/p: Δ_S = A_inf{ξ/p}^∧ = φ^{−1}(A_crys) and A_crys(S) = A_inf{φ(ξ)/p}^∧ is Fontaine's A_crys. The identification is not W(k)-linear: for S = k/(x), [x]/p lies in Δ_S but not in A_crys(S) ⊂ W(k)[1/p].

### Acceptance example: a singular quasiregular semiperfectoid algebra

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/singular-qrsp-example` · application. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.Semiperfectoid` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/Semiperfectoid/Examples`.

Let R be a perfectoid ring with perfect prism (A, (d)), B := R⟨x, y⟩/(xy) the p-completed node, and S := R⟨x^{1/p^∞}, y^{1/p^∞}⟩/(xy). Then: (1) B is quasisyntomic and not p-completely smooth over R; B → S is a quasisyntomic cover; S is quasiregular semiperfectoid and not perfectoid, since x^{1/p}y^{1/p} is a nonzero nilpotent when R ≠ 0. (2) Δ_S ≃ A′{[x^♭][y^♭]/d}^∧ with A′ = A_inf(R⟨x^{1/p^∞}, y^{1/p^∞}⟩); Δ̄_S is p-completely faithfully flat over S, with gr_i^conj ≃ S{−i} generated by the i-th divided power of the class of xy. (3) Δ_{B/A} ≃ lim_{[n] ∈ Δ} Δ_{S^n}, where S^n is the (n+1)-fold completed tensor power of S over B; each S^n is quasiregular semiperfectoid, for instance S^1 = R⟨x^{1/p^∞}, y^{1/p^∞}, x′^{1/p^∞}, y′^{1/p^∞}⟩/(xy, x − x′, y − y′). (4) gr_i^conj Δ̄_{B/A} ≃ (∧^i L_{B/R}){−i}[−i] with L_{B/R} ≃ [B → B dx ⊕ B dy], 1 ↦ y dx + x dy, in degrees −1, 0; for i ≥ 2 the complex ∧^i L_{B/R}[−i] is the Koszul complex of (y, x) on B placed in degrees 0, 1, 2, with H^0 = 0, H^2 = B/(x, y) = R and H^1 ≠ 0. So the conjugate filtration of the singular B has infinitely many nonzero graded pieces, in contrast with a p-completely smooth algebra of relative dimension 1. (5) A quasiregular semiperfectoid ring that is not a quotient by a finite regular sequence: S′ = R⟨X_j^{1/p^∞} : j ∈ J⟩/(X_j − f_j : j ∈ J)^∧ for an infinite family (f_j); Δ_{S′} is the completed filtered colimit of the envelopes of the finite subfamilies.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** Quasiregular semiperfectoid rings are those of BMS2 Definition 4.20, equivalently of BS22 Notation 7.1 (BMS2 Remarks 4.21–4.22, Lemma 4.25): S is p-complete with bounded p^∞-torsion, receives a surjection from a perfectoid ring, and L_{S/Z_p}[−1] is p-completely flat over S. The definition and these equivalences are supplied by DerivedDeRhamCohomology DD.0/DD.5 and are not restated as a node here. M{n} := M ⊗_{A/I} (I/I²)^{⊗n} is the Breuil–Kisin twist of an A/I-module or complex M, for n ∈ Z; I/I² is an invertible A/I-module. R ≠ 0 in the non-vanishing assertions.

**Construction or proof.**

1. (1): B is the quotient of the p-completely smooth R⟨x, y⟩ by the nonzerodivisor xy, so L_{B/R} has Tor-amplitude in [−1, 0]; S is the p-completed base change of B along R⟨x, y⟩ → R⟨x^{1/p^∞}, y^{1/p^∞}⟩, a quasisyntomic cover (BMS2 Lemma 4.16), and S is a regular quotient of a perfectoid ring.
2. (2): node regular-quotient-prismatic-envelope with r = 1 and node qrsp-prism.
3. (3): node quasisyntomic-descent, part (3).
4. (4): node derived-hodge-tate-comparison; the derived exterior power of the cofibre of B → B² is the Koszul-type complex Γ^i(B) → Γ^{i−1}(B) ⊗ B² → Γ^{i−2}(B) ⊗ ∧²B² (DD.0). In B, x a = y b forces both sides to vanish, which gives H^0 = 0 and identifies H^1 with a nonzero quotient of (y) ⊕ (x).
5. (5): the proof of BS22 Proposition 7.10 and node kunneth-formula for filtered colimits.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/qrsp-prism`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-qrsp-prism); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/regular-quotient-prismatic-envelope`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-regular-quotient-prismatic-envelope); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/quasisyntomic-descent`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-quasisyntomic-descent); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/derived-hodge-tate-comparison`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-derived-hodge-tate-comparison); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/kunneth-formula`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-kunneth-formula); `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.0`; `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.5`.

**Acceptance.** gr_1^conj Δ̄_S is free of rank 1 over S. H^2(gr_i^conj Δ̄_{B/A}) = R{−i} for every i ≥ 2. For R = F_p: S = F_p[x^{1/p^∞}, y^{1/p^∞}]/(xy) and Δ_S is the p-completed PD envelope of ((xy)^{1/p}) in Z_p[x^{1/p^∞}, y^{1/p^∞}]^∧. S^1 is a quotient of a perfectoid ring by a regular sequence of length 3.

### Acceptance example: a regular semiperfectoid quotient

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/regular-semiperfectoid-example` · application. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.Semiperfectoid` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/Semiperfectoid/Examples`.

Let R be a perfectoid ring with perfect prism (A, (d)) = (A_inf(R), ker θ), let f_1,…,f_r ∈ R, R_∞ := R⟨X_1^{1/p^∞},…,X_r^{1/p^∞}⟩ and T := R_∞/(X_1 − f_1,…,X_r − f_r). Then: (1) T is a p-completely free R-module (topologically free on the monomials X^a with exponents in [0,1) ∩ Z[1/p]), X_1 − f_1,…,X_r − f_r is a regular sequence in R_∞, and T is quasiregular semiperfectoid. (2) With A′ := A_inf(R_∞) and g_i := [X_i^♭] − f̃_i for lifts f̃_i ∈ A′ of f_i, Δ_T ≃ A′{g_1/d,…,g_r/d}^∧, the prismatic envelope of (d, g_1,…,g_r), which is (p, d)-completely flat over A = A_inf(R) (and not over A′ when R ≠ 0 and r ≥ 1). (3) Δ̄_T is a p-completely faithfully flat T-algebra with gr_i^conj ≃ Γ^i_T(T^r){−i}. (4) Characteristic p: for R = F_p, r = 1, f = 0, T = F_p[X^{1/p^∞}]/(X), one has Δ_T = (Z_p[X^{1/p^∞}]^∧){X/p}^∧, the p-completed PD envelope of the ideal (X^{1/p}), which contains (X^{1/p})^n/n! for all n. (5) Mixed characteristic: for C a complete algebraically closed extension of Q_p, R = O_C and S = O_C/p, one has Δ_S = A_inf{p/ξ}^∧ = A_inf{ξ/p}^∧; in Δ_S the ideals (ξ) and (p) coincide, and φ maps Δ_S isomorphically onto Fontaine's A_crys = A_inf{φ(ξ)/p}^∧.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** Quasiregular semiperfectoid rings are those of BMS2 Definition 4.20, equivalently of BS22 Notation 7.1 (BMS2 Remarks 4.21–4.22, Lemma 4.25): S is p-complete with bounded p^∞-torsion, receives a surjection from a perfectoid ring, and L_{S/Z_p}[−1] is p-completely flat over S. The definition and these equivalences are supplied by DerivedDeRhamCohomology DD.0/DD.5 and are not restated as a node here. M{n} := M ⊗_{A/I} (I/I²)^{⊗n} is the Breuil–Kisin twist of an A/I-module or complex M, for n ∈ Z; I/I² is an invertible A/I-module.

**Construction or proof.**

1. (1): R_∞ is topologically free over R⟨X_1,…,X_r⟩ on the monomials with exponents in [0,1); dividing by X_i − f_i identifies T with the completed direct sum of copies of R. L_{T/R_∞} is free of rank r in degree −1, so T is quasiregular semiperfectoid by BMS2 Lemma 4.25 (DD.5).
2. (2), (3): node regular-quotient-prismatic-envelope over the perfect prism (A′, (d)) and independence of the perfectoid base (node qrsp-prism).
3. (4): [X] has δ([X]) = 0, so A′{X/p} = A′{φ(X^{1/p})/p} is the PD envelope of (X^{1/p}) (PR.0, pd-envelope-as-delta-envelope).
4. (5): in Δ_S the distinguished element ξ divides the distinguished element p, so they differ by a unit (PR.0, distinguished-factor-rigidity); hence ξ/p ∈ Δ_S and Δ_S = A_inf{ξ/p}^∧. Apply φ and node qrsp-char-p-acrys.

## PR.3. Nygaard filtration, divided Frobenius and twists

On the quasiregular semiperfectoid basis, Nygaard steps express divisibility under Frobenius; descent extends them to quasisyntomic rings. Divided Frobenius has a twisted, orientation-independent target. In oriented formulas, changing d to ud changes division by u^(−i). Construct the transversal cotangent-line limit and descend the Breuil–Kisin line to arbitrary bounded prisms, with Frobenius for every integer tensor power. The relative filtered Frobenius and its canonical map v give the Hodge triangle and the general de Rham comparison. Completion needs the joint Nygaard and (p,I)-adic δ-continuity estimate. The full integer-indexed Beilinson and E∞ enhancements are requested precisely; a finite nonnegative filtration does not stand in for them.
