<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-3-nygaard-filtration-qrsp"></a>

### Nygaard filtration of a quasiregular semiperfectoid ring

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/nygaard-filtration-qrsp` · definition. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.Nygaard` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/Nygaard/Basic`.

Let (B, J) be a prism with Frobenius φ_B. For i ≥ 0 put Fil^i_N B = φ_B^{-1}(J^i) = {x ∈ B : φ_B(x) ∈ J^i}, an ideal of B, and Fil^i_N B = B for i ≤ 0; gr^i_N B = Fil^i_N B / Fil^{i+1}_N B. For a quasiregular semiperfectoid ring S the Nygaard filtration of S is this filtration on its initial prism (Δ_S, IΔ_S) (PR.2/qrsp-prism): Fil^i_N Δ_S = {x ∈ Δ_S : φ(x) ∈ I^i Δ_S} = {x : φ(x) ∈ d^i Δ_S}, where d is the image of a generator of ker(θ : A_inf(R) → R) for any perfectoid ring R mapping to S (the ideal IΔ_S is principal and does not depend on R). It is an N-indexed decreasing filtration by ideals, multiplicative (Fil^i_N · Fil^j_N ⊂ Fil^{i+j}_N), and functorial: a map of prisms (B, J) → (B', J') carries Fil^i_N B into Fil^i_N B', so a map S → S' of quasiregular semiperfectoid rings carries Fil^i_N Δ_S into Fil^i_N Δ_{S'}. The filtration is by the Frobenius-divisibility condition itself; it is not the IΔ_S-adic filtration, not the powers of Fil^1_N, and not a divided-power filtration. It is not separated in general, and Δ_S need not be complete for it (PR.3/nygaard-incomplete-example).

**Hypotheses and conventions.** p is a fixed prime; prisms are those of PR.0/prism (δ-ring, invertible ideal, derived (p, I)-complete, p ∈ I + φ(I)). S is quasiregular semiperfectoid in the sense used by PR.2/qrsp-prism (BMS2 Definition 4.20); Δ_S is its initial prism, a discrete ring. No orientation is chosen in the definition: the condition φ(x) ∈ J^i uses only the ideal J. When J = (d) it reads φ(x) ∈ d^i B. The index set is N; negative indices give the whole ring.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Fil^i_N B is the preimage of the ideal J^i under the ring map φ_B, hence an ideal (Mathlib: comap of an ideal); it decreases with i because J^{i+1} ⊂ J^i.
2. Multiplicativity: φ(xy) = φ(x)φ(y) ∈ J^i J^j = J^{i+j}. Functoriality: a map of prisms f commutes with φ and f(J) ⊂ J', so f(φ^{-1}(J^i)) ⊂ φ^{-1}(J'^i).
3. For S quasiregular semiperfectoid apply this to (Δ_S, IΔ_S) of PR.2/qrsp-prism (BS22 Proposition 7.10); the ideal is generated by the image d of a generator of the perfect prism of any perfectoid R → S (perfect prisms are orientable, PR.0/perfect-prisms-perfectoid-rings), which gives the printed form of BS22 Definition 12.1.
4. The failure of completeness is computed in PR.3/nygaard-incomplete-example (there the filtration is separated). Non-separatedness is quoted from the warning after BS22 Definition 12.1 and is not exhibited by a node; since Δ_S is d-adically separated, ∩_i Fil^i_N Δ_S = ker(φ), so the filtration is separated exactly when φ is injective on Δ_S.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/qrsp-prism`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-qrsp-prism); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/prism`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-prism); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/prism-category`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-prism-category); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/perfect-prisms-perfectoid-rings`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-perfect-prisms-perfectoid-rings); [`mathlib:Ideal.comap`](#mathlib-ideal-comap); [`mathlib:Ideal.mem_comap`](#mathlib-ideal-mem-comap).

**Consumers.** BS22 Theorem 12.2: the filtration whose graded pieces are the conjugate filtration pieces. BS22 Theorem 13.1 and BMS2 Theorem 7.2: its completion is π_0 TC^-(S; Z_p) with the Nygaard filtration of BMS2. BS22 §14 and PR.4 (syntomic complexes): Z_p(n)(S) is the fibre of φ_n − 1 on Fil^n_N of the completion. Anschütz–Le Bras §4 (prismatic Dieudonné theory): Δ_S / Fil^1_N Δ_S ≅ S makes the structure sheaf of the quasisyntomic site a quotient of the prismatic sheaf. PR.5 (Bhatt–Lurie Corollary 5.6.3): the absolute Nygaard filtration restricted to quasiregular semiperfectoid rings is this filtration.

**Planning API.**

- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Nygaard.fil` (constructor): For a prism (B, J) and i ∈ N, the ideal Fil^i_N B = φ_B^{-1}(J^i) of B.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Nygaard.mem_fil_iff` (characterisation): x ∈ Fil^i_N B if and only if φ_B(x) ∈ J^i.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Nygaard.fil_zero` (simp): Fil^0_N B = B.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Nygaard.fil_antitone` (structure): If i ≤ j then Fil^j_N B ⊂ Fil^i_N B.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Nygaard.fil_mul_le` (structure): Fil^i_N B · Fil^j_N B ⊂ Fil^{i+j}_N B.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Nygaard.fil_map_le` (functoriality): For a map of prisms f : (B, J) → (B′, J′), f(Fil^i_N B) ⊂ Fil^i_N B′.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Nygaard.fil_eq_span_pow_of_perfect` (characterisation): If (B, (d)) is a perfect prism and φ(e) = d then Fil^i_N B = (e^i).
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Nygaard.gr` (data): The graded piece gr^i_N B = Fil^i_N B / Fil^{i+1}_N B as a B-module.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Nygaard.intersection_fil` (characterisation): For quasiregular semiperfectoid S, ⋂_(i≥0)Fil^i_NΔ_S=ker(φ:Δ_S→Δ_S), since Fil^i_N=φ^(-1)(I^iΔ_S) and Δ_S is I-adically separated. This is the kernel of the map to its Nygaard completion.

**Unit tests.**

- `pr3_nygaard_fil_zero` (degenerate): Fil^0_N B = B for every prism (B, J).
- `pr3_nygaard_fil_frobenius_id` (degenerate): If φ_B is the identity (for example (Z_p, (p))) then Fil^i_N B = J^i.
- `pr3_nygaard_fil_perfect` (computation): For a perfect prism (B, (d)) with e = φ^{-1}(d): Fil^i_N B = (e^i); for B the (p, [p]_q)-completion of Z_p[q^{1/p^∞}] and d = [p]_q this is ([p]_{q^{1/p}})^i.
- `pr3_nygaard_fil_one_perfect` (characterisation): For a perfect prism (B, (d)): x ∈ Fil^1_N B if and only if x maps to 0 under B → B/dB composed with φ, that is, Fil^1_N B is the kernel of θ ∘ φ.
- `pr3_nygaard_fil_not_powers` (non-example): It is false that Fil^i_N B = (Fil^1_N B)^i for all prisms and all i: in the key case Y^p/[p]_q! lies in Fil^p_N Δ_S and not in (Fil^1_N Δ_S)^p.

**Acceptance.** For S perfectoid, Δ_S = A_inf(S) and Fil^i_N = (φ^{-1}(d))^i A_inf(S); for S = Z_p[ζ_{p^∞}]^∧ this is ([p]_{q^{1/p}})^i. For the key case S = (Z_p[ζ_{p^∞}, X^{1/p^∞}]/X)^∧ the filtration is the one of PR.3/nygaard-key-case. The definition is intrinsic to S: it does not use a perfectoid ring mapping to S, while the conjugate filtration it is compared with does (BS22 Example 12.3).

**Sources.** [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Definition 12.1. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 86. the definition, stated for the initial prism of S; the node also records the same formula for an arbitrary prism. [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Theorem 1.14 (4) and the warning after Definition 12.1. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed pages 7, 86. the orientation-free form with I^j and the warning on separatedness. [ALB23](https://arxiv.org/abs/1907.10525v4), the paragraph before Theorem 3.4.4. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 25. restates the definition with a generator d of I.

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-3-transversal-prism"></a>

### Transversal prisms and the ideals I_r

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/transversal-prism` · definition. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.BKTwist` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/BKTwist/Transversal`.

A prism (A, I) is transversal if A/I is p-torsion-free; more generally a preprism (a δ-ring A with an ideal I that is an invertible A-module) is transversal under the same condition. For a transversal prism: (1) A is p-torsion-free and (A, I) is bounded; (A, I) is transversal if and only if A is p-torsion-free and I/pI → A/pA is injective, and then the image is an invertible ideal of A/pA. (2) For every r ≥ 0 the map (φ_A^r)^*(I) → A induced by I ⊂ A is injective with p-torsion-free cokernel; its image is the ideal φ_A^r(I)A, again written (φ_A^r)^*(I). Put I_r = I · φ_A^*(I) ⋯ (φ_A^{r−1})^*(I), an invertible ideal (I_0 = A, I_1 = I). (3) I_r and I^{(p^r−1)/(p−1)} have the same image in A/pA; A/I_r is p-torsion-free; A = lim_r A/I_r = lim_r A/φ_A^*(I_r). (4) For r > 0 the natural map (φ_A^r)^*(I)/I_{r+1} → A/I_r is injective with image the principal ideal (p); and I_r = ∩_{0 ≤ s < r} (φ_A^s)^*(I). (5) I_r/I_r² is p-torsion-free; the canonical map I_{r+1}/I_{r+1}² → I_r/I_r² is p times a unique surjection c_r, and c_r induces an isomorphism I_{r+1}/I_rI_{r+1} ≅ I_r/I_r² of invertible A/I_r-modules. (6) For a map of prisms (A, I) → (B, J), J_r = I_r B; a flat map of prisms out of a transversal prism has transversal target, and the converse holds for faithfully flat maps.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** p is a fixed prime; (A, I) is a prism in the sense of PR.0/prism. Bhatt–Lurie's Definition 2.1.3 (ρ : φ^*(I) → A/I surjective, A derived p- and I-complete) defines the same class of objects. For an oriented prism (A, (d)) transversality says that (d, p) is a regular sequence, the hypothesis of PR.0/transversal-prism-regular-sequences (Anschütz–Le Bras). Flat and faithfully flat maps of prisms are those for which A/I → B/J is p-completely (faithfully) flat. In the proof of BL22 Corollary 2.2.9 the last line reads 'x belongs to I_r' where 'I_{r+1}' is meant (source issue PrismaticCohomology/E31).

**Construction or proof.**

1. (1): I^m/I^{m+1} is an invertible A/I-module, hence p-torsion-free, so A/I^n is p-torsion-free for all n and A, being I-complete, is p-torsion-free (BL22 Remark 2.1.7); the criterion is Remark 2.1.8.
2. (2), (3): (φ^r)^*(I) is invertible, hence p-adically separated, and modulo p it maps isomorphically onto Ī^{p^r} ⊂ A/p (BL22 Lemma 2.2.1, Remark 2.2.3); A/I_{r+1} is an extension of A/I_r by I_r ⊗ A/(φ^r)^*(I) (Lemma 2.2.5); the limit statements reduce modulo p to Ī-adic completeness of A/p (Remarks 2.2.6, 2.2.7).
3. (4): (φ^r)^*(I) ⊂ (p) + I_r by (3); writing f = p f_0 one computes f_0(x) ≡ φ^{r−1}(δ(x)) modulo (φ^{r−1})^*(I) for x ∈ I, and the δ(x), x ∈ I, generate the unit ideal because (A, I) is a prism (BL22 Lemma 2.2.8). The intersection formula follows by induction (Corollary 2.2.9).
4. (5) follows from (3) and (4) (BL22 Corollary 2.2.10). (6): Remarks 2.2.4 and 2.4.4.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/prism`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-prism); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/prism-category`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-prism-category); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/transversal-prism-regular-sequences`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-transversal-prism-regular-sequences); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/bounded-prism-complete-flatness`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-bounded-prism-complete-flatness); [`mathlib:Ideal.map`](#mathlib-ideal-map).

**Consumers.** BL22 Construction 2.2.11: A{1} is the inverse limit of the modules I_r/I_r² along the maps c_r. BL22 Proposition 2.4.1 and Corollary 2.4.8: every prism is approximated by transversal prisms; this defines twists in general. BL22 §2.3 (prismatic logarithm) and PR.4/prismatic-logarithm: log_Δ(u) is the limit of the classes of u^{p^r} − 1 in I_r/I_r². Anschütz–Le Bras §2.1 and PR.0/transversal-prism-regular-sequences: regularity of (p, φ^r(d)) and (φ^r(d), φ^s(d)) in a transversal prism.

**Planning API.**

- `TauCeti.Prismatic.BKTwist.IsTransversal` (constructor): The predicate on a prism (A, I): A/I is p-torsion-free.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.BKTwist.frobeniusIdeal` (data): The ideal (φ_A^r)^*(I) = φ_A^r(I)A of A.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.BKTwist.Ir` (data): The ideal I_r = ∏_{0 ≤ s < r} (φ_A^s)^*(I).
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.BKTwist.Ir_zero` (simp): I_0 = A.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.BKTwist.Ir_one` (simp): I_1 = I.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.BKTwist.Ir_succ_le` (structure): I_{r+1} ⊂ I_r.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.BKTwist.IsTransversal.torsionFree` (other): For a transversal prism, A is p-torsion-free.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.BKTwist.IsTransversal.quotient_Ir_torsionFree` (other): For a transversal prism, A/I_r is p-torsion-free for all r.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.BKTwist.IsTransversal.frobeniusIdeal_le` (relation): For a transversal prism and r > 0: (φ_A^r)^*(I) ⊂ I_r + (p).
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.BKTwist.IsTransversal.Ir_eq_iInf` (characterisation): For a transversal prism: I_r = ∩_{0 ≤ s < r} (φ_A^s)^*(I).
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.BKTwist.IsTransversal.cotangent_transition` (relation): For a transversal prism the canonical map I_{r+1}/I_{r+1}² → I_r/I_r² has image in p · (I_r/I_r²).
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.BKTwist.Ir_map` (functoriality): For a map of prisms (A, I) → (B, J): J_r = I_r B.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.BKTwist.cotangentTransition` (data): For r≥1, c_r:I_(r+1)/I_(r+1)^2→I_r/I_r^2 is the unique A-linear map satisfying p·c_r = the map induced by ideal inclusion. It exists because that inclusion map has image in p(I_r/I_r^2), and is unique because I_r/I_r^2 is p-torsion-free. Thus c_r itself is the divided transition used to define A{1}.

**Unit tests.**

- `pr3_transversal_ir_zero_one` (degenerate): I_0 = A and I_1 = I for every prism.
- `pr3_transversal_q_de_rham_ir` (computation): If I = ([p]_q) with δ(q) = 0, then I_r = ([p^r]_q) where [p^r]_q = 1 + q + … + q^{p^r − 1}.
- `pr3_transversal_torsion_free` (characterisation): For a transversal prism, p x = 0 in A implies x = 0.
- `pr3_transversal_not_crystalline` (non-example): A crystalline prism (A, (p)) with A/p ≠ 0 is not transversal.

**Acceptance.** The q-de Rham prism (Z_p[[q−1]], ([p]_q)) is transversal, with I_r = ([p^r]_q). A nonzero crystalline prism (A, (p)) is not transversal: A/I = A/p is killed by p. The Breuil–Kisin prism (W(k)[[u]], (E(u))) is transversal: the quotient O_K is p-torsion-free. A perfect prism (A_inf(R), ker θ) is transversal exactly when R is p-torsion-free.

**Sources.** [BL22](https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.06120v1), Definitions 2.1.1 and 2.1.3, Remarks 2.1.7 and 2.1.8. [BL22](https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.06120v1), Lemmas 2.2.1, 2.2.5 and 2.2.8; Corollaries 2.2.9–2.2.10; §2.2. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed pages 21, 22, 23. The injectivity and regularity statements, successive quotient calculations, and the inclusion map on conormal modules prove parts (2)–(5).. [BL22](https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.06120v1), Remarks 2.2.4 and 2.4.4. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed pages 21, 27. part (6).

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-3-large-quasisyntomic-algebra"></a>

### Large quasisyntomic algebras over A/I

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/large-quasisyntomic-algebra` · definition. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.Nygaard` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/Nygaard/Large`.

Let (A, I) be a bounded prism and Ā = A/I. A quasisyntomic Ā-algebra is a derived p-complete Ā-algebra S that is p-completely flat over Ā and whose cotangent complex L_{S/Ā} has p-complete Tor amplitude in [−1, 0]; such an S is classically p-complete. A quasisyntomic Ā-algebra S is large if there is a surjection Ā⟨X_t^{1/p^∞} | t ∈ T⟩ → S for some set T; equivalently, S/pS is generated as an Ā-algebra by the images of elements of S that admit compatible systems of p-power roots in S. For a large quasisyntomic S: Ω^1_{S/Ā} vanishes after p-completion, so L_{S/Ā}[−1] is a p-completely flat S-module, and every (∧^i L_{S/Ā})[−i]^∧ is a p-completely flat S-module. Large quasisyntomic algebras form a basis of the quasisyntomic site of Ā: every quasisyntomic Ā-algebra has a quasisyntomic cover by a large one, and the terms of the Čech nerve of such a cover are large. The standard examples are Ā⟨X_1^{1/p^∞}, …, X_n^{1/p^∞}⟩/(f_1, …, f_m) with (f_1, …, f_m) p-completely regular relative to Ā.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** (A, I) is a bounded prism; Ā has bounded p^∞-torsion. Quasisyntomic algebras, covers and the site are those of DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.5 (BMS2 §4) over the base Ā. Ā⟨X_t^{1/p^∞}⟩ is the p-adic completion of the perfected polynomial ring Ā[X_t^{1/p^∞}]. The second formulation is the one of Bhatt–Lurie (S/pS generated by the images of Ā and of (S/pS)^♭); for p-complete S the two agree because compatible systems of p-power roots lift uniquely from S/pS to S.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Equivalence: a surjection from Ā⟨X_t^{1/p^∞}⟩ exhibits generators with compatible roots; conversely generators x_t of S/p with compatible roots in S define Ā⟨X_t^{1/p^∞}⟩ → S, surjective modulo p and hence surjective by p-completeness. The map S^♭ = lim_{x ↦ x^p} S → (S/p)^♭ is bijective for p-complete S.
2. Ω^1: if x = y^p then dx = p y^{p−1} dy, so Ω^1_{S/Ā}/p is generated by zero; with the Tor amplitude condition this gives p-complete flatness of L_{S/Ā}[−1] and of its divided and exterior powers (DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.0).
3. Basis: for quasisyntomic S choose generators and adjoin compatible p-power roots, S → S ⊗̂_{Ā⟨X_t⟩} Ā⟨X_t^{1/p^∞}⟩, a quasisyntomic cover with large target (BS22, the paragraph after Definition 15.1; BMS2 Lemma 4.28).

**Direct prerequisites.** `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.5`; `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.0`; [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/prism`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-prism).

**Consumers.** BS22 Theorem 15.2: the rings on which Δ_{S/A} is discrete and the relative Nygaard filtration is defined by Frobenius divisibility. BS22 Theorem 15.3 and BL22 Proposition 5.1.1: a basis of the quasisyntomic site on which sheaves are defined and from which they are right Kan extended. PR.5 (Bhatt–Lurie §5.5): the same class of rings supports the absolute Nygaard filtration by descent.

**Planning API.**

- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Nygaard.IsLarge` (constructor): The predicate on an Ā-algebra S: S/pS is generated over Ā by images of elements with compatible p-power roots in S.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Nygaard.HasCompatibleRoots` (data): x ∈ S admits a sequence x = x_0, x_1, x_2, … with x_{n+1}^p = x_n.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Nygaard.isLarge_iff_exists_family` (characterisation): S is large iff there is a family (x_t) of elements with compatible p-power roots such that every s ∈ S is congruent modulo p to an element of the Ā-subalgebra generated by the x_t.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Nygaard.IsLarge.of_surjective` (functoriality): If S is large and S → S′ is a surjective map of Ā-algebras then S′ is large.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Nygaard.IsLarge.kaehler_eq_smul` (other): For large S: Ω^1_{S/Ā} = p · Ω^1_{S/Ā}.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Nygaard.isLarge_bar` (example): Ā is a large Ā-algebra.

**Unit tests.**

- `pr3_large_base` (degenerate): Ā is large over itself.
- `pr3_large_generated_by_roots` (characterisation): If S is generated as an Ā-algebra by elements with compatible p-power roots, then S is large; this covers Ā[X^{1/p^∞}]/(X).
- `pr3_large_kaehler` (compatibility): For large S every Kähler differential of S over Ā is p times another one.
- `pr3_large_not_polynomial` (non-example): If p is not a unit of Ā, the polynomial ring Ā[X] is not large.

**Acceptance.** Ā itself is large (T empty). For a perfect prism, a quasiregular semiperfectoid Ā-algebra that is quasisyntomic over Ā is large; large algebras replace quasiregular semiperfectoid rings when the base prism is not perfect. Ā⟨X⟩ is not large: dX is not divisible by p in Ω^1.

**Sources.** [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Definition 15.1 and the paragraph after it. [BL22](https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.06120v1), proof of Proposition 5.1.1, first paragraph. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 115. the reformulation through (R/pR)^♭ and the discreteness of the prismatic complex on this class.

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-3-nygaard-key-case"></a>

### The key case: q-divided powers and the Nygaard filtration of Z_p^cycl⟨X^{1/p^∞}⟩/X

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/nygaard-key-case` · theorem. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.Nygaard` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/Nygaard/KeyCase`.

Let A be the (p, [p]_q)-adic completion of Z_p[q^{1/p^∞}] with δ(q^{1/p^n}) = 0, I = ([p]_q), [p]_q = 1 + q + … + q^{p−1}; (A, I) is the perfect prism of R = Z_p[ζ_{p^∞}]^∧, with q^{1/p^n} ↦ ζ_{p^{n+1}}. Let S = (Z_p[ζ_{p^∞}, X^{1/p^∞}]/X)^∧. Write [n]_q = (q^n − 1)/(q − 1), [n]_q! = ∏_{i=1}^n [i]_q. (a) Δ_S = A⟨Y^{1/p^∞}⟩{Y^p/[p]_q}^∧ (prismatic envelope), with δ(Y^{1/p^n}) = 0 and S → Δ̄_S sending X^{1/p^n} ↦ Y^{1/p^{n−1}}; Δ_S is flat over Z_p[[q−1]]. (b) (q-divided powers, BS22 Lemma 12.5) If D is a derived (p, [p]_q)-complete, (p, [p]_q)-completely flat Z_p[[q−1]]-algebra with a ring endomorphism φ, φ(q) = q^p, and x ∈ D satisfies φ(x) = x^p ∈ [p]_q D, then x^n ∈ [n]_q! D for all n ≥ 0. (c) (BS22 Lemma 12.6) In Z_p[[q−1]]: [mp]_q! = u · φ([m]_q!) · [p]_q^m with u a unit, for m ∈ N; and [⌊i⌋p]_q! = v · [⌊ip⌋]_q! with v a unit, for i ∈ N[1/p]. (d) (BS22 Lemma 12.4) Y^n/[n]_q! ∈ Δ_S for all n, and Δ_S is the (p, [p]_q)-adic completion of the free A-module ⊕_{i ∈ N[1/p]} A · Y^i/[⌊i⌋]_q!. On this basis φ(Y^i/[⌊i⌋]_q!) = u_i · [p]_q^{⌊i⌋} · Y^{ip}/[⌊ip⌋]_q! with u_i a unit. (e) (BS22 Lemma 12.7) Fil^n_N Δ_S is the completion of ⊕_i [p]_{q^{1/p}}^{max(n−⌊i⌋, 0)} · A · Y^i/[⌊i⌋]_q!. The image of φ/[p]_q^n : Fil^n_N Δ_S → Δ̄_S = (⊕_i R · Y^i/[⌊i⌋]_q!)^∧ is the span of the summands with i < p(n+1), and the conjugate filtration Fil_n Δ̄_S relative to R is the same span. In particular Theorem 12.2 holds for S, and Δ_S/Fil^1_N Δ_S = ⊕_{i<1} (A/[p]_{q^{1/p}}) · Y^i, which φ maps isomorphically onto the image ⊕_{j<p} R · Y^j of S in Δ̄_S (Y^i ↦ Y^{pi}, the image of X^i).

**Hypotheses and conventions.** p is a fixed prime; R, A, S, Y as in the statement; N[1/p] is the monoid of non-negative elements of Z[1/p]. The normalisation X^{1/p^n} ↦ Y^{1/p^{n−1}} is that of BS22 §12.2 (so X ↦ Y^p). In (e) the exponent of [p]_{q^{1/p}} is max(n − ⌊i⌋, 0): the factor is 1 as soon as i ≥ n. In the proof of BS22 Lemma 12.6 the display reads ∏[ip]_q! where ∏[ip]_q is meant (register id PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22/E21); the node states the corrected identity.

**Construction or proof.**

1. (a): Δ_S is the prismatic envelope of (I, Y^p) in A⟨Y^{1/p^∞}⟩ by PR.2/qrsp-prism and PR.0/regular-prismatic-envelopes (BS22 Proposition 3.13); it is (p, I)-completely flat over A, hence flat over the noetherian ring Z_p[[q−1]].
2. (c): [k]_q is a unit of Z_p[[q−1]] when p ∤ k, and ∏_{i=1}^m [ip]_q = ∏ (q^{ip}−1)/(q^p−1) · (q^p−1)/(q−1) = φ([m]_q!) [p]_q^m. (b): reduce to showing x^m ∈ [m]_q! D ⇒ x^{mp} ∈ [mp]_q! D; φ([m]_q!) is a nonzerodivisor modulo [p]_q in D by flatness, x^{mp} = φ(x^m) ∈ φ([m]_q!)D and x^{mp} = (x^p)^m ∈ [p]_q^m D.
3. (d): (b) gives Y^n/[n]_q! ∈ Δ_S; the map from the completed free module is an isomorphism because it is one after base change along A → A/(q−1), where the envelope becomes the p-completed divided power envelope of (Y) (PR.0/pd-envelope-as-delta-envelope, BS22 Corollary 2.39) with its standard basis (CrystallineCohomology:CR.0).
4. (e): φ is graded for the N[1/p]-grading, multiplying degrees by p, so Fil^n_N is graded; the formula of (d) for φ on basis elements and bijectivity of φ on A identify Fil^n_N degree by degree and give the image of φ/[p]_q^n. For the conjugate filtration: Fil_0 is the image of S (summands i < p), gr_1 is generated by Y^p/[p]_q (BS22 Example 7.9, PR.2/derived-hodge-tate-comparison), and multiplicativity with (c) gives Fil_n.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/nygaard-filtration-qrsp`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-3-nygaard-filtration-qrsp); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/qrsp-prism`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-qrsp-prism); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/derived-hodge-tate-comparison`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-derived-hodge-tate-comparison); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/regular-prismatic-envelopes`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-regular-prismatic-envelopes); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/pd-envelope-as-delta-envelope`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-pd-envelope-as-delta-envelope); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/q-de-rham-prism`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-q-de-rham-prism); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/perfect-prisms-perfectoid-rings`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-perfect-prisms-perfectoid-rings); `CrystallineCohomology:CR.0`; [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/bounded-prism-complete-flatness`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-bounded-prism-complete-flatness).

**Acceptance.** n = 0: Fil^0_N = Δ_S and the image of φ in Δ̄_S is the span of Y^i, i < p, which is the image of S. n = 1: for i < 2 the generator [p]_{q^{1/p}}^{1−⌊i⌋} Y^i/[⌊i⌋]_q! of Fil^1_N in degree i maps under φ/[p]_q to a unit multiple of Y^{ip}/[⌊ip⌋]_q!, and for i ≥ 2 to a multiple of [p]_q; the image in Δ̄_S is the span of the degrees j < 2p. Reduction modulo q − 1 recovers a divided power algebra: Δ_S/(q−1) is the p-completion of ⊕_{i ∈ N[1/p]} (A/(q−1)) · Y^i/⌊i⌋!, the p-completed divided power envelope of (Y) in A/(q−1)⟨Y^{1/p^∞}⟩ (A/(q−1) is the p-completion of Z_p[q^{1/p^∞}]/(q−1), not Z_p). Its base change along A → Z_p, q^{1/p^n} ↦ 1, is the p-completion of ⊕ Z_p · Y^i/⌊i⌋! (PR.3/nygaard-incomplete-example). Perfectoid quotient acceptance example of the stage: S is the quotient of the perfectoid ring R⟨X^{1/p^∞}⟩ by the regular element X.

**Sources.** [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Lemmas 12.4–12.7 and their proofs (§12.2). Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed pages 88, 89. parts (a)–(e) are Lemmas 12.4, 12.5, 12.6 and 12.7 with the corrections named in the hypotheses. [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Lemma 12.5. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 88. part (b), in the generality of the source; it is reused in the proof of Theorem 13.1.

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-3-transversal-approximation"></a>

### Approximation of prisms by transversal prisms

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/transversal-approximation` · theorem. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.BKTwist` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/BKTwist/Approximation`.

(1) (BL22 Proposition 2.1.10) For a transversal preprism (A, I) there is a preprism map f : (A, I) → (B, J) to a prism (B, J) such that every preprism map from (A, I) to a prism factors uniquely through f; (B, J) is transversal and Spec(B/(J + (p))) → Spec(A/(I + (p))) is an open immersion. (2) (Proposition 2.4.1) For every prism (A, I) there is a map of prisms (B, J) → (A, I) with (B, J) transversal. (3) (Proposition 2.4.5, Corollary 2.4.7, Proposition 2.4.9) If (A, I) is transversal and (B, J) is bounded, the coproduct (A, I) ⊔ (B, J) exists in the category of prisms and (B, J) → (A, I) ⊔ (B, J) is flat; it is faithfully flat when A ≠ 0; if (B, J) is also transversal then so is the coproduct. (4) (Corollary 2.4.8) For every prism (A, I), the category of transversal prisms (A_0, I_0) with a map of prisms to (A, I) is non-empty and has pairwise coproducts; hence it is sifted and its nerve is weakly contractible. (5) (Corollary 2.4.10) A bounded prism (A, I) is transversal if and only if for every bounded prism (B, J) the coproduct (A, I) ⊔ (B, J) exists and is flat over (B, J), if and only if this holds for one nonzero transversal (B, J).

**Hypotheses and conventions.** Prisms are those of PR.0/prism; (2) and (4) hold for every prism, bounded or not. In (3) the coproduct is the prismatic envelope of PR.0/regular-prismatic-envelopes applied to the (J, p)-completion of A ⊗_Z B and the image of a generator of I, after localising so that I is principal. The free p-complete δ-ring on a ring R is the p-completion of the free δ-ring (PR.0/free-delta-ring). In the proof of BL22 Lemma 2.4.2 the scheme of idempotent n × n matrices is a closed subscheme of the affine space of dimension n², printed as A^{2n} (source issue PrismaticCohomology/E32).

**Construction or proof.**

1. (1): lift ρ : φ^*(I) → A/I to ρ̃ : φ^*(I) → A, let Spec A′ ⊂ Spec A be the non-vanishing locus of ρ̃ and B the (I, p)-completion of A′; the Frobenius extends because φ is the identity on the underlying space of A/(I^k, p^k), the δ-structure exists because B is p-torsion-free, and the universal property is checked through Witt vectors of length two.
2. (2): write I as the base change of an invertible module J_0 over a smooth Z-algebra B_0 (BL22 Lemma 2.4.2), let B_1 = Sym_{B_0}(J_0), B_2 the free p-complete δ-ring on B_1, which is flat over B_1 (Lemma 2.4.3: a retraction argument through W_n and formal smoothness of B_1/p), so (B_2, J_1B_2) is a transversal preprism mapping to (A, I); apply (1).
3. (3): reduce to I = (d); d is (J, p)-completely regular relative to B in the completion of A ⊗_Z B because A/d is flat over Z; apply PR.0/regular-prismatic-envelopes (BS22 Proposition 3.13) and PR.0/rigidity-prism-ideal. Faithful flatness: lift a point of Spec(B/(p, J)) to a map of prisms to (W(k), (p)) and use the coproduct property.
4. (4) is (2) and (3); (5) follows from (3) and part (6) of PR.3/transversal-prism.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/transversal-prism`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-3-transversal-prism); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/free-delta-ring`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-free-delta-ring); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/regular-prismatic-envelopes`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-regular-prismatic-envelopes); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/rigidity-prism-ideal`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-rigidity-prism-ideal); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-witt-section-equivalence`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-delta-witt-section-equivalence); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/local-distinguished-prism-generators`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-local-distinguished-prism-generators); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/crystalline-prism`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-crystalline-prism).

**Acceptance.** For a crystalline prism (A, (p)): the map q ↦ 1 from the q-de Rham prism is a transversal approximation. For a perfect prism of a perfectoid ring with p-torsion (for example (Z_p, (p)), R = F_p) a transversal approximation exists although the prism is not transversal. The coproduct of the q-de Rham prism with itself is transversal; it is the prism on which the two generators e_A of PR.3/breuil-kisin-twist-examples are compared.

**Sources.** [BL22](https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.06120v1), Proposition 2.4.1 with Lemmas 2.4.2, 2.4.3 and Proposition 2.1.10. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed pages 20, 25. parts (1), (2). [BL22](https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.06120v1), Proposition 2.4.5, Corollaries 2.4.7, 2.4.8, Proposition 2.4.9, Corollary 2.4.10. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 27. parts (3)–(5).

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-3-breuil-kisin-twist-transversal"></a>

### Breuil–Kisin twist of a transversal prism

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/breuil-kisin-twist-transversal` · construction. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.BKTwist` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/BKTwist/Transversal`.

Let (A, I) be a transversal prism with the ideals I_r and the surjections c_r : I_{r+1}/I_{r+1}² → I_r/I_r² (the canonical map divided by p) of PR.3/transversal-prism. Define A{1} = lim (⋯ → I_3/I_3² → I_2/I_2² → I/I²), the inverse limit along the maps c_r, with projections π_r : A{1} → I_r/I_r². Then: (1) A{1} is an invertible A-module, and π_r induces an isomorphism A{1}/I_rA{1} ≅ I_r/I_r² for every r ≥ 0; in particular A{1}/IA{1} ≅ I/I². (2) For a map f of transversal prisms (A, I) → (B, J) there is a unique A-linear f{1} : A{1} → B{1} compatible with the maps I_r/I_r² → J_r/J_r², and it induces B ⊗_A A{1} ≅ B{1}. (3) The canonical isomorphisms φ_A^*(I_r) ≅ I^{−1} ⊗ I_{r+1} induce, modulo φ_A^*(I_r) and in the limit over r, an isomorphism φ_A^*(A{1}) ≅ I^{−1} ⊗_A A{1}, that is, a φ_A-semilinear Frobenius φ_{A{1}} : A{1} → I^{−1} ⊗_A A{1}. On compatible systems it sends (x_r mod I_r²)_r, x_r ∈ I_r, to the system of the classes of φ_A(x_r) ∈ φ_A^*(I_r) = I^{−1} I_{r+1}.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** (A, I) is a transversal prism; all the statements of PR.3/transversal-prism are available. The transition maps are the canonical maps divided by p; the canonical maps themselves are divisible by p and their inverse limit is not the twist. I^{−1} denotes the dual invertible module Hom_A(I, A); I^{−1} ⊗ M is written I^{−1}M.

**Construction or proof.**

1. A{1} is p-complete and p-torsion-free because each I_r/I_r² is; by the criterion for invertibility modulo p^n it suffices that A{1}/p is invertible over A/p, where it is the limit of the modules Ī^{m_r}/Ī^{2m_r}, m_r = (p^r − 1)/(p − 1), invertible over (A/p)/Ī^{m_r}, and A/p is Ī-adically complete (BL22 Proposition 2.2.12).
2. (2): uniqueness and existence of f{1} are formal from J_r = I_rB; the base change statement is checked modulo each J_r (BL22 Remark 2.2.13).
3. (3): φ_A^*(I_r) = φ^*(I) ⋯ (φ^r)^*(I) = I^{−1}I_{r+1}; reduce modulo φ_A^*(I_r) ⊃ I_{r+1}, use (1) for r and r + 1, and pass to the limit using A = lim A/φ_A^*(I_r) (BL22 Construction 2.2.14).

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/transversal-prism`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-3-transversal-prism); [`mathlib:Module.Invertible`](#mathlib-module-invertible); [`mathlib:Ideal.Cotangent`](#mathlib-ideal-cotangent); [`mathlib:Ideal.toCotangent`](#mathlib-ideal-tocotangent).

**Consumers.** BL22 Proposition 2.5.1: the twist of a general prism is the base change of the twist of a transversal approximation. BL22 Proposition 2.6.1: the generator e_A over the q-de Rham prism is given by its images [p^r]_q in I_r/I_r². BL22 Construction 2.3.2 and PR.4/prismatic-logarithm: the prismatic logarithm of a rank one unit u ∈ 1 + I is the system of classes of u^{p^r} − 1.

**Planning API.**

- `TauCeti.Prismatic.BKTwist.transversalProj` (projection): For a transversal prism, the A-linear projection π_r : A{1} → I_r/I_r².
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.BKTwist.transversalProj_surjective` (other): π_r is surjective.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.BKTwist.ker_transversalProj` (characterisation): The kernel of π_r is I_r · A{1}.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.BKTwist.transversalProj_transition` (relation): If y ∈ I_{r+1} represents π_{r+1}(x), then the class of y in I_r/I_r² is p · π_r(x).
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.BKTwist.transversal_ext` (extensionality): Two elements of A{1} with the same image under every π_r are equal.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.BKTwist.transversal_lift` (universal-property): A family x_r ∈ I_r/I_r² with (class of a representative of x_{r+1}) = p · x_r for all r comes from a unique element of A{1}.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.BKTwist.transversalFrobenius_projection` (characterisation): For r≥1, the identity φ_A^*I_r ≃ I^(-1)I_(r+1) induces, after reduction modulo φ_A^*I_r, an isomorphism φ_A^*(A{1})⊗A/(φ_A^*I_r) ≃ I^(-1)A{1}⊗A/(φ_A^*I_r). The Frobenius on A{1} is characterized by these projected maps for all r. Thus its projections are obtained from φ applied to π_r and the specified ideal identification, not by an arbitrary identification of invertible modules (BL Construction 2.2.14).
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.BKTwist.transversalTwist_projection` (compatibility): For r≥1, π_r:A{1}→I_r/I_r² identifies A{1}/I_r A{1} with I_r/I_r². The maps satisfy π_r=c_r∘π_(r+1), where c_r is the divided transition of cotangentTransition.

**Unit tests.**

- `pr3_bk_transversal_proj_one` (characterisation): π_1 induces A{1}/IA{1} ≅ I/I²: it is surjective with kernel I · A{1}.
- `pr3_bk_transversal_q_system` (computation): If I = ([p]_q) with δ(q) = 0 on a transversal prism, then [p^{r+1}]_q − p [p^r]_q ∈ I_r² for all r, so the classes of [p^r]_q are a compatible system.
- `pr3_bk_transversal_undivided` (non-example): The canonical maps I_{r+1}/I_{r+1}² → I_r/I_r² are not the transition maps: each has image in p · (I_r/I_r²).
- `pr3_bk_transversal_proj_zero` (degenerate): π_0 is the zero map to I_0/I_0² = 0.

**Acceptance.** For the q-de Rham prism the classes of [p^r]_q form a compatible system, since [p^{r+1}]_q ≡ p [p^r]_q modulo I_r², and define a generator (PR.3/breuil-kisin-twist-examples). Reduction: A{1} ⊗_A A/I ≅ I/I², the twist of BS22 used in the Hodge–Tate comparison. Frobenius has a simple pole along I: φ_{A{1}} takes values in I^{−1} ⊗ A{1}, not in A{1}.

**Prototype boundary.** `TauCeti.Prismatic.BKTwist.transversalFrobenius_projection` needs its supplier carrier: The projected identity requires the DD.1 completed semilinear tensor, reduction modulo φ*I_r, and their compatibility with the cotangent-line inverse system. The typed cotangent transition and projections above fix the system; a freely chosen invertible-module isomorphism cannot replace its Frobenius compatibility.

**Sources.** [BL22](https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.06120v1), Construction 2.2.11 and Proposition 2.2.12. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 23. the definition and part (1). [BL22](https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.06120v1), Remark 2.2.13 and Construction 2.2.14. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed pages 23, 24. parts (2) and (3).

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-3-nygaard-regular-semiperfectoid"></a>

### Good filtrations and the Nygaard filtration of regular semiperfectoid quotients

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/nygaard-regular-semiperfectoid` · theorem. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.Nygaard` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/Nygaard/Regular`.

Let R be a perfectoid ring with perfect prism (A, (d)). For a quasiregular semiperfectoid R-algebra S, a multiplicative filtration Fil^•_M of Δ_S by ideals (i ≥ 0) is good if Fil^0_M = Δ_S, φ(Fil^i_M) ⊂ d^i Δ_S for all i and φ/d^i induces an isomorphism of gr^i_M Δ_S onto Fil_i Δ̄_S ⊂ Δ̄_S (conjugate filtration relative to R). (1) A good filtration equals the Nygaard filtration. (2) If Δ_S carries a good filtration then Theorem 12.2 holds for S. (3) Let S → S′ be relatively perfect (the base change of a map of perfectoid R-algebras). If Fil^•_M is good on Δ_S then Fil^i_M Δ_S ⊗̂^L_{Δ_S} Δ_{S′} is concentrated in degree 0 and is a good filtration of Δ_{S′}; hence Fil^i_N Δ_{S′} = Fil^i_N Δ_S ⊗̂_{Δ_S} Δ_{S′}. (4) Let S → T be relatively perfect and p-completely faithfully flat. If Δ_T carries a good filtration then so does Δ_S. (5) Consequently Theorem 12.2 holds for S = R⟨X_1^{1/p^∞}, …, X_n^{1/p^∞}⟩/(f_1, …, f_m) with f_1, …, f_m a p-completely regular sequence relative to R, and the Nygaard filtration of S(m) = R⟨X_1^{1/p^∞}, …, X_m^{1/p^∞}⟩/(X_1, …, X_m) is the completed tensor product over A of the Nygaard filtrations of the factors R⟨X_j^{1/p^∞}⟩/(X_j).

**Hypotheses and conventions.** R is perfectoid, (A, (d)) its perfect prism, S, S′, T quasiregular semiperfectoid R-algebras. The regular sequence in (5) is p-completely regular relative to R (BS22 Definition 2.42 with I = (p)); this is the reading used when the same class of rings is quoted in the proof of BS22 Theorem 13.1. Completed tensor products are derived (p, d)-completed (DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1). In the proof of BS22 Proposition 12.8 'p-power roots in f_i' reads 'in R′' (register id PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22/E22).

**Construction or proof.**

1. (1): induction on i with the map of short exact sequences 0 → Fil^{i+1}_M → Fil^i_M → gr^i_M → 0 to 0 → d^{i+1}Δ_S → d^iΔ_S → d^iΔ_S/d^{i+1}Δ_S → 0 given by φ; the right vertical map is injective, so Fil^{i+1}_M = {x ∈ Fil^i_M : φ(x) ∈ d^{i+1}Δ_S}. (2) follows from (1).
2. (3): the conjugate filtration is compatible with base change along relatively perfect maps (PR.2/derived-hodge-tate-comparison), so gr^i_{M′} ≅ Fil_i Δ̄_{S′} is discrete, the quotients Δ_{S′}/Fil^i_{M′} are discrete and Fil^i_{M′} are ideals; the Frobenius of Δ_{S′} is the base change of that of Δ_S.
3. (4): on the Čech nerve T^• every term carries, by (3) and (1), its Nygaard filtration, which is a cartesian cosimplicial (p, d)-complete complex over Δ_{T^•}; (p, d)-completely faithfully flat descent along Δ_S → Δ_T (DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1, PR.2/quasisyntomic-descent) gives a filtration of Δ_S in the filtered derived category, which is by ideals (connective by faithful flatness, coconnective by the limit formula) and good.
4. (5): PR.3/nygaard-key-case gives S(1) over R_0 = Z_p[ζ_{p^∞}]^∧; for a perfectoid R_0-algebra R, S(1)_R = S(1)_{R_0} ⊗̂_{R_0} R is relatively perfect over it and (3) applies (the conjugate filtrations relative to R_0 and to R agree because the p-completed cotangent complex of R over R_0 vanishes); for a general perfectoid R choose R → R_∞ by André's lemma (PerfectoidQuotients:Q3), which contains compatible p-power roots of unity, and apply (4) to S(1)_R → S(1)_{R_∞}; the Künneth formula (PR.2/kunneth-formula) gives S(m), the tensor product filtration being good; a quotient R′/(f_1, …, f_r) with R′ perfectoid and f_i having compatible p-power roots receives a relatively perfect map from S(r), so (3) applies; André's lemma (PerfectoidQuotients:Q3, BS22 Theorem 7.14) gives a relatively perfect p-completely faithfully flat cover of the general S by such rings, so (4) applies.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/nygaard-filtration-qrsp`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-3-nygaard-filtration-qrsp); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/nygaard-key-case`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-3-nygaard-key-case); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/qrsp-prism`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-qrsp-prism); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/derived-hodge-tate-comparison`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-derived-hodge-tate-comparison); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/kunneth-formula`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-kunneth-formula); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/quasisyntomic-descent`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-quasisyntomic-descent); `PerfectoidQuotients:Q3`; `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`.

**Acceptance.** For S = R perfectoid the filtration (φ^{-1}(d))^i A is good: φ/d^i maps (e^i)/(e^{i+1}) isomorphically onto A/d = R = Fil_i Δ̄_R. For R → F_p (q ↦ 1) and S the key case, (3) gives the Nygaard filtration of F_p[X^{1/p^∞}]/X used in PR.3/nygaard-incomplete-example. S(2) = R⟨X_1^{1/p^∞}, X_2^{1/p^∞}⟩/(X_1, X_2) with R a perfectoid Z_p[ζ_{p^∞}]^∧-algebra: Fil^n_N is spanned by [p]_{q^{1/p}}^{max(n−⌊i_1⌋−⌊i_2⌋, 0)} Y_1^{i_1}Y_2^{i_2}/([⌊i_1⌋]_q![⌊i_2⌋]_q!), the formula used in the proof of BS22 Lemma 14.4.

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-3-breuil-kisin-twist"></a>

### Breuil–Kisin twists A{n} of a prism

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/breuil-kisin-twist` · construction. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.BKTwist` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/BKTwist/Basic`.

Let (A, I) be a prism and C the category of transversal prisms (A_0, I_0) with a map of prisms to (A, I) (PR.3/transversal-approximation (4)). The diagram C → Mod_A, (A_0, I_0) ↦ A ⊗_{A_0} A_0{1} (PR.3/breuil-kisin-twist-transversal) has invertible transition maps and a colimit A{1}, the Breuil–Kisin twist of A; for every object of C the map A ⊗_{A_0} A_0{1} → A{1} is an isomorphism. (1) A{1} is an invertible A-module. For n ∈ Z put A{n} = A{1}^{⊗ n} (negative powers are duals) and, for an A-module or an object M of D(A), M{n} = M ⊗_A A{n}. (2) Functoriality: a map of prisms (A, I) → (B, J) induces an isomorphism B ⊗_A A{1} ≅ B{1}, compatibly with composition and identities. Hence for a faithfully flat map of bounded prisms (A, I) → (B, IB), A{1} is the equaliser of B{1} ⇉ (B ⊗̂_A B){1}: when I is not principal the twist is obtained by descent from a cover on which I is oriented. (3) There is a canonical isomorphism β : A{1}/IA{1} ≅ I/I² of invertible A/I-modules, functorial in the prism and equal to that of PR.3/breuil-kisin-twist-transversal (1) for transversal prisms. Consequently, for an A/I-module N, N{n} ≅ N ⊗_{A/I} (I/I²)^{⊗ n}, the twist of Bhatt–Scholze. (4) A{1} is a free A-module if and only if I is principal. (5) Frobenius: there is a canonical φ_A-semilinear map φ_{A{1}} : A{1} → I^{−1} ⊗_A A{1} inducing an A-linear isomorphism φ_A^*(A{1}) ≅ I^{−1} ⊗_A A{1}, functorial in the prism and equal to that of PR.3/breuil-kisin-twist-transversal (3) for transversal prisms; its tensor powers are φ_{A{n}} : A{n} → I^{−n} ⊗_A A{n}, n ∈ Z.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** (A, I) is any prism; boundedness is needed only for the descent statement in (2). For a transversal prism the definition returns the inverse limit of PR.3/breuil-kisin-twist-transversal, because the identity is then an object of C. A{1} has no canonical generator even when I is principal; a generator is extra structure (PR.3/breuil-kisin-twist-examples). The prismatic logarithm log_Δ : (1 + I)_{rk=1} → A{1} of Bhatt–Lurie §§2.3, 2.5, 2.7 is not part of this node; no target of the stage uses it.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Existence: C has weakly contractible nerve (PR.3/transversal-approximation (4)) and the diagram has invertible transition maps by part (2) of PR.3/breuil-kisin-twist-transversal, so the colimit exists and every structure map is an isomorphism (BL22 Proposition 2.5.1).
2. (1): invertibility is inherited from the transversal case. (2): for (A, I) → (B, J), a transversal approximation of (A, I) is one of (B, J); compatibility with composition is formal. The descent statement follows because A → B ⇉ B ⊗̂_A B is an equaliser (PR.1/prismatic-structure-sheaf) and A{1} is flat over A.
3. (3), (5): the isomorphisms and maps of the transversal case are compatible with maps of transversal prisms, hence descend along the colimit; uniqueness is forced by functoriality (BL22 Remarks 2.5.7, 2.5.9).
4. (4): by (3) and I-completeness of A, both conditions are equivalent to triviality of the invertible A/I-module I/I² (BL22 Remark 2.5.8).

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/transversal-approximation`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-3-transversal-approximation); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/breuil-kisin-twist-transversal`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-3-breuil-kisin-twist-transversal); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/prism-category`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-prism-category); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/prismatic-structure-sheaf`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-prismatic-structure-sheaf); [`mathlib:Module.Invertible`](#mathlib-module-invertible); [`mathlib:ModuleCat.extendScalars`](#mathlib-modulecat-extendscalars); [`mathlib:Ideal.Cotangent`](#mathlib-ideal-cotangent); [`mathlib:Module.Dual`](#mathlib-module-dual).

**Consumers.** BS22 Theorem 12.2 and PR.3/divided-frobenius: the target Δ̄_S{i} of the divided Frobenius and its lift Δ_S{i}. BMS2 §7.4, BS22 §14, PR.4: Z_p(n)(S) = fib(φ_n − 1 : Fil^n_N Δ̂_S{n} → Δ̂_S{n}). Bhatt–Lurie §§3–5, PR.5: the twists Δ_R{n} of absolute prismatic cohomology and the invertible sheaf O{1} on the Cartier–Witt stack. Bhatt–Lurie Remark 2.5.6 and Variant 9.1.6: A{−1} ≅ H²_Δ(P^1_A / A).

**Planning API.**

- `TauCeti.Prismatic.BKTwist.twist` (constructor): The A-module A{1} of a prism (A, I).
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.BKTwist.twist_invertible` (instance): A{1} is an invertible A-module.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.BKTwist.twistPow` (constructor): The A-module A{n} = A{1}^{⊗ n} for n ∈ Z.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.BKTwist.twistModule` (constructor): For an A-module M and n ∈ Z, the A-module M{n} = A{n} ⊗_A M.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.BKTwist.twistBaseChange` (functoriality): For a map of prisms f : (A, I) → (B, J), the isomorphism B ⊗_A A{1} ≅ B{1}.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.BKTwist.twistReduction` (compatibility): The isomorphism β : A{1}/IA{1} ≅ I/I².
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.BKTwist.twist_free_iff` (characterisation): A{1} is isomorphic to A if and only if I is principal.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.BKTwist.twistFrobenius` (data): The A-linear isomorphism φ_A^*(A{1}) ≅ I^{−1} ⊗_A A{1}.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.BKTwist.twistFrobeniusMap` (data): The additive φ_A-semilinear map φ_{A{1}} : A{1} → I^{−1} ⊗_A A{1}.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.BKTwist.twistFrobeniusMap_smul` (relation): φ_{A{1}}(a x) = φ_A(a) φ_{A{1}}(x).
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.BKTwist.twistModule_of_bar` (compatibility): If I M = 0 then M ⊗_A A{1} ≅ M ⊗_A I/I².
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.BKTwist.twistPowFrobeniusMap` (data): For every integer n, φ_{A{n}}:A{n}→I^(−n)⊗_A A{n} is φ_A-semilinear. Positive powers use tensor products, negative powers use the inverse dual of the linearized map; n=0 gives φ_A. It is compatible with tensor addition and with base change along prism maps.

**Unit tests.**

- `pr3_bk_twist_pow_zero` (degenerate): A{0} ≅ A.
- `pr3_bk_twist_module_add` (compatibility): (M{m}){n} ≅ M{m+n} for all m, n ∈ Z.
- `pr3_bk_twist_free_of_principal` (characterisation): If I = (d) then A{1} is free of rank one.
- `pr3_bk_twist_q_generator` (computation): If δ(q) = 0 and I = ([p]_q), then A{1} has a generator e with [p]_q · φ_{A{1}}(e) = e in I^{−1} ⊗ A{1}, where e is viewed in I^{−1} ⊗ A{1} through I ⊂ A.
- `pr3_bk_twist_no_fixed_generator` (non-example): For a crystalline prism (A, (p)) with A ≠ 0 no generator e of A{1} satisfies φ_{A{1}}(e) = e: the twist is not the unit Frobenius module.

**Acceptance.** A{0} = A and (M{m}){n} ≅ M{m+n}. For A/I-modules the twist agrees with M ⊗ (I/I²)^{⊗ n} of BS22 Theorem 1.8 (2): H^i(Δ̄_{R/A}){i} in the Hodge–Tate comparison is unchanged. Over the q-de Rham prism A{1} = A · e_A with φ(e_A) = e_A/[p]_q; over a crystalline prism φ(e_A) = e_A/p (PR.3/breuil-kisin-twist-examples). Consumers: PR.4 (Z_p(n) uses Δ̂{n}), PR.5 (absolute prismatic cohomology with twists, the line bundle O_WCart{1}).

**Sources.** [BL22](https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.06120v1), Proposition 2.5.1, Definition 2.5.2, Notation 2.5.4. <a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-3-nygaard-filtration"></a>

### Nygaard filtration on prismatic cohomology over a perfectoid base

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/nygaard-filtration` · construction. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.Nygaard` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/Nygaard/Descent`.

Let R be a perfectoid ring with perfect prism (A, I), I = (d). (a) For a p-completely smooth R-algebra B choose a surjection R⟨X_1, …, X_n⟩ → B and put B̃ = R⟨X_1^{1/p^∞}, …, X_n^{1/p^∞}⟩ ⊗̂_{R⟨X_1,…,X_n⟩} B, with Čech nerve B̃^• of B → B̃; all B̃^k are semiperfectoid and Zariski locally of the form of PR.3/nygaard-regular-semiperfectoid (5), and Δ_{B/A} ≅ Tot(Δ_{B̃^•}). Define Fil^i_N Δ_{B/A} = Tot(Fil^i_N Δ_{B̃^•}) → Δ_{B/A}. It is independent of the surjection and functorial in B, a decreasing N-indexed multiplicative filtration of Δ_{B/A} in D(A) with gr^i_N Δ_{B/A} ≅ τ^{≤ i} Δ̄_{B/A}{i}, the isomorphism induced by φ/d^i (it is φ_A-semilinear). (b) For a derived p-complete simplicial R-algebra S define Fil^i_N Δ_{S/A} → Δ_{S/A} as the derived (p, I)-completed left Kan extension of B ↦ Fil^i_N Δ_{B/A} from p-completed polynomial R-algebras. Then Fil^0_N = Δ_{S/A}, the filtration is multiplicative and functorial, and φ/d^i induces a φ_A-semilinear isomorphism gr^i_N Δ_{S/A} ≅ Fil_i^conj Δ̄_{S/A}{i} (conjugate filtration relative to R), that is, an A-linear isomorphism gr^i_N Δ_{S/A} ≅ (φ_A)_* Fil_i^conj Δ̄_{S/A}{i}. (c) Each functor S ↦ Fil^i_N Δ_{S/A} on quasisyntomic R-algebras is a sheaf for the quasisyntomic topology with values in D(A).

**Hypotheses and conventions.** R is perfectoid and (A, I) is its perfect prism; B is p-completely smooth over R; S is a derived p-complete simplicial R-algebra. Filtered objects are objects of the filtered derived category DF(A) of functors (Z, ≥) → D(A) (DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1); the filtration is N-indexed in the sense that Fil^i = Fil^0 for i ≤ 0. BS22 Proposition 12.10 prints gr^i_N Δ_{B/A} ≅ τ^{≤i} Δ_{B/A}; the correct target is τ^{≤i} Δ̄_{B/A}{i} (register id PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22/E23), which is what the node states. The identification of this filtration, on quasiregular semiperfectoid S, with the ideals of PR.3/nygaard-filtration-qrsp is part of PR.3/nygaard-graded-pieces (BS22 Proposition 12.11).

**Construction or proof.**

1. (a): each B̃^k satisfies Theorem 12.2 by PR.3/nygaard-regular-semiperfectoid and Zariski localisation; Δ_{B̃^•} computes Δ_{B/A} by the Hodge–Tate comparison and quasisyntomic descent (PR.2/quasisyntomic-descent). Totalising gr^i_N Δ_{B̃^•} ≅ Fil_i Δ̄_{B̃^•}{i} gives τ^{≤i}Δ̄_{B/A}{i}, because the conjugate filtration of the smooth algebra B is the canonical filtration (PR.1/hodge-tate-comparison) and Fil_i^conj is a quasisyntomic sheaf.
2. Independence of the surjection: adding variables gives a comparison map of the two filtrations which is an isomorphism on every gr^i, hence on every Fil^i by induction on i using Δ/Fil^i (BS22, the paragraph after Proposition 12.10).
3. (b): left Kan extension (EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E3) commutes with cofibres, so gr^i of the extension is the left Kan extension of B ↦ τ^{≤i}Δ̄_{B/A}{i}, which is Fil_i^conj Δ̄_{S/A}{i} by the construction of the conjugate filtration (PR.2/derived-hodge-tate-comparison).
4. (c): Δ_{−/A} is a quasisyntomic sheaf (PR.2/quasisyntomic-descent); Δ_{S/A}/Fil^i_N has a finite filtration with graded pieces Fil_j^conj Δ̄{j}, j < i, which are sheaves by flat descent for the exterior powers of the cotangent complex (DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.5).

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/nygaard-regular-semiperfectoid`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-3-nygaard-regular-semiperfectoid); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/quasisyntomic-descent`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-quasisyntomic-descent); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/derived-prismatic-cohomology`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-derived-prismatic-cohomology); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/derived-hodge-tate-comparison`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-derived-hodge-tate-comparison); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/hodge-tate-comparison`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-hodge-tate-comparison); `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E3`; `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.5`; `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`.

**Consumers.** BS22 Proposition 12.11: the derived filtration is compared with the ideals Fil^i_N Δ_S to finish Theorem 12.2. BS22 Theorem 13.1: BMS2 endows its non-completed Δ^nc_{S/A} with a Nygaard filtration by the same procedure; the two are compared. PR.4 (syntomic complexes over a perfectoid base): Z_p(n) is built from Fil^n_N of the Nygaard completion on quasisyntomic R-algebras. PR.5 (Bhatt–Lurie Theorem 5.6.2): for a perfect prism the absolute Nygaard filtration agrees with this one.

**Planning API.**

- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Nygaard.filDerived` (constructor): For a perfect prism (A, I) and a derived p-complete simplicial A/I-algebra S, the filtered object i ↦ Fil^i_N Δ_{S/A} of DF(A).
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Nygaard.filDerivedZeroIso` (simp): Fil^0_N Δ_{S/A} ≅ Δ_{S/A}.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Nygaard.grDerived` (data): The graded piece gr^i_N Δ_{S/A} = cofibre of Fil^{i+1}_N → Fil^i_N.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Nygaard.grDerivedIsoConj` (characterisation): gr^i_N Δ_{S/A} ≅ (φ_A)_* Fil_i^conj Δ̄_{S/A}{i} in D(A), induced by φ/d^i (a φ_A-semilinear isomorphism onto Fil_i^conj Δ̄_{S/A}{i}).
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Nygaard.grDerived_smooth` (characterisation): For B p-completely smooth over A/I: gr^i_N Δ_{B/A} ≅ (φ_A)_* τ^{≤i} Δ̄_{B/A}{i}; in particular H^n(gr^i_N Δ_{B/A}) = 0 for n > i.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Nygaard.filDerivedMap` (functoriality): A map S → S′ induces a map of filtered objects Fil^•_N Δ_{S/A} → Fil^•_N Δ_{S′/A}, compatibly with composition.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Nygaard.filDerived_isSheaf` (other): S ↦ Fil^i_N Δ_{S/A} satisfies quasisyntomic descent on quasisyntomic A/I-algebras.

**Unit tests.**

- `pr3_nygaard_derived_fil_zero` (degenerate): Fil^0_N Δ_{S/A} ≅ Δ_{S/A} for every S.
- `pr3_nygaard_derived_gr_zero` (characterisation): gr^0_N Δ_{S/A} ≅ (φ_A)_* S (derived p-completion of S, with A acting through φ_A), for every S; for S = A/I it is concentrated in degree 0.
- `pr3_nygaard_derived_base` (computation): For S = A/I perfectoid: gr^i_N Δ_{S/A} ≅ (φ_A)_*(I^i/I^{i+1}) in degree 0 for all i ≥ 0; concretely it is (e^i)/(e^{i+1}) with e = φ_A^{-1}(d).
- `pr3_nygaard_derived_not_truncation` (non-example): For R = A/I ≠ 0, gr^0_N Δ_{R/A} is not isomorphic to τ^{≤0} Δ_{R/A} = A: the graded pieces are truncations of Hodge–Tate cohomology, not of prismatic cohomology.

**Acceptance.** For B = R: Fil^i_N Δ_{R/A} = (φ^{-1}(d))^i A and gr^i is identified with R{i} by φ/d^i, concentrated in degree 0. For B = R⟨T^{±1}⟩ and i ≥ 1: gr^i_N has cohomology B{i} in degree 0 and Ω^1_{B/R}{i−1} in degree 1. For S quasiregular semiperfectoid the filtration is the one of PR.3/nygaard-filtration-qrsp (PR.3/nygaard-graded-pieces). Comparison with the relative filtration: for the perfect prism (A, I), φ_A^* Fil^•_N Δ_{S/A} = Fil^•_N φ_A^*Δ_{S/A} (PR.3/relative-nygaard-filtration).

**Prototype boundary.** `TauCeti.Prismatic.Nygaard.filDerived_isSheaf` needs its supplier carrier: DD.5 supplies the quasisyntomic site and its hyperdescent carrier; the ordinary decreasing filtration above does not contain this site.

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-3-breuil-kisin-twist-examples"></a>

### Breuil–Kisin twists over the q-de Rham prism and over crystalline prisms

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/breuil-kisin-twist-examples` · application. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.BKTwist` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/BKTwist/Examples`.

(1) Let (A, I) = (Z_p[[q−1]], ([p]_q)) be the q-de Rham prism. It is transversal with I_r = ([p^r]_q), [p^r]_q = (q^{p^r} − 1)/(q − 1), and [p^{r+1}]_q = [p]_{q^{p^r}} [p^r]_q ≡ p [p^r]_q modulo I_r². There is a unique e_A ∈ A{1} whose image in I_r/I_r² is the class of [p^r]_q for every r; A{1} is the free A-module on e_A, and φ_{A{1}}(e_A) = [p]_q^{−1} e_A. (2) For a map of prisms f : (Z_p[[q−1]], ([p]_q)) → (B, J), the image e_B of e_A generates B{1} and φ_{B{1}}(λ e_B) = φ_B(λ) f([p]_q)^{−1} e_B; e_B depends on f and not only on (B, J). (3) For a crystalline prism (B, (p)) the map q ↦ 1 gives a canonical generator e_B of B{1} with φ_{B{1}}(e_B) = e_B/p; hence (B{n}, φ_{B{n}}) ≅ (B, p^{−n} φ_B) for all n ∈ Z, and the twisted divided Frobenius of PR.3/divided-frobenius is φ/p^i. (4) For an oriented prism (B, (d)) and a generator e of B{1}, φ_{B{1}}(e) = u d^{−1} e for a unit u; replacing e by v e replaces u by φ(v) v^{−1} u.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** The q-de Rham prism is PR.0/q-de-rham-prism: φ(q) = q^p, δ(q) = 0. Bhatt–Lurie characterise e_A by (q − 1) e_A = log_Δ(q^p); the node uses the equivalent description by the classes of [p^r]_q, which is the one their proof establishes, so that no logarithm is needed. BL22 Remark 2.6.2 and Notation 2.6.3 write the target of the Frobenius as I^{−1}{1}; by Notation 2.5.4 this is A{1} ⊗_A I^{−1}, the module written I^{−1}A{1} in Remark 2.5.9.

**Construction or proof.**

1. (1): I_r is generated by φ^s([p]_q) = [p]_{q^{p^s}}, s < r, whose product is [p^r]_q; q^{p^r} ≡ 1 modulo I_r gives [p]_{q^{p^r}} ≡ p modulo I_r, hence the congruence modulo I_r². The compatible system defines e_A by PR.3/breuil-kisin-twist-transversal, and it generates because its image generates each I_r/I_r².
2. Frobenius: φ_A([p^r]_q) = [p^r]_{q^p} = [p^{r+1}]_q/[p]_q, which under φ_A^*(I_r) = I^{−1}I_{r+1} is [p]_q^{−1} times the class of [p^{r+1}]_q (BL22 Remark 2.6.2 obtains the same formula from φ(log_Δ) = log_Δ).
3. (2), (3): functoriality of the twist and of its Frobenius (PR.3/breuil-kisin-twist (2), (5)); for a crystalline prism q ↦ 1 is a map of prisms with [p]_q ↦ p (BL22 Example 2.6.4).
4. (4): B{1} is free by PR.3/breuil-kisin-twist (4) and φ_B^*(B{1}) ≅ d^{−1} B{1}.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/breuil-kisin-twist`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-3-breuil-kisin-twist); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/breuil-kisin-twist-transversal`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-3-breuil-kisin-twist-transversal); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/transversal-prism`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-3-transversal-prism); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/q-de-rham-prism`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-q-de-rham-prism); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/crystalline-prism`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-crystalline-prism).

**Acceptance.** Crystalline prism acceptance example of the stage: for (Z_p, (p)), Z_p{n} = Z_p · e^n with φ(e^n) = p^{−n} e^n. Under reduction modulo I the generator e_A maps to the class of [p]_q in I/I². The two generators of the twist of the coproduct of the q-de Rham prism with itself differ by a unit that is not 1, which is why e_B depends on f.

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-3-nygaard-graded-pieces"></a>

### Graded pieces of the Nygaard filtration (BS22 Theorem 12.2)

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/nygaard-graded-pieces` · theorem. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.Nygaard` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/Nygaard/Graded`.

Let S be a quasiregular semiperfectoid ring, R a perfectoid ring mapping to S with perfect prism (A, (d)), and Fil_i Δ̄_S ⊂ Δ̄_S the conjugate filtration relative to R (increasing, exhaustive, multiplicative, gr_i Δ̄_S ≅ (∧^i L_{S/R}[−i])^∧{−i}). For every i ≥ 0: (1) the image of Fil^i_N Δ_S → Δ̄_S, x ↦ (φ(x)/d^i mod d), is Fil_i Δ̄_S, and its kernel is Fil^{i+1}_N Δ_S; (2) hence x ↦ φ(x) mod I^{i+1}Δ_S induces a natural isomorphism gr^i_N Δ_S ≅ Fil_i Δ̄_S{i}, where Δ̄_S{i} = I^iΔ_S/I^{i+1}Δ_S; it is φ-semilinear (Δ_S acts on the target through φ), and the left side does not depend on R; (3) in particular Δ_S / Fil^1_N Δ_S ≅ S, the isomorphism being induced by φ : Δ_S → Δ̄_S, whose image is S = Fil_0 Δ̄_S; (4) (BS22 Proposition 12.11) the derived Nygaard filtration Fil^i_N Δ_{S/A} of PR.3/nygaard-filtration (b) is concentrated in degree 0 and equals the ideal Fil^i_N Δ_S ⊂ Δ_S of PR.3/nygaard-filtration-qrsp; consequently on quasisyntomic R-algebras the filtration of PR.3/nygaard-filtration is the quasisyntomic unfolding of S′ ↦ Fil^•_N Δ_{S′} from quasiregular semiperfectoid S′, and it does not depend on R. Each gr^i_N Δ_S is a derived p-complete, p-completely flat S-module.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** S is quasiregular semiperfectoid; R → S is any map from a perfectoid ring; d is the image of a generator of ker θ. The conjugate filtration depends on R in general (BS22 Example 12.3, S = O_{C_p} ⊗̂_{Z_p} O_{C_p}); the Nygaard filtration and its graded pieces do not. BS22 §12.5 prints that the derived filtration of a quasiregular semiperfectoid ring is concentrated in degrees 0 and −1; the correct degrees are 0 and 1 (register id PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22/E24). The argument below uses the corrected range. The twist {i} is ⊗_{A/I} (I/I²)^{⊗ i}; it is trivialised by d^i, which is how the printed statement, with φ/d^i, reads.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Induction on i on the statement Fil^i_{N′} = Fil^i_N, where N′ is the derived filtration of PR.3/nygaard-filtration (b); i = 0 is clear. Since gr^j_{N′} ≅ Fil_j Δ̄_S{j} is discrete for all j, each Fil^i_{N′} has cohomology only in degrees 0 and 1.
2. Assume Fil^i_{N′} = Fil^i_N. The image of φ/d^i : Fil^i_N Δ_S → Δ̄_S is contained in Fil_i Δ̄_S because the map factors through gr^i_{N′}. It contains Fil_i Δ̄_S: choose a surjection S′ = R⟨X_a^{1/p^∞}, Y_b^{1/p^∞}⟩/(Y_b) → S that is surjective on cotangent complexes (DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.0), so Fil_i Δ̄_{S′} → Fil_i Δ̄_S is surjective, and use PR.3/nygaard-regular-semiperfectoid for S′ (and filtered colimits for infinitely many variables).
3. Therefore Fil^i_{N′} → gr^i_{N′} is surjective, its fibre Fil^{i+1}_{N′} is concentrated in degree 0 and equals the kernel of φ/d^i on Fil^i_N, which is Fil^{i+1}_N by definition. This proves (1), (2), (4).
4. (3) is the case i = 0: Fil_0 Δ̄_S = gr_0 = S. Flatness: Fil_i Δ̄_S is a finite extension of the modules (∧^j L_{S/R}[−j])^∧, which are p-completely flat over S (PR.2/qrsp-prism).

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/nygaard-filtration-qrsp`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-3-nygaard-filtration-qrsp); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/nygaard-regular-semiperfectoid`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-3-nygaard-regular-semiperfectoid); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/nygaard-filtration`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-3-nygaard-filtration); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/qrsp-prism`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-qrsp-prism); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/derived-hodge-tate-comparison`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-derived-hodge-tate-comparison); `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.0`; `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.5`.

**Acceptance.** S perfectoid with A = A_inf(S): gr^i_N = (e^i)/(e^{i+1}) ≅ S and A_inf(S)/Fil^1_N ≅ S via θ ∘ φ. Key case: the summands with i < p(n+1) (PR.3/nygaard-key-case (e)). Anschütz–Le Bras Theorem 3.4.4 is this statement; they use Δ_R/N^{≥1}Δ_R ≅ R to present the structure sheaf of the quasisyntomic site as a quotient of the prismatic sheaf.

**Sources.** [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Theorem 12.2, with Proposition 12.11 and its proof. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed pages 86, 92. parts (1), (2); part (4) is Proposition 12.11, whose proof completes the theorem. [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Proposition 12.11. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 92. the induction that identifies the derived and the naive filtrations. [ALB23](https://arxiv.org/abs/1907.10525v4), Theorem 3.4.4 (published: Theorem 3.29). <a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-3-divided-frobenius"></a>

### Divided Frobenius

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/divided-frobenius` · construction. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.Nygaard` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/Nygaard/DividedFrobenius`.

(a) Let (B, J) be a prism with J = (d). For i ≥ 0 the divided Frobenius φ_i = φ/d^i : Fil^i_N B → B is the unique map with d^i φ_i(x) = φ(x) (d is a nonzerodivisor). It is additive and φ-semilinear, φ_0 = φ, φ_{i+j}(xy) = φ_i(x)φ_j(y) for x ∈ Fil^i_N, y ∈ Fil^j_N, φ_i(x) = d · φ_{i+1}(x) for x ∈ Fil^{i+1}_N, and φ_i(x) ∈ dB if and only if x ∈ Fil^{i+1}_N. Replacing d by ud (u a unit) replaces φ_i by u^{−i}φ_i. (b) Without an orientation the invariant object is the filtered Frobenius Fil^i(φ) : Fil^i_N B → J^i, x ↦ φ(x). With the Breuil–Kisin twists of PR.3/breuil-kisin-twist it becomes the twisted divided Frobenius φ_i : Fil^i_N B ⊗_B B{i} → B{i}, x ⊗ e ↦ φ(x) · φ_{B{i}}(e), where φ_{B{i}} : B{i} → J^{−i} ⊗ B{i}; it is φ-semilinear and independent of all choices. For J = (d) and a generator e of B{1} with φ_{B{1}}(e) = d^{−1}e it is φ/d^i ⊗ 1. (c) For S quasiregular semiperfectoid these are the maps φ_i : Fil^i_N Δ_S → Δ_S and φ_i : Fil^i_N Δ_S{i} → Δ_S{i}, and φ_i induces the isomorphism gr^i_N Δ_S ≅ Fil_i Δ̄_S{i} of PR.3/nygaard-graded-pieces. (d) Over a perfectoid ring R with perfect prism (A, (d)), the maps φ/d^i on the terms of the Čech nerve of PR.3/nygaard-filtration (a) totalise to a natural φ_A-semilinear map φ_i : Fil^i_N Δ_{B/A} → Δ_{B/A} for B p-completely smooth over R, projecting to the isomorphism gr^i_N Δ_{B/A} ≅ τ^{≤i}Δ̄_{B/A}{i}; left Kan extension gives φ_i : Fil^i_N Δ_{S/A} → Δ_{S/A} for all derived p-complete simplicial R-algebras S, with φ_i ∘ (Fil^{i+1} → Fil^i) = d · φ_{i+1}.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** (B, J) is a prism; in (a) J is principal with chosen generator d. The twist B{i} is the i-th tensor power of the Breuil–Kisin twist B{1} (PR.3/breuil-kisin-twist); Fil^i_N B{i} means Fil^i_N B ⊗_B B{i}, a submodule of B{i} because B{i} is invertible. Semilinearity is over the Frobenius of B (and of A in (d)). BS22 Proposition 12.10 is quoted with the corrected target τ^{≤i}Δ̄_{B/A}{i} (register id PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22/E23).

**Construction or proof.**

1. (a): J = (d) is invertible, so d is a nonzerodivisor and x ∈ Fil^i_N means φ(x) ∈ d^iB; φ_i(x) is the unique quotient. The identities follow by cancelling powers of d; φ_i(x) ∈ dB ⇔ φ(x) ∈ d^{i+1}B ⇔ x ∈ Fil^{i+1}_N.
2. (b): φ_{B{i}} is the i-th tensor power of the Frobenius of B{1} (PR.3/breuil-kisin-twist, BL22 Remark 2.5.9); φ(x) ∈ J^i and φ_{B{i}}(e) ∈ J^{−i} ⊗ B{i} multiply to an element of B{i}.
3. (c): apply (a), (b) to (Δ_S, IΔ_S); the statement on graded pieces is PR.3/nygaard-graded-pieces (1).
4. (d): BS22 Proposition 12.10: totalise φ/d^i over the cosimplicial δ-ring Δ_{B̃^•}; the relation with d · φ_{i+1} holds termwise. Left Kan extension as in PR.3/nygaard-filtration (b).

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/nygaard-filtration-qrsp`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-3-nygaard-filtration-qrsp); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/nygaard-filtration`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-3-nygaard-filtration); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/nygaard-graded-pieces`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-3-nygaard-graded-pieces); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/breuil-kisin-twist`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-3-breuil-kisin-twist); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/frobenius-on-prismatic-cohomology`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-frobenius-on-prismatic-cohomology); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/prism`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-prism).

**Consumers.** BS22 Theorem 12.2 and Proposition 12.10: φ/d^i identifies the graded pieces with the conjugate filtration. BS22 §14 and PR.4 (syntomic complexes): Z_p(n) = fib(φ_n − 1 : Fil^n_N Δ̂{n} → Δ̂{n}) uses the twisted divided Frobenius. BMS2 Theorem 7.2 (4) and Lemma 7.22: the divided Frobenius of π_0 TC^-; it contracts high Nygaard levels modulo p. BS22 Theorem 15.3: the filtered Frobenius Fil^•_N → I^• is the map that factors through Lη_I.

**Planning API.**

- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Nygaard.dividedFrobenius` (constructor): For a prism (B, (d)) and i ∈ N, the map φ_i = φ/d^i : Fil^i_N B → B.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Nygaard.dividedFrobenius_spec` (characterisation): d^i · φ_i(x) = φ(x) for x ∈ Fil^i_N B, and φ_i(x) is the unique such element.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Nygaard.dividedFrobenius_mul` (relation): φ_{i+j}(xy) = φ_i(x) φ_j(y) for x ∈ Fil^i_N B, y ∈ Fil^j_N B.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Nygaard.dividedFrobenius_succ` (relation): φ_i(x) = d · φ_{i+1}(x) for x ∈ Fil^{i+1}_N B.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Nygaard.dividedFrobenius_mem_iff` (characterisation): φ_i(x) ∈ dB if and only if x ∈ Fil^{i+1}_N B.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Nygaard.dividedFrobenius_unit` (compatibility): For a unit u, the divided Frobenius for the generator ud is u^{−i} times the one for d.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Nygaard.frobeniusFil` (data): The additive, φ-semilinear map Fil^i_N B → J^i, x ↦ φ(x), for any prism (B, J).
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Nygaard.twistedDividedFrobenius` (constructor): The φ-semilinear map φ_i : Fil^i_N B ⊗_B B{i} → B{i}, x ⊗ e ↦ φ(x) φ_{B{i}}(e).
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Nygaard.dividedFrobeniusDerived` (data): For an algebra over a perfectoid base with its chosen perfect prism, φ_i:Fil^i_NΔ_(R/A){i}→Δ_(R/A){i} is the derived divided Frobenius. It is natural, compatible with Nygaard products and agrees with division of φ by d^i on quasiregular semiperfectoid charts after an adapted trivialisation.

**Unit tests.**

- `pr3_divided_frobenius_zero` (degenerate): φ_0(x) = φ(x) for all x.
- `pr3_divided_frobenius_perfect` (computation): For a perfect prism (B, (d)) and φ(e) = d: φ_i(e^i a) = φ(a) for all a ∈ B.
- `pr3_divided_frobenius_crystalline` (computation): For a crystalline prism (B, (p)) with φ = id (for example Z_p): φ_i(p^i a) = a.
- `pr3_divided_frobenius_kernel` (characterisation): φ_i(x) ∈ dB exactly when x ∈ Fil^{i+1}_N B, so φ_i induces an injection gr^i_N B → B/dB.
- `pr3_divided_frobenius_not_multiplicative` (non-example): φ_1 is not multiplicative: for x, y ∈ Fil^1_N B one has φ_1(xy) = d · φ_1(x)φ_1(y); for a perfect prism and x = y = φ^{-1}(d) this gives φ_1(x²) = d and φ_1(x)² = 1.

**Acceptance.** φ_0 = φ. Perfect prism (A, (d)), e = φ^{-1}(d): φ_i(e^i a) = φ(a), so φ_i : Fil^i_N A → A is bijective. Key case: φ_n([p]_{q^{1/p}}^{n−⌊i⌋} Y^i/[⌊i⌋]_q!) is a unit multiple of Y^{ip}/[⌊ip⌋]_q! for i < n+1. BMS2 Theorem 7.2 (4): on π_0 TC^-(S; Z_p) the cyclotomic Frobenius restricted to the i-th Nygaard level is ξ̃^i times a divided Frobenius; under the identification of BS22 Theorem 13.1, which RefinedTraceMethods:RT.6 proves from PR.3/bms2-comparison, it is the completion of φ_i.

**Sources.** [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Proposition 12.10. ### Relative Nygaard filtration of a large quasisyntomic algebra (BS22 Theorem 15.2)

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/relative-nygaard-large-quasisyntomic` · theorem. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.Nygaard` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/Nygaard/Relative`.

Let (A, I) be a bounded prism and S a large quasisyntomic A/I-algebra. (1) The derived prismatic cohomology Δ_{S/A} is concentrated in degree 0 and is a (p, I)-completely flat δ-A-algebra; (Δ_{S/A}, IΔ_{S/A}) is the initial object of the relative prismatic site (S/A)_Δ. Let Δ^{(1)}_{S/A} = Δ_{S/A} ⊗̂^L_{A, φ_A} A (the Frobenius twist, a discrete (p, I)-completely flat A-algebra) and φ_{S/A} : Δ^{(1)}_{S/A} → Δ_{S/A} the relative Frobenius, an A-algebra map. Put Fil^i_N Δ^{(1)}_{S/A} = {x ∈ Δ^{(1)}_{S/A} : φ_{S/A}(x) ∈ I^i Δ_{S/A}}. (2) φ_{S/A} induces an injection gr^i_N Δ^{(1)}_{S/A} → Δ̄_{S/A}{i} = I^iΔ_{S/A}/I^{i+1}Δ_{S/A} whose image is Fil_i^conj Δ̄_{S/A}{i}, for every i ≥ 0. (3) The formation of Fil^i_N commutes with base change in A: for a map of bounded prisms (A, I) → (B, J) and S_B the p-completion of S ⊗_A B, Fil^i_N Δ^{(1)}_{S/A} ⊗̂_A B ≅ Fil^i_N Δ^{(1)}_{S_B/B}.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** (A, I) is a bounded prism; S is large and quasisyntomic over A/I (PR.3/large-quasisyntomic-algebra). The filtration lives on the Frobenius twist Δ^{(1)}_{S/A} = φ_A^*Δ_{S/A}, not on Δ_{S/A}: the relative Frobenius is A-linear only as a map out of the twist. For a perfect prism φ_A is an isomorphism and Fil^i_N Δ^{(1)}_{S/A} = φ_A^* Fil^i_N Δ_{S/A}. The conjugate filtration is the one of PR.2/derived-hodge-tate-comparison relative to A/I; on large S its pieces are discrete, p-completely flat S-modules. Completed tensor products are derived (p, I)-completed; on completely flat modules over a bounded prism they are classical completions (PR.0/bounded-prism-complete-flatness).

**Construction or proof.**

1. (1): by the derived Hodge–Tate comparison the graded pieces of the conjugate filtration of Δ̄_{S/A} are (∧^i L_{S/(A/I)})[−i]^∧{−i}, discrete and p-completely flat over S, so Δ_{S/A} is discrete and (p, I)-completely flat; initiality follows from PR.2/derived-agrees-with-site (BS22 Lemma 7.7) once a functorial idempotent endomorphism of Δ_{S/A} is shown to be the identity, as in the proof of PR.2/qrsp-prism (BS22 Proposition 7.10).
2. (3): if (2) holds for S over A, the base change of Fil^•_N to B is a filtration of Δ^{(1)}_{S_B/B} satisfying (2), and a filtration by ideals satisfying (2) is the Nygaard filtration by the induction of PR.3/nygaard-regular-semiperfectoid (1).
3. (2), reduction: by descent to smooth algebras and left Kan extension it suffices to treat S = (A/I)⟨X_1^{1/p^∞}, …, X_n^{1/p^∞}⟩/(f_1, …, f_m); by PR.2/quasisyntomic-descent (BS22 Proposition 7.11) a flat base change in A gives compatible p-power roots of the f_j; the devissage of PR.3/nygaard-regular-semiperfectoid reduces to S = (A/I)⟨X^{1/p^∞}⟩/(X).
4. (2), the key case over a general base: localise on A so that I = (d) (PR.0/local-distinguished-prism-generators), base change from the universal oriented prism, whose Frobenius is faithfully flat (PR.0/free-delta-ring), so its perfection A → A_∞ is (p, I)-completely faithfully flat (PR.0/prism-perfection); over the perfect prism A_∞ the statement is PR.3/nygaard-graded-pieces, and it descends along A → A_∞ because on the Čech nerve the filtration is the base change from A_∞ by (3).

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/large-quasisyntomic-algebra`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-3-large-quasisyntomic-algebra); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/nygaard-graded-pieces`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-3-nygaard-graded-pieces); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/nygaard-regular-semiperfectoid`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-3-nygaard-regular-semiperfectoid); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/nygaard-filtration`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-3-nygaard-filtration); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/derived-prismatic-cohomology`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-derived-prismatic-cohomology); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/derived-hodge-tate-comparison`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-derived-hodge-tate-comparison); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/derived-agrees-with-site`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-derived-agrees-with-site); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/qrsp-prism`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-qrsp-prism); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/quasisyntomic-descent`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-quasisyntomic-descent); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/prismatic-base-change`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-prismatic-base-change); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/frobenius-on-prismatic-cohomology`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-frobenius-on-prismatic-cohomology); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/prism-perfection`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-prism-perfection); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/free-delta-ring`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-free-delta-ring); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/local-distinguished-prism-generators`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-local-distinguished-prism-generators); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/bounded-prism-complete-flatness`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-bounded-prism-complete-flatness); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/universal-oriented-prism`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-universal-oriented-prism).

**Acceptance.** S = A/I: Δ^{(1)}_{S/A} = A, φ_{S/A} = id, Fil^i_N = I^i and gr^i = I^i/I^{i+1} = (A/I){i} = Fil_i^conj Δ̄{i} (BL22 Example 5.1.4). S = (A/I)⟨X^{1/p^∞}⟩/(X) over the q-de Rham prism: the base change to the perfection is the key case of PR.3/nygaard-key-case. i = 0: gr^0_N Δ^{(1)}_{S/A} ≅ S.

**Sources.** [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Theorem 15.2 and its proof.
