<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-3-relative-nygaard-filtration"></a>

### Relative Nygaard filtration on the Frobenius twist φ_A^*Δ_{R/A}

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/relative-nygaard-filtration` · construction. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.Nygaard` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/Nygaard/Relative`.

Let (A, I) be a bounded prism, Ā = A/I. For an animated commutative Ā-algebra R write φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} = Δ^{(1)}_{R/A} = Δ_{R/A} ⊗̂^L_{A, φ_A} A for the Frobenius twist of derived prismatic cohomology and φ_{R/A} : φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} → Δ_{R/A} for the relative Frobenius, a map of commutative algebra objects of the (p, I)-complete derived category of A. The relative Nygaard filtration is a decreasing filtration Fil^•_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A}, an object of the I-complete filtered derived category DF(A), with a refinement Fil^•(φ) : Fil^•_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} → I^• ⊗_A Δ_{R/A} of φ_{R/A} to a map of filtered objects, constructed in three steps. (a) For R large quasisyntomic, Fil^i_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} is the ideal {x : φ_{R/A}(x) ∈ I^iΔ_{R/A}} of PR.3/relative-nygaard-large-quasisyntomic. (b) For R quasisyntomic over Ā it is the right Kan extension of (a) along the inclusion of large algebras, equivalently the quasisyntomic unfolding: each R ↦ Fil^i_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} is a quasisyntomic sheaf and Fil^0_N = φ_A^*Δ_{R/A}. For X = Spf R affine and smooth over Ā this reads RΓ_Δ(X/A) ≅ RΓ(X_qsyn, Δ_{−/A}) and Fil^i_N RΓ_Δ(X/A)^{(1)} = RΓ(X_qsyn, Fil^i_N Δ^{(1)}_{−/A}); for a smooth formal Ā-scheme X the filtrations on affine opens glue to a filtered object Fil^•_N Δ^{(1)}_{X/A} of D(X_ét, A). (c) For all animated R it is the (p, I)-completed left Kan extension of its restriction to finitely generated polynomial Ā-algebras; on quasisyntomic algebras this agrees with (b). Characterisation (Bhatt–Lurie Proposition 5.1.1): the pair (Fil^•_N, Fil^•(φ)), functorial in R, is determined up to essentially unique isomorphism by: (1) each R ↦ Fil^n_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} commutes with sifted colimits; (2) for R a finitely generated polynomial Ā-algebra, gr^n(φ) : gr^n_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} → Δ̄_{R/A}{n} is an isomorphism on H^m for m ≤ n and H^m(gr^n_N) = 0 for m > n. Properties: gr^n_N = 0 for n < 0, so the filtration is N-indexed; it is multiplicative (a commutative algebra object of DF(A) refining φ_A^*Δ_{R/A}), giving in particular v : I ⊗^L_A Fil^•_N → Fil^{•+1}_N whose composite with Fil^{•+1}_N → Fil^•_N is induced by I ⊂ A; for a map of bounded prisms (A, I) → (B, J) there is a canonical isomorphism B ⊗̂^L_A Fil^•_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} ≅ Fil^•_N φ_B^*Δ_{(B ⊗^L_A R)/B}; for R = Ā, Fil^n_N = I^n ⊂ A; for a perfect prism, Fil^•_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} = φ_A^*(Fil^•_N Δ_{R/A}) with the filtration of PR.3/nygaard-filtration.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** (A, I) is a bounded prism; R is an animated commutative Ā-algebra (derived prismatic cohomology depends only on the derived p-completion of R). The filtration is on the Frobenius twist φ_A^*Δ_{R/A}. It is not a filtration of Δ_{R/A} unless φ_A is an isomorphism. DF(A) is the filtered derived category of DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1; the I-adic filtration I^• ⊗ Δ_{R/A} is Z-indexed, with i-th term I^{⊗ i} ⊗_A Δ_{R/A} for all i ∈ Z (negative powers are powers of the dual), as in BMS2 Proposition 5.8 and Bhatt–Lurie. Since gr^n_N = 0 for n < 0 the filtered Frobenius factors through its truncation to i ≥ 0, and for p-completely smooth R (Δ̄ ∈ D^{≥0}) the Beilinson connective covers of the two filtrations agree. BL22 Proposition 5.1.1 (1) prints the target of R ↦ Fil^n_N as the complete derived category of Ā; the objects are A-complexes (for R = Ā they are the ideals I^n), so the target is the (p, I)-complete derived category of A (source issue PrismaticCohomology/E34). Bhatt–Lurie's and Bhatt–Scholze's constructions agree wherever both apply: BL22 defines the filtration on large algebras by the formula of BS22 Theorem 15.2 and extends it by the same Kan extensions.

**Construction or proof.**

1. (a) is PR.3/relative-nygaard-large-quasisyntomic. (b): large algebras form a basis of the quasisyntomic site (PR.3/large-quasisyntomic-algebra); R ↦ φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} and R ↦ I^•Δ_{R/A} satisfy quasisyntomic descent (BL22 Lemma 5.1.7, from the conjugate filtration and flat descent for exterior powers of the cotangent complex, DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.5; PR.2/quasisyntomic-descent), hence are right Kan extended from large algebras, and so is the filtered Frobenius. For smooth X, BS22 Theorem 15.3 states the same definition on X_qsyn.
2. (c): by induction on n, R ↦ Fil^n_N on quasisyntomic algebras is left Kan extended from polynomial algebras, because gr^n_N ≅ Fil_n^conj Δ̄{n} is (PR.3/relative-nygaard-large-quasisyntomic (2) on large algebras, extended by descent); then extend to animated rings by the universal property of animation (EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E3, EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E5:animation).
3. Uniqueness: a second pair satisfying (1), (2) is, on large algebras, an honest filtration by subgroups equal to the Frobenius-divisibility ideals, by induction on n using the fibre sequence Fil′^{n+1} → Fil′^n → Fil_n^conj Δ̄{n}; the resulting comparison map is an isomorphism on polynomial algebras by (2), hence in general by (1) (BL22, proof of Proposition 5.1.1).
4. Multiplicativity, the map v and change of prism are checked on large algebras, where they are statements about ideals (φ(xy) = φ(x)φ(y); PR.3/relative-nygaard-large-quasisyntomic (3)), and extended by the Kan extensions (BL22 Remarks 5.1.8–5.1.10).

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/relative-nygaard-large-quasisyntomic`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-3-relative-nygaard-large-quasisyntomic); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/large-quasisyntomic-algebra`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-3-large-quasisyntomic-algebra); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/nygaard-filtration`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-3-nygaard-filtration); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/derived-prismatic-cohomology`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-derived-prismatic-cohomology); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/quasisyntomic-descent`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-quasisyntomic-descent); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/derived-hodge-tate-comparison`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-derived-hodge-tate-comparison); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/prismatic-base-change`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-prismatic-base-change); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/frobenius-on-prismatic-cohomology`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-frobenius-on-prismatic-cohomology); `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.5`; `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`; `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E3`; `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E5:animation`; [`mathlib:DerivedCategory`](#mathlib-derivedcategory).

**Consumers.** BS22 Theorem 15.3 (= Theorem 1.16): the filtered Frobenius out of this filtration factors through Lη_I and identifies φ_A^*Δ with Lη_IΔ. BS22 Proposition 15.7 and BMS2 §11: its completion for the Breuil–Kisin prism is π_0 TP(−/S[u]; Z_p). Bhatt–Lurie §§5.2–5.5 and PR.5: the absolute Nygaard filtration is glued from the relative one over the Cartier–Witt stack and the Hodge filtration. PR.6 (BS22 Theorem 17.2) and BMS2 Proposition 9.10: under AΩ ≃ φ_A^*Δ the filtration is the décalage filtration of AΩ ≃ Lη_ξ φ_* AΩ. PR.8 (logarithmic Nygaard filtration): the log variant is modelled on this construction.

**Planning API.**

- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Nygaard.frobeniusTwist` (constructor): The object φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} of D(A) for a prism (A, I) and an A/I-algebra R.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Nygaard.relativeFrobenius` (data): The A-linear relative Frobenius φ_{R/A} : φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} → Δ_{R/A}.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Nygaard.relFil` (constructor): The filtered object i ↦ Fil^i_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A}, a functor from (N, ≥) to D(A).
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Nygaard.relFilZeroIso` (simp): Fil^0_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} ≅ φ_A^*Δ_{R/A}.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Nygaard.relGr` (data): The graded piece gr^i_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A}.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Nygaard.relGr_triangle` (structure): There is a distinguished triangle Fil^{i+1}_N → Fil^i_N → gr^i_N → Fil^{i+1}_N[1].
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Nygaard.relFilMap` (functoriality): A map R → R′ of A/I-algebras induces a natural transformation Fil^•_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} → Fil^•_N φ_A^*Δ_{R′/A}.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Nygaard.relFil_bar` (example): For R = A/I: Fil^i_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} is the ideal I^i of A placed in degree 0.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Nygaard.relFil_large` (compatibility): For R large quasisyntomic, Fil^i_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} is concentrated in degree 0 (it is the ideal of Frobenius-divisible elements).
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Nygaard.relFilBaseChange` (compatibility): For a map of bounded prisms (A, I) → (B, J) with completed base change functor B ⊗̂^L_A −: B ⊗̂^L_A Fil^i_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} ≅ Fil^i_N φ_B^*Δ_{R_B/B}.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Nygaard.relativeFilteredFrobenius` (data): The filtered linearized Frobenius Fil^•_N(φ_A^*Δ)→I^•Δ has in degree i the map to I^i⊗Δ, with I^• indexed by all integers using inverse powers for negative i. Transition maps and multiplication commute with Frobenius.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Nygaard.relativeV` (relation): Multiplication gives v:I⊗Fil^i_N(φ_A^*Δ)→Fil^(i+1)_N(φ_A^*Δ), natural in R and the prism. Its composite with the transition to Fil^i_N is the multiplication map I⊗Fil^i_N→Fil^i_N; its composite with filtered Frobenius is multiplication by I on I^iΔ.

**Unit tests.**

- `pr3_rel_fil_zero` (degenerate): Fil^0_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} ≅ φ_A^*Δ_{R/A}.
- `pr3_rel_fil_base` (computation): For R = A/I and all i: Fil^i_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} ≅ I^i in degree 0.
- `pr3_rel_gr_zero_base` (computation): For R = A/I: gr^0_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} ≅ A/I in degree 0.
- `pr3_rel_fil_needs_twist` (non-example): The Nygaard ideal Fil^1_N A = φ_A^{-1}(I) of the base prism is not I in general: for the q-de Rham prism it is (q − 1), while the relative filtration of R = A/I on φ_A^*Δ = A is I = ([p]_q).

**Acceptance.** R = Ā: φ_A^*Δ = A and Fil^n_N = I^n. Crystalline prism (W(k), (p)), k a perfect field, and R smooth over k: φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} ≅ RΓ_crys(R/A) (PR.1/crystalline-comparison) and Fil^•_N is the Nygaard filtration of crystalline cohomology; in coordinates it is p^{max(i−•, 0)} Ω^• (PR.3/nygaard-filtration-in-coordinates). Perfect prism: agreement with PR.3/nygaard-filtration after applying φ_A^*. Change of prism along the q-de Rham prism → its perfection recovers the key case.

**Prototype boundary.** `TauCeti.Prismatic.Nygaard.relFil_large` needs its supplier carrier: DD.5 supplies the large quasisyntomic condition; DD.1 and E5 supply the animated completed base change R_B and Frobenius-twisted filtered scalar extension. The ordinary-ring prototypes above give their discrete shadows. `TauCeti.Prismatic.Nygaard.relFilBaseChange` needs its supplier carrier: DD.5 supplies the large quasisyntomic condition; DD.1 and E5 supply the animated completed base change R_B and Frobenius-twisted filtered scalar extension. The ordinary-ring prototypes above give their discrete shadows.

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-3-relative-nygaard-graded-pieces"></a>

### Graded pieces of the relative Nygaard filtration

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/relative-nygaard-graded-pieces` · theorem. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.Nygaard` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/Nygaard/Relative`.

Let (A, I) be a bounded prism, Ā = A/I, and R an animated commutative Ā-algebra. (1) For every n ≥ 0 the map gr^n(φ) : gr^n_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} → I^n/I^{n+1} ⊗^L_A Δ_{R/A} = Δ̄_{R/A}{n} factors through an isomorphism gr^n_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} ≅ Fil_n^conj Δ̄_{R/A}{n}, functorial in R; gr^n_N = 0 for n < 0. (2) gr^0_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} ≅ R̂, the derived p-completion of R. (3) If the p-completion of R is p-completely smooth over Ā (for example X = Spf R affine smooth), then gr^n_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} ≅ τ^{≤ n} Δ̄_{R/A}{n}: H^m(gr^n_N) ≅ Ω̂^m_{R/Ā}{n − m} for 0 ≤ m ≤ n and H^m(gr^n_N) = 0 otherwise. (4) gr^1_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} ≅ L_{R/A}[−1]^∧, the shifted p-completed cotangent complex of R over A. (5) For every R the filtered object Fil^•_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} is connective for the Beilinson t-structure of DF(A): gr^n_N lies in D^{≤ n} for all n.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** (A, I) bounded prism; R animated Ā-algebra; the conjugate filtration and the twist {n} = ⊗ (I/I²)^{⊗ n} are those of PR.2/derived-hodge-tate-comparison. The isomorphism in (1) is A-linear: the semilinearity of the perfectoid statement PR.3/nygaard-graded-pieces has been absorbed into the Frobenius twist. (4) is BS22 Remark 15.6, which prints L_{X/A} ≃ gr^1_N Δ^{(1)}_{X/A} without the shift and cites Theorem 1.16 (2) for (3) (register id PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22/E26); the node states the corrected form. The Beilinson t-structure is requested from DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1 (BMS2 Definition 5.3).

**Construction or proof.**

1. (1) on large quasisyntomic algebras is PR.3/relative-nygaard-large-quasisyntomic (2); both sides are right Kan extended from large algebras on quasisyntomic ones and left Kan extended from polynomial algebras in general (PR.3/relative-nygaard-filtration; the conjugate filtration commutes with sifted colimits), which gives the functorial isomorphism for all R (BL22 Remark 5.1.2 and the proof of Proposition 5.1.1).
2. (2): Fil_0^conj Δ̄_{R/A} ≅ R̂ (PR.2/derived-hodge-tate-comparison). (3): for p-completely smooth R the conjugate filtration is the canonical filtration and H^m(Δ̄_{R/A}) ≅ Ω̂^m{−m} (PR.1/hodge-tate-comparison); this is BS22 Theorem 15.3, second display, obtained there by descent from Theorem 15.2 (2).
3. (4): combine (1) for n = 1 with PR.2/first-conjugate-piece-cotangent (Fil_1^conj Δ̄_{R/A} ≅ L_{R/A}{−1}[−1]^∧).
4. (5): Fil_n^conj Δ̄_{R/A} has graded pieces (∧^j L_{R/Ā})[−j]^∧, j ≤ n, which lie in D^{≤ j} ⊂ D^{≤ n}.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/relative-nygaard-filtration`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-3-relative-nygaard-filtration); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/relative-nygaard-large-quasisyntomic`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-3-relative-nygaard-large-quasisyntomic); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/derived-hodge-tate-comparison`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-derived-hodge-tate-comparison); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/hodge-tate-comparison`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-hodge-tate-comparison); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/first-conjugate-piece-cotangent`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-first-conjugate-piece-cotangent); `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`.

**Acceptance.** R = Ā: gr^n = I^n/I^{n+1} = Ā{n}. R = Ā⟨T⟩: gr^n_N has H^0 = R{n} and, for n ≥ 1, H^1 = Ω̂^1_{R/Ā}{n−1}. R large quasisyntomic: gr^n_N is the discrete module Fil_n^conj Δ̄_{R/A}{n}. Comparison with the Hodge–Tate side: the associated graded of the Nygaard filtration is the conjugate (Hodge–Tate) filtration, twisted; comparison with the de Rham side is PR.3/nygaard-hodge-comparison.

**Sources.** [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Theorem 15.3 (= Theorem 1.16 (3)) and Theorem 15.2 (2). Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed pages 8, 102, 103. part (3) for affine smooth X; part (1) on large algebras. [BL22](https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.06120v1), Remarks 5.1.2, 5.1.3, 5.1.5. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 115. parts (1), (2), (3), (5) for animated Ā-algebras. [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Remark 15.6. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 105. part (4), with the shift corrected.

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-3-nygaard-completion"></a>

### Nygaard completion

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/nygaard-completion` · construction. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.Nygaard` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/Nygaard/Completion`.

(a) For a prism (B, J) the Nygaard completion is the ring B̂ = lim_i B/Fil^i_N B (inverse limit along the surjections B/Fil^{i+1}_N → B/Fil^i_N), with the canonical map c : B → B̂ and the filtration Fil^i_N B̂ = ker(B̂ → B/Fil^i_N B). Then ker(c) = ∩_i Fil^i_N B; B̂/Fil^i_N B̂ = B/Fil^i_N B; gr^i_N B̂ = gr^i_N B; and B̂ is complete for its filtration. For S quasiregular semiperfectoid, Δ̂_S denotes the Nygaard completion of Δ_S; Δ̂_S/Fil^1_N Δ̂_S ≅ S and gr^i_N Δ̂_S ≅ Fil_i Δ̄_S{i} (PR.3/nygaard-graded-pieces). (b) Frobenius. Assume J = (d) (then B is d-adically complete). Since φ(Fil^n_N B) ⊂ d^n B, φ induces a ring map φ̂ : B̂ → lim_n B/d^n B = B with φ̂ ∘ c = φ; the Frobenius of B̂ is c ∘ φ̂, so it factors through B. Likewise the divided Frobenius extends to φ_i : Fil^i_N B̂ → B with d^i φ_i = φ̂ on Fil^i_N B̂, and with twists to φ_i : Fil^i_N B̂ ⊗_B B{i} → B̂{i}. (c) Filtered objects. For a filtered object Fil^• of DF(A) with underlying object M = Fil^0 (N-indexed), the completion is M̂ = lim_i M/Fil^i with Fil^i M̂ = lim_{j ≥ i} Fil^i/Fil^j; M → M̂ is an isomorphism if and only if lim_i Fil^i = 0, and then M is called Nygaard-complete. This defines the Nygaard completions of φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} (PR.3/relative-nygaard-filtration) and of Δ_{S/A} over a perfectoid base (PR.3/nygaard-filtration); for a tower of surjections of discrete modules the derived limit is the limit, so (a) is a special case. (d) On quasisyntomic algebras over a perfectoid ring R, S ↦ Fil^•_N Δ̂_{S/A} is a quasisyntomic sheaf of complete filtered objects, the unfolding of (a) from quasiregular semiperfectoid rings. The map Δ → Δ̂ is not an isomorphism in general; PR.3/nygaard-completeness states when it is, and PR.3/nygaard-incomplete-example gives a ring S for which Δ_S → Δ̂_S is injective and not surjective.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** (B, J) is a prism; in (b) J is principal, which holds for the initial prism of a quasiregular semiperfectoid ring. Completion means completion with respect to the Nygaard filtration only; no (p, J)-adic completion is applied, and by BS22 Lemma 13.2 (2) none is needed for Δ_S (PR.3/bms2-comparison). Statement (b) is not printed in the sources in this form; it is immediate from the definition of the filtration and is recorded because the syntomic complexes of PR.4 need φ_i on the completion without passing through topological Hochschild homology. Δ and Δ̂ are distinct objects: no statement of the stage identifies them outside the cases listed in PR.3/nygaard-completeness.

**Construction or proof.**

1. (a): the inverse limit of rings along surjections; the kernel of B̂ → B/Fil^i_N B is the limit of Fil^i_N/Fil^j_N, the transition maps are surjective, so B̂ → B/Fil^i_N is surjective and the quotients and graded pieces are unchanged; completeness of B̂ is the standard statement for limits of towers.
2. (b): a prism is derived J-complete and d is a nonzerodivisor, so B is classically d-adically complete. For x ∈ Fil^i_N B̂ represented by x_n ∈ Fil^i_N B with x_{n+1} − x_n ∈ Fil^n_N B, the elements φ_i(x_n) satisfy φ_i(x_{n+1}) − φ_i(x_n) ∈ d^{n−i}B and converge d-adically; the limit is φ_i(x). Twists: tensor with the invertible module B{i} (PR.3/divided-frobenius (b)).
3. (c): completion of filtered objects (BMS2 Lemma 5.2 (2), requested from DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1): F̂(i) = F(i)/F(∞), and gr^i is unchanged.
4. (d): each gr^i_N is a quasisyntomic sheaf (PR.3/nygaard-filtration (c)); a limit of sheaves is a sheaf.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/nygaard-filtration-qrsp`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-3-nygaard-filtration-qrsp); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/nygaard-graded-pieces`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-3-nygaard-graded-pieces); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/divided-frobenius`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-3-divided-frobenius); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/nygaard-filtration`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-3-nygaard-filtration); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/relative-nygaard-filtration`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-3-relative-nygaard-filtration); `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`; [`mathlib:Ideal.Quotient.factor`](#mathlib-ideal-quotient-factor); [`mathlib:IsAdicComplete`](#mathlib-isadiccomplete).

**Consumers.** BS22 Theorem 13.1: Δ̂_S is identified with π_0 TC^-(S; Z_p) of BMS2 (proved in RefinedTraceMethods:RT.6 from PR.3/bms2-comparison). BS22 §14 and PR.4: Z_p(n)(S) = fib(φ_n − 1 : Fil^n_N Δ̂_S{n} → Δ̂_S{n}). BS22 Proposition 15.7: the Nygaard completion of Δ^{(1)}_{S/𝔖} is π_0 TP(S/S[u]; Z_p). Bhatt–Lurie §5.8 and PR.5: the Nygaard-completed absolute prismatic complex and its comparison with the Hodge-completed derived de Rham complex.

**Planning API.**

- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Nygaard.completion` (constructor): The ring B̂ = lim_i B/Fil^i_N B, realised as the subring of compatible families in ∏_i B/Fil^i_N B.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Nygaard.mem_completion_iff` (characterisation): A family (x_i) lies in B̂ iff x_j maps to x_i under B/Fil^j_N → B/Fil^i_N for all i ≤ j.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Nygaard.toCompletion` (data): The canonical ring map c : B → B̂.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Nygaard.toCompletion_apply` (simp): The i-th component of c(x) is the class of x in B/Fil^i_N B.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Nygaard.ker_toCompletion` (characterisation): ker(c) = ∩_i Fil^i_N B.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Nygaard.completionProj` (projection): The ring map B̂ → B/Fil^i_N B.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Nygaard.completionProj_surjective` (other): B̂ → B/Fil^i_N B is surjective.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Nygaard.completionFil` (data): The ideal Fil^i_N B̂ = ker(B̂ → B/Fil^i_N B).
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Nygaard.completionFrobenius` (data): For J = (d) and B d-adically complete, the ring map φ̂ : B̂ → B with φ̂ ∘ c = φ.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Nygaard.completionFrobenius_toCompletion` (simp): φ̂(c(x)) = φ(x).

With Breuil–Kisin twists this is independent of orientation and is the map used in the syntomic fibre; the target is Δ, not an arbitrary completion.

**Unit tests.**

- `pr3_completion_perfect` (compatibility): For a perfect prism (B, (d)) with B classically (p, d)-adically complete, c : B → B̂ is bijective.
- `pr3_completion_quotient` (characterisation): B̂ → B/Fil^i_N B is surjective with kernel Fil^i_N B̂, and c^{-1}(Fil^i_N B̂) = Fil^i_N B.
- `pr3_completion_frobenius` (compatibility): φ̂ ∘ c = φ: the Frobenius of the completion restricts to φ on B.
- `pr3_completion_not_surjective` (non-example): It is false that c is surjective for every prism: for the prism of F_p[X^{1/p^∞}]/(X) the element Σ_m Y^m/m! of B̂ is not in the image.

S = F_p[X^{1/p^∞}]/(X): Δ̂_S is strictly larger than Δ_S (PR.3/nygaard-incomplete-example). φ̂ ∘ c = φ and the Frobenius of Δ̂_S has image in the image of Δ_S. Export: Δ̂_S with its filtration, Frobenius and divided Frobenius is the object that RefinedTraceMethods:RT.6 compares with π_0 TC^-(S; Z_p), and the object from which PR.4 builds Z_p(n).

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-3-leta-frobenius-factorisation"></a>

### The Lη_I factorisation of Frobenius (BS22 Theorem 15.3)

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/leta-frobenius-factorisation` · theorem. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.Nygaard` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/Nygaard/Decalage`.

Let (A, I) be a bounded prism and R a p-completely smooth A/I-algebra, X = Spf R, Δ = Δ_{R/A} = RΓ_Δ(X/A). (1) The filtered Frobenius Fil^•(φ) : Fil^•_N φ_A^*Δ → I^• ⊗ Δ factors uniquely through the connective cover τ^{≤0}_B(I^• ⊗ Δ) for the Beilinson t-structure, whose underlying complex is Lη_I Δ. On underlying complexes this gives a canonical map φ̃ : φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} → Lη_I Δ_{R/A} such that the relative Frobenius factors as φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} → Lη_I Δ_{R/A} → Δ_{R/A}, the second map being the canonical one (it exists because Δ lies in D^{≥0} and H^0(Δ) is I-torsion-free). (2) φ̃ is an isomorphism. (3) The filtered map Fil^•_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} → τ^{≤0}_B(I^• ⊗ Δ_{R/A}) is an isomorphism of filtered objects: Fil^•(φ) exhibits the Nygaard filtration as the Beilinson connective cover of the I-adic filtration. For an I-torsion-free complex K^• representing Δ, Fil^i_N corresponds under φ̃ to the subcomplex I^iK^• ∩ η_I K^• of η_I K^•. In particular lim_i Fil^i_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} = 0. (4) φ̃ is a map of commutative algebra objects, compatible with base change in (A, I) and with étale localisation on R; for a smooth formal A/I-scheme X it globalises to an isomorphism φ̃ : Δ^{(1)}_{X/A} ≅ Lη_I Δ_{X/A} in D(X_ét, A).

**Hypotheses and conventions.** (A, I) is a bounded prism; R is p-completely smooth over A/I. No orientation of I and no hypothesis on W(A/I) is made. Lη_I is the derived décalage functor of AInfCohomology:AI.1 for the invertible ideal I ⊂ A (on the ringed topos (X_ét, A) in the global statement); it is not exact, and the statement is one about objects and maps in D(A). The Beilinson t-structure, τ^{≤0}_B, and the identification of Lη_I K with the underlying complex of τ^{≤0}_B(I^• ⊗ K) (BMS2 Theorem 5.4 and Proposition 5.8) are requested from DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1 and AInfCohomology:AI.1.

**Construction or proof.**

1. (1): by PR.3/relative-nygaard-graded-pieces (3), gr^i_N ≅ τ^{≤i}Δ̄{i} ∈ D^{≤i}, so Fil^•_N φ_A^*Δ is Beilinson connective and the filtered Frobenius factors uniquely through τ^{≤0}_B(I^•Δ); its underlying complex is Lη_IΔ (BMS2 Proposition 5.8). Since Δ̄ ∈ D^{≥0}, the graded pieces of τ^{≤0}_B(I^•Δ) vanish in negative degrees, so the cover is N-indexed and its map to I^0Δ = Δ is the map Lη_IΔ → Δ of BMS1 Lemma 6.10.
2. (2): by derived Nakayama it suffices to check modulo I. Lη_IΔ ⊗^L_A A/I is the Bockstein complex (H^•(Δ̄){•}, β_I) (AInfCohomology:AI.1/bockstein-reduction, BMS1 Proposition 6.12), which is Ω̂^•_{R/(A/I)} by the Hodge–Tate comparison (PR.1/hodge-tate-comparison). After reduction modulo I, both sides commute with change of prism and with étale localisation: on the right this follows from the Bockstein description and the p-completely flat completed differential forms of smooth R, rather than from an unrestricted scalar-extension theorem for Lη; reduce to a polynomial algebra, then by base change to an oriented prism, to the universal oriented prism, to a crystalline prism (BS22 Construction 6.1, as in PR.1/hodge-tate-comparison) and to A = Z_p, where the claim is the crystalline comparison (PR.1/crystalline-comparison) and the Cartier isomorphism (DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.3/polynomial-cartier-map).
3. (3): the filtered map is an isomorphism on every gr^i, by (1) of PR.3/relative-nygaard-graded-pieces and gr^i τ^{≤0}_B = τ^{≤i} gr^i. Its fibre is therefore a constant filtered object, equal to the fibre of φ̃ in filtration degree 0, which vanishes by (2). The subcomplex description is the filtration G^i = I^iK^• ∩ η_IK^• in the proof of BMS2 Proposition 5.8, and lim_i G^i = lim_i I^iΔ = 0.
4. (4): τ^{≤0}_B is lax symmetric monoidal because the Beilinson t-structure is compatible with the tensor product (BMS2 Theorem 5.4 (1)); étale localisation follows from flat base change for Lη (AInfCohomology:AI.1). For an arbitrary change of bounded prism, construct the natural comparison and reduce it modulo the target prism ideal. The Bockstein formula, the Hodge–Tate comparison and p-complete flatness of smooth differential forms identify that reduction with scalar extension of the de Rham complex; complete Nakayama makes the comparison an isomorphism. Combine this with PR.1/prismatic-base-change and PR.3/relative-nygaard-filtration. No arbitrary-base-change property of Lη is assumed.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/relative-nygaard-filtration`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-3-relative-nygaard-filtration); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/relative-nygaard-graded-pieces`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-3-relative-nygaard-graded-pieces); `AInfCohomology:AI.1/derived-decalage`; `AInfCohomology:AI.1/bockstein-reduction`; `AInfCohomology:AI.1/decalage-cohomology`; `AInfCohomology:AI.1`; `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`; [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/hodge-tate-comparison`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-hodge-tate-comparison); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/crystalline-comparison`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-crystalline-comparison); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/prismatic-base-change`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-prismatic-base-change); `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.3/polynomial-cartier-map`; [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/crystallization-of-oriented-prism`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-crystallization-of-oriented-prism); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/universal-oriented-prism`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-universal-oriented-prism); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/etale-localization`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-etale-localization); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/bounded-prism-complete-flatness`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-bounded-prism-complete-flatness).

**Acceptance.** R = A/I: φ_A^*Δ = A = Lη_I A and φ̃ is the identity. Crystalline prism (W(k), (p)): the statement is the Berthelot–Ogus isomorphism φ : RΓ_crys ≅ Lη_p RΓ_crys, with the Nygaard filtration on the source and the décalage filtration on the target (BMS2 Proposition 8.5 and its corollary). Cohomology: H^i(φ_A^*Δ_{R/A}) ≅ (H^i(Δ_{R/A})/H^i(Δ_{R/A})[I]) ⊗ I^{⊗ i} (AInfCohomology:AI.1/decalage-cohomology). Consumers: PR.3/de-rham-comparison-general, PR.3/image-of-frobenius, PR.6 (AΩ ≃ φ_A^*Δ carries the décalage filtration to the Nygaard filtration), PR.8.

**Sources.** [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Theorem 15.3 (= Theorem 1.16 (4)) and its proof. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed pages 8, 103. parts (1), (2); the proof is the one in the source. [BL22](https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.06120v1), Corollaries 5.2.11 and 5.2.14.  part (3): the Nygaard filtration is the Beilinson connective cover of the I-adic filtration. <a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-3-nygaard-incomplete-example"></a>

### A quasiregular semiperfectoid ring whose prism is not Nygaard-complete

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/nygaard-incomplete-example` · application. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.Nygaard` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/Nygaard/KeyCase`.

Let S_0 = F_p[X^{1/p^∞}]/(X), a quasiregular semiperfect F_p-algebra, with perfect base prism (Z_p, (p)). (1) Δ_{S_0} = Z_p⟨Y^{1/p^∞}⟩{Y^p/p}^∧, the p-completed divided power envelope of (Y) in Z_p[Y^{1/p^∞}], with δ(Y^{1/p^n}) = 0 and X^{1/p^n} ↦ Y^{1/p^{n−1}}; it is the p-completion of ⊕_{i ∈ N[1/p]} Z_p · Y^i/⌊i⌋!. (2) Fil^n_N Δ_{S_0} is the p-completion of ⊕_i p^{max(n−⌊i⌋, 0)} Z_p · Y^i/⌊i⌋!; equivalently it is generated by the elements p^a · Y^b/b! · Y^ε with a + b ≥ n, b ∈ N, 0 ≤ ε < 1. (3) ∩_n Fil^n_N Δ_{S_0} = 0, and Δ̂_{S_0} is the set of families (a_i)_{i ∈ N[1/p]} of p-adic integers, written Σ a_i Y^i/⌊i⌋!, such that for every n only finitely many i with ⌊i⌋ < n have a_i ∉ p^{n−⌊i⌋}Z_p; Δ_{S_0} is the subset of families with a_i → 0 p-adically. (4) The element exp(Y) = Σ_{m ≥ 0} Y^m/m! lies in Δ̂_{S_0} and not in Δ_{S_0}. Hence c : Δ_{S_0} → Δ̂_{S_0} is injective and not surjective, and lim^1_n Fil^n_N Δ_{S_0} ≠ 0. (5) The same holds for the key case S = (Z_p[ζ_{p^∞}, X^{1/p^∞}]/X)^∧ of PR.3/nygaard-key-case, with Σ_m Y^m/[m]_q! ∈ Δ̂_S ∖ Δ_S. By contrast Δ_S = Δ̂_S for S perfectoid.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** S_0 is the reduction of the key case along Z_p[ζ_{p^∞}]^∧ → F_p; the description (1), (2) is that of PR.3/nygaard-key-case at q = 1. Bhatt–Lurie state the example for k[x^{1/p^∞}]/(x) in the coordinates of A_crys, which differ from the present ones by the Frobenius twist of Anschütz–Le Bras Remark 3.4.3 (x corresponds to Y); the filtration is the ideal generated by p^a x^b/b! with a + b ≥ m. The example concerns the prism of a quasiregular semiperfectoid ring as defined in PR.3/nygaard-filtration-qrsp; no absolute prismatic cohomology is used.

**Construction or proof.**

1. (1): Δ_{S_0} is the prismatic envelope Z_p⟨Y^{1/p^∞}⟩{Y^p/p}^∧ (PR.2/qrsp-prism), which is the p-completed divided power envelope of (Y) by PR.0/pd-envelope-as-delta-envelope (BS22 Corollary 2.39) since Y^p = φ(Y); its basis is the standard one (CrystallineCohomology:CR.0).
2. (2): S → S_0 is relatively perfect over the map of perfectoid rings Z_p[ζ_{p^∞}]^∧ → F_p, so by PR.3/nygaard-regular-semiperfectoid (3) the Nygaard filtration is the base change of that of PR.3/nygaard-key-case (e) along q ↦ 1, where [p]_{q^{1/p}} ↦ p and [n]_q! ↦ n!. It agrees with BL22 Proposition 5.3.6.
3. (3): Fil^n_N is graded and its degree i part is p^{max(n−⌊i⌋,0)}Z_p, with zero intersection over n; Δ/Fil^n = ⊕_{⌊i⌋<n} Z/p^{n−⌊i⌋}, and the limit over n is the stated set of families.
4. (4): for exp(Y) the family is a_m = 1 for m ∈ N and 0 otherwise; for each n only the indices m < n are non-zero modulo Fil^n, and a_m does not tend to 0. (5): the same argument with [p]_{q^{1/p}}-adic separatedness of A; the perfectoid case is PR.3/nygaard-completeness (2).

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/nygaard-key-case`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-3-nygaard-key-case); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/nygaard-regular-semiperfectoid`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-3-nygaard-regular-semiperfectoid); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/nygaard-completion`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-3-nygaard-completion); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/nygaard-filtration-qrsp`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-3-nygaard-filtration-qrsp); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/qrsp-prism`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-qrsp-prism); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/pd-envelope-as-delta-envelope`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-pd-envelope-as-delta-envelope); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/crystalline-prism`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-crystalline-prism); `CrystallineCohomology:CR.0`.

**Acceptance.** Acceptance example of the stage: a case where Δ and its Nygaard completion visibly differ. Δ_{S_0}/Fil^1_N = ⊕_{i<1} F_p Y^i ≅ S_0. gr^n_N Δ_{S_0} is the F_p-span of the classes of p^{n−⌊i⌋} Y^i/⌊i⌋! for ⌊i⌋ ≤ n, a free S_0-module of rank n + 1, matching Fil_n^conj of the divided power algebra. The partial sums Σ_{m<n} Y^m/m! are a Cauchy sequence for the Nygaard topology with no limit in Δ_{S_0}.

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-3-delta-nygaard-continuity"></a>

### δ on the Nygaard completion

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/delta-nygaard-continuity` · lemma. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/PR3`.

For Δ_S of a quasiregular semiperfectoid S over an oriented perfect prism (A,(d)), δ is uniformly continuous for the topology generated by Fil^i_NΔ_S+(p,d)^jΔ_S. It extends uniquely to the Nygaard completion as a δ-structure. It commutes with the extended Frobenius and agrees with δ on Δ_S; this is not an application of δ-adic completion with the Nygaard filtration as an adic ideal.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** Δ_S is a δ-ring, derived (p,d)-complete and classically complete by bounded complete flatness. Fil^i_N=φ^(-1)(d^iΔ_S); d is distinguished.

**Construction or proof.**

1. The product formula gives δ((d)^(i+1))⊂(d)^i and δ((p,d)^(j+1))⊂(p,d)^j.
2. Use δφ=φδ to get δ(Fil^(i+1)_N)⊂Fil^i_N. The integral addition correction lies in any ideal containing its second argument, so perturbations in Fil^(i+1)_N+(p,d)^(j+1) change δ by Fil^i_N+(p,d)^j.
3. Extend the resulting uniformly continuous operation to the separated completion. Extend the polynomial δ-identities by continuity; uniqueness follows from density.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-frobenius-dictionary`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-delta-frobenius-dictionary); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/correction-identity`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-correction-identity); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/qrsp-prism`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-qrsp-prism); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/nygaard-filtration-qrsp`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-3-nygaard-filtration-qrsp); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/nygaard-completion`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-3-nygaard-completion); `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`.

**Acceptance.** For S perfectoid, this extension agrees with the complete δ-ring on A_inf(S). The proof uses filtration estimates, and does not assert that the Nygaard topology is generated by powers of one ideal.

**Sources.** [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Theorem 13.1, Lemma 13.2 and the proof of Theorem 14.1, §§13–14. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed pages 94, 97. §13, pp.94–95; proof of Theorem 14.1, pp.100–101. The continuity estimate is supplied by this node rather than attributed to an unstated source lemma. The completion is the one entering the BMS comparison; the continuity estimate supplies the δ-extension explicitly..

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-3-de-rham-comparison-general"></a>

### De Rham comparison for every bounded prism (BS22 Corollary 15.4)

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/de-rham-comparison-general` · theorem. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.Nygaard` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/Nygaard/Decalage`.

(1) Fix a bounded (A,I), and let X be a smooth p-adic formal scheme over A/I (locally p-completely smooth, with the usual finite presentation condition). On X_ét, the following canonical equivalence respects its E_∞-algebra structure: Δ_{X/A} ⊗̂^L_{A, φ_A} A/I ≅ Ω^•_{X/(A/I)}, the p-completed de Rham complex. No hypothesis on W(A/I) is needed. (2) For R p-completely smooth over A/I the isomorphism φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} ⊗^L_A A/I ≅ Ω̂^•_{R/(A/I)} is the composite of φ̃ ⊗ A/I (PR.3/leta-frobenius-factorisation), the Bockstein reduction Lη_IΔ_{R/A} ⊗^L_A A/I ≃ (H^•(Δ̄_{R/A}){•}, β_I), and the Hodge–Tate comparison (H^•(Δ̄_{R/A}){•}, β_I) ≅ (Ω̂^•_{R/(A/I)}, d). (3) (Derived form, Bhatt–Lurie Proposition 5.2.5) For every animated commutative A/I-algebra R there is a natural isomorphism A/I ⊗^L_A φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} ≅ dR^∧_{R/(A/I)} with the p-completed derived de Rham complex, the left Kan extension of (2) from polynomial algebras.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** (A, I) is a bounded prism; X is a smooth p-adic formal scheme over A/I, not necessarily affine or proper. The scalar extension is along φ_A followed by A → A/I and is derived (p, I)-completed; it is not the untwisted reduction Δ̄_{X/A}, whose cohomology is the Hodge–Tate cohomology. BS22 Corollary 15.4 prints the right-hand side as Ω^*_{R/(A/I)}; it is Ω^*_{X/(A/I)} (register id PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22/E1). PR.1/de-rham-comparison is the same statement under the hypothesis that W(A/I) is p-torsion-free (BS22 Theorem 6.4), proved without Lη. The sources do not compare the two isomorphisms when both are defined, and the node does not assert that they coincide (red-team finding RT-AREA-padic-2/27). Bhatt–Lurie prove (3) through the Hodge–Tate divisor of the Cartier–Witt stack; the plan uses the Bhatt–Scholze route, which needs nothing from PR.5.

**Construction or proof.**

1. (2): reduce φ̃ : φ_A^*Δ ≅ Lη_IΔ modulo I and apply AInfCohomology:AI.1/bockstein-reduction (BMS1 Proposition 6.12): Lη_IΔ ⊗^L A/I is represented by the complex with terms H^i(Δ̄){i} and the Bockstein differential β_I. The Hodge–Tate comparison map of PR.1/hodge-tate-comparison-map is by construction a map of differential graded algebras (Ω̂^•, d) → (H^•(Δ̄){•}, β_I), an isomorphism by PR.1/hodge-tate-comparison.
2. Multiplicativity: φ̃ is a map of commutative algebra objects (PR.3/leta-frobenius-factorisation (4)); the Bockstein reduction is multiplicative (BMS1 Lemma 6.13 and the remark before it, requested from AInfCohomology:AI.1; equivalently H^0_B is symmetric monoidal on Beilinson-connective objects, BMS2 Theorem 5.4 (3)).
3. (1): the affine isomorphisms are functorial for étale maps and Lη_I, the Bockstein complex and the de Rham complex are compatible with étale localisation, so they glue on X_ét (PR.3/leta-frobenius-factorisation (4)).
4. (3): both sides commute with sifted colimits in R (the left side by PR.2/derived-prismatic-cohomology, the right side by definition of derived de Rham cohomology, DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.2), and (2) for polynomial algebras is natural; left Kan extend (EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E3).

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/leta-frobenius-factorisation`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-3-leta-frobenius-factorisation); `AInfCohomology:AI.1/bockstein-reduction`; `AInfCohomology:AI.1/bockstein-differential`; `AInfCohomology:AI.1`; [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/hodge-tate-comparison`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-hodge-tate-comparison); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/hodge-tate-comparison-map`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-hodge-tate-comparison-map); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/de-rham-comparison`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-de-rham-comparison); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/derived-prismatic-cohomology`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-derived-prismatic-cohomology); `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.2`; `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.2/ordinary-de-rham-complex`; `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E3`.

**Acceptance.** Crystalline prism: reduces modulo p the crystalline comparison φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} ≅ RΓ_crys(R/A). The q-de Rham prism: Δ_{R/A} ⊗̂_{A, φ} A/([p]_q) is de Rham cohomology over Z_p[ζ_p]; here A/I = Z_p[ζ_p] is p-torsion-free, so PR.1/de-rham-comparison also applies. A prism where Theorem 6.4 does not apply: a crystalline prism (A, (p)) with A/p non-reduced has p-torsion in W(A/p); the present node still applies. R = A/I: both sides are A/I.

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-3-image-of-frobenius"></a>

### The image of Frobenius on prismatic cohomology (BS22 Corollary 15.5)

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/image-of-frobenius` · theorem. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.Nygaard` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/Nygaard/Decalage`.

Let (A, I) be a bounded prism and X a smooth formal A/I-scheme. For every i ≥ 0 there is a natural map V_i : τ^{≤ i}Δ_{X/A} ⊗_A I^{⊗ i} → τ^{≤ i}Δ^{(1)}_{X/A} in D(X_ét, A) such that φ ∘ V_i is the natural map τ^{≤ i}Δ_{X/A} ⊗_A I^{⊗ i} → τ^{≤ i}Δ_{X/A} induced by I^{⊗ i} → A, and V_i ∘ (φ ⊗ 1) : τ^{≤ i}Δ^{(1)}_{X/A} ⊗_A I^{⊗ i} → τ^{≤ i}Δ^{(1)}_{X/A} is the natural map. In particular V_i induces V_i : H^i_Δ(X/A) ⊗_A I^{⊗ i} → H^i(X_ét, Δ^{(1)}_{X/A}), an inverse of φ up to I^{⊗ i}; when I = (d), V_i φ = φ V_i = d^i on H^i. For X quasi-compact and quasi-separated, H^i(X_ét, Δ^{(1)}_{X/A}) = H^i(φ_A^* RΓ_Δ(X/A)) and the linearised Frobenius φ_A^* RΓ_Δ(X/A) → RΓ_Δ(X/A) becomes an isomorphism after inverting I.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** (A, I) bounded prism; X smooth p-adic formal scheme over A/I; Δ^{(1)}_{X/A} = Δ_{X/A} ⊗̂^L_{A, φ_A} A as a sheaf on X_ét. BS22 Corollary 15.5 prints the induced map as H^i(X_ét, Δ^{(1)}_{X/A}) ⊗ I^{⊗ i} → H^i_Δ(X/A); source and target are interchanged (register id PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22/E25). The node states the corrected direction, which is that of BS22 Theorem 1.8 (6). The identification H^i(X_ét, Δ^{(1)}_{X/A}) = H^i(φ_A^*RΓ_Δ(X/A)) uses the completed quasi-coherent projection formula on a quasi-compact quasi-separated X, established through finite affine descent as in PR.1/prismatic-base-change; the sheaf-level statement needs no such hypothesis.

**Construction or proof.**

1. By PR.3/leta-frobenius-factorisation, φ̃ : Δ^{(1)}_{X/A} ≅ Lη_I Δ_{X/A} and φ = (Lη_IΔ → Δ) ∘ φ̃.
2. BMS1 Lemma 6.9 (requested from AInfCohomology:AI.1) gives natural transformations I^{⊗ m} ⊗ τ^{≤ m} → τ^{≤ m} Lη_I and, on objects with I-torsion-free H^n, τ^{≥ n} Lη_I → I^{⊗ n} ⊗ τ^{≥ n}, whose composites in both orders on τ^{[n, m]} are the natural inclusions. Take n = 0, m = i and K = Δ_{X/A}, which lies in D^{≥0} with I-torsion-free H^0; define V_i as φ̃^{-1} composed with the first transformation.
3. H^i(X_ét, τ^{≤ i}K) → H^i(X_ét, K) is an isomorphism for every K, which gives the statement on H^i; after inverting I the maps φ and V_i are mutually inverse up to the unit d^i locally.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/leta-frobenius-factorisation`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-3-leta-frobenius-factorisation); `AInfCohomology:AI.1`; `AInfCohomology:AI.1/decalage-truncations`; `AInfCohomology:AI.1/derived-decalage`.

**Acceptance.** i = 0: V_0 φ = φ V_0 = 1 on τ^{≤0}, so φ : H^0(Δ^{(1)}_{X/A}) → H^0(Δ_{X/A}) is an isomorphism. Crystalline prism: V_i is the classical operator with V_i φ = φ V_i = p^i on H^i_crys (Berthelot–Ogus). X = P^1 and i = 2: φ on H^2_Δ(P^1/A) = A{−1} is divisible by exactly I, consistent with φ_{A{−1}} : A{−1} → I ⊗ A{−1}. Consumer: finiteness and isogeny statements for prismatic cohomology (BS22 Theorem 1.8 (6)); PR.7 uses the isogeny property of Frobenius on prismatic F-crystals of geometric origin.

**Sources.** [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Corollary 15.5 and its proof. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 104. the statement, with the direction of the induced map on H^i corrected. [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Theorem 1.8 (6). Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 4. the consequence for the linearised Frobenius and the direction of V_i. [BMS1](https://arxiv.org/abs/1602.03148v3), Lemma 6.9. ### The Nygaard filtration in coordinates (de Rham and q-de Rham models)

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/nygaard-filtration-in-coordinates` · theorem. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.Nygaard` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/Nygaard/Coordinates`.

Let (A, (d)) be a perfect prism, d′ = φ_A(d), and R a p-completely smooth A/d-algebra. Let M^• be a cochain complex of A-modules in degrees ≥ 0 whose terms are d-torsion-free, d′-torsion-free and d-adically complete, with a φ_A-semilinear endomorphism φ_M of complexes, and an isomorphism M^• ≅ φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} in D(A) carrying φ_M to the Frobenius. Assume (a) φ_M(M^n) ⊂ d′^n M^n for all n, and (b) for all n the map M^n/dM^n → H^n(M^•/d′M^•), x ↦ class of φ_M(x)/d′^n, is bijective. Then the subcomplexes N^iM^• = d^{max(i − •, 0)} M^• (in degree n: d^{max(i−n,0)}M^n), with φ_M : N^iM^• → d′^iM^•, represent the relative Nygaard filtration and its filtered Frobenius: there is a unique isomorphism N^•M^• ≅ Fil^•_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} in DF(A) compatible with the maps to the I-adic filtration of Δ_{R/A}. If moreover φ_M/d′^n : M^n/d → M^n/d′ is injective for all n, then N^iM^n = {x ∈ M^n : φ_M(x) ∈ d′^i M^n}. Instances. (i) (BMS2 Proposition 8.7) A = W(k) with k a perfect field, d = d′ = p, R smooth over k, Ã a p-completely smooth lift of R with a Frobenius lift, M^• the p-completed de Rham complex of Ã over W(k): the Nygaard filtration of crystalline cohomology is p^{max(i − •, 0)} Ω^•_{Ã/W(k)}. (ii) (BMS2 Remark 9.11) A = A_inf(O_C), d = ξ, d′ = ξ̃ = [p]_q with q = [ε], R with a framing, M^• the framed q-de Rham complex q-Ω^•_{R̃/A_inf} with φ(T_j) = T_j^p: the Nygaard filtration is ξ^{max(i − •, 0)} q-Ω^•_{R̃/A_inf}.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** (A, (d)) is a perfect prism; under Δ_{R/A} = (φ_A)_* φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} the ideal I^i Δ corresponds to d′^i M, which is why d′ appears in (a) and d in the conclusion. Hypothesis (b) is the Cartier isomorphism in the model M: in (i) it is the inverse Cartier isomorphism (DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.3), in (ii) its q-analogue. In instance (ii) the identification of the framed q-de Rham complex with φ_A^*Δ_{R/A_inf} (through AΩ) and hypothesis (b) are supplied by PR.6, which applies this node; the present stage proves the criterion and instance (i). BMS2 Remark 9.11 prints q = [ε] − 1; the q-de Rham complex of BMS1 Definition 9.5 is taken with q = [ε], so that q − 1 = μ (source issue PrismaticCohomology/E37). BMS2 prove (i) through the de Rham–Witt complex; the plan derives it from the Lη_I factorisation, which needs no de Rham–Witt theory.

**Construction or proof.**

1. N^iM^• is a subcomplex and φ_M(N^iM^n) ⊂ d′^{max(i−n,0)+n}M^n ⊂ d′^iM^n by (a), so φ_M is a filtered map from N^•M^• to the I-adic filtration of Δ_{R/A} refining the relative Frobenius.
2. gr^i N is ⊕_{n ≤ i} (M^n/d)[−n] with zero differential, so N^• is Beilinson connective; it is complete because each M^n is d-adically complete and d-torsion-free. On H^n of gr^i (n ≤ i) the map to gr^i of the I-adic filtration is x ↦ class of φ_M(x)/d′^n, bijective by (b).
3. By the criterion for connective covers (BL22, the remark characterising Beilinson connective covers; BMS2 Theorem 5.4 (2)), N^• is the Beilinson connective cover of the I-adic filtration of Δ_{R/A}; so is Fil^•_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} by PR.3/leta-frobenius-factorisation (3). Connective covers are unique.
4. (i): M ≅ RΓ_crys(R/W(k)) ≅ φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} compatibly with Frobenius (CrystallineCohomology:CR.2, PR.1/crystalline-comparison); φ̃ is divisible by p^n on n-forms, and (b) is the Cartier isomorphism. (ii): φ(d_q log T_j) = ξ̃ d_q log T_j gives (a).

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/leta-frobenius-factorisation`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-3-leta-frobenius-factorisation); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/relative-nygaard-filtration`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-3-relative-nygaard-filtration); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/relative-nygaard-graded-pieces`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-3-relative-nygaard-graded-pieces); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/crystalline-comparison`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-crystalline-comparison); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/perfect-prisms-perfectoid-rings`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-perfect-prisms-perfectoid-rings); `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.3/polynomial-cartier-map`; `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`; `CrystallineCohomology:CR.2`; `AInfCohomology:AI.1/ideal-decalage-complex`; `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.3`.

**Acceptance.** R = k[T], Ã = W(k)⟨T⟩, φ̃(T) = T^p: Fil^i_N is p^iW(k)⟨T⟩ → p^{i−1}W(k)⟨T⟩dT for i ≥ 1; modulo p · Fil^{i−1}_N this is Ω^{≥ i}, as in PR.3/nygaard-hodge-comparison. i = 1: Fil^1_N = (pÃ → Ω^1 → ⋯), the kernel of Ω^•_{Ã} → R. Routed item PAPER-BHATT-MORROW-SCHOLZE-19/098 is instance (ii); its q-de Rham input is PR.6's. The filtration depends on the Frobenius lift only up to filtered quasi-isomorphism.

**Sources.** [BMS2](https://arxiv.org/abs/1802.03261v2), Proposition 8.7. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 57. instance (i), proved there with the de Rham–Witt complex. [BMS2](https://arxiv.org/abs/1802.03261v2), Remark 9.11. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 73. instance (ii); the direct computation alluded to is the criterion of the node. [BMS2](https://arxiv.org/abs/1802.03261v2), Proposition 9.10. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 72. the Nygaard filtration as the décalage filtration, the form used in the proof.

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-3-bms2-comparison"></a>

### The prismatic half of the comparison with BMS2 (BS22 Lemma 13.2 and Theorem 13.1)

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/bms2-comparison` · theorem. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.Nygaard` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/Nygaard/Completion`.

Let S be a quasiregular semiperfectoid ring with prism (Δ_S, (d)). (1) (BS22 Lemma 13.2 (1)) δ(Fil^i_N Δ_S) ⊂ Fil^{pi}_N Δ_S + (d, p)^{i−1} Δ_S for all i ≥ 1. (2) (Lemma 13.2 (2)) The completion of Δ_S for the ideals Fil^i_N Δ_S agrees with its completion for the ideals Fil^i_N Δ_S + (d, p)^j Δ_S; this follows because every gr^i_N Δ_S is classically (d, p)-adically complete. (3) Hence the δ-structure of Δ_S extends uniquely to a continuous δ-structure on the Nygaard completion Δ̂_S, functorially in S; its Frobenius is the Frobenius c ∘ φ̂ of PR.3/nygaard-completion, it maps Fil^i_N Δ̂_S into d^i Δ̂_S, and (Δ̂_S, φ, Fil^•_N) satisfies Δ̂_S/Fil^1_N ≅ S and gr^i_N Δ̂_S ≅ Fil_i Δ̄_S{i} via φ/d^i. (4) (Recognition in the key case) Let R = Z_p[ζ_{p^∞}]^∧ with prism (A, ([p]_q)) and S = R⟨X^{1/p^∞}⟩/(X). Let D be a derived (p, [p]_q)-complete, (p, [p]_q)-completely flat A-algebra with an endomorphism φ_D over φ_A and an A-algebra map A⟨Y^{1/p^∞}⟩ → D commuting with the Frobenius lifts (φ(Y^{1/p^n}) = Y^{1/p^{n−1}}), such that the image of Y^p lies in [p]_q D. Then there is a unique map Δ_S → D of A⟨Y^{1/p^∞}⟩-algebras commuting with φ, and it is an isomorphism if and only if it is one after derived reduction modulo (p, [p]_q). Export. These statements, with PR.3/nygaard-key-case, PR.3/nygaard-regular-semiperfectoid, PR.3/nygaard-graded-pieces and PR.3/nygaard-completion, are the prismatic input of BS22 Theorem 13.1: the identification of (Δ̂_S, φ, Fil^•_N) with π_0 TC^-(S; Z_p), its cyclotomic Frobenius and the Nygaard filtration of BMS2, and likewise BS22 Proposition 15.7 for π_0 TP(S/S[u]; Z_p) and the Nygaard completion of Δ^{(1)}_{S/𝔖}. Those identifications are proved in RefinedTraceMethods:RT.6, which imports this node; they are not asserted here.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** S is quasiregular semiperfectoid; d is the image of a generator of ker θ for a perfectoid ring mapping to S. The node contains no statement about topological Hochschild homology and has no trace-theoretic prerequisite. In the proof of BS22 Theorem 13.1 the inputs from BMS2 (the non-completed theory of Construction 7.12 with its Nygaard filtration, the Hodge–Tate comparison from the Segal conjecture, Corollary 9.12, and the characteristic p comparison, Theorem 8.17) belong to RefinedTraceMethods:RT.6; the steps planned here are the lemma, the extension of the δ-structure, and the construction of the comparison map from the q-divided power structure. The interface entry for this node described it as the identification with π_0 TC^-(S; Z_p); the stage edge PR.3 → RT.6 makes RT.6 the owner of that identification, and the node is sharpened accordingly. In (1) the case i = 1 is empty of content: (d, p)^0 Δ_S = Δ_S.

**Construction or proof.**

1. (1): choose a surjection S′ = R⟨X_a^{1/p^∞}, Y_b^{1/p^∞}⟩/(X_a) → S inducing a surjection on cotangent complexes, hence on Δ and on every Fil^i_N (PR.3/nygaard-graded-pieces); reduce to S′, absorb the Y_b into R, pass to finitely many X_a by filtered colimits and to one variable by the Künneth formula (PR.2/kunneth-formula, PR.3/nygaard-regular-semiperfectoid (5)), using that the claim is stable under products: for x ∈ Fil^j_N, y ∈ Fil^k_N the formula δ(xy) = x^pδ(y) + y^pδ(x) + pδ(x)δ(y) and φ = x^p + pδ(x) give δ(xy) ∈ Fil^{p(j+k)}_N + (d, p)^{j+k−1}.
2. In one variable (PR.3/nygaard-key-case) the filtration is generated multiplicatively by [p]_{q^{1/p}} ∈ Fil^1_N, where the claim is empty, and by Y^i/[i]_q! ∈ Fil^i_N, where δ of the element is homogeneous of degree pi and every homogeneous element of degree pi lies in Fil^{pi}_N.
3. (2): gr^i_N Δ_S ≅ Fil_i Δ̄_S{i} semilinearly (PR.3/nygaard-graded-pieces), and Fil_i Δ̄_S is derived p-complete and p-completely flat over S, hence classically p-adically complete; φ(d) is a unit multiple of p modulo d. (3): by (1), δ is continuous for the topology of (2), so it extends to the completion (the extension of a δ-structure to a completion by PR.3/delta-nygaard-continuity); the remaining assertions are PR.3/nygaard-completion.
4. (4): BS22 Lemma 12.5 (PR.3/nygaard-key-case (b)) applied to D and x = Y gives Y^n/[n]_q! ∈ D, and the basis of PR.3/nygaard-key-case (d) gives the map, unique because D is [n]_q-torsion-free; both sides are derived (p, [p]_q)-complete, so derived Nakayama applies.
5. For a general perfectoid base first apply André’s root cover of PR.3/nygaard-regular-semiperfectoid to reach the cyclotomic key case. Check the inclusion of Nygaard ideals on the explicit q-divided-power generators there and descend the inclusion along the completely faithfully flat map; the one-variable calculation by itself is only cyclotomic.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/nygaard-completion`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-3-nygaard-completion); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/nygaard-graded-pieces`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-3-nygaard-graded-pieces); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/nygaard-key-case`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-3-nygaard-key-case); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/nygaard-regular-semiperfectoid`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-3-nygaard-regular-semiperfectoid); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/nygaard-filtration-qrsp`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-3-nygaard-filtration-qrsp); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/kunneth-formula`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-kunneth-formula); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/qrsp-prism`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-qrsp-prism); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-classical-completion`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-delta-classical-completion); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-frobenius-dictionary`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-delta-frobenius-dictionary); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/delta-nygaard-continuity`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-3-delta-nygaard-continuity).

**Acceptance.** S perfectoid: Δ̂_S = A_inf(S) with its δ-structure; (1) reads δ(e^i A) ⊂ e^{pi}A + (d, p)^{i−1}A. Key case: δ(Y^i/[i]_q!) is homogeneous of degree pi. (4) with D = Δ_S gives the identity; with D the non-completed ring of BMS2 it gives the comparison map of the proof of Theorem 13.1. Consumer: RefinedTraceMethods:RT.6 (Theorem 13.1, Proposition 15.7, and through them the identification of the BMS2 syntomic complexes with those of PR.4).

**Sources.** [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Lemma 13.2 and its proof. <a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-3-nygaard-hodge-comparison"></a>

### Comparison of the Nygaard filtration with the Hodge filtration of derived de Rham cohomology

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/nygaard-hodge-comparison` · theorem. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.Nygaard` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/Nygaard/Hodge`.

Let (A, I) be a bounded prism, Ā = A/I, and R an animated commutative Ā-algebra. (1) (Bockstein and de Rham complex) Let β : H^n(gr^n_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A}) → H^{n+1}(gr^{n+1}_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A}) be the boundary map of gr^{n+1}_N → Fil^n_N/Fil^{n+2}_N → gr^n_N. Then (⊕_n H^n(gr^n_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A}), β) is a commutative differential graded algebra and there is a unique isomorphism of commutative differential graded algebras θ onto the p-completed de Rham complex (Ω̂^•_{R/Ā}, d) that in degree 0 is the isomorphism H^0(gr^0_N) ≅ H^0(R̂). (2) There is a canonical map of commutative algebra objects of DF(A), Fil^•(γ_R) : Fil^•_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} → Fil^•_Hodge dR^∧_{R/Ā}, to the p-completed derived de Rham complex with its Hodge filtration, determined by functoriality in R and by gr^0(γ_R) being the isomorphism gr^0_N ≅ R̂ ≅ gr^0_Hodge. (3) There is a functorial fibre sequence in DF(A): I ⊗^L_A Fil^{•−1}_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} → Fil^•_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} → Fil^•_Hodge dR^∧_{R/Ā}, the first map being the multiplication v of PR.3/relative-nygaard-filtration and the second Fil^•(γ_R). In filtration degree 0 it is the de Rham comparison PR.3/de-rham-comparison-general (3). (4) Consequently Ā ⊗^L_A lim_m Fil^m_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} ≅ lim_m Fil^m_Hodge dR^∧_{R/Ā}; and if the p-completion of R is p-completely smooth of relative dimension ≤ d over Ā then v : I ⊗^L_A Fil^n_N → Fil^{n+1}_N is an isomorphism for n ≥ d, so Fil^n_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} ≅ I^{⊗(n−d)} ⊗_A Fil^d_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} for n ≥ d.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** (A, I) bounded prism; R animated Ā-algebra; dR^∧_{R/Ā} and its Hodge filtration are those of DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.2, p-completed; for p-completely smooth R they are the p-completed de Rham complex with its stupid filtration. In (1) the de Rham complex is that of π_0(R) relative to Ā, and Ω̂^n is H^0 of the derived p-completion of Ω^n_{π_0(R)/Ā} (Bhatt–Lurie's convention; it need not be p-adically separated and agrees with the classical completion when Ω^n has bounded p^∞-torsion). In the proof of BL22 Corollary 5.2.8 the Hodge–Tate comparison is printed gr_n^conj Δ̄_{R/A}{n} ≃ LΩ̂^n_{R/Ā}[n]; the shift is [−n] (source issue PrismaticCohomology/E35). The fibre sequence compares three filtrations at once: on graded pieces it reads Fil_{n−1}^conj Δ̄{n} → Fil_n^conj Δ̄{n} → gr_n^conj Δ̄{n} ≅ LΩ̂^n_{R/Ā}[−n].

**Construction or proof.**

1. (1): H^n(gr^n_N) ≅ H^n(Fil_n^conj Δ̄{n}) ≅ Ω̂^n_{R/Ā} by PR.3/relative-nygaard-graded-pieces and the connectivity of the conjugate filtration; the Bockstein is identified with d on polynomial algebras through the Hodge–Tate comparison (PR.1/hodge-tate-comparison-map), hence in general; uniqueness because the de Rham complex is generated in degree 0 (BL22 Proposition 5.2.2).
2. (2): left Kan extend from polynomial algebras, where Fil^•_Hodge is the object (Ω̂^{≥ •}, d) of the heart of the Beilinson t-structure and Fil^•_N is Beilinson connective (PR.3/relative-nygaard-graded-pieces (5)), so maps Fil^•_N → Fil^•_Hodge are maps of complexes H^0_B(Fil^•_N) = (⊕ H^n(gr^n_N), β) → (Ω̂^•, d); take θ (BL22 Proposition 5.2.3).
3. (3): the composite Fil^•(γ) ∘ v is canonically null because I ⊗ Fil^{•−1}_N lies in DF^{≤ −1} and the target in the heart, on polynomial algebras; the induced map from the cofibre of v to Fil^•_Hodge is an isomorphism in degrees ≤ 0 by PR.3/de-rham-comparison-general (3) and on graded pieces by the Hodge–Tate comparison, hence in all degrees by induction (BL22 Corollary 5.2.8).
4. (4): take limits in (3) (BL22 Corollary 5.2.9); for smooth R of dimension ≤ d, Fil^{n}_Hodge = Ω̂^{≥ n} vanishes for n > d (BL22 Corollary 5.2.15).
5. Identify γ_R under Fil_N=τ_B^(≤0)(I^•Δ) with the map τ_B^(≤0)→H_B^0. Its reduction modulo I in filtration degree zero is exactly the canonical Lη_I reduction of BMS1 Proposition 6.12 followed by the Hodge–Tate identification, not merely some isomorphism of the same objects. Derived Nakayama therefore applies to this specified map.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/relative-nygaard-filtration`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-3-relative-nygaard-filtration); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/relative-nygaard-graded-pieces`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-3-relative-nygaard-graded-pieces); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/de-rham-comparison-general`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-3-de-rham-comparison-general); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/hodge-tate-comparison-map`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-hodge-tate-comparison-map); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/derived-hodge-tate-comparison`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-derived-hodge-tate-comparison); `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.2`; `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`.

**Acceptance.** R = Ā: the sequence is I ⊗ I^{n−1} → I^n → 0 for n ≥ 1 and I ⊗ A → A → Ā for n = 0. Crystalline prism (Z_p, (p)) and R regular Noetherian over F_p: the sequence is p · N^{n−1}WΩ → N^nWΩ → Ω^{≥ n}, the defining property of Nygaard's filtration on the de Rham–Witt complex. R p-completely smooth of dimension d: the Nygaard filtration is I-adic from degree d on.

**Sources.** [BL22](https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.06120v1), Construction 5.2.1, Propositions 5.2.2 and 5.2.3. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed pages 119, 120. parts (1), (2). [BL22](https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.06120v1), Corollaries 5.2.8, 5.2.9, 5.2.15.  parts (3), (4).

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-3-nygaard-completeness"></a>

### Completeness of the Nygaard filtration: exact statements

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/nygaard-completeness` · theorem. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.Nygaard` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/Nygaard/Completion`.

(1) (Criterion) For a prism (B, J): c : B → B̂ is injective iff ∩_i Fil^i_N B = 0, and bijective iff moreover lim^1_i Fil^i_N B = 0; for a filtered object, M → M̂ is an isomorphism iff lim_i Fil^i = 0. (2) (Perfectoid rings) If S is perfectoid then Δ_S = A_inf(S) is Nygaard-complete: Fil^i_N = (e^i) with e = φ^{-1}(d), and A_inf(S) is e-adically complete. (3) (Relative criterion, Bhatt–Lurie Corollary 5.2.10) For a bounded prism (A, I) and an animated A/I-algebra R: φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} is Nygaard-complete if and only if the p-completed derived de Rham complex dR^∧_{R/(A/I)} is Hodge-complete (lim_m Fil^m_Hodge = 0). (4) (Smooth case, Corollary 5.2.11) If R is p-completely flat over A/I and R/pR is a filtered colimit of smooth (A/I)/p-algebras, in particular if R is p-completely smooth, then φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} is Nygaard-complete; if R is p-completely smooth of relative dimension ≤ d then moreover Fil^n_N = I^{⊗(n−d)} ⊗ Fil^d_N for n ≥ d. (5) (Perfect base) For a perfect prism (A, I) and a derived p-complete simplicial A/I-algebra S: Δ_{S/A} is Nygaard-complete for the filtration of PR.3/nygaard-filtration iff dR^∧_{S/(A/I)} is Hodge-complete. In particular Δ_S ≠ Δ̂_S for S = F_p[X^{1/p^∞}]/(X) (PR.3/nygaard-incomplete-example). (6) (Exhaustiveness) The Nygaard filtration is exhaustive in the trivial sense Fil^0_N = Δ; the non-trivial exhaustiveness statement is PR.3/nygaard-frobenius-colimit.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** Completeness always refers to the Nygaard filtration; all objects are already derived (p, I)-complete. In (3), (4) the filtration is the relative one on the Frobenius twist; in (2), (5) the base prism is perfect and the filtration is on Δ itself. Hodge-completeness of derived de Rham cohomology is a property owned by DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.2; for p-completely smooth R the Hodge filtration is the finite stupid filtration. BL22 Remark 5.8.4 prints Fil^n ≃ I^{n−d} Fil^{n−d}; the correct right-hand side is I^{n−d} ⊗ Fil^d (source issue PrismaticCohomology/E36); (4) states the relative form.

**Construction or proof.**

1. (1): the Milnor sequence for the tower Fil^i_N B: 0 → lim Fil^i → B → lim B/Fil^i → lim^1 Fil^i → 0.
2. (2): φ is bijective, so Fil^i_N = φ^{-1}(d^i A) = (e^i) (PR.3/nygaard-filtration-qrsp); A_inf(S) is classically (p, d)-complete, e^p ≡ d modulo p, so it is derived e-complete and e-adically separated, hence e-adically complete.
3. (3): PR.3/nygaard-hodge-comparison (4) gives A/I ⊗^L_A lim_m Fil^m_N ≅ lim_m Fil^m_Hodge; lim_m Fil^m_N is derived I-complete, so it vanishes iff its reduction does. (4): for such R the Hodge filtration of dR^∧ is the stupid filtration of the p-completed de Rham complex (DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.2), which is complete; the last assertion is PR.3/nygaard-hodge-comparison (4); for smooth R completeness also follows from PR.3/leta-frobenius-factorisation (3).
4. (5): for a perfect prism φ_A^* is an equivalence carrying Fil^•_N Δ_{S/A} to Fil^•_N φ_A^*Δ_{S/A} (PR.3/relative-nygaard-filtration); apply (3).

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/nygaard-completion`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-3-nygaard-completion); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/nygaard-hodge-comparison`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-3-nygaard-hodge-comparison); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/leta-frobenius-factorisation`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-3-leta-frobenius-factorisation); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/relative-nygaard-filtration`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-3-relative-nygaard-filtration); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/nygaard-filtration-qrsp`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-3-nygaard-filtration-qrsp); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/nygaard-filtration`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-3-nygaard-filtration); `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.2`; [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/perfect-prisms-perfectoid-rings`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-perfect-prisms-perfectoid-rings).

**Acceptance.** (Z_p, (p)), S = F_p: Δ = Z_p, Fil^i = (p^i), complete. R = A/I⟨T⟩: complete, with Fil^n_N = I^{n−1} ⊗ Fil^1_N for n ≥ 1. S = F_p[X^{1/p^∞}]/(X): dR^∧_{S/F_p} is the divided power algebra with its divided power filtration, which is not complete; correspondingly Δ_S ≠ Δ̂_S. The statement of BS22 Theorem 13.1 involves Δ̂_S and not Δ_S for exactly this reason.

**Sources.** [BL22](https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.06120v1), Corollaries 5.2.9, 5.2.10, 5.2.11.  parts (3), (4). [BL22](https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.06120v1), Example 5.8.1 and Proposition 5.8.2. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 147. the failure of completeness for a quasiregular semiperfect ring, part (5). [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), the warning after Definition 12.1. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 86. the caution behind (1).

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-3-nygaard-frobenius-colimit"></a>

### Prismatic cohomology as the completed colimit of the Nygaard pieces

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/nygaard-frobenius-colimit` · theorem. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.Nygaard` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/Nygaard/Hodge`.

Let (A, I) be a bounded prism and R an animated commutative A/I-algebra. The maps v : I ⊗^L_A Fil^m_N → Fil^{m+1}_N of PR.3/relative-nygaard-filtration give a diagram φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} → I^{−1} ⊗ Fil^1_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} → I^{−2} ⊗ Fil^2_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} → ⋯, and the maps I^{−m} ⊗ Fil^m(φ) : I^{−m} ⊗ Fil^m_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} → Δ_{R/A} are compatible with it. (1) The induced map from the (p, I)-completed colimit of this diagram to Δ_{R/A} is an isomorphism: the relative Frobenius exhibits Δ_{R/A} as the completed union of the twisted Nygaard pieces. (2) If the p-completion of R is p-completely smooth of relative dimension ≤ d, the diagram is constant from m = d on and Fil^m(φ) : Fil^m_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} → I^{⊗ m} ⊗_A Δ_{R/A} is an isomorphism for every m ≥ d. (3) Consequently for X smooth over A/I of dimension ≤ d and i ≥ d, RΓ(X_qsyn, Fil^i_N Δ^{(1)}_{−/A}) ≅ RΓ_Δ(X/A) ⊗_A I^{⊗ i}.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** (A, I) bounded prism; R animated A/I-algebra; I^{−m} is the dual of I^{⊗ m}. The colimit is formed in the (p, I)-complete derived category of A. BS22 states (3) for the Nygaard-completed sheaf; by PR.3/nygaard-completeness (4) completion changes nothing for smooth X.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Both sides of (1) commute with filtered (indeed sifted) colimits in R, so R may be taken a polynomial algebra in d variables.
2. By PR.3/nygaard-hodge-comparison (4) the diagram is constant for m ≥ d. It remains to see that Fil^d(φ) : Fil^d_N → I^d ⊗ Δ is an isomorphism; by derived Nakayama and the same result it suffices that gr^d(φ) : gr^d_N → Δ̄{d} is one.
3. By PR.3/relative-nygaard-graded-pieces, gr^d(φ) is the inclusion Fil_d^conj Δ̄{d} → Δ̄{d}, an isomorphism because gr_n^conj Δ̄ ≅ (∧^n L)[−n]^∧{−n} vanishes for n > d and the conjugate filtration is exhaustive (PR.2/derived-hodge-tate-comparison).
4. (3): apply (2) on affines and glue (BS22, the paragraph after Proposition 15.7).

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/relative-nygaard-filtration`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-3-relative-nygaard-filtration); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/relative-nygaard-graded-pieces`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-3-relative-nygaard-graded-pieces); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/nygaard-hodge-comparison`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-3-nygaard-hodge-comparison); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/derived-hodge-tate-comparison`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-derived-hodge-tate-comparison).

**Acceptance.** R = A/I (d = 0): Fil^m_N = I^m and I^{−m} ⊗ I^m = A = Δ for all m. Perfect prism and S perfectoid: e^{−m}(e^m) = A_inf(S). After inverting I the relative Frobenius φ_A^*Δ_{R/A}[1/I] → Δ_{R/A}[1/I] is an isomorphism for smooth R, in agreement with PR.3/image-of-frobenius.

**Sources.** [BL22](https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.06120v1), Corollary 5.2.16 and its proof. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 123. parts (1), (2). [BL22](https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.06120v1), Corollary 5.2.15. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 123. the constancy of the diagram for smooth algebras. [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), §15.2, the paragraph after Proposition 15.7. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 105. part (3), stated there for the completed sheaf.

<a id="pr-5"></a>

## PR.5. Absolute prismatics and geometric coefficient packages

The absolute site varies the bounded prism and the map to the formal scheme. Its category, functoriality and opposite convention are fixed before crystals are used. Generalized Cartier divisors and Cartier–Witt divisors define WCart, with local principalization preceding its quotient presentation. Generic stack and QCoh machinery is imported, while formal QCoh and classifying stacks for the infinite groups have explicit supplier gaps. The Hodge–Tate gerbe, cyclotomic chart and triangular Sen calculation control absolute comparison and Nygaard graded pieces. PR.3 supplies prism twists; this layer owns absolute cohomology, its filtration and absolute Frobenius. For every integer n the canonical e^n lies in H⁰(gr⁰_NΔ_R{n}); it gives periodicity of the graded pieces. Completed filtered Frobenius has ideal index •−n.

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-5-absolute-prismatic-site"></a>

### The absolute prismatic site of a p-adic formal scheme

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.5/absolute-prismatic-site` · definition. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.Absolute` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/Absolute/Site`.

Let X be a p-adic formal scheme. The absolute prismatic site X_Δ is the opposite of the category whose objects are triples (A, I, u), with (A, I) a bounded prism and u : Spf(A/I) → X a morphism of p-adic formal schemes (A/I carries the p-adic topology), and whose morphisms (A, I, u) → (B, J, v) are the maps of prisms f : (A, I) → (B, J) with u ∘ Spf(f mod I) = v. The flat topology on X_Δ is generated by the finite families {(A, I, u) → (A_s, I_s, u_s)}_s of maps of prisms over X for which A → ∏_s A_s is (p, I)-completely faithfully flat. The structure sheaf is O_Δ(A, I, u) = A, with its δ-structure and Frobenius φ; the prism-ideal sheaf (the ideal sheaf of the Hodge–Tate divisor) is I_Δ(A, I, u) = I ⊂ A; the reduced structure sheaf is Ō_Δ(A, I, u) = A/I = O_Δ/I_Δ. For all integers m, n the presheaf (A, I, u) ↦ I^m ⊗_A A{n} is a sheaf with values in the p-complete derived ∞-category D̂(Z_p), and RΓ^{site,[m]}_Δ(X){n} denotes the limit of I^m{n} over the category of triples (A, I, u). Comparison with relative sites: if X lies over Spf(A/I) for a bounded prism (A, I), the relative site (X/A)_Δ is the category of objects (B, J, v) of X_Δ together with a map of prisms (A, I) → (B, J) such that v lies over Spf(B/J) → Spf(A/I); the forgetful functor (X/A)_Δ → X_Δ carries covers to covers and O_Δ, I_Δ, Ō_Δ to the relative sheaves. If (A, I) is a perfect prism this functor is an equivalence (X/A)_Δ ≃ X_Δ.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** X is a p-adic formal scheme; Bhatt–Lurie assume in addition that X is bounded (locally Spf of a p-complete ring with bounded p-power torsion) wherever the site computes cohomology. Every prism in the site is bounded; the convention is that of Bhatt–Scholze (the site is the opposite category), while Bhatt–Lurie write (X)_Δ for the category of triples itself and put the topology on its opposite. Register entry PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22/E5: for a semiperfectoid ring the category having an initial object consists of all prisms, not only bounded ones; the absolute site here always uses bounded prisms. Complete flatness and the complete derived category are those of DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Category: triples (A, I, u) with the maps of prisms of PR.0/prism-category compatible with the structure maps; composition and identities are those of prisms (Bhatt–Scholze F-crystals, Definition 2.3; Bhatt–Lurie, Definition 4.4.27).
2. Topology and sheaves: covers are tested on underlying prisms, so O_Δ and Ō_Δ are sheaves with vanishing higher Čech cohomology by PR.1/prismatic-structure-sheaf (Bhatt–Scholze, Corollary 3.12); I_Δ = I is a sheaf because I ⊗_A B = IB for a map of prisms (PR.0/rigidity-prism-ideal); I^m{n} is a sheaf by completely faithfully flat descent for invertible modules and the base-change compatibility of the twists A{n} of PR.3/breuil-kisin-twist (Bhatt–Lurie, Remark 4.4.28).
3. Relative comparison: unwind Bhatt–Lurie Definition 4.1.1 against Definition 4.4.27; for a perfect prism every ring map A/I → B/J lifts uniquely to a map of prisms (A, I) → (B, J) (the lemma inside Bhatt–Scholze Remark 4.7), which gives the equivalence.
4. Repleteness of the topos Shv(X_Δ), so that derived limits behave well: Bhatt–Scholze F-crystals, Remark 2.4, with the replete topoi of EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E2.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/prism`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-prism); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/prism-category`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-prism-category); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/rigidity-prism-ideal`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-rigidity-prism-ideal); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/perfect-prisms-perfectoid-rings`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-perfect-prisms-perfectoid-rings); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/prismatic-structure-sheaf`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-prismatic-structure-sheaf); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/relative-prismatic-site`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-relative-prismatic-site); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/breuil-kisin-twist`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-3-breuil-kisin-twist); `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`; `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E2/replete-topoi`; [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/perfect-prism-initial`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-perfect-prism-initial).

**Consumers.** Bhatt–Lurie, Theorem 4.4.30: absolute prismatic cohomology of a p-quasisyntomic formal scheme is the cohomology of this site with coefficients in I^m{n}. Bhatt–Lurie, Remark after Proposition 3.3.5: quasi-coherent complexes on the Cartier–Witt stack are crystals of complete complexes on (Spf Z_p)_Δ. PrismaticCohomology:PR.7 (prismatic F-crystals): vector bundles and perfect complexes over O_Δ, O_Δ[1/I_Δ] on X_Δ are the crystals of that layer. PrismaticCohomology:PR.4 (syntomic complexes): the sheaves I_Δ^m{n} are the coefficients of the absolute theory from which Z_p(n) is built.

**Planning API.**

- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Absolute.SiteObj` (structure): An object of (Spf R)_Δ: a ring A with a prism structure (A, I), boundedness of A/I, and a ring map R → A/I.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Absolute.SiteObj.Hom` (structure): A morphism (A, I, u) → (B, J, v): a map of prisms whose reduction carries u to v.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Absolute.SiteObj.ofPrism` (constructor): The tautological object (A, I, id) of (Spf A/I)_Δ attached to a bounded prism.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Absolute.SiteObj.idealSheaf` (data): The value I of the prism-ideal sheaf I_Δ on an object; the quotient of the structure sheaf by it is the reduced sheaf.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Absolute.RelativeObj` (compatibility): An object of the relative site (R/A)_Δ is an object of (Spf R)_Δ with a map of prisms from (A, I) compatible with the structure maps.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Absolute.SiteObj.existsUnique_hom_of_perfect` (universal-property): For a perfect prism (A, I), every object of (Spf A/I)_Δ receives a unique morphism from (A, I, id); hence (X/A)_Δ ≃ X_Δ for X over A/I.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Absolute.SiteObj.category` (structure): Triples (A,I,f:Spf(A/I)→X) form a category with δ-ring prism maps and commuting triangles over X; identities and composition are inherited from prism maps. The site X_Δ is its opposite category.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Absolute.SiteObj.map` (functoriality): A map g:Y→X gives Y_Δ→X_Δ by composing Spf(A/I)→Y with g. It preserves finite jointly completely faithfully flat covers, commutes with O_Δ and its reduction, and obeys identity and composition laws.

**Unit tests.**

- `pr5_site_perfect_initial` (characterisation): For a perfect prism (A,I), the triple (A,I,id) is initial in the category of triples of Spf(A/I), hence final in its opposite prismatic site: every site object has exactly one arrow to it.
- `pr5_site_char_p_crystalline` (computation): If R has characteristic p then every object (A, I, u) of (Spf R)_Δ has I = (p).
- `pr5_site_structure_map_matters` (non-example): A prism endomorphism of (A, I) that does not induce the identity on A/I is not a morphism of the object (A, I, id) of (Spf A/I)_Δ: the site is not the category of all bounded prisms.

**Acceptance.** For a quasiregular semiperfectoid ring R the site (Spf R)_Δ has a final object, the prism (Δ_R, I) of PR.2/qrsp-prism (Bhatt–Scholze F-crystals, Example 2.5; Bhatt–Lurie, Example 4.4.29). For X = Spf(O_K), K a complete discretely valued field of mixed characteristic with perfect residue field, the Breuil–Kisin prism (W(k)[[u]], (E(u))) and the A_inf-prism of O_C are objects of X_Δ that cover the final object (Bhatt–Scholze F-crystals, Example 2.6). For an F_p-algebra R every object (A, I, u) of (Spf R)_Δ is crystalline: I = (p).
