<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-5-absolute-relative-comparison"></a>

### Absolute versus relative prismatic cohomology

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.5/absolute-relative-comparison` · theorem. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.Absolute` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/Absolute/Relative`.

Let (B, J) be a bounded prism with B̄ = B/J and let R be an animated commutative ring. (1) By construction ρ_B^* H_Δ(R) = Δ_{(B̄ ⊗^L R)/B} in D̂(B), compatibly with maps of bounded prisms. If R is an animated B̄-algebra, the multiplication B̄ ⊗^L R → R induces ξ : H_Δ(R) → ρ_{B*} Δ_{R/B} in D(WCart) and, on global sections, comparison maps Δ_R^{[m]}{n} → J^m ⊗ Δ_{R/B}{n} for all integers m, n; for X over B̄ these give RΓ_Δ^{[m]}(X){n} → J^m{n} ⊗^L_B RΓ_Δ(X/B). (2) If (B, J) is a perfect prism, ξ is an isomorphism H_Δ(R) ≅ ρ_{B*} Δ_{R/B}; hence Δ_R^{[m]}{n} ≅ J^m Δ_{R/B}{n} for all m, n, RΓ_Δ^{[m]}(X){n} ≅ J^m{n} ⊗^L_B RΓ_Δ(X/B) for X over B̄, and H_Δ(𝔛) ≅ ρ_{B*} RΓ_Δ(𝔛/B) for a bounded qcqs p-adic formal scheme 𝔛 over B̄. (3) For a quasiregular semiperfectoid ring R: Δ_R is concentrated in degree 0, (Δ_R, Δ_R^{[1]}) is a prism, equal to the initial prism of R, and H_Δ(R) is the pushforward of the structure sheaf along Spf(Δ_R) → WCart. For a prism that is not perfect the maps in (1) are not isomorphisms in general: the pullback ρ_B^* H_Δ(R) is the relative complex of B̄ ⊗^L R, not of R.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** (1) holds for every bounded prism; the isomorphisms of (2) require the prism to be perfect. R is an animated algebra over B̄ = B/J in (2); no finiteness or completeness hypothesis. The comparison is not an isomorphism for every bounded prism: for a bounded prism only the identity ρ_B^* H_Δ(R) = Δ_{(B̄ ⊗^L R)/B} holds.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Fix a nonzero transversal prism (A, I) (the q-de Rham prism); ρ_A is faithfully flat (wcart-fibre-products-of-prisms), so it suffices to prove that ρ_A^*(ξ) is an isomorphism.
2. With (C, K) = (A, I) ⊔ (B, J) and Spf(C) = Spf(A) ×_{WCart} Spf(B), base change for ρ_{B*} identifies ρ_A^*(ξ) with the composite Δ_{(Ā ⊗^L R)/A} → Δ_{(C̄ ⊗^L R)/C} → Δ_{(C̄ ⊗^L_{B̄} R)/C}.
3. This composite is the base change of Δ_{(Ā ⊗^L B̄)/A} → Δ_{C̄/C} = C along Δ_{(Ā ⊗^L B̄)/A} → Δ_{(Ā ⊗^L R)/A}: the squares are pushouts of commutative algebras by base change (PR.1/prismatic-base-change) and the Künneth formula (PR.2/kunneth-formula).
4. Δ_{(Ā ⊗^L B̄)/A} ≅ C by relative-site-comparison (4) (Bhatt–Lurie, Example 4.3.15, Proposition 4.4.8). (2) follows by tensoring with I^m{n}, the projection formula and global sections (Proposition 4.4.12); (3) is Example 4.4.13 with PR.2/qrsp-prism.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.5/absolute-prismatic-cohomology`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-5-absolute-prismatic-cohomology); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.5/relative-site-comparison`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-5-relative-site-comparison); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.5/wcart-fibre-products-of-prisms`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-5-wcart-fibre-products-of-prisms); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.5/transversal-prism-coproducts`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-5-transversal-prism-coproducts); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.5/quasi-coherent-complexes-on-wcart`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-5-quasi-coherent-complexes-on-wcart); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.5/prismatic-crystals-on-wcart`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-5-prismatic-crystals-on-wcart); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/derived-prismatic-base-change`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-derived-prismatic-base-change); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/kunneth-formula`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-kunneth-formula); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/qrsp-prism`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-qrsp-prism); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/perfect-prisms-perfectoid-rings`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-perfect-prisms-perfectoid-rings); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/q-de-rham-prism`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-q-de-rham-prism).

**Acceptance.** For a perfect field k and a k-scheme X: RΓ_Δ(X) ≅ RΓ_Δ(X/W(k)). For O_C and a formal scheme 𝔛 over O_C: RΓ_Δ(𝔛) ≅ RΓ_Δ(𝔛/A_inf), with the prism of PR.0/ainf-prism. For the Breuil–Kisin prism (W(k)[[u]], (E)) and R = O_K the comparison map Δ_{O_K} → Δ_{O_K/W(k)[[u]]} = W(k)[[u]] is not claimed to be an isomorphism.

**Sources.** [BL22](https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.06120v1), Propositions 4.4.8 and 4.4.12 with their proofs. <a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-5-absolute-prismatic-descent"></a>

### Descent and continuity properties of absolute prismatic cohomology

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.5/absolute-prismatic-descent` · theorem. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.Absolute` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/Absolute/Cohomology`.

Fix integers m, n. (1) The functor R ↦ Δ_R^{[m]}{n} from animated commutative rings to D̂(Z_p) satisfies descent for the étale topology, and X ↦ RΓ_Δ^{[m]}(X){n} satisfies étale descent. (2) Derived descent: for every animated ring R, with R^• = R ⊗^L F_p^{⊗•+1}, the map Δ_R^{[m]}{n} → Tot Δ_{R^•}^{[m]}{n} is an isomorphism; each R^k is an animated F_p-algebra. (3) Δ_R^{[m]}{n} ≅ lim_k Δ^{[m]}_{(Z/p^k) ⊗^L R}{n}. (4) Δ_R^{[m]}{n} ≅ Δ_{R̂}^{[m]}{n} for the derived p-completion R̂ of R. (5) If X is a scheme whose structure sheaf has bounded p-power torsion and 𝔛 = Spf(Z_p) × X is its p-adic formal scheme, then RΓ_Δ^{[m]}(X){n} ≅ RΓ_Δ^{[m]}(𝔛){n}; for a ring R with bounded p-power torsion, Δ_R^{[m]}{n} ≅ RΓ_Δ^{[m]}(Spf R̂){n}. (6) On the category of p-quasisyntomic p-adic formal schemes the functor 𝔛 ↦ RΓ_Δ^{[m]}(𝔛){n} satisfies descent for the p-quasisyntomic topology. The functor R ↦ Δ_R does not commute with filtered colimits as a functor to D̂(Z_p).

**Hypotheses and conventions.** (1)–(4) hold for all animated commutative rings. (5) requires bounded p-power torsion; (6) is stated on p-quasisyntomic formal schemes: affine opens Spf R with R p-complete, of bounded p-power torsion, and L_{R/Z_p} ⊗^L R/p of Tor-amplitude in [−1, 0]. Descent is for D̂(Z_p)-valued functors: limits are p-completed derived limits.

**Construction or proof.**

1. (1): étale descent of R ↦ H_Δ(R) in D(WCart) follows from that of the relative complexes (relative-site-comparison (1)); tensoring with the invertible sheaf I^m{n} and taking global sections preserves limits (Bhatt–Lurie, Remark 4.4.3, Proposition 4.4.14, Remark 4.4.22).
2. (2): H_Δ(R) ≅ Tot H_Δ(R^•) by the relative statement over every prism (relative-site-comparison (1), which rests on faithful flatness of F on W^×), then global sections (Remark 4.4.4, Proposition 4.4.15).
3. (3), (4), (5): by (2) reduce to algebras over F_p ⊗^L Z, where the towers {Z/p^k ⊗^L R} and {R/p^k} are pro-constant or pro-isomorphic; combine with étale descent and the description of a formal scheme as the colimit of its reductions (Corollaries 4.4.17, 4.4.18, Proposition 4.4.25, Corollary 4.4.26).
4. (6): étale descent reduces to affines; for a p-quasisyntomic cover R → R⁰ with Čech nerve R^•, H_Δ(R) ≅ Tot H_Δ(R^•) by the relative quasisyntomic descent of relative-site-comparison applied over each transversal prism; tensor with I^m{n} and take global sections (Proposition 4.4.32).

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.5/absolute-prismatic-cohomology`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-5-absolute-prismatic-cohomology); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.5/relative-site-comparison`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-5-relative-site-comparison); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.5/divided-power-multiplicative-group`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-5-divided-power-multiplicative-group); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.5/quasi-coherent-complexes-on-wcart`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-5-quasi-coherent-complexes-on-wcart); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/quasisyntomic-descent`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-quasisyntomic-descent); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/kunneth-formula`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-kunneth-formula); `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.5`; `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E2/hypercovers-and-cohomological-descent`; `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E5:animation/animated-commutative-rings`.

**Acceptance.** Δ_R = 0 when p is invertible in R; Δ_{Z[1/N]} ≅ Δ_Z for N prime to p. Δ_R ≅ Tot of the derived crystalline cohomology of the animated F_p-algebras R ⊗^L F_p^{⊗k+1}. Quasisyntomic test: for R p-quasisyntomic with a quasiregular semiperfectoid cover R → S, Δ_R is the totalization of the cosimplicial ring Δ_{S^•}.

**Sources.** [BL22](https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.06120v1), Propositions 4.4.14 and 4.4.15, Corollaries 4.4.17 and 4.4.18. <a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-5-frobenius-pullback-square"></a>

### The Frobenius pullback square for global sections on WCart

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.5/frobenius-pullback-square` · theorem. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.WCart` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/WCart/Frobenius`.

Let E be a quasi-coherent complex on the Cartier–Witt stack WCart. The commutative square of stacks formed by WCart^HT ⊂ WCart, F : WCart → WCart, WCart^HT → Spf(Z_p) and ρ_dR induces a pullback square in D̂(Z_p): RΓ(WCart, E) is the fibre product of RΓ(WCart, F^* E) and RΓ(Spf Z_p, ρ_dR^* E) over RΓ(WCart^HT, (F^* E)|_{WCart^HT}). Moreover (F^* E)_η ≅ ρ_dR^* E with trivial Sen operator, so RΓ(WCart^HT, (F^* E)|_{WCart^HT}) ≅ ρ_dR^* E ⊕ ρ_dR^* E[−1] and there is a fibre sequence RΓ(WCart, E) → RΓ(WCart, F^* E) → ρ_dR^* E[−1]. Consequently the functor (F^*, ρ_dR^*) : D(WCart) → D(WCart) ×_{D(WCart^HT)} D(Spf Z_p) is fully faithful; it is not an equivalence.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** E is a quasi-coherent complex on WCart; Bhatt–Lurie Theorem 3.6.7 prints "on the Cartier–Witt stack WCart^HT", a misprint (source issue PrismaticCohomology/E52): the square involves RΓ(WCart, E), F^* E and ρ_dR^* E. The square is a pullback in the p-complete derived category D̂(Z_p). No hypothesis on p.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Reduction to the Hodge–Tate divisor: E is the limit of the E/I^n E, so by induction it suffices to treat E = ι_* G with G ∈ D(WCart^HT) (Bhatt–Lurie, proof of Theorem 3.6.7).
2. Transversality (Remark 3.6.20): the squares relating WCart^HT, F^{−1}WCart^HT and WCart^HT × Spec F_p are pushouts of animated rings on the Čech nerve, because I^n ⊂ A^n stays injective after base change along φ_{A^n} for the transversal prisms A^n (Bhatt–Lurie, Lemma 2.2.1); this identifies the square for ι_* G with one on F^{−1}WCart^HT.
3. The square on F^{−1}WCart^HT (Lemma 3.6.19): by colimit-preservation of global sections and generation by twists (sen-operator-classification) reduce to G = O{n}; the cases are settled by Lemmas 3.6.15–3.6.17 and Proposition 3.6.18, which says that F^* : H^1(WCart^HT, O) → H^1(F^{−1}WCart^HT, O) is the inclusion pZ_p ⊂ Z_p.
4. Fibre sequence: Proposition 3.6.6 gives (F^* E)_η ≅ ρ_dR^* E with trivial Sen operator and the fibre sequence of sen-operator-classification splits (Remark 3.6.8). Full faithfulness: reduce to Hom(I^n, −) by generation of D(WCart) by the I^n and twist (Corollary 3.6.9); failure of essential surjectivity is Warning 3.6.11.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.5/wcart-frobenius`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-5-wcart-frobenius); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.5/sen-operator-classification`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-5-sen-operator-classification); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.5/sen-operator`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-5-sen-operator); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.5/hodge-tate-divisor`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-5-hodge-tate-divisor); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.5/quasi-coherent-complexes-on-wcart`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-5-quasi-coherent-complexes-on-wcart); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.5/prismatic-crystals-on-wcart`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-5-prismatic-crystals-on-wcart); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.5/wcart-fibre-products-of-prisms`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-5-wcart-fibre-products-of-prisms); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.5/prism-point-of-wcart`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-5-prism-point-of-wcart); `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`; [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/transversal-prism`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-3-transversal-prism).

**Acceptance.** For E = O_WCart: a fibre sequence RΓ(WCart, O) → RΓ(WCart, O) → Z_p[−1] whose first map is the Frobenius. For E the prismatic cohomology sheaf of R twisted by n: the pullback square of Bhatt–Lurie Corollary 5.4.14 with corner the p-completed derived de Rham complex.

**Sources.** [BL22](https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.06120v1), Theorem 3.6.7 with its proof, Remark 3.6.8, Corollary 3.6.9 and Warning 3.6.11. <a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-5-absolute-site-comparison"></a>

### Absolute prismatic cohomology as cohomology of the absolute prismatic site

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.5/absolute-site-comparison` · comparison. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.Absolute` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/Absolute/Site`.

Let 𝔛 be a bounded p-adic formal scheme. For integers m, n let RΓ^{site,[m]}_Δ(𝔛){n} be the limit of I^m{n} over the category of triples (A, I, u) of the absolute prismatic site, formed in D̂(Z_p); it is RΓ(𝔛_Δ, I_Δ^m{n}). For every object (A, I, u), restriction along u gives RΓ_Δ^{[m]}(𝔛){n} → RΓ_Δ^{[m]}(Spf A/I){n} ≅ Δ_Ā^{[m]}{n} → I^m{n} ⊗^L_A Δ_{Ā/A} = I^m{n}, and in the limit a comparison map ξ : RΓ_Δ^{[m]}(𝔛){n} → RΓ^{site,[m]}_Δ(𝔛){n}. Theorem: if for every affine open Spf(R) ⊂ 𝔛 the ring R is p-quasisyntomic, then ξ is an isomorphism in D̂(Z_p) for all m, n. In particular RΓ_Δ(𝔛) ≅ RΓ(𝔛_Δ, O_Δ) compatibly with the E_∞-algebra structures. Supplements: 𝔛 ↦ RΓ^{site,[m]}_Δ(𝔛){n} satisfies p-quasisyntomic descent on all bounded p-adic formal schemes; for R quasiregular semiperfectoid the category of triples has the initial object (Δ_R, Δ_R^{[1]}) (a final object of the site) and both sides are I^m{n} of it.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** 𝔛 is bounded and every affine open is the formal spectrum of a p-quasisyntomic ring; quasi-compactness is not needed. Without the quasisyntomic hypothesis ξ is still defined, and it is not claimed to be an isomorphism: the animated theory and the underived site cohomology of a general formal scheme differ. Smooth formal schemes over Spf Z_p, Spf W(k) or Spf O_K satisfy the hypothesis.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Quasiregular semiperfectoid case: by absolute-relative-comparison (3) and PR.2/qrsp-prism the site (Spf R)_Δ has the initial object (Δ_R, Δ_R^{[1]}), so the limit is evaluation there (Bhatt–Lurie, Example 4.4.29).
2. The site-theoretic side is a p-quasisyntomic sheaf: for a cover 𝔛_0 → 𝔛 the totalization over the Čech nerve is the limit over the triples whose structure map factors through 𝔛_0, a covering sieve for the flat topology by the lifting of quasisyntomic covers to flat covers of prisms in PR.2/quasisyntomic-descent (Bhatt–Scholze, Proposition 7.11; Bhatt–Lurie, Proposition 4.4.31).
3. The stack-theoretic side is a p-quasisyntomic sheaf on p-quasisyntomic formal schemes by absolute-prismatic-descent (6).
4. Quasiregular semiperfectoid rings form a basis of the p-quasisyntomic topology (DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.5), so the two sheaves agree (proof of Theorem 4.4.30).

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.5/absolute-prismatic-site`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-5-absolute-prismatic-site); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.5/absolute-prismatic-cohomology`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-5-absolute-prismatic-cohomology); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.5/absolute-relative-comparison`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-5-absolute-relative-comparison); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.5/absolute-prismatic-descent`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-5-absolute-prismatic-descent); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/qrsp-prism`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-qrsp-prism); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/quasisyntomic-descent`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-quasisyntomic-descent); `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.5`; `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`; [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/quasisyntomic-covers-lift-to-prisms`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-quasisyntomic-covers-lift-to-prisms).

**Acceptance.** For 𝔛 = Spf(O_K): RΓ_Δ(Spf O_K) is the cohomology of the structure sheaf of (Spf O_K)_Δ, computed by the Čech nerve of the Breuil–Kisin prism. For R = Z_p[x_1, …, x_d]^∧ the absolute prismatic complex is the limit of A over all bounded prisms (A, I) with a map R → A/I. For 𝔛 = Spf(R) with R quasiregular semiperfectoid both sides are Δ_R.

**Sources.** [BL22](https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.06120v1), Theorem 4.4.30 with its proof, Example 4.4.29. ### Absolute Hodge–Tate cohomology and the diffracted Hodge complex

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.5/absolute-hodge-tate-cohomology` · construction. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.Absolute` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/Absolute/HodgeTate`.

Let R be an animated commutative ring. The Hodge–Tate cohomology sheaf H_Δ̄(R) ∈ D(WCart^HT) is the object given on bounded prisms by (A, I) ↦ Δ̄_{(Ā ⊗^L R)/A} ∈ D̂(Ā); it equals ι^* H_Δ(R). It carries the conjugate filtration Fil_n^conj H_Δ̄(R), given by (A, I) ↦ Fil_n^conj Δ̄_{(Ā ⊗^L R)/A}: an exhaustive increasing filtration with Fil_0^conj = R ⊗ O_{WCart^HT} and graded pieces gr_n^conj H_Δ̄(R) ≅ LΩ^n_R ⊗ O_{WCart^HT}{−n}[−n]. The absolute Hodge–Tate complexes are Δ̄_R{n} = RΓ(WCart^HT, H_Δ̄(R){n}) ∈ D̂(R), with Δ̄_R = Δ̄_R{0}, and Fil_m^conj Δ̄_R{n} = RΓ(WCart^HT, Fil_m^conj H_Δ̄(R){n}), whose colimit over m is Δ̄_R{n}. For all m, n there is a fibre sequence I^{m+1} ⊗ H_Δ(R){n} → I^m ⊗ H_Δ(R){n} → ι_*(H_Δ̄(R){m+n}) in D(WCart), and on global sections Δ_R^{[m+1]}{n} → Δ_R^{[m]}{n} → Δ̄_R{m+n}. Thus Δ_R^{[•]}{n} is a filtered object of D̂(Z_p) with gr^m = Δ̄_R{m+n}; it is filtration-complete, and R ↦ Δ_R^{[•]}{n}, as a functor to filtration-complete p-complete filtered complexes, commutes with sifted colimits, as do R ↦ Fil_m^conj Δ̄_R{n} and R ↦ Δ̄_R{n}. The p-complete diffracted Hodge complex is Ω̂^DHod_R = η^* H_Δ̄(R) ∈ D̂(R), with conjugate filtration Fil_n^conj Ω̂^DHod_R = η^* Fil_n^conj H_Δ̄(R), graded pieces LΩ̂^n_R[−n], and Sen operator Θ acting by −n on gr_n^conj; Fil_n^conj Ω̂^DHod_R lies in D^{≤n}. For every n there is a canonical isomorphism Δ̄_R{n} ≅ fib(Θ + n : Ω̂^DHod_R → Ω̂^DHod_R), and likewise for each step of the conjugate filtration. If (A, I) is a perfect prism and R an animated Ā-algebra, then Δ̄_R{n} ≅ Δ̄_{R/A}{n}.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** R is an arbitrary animated commutative ring; LΩ^n_R is the n-th derived exterior power of the cotangent complex of R over Z, and LΩ̂^n_R its p-completion (DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.0). Corrected misprint (source issue PrismaticCohomology/E58): the graded pieces of the diffracted Hodge complex are LΩ̂^n_R[−n]; the display in Bhatt–Lurie Construction 4.7.1 omits the shift. Δ̄_R is not the reduction of Δ_R modulo an ideal; it is the first graded piece of the filtration Δ_R^{[•]}. The Hodge-completed and derived de Rham theories are owned by DerivedDeRhamCohomology and are not constructed here.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Sheaf and conjugate filtration: the relative conjugate filtration of PR.2/derived-hodge-tate-comparison is compatible with base change, so it defines filtered objects of D(WCart^HT) ≃ lim D̂(A/I) (sen-operator; Bhatt–Lurie, Construction 4.5.1, Remarks 4.5.2–4.5.4); the graded pieces use A{1}/I ≅ I/I² (PR.3/breuil-kisin-twist).
2. Global sections commute with the colimit over the conjugate filtration because RΓ(WCart^HT, −) preserves colimits (sen-operator-classification (4)); this also gives the sifted-colimit statements (Bhatt–Lurie, Construction 4.5.5, Propositions 4.5.8 and 4.5.10).
3. Fibre sequence: tensor I → O_WCart → ι_* O_{WCart^HT} with I^m ⊗ H_Δ(R){n} and use ι^* I^m ≅ O_{WCart^HT}{m} (Remark 4.5.7); completeness of Δ_R^{[•]}{n}: the limit of I^m ⊗ H_Δ(R) vanishes because every ρ_A^* of it is I-adically complete.
4. Diffracted Hodge complex and the fibre formula: apply the fibre sequence of sen-operator-classification (2) to H_Δ̄(R){n}, whose Sen operator on the fibre is Θ + n (Bhatt–Lurie, Construction 4.7.1, Notation 4.7.2, Remarks 4.7.3 and 4.7.5). Perfect prism: Example 4.5.6, from absolute-relative-comparison.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.5/absolute-prismatic-cohomology`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-5-absolute-prismatic-cohomology); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.5/absolute-relative-comparison`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-5-absolute-relative-comparison); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.5/sen-operator`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-5-sen-operator); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.5/sen-operator-classification`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-5-sen-operator-classification); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.5/hodge-tate-divisor`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-5-hodge-tate-divisor); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.5/quasi-coherent-complexes-on-wcart`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-5-quasi-coherent-complexes-on-wcart); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.5/prismatic-crystals-on-wcart`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-5-prismatic-crystals-on-wcart); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/hodge-tate-cohomology`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-hodge-tate-cohomology); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/derived-hodge-tate-comparison`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-derived-hodge-tate-comparison); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/breuil-kisin-twist`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-3-breuil-kisin-twist); `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.0`; `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`.

**Consumers.** Bhatt–Lurie, Remark 5.5.8: the graded pieces of the absolute Nygaard filtration are fibres of Θ + m on the conjugate filtration of the diffracted Hodge complex. Bhatt–Lurie, Theorem 4.6.1: the characterising square of the crystalline comparison ends in absolute Hodge–Tate cohomology. PrismaticCohomology:PR.4: the graded pieces Δ̄{m+n} of Δ^{[•]}{n} control the syntomic complexes. RefinedTraceMethods:RT.6: the diffracted Hodge complex is the associated graded of the motivic filtration on p-completed Hochschild homology (Bhatt–Lurie §6), which that roadmap owns.

**Planning API.**

- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Absolute.hodgeTateSheaf` (data): H_Δ̄(R) = ι^* H_Δ(R) ∈ D(WCart^HT).
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Absolute.absoluteHodgeTate` (data): Δ̄_R{n} = RΓ(WCart^HT, H_Δ̄(R) ⊗ O{n}).
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Absolute.diffractedHodge` (data): Ω̂^DHod_R = η^* H_Δ̄(R), with its Sen operator given by senOperator.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Absolute.diffractedHodgeFil` (data): The conjugate filtration Fil_i^conj Ω̂^DHod_R with its maps to Ω̂^DHod_R.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Absolute.absolutePrismatic_fibre_sequence` (relation): The fibre sequence Δ_R^{[m+1]}{n} → Δ_R^{[m]}{n} → Δ̄_R{m+n}.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Absolute.absoluteHodgeTate_fibre_sequence` (characterisation): The fibre sequence Δ̄_R{n} → η^*(H_Δ̄(R){n}) → η^*(H_Δ̄(R){n}) whose second map is the Sen operator, that is Θ + n on Ω̂^DHod_R.

**Unit tests.**

- `pr5_ht_integers_h1` (computation): H^1(Δ̄_Z) ≅ Z_p.
- `pr5_ht_integers_twist_h0` (non-example): H^0(Δ̄_Z{n}) = 0 for n ≠ 0: the twist cannot be ignored.
- `pr5_ht_sheaf_integers` (degenerate): H_Δ̄(Z) is the unit object of D(WCart^HT).
- `pr5_ht_diffracted_integers` (degenerate): Ω̂^DHod_Z is Z_p in degree 0.

**Acceptance.** Δ̄_Z = RΓ(WCart^HT, O) = Z_p ⊕ Z_p[−1], and Δ̄_Z{n} ≅ (Z_p/n)[−1] for n ≠ 0. For a perfectoid ring R the complex Ω̂^DHod_R is the coordinate ring of the G_m^♯-torsor of the Hodge–Tate point of R, concentrated in degree 0. For R p-torsion-free with R/pR regular Noetherian the conjugate filtration of Ω̂^DHod_R is its Postnikov filtration.

**Sources.** [BL22](https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.06120v1), Constructions 4.5.1 and 4.5.5, Remark 4.5.7, Propositions 4.5.8 and 4.5.10. <a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-5-absolute-crystalline-comparison"></a>

### Absolute prismatic cohomology in characteristic p is crystalline cohomology

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.5/absolute-crystalline-comparison` · theorem. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.Absolute` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/Absolute/Comparison`.

Let X be a quasisyntomic F_p-scheme. There is a canonical isomorphism γ : RΓ_Δ(X) ≅ RΓ_crys(X/Z_p) of commutative algebra objects of D̂(Z_p), characterised up to homotopy by functoriality in X and by the commutativity of the square whose top row is RΓ_crys(X/Z_p) → RΓ_Δ(X) → RΓ_Δ(X) (γ^{−1} followed by the Frobenius φ), whose left side is the crystalline augmentation ε_crys : RΓ_crys(X/Z_p) → RΓ(X, O_X), whose bottom row is RΓ(X, O_X) ≅ Fil_0^conj RΓ_Δ̄(X/Z_p) → RΓ_Δ̄(X), and whose right side is the reduction RΓ_Δ(X) → RΓ_Δ̄(X). Supplements: (1) for a perfect field k and a quasisyntomic k-scheme X, RΓ_Δ(X) = RΓ_Δ(X/W(k)) and the identification with RΓ_crys(X/W(k)) is Frobenius-semilinear: RΓ_crys(X/W(k)) ≅ F^* RΓ_Δ(X/W(k)) in D(W(k)); for a perfect F_p-algebra R, under Δ_R = W(R) = A_crys(R), γ^{−1} is W(φ_R^{−1}). (2) On animated F_p-algebras R ↦ Δ_R commutes with sifted colimits and agrees with RΓ_crys(−/Z_p) on polynomial algebras: Δ_R is derived crystalline cohomology. (3) For an arbitrary F_p-scheme X there is a natural map RΓ_Δ(X) → RΓ_crys(X/Z_p), which need not be an isomorphism. (4) X ↦ RΓ_crys(X/Z_p) satisfies p-quasisyntomic descent on quasisyntomic F_p-schemes, and A_crys(R) is p-torsion-free for a quasiregular semiperfect F_p-algebra R. Here φ means the relative Frobenius over (Z_p,(p)) transported through Δ_X≃Δ_(X/Z_p); this construction uses only the relative Frobenius constructed in PR.1.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** X is a quasisyntomic F_p-scheme: Zariski-locally the spectrum of a p-quasisyntomic F_p-algebra; no quasi-compactness or smoothness is assumed. RΓ_crys(X/Z_p) is the crystalline cochain complex relative to (Z_p, (p)) of CrystallineCohomology:CR.2. The isomorphism is not linear over W(k): the Frobenius twist is the φ_A-twist of PR.1/crystalline-comparison.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Quasiregular semiperfect R: Δ_R is a p-torsion-free ring with Δ_R^{[1]} = (p) (absolute-relative-comparison (3)); the composite Δ_R → Δ_R → Δ̄_R (φ, then reduction) has image R = Fil_0^conj (PR.3/nygaard-graded-pieces) and kernel J = {x : φ(x) ∈ pΔ_R}, which has divided powers; the universal property of A_crys(R) (CrystallineCohomology:CR.0) gives β_R : A_crys(R) → Δ_R (Bhatt–Lurie, Lemma 4.6.8).
2. Globalise β to β_X : RΓ_crys(X/Z_p) → RΓ_Δ(X) for quasisyntomic X by quasisyntomic descent of RΓ_Δ and RΓ_Δ̄ (absolute-prismatic-descent (6); Corollary 4.6.10).
3. β_R is an isomorphism for R quasiregular semiperfect: modulo p, β̄_R carries γ_{pn}(x) into Fil_n^conj with leading term λ(n) γ_n(x̄), λ(n) ∈ F_p^×, by an eigenvalue computation on k[x^{1/p^∞}]/(x); with the surjection Γ^*_R(I/I²) → gr^conj(A_crys(R)/p) and the Hodge–Tate comparison this shows gr(β̄_R) is an isomorphism (Lemmas 4.6.11, 4.6.13; conjugate filtration of A_crys/p from CrystallineCohomology:CR.4; DD.4 supplies its derived de Rham reduction modulo p).
4. General X: Zariski-locally X = Spec R; choose a polynomial algebra P ↠ R, let P⁰ be its perfection and R^• = P^• ⊗_P R, whose terms are quasiregular semiperfect; both sides descend along R → R^• (crystalline descent to semiperfect rings from CR.4 (BL Proposition F.4); absolute-prismatic-descent (6)) (proof of Theorem 4.6.1). The supplements are Warning 4.6.2, Example 4.6.9, Remarks 4.6.5 and 4.6.6, Corollaries 4.6.7 and 4.6.15.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.5/absolute-prismatic-cohomology`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-5-absolute-prismatic-cohomology); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.5/absolute-relative-comparison`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-5-absolute-relative-comparison); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.5/absolute-prismatic-descent`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-5-absolute-prismatic-descent); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.5/absolute-hodge-tate-cohomology`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-5-absolute-hodge-tate-cohomology); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/crystalline-comparison`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-crystalline-comparison); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/qrsp-prism`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-qrsp-prism); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/derived-hodge-tate-comparison`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-derived-hodge-tate-comparison); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/nygaard-graded-pieces`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-3-nygaard-graded-pieces); `CrystallineCohomology:CR.0`; `CrystallineCohomology:CR.2`; `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.4`; `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.5`; [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/frobenius-on-prismatic-cohomology`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-frobenius-on-prismatic-cohomology); `CrystallineCohomology:CR.4`.

**Acceptance.** For a smooth F_p-scheme the isomorphism is the case A = Z_p of PR.1/crystalline-comparison. For R = F_p[x^{1/p^∞}]/(x): Δ_R ≅ A_crys(R), the p-completed divided power envelope of (x) in W(F_p[x^{1/p^∞}]). For R perfect, Δ_R = W(R) and the comparison is the inverse Witt vector Frobenius.

**Sources.** [BL22](https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.06120v1), Theorem 4.6.1 with its proof, Lemmas 4.6.8, 4.6.11 and 4.6.13. <a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-5-cyclotomic-hodge-tate-chart"></a>

### Cyclotomic chart and its Hodge–Tate torsor

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.5/cyclotomic-hodge-tate-chart` · construction. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/PR5`.

Write q=1+t and p̃=∑_(e∈F_p)q^[e] in Z_p[[t]], where [e] is the Teichmüller representative. Then (p̃)=([p]_q), Z_p[[t]]^(F_p^×)=Z_p[[p̃]], and (Z_p[[p̃]],(p̃)) is a transversal prism. Its Hodge–Tate point is isomorphic to the canonical point η:Spf Z_p→WCart^HT. Choosing this isomorphism trivializes the G_m^♯-torsor after every perfect-prism base change; choices differ by G_m^♯(Z_p)=(1+pZ_p)^×.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** The F_p^× action is through Teichmüller units by q↦q^u. The torsor trivialization is a choice, not a canonical identity. The chart and torsor identification work also at p=2; the separate fully faithful quotient calculation of BL Theorem 3.8.3 requires odd p and is not asserted here.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Each q^[e] differs from q^e by a multiple of q^p−1; therefore p̃=[p]_q(1+t f) with the last factor a unit.
2. Invariants under F_p^× are exact because p−1 is invertible. Modulo p̃ they are Z_p, and completeness gives Z_p[[p̃]] (BL Corollary 3.8.8).
3. The Witt lift of the cyclotomic quotient sends p̃ to V(1): applying F gives p and p-torsion-freeness forces the coefficient to be 1. Descend the resulting Hodge–Tate-point isomorphism under F_p^× (BL Proposition 3.8.12).
4. Base change the isomorphism to a perfect prism; the Hodge–Tate gerbe description and G_m^♯ classify its trivialization and ambiguity.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/q-de-rham-prism`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-q-de-rham-prism); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.5/prism-point-of-wcart`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-5-prism-point-of-wcart); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.5/hodge-tate-divisor`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-5-hodge-tate-divisor); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.5/divided-power-multiplicative-group`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-5-divided-power-multiplicative-group); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.5/absolute-hodge-tate-cohomology`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-5-absolute-hodge-tate-cohomology).

**Consumers.** PR.5/perfect-prism-sen-calculation: Trivializes the G_m^♯ torsor so the Sen operator is explicit..

**Planning API.**

- `TauCeti.Prismatic.WCart.cyclotomicChart` (constructor): Construct the invariant prism with ideal (p̃) and its map to the q-de Rham prism.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.WCart.cyclotomicHTTrivialization` (compatibility): A choice of the Hodge–Tate-point isomorphism yields a G_m^♯-equivariant identification of each base-changed torsor with G_m^♯; choices form a torsor under G_m^♯(Z_p).
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.WCart.cyclotomicChart_ideal` (characterisation): The Cartier ideal on the invariant coefficient chart Z_p[[p̃]] is (p̃). Under its map to Z_p[[q−1]], this ideal becomes ([p]_q); the Hodge–Tate fibre sets [p]_q=0 and the de Rham fibre sets q−1=0.

**Unit tests.**

- `pr5_cyclotomic_two` (computation): p=2 gives p̃=[2]_q.
- `pr5_cyclotomic_three` (computation): p=3 gives p̃=q^(-1)[3]_q, so the ideals agree.
- `pr5_cyclotomic_not_unique` (non-example): The Hodge–Tate trivialization is ambiguous by G_m^♯(Z_p); treating it as unique discards its automorphisms.

**Acceptance.** At p=2, p̃=1+q=[2]_q. At p=3, p̃=1+q+q^(-1)=q^(-1)[3]_q. A chosen torsor trivialization changes under multiplication by a G_m^♯ point; no uniqueness is claimed.

**Prototype boundary.** `TauCeti.Prismatic.WCart.cyclotomicHTTrivialization` needs its supplier carrier: D0 supplies the G_m^sharp gerbe and its torsor actions; SF.1 supplies the base-changed torsor carrier. The coefficient-ring chart above is not this equivariant gerbe trivialization.

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-5-absolute-de-rham-comparison"></a>

### The absolute de Rham comparison and the de Rham point

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.5/absolute-de-rham-comparison` · theorem. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.Absolute` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/Absolute/Comparison`.

Let R be an animated commutative ring, R̄ = F_p ⊗^L R, and let dR̂_R be the p-complete derived de Rham complex of R (over Z) with its Hodge filtration. (1) There is a canonical isomorphism α_R : ρ_dR^* H_Δ(R) ≅ dR̂_R in D̂(Z_p), functorial in R and characterised by the requirement that α_R ⊗ O_{WCart^HT} is the isomorphism (F^* H_Δ(R))|_{WCart^HT} ≅ dR̂_R ⊗ O_{WCart^HT} obtained from the relative de Rham comparison Ā ⊗^L_A F^* Δ_{R′/A} ≅ dR̂_{R′/Ā} over all bounded prisms and from F ∘ ι ≅ ρ_dR ∘ (WCart^HT → Spf Z_p). (2) Consequently Δ_{R̄} ≅ dR̂_R as commutative algebra objects of D̂(Z_p), functorially in R. (3) The de Rham comparison map γ^dR{n} : Δ_R{n} → dR̂_R is the restriction to the de Rham point composed with α_R, using the trivialisation of ρ_dR^* O_WCart{n} by the generator e^n of Z_p{n}; the prismatic augmentation ε_Δ : Δ_R → R̂ is γ^dR followed by dR̂_R → gr^0_Hodge = R̂. (4) For every n the square with corners Δ_R{n}, dR̂_R, RΓ(WCart, F^*(H_Δ(R){n})) and dR̂_R ⊗̂ RΓ(WCart^HT, O) is a pullback square, and there is a fibre sequence Δ_R{n} → RΓ(WCart, F^*(H_Δ(R){n})) → dR̂_R[−1]. (5) For a p-adic formal scheme 𝔛 flat over Spf Z_p with regular Noetherian special fibre X, RΓ_crys(X/Z_p) ≅ RΓ_dR(𝔛) (Berthelot).

**Hypotheses and conventions.** R is an arbitrary animated commutative ring; dR̂_R is the p-completed derived de Rham complex, not Hodge-completed, owned by DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.2. Corrected misprint (new source issue to be registered): in Bhatt–Lurie Corollary 5.4.14 the source of γ^dR{n} is Δ_R{n}. (5) needs flatness over Z_p and a regular Noetherian special fibre, for example 𝔛 smooth over Spf W(k).

**Construction or proof.**

1. ρ_dR^* H_Δ(R) = Δ_{R̄/Z_p} by construction, and Δ_{R̄/Z_p} ≅ Δ_{R̄} because (Z_p, (p)) is perfect (absolute-relative-comparison; Bhatt–Lurie, Example 5.4.5).
2. The isomorphism on the Hodge–Tate divisor: F^* H_Δ(R) pulls back to F^* Δ_{(Ā ⊗^L R)/A}, whose reduction modulo I is the derived de Rham complex by PR.3/de-rham-comparison-general in its animated form (Bhatt–Lurie, Proposition 5.2.5), compatibly in the prism; combine with wcart-frobenius (Construction 5.4.7, Remark 5.4.6).
3. Descent of the isomorphism to the de Rham point: the composite ρ_dR^* H_Δ(R) → dR̂_R ⊗̂ RΓ(WCart^HT, O) = dR̂_R ⊕ dR̂_R[−1] has second component functorially null: the source is left Kan extended from p-torsion-free p-quasisyntomic rings, the target is right Kan extended from quasiregular semiperfectoid rings (quasisyntomic descent of dR̂ from DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.5), and for such rings both are concentrated in degree 0 (Proposition 5.4.8).
4. (4): apply frobenius-pullback-square to E = H_Δ(R){n} and insert (1) (Corollary 5.4.14, Remark 5.4.15). (5): combine (2) with absolute-crystalline-comparison and the comparison of derived and classical de Rham complexes of DD.2 (the Remark after Theorem 5.4.2).

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.5/absolute-prismatic-cohomology`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-5-absolute-prismatic-cohomology); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.5/absolute-relative-comparison`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-5-absolute-relative-comparison); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.5/frobenius-pullback-square`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-5-frobenius-pullback-square); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.5/wcart-frobenius`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-5-wcart-frobenius); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.5/sen-operator-classification`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-5-sen-operator-classification); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.5/prismatic-crystals-on-wcart`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-5-prismatic-crystals-on-wcart); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.5/absolute-crystalline-comparison`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-5-absolute-crystalline-comparison); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/de-rham-comparison-general`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-3-de-rham-comparison-general); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/relative-nygaard-filtration`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-3-relative-nygaard-filtration); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/breuil-kisin-twist`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-3-breuil-kisin-twist); `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.2`; `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.5`; `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E5:animation/universal-property-of-animation`.

**Acceptance.** For R = Z_p[x_1, …, x_d]^∧: Δ_{F_p[x_1, …, x_d]} ≅ the p-completed de Rham complex of R. For R = Z: ρ_dR^* O_WCart = Z_p = dR̂_Z and the fibre sequence of (4) is RΓ(WCart, O) → RΓ(WCart, O) → Z_p[−1]. For a perfectoid ring Ā = A/I the prismatic augmentation Δ_Ā = A → Ā is φ followed by the quotient map.

**Sources.** [BL22](https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.06120v1), Theorem 5.4.2, Proposition 5.4.8 with its proof, Constructions 5.4.7, 5.4.9 and 5.4.10. [BL22](https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.06120v1), Corollary 5.4.14 and Remark 5.4.15. <a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-5-perfect-prism-sen-calculation"></a>

### Sen calculation over the cyclotomic chart

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.5/perfect-prism-sen-calculation` · lemma. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/PR5`.

For a perfect prism (A,I) with a prism map from (Z_p[[p̃]],(p̃)), put R=A/I. The map (Θ+m,ξ):Fil_m^conj Ω̂_R^D→Fil_(m−1)^conj Ω̂_R^D⊕R is an isomorphism for every m≥0, where ξ is the relative-prismatic evaluation. Both sides are free R-modules of rank m+1.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** Use the torsor trivialization supplied by cyclotomic-hodge-tate-chart. Fil_(−1)^conj=0; no odd-prime restriction is added.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Trivialize Ω̂_R^D as R⊗̂O(G_m^♯). Put γ_n=(1−t^(-1))^n/n! in this coordinate description.
2. The completed expansion ∑c_nγ_n has coefficients tending p-adically to zero; Θ sends it to ∑(c_(n+1)−nc_n)γ_n and ξ takes c_0.
3. Induct using the rank-one conjugate graded pieces to identify Fil_m^conj with the span of γ_0,…,γ_m.
4. In descending bases the map is triangular with diagonal entries 1, hence invertible over R. This is the calculation that proves BL Proposition 5.6.8.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.5/cyclotomic-hodge-tate-chart`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-5-cyclotomic-hodge-tate-chart); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.5/absolute-hodge-tate-cohomology`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-5-absolute-hodge-tate-cohomology); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.5/sen-operator`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-5-sen-operator).

**Acceptance.** For m=0 the map is ξ:R→R. For m=1 its determinant is 1, including at p=2.

**Sources.** [BL22](https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.06120v1), Lemma 5.6.14 and proof, §5.6. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 142. Lemma 5.6.14 and proof, pp.142–143; its use in the proof of Proposition 5.6.8 on p.144. Explicit divided-power coordinates give the invertible Sen/evaluation matrix..

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-5-absolute-nygaard-filtration"></a>

### The absolute Nygaard filtration

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.5/absolute-nygaard-filtration` · construction. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.Absolute` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/Absolute/Nygaard`.

Let R be an animated commutative ring and n an integer. (a) For a bounded prism (A, I) the relative Nygaard filtration Fil^m_N F^* Δ_{(Ā ⊗^L R)/A} is compatible with completed base change in the prism, so it defines a decreasing filtered object Fil^•_N F^* H_Δ(R) of D(WCart) with Fil^0_N = F^* H_Δ(R). (b) There is a fibre sequence of filtered objects I ⊗ Fil^{•−1}_N F^* H_Δ(R) → Fil^•_N F^* H_Δ(R) → ι_*(Fil^•_Hodge dR̂_R ⊗ O_{WCart^HT}). (c) Put Fil^•_N F^*(H_Δ(R){n}) = Fil^•_N F^* H_Δ(R) ⊗ F^* O_WCart{n}; since F^* O_WCart{n} ≅ I^{−n} O_WCart{n} is canonically trivial on WCart^HT, (b) gives a map RΓ(WCart, Fil^•_N F^*(H_Δ(R){n})) → Fil^•_Hodge dR̂_R ⊗̂ RΓ(WCart^HT, O). (d) The absolute Nygaard filtration Fil^•_N Δ_R{n} is the fibre product, in the filtered derived category of p-complete complexes, of RΓ(WCart, Fil^•_N F^*(H_Δ(R){n})) and Fil^•_Hodge dR̂_R over Fil^•_Hodge dR̂_R ⊗̂ RΓ(WCart^HT, O). Then Fil^0_N Δ_R{n} = Δ_R{n}, Fil^0_N Δ_R{n} → Fil^m_N Δ_R{n} is an isomorphism for m ≤ 0, and the projection Fil^•(γ^dR{n}) : Fil^•_N Δ_R{n} → Fil^•_Hodge dR̂_R is the filtered de Rham specialisation. (e) There is a fibre sequence of filtered complexes Fil^•_N Δ_R{n} → RΓ(WCart, Fil^•_N F^*(H_Δ(R){n})) → Fil^•_Hodge dR̂_R[−1]. (f) ⊕_n Fil^•_N Δ_R{n} is a graded commutative algebra in filtered complexes; Fil^•_N Δ_R is a filtered E_∞-algebra and each Fil^•_N Δ_R{n} a module over it. (g) Graded pieces: gr^m_N Δ_R{n} = cofib(Fil^{m+1}_N → Fil^m_N) sits in a fibre sequence gr^m_N Δ_R{n} → Fil_m^conj Ω̂^DHod_R → Fil_{m−1}^conj Ω̂^DHod_R whose second map is Θ + m; there is a unique class e^n ∈ H^0(gr^0_N Δ_R{n}) with image 1 in H^0(gr^0_Hodge dR̂_R), and multiplication by e^n is an isomorphism gr^m_N Δ_R ≅ gr^m_N Δ_R{n}. (h) For a scheme, formal scheme or stack X, Fil^m_N RΓ_Δ(X){n} is the limit of Fil^m_N Δ_R{n} over the points Spec R → X. (i) The Nygaard-completed complexes are Fil^m_N Δ̂_R{n} = lim_k Fil^m_N Δ_R{n}/Fil^{m+k}_N Δ_R{n}, with Δ̂_R{n} = Fil^0_N Δ̂_R{n}; Δ_R{n} is Nygaard-complete when lim_m Fil^m_N Δ_R{n} = 0.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** R is an arbitrary animated commutative ring; the filtration is decreasing, indexed by all integers and constant in degrees ≤ 0. The relative Nygaard filtration and its base-change compatibility are imported from PR.3/relative-nygaard-filtration; the Breuil–Kisin twists from PR.3/breuil-kisin-twist (red-team finding RT-AREA-padic-2/28). The Hodge filtration is that of the p-complete derived de Rham complex of DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.2; no Hodge completion is used in (a)–(h). Corrected misprint (source issue PrismaticCohomology/E54): in (h) the limit is over the absolute complexes Fil^m_N Δ_R{n}. Syntomic complexes built from this filtration are owned by PR.4 and are not defined here.

**Construction or proof.**

1. (a): the base-change isomorphism B ⊗̂^L_A Fil^•_N F^* Δ_{R′/A} ≅ Fil^•_N F^* Δ_{(B ⊗^L_A R′)/B} of the relative filtration (Bhatt–Lurie, Remark 5.1.10) and prismatic-crystals-on-wcart give the filtered sheaf (Notation 5.5.1).
2. (b): globalise the fibre sequence I ⊗ Fil^{•−1}_N F^* Δ_{R′/A} → Fil^•_N F^* Δ_{R′/A} → Fil^•_Hodge dR̂_{R′/Ā} (Bhatt–Lurie, Corollary 5.2.8, part of PR.3/relative-nygaard-filtration with PR.3/de-rham-comparison-general) over all bounded prisms; in filtration degree 0 it is the isomorphism of absolute-de-rham-comparison (Remark 5.5.2).
3. (c), (d), (e): twist using wcart-frobenius, take global sections, and form the pullback; in degree 0 the pullback is Δ_R{n} by absolute-de-rham-comparison (4) (Construction 5.5.3, Remark 5.5.6).
4. (f), (g): multiplicativity of the relative filtration (Remark 5.5.7); graded pieces from gr^m_N F^* H_Δ(R) ≅ ι_* Fil_m^conj H_Δ̄(R){m} and the fibre sequence of sen-operator-classification, where the Sen operator of the twist by {m} is Θ + m (Remark 5.5.8, Corollary 5.5.14, Remark 5.5.15).
5. (h), (i): Notation 5.5.23 and Definition 5.8.5; for quasiregular semiperfectoid and quasisyntomic rings the completion agrees with PR.3/nygaard-completion by absolute-nygaard-perfect-prism.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.5/absolute-de-rham-comparison`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-5-absolute-de-rham-comparison); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.5/absolute-prismatic-cohomology`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-5-absolute-prismatic-cohomology); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.5/absolute-hodge-tate-cohomology`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-5-absolute-hodge-tate-cohomology); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.5/frobenius-pullback-square`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-5-frobenius-pullback-square); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.5/wcart-frobenius`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-5-wcart-frobenius); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.5/sen-operator-classification`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-5-sen-operator-classification); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.5/prismatic-crystals-on-wcart`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-5-prismatic-crystals-on-wcart); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.5/quasi-coherent-complexes-on-wcart`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-5-quasi-coherent-complexes-on-wcart); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/relative-nygaard-filtration`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-3-relative-nygaard-filtration); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/de-rham-comparison-general`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-3-de-rham-comparison-general); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/breuil-kisin-twist`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-3-breuil-kisin-twist); `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`; `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.2`; [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/nygaard-hodge-comparison`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-3-nygaard-hodge-comparison); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/relative-nygaard-graded-pieces`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-3-relative-nygaard-graded-pieces).

**Consumers.** Bhatt–Lurie, Theorem 5.6.2 and Corollary 5.6.3: compared with the relative Nygaard filtration over a perfect prism and with the Frobenius-divisibility filtration of a quasiregular semiperfectoid ring. Bhatt–Lurie, Notation 5.7.5: the source of the Frobenius φ{n} : Fil^n_N Δ_R{n} → Δ_R{n}. PrismaticCohomology:PR.4: Z_p(n)(R) is the fibre of φ{n} − 1 on Fil^n_N Δ̂_R{n}. RefinedTraceMethods:RT.6: the Nygaard-completed absolute complexes are the graded pieces of the motivic filtration on TC^−, an identification that roadmap proves.

**Planning API.**

- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Absolute.nygaardFil` (data): Fil^m_N Δ_R{n} ∈ D(Z_p), for integers n and m.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Absolute.nygaardTransition` (data): The transition map Fil^{m+1}_N Δ_R{n} → Fil^m_N Δ_R{n}.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Absolute.nygaardFil_of_nonpos` (simp): Fil^m_N Δ_R{n} ≅ Δ_R{n} for m ≤ 0.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Absolute.nygaardGr` (data): gr^m_N Δ_R{n}, the cofibre of the transition map.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Absolute.nygaard_fibre_sequence` (relation): Fil^{m+1}_N Δ_R{n} → Fil^m_N Δ_R{n} → gr^m_N Δ_R{n} is a fibre sequence.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Absolute.nygaardGr_fibre_sequence` (characterisation): The fibre sequence gr^m_N Δ_R{n} → Fil_m^conj Ω̂^DHod_R → Fil_{m−1}^conj Ω̂^DHod_R with second map Θ + m.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Absolute.nygaardToHodge` (compatibility): The filtered de Rham specialisation Fil^m_N Δ_R{n} → Fil^m_Hodge dR̂_R.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Absolute.nygaardCompleted` (data): Δ̂_R{n}=lim_m Δ_R{n}/Fil^m_N, with its filtration, completion map and compatible canonical inclusion.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Absolute.absoluteNygaardCup` (structure): Fil^i_NΔ_R{m}⊗̂Fil^j_NΔ_R{n}→Fil^(i+j)_NΔ_R{m+n}, compatible with transitions, twists and the unit.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Absolute.absoluteNygaardMap` (functoriality): A map R→S induces a filtered map on absolute Nygaard complexes and their completions, with identity and composition laws; all inclusions and graded comparisons commute with it.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Absolute.absoluteNygaardClass` (data): For each integer n, e^n is the unique element of H⁰(gr⁰_NΔ_R{n}) whose degree-zero de Rham image is 1. These classes satisfy e^0=1 and e^m e^n=e^(m+n), commute with base change, and act by multiplication on every Nygaard graded piece. The degree-zero class is canonical; a lift to Δ_R{1} requires a cyclotomic choice.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Absolute.absoluteNygaardPeriodicity` (equivalence): For all integers m,n, multiplication by e^n gives gr^m_NΔ_R≃gr^m_NΔ_R{n}, with inverse multiplication by e^(−n). The graded degree m is independent of the twist n.

**Unit tests.**

- `pr5_nyg_fil_zero` (degenerate): Fil^0_N Δ_R{n} ≅ Δ_R{n}.
- `pr5_nyg_gr_fp` (computation): gr^m_N Δ_{F_p} ≅ F_p in degree 0 for every m ≥ 0: the filtration of Z_p by the ideals p^m Z_p.
- `pr5_nyg_gr_zero_integers` (computation): gr^0_N Δ_Z ≅ Z_p in degree 0.
- `pr5_nyg_gr_one_integers` (non-example): gr^1_N Δ_Z = 0, whereas the first graded piece of the p-adic filtration of Δ_Z is not zero.

**Acceptance.** Fil^0_N Δ_R{n} = Δ_R{n} and Δ_R/Fil^1_N Δ_R ≅ R̂ through the prismatic augmentation. For R = F_p: Fil^m_N Δ_{F_p} = p^m Z_p and gr^m_N Δ_{F_p} = F_p in degree 0. For R = Z: gr^1_N Δ_Z = 0, so the Nygaard filtration is not the p-adic filtration.

**Sources.** [BL22](https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.06120v1), Notation 5.5.1, Remark 5.5.2, Construction 5.5.3 and Remark 5.5.6. <a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-5-absolute-nygaard-graded-pieces"></a>

### Graded pieces, de Rham specialisation, descent and completeness of the absolute Nygaard filtration

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.5/absolute-nygaard-graded-pieces` · theorem. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.Absolute` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/Absolute/Nygaard`.

Let R be an animated commutative ring and m, n integers. (1) For every m ≥ 0 the map Δ_R{n}/Fil^m_N Δ_R{n} → dR̂_R/Fil^m_Hodge dR̂_R induced by the filtered de Rham specialisation is an isogeny: its fibre is annihilated by a power of p. For 0 ≤ m < p it is an isomorphism. In particular gr^m_N Δ_R ≅ LΩ̂^m_R[−m] for m < p, and Fil^1_N Δ_R → Δ_R → R̂ is a fibre sequence, the second map being the prismatic augmentation. (2) gr^m_N Δ_R{n} has cohomology in degrees ≤ m: the filtered complex Fil^•_N Δ_R{n} is connective for the Beilinson t-structure. (3) R ↦ gr^m_N Δ_R{n} commutes with sifted colimits and satisfies descent for the p-completely faithfully flat topology. R ↦ Fil^m_N Δ_R{n} satisfies étale descent on animated rings, p-quasisyntomic descent on p-quasisyntomic rings, derived descent Fil^m_N Δ_R{n} ≅ Tot Fil^m_N Δ_{R ⊗^L F_p^{⊗•+1}}{n}, and Fil^m_N Δ_R{n} ≅ lim_k Fil^m_N Δ_{(Z/p^k) ⊗^L R}{n} ≅ Fil^m_N Δ_{R̂}{n}; it does not commute with sifted colimits (already for m = 0). (4) If R is a p-torsion-free ring with R/pR regular Noetherian, then Δ_R{n} is Nygaard-complete for every n. For R = k[x^{1/p^∞}]/(x), k a perfect field of characteristic p, Δ_R is not Nygaard-complete.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** (1)–(3) hold for every animated commutative ring; (4) requires R p-torsion-free with R/pR regular Noetherian. The isomorphism range in (1) is m < p; for m ≥ p only an isogeny is claimed. The Beilinson t-structure on filtered complexes and filtration-completeness are those of DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1.

**Construction or proof.**

1. (1): the fibre of gr^m of the de Rham specialisation is (Fil_{m−1}^conj Ω̂^DHod_R)^{Θ=−m}; on gr_i^conj, i < m, the operator Θ + m is multiplication by m − i, nonzero, and a unit of Z_p when m < p; induct on m (Bhatt–Lurie, Proposition 5.5.12, Example 5.5.13, the Corollary after Warning 5.5.17).
2. (2): the fibre sequence for gr^m_N of absolute-nygaard-filtration (g) and Fil_i^conj Ω̂^DHod_R ∈ D^{≤i} (Proposition 5.5.19).
3. (3): the same fibre sequence reduces to flat descent and sifted-colimit preservation of Fil_d^conj Ω̂^DHod_R, that is of the completed derived exterior powers of the cotangent complex (DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.0 and DD.5); the statements for Fil^m follow by induction on m from absolute-prismatic-descent (Remark 5.5.10, Propositions 5.5.20 and 5.5.24, Corollaries 5.5.21, 5.5.22, 5.5.25 and 5.5.26).
4. (4): F^* H_Δ(R) is complete for its Nygaard filtration, checked on the Čech nerve A^• by the relative completeness for p-completely flat algebras with p-completely flat cotangent complex (PR.3/relative-nygaard-filtration; Bhatt–Lurie, Lemma 5.8.3); the derived de Rham complex of R is Hodge-complete because it is the completed de Rham complex with its stupid filtration (DD.2); conclude with the fibre sequence (e) (Proposition 5.8.2). The counterexample is Example 5.8.1: the series exp(x) defines an element of the completion not in A_crys(R).

### The absolute Nygaard filtration over a perfect prism, for quasiregular semiperfectoid rings and in characteristic p

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.5/absolute-nygaard-perfect-prism` · theorem. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.Absolute` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/Absolute/Nygaard`.

(1) Let (A, I) be a perfect prism, R an animated Ā-algebra and n an integer. Let Fil^•_N F^*(Δ_{R/A}{n}) be the relative Nygaard filtration of F^* Δ_{R/A} tensored with F^*(A{n}) ≅ I^{−n} A{n}. The comparison map Fil^•_N Δ_R{n} → Fil^•_N F^*(Δ_{R/A}{n}), obtained by restricting to the point ρ_A and composing with Δ_{(Ā ⊗^L R)/A} → Δ_{R/A}, is an isomorphism of filtered complexes. (2) Let R be a quasiregular semiperfectoid ring, so that (Δ_R, Δ_R^{[1]}) is a prism. For all integers m, n the map Fil^m_N Δ_R{n} → Δ_R{n} identifies Fil^m_N Δ_R{n} with the subgroup {x ∈ Δ_R{n} : φ(x) ∈ Δ_R^{[m−n]}{n}}; in particular Fil^m_N Δ_R{n} and gr^m_N Δ_R{n} are concentrated in degree 0, and for n = 0 the filtration is {x : φ(x) ∈ I^m Δ_R}, the Nygaard filtration of PR.3/nygaard-filtration-qrsp. For a p-quasisyntomic ring R the absolute Nygaard filtration is the totalization of this filtration over a quasiregular semiperfectoid Čech nerve, so it agrees with PR.3/nygaard-filtration. (3) Crystalline case, (A, I) = (Z_p, (p)) and R an F_p-algebra, where F^* is the identity: the comparison γ : Δ_{R/Z_p} → RΓ_crys(R/Z_p) carries the prismatic augmentation to the crystalline augmentation, so Fil^1_N corresponds to fib(ε_crys) when R is quasisyntomic, and the Frobenius divided by p is defined on it. For R quasiregular semiperfect, with I = ker(R^♭ → R): Fil^n_N A_crys(R) = {x : φ(x) ∈ p^n A_crys(R)} is the ideal generated by the elements p^{m_0} γ_{m_1}([x_1]) ⋯ γ_{m_k}([x_k]) with x_i ∈ I and m_0 + ⋯ + m_k ≥ n. For R a regular Noetherian F_p-algebra, γ extends to an isomorphism of filtered complexes Fil^•_N Δ_{R/Z_p} ≅ N^• WΩ_R with the Nygaard filtration of the de Rham–Witt complex.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** (1) requires (A, I) perfect; for a bounded prism only the comparison map is defined. (2): R quasiregular semiperfectoid; the index of the ideal filtration is m − n (source issue PrismaticCohomology/E51 concerns the same index in Bhatt–Lurie §5.7). (3): R an F_p-algebra; quasisyntomic, quasiregular semiperfect or regular Noetherian as stated in each assertion. The relative Nygaard filtration and the filtrations of quasiregular semiperfectoid and quasisyntomic rings are owned by PR.3; this node only compares with them.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Reduce (1) to graded pieces by induction on m, the case m = 0 being absolute-relative-comparison and bijectivity of φ_A; both gr^m_N Δ_R{n} and Fil_m^conj Δ̄_{R/A}{m} commute with sifted colimits and satisfy p-completely faithfully flat descent (absolute-nygaard-graded-pieces (3); PR.2/derived-hodge-tate-comparison), so it suffices to treat quasiregular semiperfectoid Ā-algebras admitting a map from Z_p^cyc, a basis of the quasisyntomic topology (Bhatt–Lurie, proof of Theorem 5.6.2).
2. For such R the relative filtration is {y : φ(y) ∈ I^m Δ_{R/A}} (PR.3/nygaard-filtration-qrsp), so (1) for R is equivalent to (2) for R, a statement independent of the prism; hence it suffices to prove (1) for the perfection of the q-de Rham prism, with quotient Z_p^cyc (Remark 5.6.7, Proposition 5.6.8).
3. Over Z_p^cyc reduce by sifted colimits to polynomial algebras and by induction on the number of variables to R = Z_p^cyc, where the claim is that (Θ + m, ξ) : Fil_m^conj Ω̂^DHod → Fil_{m−1}^conj Ω̂^DHod ⊕ Z_p^cyc is an isomorphism of free modules of rank m + 1, an explicit computation with the prism (Z_p[[p̃]], (p̃)) and the q-de Rham prism of PR.0 (Lemma 5.6.14).
4. (2): Corollary 5.6.3 and Corollary 5.6.4; the quasisyntomic statement by descent (absolute-nygaard-graded-pieces (3); Remark 5.6.5).
5. (3): Proposition 5.3.1 (compatibility of augmentations, by reduction to quasiregular semiperfect rings), Proposition 5.3.6 (induction on n using gr^n_N ≅ Fil_n^conj and the divided power description of gr^conj(A_crys/p)), Proposition 5.3.8 (comparison with the de Rham–Witt complex of CrystallineCohomology:CR.4, essentially Bhatt–Morrow–Scholze Theorem 8.17).
6. Use perfect-prism-sen-calculation for the kernel/cokernel computation in BL Proposition 5.6.8, then descend from the cyclotomic chart; the all-prime proof is not Theorem 3.8.3.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.5/absolute-nygaard-filtration`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-5-absolute-nygaard-filtration); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.5/absolute-nygaard-graded-pieces`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-5-absolute-nygaard-graded-pieces); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.5/absolute-relative-comparison`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-5-absolute-relative-comparison); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.5/absolute-crystalline-comparison`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-5-absolute-crystalline-comparison); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.5/absolute-hodge-tate-cohomology`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-5-absolute-hodge-tate-cohomology); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/relative-nygaard-filtration`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-3-relative-nygaard-filtration); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/nygaard-filtration-qrsp`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-3-nygaard-filtration-qrsp); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/nygaard-filtration`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-3-nygaard-filtration); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/nygaard-graded-pieces`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-3-nygaard-graded-pieces); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/derived-hodge-tate-comparison`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-derived-hodge-tate-comparison); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/q-de-rham-prism`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-q-de-rham-prism); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/prism-perfection`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-prism-perfection); `CrystallineCohomology:CR.0`; `CrystallineCohomology:CR.4`; `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.4`; `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.5`; [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.5/perfect-prism-sen-calculation`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-5-perfect-prism-sen-calculation).

**Acceptance.** For a perfectoid ring Ā = A/I: Fil^m_N Δ_Ā = φ^{−1}(I^m) ⊂ A and gr^m_N Δ_Ā is an invertible Ā-module. For R = F_p[x^{1/p^∞}]/(x): Fil^m_N Δ_R is the ideal of A_crys(R) generated by p^a x^b/b! with a + b ≥ m. For a smooth algebra R over a perfect field k the filtration is the classical Nygaard filtration of WΩ_R.

**Sources.** [BL22](https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.06120v1), Theorem 5.6.2 with its proof from Proposition 5.6.8, Construction 5.6.1, Lemma 5.6.14. ### The Frobenius on absolute prismatic cohomology

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.5/absolute-frobenius` · construction. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.Absolute` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/Absolute/Frobenius`.

Let R be an animated commutative ring. (a) Relative Frobenius: the maps Fil^•(φ) : Fil^•_N F^* Δ_{R′/A} → I^• Δ_{R′/A} of the relative theory, for R′ = Ā ⊗^L R over all bounded prisms, define a morphism of filtered objects Fil^•(Φ) : Fil^•_N F^* H_Δ(R) → I^• ⊗ H_Δ(R) of D(WCart); in degree 0 it is Φ : F^* H_Δ(R) → H_Δ(R), and gr^m(Φ) factors through an isomorphism gr^m_N F^* H_Δ(R) ≅ ι_* Fil_m^conj H_Δ̄(R){m}. Φ exhibits H_Δ(R) as the colimit of F^* H_Δ(R) → I^{−1} Fil^1_N F^* H_Δ(R) → I^{−2} Fil^2_N F^* H_Δ(R) → ⋯, with successive quotients ι_*(Fil^n_Hodge dR̂_R ⊗ O_{WCart^HT}{−n}). (b) Twisting by F^* O_WCart{n} ≅ I^{−n} O_WCart{n} gives Φ{n} : Fil^n_N F^*(H_Δ(R){n}) → H_Δ(R){n}, and the Frobenius φ{n} : Fil^n_N Δ_R{n} → Δ_R{n} is the composite of Fil^n_N Δ_R{n} → RΓ(WCart, Fil^n_N F^*(H_Δ(R){n})) with RΓ(WCart, Φ{n}). For n = 0 this is the Frobenius endomorphism φ : Δ_R → Δ_R, equal to the pullback RΓ(WCart, H_Δ(R)) → RΓ(WCart, F^* H_Δ(R)) along F followed by RΓ(WCart, Φ). (c) φ{n} refines to a map of filtered complexes Fil^•(φ{n}) : Fil^•_N Δ_R{n} → Δ_R^{[•−n]}{n}, whose graded piece gr^m_N Δ_R{n} → Δ̄_R{m} is the natural map fib(Θ + m : Fil_m^conj Ω̂^DHod_R → Fil_{m−1}^conj Ω̂^DHod_R) → fib(Θ + m on Ω̂^DHod_R). (d) If R is a p-torsion-free ring with R/pR regular Noetherian, Fil^•(φ{n}) exhibits Fil^•_N Δ_R{n} as the connective cover of Δ_R^{[•−n]}{n} for the Beilinson t-structure. (e) If R is p-completely smooth of relative dimension ≤ d over W(k), k a perfect field, then φ{n} : Fil^n_N Δ_R{n} → Δ_R{n} is an isomorphism for n > d; for R = W(k) there is a fibre sequence Δ_{W(k)} → Δ_{W(k)} → W(k)[−1] with first map φ. (f) The augmentation identity ε_Δ followed by R̂→Δ̄_R equals the absolute Frobenius followed by Δ_R→Δ̄_R; compare the de Rham-point map with the Hodge–Tate restriction after φ is constructed. (g) The filtered map factors uniquely through Nygaard completion. Thus φ̂{n}:Fil^n_NΔ̂_R{n}→Δ̂_R{n} is defined. The functor R↦Fil^•_NΔ̂_R{n}, valued in filtration-complete complexes, preserves sifted colimits; on finitely generated polynomial Z-algebras it is the Beilinson connective cover of Δ_R^[•−n]{n} (BL Remark 5.7.10).

**Hypotheses and conventions.** R is an arbitrary animated commutative ring in (a)–(c); (d) requires R p-torsion-free with R/pR regular Noetherian; (e) requires p-complete smoothness over W(k). Corrected index (source issue PrismaticCohomology/E51): the target of Fil^m(φ{n}) is Δ_R^{[m−n]}{n}; Bhatt–Lurie Remark 5.7.8, Proposition 5.7.9 and Remark 5.7.10 print the index • + n, which contradicts Notation 5.7.5, Corollary 5.6.3 and the stated graded piece Δ̄_R{m}. φ is an endomorphism of the E_∞-Z_p-algebra Δ_R; it is not linear over a base prism.

**Construction or proof.**

1. (a): the relative filtered Frobenius and its graded pieces are PR.3/relative-nygaard-filtration and PR.3/divided-frobenius in the animated form of Bhatt–Lurie Proposition 5.1.1; compatibility with base change in the prism globalises them to D(WCart) (Construction 5.7.1, Remarks 5.7.2 and 5.7.3).
2. (b): tensor with the twist isomorphism of wcart-frobenius and take global sections; compose with the first projection of the pullback square defining Fil^•_N Δ_R{n} (Notation 5.7.5).
3. (c): the same construction in every filtration degree gives a target I^{m−n} ⊗ H_Δ(R){n}, with global sections Δ_R^{[m−n]}{n}; the graded pieces are computed by the fibre sequences of absolute-nygaard-filtration (g) and absolute-hodge-tate-cohomology (Remark 5.7.8).
4. (d): Nygaard completeness (absolute-nygaard-graded-pieces (4)) reduces to showing that gr^m(φ{n}) is the truncation to degrees ≤ m; its cofibre is the fibre of Θ + m on the quotients Ω̂^DHod_R/Fil_m^conj and Ω̂^DHod_R/Fil_{m−1}^conj, which lie in degrees > m and ≥ m because the conjugate filtration is the Postnikov filtration (Proposition 5.7.9). (e): Examples 5.7.4, 5.7.6 and 5.7.7, from the vanishing of Fil^n_Hodge for n > d.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.5/absolute-nygaard-filtration`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-5-absolute-nygaard-filtration); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.5/absolute-nygaard-graded-pieces`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-5-absolute-nygaard-graded-pieces); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.5/absolute-hodge-tate-cohomology`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-5-absolute-hodge-tate-cohomology); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.5/absolute-prismatic-cohomology`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-5-absolute-prismatic-cohomology); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.5/absolute-de-rham-comparison`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-5-absolute-de-rham-comparison); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.5/wcart-frobenius`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-5-wcart-frobenius); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.5/frobenius-pullback-square`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-5-frobenius-pullback-square); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/frobenius-on-prismatic-cohomology`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-frobenius-on-prismatic-cohomology); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/relative-nygaard-filtration`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-3-relative-nygaard-filtration); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/divided-frobenius`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-3-divided-frobenius); `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`; `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.2`; [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/relative-nygaard-graded-pieces`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-3-relative-nygaard-graded-pieces); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/nygaard-frobenius-colimit`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-3-nygaard-frobenius-colimit).

**Consumers.** PrismaticCohomology:PR.4 (Bhatt–Lurie §7.4): the syntomic complex Z_p(n)(R) is the fibre of φ{n} − 1 : Fil^n_N Δ̂_R{n} → Δ̂_R{n}. Bhatt–Lurie, Theorem 4.6.1 and Construction 5.4.10: the crystalline comparison and the prismatic augmentation are characterised through φ. PrismaticCohomology:PR.7: the Frobenius structure of the prismatic F-crystal attached to a smooth proper formal scheme is Φ. RefinedTraceMethods:RT.6: the cyclotomic Frobenius on graded pieces of the motivic filtration corresponds to φ{n}.

**Planning API.**

- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Absolute.relativeFrobenius` (data): Φ : F^* H_Δ(R) → H_Δ(R) in D(WCart).
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Absolute.frobeniusEnd` (data): φ : Δ_R → Δ_R, the pullback along F followed by RΓ(WCart, Φ).
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Absolute.absoluteFrobenius` (data): φ{n} : Fil^n_N Δ_R{n} → Δ_R{n}.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Absolute.nygaardToIdealFil` (compatibility): Fil^m(φ{n}) : Fil^m_N Δ_R{n} → Δ_R^{[m−n]}{n}.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Absolute.prismaticSheafMap_relativeFrobenius` (functoriality): Φ is natural in R: it commutes with the maps induced by a ring map R → S.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Absolute.completedNygaard_polynomial_characterization` (universal-property): The completed filtered functor is the sifted-colimit extension, in the category of filtration-complete objects, of the Beilinson connective cover of Δ_R^[•−n]{n} on finitely generated polynomial Z-algebras. The shift is •−n.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Absolute.completedFilteredFrobenius` (data): For integers m,n, the filtered Frobenius factors through Fil^m_NΔ̂_R{n}→Δ_R^[m−n]{n}; its source is Nygaard-completed and its target is the filtration-complete ideal-adic complex. At m=n, compose with Δ_R{n}→Δ̂_R{n} to obtain the Frobenius used in the completed syntomic fibre. This factorization uses the shift •−n.

**Unit tests.**

- `pr5_frob_fp_iso` (computation): φ is an isomorphism of Δ_{F_p}.
- `pr5_frob_zp_not_iso` (non-example): φ is not an isomorphism of Δ_{Z_p}: its cofibre is Z_p[−1].
- `pr5_frob_twist_zp_iso` (computation): φ{n} : Fil^n_N Δ_{Z_p}{n} → Δ_{Z_p}{n} is an isomorphism for n > 0.

**Acceptance.** On Δ_{F_p} = Z_p the Frobenius is the identity, and on Δ_R = W(R) for R perfect it is the Witt vector Frobenius. For a quasiregular semiperfectoid ring R, φ is the Frobenius of the δ-ring Δ_R and φ{n} restricted to Fil^n_N is the divided Frobenius of PR.3/divided-frobenius. Under absolute-crystalline-comparison φ corresponds to the crystalline Frobenius.

**Prototype boundary.** `TauCeti.Prismatic.Absolute.completedNygaard_polynomial_characterization` needs its supplier carrier: DD.1 supplies the integer-indexed filtered derived ∞-category, its Beilinson connective-cover functor and filtered completion; E5 supplies the sifted-colimit extension on animated rings.

## PR.6. q-crystalline charts and the AΩ comparison

A q-PD pair includes its δ-base map, complete prism condition and finite complete Tor-amplitude. Its envelope is universal for δ-maps preserving q and the q-PD ideals, under complete flatness and relative regularity. The q-crystalline site uses these actual envelopes. The Čech–Alexander complex and its small variant lead to the q-Poincaré argument and q-de Rham comparison. Framed automorphisms and q-differences have one owner, the requested QW.6 prefix; its split and extension to A_inf bases require acceptance. Naturality uses injective coordinate maps. The additive comparison does not discharge the recorded E₁ multiplicativity gap. AΩ comparisons use the fixed all-coordinates tower over O_C, with its actual Frobenius, rather than a freely chosen derived complex.

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-6-q-divided-power-operation"></a>

### The q-analogue [p]_q and the operation γ

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/q-divided-power-operation` · definition. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/QCrys/Basic`.

Let A = Z_p[[q−1]] with the δ-structure δ(q) = 0, so φ(q) = q^p, and let [p]_q = (q^p − 1)/(q − 1) = 1 + q + … + q^{p−1} ∈ A, the value at q of the p-th cyclotomic polynomial; (A, ([p]_q)) is the q-de Rham prism of PR.0. For a δ-A-algebra D put N(D) := φ^{-1}([p]_q D) = {x ∈ D : φ(x) ∈ [p]_q D}; it is an ideal of D. If D is [p]_q-torsion-free, the operation γ : N(D) → D is γ(x) := φ(x)/[p]_q − δ(x). The following facts are fixed with the definition. (i) φ(q−1) = q^p − 1 = (q−1)·[p]_q, so q − 1 ∈ N(D). (ii) [p]_q ≡ p modulo (q−1). (iii) A/[p]_q ≅ Z_p[ζ_p] with ζ_p a primitive p-th root of 1, and in this ring (q−1)^{p−1} and p differ by a unit; hence derived (p,[p]_q)-completion and derived (p, q−1)-completion agree on every complex of A-modules. (iv) δ([p]_q) ≡ 1 modulo [p]_q A. (v) For x, y ∈ N(D): γ(x+y) = γ(x) + γ(y) + ((x+y)^p − x^p − y^p)/p, where the last term is the integral polynomial Σ_{0<i<p} (binom(p,i)/p) x^i y^{p−i}. (vi) For x ∈ N(D) and f ∈ D: γ(fx) = φ(f)γ(x) − x^p δ(f). (vii) Hence for every ideal I ⊂ D the subset {x ∈ I : φ(x) ∈ [p]_q D and γ(x) ∈ I} is an ideal of D, and the two conditions φ(I) ⊂ [p]_q D, γ(I) ⊂ I may be checked on a generating set of I. (viii) If q = 1 in D then [p]_q = p and γ(x) = x^p/p. Convention: γ is the divided [p]_q-th power without the unit factor ∏_{j=1}^{p−1} [j]_q; the source keeps this normalisation and so does this node.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** p is a prime; A = Z_p[[q−1]] with δ(q) = 0. D is a δ-A-algebra; γ is defined only when D is [p]_q-torsion-free, and only on N(D). The general q-integers [n]_q, the q-derivative and their identities are owned by QWittVectors:QW.6; this node uses only [p]_q, which PR.0 owns as the generator of the q-de Rham prism. Fact (iii) corrects the printed sentence 'derived (p,[p]_q)-completion coincides with derived (p,[p]_q)-completion' to '(p, q−1)-completion'; the misprint is registered as PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22/E27. Fact (iv) is not printed in the source; it is the analogue for [p]_q of the computation δ(ξ) ≡ 1 mod ξ in Example 16.9 (2) and is used in smallest-largest-q-pd-ideals.

**Construction or proof.**

1. [p]_q and the prism (A, ([p]_q)) come from PR.0's q-de Rham prism. Facts (i) and (ii) are the identities Φ_p(q)·(q−1) = q^p − 1 and Φ_p(1) = p for the p-th cyclotomic polynomial, which Mathlib has (cyclotomic_prime, cyclotomic_prime_mul_X_sub_one, eval_one_cyclotomic_prime).
2. N(D) is the preimage of the ideal [p]_q D under the ring homomorphism φ of the δ-ring D, so it is an ideal; γ is well defined because [p]_q is a nonzerodivisor on D (Notation 16.1).
3. Facts (v) and (vi) (Remark 16.6): expand φ(x+y) = φ(x) + φ(y) and φ(fx) = φ(f)φ(x), and use the δ-ring formulas for δ(x+y) and δ(fx) from PR.0; for (vi), φ(f)(γ(x)+δ(x)) − f^pδ(x) − x^pδ(f) − pδ(f)δ(x) = φ(f)γ(x) − x^pδ(f).
4. Fact (vii): by (v) the correction term is a multiple of xy and by (vi) γ(fx) ∈ I when γ(x) ∈ I and x ∈ I, so the subset is closed under sums and multiples (Remark 16.6).
5. Fact (iv): pδ([p]_q) = φ([p]_q) − [p]_q^p, and φ([p]_q) = Σ_{i<p} q^{pi} ≡ p modulo [p]_q because q^p ≡ 1 modulo [p]_q; p is a nonzerodivisor in A/[p]_q ≅ Z_p[ζ_p], so δ([p]_q) − 1 ∈ [p]_q A. Fact (viii) is the definition with [p]_q = p: pγ(x) = φ(x) − pδ(x) = x^p.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/q-de-rham-prism`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-q-de-rham-prism); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-frobenius-dictionary`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-delta-frobenius-dictionary); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/associated-frobenius`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-associated-frobenius); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/distinguished-element`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-distinguished-element); [`mathlib:Polynomial.cyclotomic_prime`](#mathlib-polynomial-cyclotomic-prime); [`mathlib:Polynomial.cyclotomic_prime_mul_X_sub_one`](#mathlib-polynomial-cyclotomic-prime-mul-x-sub-one); [`mathlib:Polynomial.eval_one_cyclotomic_prime`](#mathlib-polynomial-eval-one-cyclotomic-prime); [`mathlib:geom_sum_mul`](#mathlib-geom-sum-mul).

BS22 Lemma 16.7, Corollary 16.8 and Lemma 16.10: stability of φ^{-1}([p]_q D) under γ and the generation of the ideal K of a q-PD envelope. BS22 Lemma 16.21: the extension of γ_s uses φ((q−1)X_s) = [p]_q (q−1) X_s^p, a consequence of fact (i). **Planning API.**

- `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys.pAnalog` (data): [p]_q := Σ_{i<p} q^i for an element q of a commutative ring; for D a δ-A-algebra it is the image of PR.0's generator of the q-de Rham prism.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys.pAnalog_eq_eval_cyclotomic` (compatibility): [p]_q is the value at q of Mathlib's p-th cyclotomic polynomial.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys.pAnalog_mul_sub_one` (relation): [p]_q·(q−1) = q^p − 1.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys.pAnalog_one` (simp): At q = 1: [p]_1 = p.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys.frobeniusPreimageIdeal` (constructor): The ideal N(D) = φ^{-1}([p]_q D) of a δ-ring D with a chosen element q.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys.gamma` (constructor): γ(x) for x ∈ N(D): an element with [p]_q·(γ(x) + δ(x)) = φ(x); unique when [p]_q is a nonzerodivisor on D.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys.pAnalog_mul_gamma` (characterisation): [p]_q·(γ(x) + δ(x)) = φ(x) for x ∈ N(D).
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys.gamma_add` (relation): For [p]_q a nonzerodivisor and x, y ∈ N(D): γ(x+y) = γ(x) + γ(y) + ((x+y)^p − x^p − y^p)/p, the last term being the integral polynomial of PR.0's addition correction with the opposite sign.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys.gamma_mul` (relation): For [p]_q a nonzerodivisor, x ∈ N(D) and f ∈ D: γ(fx) = φ(f)γ(x) − x^p δ(f).
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys.delta_pAnalog_sub_one_mem` (relation): If δ(q) = 0 then δ([p]_q) − 1 ∈ [p]_q D.

**Unit tests.**

- `pr6_gamma_q_sub_one` (computation): If δ(q) = 0 and [p]_q is a nonzerodivisor on D then q − 1 ∈ N(D) and γ(q−1) = (q−1) − δ(q−1).
- `pr6_gamma_at_q_one` (degenerate): If q = 1 then p·γ(x) = x^p for every x ∈ N(D).
- `pr6_gamma_p_padic` (computation): In Z_p with q = 1 (any δ-structure): p ∈ N(Z_p) and γ(p) = p^{p−1}.
- `pr6_pAnalog_two` (computation): For p = 2: [2]_q = 1 + q.
- `pr6_p_not_mem_frobenius_preimage` (non-example): In Z_p[[q−1]] with q = 1 + X, for every δ-structure: p ∉ N; so a definition of N as (p, q−1) is wrong.

**Acceptance.** γ(q−1) = (q−1) − δ(q−1) in every [p]_q-torsion-free δ-A-algebra (the computation of Corollary 16.8). For D = Z_p with q = 1: γ(p) = p^{p−1}, since δ(p) = 1 − p^{p−1}. In A itself N(A) = (q−1)A: φ(f) ∈ [p]_q A exactly when f(1) = 0.

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-6-hodge-tate-comparison-criterion"></a>

### A criterion for comparison maps to be isomorphisms

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/hodge-tate-comparison-criterion` · lemma. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.AOmega` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/AOmega/Basic`.

(a) Work over a commutative A, choose a regular element d, and assume R is smooth over A/d. Take commutative derived A-algebras E,F, complete for d, whose reductions are coconnective and have strictly graded commutative cohomology rings. Choose structure maps η_E:R→H^0(E/d), η_F:R→H^0(F/d). Require that the maps (Ω^*_{R/(A/d)}, d_dR) → (H^*(E/d), β_d) and (Ω^*_{R/(A/d)}, d_dR) → (H^*(F/d), β_d), induced by the universal property of the de Rham complex, are isomorphisms; here β_d is the Bockstein differential. Then every commutative A-algebra map α : E → F that intertwines η_E with η_F is an isomorphism. (b) The same holds if (A, (d)) is a bounded prism, R is p-completely smooth over A/d (with the p-completed de Rham complex), and E and F are derived (p, d)-complete. (c) In both cases it suffices that α is a map in D(A) for which H^*(α/d) is a homomorphism of graded rings; in particular the criterion applies to maps of E_1-algebras.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** d is a nonzerodivisor; E, F are derived d-complete (resp. (p, d)-complete); E/d, F/d coconnective with strictly graded commutative cohomology rings. (c) is what the printed proof uses, and it is the form in which the proof of Theorem 17.2 applies the lemma, the comparison map being a priori a map of E_1-algebras (Remark 17.3). The Bockstein differential and the map from the de Rham complex are those of PR.1's hodge-tate-comparison-map and AI.1.

**Construction or proof.**

1. α is an isomorphism if and only if α/d : E/d → F/d is, by derived d-completeness (resp. (p, d)-completeness) and derived Nakayama (DD.1); so it suffices that H^*(α/d) is an isomorphism.
2. H^*(α/d) is a map of graded A/d-algebras that commutes with the Bockstein differentials (naturality of β_d), so it is a map of commutative differential graded algebras (H^*(E/d), β_d) → (H^*(F/d), β_d).
3. It intertwines η_E with η_F, so by the universal property of the de Rham complex it forms a commutative triangle with the two maps from (Ω^*_{R/(A/d)}, d_dR); these are isomorphisms, hence so is H^*(α/d).

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/hodge-tate-comparison-map`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-hodge-tate-comparison-map); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/prism`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-prism); `AInfCohomology:AI.1/bockstein-differential`; `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`.

**Acceptance.** E = F = Δ_{R/A} over a bounded oriented prism, with η the Hodge–Tate structure map: every η-compatible endomorphism is an automorphism. The identity of E satisfies the hypothesis and the conclusion. The unit map A → Δ_{R/A} for R ≠ A/d is not an isomorphism: A does not satisfy the de Rham hypothesis for R.

**Sources.** [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Lemma 17.4. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 120. the statement, both versions.
