<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-6-q-pd-pair"></a>

### q-PD pairs

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/q-pd-pair` · definition. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/QCrys/Basic`.

A q-PD pair is a δ-pair (D, I) (a δ-ring D with an ideal I ⊂ D) with a map of δ-pairs (A, (q−1)) → (D, I), A = Z_p[[q−1]] with δ(q) = 0 (so D is a δ-A-algebra and q − 1 ∈ I), such that D and I are derived (p,[p]_q)-complete and the following three conditions hold. (1) φ(I) ⊂ [p]_q D (so γ is defined on I) and γ(I) ⊂ I. (2) Require [p]_q to be regular in D and require bounded p-power torsion in D/([p]_q). Together with the δ-A-algebra structure, these conditions make (D, ([p]_q)) a bounded prism receiving the base prism (A, ([p]_q)). (3) The ring D/(q−1) is p-torsion-free and has finite (p,[p]_q)-complete Tor-amplitude over D; equivalently finite p-complete Tor-amplitude, because [p]_q ≡ p mod (q−1). The map D → D/I is called a q-PD thickening and I a q-PD ideal. Being a q-PD pair is a property of a δ-pair over (A, (q−1)), not extra structure. Morphisms of q-PD pairs are maps of δ-pairs over (A, (q−1)): δ-ring maps D → D′ sending q to q and I into I′. A δ-PD pair is a q-PD pair with q − 1 = 0 in D; δ-PD pairs form a full subcategory. Two sufficient cases for (2) and (3) are a derived (p,[p]_q)-complete D completely flat over A, or a p-complete, p-torsion-free D in which q=1. By (2) and PR.0's Lemma 3.7, D is classically (p,[p]_q)-adically complete.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** The source's phrase 'derived (p,[p]_q)-complete δ-pair (D, I)' is read as: both D and I are derived (p,[p]_q)-complete. Remark 16.3 (a) and the proof of Corollary 16.8 confirm that completeness of the ideal is part of the definition. Condition (3) is a technical condition; condition (2) could be weakened to D being [p]_q-torsion-free. The source works with bounded prisms and so does this node. The conditions γ(I) ⊂ I, q − 1 ∈ I and the p-torsion-freeness of D/(q−1) are part of Definition 16.2 and are easily overlooked. Derived completeness, complete flatness and complete Tor-amplitude are DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1's notions.

**Construction or proof.**

1. State the data (D, I, the δ-A-algebra structure) and the conditions; by (1) and (2) the operation γ of q-divided-power-operation is defined on I.
2. Classical completeness: (D, ([p]_q)) is a bounded prism by (2), so D is classically (p,[p]_q)-complete by PR.0's bounded-prism-complete-flatness (BS22 Lemma 3.7).
3. The two standard sources of (2) and (3) (text after Definition 16.2): if D is (p,[p]_q)-completely flat over A then D/[p]_q is p-completely flat over Z_p[ζ_p] and D/(q−1) = D ⊗^L_A A/(q−1) is p-completely flat over Z_p with Tor-amplitude in [−1, 0]; if q = 1 in D and D is p-torsion-free then [p]_q = p and D/(q−1) = D.
4. Morphisms compose and the identity is a morphism, so q-PD pairs form a category; δ-PD pairs are the full subcategory on the pairs with q = 1.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/q-divided-power-operation`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-6-q-divided-power-operation); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/prism`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-prism); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/prism-category`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-prism-category); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/q-de-rham-prism`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-q-de-rham-prism); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/bounded-prism-complete-flatness`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-bounded-prism-complete-flatness); `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`; [`mathlib:IsAdicComplete`](#mathlib-isadiccomplete).

**Consumers.** BS22 Definition 16.12: the objects of the q-crystalline site are q-PD pairs over the base pair. BS22 Lemma 16.10 and Theorem 16.17: q-PD envelopes are universal maps to q-PD pairs; invariance compares two q-PD ideals on one δ-ring. BS22 Notation 17.1: the pair (A_inf, (ξ)) is the base of the comparison with AΩ. HabiroCohomologyFoundations:HQ.1: imports the local q-crystalline site, whose base is the q-PD pair (Z_p[[q−1]], (q−1)).

**Planning API.**

- `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys.QPDPair` (structure): A q-PD pair on a commutative ring D: a δ-structure, an element q with δ(q) = 0, an ideal I ∋ q−1, with conditions (1), (2), the p-torsion-freeness of D/(q−1) and classical (p,[p]_q)-completeness of D. The derived completeness of I and the Tor-amplitude part of (3) are DD.1's notions.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys.QPDPair.Hom` (structure): A morphism of q-PD pairs: a ring map commuting with δ, sending q to q and I into I′.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys.QPDPair.prism` (projection): The bounded prism (D, ([p]_q)) of a q-PD pair.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys.QPDPair.prism_I` (simp): The ideal of that prism is the principal ideal generated by [p]_q.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys.QPDPair.IsDeltaPD` (characterisation): A q-PD pair is a δ-PD pair when q = 1 in D.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys.QPDPair.frobenius_mem` (relation): φ(x) ∈ [p]_q D for x ∈ I.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys.QPDPair.gamma_mem` (relation): γ(x) ∈ I for x ∈ I.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys.QPDPair.isAdicComplete` (compatibility): D is (p,[p]_q)-adically complete in Mathlib's sense (IsAdicComplete); under condition (2) this is equivalent to derived completeness of D.

**Unit tests.**

- `pr6_qpd_pair_initial` (computation): There is a q-PD pair on Z_p[[X]] with q = 1 + X and I = (X).
- `pr6_qpd_pair_classical` (compatibility): There is a q-PD pair on Z_p with q = 1 and I = (p): the classical PD pair (Z_p, (p)).

**Acceptance.** (Z_p[[q−1]], (q−1)) is a q-PD pair, and it is initial (smallest-largest-q-pd-ideals). (A_inf, (ξ)) with ξ = φ^{-1}([p]_q) is a q-PD pair (ainf-q-pd-pair). (Z_p, (p)) with q = 1 is a δ-PD pair; (Z_p[[q−1]], (p, q−1)) is not a q-PD pair, since φ(p) = p ∉ [p]_q Z_p[[q−1]].

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-6-delta-pd-pairs"></a>

### δ-PD pairs and reduction modulo q − 1

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/delta-pd-pairs` · comparison. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/QCrys/Basic`.

(a) (Remark 16.3.) Let D be a δ-ring, regarded as an A-algebra through q ↦ 1, and I ⊂ D an ideal. Then (D, I) is a δ-PD pair if and only if (i) D is p-torsion-free and both D and I are p-adically complete, and (ii) I admits divided powers: x^n/n! ∈ I for every x ∈ I and n > 0. (b) (Remark 16.4.) If (D, I) is a q-PD pair then (D/(q−1), I·D/(q−1)) is a δ-PD pair, and (D, I) ↦ (D/(q−1), I·D/(q−1)) is left adjoint to the inclusion of δ-PD pairs into q-PD pairs. (c) (Example 16.9 (3).) For a p-torsion-free p-complete δ-ring D with a p-complete ideal I, (D, I) is a δ-PD pair exactly when every x ∈ I has all its divided powers x^n/n! in I. In particular a δ-PD pair is a p-adically complete PD pair in the sense of CrystallineCohomology:CR.0 whose ring is p-torsion-free and carries a δ-structure.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** In (a) the ideal is an ideal of D; the other ambient-ring letter in the source is a notation error (PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22/E27). In (c) every divided power of an element of I must lie in I, rather than merely in D; Remark 16.3 (b) supplies the needed condition (PrismaticCohomology/E62). The divided powers are unique because D is p-torsion-free: γ_n(x) = x^n/n!.

**Construction or proof.**

1. (⇐ of (a)) With q = 1 one has [p]_q = p and γ(x) = x^p/p, which lies in I by (ii); D is p-torsion-free and p-complete, so (D, (p)) is a bounded prism, and D/(q−1) = D gives (3).
2. (⇒ of (a)) Completeness and torsion-freeness in (i) are conditions (2), (3) and the completeness in the definition. For (ii): condition (1) gives x^p/p ∈ I; as (p−1)! is a unit, x^p/p! ∈ I; for n < p, x^n/n! is a unit multiple of x^n; the general case follows by induction from γ_{kp}(x) = u·γ_k(γ_p(x)) with u a p-adic unit (the composition rule of divided powers, Mathlib's DividedPowers.dpow_comp and CR.0).
3. (b) Conditions (2), (3) make D/(q−1) p-torsion-free and p-complete; the image of I satisfies x^p/p ∈ Ī by (1) reduced modulo q−1, and it is p-complete as the image of a derived complete module; apply (a). Adjunction: a map of q-PD pairs to a δ-PD pair kills q − 1, so it factors uniquely through the reduction.
4. (c) is (a) for the given D.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/q-pd-pair`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-6-q-pd-pair); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/q-divided-power-operation`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-6-q-divided-power-operation); [`mathlib:DividedPowers`](#mathlib-dividedpowers); `CrystallineCohomology:CR.0`; `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`; [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/crystalline-prism`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-crystalline-prism).

**Acceptance.** (Z_p, (p)) is a δ-PD pair; (Z_p[[q−1]], (q−1)) reduces to (Z_p, 0). (A_inf, (ξ)) reduces to (A_inf/(q−1), (ξ)), so ξ has divided powers in A_inf/(q−1). For D the p-completed PD polynomial algebra on t over Z_p with δ(t) = 0, the ideal tD is not a q-PD ideal although every element of tD has all divided powers in D: t^p/p ∉ tD.

**Sources.** [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Remark 16.3. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 107. the characterisation (a) and its proof. [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Remark 16.4. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 107. statement (b), the reduction functor and its adjunction.

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-6-smallest-largest-q-pd-ideals"></a>

### Higher q-divided powers and the smallest and largest q-PD ideals

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/smallest-largest-q-pd-ideals` · theorem. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/QCrys/Basic`.

(a) (Existence of higher q-divided powers, Lemma 16.7.) Let D be a δ-A-algebra and let f, z ∈ D satisfy [p]_q·z = φ(f). Then φ(z − δ(f)) ∈ [p]_q D. In particular, if D is [p]_q-torsion-free, the ideal N(D) = φ^{-1}([p]_q D) is stable under γ: if γ(x) is defined then so is γ(γ(x)). (b) (Corollary 16.8.) Let D be a derived (p,[p]_q)-complete δ-A-algebra satisfying conditions (2) and (3) of q-pd-pair. Then (q−1)D is the smallest q-PD ideal of D and N(D) is the largest q-PD ideal of D. (c) (Example 16.9 (1).) The pair (A, (q−1)) is a q-PD pair and is the initial object of the category of q-PD pairs; more generally (D, (q−1)) is a q-PD pair for every derived (p,[p]_q)-complete, (p,[p]_q)-completely flat δ-A-algebra D.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** (a) is stated for every δ-A-algebra, with no torsion-freeness, flatness or completeness. The source states it for [p]_q-torsion-free D and proves it by reduction to a universal case whose flatness is taken from Proposition 3.13; that proposition concerns the completed envelope, so the printed argument covers derived (p,[p]_q)-complete D, which is all the source uses (source issue PrismaticCohomology/E61). The proof steps give a direct argument. (b): the coefficient algebra must carry a compatible δ-structure, a condition omitted in the source’s notation (PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22/E27). A q-PD ideal of D is an ideal I such that (D, I) is a q-PD pair.

**Construction or proof.**

1. (a), direct argument: apply δ to [p]_q·z = φ(f) and use δ∘φ = φ∘δ and the product formula for δ: φ(δ(f)) = δ(z)·φ([p]_q) + z^p·δ([p]_q). With φ([p]_q) = [p]_q^p + pδ([p]_q) this gives φ(z) − φ(δ(f)) = (1 − δ([p]_q))·φ(z) − δ(z)·[p]_q^p, which lies in [p]_q D by fact (iv) of q-divided-power-operation.
2. (a), the source's route: in the universal case A{f, φ(f)/[p]_q}, flat over A by PR.0's regular-prismatic-envelopes (Proposition 3.13), φ([p]_q) = p is a nonzerodivisor modulo [p]_q, and φ²(f) = φ(f)^p + pφ(δ(f)) ≡ pφ(δ(f)) modulo [p]_q.
3. (b), smallest: (q−1)D is derived complete as the image of multiplication by q − 1 on D. φ(q−1) = (q−1)[p]_q, and γ(q−1) = (q−1) − δ(q−1); pδ(q−1) = (q^p − 1) − (q−1)^p = (q−1)([p]_q − (q−1)^{p−1}) and D/(q−1) is p-torsion-free, so δ(q−1) ∈ (q−1). Fact (vii) of q-divided-power-operation extends this to the ideal. Every q-PD ideal contains q − 1 by definition.
4. (b), largest: N(D) is the limit of D →φ φ_*D ← φ_*D (multiplication by [p]_q), hence derived complete; it is stable under γ by (a); every q-PD ideal lies in N(D) by condition (1).
5. (c) A satisfies (2) and (3), so (b) applies; it is initial because a q-PD pair is by definition a δ-pair over (A, (q−1)). The same argument applies to completely flat D.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/q-divided-power-operation`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-6-q-divided-power-operation); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/q-pd-pair`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-6-q-pd-pair); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/q-de-rham-prism`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-q-de-rham-prism); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/regular-prismatic-envelopes`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-regular-prismatic-envelopes); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-frobenius-dictionary`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-delta-frobenius-dictionary); `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`.

**Acceptance.** In A = Z_p[[q−1]] one has N(A) = (q−1)A, so (q−1) is the only q-PD ideal of A. In Z_p with q = 1: the smallest q-PD ideal is 0 and the largest is N(Z_p) = pZ_p. In A_inf: N(A_inf) = φ^{-1}(φ(ξ)A_inf) = (ξ), so (q−1) is the smallest and (ξ) the largest q-PD ideal of A_inf.

**Sources.** [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Lemma 16.7 and its proof. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 108. statement (a); the node proves it in a wider generality by a direct computation and records the printed reduction as the alternative route. [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Corollary 16.8 and its proof. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 109. statement (b). [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Example 16.9 (1). Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 109. statement (c).

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-6-q-crystalline-site"></a>

### The q-crystalline site and q-crystalline cohomology

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/q-crystalline-site` · definition. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/QCrys/Basic`.

Fix a q-PD pair (D, I) and a p-completely smooth D/I-algebra R. Write (R/D)_{q-crys} for the site whose underlying category reverses the arrows between relative q-PD thickenings of R: its objects are q-PD pairs (E, J) over (D, I) together with a D/I-algebra map R → E/J. A map of thickenings is a map of q-PD pairs over (D, I) compatible with R; an arrow in the site is its opposite. The category carries the indiscrete topology, so every presheaf is a sheaf. The structure presheaf O_{q-crys} sends (E, J) to E; it takes values in δ-D-algebras. The q-crystalline cohomology of R relative to D is qΩ_{R/D} := RΓ((R/D)_{q-crys}, O_{q-crys}), the derived limit of the rings E over all q-PD thickenings; it is a derived (p,[p]_q)-complete commutative algebra object of D(D), equipped with the φ_D-semilinear endomorphism φ_{R/D} induced by the Frobenius lifts of the δ-rings E. It is functorial in R and in the base pair (D, I).

**Hypotheses and conventions.** (D, I) is a q-PD pair; R is p-completely smooth over D/I: derived p-complete with R ⊗^L_{D/I} (D/I)/p smooth over (D/I)/p. The structure presheaf has the D-algebra structure; the different coefficient-ring letter in the source is a notation error (PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22/E27). The objects only carry a map R → E/J; it need not be an isomorphism. The category is not small; the cohomology is computed by a weakly initial object and its Čech nerve (q-crystalline-cech-alexander), which is how the derived limit is given a meaning.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Objects, morphisms and the topology are as stated; with the indiscrete topology the cohomology of a presheaf is its derived limit over the opposite category.
2. O_{q-crys} is a presheaf of δ-D-algebras, so its derived global sections are a commutative algebra object of D(D) with an endomorphism induced by the Frobenii φ_E, semilinear over φ_D.
3. Completeness: each E is derived (p,[p]_q)-complete and derived complete objects are closed under limits (DD.1).
4. Functoriality: a map R → R′ over D/I induces (R′/D)_{q-crys} → (R/D)_{q-crys} by composing structure maps; a map of q-PD pairs (D, I) → (D′, I′) acts by restriction of the base.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/q-pd-pair`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-6-q-pd-pair); `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`; `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E5:abstract/algebra-objects`.

**Consumers.** BS22 Theorems 16.14, 16.17, 16.18 and 16.22: qΩ_{R/D} is the object compared with crystalline, prismatic and q-de Rham cohomology. BS22 Theorem 17.2: qΩ_{R/A_inf} is the intermediary between AΩ_R and φ_A^*Δ_{R/A_inf}. HabiroCohomologyFoundations:HQ.1: imports the local q-crystalline site and glues the p-complete theories over all primes. AInfCohomology:AI.7 and CohomologyComparisons:CP.1: import the comparison with AΩ that is built from qΩ_{R/A_inf}.

**Planning API.**

- `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys.Thickening` (structure): An object of (R/D)_{q-crys}: a ring E with a q-PD pair, a morphism of q-PD pairs from (D, I) and a ring map R → E/J compatible with D/I.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys.Thickening.Hom` (structure): A morphism of q-PD thickenings: a morphism of q-PD pairs commuting with the maps from D and from R.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys.Thickening.base` (example): The thickening (D, I) of R = D/I, initial among thickenings, hence terminal in the opposite site of D/I.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys.qCrystallineCohomology` (constructor): qΩ_{R/D} as an object of the derived category of D-modules.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys.qCrystallineFrobenius` (data): φ_{R/D} : qΩ_{R/D} → φ_{D,*} qΩ_{R/D}.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys.qCrystallineEval` (projection): For every q-PD thickening (E, J) of R the canonical map qΩ_{R/D} → E in D(D).
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys.qCrystallineMap` (functoriality): For a D/I-algebra map R → R′ the induced map qΩ_{R/D} → qΩ_{R′/D}.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys.qCrystallineBaseIso` (example): qΩ_{(D/I)/D} ≅ D, the complex with D in degree 0.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys.qCrystallineUnit` (constructor): The unit D[0] → qΩ_(R/D), induced by the structure maps D → E.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys.qCrystallineCup` (structure): The cup product qΩ_(R/D) ⊗^L_D qΩ_(R/D) → qΩ_(R/D), induced by multiplication on the structure sheaf.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys.qCrystallineAlgebraLaws` (compatibility): The unit and cup product form a commutative algebra object in the completed derived category: associativity, both unit laws and symmetry, with the E_∞ coherences from E5. Evaluation and all functorial maps preserve this structure.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys.qCrystallineMap_id` (simp): qCrystallineMap(id_R) = id_(qΩ_(R/D)).
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys.qCrystallineMap_comp` (simp): For R → R′ → R″, qCrystallineMap(g ∘ f) = qCrystallineMap(f) ≫ qCrystallineMap(g).
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys.thickeningValueMap` (functoriality): For a morphism of thickenings (E,J) → (E′,J′), the canonical D-linear map E[0] → E′[0] induced by its ring map.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys.qCrystallineEval_natural` (compatibility): For a thickening morphism f:T→T′, eval_T ≫ thickeningValueMap(f) = eval_(T′); the map on values is the specified ring map, not an existentially chosen factorization.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys.thickeningValueFrobenius` (data): The φ_D-semilinear map E[0] → φ_(D,*)E[0] induced by φ_E at a thickening.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys.qCrystallineEval_frobenius` (compatibility): eval_T ≫ φ_E = φ_(R/D) ≫ φ_(D,*)(eval_T), expressing compatibility of evaluation with Frobenius.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys.qCrystallineBasePairMap` (functoriality): For a map of q-PD bases (D,I)→(D′,I′) and a compatible map R→R′, the natural map qΩ_(R/D) → Res_(D′/D)qΩ_(R′/D′). Its completed adjoint is the usual scalar-extension comparison. This API asserts a map, not an unconditional base-change isomorphism.

**Unit tests.**

- `pr6_qcrys_base` (degenerate): For R = D/I the evaluation map at the thickening (D, I) is an isomorphism qΩ_{(D/I)/D} ≅ D.
- `pr6_qcrys_eval_natural` (characterisation): Evaluation maps are compatible with morphisms of thickenings: for a morphism (E, J) → (E′, J′) the evaluation at E′ factors through the evaluation at E.
- `pr6_qcrys_map_id` (compatibility): The map induced by the identity of R is the identity of qΩ_{R/D}.
- `pr6_qcrys_not_structure_ring` (non-example): Evaluation at a thickening is not an isomorphism in general: over D = Z_p[[q−1]] there are R and a thickening, namely R = Z_p⟨T⟩ and (D⟨T⟩, (q−1)), for which qΩ_{R/D} → D⟨T⟩ is not an isomorphism.

**Acceptance.** For R = D/I the pair (D, I) is the initial q-PD thickening, so qΩ_{(D/I)/D} = D with φ_{R/D} = φ_D. For D with q = 1 the site consists of p-complete PD thickenings carrying δ-structures and qΩ_{R/D} is crystalline cohomology (q-crystalline-crystalline-comparison). For D = Z_p[[q−1]], I = (q−1), R = Z_p⟨T⟩: H^0(qΩ_{R/D}) = D, so qΩ_{R/D} is not the value D⟨T⟩ of the structure presheaf on the thickening (D⟨T⟩, (q−1)).

**Sources.** [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Definition 16.12. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 111. the definition of the site, its structure presheaf and qΩ_{R/D} with its Frobenius.

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-6-q-pd-homological-properties"></a>

### Homological properties of q-PD pairs

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/q-pd-homological-properties` · lemma. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/QCrys/Basic`.

Let (D, I) be a q-PD pair. (1) D is derived f-complete for every f ∈ I. (2) The functor M ↦ M ⊗̂^L_D D/(q−1) of (p,[p]_q)-completed base change along D → D/(q−1) is conservative on derived (p,[p]_q)-complete complexes. (3) This functor commutes with totalisations of cosimplicial derived (p,[p]_q)-complete complexes in D^{≥0}. (4) Let I_0 ⊂ D be an ideal containing q − 1 such that (D, I_0) satisfies conditions (1)–(3) of q-pd-pair, with D derived (p,[p]_q)-complete and I_0 not assumed derived complete, and let I′ ⊂ D be the derived (p,[p]_q)-complete ideal generated by I_0, that is, the image of I_0^∧ → D. Completing this ideal therefore gives a q-PD pair (D,I′). (5) This property also survives scalar extension: take a δ-A-map D→D′ which is completely flat for (p,[p]_q), assume D′ is derived complete for that ideal, and complete the ideal generated by the image of I. The resulting pair on D′ satisfies the q-PD conditions.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** (3): the cosimplicial complexes must be derived (p,[p]_q)-complete; the source’s abbreviated term omits the completeness condition (PrismaticCohomology/E62). (4): the source states it for a q-PD pair (D, I); since the ideal of a q-PD pair is already derived complete that statement is empty, and the proof of (5) and of Theorem 16.17 apply (4) to an ideal that is not known to be complete. The node states the form that the printed proof of (4) proves (source issue PrismaticCohomology/E63). Completed base change, conservativity (derived Nakayama) and Tor-amplitude are DD.1's.

**Construction or proof.**

1. (1) For f ∈ I, φ(f) = f^p + pδ(f) ∈ [p]_q D, so f^p ∈ (p, [p]_q); derived (p,[p]_q)-completeness gives derived f^p-completeness, hence derived f-completeness.
2. (2) It suffices that base change to D/(q−1, p) is conservative. If M ⊗^L_D D/(q−1, p) = 0 then M ⊗^L_D Kos(D; [p]_q, q−1) = 0, because this Koszul complex has at most two nonzero cohomology groups, each a D/(q−1, p)-module; then M = 0 by derived Nakayama (DD.1).
3. (3) Condition (3) of q-pd-pair gives finite complete Tor-amplitude of D → D/(q−1); a completed base change of finite complete Tor-amplitude commutes with totalisations in D^{≥0} (BS22 Lemma 4.22, a statement of DD.1).
4. (4) φ^{-1}([p]_q D) is derived complete, so φ(I′) ⊂ [p]_q D. As q − 1 ∈ I_0, I′ is the preimage of its image in D/(q−1), and that image is the p-complete ideal generated by the image of I_0 (derived completion preserves surjections). This reduces γ(I′) ⊂ I′ to q = 1, where it is the p-adic continuity of divided powers in a p-torsion-free ring (delta-pd-pairs).
5. (5) Condition (1) for (D′, I′): the generators of I·D′ satisfy it by fact (vii) of q-divided-power-operation, then apply (4) to I_0 = I·D′. Condition (2): PR.0's bounded-prism-complete-flatness (BS22 Lemma 3.7). Condition (3): the p-completed base change of D → D′ along D → D/(q−1) is p-completely flat with p-torsion-free source, so it is discrete and p-torsion-free and equals D′/(q−1); D′ → D′/(q−1) is the completed base change of D → D/(q−1), so it has finite p-complete Tor-amplitude.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/q-pd-pair`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-6-q-pd-pair); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/q-divided-power-operation`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-6-q-divided-power-operation); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/delta-pd-pairs`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-6-delta-pd-pairs); `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`; [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/bounded-prism-complete-flatness`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-bounded-prism-complete-flatness).

**Acceptance.** For (D, I) = (A_inf, (ξ)): A_inf is derived ξ-complete, and a derived (p, ξ)-complete complex M with M ⊗^L A_inf/(q−1) = 0 is zero. For D = Z_p[[q−1]] → D′ = Z_p[[q−1]]⟨T⟩ (completed polynomial ring, δ(T) = 0): (D′, (q−1)) is a q-PD pair. (2) fails without completeness: for D = Z_p[[q−1]], M = D[1/(q−1)] has zero base change and is not zero.

**Sources.** [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Lemma 16.5 and its proof. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 107. the five statements and their proofs; (3) and (4) are stated in the corrected forms explained in the hypotheses.

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-6-ainf-q-pd-pair"></a>

### The q-PD pair (A_inf, (ξ))

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/ainf-q-pd-pair` · lemma. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.AOmega` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/AOmega/Basic`.

(a) (Example 16.9 (2).) Let A_∞ be the (p,[p]_q)-completed perfection of A = Z_p[[q−1]] (PR.0's perfection of the q-de Rham prism) and ξ := φ^{-1}([p]_q) ∈ A_∞. Then (A_∞, (ξ)) is a q-PD pair. (b) (Notation 17.1.) Let C be a perfectoid field of characteristic 0 containing μ_{p^∞}, with a compatible system (ζ_{p^n})_n of primitive p-power roots of 1, ε = (1, ζ_p, ζ_{p²}, …) ∈ O_C^♭ and A_inf = A_inf(O_C) = W(O_C^♭). Then q := [ε] has δ(q) = 0, so A_inf is a perfect δ-A-algebra; it is (p, q−1)-completely flat over A, hence flat over A; the element ξ := φ^{-1}([p]_q) = 1 + [ε^{1/p}] + … + [ε^{(p−1)/p}] generates the kernel of Fontaine's map θ : A_inf → O_C; and (A_inf, (ξ)) is a q-PD pair whose q-PD thickening is θ : A_inf → A_inf/(ξ) ≅ O_C. Moreover [p]_q = φ(ξ) =: ξ̃ generates the kernel of θ̃ := θ∘φ^{-1}, the prism (A_inf, ([p]_q)) is the image of the perfect prism (A_inf, (ξ)) under the automorphism φ, and q − 1 = (q^{1/p} − 1)·ξ.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** C is a perfectoid field of characteristic 0 containing all p-power roots of 1; the system (ζ_{p^n}) is fixed. The ideals (q−1) and (ξ) do not depend on the choice. A_inf, θ and the element [ε] are owned by PerfectoidQuotients:Q0:integral-algebra; the perfect prism (A_inf, ker θ) by PR.0.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Conditions (2) and (3): A_∞ and A_inf are (p,[p]_q)-completely flat over A (A_∞ is a completed colimit along the flat Frobenius of A; for A_inf, (p, q−1) is a regular sequence and A_inf/(p, q−1) = O_C^♭/(ε−1) is flat over F_p), so the remark after Definition 16.2 applies; flatness over the noetherian ring A follows from complete flatness and derived completeness (the implication quoted in Notation 17.1; DD.1).
2. Condition (1) on the generator: φ(ξ) = [p]_q, so γ(ξ) = 1 − δ(ξ), and one needs δ(ξ) ≡ 1 modulo ξ. As p is a nonzerodivisor modulo ξ it suffices that φ(ξ) ≡ p modulo ξ; and φ(ξ) = [p]_q ≡ p modulo (q−1), while ξ divides q − 1 because q − 1 = φ^{-1}((q−1)[p]_q) = (q^{1/p} − 1)·ξ.
3. By fact (vii) of q-divided-power-operation the conditions hold on the ideal (ξ), which is derived complete (principal, generated by a nonzerodivisor of a derived complete ring) and contains q − 1.
4. (b): q = [ε] is a Teichmüller element, so δ(q) = 0 (PR.0, Q0:integral-algebra); θ(ξ) = 1 + ζ_p + … + ζ_p^{p−1} = 0 and ξ is distinguished, so it generates ker θ (PR.0's perfect-prisms-perfectoid-rings). The statements about ξ̃ and θ̃ follow by applying φ.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/smallest-largest-q-pd-ideals`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-6-smallest-largest-q-pd-ideals); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/q-pd-pair`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-6-q-pd-pair); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/q-divided-power-operation`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-6-q-divided-power-operation); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/prism-perfection`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-prism-perfection); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/ainf-prism`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-ainf-prism); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/perfect-prisms-perfectoid-rings`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-perfect-prisms-perfectoid-rings); `PerfectoidQuotients:Q0:integral-algebra`; `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`; [`mathlib:WittVector.teichmuller`](#mathlib-wittvector-teichmuller); [`mathlib:WittVector.fontaineTheta`](#mathlib-wittvector-fontainetheta).

**Acceptance.** γ(ξ) = 1 − δ(ξ) ∈ (ξ). The reduction (A_inf/(q−1), (ξ)) is a δ-PD pair: ξ has divided powers in A_inf/(q−1). (A_inf, (q−1)) is also a q-PD pair, with A_inf/(q−1) a p-torsion-free lift of O_C modulo the divided power ideal (ξ); q-pd-thickening-invariance compares the two.

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-6-q-pd-envelope"></a>

### q-PD envelopes

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/q-pd-envelope` · construction. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/QCrys/Basic`.

Let (D, I) be a q-PD pair, P a derived (p,[p]_q)-complete, (p,[p]_q)-completely flat δ-D-algebra and x_1, …, x_r ∈ P a sequence that is (p,[p]_q)-completely regular relative to D; let J = (I, x_1, …, x_r) ⊂ P. (1) The derived (p,[p]_q)-complete simplicial δ-P-algebra E := P{φ(x_1)/[p]_q, …, φ(x_r)/[p]_q}^∧ obtained by freely adjoining the elements φ(x_i)/[p]_q has complete flatness over D for the ideal (p,[p]_q). Its higher homotopy groups vanish and multiplication by [p]_q on its underlying ring is injective. (2) Let K ⊂ E be the minimal derived (p,[p]_q)-complete ideal containing the image of J and stable under γ. Then P/J → E/K is an isomorphism, (E, K) is a q-PD pair, and (P, J) → (E, K) is the universal map of δ-pairs from (P, J) to a q-PD pair: every map of δ-pairs (P, J) → (E′, K′) to a q-PD pair factors uniquely through (E, K). One writes D_{J,q}(P) := E and calls (D_{J,q}(P), K) the q-PD envelope of (P, J); it depends only on the ideal J, not on the generators. (3) Extension used by the Čech–Alexander construction: the same statements hold when J is, Zariski locally on Spf(P), generated by I and a sequence as above, and when (P, J) is a filtered colimit (completed) of such pairs.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** (D, I) is a q-PD pair; P is derived (p,[p]_q)-complete and (p,[p]_q)-completely flat over D; the sequence is (p,[p]_q)-completely regular relative to D (DD.1's notion, BS22 Definition 2.42). The source does not state that P is derived complete. Without it E/K is the derived p-completion of P/J, so the isomorphism P/J ≅ E/K needs it (source issue PrismaticCohomology/E62). Part (3) is not stated in Lemma 16.10, but Construction 16.13 and Remark 16.16 apply the lemma to such ideals (source issue PrismaticCohomology/E64). Free adjunction of elements to simplicial δ-rings is PR.0's animated-delta-rings.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Let Ẽ be the derived (p,[p]_q)-complete simplicial commutative δ-P-algebra freely adjoining φ(x_i)/[p]_q. Complete flatness of Ẽ over D may be checked after derived base change along D → D/(q−1) (q-pd-homological-properties); there [p]_q = p and the claim is BS22 Corollary 2.44 with Lemma 2.43 (PR.0), the sequence φ(x_i) ≡ x_i^p being p-completely regular relative to D/(q−1). So Ẽ is discrete, equal to E, and [p]_q-torsion-free (PR.0, Lemma 3.7).
2. The map E → P/J: E/(q−1) is the p-completed PD envelope of P/(q−1) along (x_1, …, x_r) (PR.0's pd-envelope-as-delta-envelope), which maps to P/(q−1, x_1, …, x_r) → P/J. Let K′ be the kernel of E → P/J; it is the preimage of the kernel K̄′ of E/(q−1) → P/J, and K̄′ has divided powers.
3. (E, K′) is a q-PD pair: put K″ = K′ ∩ φ^{-1}([p]_q E). γ(K″) ⊂ K″, because γ(f) ∈ φ^{-1}([p]_q E) by smallest-largest-q-pd-ideals (a), and γ(f) reduces to f^p/p ∈ K̄′. K″ is the preimage of its image in E/(q−1), since x + (q−1)y ∈ K″ for x ∈ K″. It contains (I, x_1, …, x_r). By BS22 Lemma 16.11 (CR.0: the ideal of a PD envelope is the smallest ideal containing the generators and stable under f ↦ f^p/p) one gets K″ = K′ = K.
4. Universality: for a map of δ-pairs g : (P, J) → (E′, K′) to a q-PD pair, g(φ(x_i)) ∈ [p]_q E′; as E′ is [p]_q-torsion-free and derived complete, g extends uniquely to a δ-map E → E′; the preimage of K′ is a derived complete γ-stable ideal containing J, so it contains K.
5. (3): Zariski gluing by the flat-localisation property of envelopes (PR.0's regular-prismatic-envelopes (3)) together with q-pd-homological-properties (5); filtered colimits by the universal property, the envelope being the completed colimit of the envelopes.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/q-pd-pair`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-6-q-pd-pair); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/q-pd-homological-properties`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-6-q-pd-homological-properties); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/smallest-largest-q-pd-ideals`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-6-smallest-largest-q-pd-ideals); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/q-divided-power-operation`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-6-q-divided-power-operation); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/regular-prismatic-envelopes`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-regular-prismatic-envelopes); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/animated-delta-rings`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-animated-delta-rings); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/pd-envelope-as-delta-envelope`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-pd-envelope-as-delta-envelope); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/bounded-prism-complete-flatness`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-bounded-prism-complete-flatness); `CrystallineCohomology:CR.0`; `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`.

**Consumers.** BS22 Construction 16.13 and Remark 16.16: the terms of the Čech–Alexander complex computing qΩ are q-PD envelopes. BS22 Construction 16.20 and Lemma 16.21: the framed q-de Rham complex lives on D_{J,q}(P), to which the automorphisms γ_s extend. BS22 proof of Theorem 17.2: its universal property produces the map D_{J_Σ,q}(P_Σ) → A_inf(R_{Σ,∞}). HabiroCohomologyFoundations:HQ.1: imports the local q-crystalline charts, which are these envelopes.

**Planning API.**

- `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys.envelope` (constructor): The ring D_{J,q}(P) for a q-PD pair (D, I), a δ-D-algebra P and a finite sequence x in P.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys.envelopeMap` (data): The canonical ring map P → D_{J,q}(P).
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys.envelopePair` (structure): The q-PD pair (D_{J,q}(P), K); its δ-structure extends that of P and its element q is the image of q.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys.envelopeMap_delta` (compatibility): P → D_{J,q}(P) commutes with δ.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys.envelope_frobenius_mem` (relation): φ(x_i) ∈ [p]_q·D_{J,q}(P) for every i.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys.envelopeMap_mem` (relation): The image of J = (I, x_1, …, x_r) lies in K.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys.envelopeQuotientEquiv` (characterisation): P/J ≅ D_{J,q}(P)/K.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys.envelopeLift` (universal-property): A δ-ring map g from P to the ring of a q-PD pair (E′, K′) with g(q) = q and g(J) ⊂ K′ extends to a ring map D_{J,q}(P) → E′.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys.envelopeLift_comp` (universal-property): The extension restricts to g on P.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys.envelopeLift_unique` (universal-property): Two δ-ring maps out of D_{J,q}(P) into the ring of a q-PD pair that agree on P are equal.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys.envelopeLift_isDeltaHom` (compatibility): The canonical lift commutes with δ, since it is induced from the free δ-algebra and extends to derived completion by δ-continuity.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys.envelopeLift_map_I` (compatibility): The lift carries K, the smallest q-PD ideal containing J, into the target q-PD ideal K′; include this in the pair morphism.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys.envelopePair_q` (relation): The structural map carries q to the specified q of the envelope and of every target; it is a map over the fixed q-PD base.

**Unit tests.**

- `pr6_envelope_empty_sequence` (degenerate): For the empty sequence and P = D, the map D → D_{I,q}(D) is bijective.
- `pr6_envelope_frobenius_divisible` (computation): In the envelope of a one-element sequence x, there is z with [p]_q·z = φ(x) and γ(x) = z − δ(x) lies in K.
- `pr6_envelope_universal_identity` (characterisation): The lift of the envelope map itself is the identity of D_{J,q}(P).
- `pr6_envelope_not_surjective` (non-example): For D = Z_p[[q−1]] and x = X: X^p is not divisible by [p]_q in the polynomial ring D[X], nor in its completion (so P → D_{J,q}(P) is not an isomorphism, and a definition of the envelope as P itself is wrong).

**Acceptance.** For P = Z_p[[q−1]]⟨X⟩ with δ(X) = 0 and J = (q−1, X): the envelope contains z with [p]_q·z = X^p, γ(X) = z ∈ K, and its reduction modulo q − 1 is the p-completed PD polynomial algebra Z_p⟨X⟩ with X^p/p. For P = A_inf⟨x^{±1}⟩ and J = (ξ): φ(ξ)/[p]_q = 1, so D_{J,q}(P) = P. Universal property applied to the q-PD pair (A_inf(S), (ξ)) of a p-torsion-free perfectoid O_C-algebra S gives the coordinate map of ainf-omega-comparison-map.

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-6-q-pd-envelope-base-change"></a>

### q-PD envelopes: base change, PD envelopes and prismatic envelopes

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/q-pd-envelope-base-change` · theorem. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/QCrys/Basic`.

In the situation of q-pd-envelope: (a) (Lemma 16.10 (3).) The functor (P, J) ↦ (D_{J,q}(P), K) commutes with (p,[p]_q)-completed derived base change along maps (D, I) → (D′, I′) of q-PD pairs: D_{J,q}(P) ⊗̂^L_D D′ ≅ D_{J′,q}(P′) for P′ = P ⊗̂^L_D D′ and J′ = (I′, x_1, …, x_r). (b) In particular D_{J,q}(P) ⊗̂^L_D D/(q−1) = D_{J,q}(P)/(q−1) is the p-completed PD envelope of the ideal J/(q−1) ⊂ P/(q−1), relative to the PD pair (D/(q−1), I·D/(q−1)), and K/(q−1) is its PD ideal. (c) (Lemma 16.11.) Let B be a p-torsion-free Z_p-algebra and I ⊂ B an ideal generated by a sequence that is regular modulo p; let (D_I(B), J) be the PD envelope of (B, I). Then J is the smallest ideal of D_I(B) that contains I·D_I(B) and is stable under f ↦ f^p/p. (d) (Relation to prismatic envelopes.) D_{J,q}(P) is the prismatic envelope of PR.0, over the bounded prism (D, ([p]_q)), of the δ-pair (P, ([p]_q, φ(x_1), …, φ(x_r))); when q = 1 in D this is the identification of P{φ(x_i)/p}^∧ with the p-completed PD envelope of (x_1, …, x_r) (BS22 Corollary 2.39).

**Hypotheses and conventions.** (b): the comparison uses the p-completed PD envelope. Completion is implicit in the source statement but explicit in its proof and Remark 16.16 (PrismaticCohomology/E62). (c): regularity of the ideal modulo p means generation by a sequence regular modulo p, the precise interpretation used here. (d) is not printed as a statement; it is the content of the first step of the proof of Lemma 16.10 and of the reference to Proposition 3.13 in the proof of Lemma 16.7. PD envelopes and their ideals are owned by CrystallineCohomology:CR.0.

**Construction or proof.**

1. (a) E is the free derived complete δ-P-algebra on the elements φ(x_i)/[p]_q, and complete regularity relative to the base is stable under base change, so the construction commutes with completed base change; K′ is identified by the universal property.
2. (b) Take D′ = D/(q−1) with the δ-PD pair of delta-pd-pairs (b). Then [p]_q = p and P̄{φ(x_i)/p}^∧ is the p-completed PD envelope by PR.0's pd-envelope-as-delta-envelope (BS22 Lemma 2.38, Corollary 2.39), with its PD structure compatible with that of I·D/(q−1) (CR.0).
3. (c) The regularity hypothesis makes D_I(B) p-torsion-free; the description of J is the standard generation of the PD ideal by divided powers of generators, in which γ_n for general n is a unit multiple of iterates of γ_p and ordinary powers (CR.0; the source cites the Stacks project, Tag 07GS).
4. (d) Modulo (p, [p]_q) one has φ(x_i) ≡ x_i^p, and (x_1^p, …, x_r^p) is completely regular relative to D when (x_1, …, x_r) is (the remark after BS22 Lemma 2.43); apply PR.0's regular-prismatic-envelopes to the ideal ([p]_q, φ(x_1), …, φ(x_r)).

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/q-pd-envelope`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-6-q-pd-envelope); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/delta-pd-pairs`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-6-delta-pd-pairs); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/pd-envelope-as-delta-envelope`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-pd-envelope-as-delta-envelope); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/regular-prismatic-envelopes`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-regular-prismatic-envelopes); `CrystallineCohomology:CR.0`; `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`.

**Acceptance.** For D = Z_p[[q−1]], P = D⟨X⟩, J = (q−1, X): D_{J,q}(P)/(q−1) is the p-completed PD polynomial algebra on X over Z_p. For D with q = 1: D_{J,q}(P) is the p-completed PD envelope D_J(P)^∧ and K its PD ideal. Base change of the envelope of (Z_p[[q−1]]⟨x⟩, (q−1, x)) along the map of q-PD pairs (Z_p[[q−1]], (q−1)) → (A_inf, (ξ)) is the envelope of (A_inf⟨x⟩, (ξ, x)).

**Sources.** [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Lemma 16.10 (3). Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 110. statements (a) and (b). [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Lemma 16.11 and its proof. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 111. statement (c) and its proof.

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-6-framed-q-pd-datum"></a>

### Framed D-algebras and framed q-PD data

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/framed-q-pd-datum` · definition. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/QCrys/Basic`.

Fix a q-PD pair (D, I) with D flat over A = Z_p[[q−1]] and a p-completely smooth D/I-algebra R. A framed D-algebra is a pair (P, S) of a derived (p,[p]_q)-complete D-algebra P and a set S with elements X_s ∈ P (s ∈ S) such that the framing □ : D[X_s : s ∈ S]^∧ → P is (p,[p]_q)-completely ind-étale; then P is (p,[p]_q)-completely ind-smooth over D. This is the (p, q−1)-complete case, over the base ring D with its element q, of the framed algebras of QWittVectors:QW.6, and the following are imported from QW.6, not constructed here: the pairwise commuting D-algebra automorphisms γ_s of P, determined by γ_s(X_s) = qX_s, γ_s(X_t) = X_t for t ≠ s and γ_s ≡ id modulo (q−1)X_s; the q-derivatives ∇_{q,s}(f) = (γ_s(f) − f)/((q−1)X_s); the twisted Leibniz rule; the framed q-de Rham complex qΩ^{*,□}_{P/D}, the Koszul complex of the ∇_{q,s}; and its reduction modulo q − 1 to the de Rham complex. PR.6 adds: (i) the unique δ-D-algebra structures on D[S]^∧ and on P with δ(X_s) = 0 for all s, compatible along □, for which every γ_s is a δ-D-algebra automorphism; (ii) P is flat over A, so (q−1)X_s is a nonzerodivisor on P; (iii) retain a chosen framing (P,S) and a D-algebra presentation P→R. Writing J for its kernel, these data constitute the framed q-PD datum. A morphism of framed q-PD data (P, S, J) → (P′, S′, J′) is a D-algebra map P → P′ together with an injective map S → S′, s ↦ s′, such that X_s ↦ X_{s′}, carrying J into J′.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** D is flat over A = Z_p[[q−1]]: the standing assumption of BS22 §16.3. The source writes 'p-completely ind-smooth' and 'p-completely ind-étale'. The unique extension of γ_s uses that (q−1)X_s is topologically nilpotent, which holds for the (p, q−1)-adic topology and fails for the p-adic one; the conditions are therefore (p,[p]_q)-complete ones, as the source itself writes in Remark 16.16 and at the end of Construction 16.20 (source issue PrismaticCohomology/E65). Ownership (RT-AREA-etale/28): framed algebras, γ_s, ∇_{q,s}, the twisted Leibniz rule, the framed q-de Rham Koszul complex and its reduction modulo q − 1 belong to QWittVectors:QW.6 in the general form over an I-completely étale framing, I = (q−1) or (p, q−1). This node imports the (p, q−1)-complete case and adds only (i)–(iii). A morphism of framed q-PD data is injective on coordinates (the map S → S′ with X_s ↦ X_{s′} is injective); it need not be étale. Without injectivity the map does not commute with the q-derivatives: for D⟨X_0,X_1⟩ → D⟨X⟩, ∇_q(X_0X_1) ↦ 2X dX but ∇_q(X²) = (1+q)X dX.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Import from QW.6 the framed algebra (P, S) with its automorphisms and q-derivatives, for the base ring D, the element q and the ideal (p, q−1): the automorphism of D[S]^∧ scaling X_s by q is congruent to the identity modulo the topologically nilpotent element (q−1)X_s, so it extends uniquely along the completely ind-étale framing (Construction 16.19).
2. (i) D[S] has the δ-D-algebra structure with δ(X_s) = 0, that is φ(X_s) = X_s^p; it extends uniquely to the completion and along the completely ind-étale map □ (BS22 Lemma 2.18; equivalently, P being p-torsion-free, the framed Frobenius lift of QW.6 gives a δ-structure by PR.0's torsionfree-frobenius-equivalence). γ_s is a δ-map on D[S]^∧ because δ(qX_s) = 0, and on P by uniqueness of the extension.
3. (ii) P is (p,[p]_q)-completely flat over D and derived complete, D is flat over the noetherian ring A, so P is flat over A (DD.1); hence q − 1 and X_s are nonzerodivisors on P.
4. (iii) The kernel J of P → R is, locally on Spf(P), generated by I and a filtered colimit of completely regular sequences relative to D, so q-pd-envelope (3) applies to (P, J).

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/q-pd-pair`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-6-q-pd-pair); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/q-pd-envelope`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-6-q-pd-envelope); `QWittVectors:QW.6`; [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/torsionfree-frobenius-equivalence`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-torsionfree-frobenius-equivalence); `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`.

**Consumers.** BS22 Lemma 16.21 and Construction 16.20: the automorphisms γ_s are extended to the q-PD envelope of J and their Koszul complex is formed. BS22 Theorem 16.22: the framed q-PD datum is the input of the q-de Rham and q-crystalline comparison. BS22 proof of Theorem 17.2: the formal tori P_Σ over A_inf with coordinates indexed by finite sets of units are framed q-PD data. QWittVectors:QW.6 and HabiroCohomologyFoundations:HQ.1: QW.6 owns the framed algebra and its q-derivatives; HQ.1 imports them from QW.6 and the q-PD part from this stage.

**Planning API.**

- `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys.FramedAlgebra` (structure): A framed D-algebra with its imported structure: coordinates X_s, automorphisms γ_s, q-derivatives ∇_{q,s} (owner QWittVectors:QW.6) and the δ-structure with δ(X_s) = 0. The complete ind-étaleness of the framing is DD.1's and QW.6's notion.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys.FramedAlgebra.delta_coord` (relation): δ(X_s) = 0.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys.QWFramedAlgebra.gamma_coord_self` (relation): QW.6 adapter, imported from the proposed framing prefix: γ_s(X_s) = q·X_s.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys.QWFramedAlgebra.gamma_coord_of_ne` (relation): QW.6 adapter, imported from the proposed framing prefix: γ_s(X_t) = X_t for t ≠ s.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys.QWFramedAlgebra.gamma_comm` (relation): QW.6 adapter, imported from the proposed framing prefix: γ_s γ_t = γ_t γ_s.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys.FramedAlgebra.gamma_delta` (compatibility): QW.6 adapter, imported from the proposed framing prefix: γ_s commutes with δ.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys.QWFramedAlgebra.sub_one_mul_coord_mul_nabla` (characterisation): QW.6 adapter, imported from the proposed framing prefix: (q−1)·X_s·∇_{q,s}(f) = γ_s(f) − f.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys.FramedDatum` (structure): A framed q-PD datum (P, S, J): a framed D-algebra and an ideal J of P, the kernel of a surjection onto R. The typed prototype records the flat coefficient map Z_p[[q−1]]→D, δ-compatibility, completeness, complete flatness of the actual polynomial framing, an étale reduction of that framing and p-complete smoothness of R. This is a finite-presentation anchor for the full completely ind-étale construction.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys.FramedDatum.Hom` (structure): A morphism of framed q-PD data: a D-algebra map together with an injective map on coordinate indices, carrying each coordinate to its indexed coordinate and J into J′.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys.FramedDatum.coordinate_regular` (characterisation): Extend the QW.6-owned framed algebra by the q-PD presentation and the proof that (q−1)X_s is a nonzerodivisor in its envelope. This is PR.6’s addition; γ_s and q-derivations are imported.

**Unit tests.**

- `pr6_framed_nabla_coord_pow` (computation): If (q−1)X_s is a nonzerodivisor then ∇_{q,s}(X_s^{n+1}) = [n+1]_q·X_s^n, with [n+1]_q = Σ_{i≤n} q^i.
- `pr6_framed_nabla_const` (degenerate): If (q−1)X_s is a nonzerodivisor then ∇_{q,s} vanishes on the image of D.
- `pr6_framed_gamma_frobenius` (compatibility): γ_s commutes with the Frobenius lift φ of the δ-structure.
- `pr6_framed_two_framings_gamma` (non-example): If two framed structures on the same P with one coordinate have X′ = X + 1, then γ′(X) = qX + (q−1); so the automorphism depends on the framing and is not determined by P.

**Acceptance.** One polynomial coordinate: P = D⟨X⟩, S = {X}: γ(X^n) = q^n X^n and ∇_q(X^n) = [n]_q X^{n−1}. A torus: P = D⟨X^{±1}⟩ with γ(X^n) = q^n X^n for n ∈ Z and logarithmic q-derivative (γ − 1)/(q−1). Two framings: on D⟨T⟩ the coordinates T and T + 1 give automorphisms with γ^{T}(T) = qT and γ^{T+1}(T) = qT + (q−1). S = ∅ and P = D: the framed q-PD datum (D, ∅, I) of R = D/I.

**Sources.** [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Construction 16.19. <a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-6-q-crystalline-cech-alexander"></a>

### Čech–Alexander complexes for q-crystalline cohomology

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/q-crystalline-cech-alexander` · construction. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/QCrys/Basic`.

Fix a q-PD pair (D, I) and a p-completely smooth D/I-algebra R. Present R as a quotient of a polynomial D-algebra completed for (p,[p]_q); denote this presentation by P→R and its kernel by J_0. Apply the free δ-D-algebra construction to P and then derive its completion, obtaining F. In F put J=(J_0F)^∧. Let P^• and F^• be the (completed) Čech nerves of D → P and D → F; F^• is the free derived complete δ-D-algebra on P^•. Let J_0^• ⊂ P^• be the kernel of P^• → P → R and J^• = (J_0^•F^•)^∧. Then: (1) R ≅ P^•/J_0^• → F^•/J^• is the derived p-completed Čech nerve of R → F/J. (2) The q-PD envelopes D_{J^•,q}(F^•) → F^•/J^•, with kernels K^•, form a cosimplicial object (D_{J^•,q}(F^•), K^•) of (R/D)_{q-crys}, which is the Čech nerve of its 0-th term D_{J,q}(F). (3) D_{J,q}(F) is weakly initial: every q-PD thickening of R receives a map from it. (4) Hence qΩ_{R/D} ≃ lim_Δ D_{J^•,q}(F^•), the totalisation of a cosimplicial δ-D-algebra whose terms are (p,[p]_q)-completely flat over D; the Frobenius φ_{R/D} is induced by the Frobenii of the terms. (5) (Small variant, Remark 16.16.) For a (p,[p]_q)-completely smooth (or ind-smooth) δ-D-algebra P with a D-algebra surjection P → R, for instance a (p, I)-completely smooth lift of R with a δ-structure, let P^• be the completed Čech nerve of D → P and J^• = ker(P^• → R); then lim_Δ D_{J^•,q}(P^•) ≃ qΩ_{R/D} as well.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** For the augmentation P^n→R, work Zariski locally on Spec(P): its kernel is obtained from I together with a filtered colimit of ideals defined by D-relative completely regular sequences. Part (3) of q-pd-envelope consequently provides the termwise envelopes. The choice of P → R may be made functorial in R (the polynomial algebra on the set R), giving a strictly functorial complex. In (5) the weak initiality is replaced by the comparison with crystalline cohomology.

**Construction or proof.**

1. (1): push out P^• → F^• along P^• → P and then along P → R.
2. (2): the construction carrying a surjection (P → R) to the thickening D_{J,q}(F) takes tensor products of the input to coproducts in the site (universal properties of the free δ-algebra and of the q-PD envelope), so the cosimplicial object is a Čech nerve; this is the argument of BS22 Constructions 4.17–4.18 (PR.1's cech-alexander-complex).
3. (3): given a thickening (E, J_E), lift R → E/J_E to a D-algebra map P → E (P is a completed polynomial algebra and E is derived complete), extend uniquely to a δ-map F → E, note that J maps into J_E, and apply the universal property of q-pd-envelope.
4. (4): Čech theory for a weakly final object of a presheaf topos (the argument of the Stacks project, Tag 07JM, as used in PR.1; EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E2).
5. (5): run the proof of q-crystalline-crystalline-comparison with D_{J^•,q}(P^•): modulo q − 1 it is the cosimplicial p-completed PD envelope, which computes crystalline cohomology because D_{J^0}(P^0) is weakly initial among PD thickenings (CR.2); then use conservativity of reduction modulo q − 1 (q-pd-homological-properties (2), (3)).

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/q-crystalline-site`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-6-q-crystalline-site); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/q-pd-envelope`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-6-q-pd-envelope); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/q-pd-envelope-base-change`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-6-q-pd-envelope-base-change); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/q-pd-homological-properties`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-6-q-pd-homological-properties); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/free-delta-ring`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-free-delta-ring); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/cech-alexander-complex`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-cech-alexander-complex); `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E2`; `CrystallineCohomology:CR.2`; `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`.

**Consumers.** BS22 proofs of Theorems 16.14, 16.17 and 16.18: all three comparisons are proved on this cosimplicial ring. BS22 proof of Theorem 16.22: the small variant for the Čech nerve of a framed algebra is row 0 of the bicomplex. HabiroCohomologyFoundations:HQ.1: the explicit model of the local q-crystalline cohomology that the global gluing uses.

**Planning API.**

- `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys.cechAlexanderComplex` (constructor): The cochain complex of D-modules attached to the cosimplicial ring D_{J^•,q}(F^•) of a presentation P → R.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys.cechAlexanderIso` (characterisation): The image of that complex in D(D) is isomorphic to qΩ_{R/D}.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys.cechAlexanderZero` (data): The weakly initial thickening D_{J,q}(F) of R, the term of degree 0.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys.cechAlexanderZero_weaklyInitial` (universal-property): Every q-PD thickening of R receives a morphism from the term of degree 0.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys.cechAlexanderSmallComplex` (constructor): The cochain complex attached to the cosimplicial ring D_{J^•,q}(P^•) of a δ-D-algebra P with a surjection onto R (Remark 16.16).
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys.cechAlexanderSmallIso` (characterisation): For a completely (ind-)smooth δ-presentation the small complex also represents qΩ_{R/D}.

**Unit tests.**

- `pr6_cech_alexander_independent` (characterisation): The complexes of two presentations of R have isomorphic images in D(D).
- `pr6_cech_alexander_weakly_initial_base` (compatibility): The thickening (D, I) of D/I receives a morphism from the term of degree 0 of every presentation of D/I.
- `pr6_cech_alexander_base_presentation` (degenerate): For R = D/I and the presentation P = D the complex represents D in degree 0.
- `pr6_cech_alexander_not_cech_nerve` (non-example): The Čech nerve P^• of D → P without envelopes does not compute qΩ_{R/D}: for a faithfully flat P its totalisation is D in degree 0, while over Z_p[[q−1]] there is R (namely Z_p⟨T⟩) with qΩ_{R/D} not isomorphic to D in degree 0.

**Acceptance.** For R = D/I and P = D the cosimplicial ring is constant with value D. For D = Z_p[[q−1]], I = (q−1), R = Z_p⟨T⟩ and P = D⟨T⟩ (small variant): the term of degree 1 is D⟨T_0, T_1⟩{φ(T_1 − T_0)/[p]_q}^∧. Two choices of presentation give canonically isomorphic objects of D(D).

The ordinary nerve of D→P is insufficient. `pr6_cech_alexander_weakly_initial_base` needs its supplier carrier: The presentation carrier must record a completely ind-smooth δ-algebra, its surjection to R, and the termwise q-PD envelopes. <a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-6-gamma-extension-to-q-pd-envelope"></a>

### Extension of the automorphisms γ_s to the q-PD envelope

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/gamma-extension-to-q-pd-envelope` · lemma. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/QCrys/Basic`.

Let (P, S, J) be a framed q-PD datum (so D is flat over A). For each s ∈ S the automorphism γ_s of P extends uniquely to an automorphism of the q-PD envelope D_{J,q}(P) that is congruent to the identity modulo (q−1)X_s. The extensions are δ-D-algebra automorphisms and commute pairwise; (q−1)X_s is a nonzerodivisor on D_{J,q}(P), so the q-derivatives ∇_{q,s} := (γ_s − 1)/((q−1)X_s) are defined on D_{J,q}(P) and commute; and they lift the derivations ∂/∂X_s of the p-completed PD envelope D_{J,q}(P)/(q−1) of P/(q−1) → R.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** (P, S, J) is a framed q-PD datum over a q-PD pair (D, I) with D flat over A. This lemma and the resulting q-derivatives on D_{J,q}(P) are kept by PR.6 (RT-AREA-etale/28); the q-derivatives on P itself are QW.6's. The referenced statement is Lemma 16.10; the source uses the wrong statement type in that reference (PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22/E27).

**Construction or proof.**

1. It suffices to extend γ_s to an endomorphism of D_{J,q}(P) congruent to the identity modulo (q−1)X_s; such an endomorphism of a derived complete ring is an automorphism.
2. Consider P → P → D_{J,q}(P), the first map being γ_s. All rings are A-flat, so by the universal property of the envelope as a free δ-algebra (q-pd-envelope) it suffices that φ(γ_s(f)) ∈ [p]_q·D_{J,q}(P) for f ∈ J. Write γ_s(f) = f + (q−1)X_s·g with g ∈ P; then φ(γ_s(f)) = φ(f) + [p]_q·(q−1)·X_s^p·φ(g), using φ(q−1) = (q−1)[p]_q and δ(X_s) = 0.
3. The same formula shows that the extension is congruent to the identity modulo (q−1)X_s. Uniqueness and commutation: D_{J,q}(P) is topologically generated as a δ-P-algebra by the elements φ(f)/[p]_q, f ∈ J, and is [p]_q-torsion-free.
4. Lifting ∂/∂X_s: identify D_{J,q}(P)/(q−1) with the p-completed PD envelope (q-pd-envelope-base-change (b)) and reduce to the statement on P/(q−1), which is QW.6's reduction modulo q − 1, by torsion-freeness and density.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/framed-q-pd-datum`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-6-framed-q-pd-datum); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/q-pd-envelope`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-6-q-pd-envelope); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/q-pd-envelope-base-change`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-6-q-pd-envelope-base-change); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/q-divided-power-operation`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-6-q-divided-power-operation); `QWittVectors:QW.6`.

**Acceptance.** P = Z_p[[q−1]]⟨X⟩, J = (q−1, X), z = φ(X)/[p]_q: γ(z) = q^p z = z + (q−1)X·X^{p−1}, so ∇_q(z) = X^{p−1}, lifting ∂/∂X(X^p/p) = X^{p−1}. For J = (q−1)P the envelope is P and the extension is γ_s itself.

**Sources.** [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Lemma 16.21 and its proof. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 115. the statement and the proof; the node adds the consequences recorded after the lemma in Construction 16.20.

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-6-q-crystalline-crystalline-comparison"></a>

### q-crystalline and crystalline cohomology

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/q-crystalline-crystalline-comparison` · theorem. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/QCrys/Basic`.

Let (D, I) be a q-PD pair and R a p-completely smooth D/I-algebra. There is a canonical identification qΩ_{R/D} ⊗̂^L_D D/(q−1) ≃ RΓ_crys(R/(D/(q−1))) of commutative algebra objects of D(D/(q−1)), where the right side is the crystalline cohomology of Spf(R) relative to the p-adic PD thickening D/(q−1) → D/I, whose ideal I·D/(q−1) has divided powers by delta-pd-pairs. Consequences (Remark 16.15 (1)): a map of derived (p,[p]_q)-complete D-complexes is an isomorphism if and only if its completed base change to D/(q−1) is; hence R ↦ qΩ_{R/D} is a sheaf for the Zariski topology on p-completely smooth D/I-algebras, and defines a Zariski sheaf qΩ_{𝔛/D} of commutative algebras on every smooth p-adic formal scheme 𝔛 over D/I, whose reduction modulo q − 1 is the pushforward of the crystalline structure sheaf.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** (D, I) is a q-PD pair; R is p-completely smooth over D/I. The cohomology object in the proof is qΩ_{R/D}; the source abbreviation omits its relative input (PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22/E27). Crystalline cohomology over a p-adic PD base and its computation by PD envelopes are owned by CrystallineCohomology:CR.2 and CR.0. The ringed q-crystalline site of a non-affine formal scheme (Remark 16.15 (2)) is not developed in the source and is not used.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Compute qΩ_{R/D} by the cosimplicial ring D_{J^•,q}(F^•) of q-crystalline-cech-alexander.
2. The completed base change − ⊗̂^L_D D/(q−1) commutes with the totalisation (q-pd-homological-properties (3)), so the left side is computed by the cosimplicial ring D_{J^•,q}(F^•) ⊗̂^L_D D/(q−1).
3. By q-pd-envelope-base-change (b) this is the cosimplicial p-completed PD envelope of J^•/(q−1) ⊂ F^•/(q−1), a Čech–Alexander complex computing RΓ_crys(R/(D/(q−1))) (CR.2).
4. Sheaf property: D is derived (q−1)-complete (q-pd-homological-properties (1)), so derived Nakayama reduces isomorphy to D/(q−1); combine with Zariski descent for crystalline cohomology (CR.2).

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/q-crystalline-cech-alexander`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-6-q-crystalline-cech-alexander); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/q-pd-envelope-base-change`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-6-q-pd-envelope-base-change); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/q-pd-homological-properties`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-6-q-pd-homological-properties); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/delta-pd-pairs`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-6-delta-pd-pairs); `CrystallineCohomology:CR.2`; `CrystallineCohomology:CR.0`.

**Acceptance.** D = Z_p[[q−1]], I = (q−1), R p-completely smooth over Z_p: qΩ_{R/D} ⊗̂^L_D Z_p ≃ RΓ_crys(R/Z_p), the p-completed de Rham complex of R; so qΩ_{R/D} is a q-deformation of de Rham cohomology. D with q = 1: the statement is the identity, qΩ_{R/D} = RΓ_crys(R/D). D = A_inf, I = (ξ): qΩ_{R/A_inf} ⊗̂^L A_inf/(q−1) ≃ RΓ_crys(R/(A_inf/(q−1))).

**Sources.** [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Theorem 16.14 and its proof. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 112. the statement and its proof. [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Remark 16.15 (1). Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 112. the Zariski sheaf property and the globalisation.

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-6-q-pd-thickening-invariance"></a>

### Invariance under q-PD thickenings of the base

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/q-pd-thickening-invariance` · theorem. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/QCrys/Basic`.

Let (D, J) → (D, I) be a morphism of q-PD pairs that is the identity on the underlying δ-ring, so J ⊂ I are two q-PD ideals of D (for example J = (q−1)). Assume R is p-completely smooth over D/I and choose a p-completely smooth lift R̃ over D/J. Base change along D/J→D/I identifies R̃ with R; the resulting comparison qΩ_{R̃/D}≃qΩ_{R/D} is canonical, the first taken relative to (D, J) and the second relative to (D, I). It is induced by the functor (R̃/D)_{q-crys} → (R/D)_{q-crys} sending a thickening (E, K) with R̃ → E/K to (E, K_I), where K_I is the derived (p,[p]_q)-complete ideal of E generated by K and I·E, with the induced map R = R̃ ⊗̂_{D/J} D/I → E/K_I; this functor does not change the underlying δ-D-algebra.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** Both (D, J) and (D, I) are q-PD pairs on the same δ-ring; R̃ ⊗̂_{D/J} D/I ≅ R. The printed proof writes 'E → E/K ≃ R̃' for an object of the site; objects only carry a map R̃ → E/K, and the functor is defined on all of them as stated here (source issue PrismaticCohomology/E62). The identification is compatible with Frobenius and multiplication, since it is induced by a functor of sites that is the identity on structure rings.

**Construction or proof.**

1. (E, K + I·E) satisfies condition (1) of q-pd-pair: it holds on K and on the image of I, hence on the ideal they generate by fact (vii) of q-divided-power-operation; the derived complete ideal K_I it generates is then a q-PD ideal by q-pd-homological-properties (4).
2. The functor is the identity on the rings E, so it induces a map qΩ_{R̃/D} → qΩ_{R/D} of commutative algebras compatible with Frobenius.
3. Take a presentation P → R̃ and compose with R̃ → R. By inspection of the proof of q-pd-envelope the q-PD envelopes of the two kernels in F^• are the same rings, since the envelope ring only adjoins φ(x_i)/[p]_q for the regular sequence and does not depend on the base ideal; so the Čech–Alexander complex computing qΩ_{R̃/D} also computes qΩ_{R/D}.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/q-crystalline-cech-alexander`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-6-q-crystalline-cech-alexander); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/q-crystalline-site`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-6-q-crystalline-site); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/q-pd-envelope`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-6-q-pd-envelope); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/q-pd-homological-properties`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-6-q-pd-homological-properties); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/q-divided-power-operation`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-6-q-divided-power-operation).

**Acceptance.** D = A_inf, J = (q−1) ⊂ I = (ξ): for R̃ p-completely smooth over A_inf/(q−1) lifting R over O_C, qΩ_{R̃/A_inf} ≃ qΩ_{R/A_inf}. For q = 1 this is the invariance of crystalline cohomology under enlarging the PD ideal of the base. For J = I and R̃ = R the identification is the identity.

**Sources.** [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Theorem 16.17. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 113. the statement. [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Theorem 16.17, proof. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 113. the functor of sites and the comparison of Čech–Alexander complexes.

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-6-framed-q-de-rham-complex"></a>

### The q-de Rham complex of a framed q-PD datum

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/framed-q-de-rham-complex` · construction. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/QCrys/Basic`.

Let (P, S, J) be a framed q-PD datum over a q-PD pair (D, I) with D flat over A. Its q-de Rham complex is the Koszul complex of the commuting endomorphisms ∇_{q,s} (s ∈ S) of the q-PD envelope: qΩ^{*,□}_{D_{J,q}(P)/D} := (D_{J,q}(P) → D_{J,q}(P) ⊗̂_P Ω^1_{P/D} → D_{J,q}(P) ⊗̂_P Ω^2_{P/D} → …), where Ω^1_{P/D} is the completed direct sum of the P·dX_s and ∇_q(f) = Σ_s ∇_{q,s}(f) dX_s; it is a cochain complex of D-modules, and an instance of the Koszul complex of commuting q-derivations of QWittVectors:QW.6, applied to the ring D_{J,q}(P) with the elements X_s and the automorphisms of gamma-extension-to-q-pd-envelope. Properties. (a) If J = I·P with I = (q−1), then D_{J,q}(P) = P and the complex is the framed q-de Rham complex qΩ^{*,□}_{P/D} of QW.6. (b) Functoriality: a morphism of framed q-PD data (P, S, J) → (P′, S′, J′), which by definition is injective on coordinates, induces a morphism of complexes qΩ^{*,□}_{D_{J,q}(P)/D} → qΩ^{*,□′}_{D_{J′,q}(P′)/D}; a D-algebra map identifying two coordinates (for instance a codegeneracy of the Čech nerve) does not. (c) Reduction: the complex modulo q − 1 is the de Rham complex of the p-completed PD envelope of J/(q−1) ⊂ P/(q−1). (d) Frobenius: ∇_{q,s}∘φ = [p]_q·X_s^{p−1}·φ∘∇_{q,s}, so the maps f·dX_{s_1}⋯dX_{s_i} ↦ φ(f)·∏_j([p]_q X_{s_j}^{p−1})·dX_{s_1}⋯dX_{s_i} form a φ_D-semilinear endomorphism of the complex. (e) Toric form: if the X_s are units of P the complex is isomorphic to the Koszul complex of the logarithmic q-derivatives X_s∇_{q,s} = (γ_s − 1)/(q−1), which is η_{(q−1)} applied to the Koszul complex of the endomorphisms γ_s − 1 (the décalage of AInfCohomology:AI.1 on (q−1)-torsion-free complexes).

**Hypotheses and conventions.** (P, S, J) is a framed q-PD datum; D is flat over A. For infinite S the complex is the completed filtered colimit over finite subsets of S. (b): the source prints the last sentence of Construction 16.20 with the framing A[{X_s}] → P; the framing D[{X_s}] → P is meant (source issue PrismaticCohomology/E62). (d) is not printed in §16; it follows from φ∘γ_s = γ_s∘φ and φ((q−1)X_s) = [p]_q(q−1)X_s^p, and is what the Frobenius compatibility in Theorem 17.2 uses. The Koszul complex of commuting endomorphisms and the identification in (e) are AI.1's (BMS1 Definition 7.1, Lemma 7.9); the Koszul complex of q-derivations is QW.6's.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Extend the γ_s to D_{J,q}(P) and form the commuting q-derivatives ∇_{q,s} (gamma-extension-to-q-pd-envelope); take their Koszul complex (QW.6, AI.1).
2. (b): let α : D_{J,q}(P) → D_{J′,q}(P′) be induced by P → P′ and the universal property. For t ∈ S′ outside the image of S one has γ_t∘α = α: the identity holds on the étale coordinates X_s, hence on P by complete étaleness of the framing, and on the envelope because it is [p]_q-torsion-free and generated over P by the elements φ(f)/[p]_q. So α commutes with the q-derivatives indexed by S and is killed by the others.
3. (c): q-pd-envelope-base-change (b) and the last statement of gamma-extension-to-q-pd-envelope.
4. (d): apply φ to (q−1)X_s∇_{q,s}(f) = γ_s(f) − f and cancel the nonzerodivisor (q−1)X_s. (e): X_s is a unit, so the Koszul complexes of ∇_{q,s} and X_s∇_{q,s} are isomorphic; then use η_f Kos(g_i) ≅ Kos(g_i/f) for f dividing all g_i (AI.1).

BS22 proof of Theorem 17.2: for the tori P_Σ its toric form is η_{q−1} of the Koszul complex of γ_s − 1, which maps to the complex computing AΩ_R. BMS2 Remark 9.11 (PR.3) and BMS2 §10 (PR.4): the Nygaard filtration and the syntomic complexes are computed in these coordinates, using φ(dlog_q X_s) = [p]_q dlog_q X_s from (d). **Planning API.**

- `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys.FramedDatum.envelope` (constructor): The q-PD envelope D_{J,q}(P) of a framed q-PD datum.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys.FramedDatum.envelopeMap` (data): The canonical map P → D_{J,q}(P).
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys.FramedDatum.envelopeFramed` (structure): The extended structure on D_{J,q}(P): the images of the coordinates, the extended automorphisms γ_s, the q-derivatives ∇_{q,s} and the δ-structure.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys.FramedDatum.envelopeFramed_gamma` (compatibility): The extended γ_s restricts to γ_s on P.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys.FramedDatum.qDeRhamComplex` (constructor): The cochain complex qΩ^{*,□}_{D_{J,q}(P)/D} of D-modules.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys.FramedDatum.qDeRhamMap` (functoriality): The morphism of complexes induced by a morphism of framed q-PD data.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys.FramedDatum.qDeRhamFrobenius` (data): The φ_D-semilinear endomorphism of (d).
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys.FramedAlgebra.nabla_frobenius` (relation): ∇_{q,s}(φ(f)) = [p]_q·X_s^{p−1}·φ(∇_{q,s}(f)) on a framed algebra in which (q−1)X_s is a nonzerodivisor and δ(q) = 0.

**Unit tests.**

- `pr6_qdr_polynomial_nabla` (computation): In the polynomial ring D[X] with the automorphism X ↦ qX: γ(X^{n+1}) − X^{n+1} = (q−1)·X·([n+1]_q·X^n).
- `pr6_qdr_at_q_one_derivative` (compatibility): The formula Σ_n a_n [n]_q X^{n−1} for the q-derivative on D[X] specialises at q = 1 to Mathlib's Polynomial.derivative.
- `pr6_qdr_no_coordinates` (degenerate): For S = ∅ all terms of the complex in nonzero degrees vanish: the complex is D_{J,q}(P) in degree 0.
- `pr6_qdr_two_framings_differ` (non-example): For two framed structures on P with one coordinate and X′ = X + 1, with (q−1)X and (q−1)X′ nonzerodivisors: ∇′(X²) = ∇(X²) + (q−1); so the complex depends on the framing as a complex.
- `pr6_qdr_leibniz` (characterisation): The twisted Leibniz rule ∇_{q,s}(fg) = f·∇_{q,s}(g) + γ_s(g)·∇_{q,s}(f) holds when (q−1)X_s is a nonzerodivisor.

A torus: P = D⟨X^{±1}⟩: the complex is D⟨X^{±1}⟩ → D⟨X^{±1}⟩ dlog X, X^n ↦ [n]_q X^n dlog X, with [n]_q = (q^n − 1)/(q − 1) for n ∈ Z. S = ∅: the complex is the envelope D_{J,q}(P) in degree 0. It is D for the base datum P = D, J = I; a nontrivial completely étale P over D need not equal D.

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-6-q-crystalline-prismatic-comparison"></a>

### q-crystalline and prismatic cohomology

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/q-crystalline-prismatic-comparison` · theorem. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/QCrys/Basic`.

Let (D, I) be a q-PD pair and R a p-completely smooth D/I-algebra. Let R^{(1)} := R ⊗̂_{D/I, φ_D} D/([p]_q) be the p-completed base change of R along the map D/I → D/([p]_q) induced by φ_D (it exists because φ_D(I) ⊂ [p]_q D); it is a p-completely smooth D/([p]_q)-algebra. Let Δ_{R^{(1)}/D} be the prismatic cohomology of R^{(1)} relative to the bounded prism (D, ([p]_q)). Then there is a canonical isomorphism α : Δ_{R^{(1)}/D} ≃ qΩ_{R/D}. The map α is induced by the functor (R/D)_{q-crys} → (R^{(1)}/D)_Δ sending (E, J) to the prism (E, ([p]_q)) with the map R^{(1)} → E/([p]_q) obtained by linearising R → E/J → E/([p]_q), the second map being induced by φ_E. By construction α is a map of commutative algebra objects of D(D), compatible with the Frobenius endomorphisms and natural in R and in (D, I).

**Hypotheses and conventions.** (D, I) is a q-PD pair; R is p-completely smooth over D/I. The Frobenius twist R^{(1)} is part of the statement: R itself is not an algebra over D/([p]_q) unless q = 1. The printed proof writes 'E → E/J ≅ R'; objects carry only a map R → E/J, which suffices (source issue PrismaticCohomology/E62). The printed proof identifies the source and the target of α modulo q − 1 with crystalline cohomology and does not say that the reduction of α is that identification; step 5 supplies this (source issue PrismaticCohomology/E66). The reduction to I = (q−1) uses a lift of R to a p-completely smooth D/(q−1)-algebra, which the source uses implicitly.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Construction of α: for (E, J) in the site, φ_E(J) ⊂ [p]_q E, so φ_E induces a φ_D-linear map R → E/J → E/([p]_q), hence a D-linear map R^{(1)} → E/([p]_q) and an object of the prismatic site of R^{(1)} over (D, ([p]_q)); evaluating the prismatic structure sheaf gives α.
2. Reduction to I = (q−1): lift R to a p-completely smooth D/(q−1)-algebra R̃ (the kernel of D/(q−1) → D/I consists of elements f with f^p ∈ p·D/(q−1), so smooth algebras lift; DD.1) and apply q-pd-thickening-invariance; R̃^{(1)} = R^{(1)} because φ_D factors through D/I.
3. It suffices to prove that α is an isomorphism after (p,[p]_q)-completed base change to D/(q−1) (q-pd-homological-properties (2)).
4. D → D/(q−1) is a map of bounded prisms (D, ([p]_q)) → (D/(q−1), (p)); by PR.1's prismatic-base-change, Δ_{R^{(1)}/D} ⊗̂^L_D D/(q−1) ≃ Δ_{R̄^{(1)}/(D/(q−1))} = φ^*Δ_{R̄/(D/(q−1))} with R̄ = R/p; by PR.1's crystalline-comparison this is RΓ_crys(R̄/(D/(q−1))) = RΓ_crys(R/(D/(q−1))), which is qΩ_{R/D} ⊗̂^L_D D/(q−1) by q-crystalline-crystalline-comparison.
5. The reduction of α is this composite: both α and the comparison map of PR.1's crystalline-comparison (general case of BS22 Theorem 5.2) are induced by sending a (q-)PD thickening E, whose ideal is carried by φ into the prism ideal, to the prism E; the equality is checked on the Čech–Alexander complexes of q-crystalline-cech-alexander and their reductions.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/q-pd-thickening-invariance`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-6-q-pd-thickening-invariance); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/q-crystalline-crystalline-comparison`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-6-q-crystalline-crystalline-comparison); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/q-crystalline-cech-alexander`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-6-q-crystalline-cech-alexander); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/q-crystalline-site`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-6-q-crystalline-site); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/q-pd-homological-properties`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-6-q-pd-homological-properties); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/relative-prismatic-site`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-relative-prismatic-site); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/relative-prismatic-cohomology`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-relative-prismatic-cohomology); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/prismatic-base-change`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-prismatic-base-change); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/crystalline-comparison`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-crystalline-comparison); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/frobenius-on-prismatic-cohomology`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-frobenius-on-prismatic-cohomology); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/crystalline-prism`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-crystalline-prism); `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`.

**Acceptance.** D = Z_p[[q−1]], I = (q−1), R p-completely smooth over Z_p: R^{(1)} = R ⊗̂_{Z_p} Z_p[ζ_p] and Δ_{R^{(1)}/D} ≃ qΩ_{R/D}. D = A_inf, I = (ξ): R^{(1)} = R ⊗_{A_inf, φ} A_inf and Δ_{R^{(1)}/A_inf} = φ^*Δ_{R/A_inf}, the prismatic cohomology relative to (A_inf, (ξ)) pulled back along φ. q = 1: the statement is the crystalline comparison of PR.1 for the PD ideal I. R = D/I: both sides are D and α is the identity.

**Sources.** [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Theorem 16.18. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 113. the statement, with the Frobenius twist R^{(1)}.
