<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-6-q-poincare-lemma"></a>

### q-Poincaré comparison of the Čech–Koszul bicomplex

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/q-poincare-lemma` · lemma. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/PR6`.

For a framed q-PD datum (P,S,J) over D flat over Z_p[[q−1]], the augmentation from the framed q-de Rham complex of its q-PD envelope into the completed Čech–Koszul bicomplex is a quasi-isomorphism; the other augmentation identifies that total complex with q-crystalline cohomology.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** Use finite coordinate sets first and pass to the filtered colimit with derived completion. The complexes and their cofibres are derived (p,q−1)-complete.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Construct the bicomplex from the q-PD Čech nerve and the commuting γ_s on each envelope.
2. For positive de Rham degree, the cosimplicial rows are contracted by the usual extra-degeneracy argument; degree zero is the q-PD Čech complex. For each face, the column map is a quasi-isomorphism modulo q−1 and hence before reduction by completeness.
3. Modulo q−1 it is the ordinary crystalline/de Rham Poincaré comparison over the p-adic PD base, supplied by CR.2.
4. Its cofibres are derived (p,q−1)-complete, so derived Nakayama lifts both quasi-isomorphisms.
5. Infinite coordinate sets are handled by the stated completed filtered colimit; this proves the additive comparison, with multiplicativity left as its separately recorded gap.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/gamma-extension-to-q-pd-envelope`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-6-gamma-extension-to-q-pd-envelope); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/framed-q-de-rham-complex`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-6-framed-q-de-rham-complex); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/q-crystalline-cech-alexander`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-6-q-crystalline-cech-alexander); `CrystallineCohomology:CR.2`; `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`.

**Consumers.** PR.6/q-de-rham-comparison: Provides the additive Čech–Koszul quasi-isomorphism..

**Acceptance.** With no coordinates the complex is the envelope in degree zero. At q=1 the comparison reduces to the usual crystalline Poincaré lemma.

**Sources.** [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Theorem 16.22 and proof, §16. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 115. The two augmentations of the bicomplex are checked modulo q−1 and lifted by completeness..

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-6-q-de-rham-comparison"></a>

### q-de Rham and q-crystalline comparison

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/q-de-rham-comparison` · theorem. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/QCrys/Basic`.

Let (D, I) be a q-PD pair with D flat over A = Z_p[[q−1]], R a p-completely smooth D/I-algebra and (P, S, J) a framed q-PD datum with P/J ≅ R. Then there is a canonical quasi-isomorphism qΩ_{R/D} ≃ qΩ^{*,□}_{D_{J,q}(P)/D}: the q-de Rham complex of the framed q-PD datum computes q-crystalline cohomology. The identification is natural for morphisms of framed q-PD data injective on coordinate sets lying over maps R → R′, and it carries the Frobenius φ_{R/D} to the Frobenius of framed-q-de-rham-complex (d).

**Hypotheses and conventions.** (D, I) is a q-PD pair with D flat over A; (P, S, J) is a framed q-PD datum for R. The source states the quasi-isomorphism; naturality in the framed datum and the compatibility with Frobenius are visible in its proof (the bicomplex is functorial and carries the Frobenius) and are used in Theorem 17.2. For q = 1 this is the comparison of crystalline cohomology with the de Rham complex of a PD envelope, owned by CrystallineCohomology:CR.2.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Let P^• be the completed Čech nerve of D → P; the coordinates S define coordinates S^n on P^n by coproducts, and J^n = ker(P^n → P → R) gives framed q-PD data (P^n, S^n, J^n). The coface maps are morphisms of framed q-PD data (injective on coordinates); the codegeneracies are not and do not commute with ∇_q. Apply framed-q-de-rham-complex to get complexes M^{n,*} = qΩ^{*,□}_{D_{J^n,q}(P^n)} with maps of complexes for the cofaces; each row M^{•,i} = D_{J^•,q}(P^•) ⊗̂ Ω^i_{P^•/D} is a cosimplicial D-module. Form the double complex with horizontal differential the alternating sum of the cofaces. In a semi-cosimplicial module whose cofaces are all isomorphisms the cofaces of each level coincide, which is what step 4 uses.
2. Rows: for i > 0 the cosimplicial D-module M^{•,i} is homotopy equivalent to 0 as a cosimplicial module, by the standard argument for the crystalline case (Stacks project, Tag 07JP; CR.2).
3. Columns: every face map P^i → P^j induces a quasi-isomorphism M^{i,*} → M^{j,*}: modulo q − 1 this is the PD Poincaré lemma (framed-q-de-rham-complex (c); CR.2), and the terms are derived (q−1)-complete and (q−1)-torsion-free, so derived Nakayama gives the claim.
4. Therefore the complex attached to the cosimplicial module M^{•,0} is quasi-isomorphic to the column M^{0,*}. The former is the small Čech–Alexander complex of q-crystalline-cech-alexander (5) and computes qΩ_{R/D}; the latter is qΩ^{*,□}_{D_{J,q}(P)/D}.
5. Naturality and Frobenius: the bicomplex is functorial in the framed datum by framed-q-de-rham-complex (b) and carries the Frobenius of (d), which on row 0 is the Frobenius of the δ-rings D_{J^•,q}(P^•).

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/framed-q-de-rham-complex`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-6-framed-q-de-rham-complex); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/gamma-extension-to-q-pd-envelope`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-6-gamma-extension-to-q-pd-envelope); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/q-crystalline-cech-alexander`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-6-q-crystalline-cech-alexander); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/q-crystalline-crystalline-comparison`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-6-q-crystalline-crystalline-comparison); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/q-pd-envelope-base-change`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-6-q-pd-envelope-base-change); `CrystallineCohomology:CR.2`; `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`; [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/q-poincare-lemma`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-6-q-poincare-lemma).

**Acceptance.** One polynomial coordinate: qΩ_{Z_p⟨X⟩/Z_p[[q−1]]} is computed by Z_p[[q−1]]⟨X⟩ → Z_p[[q−1]]⟨X⟩dX, X^n ↦ [n]_q X^{n−1}dX. A torus over A_inf: qΩ_{O_C⟨x^{±1}⟩/A_inf} is computed by A_inf⟨x^{±1}⟩ → A_inf⟨x^{±1}⟩ dlog x, x^n ↦ [n]_q x^n dlog x. Modulo q − 1 the quasi-isomorphism reduces to the statement that the de Rham complex of the p-completed PD envelope of P/(q−1) → R computes RΓ_crys(R/(D/(q−1))).

**Sources.** [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Theorem 16.22. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 115. the statement. ### Change of framing and the cocycle identity

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/change-of-framing` · theorem. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/QCrys/Basic`.

Let (D, I) be a q-PD pair with D flat over A and R a p-completely smooth D/I-algebra. Let (P, S, J) and (P′, S′, J′) be two framed q-PD data for R; the case P = P′ with two coordinate systems is included. Put P″ = P ⊗̂_D P′ (derived (p,[p]_q)-completed), S″ = S ⊔ S′ and J″ = ker(P″ → R). Then (P″, S″, J″) is a framed q-PD datum for R, and the two morphisms of framed q-PD data induce quasi-isomorphisms qΩ^{*,□}_{D_{J,q}(P)/D} → qΩ^{*,□″}_{D_{J″,q}(P″)/D} ← qΩ^{*,□′}_{D_{J′,q}(P′)/D}. The resulting isomorphism c_{□,□′} in D(D) equals the composite of the identifications of q-de-rham-comparison with qΩ_{R/D}. Consequently c_{□,□} = id and c_{□′,□″}∘c_{□,□′} = c_{□,□″} for three framed data (the cocycle identity); the isomorphisms are compatible with Frobenius and with maps R → R′ covered by morphisms of framed data; the framed q-de Rham complex is independent of the framing up to canonical isomorphism in D(D); and on a smooth p-adic formal scheme 𝔛 over D/I the complexes of framed affine charts descend to the Zariski sheaf qΩ_{𝔛/D} of q-crystalline-crystalline-comparison.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** Both data are framed q-PD data for the same R over the same q-PD pair, D flat over A. The complexes of two framings are different complexes; only their images in D(D), with Frobenius and multiplication, are identified. The statement is what the source calls independence 'up to canonical quasi-isomorphism' of the framing; it is deduced from Construction 16.20 and the proof of Theorem 16.22, where the same argument is applied to the face maps of the Čech nerve.

**Construction or proof.**

1. (P″, S″) is a framed D-algebra: the framing is the completed tensor product of the two framings; J″ is the kernel of the surjection P″ → R.
2. The maps P → P″ ← P′ are morphisms of framed q-PD data, so framed-q-de-rham-complex (b) gives the two maps of complexes.
3. They are quasi-isomorphisms: modulo q − 1 they are the comparison maps between the PD de Rham complexes of two embeddings of R and of their product, quasi-isomorphisms by the independence of the embedding in CR.2; the terms are derived (q−1)-complete and (q−1)-torsion-free, so derived Nakayama applies. This is the column argument of the proof of Theorem 16.22.
4. Agreement with q-de-rham-comparison: the bicomplex of that proof is functorial in the framed datum, so the two maps commute with the identifications with qΩ_{R/D}. The cocycle identity and c_{□,□} = id follow formally.
5. Descent: qΩ_{−/D} is a Zariski sheaf (q-crystalline-crystalline-comparison) and the identifications are natural for localisation.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/q-de-rham-comparison`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-6-q-de-rham-comparison); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/framed-q-de-rham-complex`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-6-framed-q-de-rham-complex); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/q-crystalline-crystalline-comparison`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-6-q-crystalline-crystalline-comparison); `CrystallineCohomology:CR.2`; `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`.

**Acceptance.** Two framings: R = Z_p⟨T⟩ over Z_p[[q−1]] with coordinates T and T + 1. The complexes differ, ∇^{T+1}(T²) − ∇^{T}(T²) = q − 1, and are identified through the datum on Z_p[[q−1]]⟨T_0, T_1⟩{φ(T_1 − T_0)/[p]_q}^∧ with coordinates T_0 and T_1 + 1. Three framings T, T + 1, T + 2 of Z_p⟨T⟩: the three isomorphisms satisfy the cocycle identity. Equal framings give the identity.

**Sources.** [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Construction 16.20, functoriality. <a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-6-ainf-omega-comparison-map"></a>

### The all-coordinates comparison map from q-crystalline cohomology to AΩ

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/ainf-omega-comparison-map` · construction. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.AOmega` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/AOmega/Basic`.

Let C be a perfectoid field of characteristic 0 containing μ_{p^∞}, A = A_inf(O_C) with q = [ε] and ξ = φ^{-1}([p]_q), and the q-PD pair (A, (ξ)) of ainf-q-pd-pair. Let R be a p-completely smooth O_C-algebra that is very small: R/p is generated over O_C/p by units, and R is small, that is, there are units x_1, …, x_n of R defining a formally étale map O_C⟨x_1^{±1}, …, x_n^{±1}⟩ → R. Put S = R^× and let C_S be the filtered poset of finite subsets Σ ⊂ S such that A[x_s^{±1} : s ∈ Σ]^∧ → R, x_s ↦ s, is surjective. For Σ ∈ C_S let P_Σ = A[x_s^{±1} : s ∈ Σ]^∧ be the formal torus over A, with δ(x_s) = 0 and the automorphisms γ_s scaling x_s by q, and J_Σ = ker(P_Σ → R); (P_Σ, Σ, J_Σ) is a framed q-PD datum. (1) The q-side. qΩ_{R/A} is computed by the complex colim_{Σ ∈ C_S} Kos_c(D_{J_Σ,q}(P_Σ); {∇_{q,s}}_{s∈Σ}), which is functorial for maps injective on the chosen unit-coordinate sets. (2) The AΩ-side. Let Δ_Σ = ∏_{s∈Σ} Z_p(1) and let R_{Σ,∞} be the p-completed integral closure of R in the pro-étale Δ_Σ-torsor over R[1/p] obtained by extracting all p-power roots of the x_s; R_{Σ,∞} is perfectoid, and σ_s denotes the automorphism of A_inf(R_{Σ,∞}) induced by the s-th basis vector of Δ_Σ. Then AΩ_R is computed by colim_{Σ ∈ C_S} η_{q−1} Kos_c(A_inf(R_{Σ,∞}); {σ_s − 1}_{s∈Σ}), and already by each term whose Σ contains units x_1, …, x_n defining a formally étale map O_C⟨x_1^{±1}, …, x_n^{±1}⟩ → R. (3) The map. For each Σ ∈ C_S there is a unique map of δ-A-algebras μ_0 : D_{J_Σ,q}(P_Σ) → A_inf(R_{Σ,∞}) extending the δ-map P_Σ → A_inf(R_{Σ,∞}), x_s ↦ [(s, s^{1/p}, s^{1/p²}, …)]; it intertwines γ_s with σ_s and is compatible with enlarging Σ. It induces maps Kos_c(D_{J_Σ,q}(P_Σ); {∇_{q,s}}) ≅ η_{q−1} Kos_c(D_{J_Σ,q}(P_Σ); {γ_s − 1}) → η_{q−1} Kos_c(A_inf(R_{Σ,∞}); {σ_s − 1}), and in the colimit over Σ the comparison map μ_R : qΩ_{R/A} → AΩ_R. It is a map of E_1-A-algebras (represented by differential graded algebras), natural for maps injective on the chosen unit-coordinate sets and compatible with the Frobenius endomorphisms. Full naturality under arbitrary maps of R is a requested extension recorded in the gaps. For a general p-completely smooth O_C-algebra, and for smooth formal O_C-schemes, μ is obtained by gluing, the very small affine opens being a basis. Naturality in R is asserted for maps injective on the chosen coordinate sets; an arbitrary map identifying two units requires a different family-indexed construction.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** C is a perfectoid field of characteristic 0 containing μ_{p^∞}; R is p-completely smooth over O_C and very small. The colimit in (2) is over C_S; the printed index set is a misprint registered as PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22/E28. AΩ_R, the perfectoid rings R_{Σ,∞}, the identification of continuous cohomology of Δ_Σ with a Koszul complex and the statement that the complexes in (2) compute AΩ_R are owned by AInfCohomology AI.3 and AI.4 (BMS1 Lemma 7.3, Theorem 9.4 (iii), and the all-coordinates construction). Kos_c denotes the completed Koszul complex: for the q-derivatives it is the complex of framed-q-de-rham-complex. The source asserts that R_{Σ,∞} is perfectoid for every Σ in C_S by a general reference, and notes that the subset of those Σ containing a framing is cofinal and suffices; for these the perfectoidness follows from almost purity (AI.3, AI.4). The plan uses this cofinal subset. The construction uses all finite generating sets of units, and is independent of enlarging such a set. A map R → R′ can identify two units, so this subset-indexed construction alone does not prove arbitrary naturality. A family-indexed or descent construction with coherent transition maps remains a recorded prerequisite.

**Construction or proof.**

1. (1): q-de-rham-comparison for each Σ, the functoriality of framed-q-de-rham-complex (b) in Σ, and a filtered colimit.
2. (2): import from AI.3 and AI.4. Each Σ containing a framing gives a complex computing AΩ_R by BMS1 Theorem 9.4 (iii) and the enlargement criterion quoted in the source; the continuous cohomology of Δ_Σ is the Koszul complex by BMS1 Lemma 7.3 (AI.1).
3. (3), the map μ_0: let P_Σ → P_{Σ,∞} be the (p, ξ)-completed perfection (PR.0's prism-perfection). It is a perfect, completely flat δ-A-algebra, so P_{Σ,∞}/ξ is perfectoid, obtained from P_Σ/ξ by extracting p-power roots of the x_s, and P_{Σ,∞} ≅ A_inf(P_{Σ,∞}/ξ) (PR.0's perfect-prisms-perfectoid-rings). Composing with A_inf of the map to R_{Σ,∞} gives a δ-map P_Σ → A_inf(R_{Σ,∞}) lying over R → R_{Σ,∞}. Since A_inf(R_{Σ,∞}) → R_{Σ,∞} is a q-PD thickening (q-pd-homological-properties (5) applied to A → A_inf(R_{Σ,∞})), the universal property of q-pd-envelope extends it uniquely to μ_0.
4. Equivariance: σ_s∘μ_0 and μ_0∘γ_s are both the extension, by the universal property, of maps out of P_Σ that agree; so they coincide.
5. The Koszul map: the x_s are units, so the Koszul complex of the ∇_{q,s} is η_{q−1} of the Koszul complex of the γ_s − 1 (framed-q-de-rham-complex (e)); η_{q−1} is functorial for μ_0 on (q−1)-torsion-free complexes (AI.1). Multiplicativity: both Koszul complexes are differential graded algebras and μ_0 is a ring map (BMS1 Lemmas 7.5 and 6.13; AI.1). Frobenius: μ_0 is a δ-map.

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-6-q-de-rham-prismatic-comparison-zp"></a>

### The framed q-de Rham complex of a smooth Z_p-algebra and prismatic cohomology

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/q-de-rham-prismatic-comparison-zp` · theorem. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/QCrys/Basic`.

Let A = Z_p[[q−1]] with the q-de Rham prism (A, ([p]_q)), and let R be a p-completely smooth Z_p-algebra with a p-completely étale framing □ : Z_p⟨T_1, …, T_d⟩ → R. Let P be the (p, q−1)-completely étale A⟨T_1, …, T_d⟩-algebra lifting R (so P/(q−1) = R), framed by T_1, …, T_d, and let qΩ_R^□ := qΩ^{*,□}_{P/A} be its (p, q−1)-completed framed q-de Rham complex (QWittVectors:QW.6). Let R^{(1)} := R ⊗̂_{Z_p} Z_p[ζ_p], the p-completed base change of R along Z_p = A/(q−1) → A/([p]_q) = Z_p[ζ_p]. Then there are canonical isomorphisms in D(A), compatible with Frobenius, qΩ_R^□ ≃ qΩ_{R/A} ≃ Δ_{R^{(1)}/A} = RΓ_Δ(Spf(R^{(1)})/A). Consequently qΩ_R^□ is independent of the framing □ up to canonical quasi-isomorphism, is functorial in R as an object of D(A), and qΩ_R^□ ⊗^L_A A/(q−1) is the p-completed de Rham complex of R over Z_p. Scope: this is a statement for one prime p over the (p, q−1)-complete base Z_p[[q−1]]; it does not produce a theory over Z[[q−1]] or over the Habiro ring. The gluing over all primes is owned by HabiroCohomologyFoundations HQ.1–HQ.2.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** R is p-completely smooth over Z_p with a p-completely étale framing; the prism is (Z_p[[q−1]], ([p]_q)), not (Z_p[[q−1]], (q−1)). The base change to Z_p[ζ_p] is part of the statement: prismatic cohomology is taken of R^{(1)} = R ⊗̂ Z_p[ζ_p], not of R. The framed complex qΩ_R^□ itself is QW.6's object; this node proves its comparison.

**Construction or proof.**

1. (A, (q−1)) is a q-PD pair (smallest-largest-q-pd-ideals (c)) and A is flat over itself. (P, {T_i}, (q−1)P) is a framed q-PD datum for R, and D_{J,q}(P) = P because (P, (q−1)P) is already a q-PD pair, P being completely flat over A; so its q-de Rham complex is qΩ^{*,□}_{P/A} (framed-q-de-rham-complex (a)).
2. q-de-rham-comparison gives qΩ_R^□ ≃ qΩ_{R/A}.
3. q-crystalline-prismatic-comparison with I = (q−1) gives qΩ_{R/A} ≃ Δ_{R^{(1)}/A}; here φ_A induces Z_p = A/(q−1) → A/([p]_q) = Z_p[ζ_p], the structure map, so R^{(1)} = R ⊗̂_{Z_p} Z_p[ζ_p].
4. Independence of □ and functoriality: change-of-framing. Reduction modulo q − 1: q-crystalline-crystalline-comparison and the identification of RΓ_crys(R/Z_p) with the de Rham complex of the smooth lift (CR.2).

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/q-de-rham-comparison`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-6-q-de-rham-comparison); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/q-crystalline-prismatic-comparison`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-6-q-crystalline-prismatic-comparison); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/change-of-framing`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-6-change-of-framing); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/q-crystalline-crystalline-comparison`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-6-q-crystalline-crystalline-comparison); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/smallest-largest-q-pd-ideals`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-6-smallest-largest-q-pd-ideals); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/framed-q-de-rham-complex`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-6-framed-q-de-rham-complex); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/q-de-rham-prism`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-q-de-rham-prism); `QWittVectors:QW.6`; `CrystallineCohomology:CR.2`.

**Acceptance.** One polynomial coordinate: R = Z_p⟨T⟩: qΩ_R^□ = (A⟨T⟩ → A⟨T⟩dT), T^n ↦ [n]_q T^{n−1}dT. Modulo [p]_q the coefficient [n]_ζ is a unit for p ∤ n and 0 for p | n, so H^0 = Z_p[ζ_p]⟨T^p⟩ and H^1 = Z_p[ζ_p]⟨T^p⟩·T^{p−1}dT, which are R^{(1)} and Ω^1_{R^{(1)}/Z_p[ζ_p]} through T ↦ T^p, as the Hodge–Tate comparison for Δ_{R^{(1)}/A} predicts. A torus: R = Z_p⟨T^{±1}⟩: qΩ_R^□ = (A⟨T^{±1}⟩ → A⟨T^{±1}⟩ dlog T), T^n ↦ [n]_q T^n dlog T. Two framings T and T + 1 of Z_p⟨T⟩ give canonically isomorphic objects of D(A).

**Sources.** [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Example 1.9 (4). <a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-6-ainf-omega-comparison"></a>

### Comparison with AΩ

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/ainf-omega-comparison` · theorem. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.AOmega` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/AOmega/Basic`.

Let C be a perfectoid field of characteristic 0 containing μ_{p^∞}, A = A_inf(O_C), q = [ε], ξ = φ^{-1}([p]_q), and let R be a p-completely smooth O_C-algebra. Let AΩ_R be the complex of Bhatt–Morrow–Scholze (AInfCohomology:AI.3). Then the comparison map μ_R : qΩ_{R/A} → AΩ_R of ainf-omega-comparison-map is an isomorphism, and AΩ_R ≃ qΩ_{R/A} ≃ Δ_{R^{(1)}/A} = φ_A^*Δ_{R/A}. Here qΩ_{R/A} is taken relative to the q-PD pair (A, (ξ)); R^{(1)} = R ⊗_{A, φ} A is the Frobenius twist, an algebra over A/([p]_q); Δ_{R^{(1)}/A} is prismatic cohomology relative to the prism (A, ([p]_q)); and Δ_{R/A} is prismatic cohomology relative to the perfect prism (A, (ξ)) = (A_inf, ker θ). All these maps are isomorphisms of E_∞-A-algebras compatible with the Frobenius, natural in R. The Frobenius pullback is essential: φ_A is an automorphism of A, so φ_A^* only twists the A-module structure, but AΩ_R is not isomorphic to Δ_{R/A} in D(A) in general. (Remark 17.3.) The construction gives an isomorphism of E_1-A-algebras, natural in R and compatible with Frobenius; it is upgraded to an isomorphism of E_∞-A-algebras by left Kan extension to quasiregular semiperfectoid R-algebras, where it is an isomorphism of associative rings between discrete commutative rings, and then quasisyntomic descent.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** C is a perfectoid field of characteristic 0 containing μ_{p^∞}, with a fixed compatible system of p-power roots of 1; the introduction of the source states the result for C algebraically closed, §17 and BMS1 §§8–9 in this generality. R is a p-completely smooth O_C-algebra; AΩ_R is the value on Spf(R) of the complex AΩ of AI.3. The check that μ_R intertwines the two Hodge–Tate structure maps is left to the reader in the source (source issue PrismaticCohomology/E67); step 3 carries it out by reduction to the torus. The Hodge–Tate specialisation of AΩ used in step 2 carries the Frobenius twist that BMS1 Theorem 9.2 leaves implicit: R is an A_inf-algebra through θ̃ there.
- The source theorem includes arbitrary naturality. The subset-indexed construction in ainf-omega-comparison-map supplies only coordinate-injective naturality; its extension to all maps is explicitly recorded as a gap, alongside the multiplicative comparison. The theorem is a target, not a claim that these constructions are complete.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Second isomorphism: q-crystalline-prismatic-comparison for the q-PD pair (A, (ξ)). The Frobenius φ_A is an isomorphism of prisms (A, (ξ)) → (A, ([p]_q)) carrying R to R^{(1)}, so Δ_{R^{(1)}/A} = φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} by PR.1's prismatic-base-change.
2. μ_R is an isomorphism by hodge-tate-comparison-criterion (b), (c) with d = [p]_q: on the q-side, the Hodge–Tate comparison for Δ_{R^{(1)}/A} (PR.1) gives η_{qΩ} : R^{(1)} → H^0(qΩ_{R/A}/[p]_q) inducing (Ω^*_{R^{(1)}/(A/[p]_q)}, d_dR) ≅ (H^*(qΩ_{R/A}/[p]_q), β); on the AΩ-side, AΩ_R/[p]_q ≃ Ω̃_{R^{(1)}} (BMS1 Theorem 9.2) and the Hodge–Tate comparison for Ω̃ (BMS1 Theorem 8.3) give η_{AΩ} with the same property (AI.4).
3. μ_R intertwines η_{qΩ} with η_{AΩ}: both are ring maps out of R^{(1)}, natural in R, so for very small R it suffices to compare them on the images of the units s ∈ R^×, which topologically generate; each unit is the image of x under a map O_C⟨x^{±1}⟩ → R, so by naturality the check reduces to the torus, where μ is the inclusion A⟨x^{±1}⟩ → A⟨x^{±1/p^∞}⟩ and both maps are computed: on the q-side the coordinate of R^{(1)} goes to the class of φ(x) = x^p by the construction of q-crystalline-prismatic-comparison; on the AΩ-side the class of x^p reduces along θ̃ to x, since θ̃([x^♭]^p) = θ([x^♭]) = x.
4. Frobenius: μ_0 is a map of δ-rings, and both Frobenius endomorphisms are induced by the Frobenius lifts on the Koszul complexes (ainf-omega-comparison-map; AI.3 for AΩ).
5. E_∞ upgrade (Remark 17.3): left Kan extend both functors from p-completely smooth R-algebras to quasiregular semiperfectoid ones (EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E3, PR.2's derived-prismatic-cohomology). There the prismatic side is a discrete commutative ring (PR.2's qrsp-prism), so the E_1-isomorphism is an isomorphism of associative rings between discrete commutative rings, hence of commutative rings and of E_∞-rings. Quasisyntomic descent (PR.2's quasisyntomic-descent, DD.5) returns the isomorphism of E_∞-A-algebras on smooth algebras.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/ainf-omega-comparison-map`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-6-ainf-omega-comparison-map); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/hodge-tate-comparison-criterion`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-6-hodge-tate-comparison-criterion); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/q-crystalline-prismatic-comparison`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-6-q-crystalline-prismatic-comparison); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/ainf-q-pd-pair`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-6-ainf-q-pd-pair); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/hodge-tate-comparison`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-hodge-tate-comparison); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/prismatic-base-change`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-prismatic-base-change); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/frobenius-on-prismatic-cohomology`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-frobenius-on-prismatic-cohomology); `AInfCohomology:AI.3`; `AInfCohomology:AI.4`; [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/derived-prismatic-cohomology`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-derived-prismatic-cohomology); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/qrsp-prism`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-qrsp-prism); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/quasisyntomic-descent`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-quasisyntomic-descent); `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E3`; `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.5`; `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E5:abstract/algebra-objects`.

**Acceptance.** R = O_C: all three objects are A_inf. A torus R = O_C⟨x^{±1}⟩: AΩ_R is computed by A⟨x^{±1}⟩ → A⟨x^{±1}⟩, x^n ↦ [n]_q x^n, so H^1(AΩ_R) is the completed direct sum of the A/[n]_q for n ∈ Z, and the same complex computes φ_A^*Δ_{R/A}. The twist cannot be dropped: for the torus, H^0(Δ_{R/A} ⊗^L_A A/ξ) = R while H^0(AΩ_R ⊗^L_A A/ξ) = O_C (closed functions for the de Rham differential), so there is no isomorphism AΩ_R ≅ Δ_{R/A} in D(A).

### The θ and θ̃ specialisations under the AΩ comparison

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/theta-theta-tilde-square` · comparison. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.AOmega` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/AOmega/Basic`.

In the setting of ainf-omega-comparison let θ : A → O_C be Fontaine's map, with kernel (ξ), and θ̃ := θ∘φ_A^{-1} : A → O_C, with kernel (ξ̃), ξ̃ = φ(ξ) = [p]_q; so θ̃∘φ_A = θ. Under AΩ_R ≃ φ_A^*Δ_{R/A}: (a) (Hodge–Tate corner.) AΩ_R ⊗^L_{A,θ̃} O_C ≃ (φ_A^*Δ_{R/A}) ⊗^L_{A,θ̃} O_C = Δ_{R/A} ⊗^L_{A,θ} O_C = Δ̄_{R/A}, the Hodge–Tate cohomology of R relative to (A, (ξ)). The left side is the complex Ω̃_R of BMS1 (AInfCohomology:AI.4). The resulting isomorphism Ω̃_R ≃ Δ̄_{R/A} of commutative O_C-algebras is compatible with the maps from R to H^0 and identifies the two Hodge–Tate isomorphisms of commutative differential graded algebras (Ω^*_{R^{(1)}/(A/[p]_q)}, d_dR) ≅ (H^*(AΩ_R/[p]_q), β_{[p]_q}) and (Ω^*_{R^{(1)}/(A/[p]_q)}, d_dR) ≅ (H^*(Δ̄_{R^{(1)}/A}), β_{[p]_q}). (b) (de Rham corner.) AΩ_R ⊗^L_{A,θ} O_C ≃ (φ_A^*Δ_{R/A}) ⊗^L_{A,θ} O_C ≃ Ω^*_{R/O_C}, the p-completed de Rham complex, the last isomorphism being the de Rham comparison of PR.3 for the prism (A, (ξ)). (c) The two corners are different: for R = O_C⟨x^{±1}⟩, H^0 of (a) is R and H^0 of (b) is O_C. An identification of AΩ_R with Δ_{R/A} without the Frobenius twist would exchange the Hodge–Tate and de Rham specialisations.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** Setting and notation of ainf-omega-comparison; O_C is an A-algebra in two ways, through θ and through θ̃. (b) is the identification obtained by transporting PR.3's de Rham comparison through the isomorphism of ainf-omega-comparison. Its agreement with the de Rham specialisation of AΩ constructed in AI.4 is not asserted here; it belongs to AInfCohomology:AI.7, which proves agreement of comparison maps with comparison-uniqueness. Breuil–Kisin twists are trivialised by the generator [p]_q, as in the proof of Theorem 17.2.

**Construction or proof.**

1. (a): base change of the isomorphisms of ainf-omega-comparison along θ̃, and θ̃∘φ_A = θ. The identification of the left side with Ω̃_R is BMS1 Theorem 9.2 (i) (AI.4), in which R is an A-algebra through θ̃.
2. Compatibility with the maps from R and with the Hodge–Tate isomorphisms: step 3 of ainf-omega-comparison shows that μ_R intertwines η_{qΩ} and η_{AΩ}; both Hodge–Tate isomorphisms are induced from these maps by the universal property of the de Rham complex (PR.1's hodge-tate-comparison; BMS1 Theorem 8.3 with its Bockstein statement, AI.4).
3. (b): base change along θ and PR.3's de-rham-comparison-general (BS22 Corollary 15.4) for (A, (ξ)): φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} ⊗^L_A A/ξ ≅ Ω^*_{R/O_C}.
4. (c): for the torus, H^0(Δ̄_{R/A}) = R by the Hodge–Tate comparison, and the closed functions of the p-completed de Rham complex of O_C⟨x^{±1}⟩ over O_C are the constants.

### Uniqueness of comparison isomorphisms

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/comparison-uniqueness` · theorem. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.AOmega` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/AOmega/Basic`.

Let (A, I) be a perfect prism with perfectoid ring R = A/I. Let Sm_R be the category of p-completely smooth R-algebras and C_{Sm_R} the ∞-category of pairs (G, η) where G : Sm_R → D_{(p,I)-comp}(A) is a symmetric monoidal functor and η : id → G ⊗^L_A R is a natural transformation of symmetric monoidal functors Sm_R → D_{p-comp}(R). Prismatic cohomology with the Hodge–Tate structure maps η_S : S → Δ̄_{S/A} is an object Δ_{−/A} of C_{Sm_R}. (Theorem 18.2.) Δ_{−/A} has no nontrivial endomorphisms in C_{Sm_R}: End(Δ_{−/A}) = {1}. No compatibility with the Frobenius is imposed. (Lemma 18.3.) Let rsPerfd_R be the category of R-algebras that are quotients of p-completely flat perfectoid R-algebras by sequences that are p-completely regular relative to R. Suppose that for every S in rsPerfd_R an A-algebra endomorphism ε_S of Δ_{S/A} is given such that ε_S is functorial in S and compatible with the identity of S under η_S : S → Δ̄_{S/A}. Then ε_S = id for all S. (Use for comparison maps.) If an object (G, η_G) of C_{Sm_R} is isomorphic to Δ_{−/A}, the isomorphism is unique and every morphism between the two objects is that isomorphism or its inverse. In particular the isomorphisms of q-crystalline-prismatic-comparison over a q-PD pair whose prism (D, ([p]_q)) is perfect, such as (A_inf, (ξ)), the isomorphism AΩ ≃ φ_A^*Δ_{−/A_inf} of ainf-omega-comparison, and the comparison of PR.3 with the Nygaard complexes of topological Hochschild homology (BS22 Theorem 13.1) are the unique ones compatible with the Hodge–Tate structure maps; they do not depend on coordinates or presentations and are compatible with one another.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** (A, I) is a perfect prism, R = A/I the corresponding perfectoid ring. The theorem is about endomorphisms in the category of pairs (G, η) with the Hodge–Tate structure map, and it imposes no Frobenius compatibility; it is not a statement about automorphisms of a functor to E_∞-A-algebras with φ. Misprints of the printed proof are registered as PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22/E29 and PrismaticCohomology/E68: the sequence f_1, …, f_r lies in R′, the ring presented is A_inf(R′){g_i/d}^∧, the completeness is (p, d)-adic, and Joyal's identity reads φ^{n+1}(x) = x^{p^{n+1}} + pδ_1(x)^{p^n} + … + p^nδ_n(x)^p + p^{n+1}δ_{n+1}(x). For the AΩ comparison the perfect prism is (A_inf, ([p]_q)) with A_inf/[p]_q ≅ O_C through θ̃, and R ↦ R^{(1)} identifies the two categories of smooth algebras.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Reduction: every S in Sm_R has a quasisyntomic Čech cover S → S^• with all S^i in rsPerfd_R (DD.5). Derived prismatic cohomology with its Hodge–Tate map defines an object on rsPerfd_R (PR.2's derived-prismatic-cohomology), and by descent (PR.2's quasisyntomic-descent) it suffices to show that this object has no nontrivial endomorphisms. Its values are discrete (PR.2's qrsp-prism), which reduces the theorem to Lemma 18.3.
2. Perfectoid S: Δ_{S/A} = A_inf(S), so ε_S is an A-algebra endomorphism of A_inf(S); it preserves I·A_inf(S), and it is a δ-map because every endomorphism of a perfect p-complete δ-ring is (PR.0's perfect-delta-rings). So it is an endomorphism of the perfect prism (A_inf(S), I·A_inf(S)) inducing the identity on S, hence the identity (PR.0's perfect-prisms-perfectoid-rings).
3. General S = R′/(f_1, …, f_r): Δ_{S/A} = A_inf(R′){g_1/d, …, g_r/d}^∧ for a distinguished generator d of I and lifts g_i of f_i (PR.2's qrsp-prism, PR.0's regular-prismatic-envelopes). Let K be the kernel of ε_S − id. It is a subring; it is an A_inf(R′)-submodule containing the image of A_inf(R′), because ε_{R′} = id by step 2 and functoriality; and it is saturated for multiplication by p and by every φ^n(d), because the envelope is (p, d)-completely flat over A, so these elements are nonzerodivisors (PR.0's bounded-prism-complete-flatness).
4. K is derived (p, d)-complete, so it suffices that K contains the elements δ_n(g_i/d) for Joyal's operations δ_n, which topologically generate (PR.0's free-delta-ring). Induction on n: g_i/d ∈ K by d-saturation; φ^{n+1}(g_i/d) ∈ K because φ^{n+1}(d)·φ^{n+1}(g_i/d) = φ^{n+1}(g_i) ∈ K; Joyal's identity expresses p^{n+1}δ_{n+1}(g_i/d) through φ^{n+1}(g_i/d) and powers of the δ_j(g_i/d), j ≤ n, and K is p-saturated.
5. Use for comparison maps: two morphisms a, b between Δ_{−/A} and G with a an isomorphism differ by the endomorphism a^{-1}b of Δ_{−/A}, which is the identity.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/derived-prismatic-cohomology`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-derived-prismatic-cohomology); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/qrsp-prism`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-qrsp-prism); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/quasisyntomic-descent`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-quasisyntomic-descent); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/hodge-tate-comparison-map`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-hodge-tate-comparison-map); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/relative-prismatic-cohomology`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-relative-prismatic-cohomology); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/perfect-delta-rings`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-perfect-delta-rings); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/perfect-prisms-perfectoid-rings`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-perfect-prisms-perfectoid-rings); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/free-delta-ring`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-free-delta-ring); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/regular-prismatic-envelopes`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-regular-prismatic-envelopes); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/bounded-prism-complete-flatness`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-bounded-prism-complete-flatness); `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.5`; `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E5:abstract/symmetric-monoidal-infinity-category`; [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/q-crystalline-prismatic-comparison`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-6-q-crystalline-prismatic-comparison); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/ainf-omega-comparison`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-6-ainf-omega-comparison); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-ring-category`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-delta-ring-category).

**Acceptance.** S = R: Δ_{R/A} = A and the only A-algebra endomorphism of A is the identity. S = R⟨x^{1/p^∞}⟩/(x): Δ_{S/A} = A_inf(R⟨x^{1/p^∞}⟩){[x^♭]/d}^∧, and a functorial η-compatible endomorphism fixes [x^♭]/d and all δ_n([x^♭]/d). Condition (2) of Lemma 18.3 is needed in step 2: for a perfectoid S with a nontrivial R-automorphism τ, A_inf(τ) is an A-algebra automorphism of Δ_{S/A} that is not the identity. The comparison map of ainf-omega-comparison built from all coordinates equals the one built from any single framing.

### The Nygaard filtration in q-de Rham coordinates

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/nygaard-filtration-q-de-rham-coordinates` · theorem. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/QCrys/Nygaard`.

Let C be a perfectoid field of characteristic 0 containing μ_{p^∞}, A = A_inf(O_C), q = [ε], ξ = φ^{-1}([p]_q) and ξ̃ = [p]_q, as in ainf-q-pd-pair. Let R be a p-completely smooth O_C-algebra with a framing □ : O_C⟨T_1^{±1}, …, T_d^{±1}⟩ → R that is the p-adic completion of an étale map, and let R̃ be the (p, ξ)-completely étale A⟨T_1^{±1}, …, T_d^{±1}⟩-algebra lifting R, with the automorphisms γ_i lifting T_i ↦ qT_i (identity on the other coordinates) and the Frobenius lift φ with φ(T_i) = T_i^p. Let M^• = qΩ^•_{R̃/A} be the framed q-de Rham complex in toric form: the Koszul complex of the commuting endomorphisms ∂_q/∂_q log T_i = (γ_i − 1)/(q − 1) of R̃, with basis the forms d_q log T_{j_1} ⋯ d_q log T_{j_n} in degree n, and with the φ_A-semilinear endomorphism φ_M given on degree n by f·ω ↦ ξ̃^n·φ(f)·ω for a basis form ω. Then: (1) M^• ≅ qΩ_{R/A} ≅ φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} ≅ AΩ_R in D(A), compatibly with the Frobenius endomorphisms. (2) φ_M(M^n) ⊂ ξ̃^n M^n for every n, and the map M^n/ξM^n → H^n(M^•/ξ̃M^•), x ↦ class of φ_M(x)/ξ̃^n, is bijective. (3) The relative Nygaard filtration of φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} (PR.3) is represented by the subcomplexes N^{≥i}M^• = ξ^{max(i − •, 0)} M^•, that is ξ^i R̃ → ξ^{i−1} R̃^{⊕d} → ⋯ → ξ M^{i−1} → M^i → M^{i+1} → ⋯, with filtered Frobenius φ_M : N^{≥i}M^• → ξ̃^i M^•; moreover N^{≥i}M^n = {x ∈ M^n : φ_M(x) ∈ ξ̃^i M^n}. (4) Under (1) the map AΩ_R → Lη_ξ φ_*AΩ_R = φ_*Lη_ξ̃ AΩ_R of BMS2 is represented by φ_M : M^• → φ_*η_ξ̃ M^• ⊂ φ_*M^•.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** C is a perfectoid field of characteristic 0 containing all p-power roots of unity; R is p-completely smooth over O_C with a framing as stated (a small algebra in the sense of BMS1). The prism is (A, (ξ)) = (A_inf, ker θ); Δ_{R/A} is taken relative to it, and φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} is prismatic cohomology of the Frobenius twist relative to (A, ([p]_q)), as in ainf-omega-comparison. BMS2 Remark 9.11 prints q = [ε] − 1; the q-de Rham complex of BMS1 Definition 9.5 has q = [ε], so that q − 1 = μ (source issue PrismaticCohomology/E37). The statement depends on the framing only through the model M^•; the filtration on φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} does not depend on it (change-of-framing).

**Construction or proof.**

1. (1): (R̃, {T_i}, ξR̃) is a framed q-PD datum over the q-PD pair (A, (ξ)) of ainf-q-pd-pair whose q-PD envelope is R̃ itself; by q-de-rham-comparison its framed q-de Rham complex computes qΩ_{R/A}, by q-crystalline-prismatic-comparison qΩ_{R/A} ≅ Δ_{R^{(1)}/A} = φ_A^*Δ_{R/A}, and by ainf-omega-comparison this is AΩ_R; all three isomorphisms are compatible with Frobenius.
2. (2), divisibility: φγ_i = γ_iφ (γ_i is a δ-A-algebra automorphism) and φ(q − 1) = q^p − 1 = [p]_q·(q − 1) give ((γ_i − 1)/(q − 1))∘φ = [p]_q·(γ_i − 1)φ/(q^p − 1) = [p]_q·φ∘((γ_i − 1)/(q − 1)), that is (∂_q/∂_q log T_i)∘φ = [p]_q·φ∘(∂_q/∂_q log T_i), which is framed-q-de-rham-complex (d) in toric form (e); hence φ_M is a map of complexes and multiplies degree-n basis forms by ξ̃^n.
3. (2), bijectivity: for the torus R̃ = A⟨T^{±1}⟩ the complex is the completed direct sum over a ∈ Z^d of Koszul complexes on which ∂_q/∂_q log T_i acts by [a_i]_q; modulo ξ̃ = [p]_q the element [a]_q is a unit when p ∤ a and is 0 when p | a, so H^n(M^•/ξ̃) is the completed sum of the lines (A/ξ̃)·T^{pa}·ω, and x ↦ φ_M(x)/ξ̃^n sends T^a·ω to T^{pa}·ω over the isomorphism φ : A/ξ ≅ A/ξ̃. For a general framed R both sides are obtained from the torus by the (p, ξ)-completely étale base change R̃ ⊗̂_{A⟨T^{±1}⟩, φ} A⟨T^{±1}⟩ ≅ R̃; on the right this is étale localisation of Hodge–Tate cohomology (PR.1/etale-localization) transported through (1).
4. (3): apply PR.3/nygaard-filtration-in-coordinates with d = ξ, d′ = ξ̃ and the model M^•: its terms are finite free over R̃, which is (p, ξ)-completely flat over A, hence ξ- and ξ̃-torsion-free and ξ-adically complete; hypotheses (a) and (b) of that node are (2). The description by divisibility holds because φ : R̃/ξ → R̃/ξ̃ is injective (R̃ is the base change of R̃ along the Frobenius of the torus, which is finite free).
5. (4): by PR.3/leta-frobenius-factorisation the Frobenius of φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} factors through Lη of Δ_{R/A}; in the model this is the inclusion of φ_M(M^•) in η_ξ̃ M^•, as BMS2 Remark 9.11 states.

Graded pieces: gr^i of N^{≥•}M^• is, in degree n ≤ i, (ξ^{i−n}M^n/ξ^{i−n+1}M^n) ≅ Ω^n_{R/O_C}, with zero differential, matching gr^i_N ≅ τ^{≤i}Δ̄_{R/A}{i} of PR.3/relative-nygaard-graded-pieces. After base change along A_inf → W(k), k the residue field of O_C (so q ↦ 1 and ξ ↦ p), the filtration becomes p^{max(i − •, 0)} of the de Rham complex of the lift R̃ ⊗̂ W(k), the de Rham instance of PR.3/nygaard-filtration-in-coordinates. Modulo q − 1 alone this is not so: ξ is not p times a unit in A_inf/(q − 1). The element T^a with p ∤ a is not a cocycle modulo ξ̃ in degree 0: ∂_q/∂_q log T (T^a) = [a]_q T^a with [a]_q a unit modulo ξ̃; so H^0(M^•/ξ̃) is spanned by the T^{pa}.

## PR.4. Étale comparison and p-adic Tate twists

Over a perfect prism, derived Frobenius fixed points compute the generic-fibre étale cohomology of any p-adic algebra, with smoothness only for the smooth corollary. The nearby-cycle statement on an arbitrary pre-adic generic fibre retains its site gap; the affine scheme statement is independent of that gap. For a non-perfect prism P, extend scalars to its completed perfection and compare the resulting R_∞[1/p]. No equality with the original R[1/p] is asserted. Absolute Nygaard cohomology from PR.5 supplies the completed syntomic fibres and their multiplication at all integer weights. The logarithm, first Chern class, low weights and finite-level logarithmic de Rham–Witt exactness are individual contracts. Connectivity has an algebraic refinement gap; importing trace theory here would reverse the agreed dependency.

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-4-frobenius-fixed-points"></a>

### Derived Frobenius fixed points of a φ-module

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/frobenius-fixed-points` · construction. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.Etale` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/Etale/FixedPoints`.

Let Λ be a commutative ring (Λ = F_p, Z/p^n or Z_p in this stage), B a commutative Λ-algebra and σ a Λ-linear ring endomorphism of B (the Frobenius when B is an F_p-algebra; φ_A when B = A/p^n for a prism (A, (d))). The ∞-category D(B[F]) has as objects the pairs (M, φ_M) with M ∈ D(B) and φ_M : M → σ_*M a map in D(B), that is, a σ-semilinear endomorphism of M; it is the lax equaliser of the identity and σ_* on D(B), and a morphism is a map f : M → N with a chosen homotopy φ_N f ≃ σ_*(f) φ_M. The derived Frobenius fixed points are M^{φ=1} := fib(φ_M − 1 : M → M) ∈ D(Λ), the fibre being formed after restriction of scalars to Λ. For t ∈ B such that σ(t) becomes a unit of B[1/t] (for example σ(t) = t^p, or σ(t) ≡ t^p modulo a nilpotent ideal), φ_M extends uniquely to a σ-semilinear endomorphism of M[1/t] = M ⊗^L_B B[1/t], and (M[1/t])^{φ=1} denotes its fixed points. For a Z_p-linear φ-module M one writes (M/p^n)^{φ=1} for the fixed points of M ⊗^L_Z Z/p^n. For every i there is a short exact sequence 0 → coker(φ_M − 1 on H^{i−1}(M)) → H^i(M^{φ=1}) → ker(φ_M − 1 on H^i(M)) → 0; in particular H^0(M^{φ=1}) is in general not the group of φ-fixed vectors of H^0(M), and H^1(M^{φ=1}) can be non-zero for M concentrated in degree 0.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** Λ lies in the σ-fixed subring of B, so that φ_M − 1 is Λ-linear; it is not B-linear. The fibre is taken in D(Λ) (or D(Z)); M^{φ=1} carries no B-module structure. For (M[1/t])^{φ=1} the image of σ(t) in B[1/t] is a unit; this holds for B = A/p^n, t = d, since φ(d) ≡ d^p mod p. As a model in the pinned library a φ-module is a cochain complex of Λ-modules with an endomorphism, and the fibre is the shifted mapping cone of φ − 1.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Define D(B[F]) as in the statement of Bhatt–Scholze Lemma 9.2 and the functor (M, φ_M) ↦ fib(φ_M − 1) to D(Λ); in the library model the fibre is the mapping cone of φ − 1 shifted by −1, an object of the derived category through the localisation functor.
2. The long exact cohomology sequence of the triangle M^{φ=1} → M → M gives the short exact sequences 0 → coker(φ − 1 | H^{i−1}) → H^i(M^{φ=1}) → ker(φ − 1 | H^i) → 0.
3. Extension to M[1/t]: σ extends uniquely to B[1/t] because σ(t) is a unit there, and φ_M ⊗ σ is the required endomorphism of M ⊗^L_B B[1/t]; for σ(t) = t^p this is the colimit of φ_M along M → M → … with transition maps t.
4. Exactness: (−)^{φ=1} is a finite limit, hence commutes with all limits, with shifts and with ⊗^L_Λ Λ' for Λ → Λ' of finite Tor-dimension data used here (Z_p → Z/p^n, Z/p^n → Z/p^{n−1}); it commutes with filtered colimits in D(B), and Lemma 9.2 treats completed colimits.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`mathlib:CochainComplex.mappingCone`](#mathlib-cochaincomplex-mappingcone); [`mathlib:DerivedCategory`](#mathlib-derivedcategory); [`mathlib:DerivedCategory.Q`](#mathlib-derivedcategory-q); [`mathlib:frobenius`](#mathlib-frobenius); `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E5:abstract/stable-infinity-category`; `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`.

**Consumers.** Bhatt–Scholze Theorem 9.1 and Theorem 1.8(4): the right-hand side (Δ_{X/A}[1/d]/p^n)^{φ=1} of the étale comparison. Bhatt–Scholze Lemma 9.2 and the proof of Theorem 9.1: fixed points are compared along completed colimits and along Δ → Δ_perf. Bhatt–Scholze Theorem 11.1: RΓ(Y, j_! F_p) is obtained by applying (−/p[1/I])^{φ=1} to a fibre of perfected prismatic complexes. Bhatt–Lurie Example 8.1.3 and Theorem 8.1.9: Artin–Schreier: RΓ_ét(Spec R, Z/p) is the fixed points of Frobenius on R. PrismaticCohomology:PR.7 (étale realisation of Laurent F-crystals): the local system is the fixed points of φ on the Laurent crystal.

**Planning API.**

- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Etale.FrobeniusModule` (structure): A φ-module over Λ: a complex of Λ-modules with an endomorphism; the model of an object of D(B[F]) after restriction to Λ.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Etale.fixedPoints` (constructor): M^{φ=1} = fib(φ_M − 1), as the shifted mapping cone of φ − 1, an object of D(Λ).
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Etale.fixedPointsι` (projection): The canonical map M^{φ=1} → M, whose composite with φ_M − 1 is zero.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Etale.fixedPointsMap` (functoriality): A map of φ-modules induces a map of fixed points; quasi-isomorphisms induce isomorphisms.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Etale.fixedPoints_isGE` (characterisation): If M is concentrated in degrees ≥ a then so is M^{φ=1}; if M is in degrees ≤ b then M^{φ=1} is in degrees ≤ b + 1.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Etale.fixedPoints_isZero_of_isIso` (characterisation): M^{φ=1} = 0 if and only if φ_M − 1 is an isomorphism in D(Λ).
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Etale.invert` (constructor): The φ-module M[1/t] for t with σ(t) = t^p·u, u a unit after inverting t: the colimit of M along multiplication by t with the induced endomorphism.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Etale.reduce` (compatibility): The φ-module M/p^n = cone(p^n : M → M) and the transition maps M/p^n → M/p^{n−1}; (M/p^n)^{φ=1} ≃ M^{φ=1} ⊗^L Z/p^n.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Etale.fixedPointsTriangle` (relation): Derived fixed points are the fibre of φ−1. The canonical sequence M^(φ=1)→M→^(φ−1)M→M^(φ=1)[1] is a distinguished triangle, functorial in Frobenius-equivariant maps.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Etale.fixedPoints_cohomology_exact` (relation): For each i, 0→coker(φ−1:H^(i−1)(M)→H^(i−1)(M))→H^i(M^(φ=1))→ker(φ−1:H^i(M)→H^i(M))→0 is canonical. This gives the amplitude increase by at most one.

**Unit tests.**

- `pr4_fixed_points_fp_h1` (computation): For Λ = F_p, M = F_p in degree 0, φ = id: H^1(M^{φ=1}) ≅ F_p (and H^0 ≅ F_p).
- `pr4_fixed_points_zero_map` (degenerate): If φ_M = 0 then M^{φ=1} = 0.
- `pr4_fixed_points_identity` (computation): If φ_M = id then M^{φ=1} ≅ M ⊕ M[−1]; in particular H^1(M^{φ=1}) ≅ H^1(M) ⊕ H^0(M).
- `pr4_fixed_points_not_fixed_vectors` (non-example): For M = F_p[x] in degree 0 with its Frobenius, H^1(M^{φ=1}) ≠ 0 although M is discrete: the class of x is not of the form f^p − f.

**Acceptance.** For M = F_p in degree 0 with φ = id: H^0(M^{φ=1}) = F_p and H^1(M^{φ=1}) = F_p. For M an algebraic closure of F_p with its Frobenius: M^{φ=1} = F_p in degree 0 (Artin–Schreier equations are solvable). For M = F_p[x] with its Frobenius: H^1(M^{φ=1}) = coker(F − 1) ≠ 0, the group H^1_ét(A^1_{F_p}, F_p). If φ_M is topologically nilpotent for a complete filtration of M then M^{φ=1} = 0.

**Sources.** [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Lemma 9.2 (statement: the ∞-category D(B[F]) and the functors M ↦ M^{φ=1}, M ↦ (M[1/t])^{φ=1}). [BL22](https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.06120v1), Example 8.1.3. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 190. the Artin–Schreier fibre sequence RΓ_ét(Spec R, Z/p) → R → R is the basic instance of derived fixed points.

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-4-syntomic-complex"></a>

### Syntomic complexes Z_p(n) on quasisyntomic rings

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/syntomic-complex` · construction. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.Syntomic` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/Syntomic/Basic`.

Let S be a quasisyntomic ring (p-complete with bounded p^∞-torsion and L_{S/Z_p} of p-complete Tor-amplitude in [−1, 0]) and n an integer. Let Δ̂_S{n} be the Nygaard-completed prismatic cohomology of S with its n-th Breuil–Kisin twist, with Nygaard filtration N^{≥•}Δ̂_S{n}, obtained by quasisyntomic descent from quasiregular semiperfectoid rings (PR.3). Let can : N^{≥n}Δ̂_S{n} → Δ̂_S{n} be the canonical map and φ_n : N^{≥n}Δ̂_S{n} → Δ̂_S{n} the divided Frobenius; when S is an algebra over a perfectoid ring with perfect prism (A, (d)) and the twist is trivialised, for n ≥ 0, φ_n is the restriction of φ/d^n to N^{≥n}Δ̂_S = {x : φ(x) ∈ d^n Δ̂_S}. For n < 0 the filtration term is the entire twisted complex and the Frobenius is multiplied by d^{−n}; no negative ideal power is used. The n-th syntomic complex is Z_p(n)(S) := fib(φ_n − can : N^{≥n}Δ̂_S{n} → Δ̂_S{n}) ∈ D(Z_p), a derived p-complete complex, and Z/p^r(n)(S) := Z_p(n)(S) ⊗^L_Z Z/p^r. The functor S ↦ Z_p(n)(S) is a sheaf of complexes on the quasisyntomic site. For S quasiregular semiperfectoid, N^{≥n}Δ̂_S{n} and Δ̂_S{n} are discrete, Z_p(n)(S) is the two-term complex N^{≥n}Δ̂_S{n} → Δ̂_S{n} in degrees 0 and 1, H^0 = {x ∈ N^{≥n}Δ̂_S{n} : φ_n(x) = x} and H^1 = coker(φ_n − can). For a perfectoid ring R with perfect prism (A, I), choose a generator e of A{1} and let d be the generator of I with φ_{A{1}}(e) = d^{−1}e (for a Z_p^cycl-algebra: d = [p]_q with e = e_A; in characteristic p: d = p). For n ≥ 0, Z_p(n)(R) ≃ (φ^{−1}(d)^n A → A) with differential φ/d^n − 1. Another choice e' = ve replaces d by d·v/φ(v) and the complexes are identified by multiplication by v^n. For a generator d' = ud not of this form the two-term complex is in general not quasi-isomorphic to Z_p(n)(R) (R = Z_p^cycl, d' = u[p]_q with u ∈ Z_p^×, u^n ≢ 1 mod p: H^0 = 0 instead of Z_p).

**Hypotheses and conventions.** S is quasisyntomic; the construction is functorial for all maps of quasisyntomic rings and satisfies quasisyntomic descent. The complex is defined by the formula of BMS2 §7.4 and Theorem 1.12(5) as a fibre of prismatic data; it is not defined as a graded piece of TC (that identification belongs to RefinedTraceMethods:RT.6). The first display of BMS2 §7.4 prints gr^n TC for gr^i TC, registered as PAPER-BHATT-MORROW-SCHOLZE-19/E5. Sign convention: BMS2 writes hofib(φ − can), Bhatt–Scholze write fib(1 − φ_n); the two fibres are canonically isomorphic. The divided Frobenius is a map between different objects (source N^{≥n}, target the whole twisted complex), so Z_p(n) is not an instance of fixed points of an endomorphism for n ≥ 1.

**Construction or proof.**

1. On quasiregular semiperfectoid S: Δ_S is the initial prism (PR.2/qrsp-prism), N^{≥n}Δ_S = {x : φ(x) ∈ d^n Δ_S} (PR.3/nygaard-filtration-qrsp), the completion Δ̂_S and its filtration are PR.3/nygaard-completion, the twist is PR.3/breuil-kisin-twist and φ_n is PR.3/divided-frobenius; define the two-term complex.
2. Unfold to all quasisyntomic rings by quasisyntomic descent (PR.2/quasisyntomic-descent, PR.3/nygaard-filtration; the quasisyntomic site and its basis of quasiregular semiperfectoid rings are DD.5): each of N^{≥n}Δ̂{n}, Δ̂{n} is a sheaf, and a fibre of sheaves is a sheaf.
3. Perfectoid case: for R perfectoid Δ̂_R = A_inf(R) = A is Nygaard complete with N^{≥n}A = φ^{−1}(d)^n A for n ≥ 0, giving formula (9.3) of Bhatt–Scholze; the generator d is the one determined by a generator e of A{1} through φ_{A{1}}(e) = d^{−1}e (PR.3/divided-frobenius (b)); replacing e by ve replaces d by d·v/φ(v), and multiplication by v^n identifies the two complexes.
4. p-completeness: both terms are derived p-complete, hence so is the fibre; Z/p^r(n) is the derived reduction.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/nygaard-filtration-qrsp`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-3-nygaard-filtration-qrsp); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/nygaard-filtration`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-3-nygaard-filtration); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/nygaard-completion`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-3-nygaard-completion); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/divided-frobenius`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-3-divided-frobenius); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/breuil-kisin-twist`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-3-breuil-kisin-twist); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/qrsp-prism`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-qrsp-prism); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/quasisyntomic-descent`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-quasisyntomic-descent); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/perfect-prisms-perfectoid-rings`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-perfect-prisms-perfectoid-rings); `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.5`; [`mathlib:CochainComplex.mappingCone`](#mathlib-cochaincomplex-mappingcone); [`mathlib:DerivedCategory.Q`](#mathlib-derivedcategory-q); [`mathlib:PadicInt`](#mathlib-padicint).

**Consumers.** BMS2 Theorem 1.12(5), Section 7.4: the graded pieces of the motivic filtration on TC are Z_p(n)[2n]; RefinedTraceMethods:RT.6 proves that identification from this definition. Bhatt–Scholze Theorems 9.4 and 14.1: Z_p(n)(R) for perfectoid R is compared with étale cohomology of Spec R[1/p]; Z_p(n) is shown discrete and p-torsion-free as a quasisyntomic sheaf. BMS2 Corollary 8.21 and Theorem 10.1: pushforward to the étale site gives logarithmic de Rham–Witt sheaves in characteristic p and truncated nearby cycles over O_C. Bhatt–Lurie Sections 7.4 and 8; Bhatt–Mathew: the same complexes for animated rings and schemes, with first Chern class and étale comparison. PrismaticCohomology:PR.7 and arithmetic consumers (Colmez–Dospinescu–Nizioł §0.6.1): the defining fibre sequence Z_p(n) → N^{≥n}Δ̂{n} → Δ̂{n} is the syntomic triangle.

**Planning API.**

- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Syntomic.NygaardDatum` (structure): The imported data of a ring in weight n: complexes N^{≥n}Δ̂_S{n} and Δ̂_S{n} of Z_p-modules with the canonical map and the divided Frobenius φ_n (owners PR.3).
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Syntomic.syntomicComplex` (constructor): Z_p(n)(S) = fib(φ_n − can) as an object of D(Z_p).
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Syntomic.syntomicComplexMod` (constructor): Z/p^r(n)(S) = Z_p(n)(S) ⊗^L Z/p^r, the cone of p^r.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Syntomic.syntomicToFil` (projection): The canonical map Z_p(n)(S) → N^{≥n}Δ̂_S{n} of the defining fibre sequence.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Syntomic.syntomicMap` (functoriality): A map of data compatible with can and φ_n induces a map of syntomic complexes; quasi-isomorphisms of data induce isomorphisms.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Syntomic.syntomicComplex_isGE` (characterisation): If both complexes of the datum are concentrated in degrees ≥ 0 then Z_p(n)(S) ∈ D^{≥0}.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Syntomic.syntomicComplex_isLE` (characterisation): If both complexes are discrete (S quasiregular semiperfectoid) then Z_p(n)(S) ∈ D^{≤1}.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Syntomic.perfectoidDatum` (example): For n ≥ 0 and a perfect prism (A, (d)): the datum with terms φ^{−1}(d)^n A and A, canonical inclusion and φ/d^n.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Syntomic.syntomicCup` (structure): Natural pairings Z_p(m)⊗̂^L_ZpZ_p(n)→Z_p(m+n), for all integer weights, and a unit Z_p→Z_p(0) make the direct sum a graded commutative algebra. The pairings are induced by filtered prismatic multiplication and multiplicative divided Frobenius; they respect restriction, base change and the canonical comparison maps.

**Unit tests.**

- `pr4_syntomic_zero_weight_fp` (computation): For the datum Z_p → Z_p with can = φ_0 = id (the ring F_p in weight 0): H^1(Z_p(0)(F_p)) ≅ Z_p.
- `pr4_syntomic_equal_maps` (degenerate): If φ_n = can then Z_p(n) ≅ fib(0), with H^0 ≅ H^0(N^{≥n}) and H^1 ⊇ H^0(Δ̂{n}).
- `pr4_syntomic_contracting` (characterisation): If can is an isomorphism and φ_n − can is an isomorphism then Z_p(n) = 0 (the mechanism of the vanishing for n < 0 and of Lemma 7.22).
- `pr4_syntomic_not_fixed_points` (non-example): For the perfectoid datum with n = 1 the source φ^{−1}(d)A is a proper submodule of A when d is not a unit: Z_p(1)(R) is not fib(φ/d − 1) on A[1/d], nor fixed points of an endomorphism of A.

**Acceptance.** For R perfectoid with perfect prism (A, (d)) and n ≥ 0: Z_p(n)(R) is the two-term complex φ^{−1}(d)^n A → A, x ↦ φ(x)/d^n − x. Z_p(0)(F_p) = fib(0 : Z_p → Z_p) has H^0 = Z_p and H^1 = Z_p. Z_p(n)(S) = 0 for n < 0 and Z_p(1) is the Tate module of G_m locally (PR.4/syntomic-low-weights). For S a quasiregular semiperfect F_p-algebra: for n ≥ 0, H^0(Z_p(n)(S)) = A_crys(S)^{φ=p^n} (PR.4/syntomic-complex-char-p).

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-4-prismatic-logarithm"></a>

### The prismatic logarithm

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/prismatic-logarithm` · construction. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.Syntomic` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/Syntomic/Logarithm`.

Let (A, I) be a prism with Breuil–Kisin twist A{1} (PR.3) and (1 + I)_{rk=1} := {u ∈ 1 + I : δ(u) = 0} the group of rank-one units congruent to 1 modulo I. If (A, I) is transversal, A{1} = lim_r I_r/I_r^2 with I_r = I φ^*(I) ⋯ (φ^{r−1})^*(I) and transition maps division by p, and for u ∈ (1 + I)_{rk=1} the element log_Δ(u) ∈ A{1} is the unique element with image u^{p^r} − 1 in I_{r+1}/I_{r+1}^2 for all r ≥ 0. For a general prism log_Δ : (1 + I)_{rk=1} → A{1} is the unique function compatible with every map of prisms (B, J) → (A, I) from a transversal prism. It is a group homomorphism, natural in the prism, satisfies φ_{A{1}}(log_Δ(u)) = log_Δ(u), and log_Δ(u) ≡ (u − 1 mod I^2) under A{1}/IA{1} ≅ I/I^2. For Ā = A/I the Tate module T_p(Ā^×) = lim (μ_{p^k}(Ā), x ↦ x^p) maps to (1 + I)_{rk=1} by ρ_0 (lift x ∈ Ā^{♭×} uniquely to A^{♭×} and apply ♯), and the composite log_Δ : T_p(Ā^×) → A{1} is also called the prismatic logarithm. For the q-de Rham prism (Z_p[[q − 1]], ([p]_q)) there is a unique generator e_A of A{1} with (q − 1) e_A = log_Δ(q^p). For a crystalline prism (A, (p)) and u with φ(u) = u^p, u^p ≡ 1 mod p: log_Δ(u^p) = log(u) e_A with log(u) = Σ_{n>0} (−1)^{n−1}(u − 1)^n/n.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** (A, I) is a prism; for the Tate-module form A/I is its reduction. Transversal means A/I is p-torsion-free (so (p, I) is regular locally). Rank one means δ(u) = 0, equivalently φ(u) = u^p when A is p-torsion-free. The construction is algebraic; no K-theory or cyclotomic trace enters (Bhatt–Scholze Remark 9.5 describes the earlier trace-theoretic construction of the comparison for Z_p(1), which this replaces). Ownership: the twist A{1} is PR.3/breuil-kisin-twist; the logarithm is planned here because its consumers are the Tate twists of this stage.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Transversal case (BL Proposition 2.3.1, Construction 2.3.2): u^{p^r} ≡ 1 mod I_{r+1} because u^{p^r} = φ^s(u^{p^{r−s}}), and division by p carries the class of u^{p^r} − 1 to that of u^{p^{r−1}} − 1, since x^p − 1 ≡ p(x − 1) mod I_r^2 for x = u^{p^{r−1}}; additivity because (u^{p^r} − 1)(v^{p^r} − 1) ∈ I_{r+1}^2 (Proposition 2.3.3).
2. General prisms (BL Propositions 2.5.10, 2.5.16, Remark 2.5.17): every prism receives a map from a transversal prism through which given rank-one units lift (Lemmas 2.5.13, 2.5.15), and A{1} is the colimit of the A-modules A ⊗_B B{1} over transversal prisms (B, J) mapping to (A, I), with all transition maps isomorphisms (Proposition 2.5.1); define log_Δ by compatibility and deduce additivity, functoriality, Frobenius invariance (2.5.18) and the normalisation modulo I (2.5.19).
3. Tate modules (BL Notation 2.7.1, Propositions 2.7.2, 2.7.3, Construction 2.7.4): A^{♭×} → (A/I)^{♭×} is an isomorphism because the groups I^n/I^{n+1} are p-complete, and ♯ of an element of A^♭ has rank one.
4. Examples: q-de Rham prism (BL Proposition 2.6.1: [p^{r+1}]_q ≡ p [p^r]_q mod I_r^2 and (q − 1)[p^r]_q = q^{p^r} − 1) and crystalline prisms (BL Corollary 2.6.12), proved directly: for a crystalline prism I_r = (p^r), A{1} = lim (p^r)/(p^{2r}) with e_A the class of p^r, and put x = u − 1. Since φ(x) ∈ pA, x^p/p! = (φ(x)/p − δ(x))/(p − 1)! lies in A. The p-complete, p-torsion-free ring A is a Z_(p)-algebra, so BS22 Lemma 2.35 supplies every x^n/n!. The convergent logarithm lies in the completed divided-power ideal generated by x, and therefore itself has divided powers; hence u^{p^m} = exp(p^m log u) ≡ 1 + p^m log(u) modulo p^{2m}, the terms p^{km}(log u)^k/k! for k ≥ 2 being divisible by p^{2m}; so the class of (u^p)^{p^r} − 1 in (p^{r+1})/(p^{2r+2}) is log(u)·p^{r+1}, that is log_Δ(u^p) = log(u)e_A. This avoids the q-logarithm of Anschütz–Le Bras.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/breuil-kisin-twist`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-3-breuil-kisin-twist); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/prism`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-prism); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/prism-category`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-prism-category); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/transversal-prism-regular-sequences`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-transversal-prism-regular-sequences); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/q-de-rham-prism`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-q-de-rham-prism); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/crystalline-prism`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-crystalline-prism); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/rigidity-prism-ideal`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-rigidity-prism-ideal); `mathlib:rootsOfUnity`; `mathlib:Units`; [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/transversal-approximation`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-3-transversal-approximation); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/breuil-kisin-twist-transversal`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-3-breuil-kisin-twist-transversal); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/regular-prismatic-envelopes`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-regular-prismatic-envelopes); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/free-delta-pd-envelope`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-free-delta-pd-envelope).

**Consumers.** Bhatt–Lurie Notation 7.5.1, Proposition 7.5.2, Theorem 7.5.6: defines the syntomic first Chern class T_p(R^×) → H^0_syn(Spf R, Z_p(1)) on quasiregular semiperfectoid rings. Bhatt–Lurie Lemma 8.3.2, Proposition 8.3.3, Theorem 8.5.1: multiplication by log_Δ(ε) relates syntomic complexes of consecutive weights and is inverted to reach étale cohomology. Bhatt–Scholze Theorem 9.4 (through Remark 9.5): gives the comparison map α_1 : Z_p(1)(R) → RΓ(Spec R[1/p], Z_p(1)) without the cyclotomic trace. Bhatt–Mathew Section 1.1: the bottom map of the fibre square defining Z/p^n(i) of a ring comes from the prismatic logarithm.

**Planning API.**

- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Syntomic.rankOneUnits` (data): The subgroup (1 + I)_{rk=1} of A^× of units u ≡ 1 mod I with δ(u) = 0.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Syntomic.prismaticLog` (constructor): The group homomorphism log_Δ : (1 + I)_{rk=1} → A{1}.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Syntomic.prismaticLog_frobenius` (relation): φ_{A{1}}(log_Δ(u)) = log_Δ(u).
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Syntomic.prismaticLog_map` (functoriality): For a map of prisms f : (B, J) → (A, I): f{1}(log_Δ(u)) = log_Δ(f(u)).
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Syntomic.prismaticLog_mod` (characterisation): log_Δ(u) reduces to the class of u − 1 under A{1}/IA{1} ≅ I/I^2.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Syntomic.tateModule` (data): T_p(R^×) = lim (μ_{p^k}(R), x ↦ x^p), the kernel of ♯ : R^{♭×} → R^×.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Syntomic.tateLog` (constructor): The composite T_p((A/I)^×) → (1 + I)_{rk=1} → A{1}.

**Unit tests.**

- `pr4_prismatic_log_one` (degenerate): log_Δ(1) = 0.
- `pr4_prismatic_log_q_de_rham` (computation): In the q-de Rham prism, log_Δ(q^p) = (q − 1) e_A for a generator e_A of A{1}; in particular log_Δ(q^p) ≠ 0.
- `pr4_prismatic_log_mul` (characterisation): log_Δ(u v) = log_Δ(u) + log_Δ(v) and log_Δ(u^p) = p log_Δ(u).
- `pr4_prismatic_log_not_all_units` (non-example): In the q-de Rham prism the unit 1 + [p]_q lies in 1 + I but has δ ≠ 0, so it is not a rank-one unit and lies outside the domain of log_Δ.

**Acceptance.** q-de Rham prism: log_Δ(q^p) = (q − 1) e_A with e_A a generator of A{1}. Perfected q-de Rham prism: for ε = (1, ζ_p, ζ_{p^2}, …) ∈ T_p((A/I)^×), ρ_0(ε) = q^p and log_Δ(ε) = (q − 1) e_A. log_Δ(1) = 0 and log_Δ(uv) = log_Δ(u) + log_Δ(v). log_Δ is not defined on units of rank ≠ 1: for u ∈ 1 + I with δ(u) ≠ 0 the classes u^{p^r} − 1 need not lie in I_{r+1}.

**Sources.** [BL22](https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.06120v1), Proposition 2.3.1, Construction 2.3.2, Proposition 2.3.3 (transversal case); Propositions 2.5.10, 2.5.16, 2.5.18, 2.5.19 and Remark 2.5.17 (general prisms). [BL22](https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.06120v1), Notation 2.7.1, Propositions 2.7.2–2.7.3, Construction 2.7.4; Proposition 2.6.1, Corollary 2.6.12.
