<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-4-log-forms-divided-frobenius"></a>

### Logarithmic forms as fixed points of the divided Frobenius on the de Rham–Witt complex

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/log-forms-divided-frobenius` · theorem. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.Syntomic` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/Syntomic/CharP`.

Let k be a perfect field of characteristic p and X a smooth k-scheme, with de Rham–Witt complex WΩ^•_X and Nygaard filtration N^{≥i}WΩ^•_X ⊂ WΩ^•_X, the subcomplex p^{i−1}VW(O_X) → p^{i−2}VWΩ^1_X → ⋯ → VWΩ^{i−1}_X → WΩ^i_X → WΩ^{i+1}_X → ⋯, on which the Frobenius φ is uniquely divisible by p^i; write φ_i = φ/p^i : N^{≥i}WΩ^•_X → WΩ^•_X. Let W_rΩ^i_{X,log} ⊂ W_rΩ^i_X be the image of dlog[·] : G_m^{⊗i} → W_rΩ^i_X and WΩ^i_{X,log} = lim_r W_rΩ^i_{X,log}, as pro-étale sheaves. Then for every i ≥ 0 the sequence of complexes of pro-étale sheaves 0 → WΩ^i_{X,log}[−i] → N^{≥i}WΩ^•_X → WΩ^•_X → 0, with second map φ_i − 1, is exact in each degree, and WΩ^i_{X,log} = R lim_r W_rΩ^i_{X,log}.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** k is a perfect field of characteristic p and X is smooth over k. Exactness is degreewise and holds for sheaves on the pro-étale site of X; surjectivity of F − 1 in degree i holds only locally. The objects N^{≥i}WΩ and WΩ_log are owned by CrystallineCohomology:CR.4; this node is the statement about φ_i − 1 that the syntomic comparison needs (link CR.4 → PR.4). In the printed proof the boundary case reads 'i = n − 1'; it is n = i − 1 (register PAPER-BHATT-MORROW-SCHOLZE-19/E7).

**Construction or proof.**

1. Degrees n > i: φ_i − 1 = p^{n−i}F − 1 on WΩ^n_A, an isomorphism because p^{n−i}F is p-adically contracting and WΩ^n_A is p-adically complete.
2. Degrees n < i: N^{≥i}WΩ^n_A = p^{i−1−n}V WΩ^n_A and (φ_i − 1) ∘ p^{i−1−n}V = 1 − p^{i−1−n}V on WΩ^n_A (using FV = p and φ = p^n F), an isomorphism by p-adic completeness, and by V-adic completeness in the boundary case n = i − 1.
3. Degree n = i: φ_i − 1 = F − 1 on WΩ^i_X; the sequence of pro-sheaves 0 → {W_nΩ^i_{X,log}} → {W_nΩ^i_X} → {W_nΩ^i_X} → 0 with F − 1 is exact on X_ét [Illusie, Complexe de de Rham–Witt et cohomologie cristalline, Théorème I.5.7.2]; passing to the inverse limit gives exactness on the pro-étale site and WΩ^i_log = R lim_r W_rΩ^i_log.

**Direct prerequisites.** `CrystallineCohomology:CR.4`; `CrystallineCohomology:CR.4/verschiebung-FV`; `CrystallineCohomology:CR.4/dieudonne-dF`; `CrystallineCohomology:CR.4/saturated-F-range`; `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E2`.

**Acceptance.** i = 0: 0 → Z_p → W(O_X) → W(O_X) → 0 with F − 1, the Artin–Schreier–Witt sequence on the pro-étale site. i = 1, X = G_m: dlog[T] ∈ WΩ^1 is fixed by F, since F(dlog[T]) = dlog[T]. X = Spec k, i ≥ 1: N^{≥i}W(k) = p^{i−1}VW(k) = p^iW(k) and (φ_i − 1)(p^i x) = F(x) − p^i x is bijective onto W(k), so WΩ^i_{k,log} = 0 and the cokernel vanishes.

**Sources.** [BMS2](https://arxiv.org/abs/1802.03261v2), Definition 8.1 and Proposition 8.4 with its proof. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed pages 54, 55. statement and proof, with the boundary case corrected.

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-4-acrys-divided-frobenius-surjective"></a>

### Surjectivity of φ_i − 1 on the Nygaard pieces of Â_crys

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/acrys-divided-frobenius-surjective` · lemma. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.Syntomic` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/Syntomic/CharP`.

Let S be a quasiregular semiperfect F_p-algebra, A_crys(S) the p-completed divided power envelope of W(S^♭) → S, with Frobenius φ, Nygaard filtration N^{≥i}A_crys(S) = {x : φ(x) ∈ p^i A_crys(S)}, Nygaard completion Â_crys(S) and divided Frobenius φ_i = φ/p^i : N^{≥i}Â_crys(S) → Â_crys(S). (1) For every i > 0 the map φ_i − 1 : N^{≥i}Â_crys(S) → Â_crys(S) is surjective. (2) For every i ≥ 0 the map φ_i − 1 : N^{≥i}Â_crys(−) → Â_crys(−) is surjective as a map of sheaves on the site of quasiregular semiperfect F_p-algebras with the quasisyntomic topology.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** S is quasiregular semiperfect: Frobenius is surjective on S and L_{S/F_p} is a flat S-module placed in degree −1. In (1) i > 0 is necessary: for i = 0 and S = F_p the map φ − 1 on Z_p is zero. The inputs on A_crys(S) are BMS2 Theorem 8.14 (p-torsion-freeness; φ_i mod p identifies N^iA_crys(S) with Fil_i^conj(A_crys(S)/p); the image of N^{≥i} modulo p is the divided power filtration Fil^i_pd, the Hodge filtration of derived de Rham cohomology), requested from CrystallineCohomology:CR.4 for the crystalline and Nygaard statements, and DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.4 for the derived de Rham reduction.

**Construction or proof.**

1. (1): by p-completeness it suffices to prove surjectivity modulo p. On N^{≥i+1}Â_crys(S), φ_i is divisible by p, so φ_i − 1 is minus the canonical map and its image modulo p contains the image Fil^{i+1}_pd of N^{≥i+1} (Theorem 8.14(4)).
2. On pN^{≥i−1}Â_crys(S), φ_i − 1 agrees modulo p with φ_{i−1}, whose image modulo p is Fil^conj_{i−1}(Â_crys(S)/p) (Theorem 8.14(2)).
3. For j ≥ 1, Fil^conj_{j−1} + Fil^{pj}_pd = Â_crys(S)/p, since Fil^conj_{j−1} is generated by divided power monomials of total degree < pj and Fil^{pj}_pd by those of degree ≥ pj; with j = i and pi ≥ i + 1 this gives (1).
4. (2): for i = 0, part (1)'s argument shows the image of φ − 1 modulo p contains Fil^1_pd, and Â_crys(S) → S composed with φ − 1 is surjective on a tower of Artin–Schreier covers, which is a quasisyntomic cover; conclude by p-adic completeness.

**Direct prerequisites.** `CrystallineCohomology:CR.0`; `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.4`; `CrystallineCohomology:CR.0/pd-filtration`; `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.5`; `CrystallineCohomology:CR.4`; [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/qrsp-char-p-acrys`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-qrsp-char-p-acrys); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/nygaard-filtration-qrsp`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-3-nygaard-filtration-qrsp).

**Acceptance.** S perfect, i ≥ 1: A_crys(S) = W(S), N^{≥i} = p^iW(S), φ_i − 1 = (F − p^i)/p^i, surjective because F is bijective and p^iF^{−1} is contracting. S = F_p, i = 0: φ − 1 = 0 on Z_p is not surjective, but becomes surjective on W of an algebraic closure. S = F_p[x^{1/p^∞}]/(x), i = 1: the class of the divided power γ_p(x) is hit, since it lies in Fil^p_pd.

**Sources.** [BMS2](https://arxiv.org/abs/1802.03261v2), Lemma 8.19 and its proof. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 65. statement and proof; the identity Fil_{j−1}^conj + Fil^{pj}_pd = Â_crys(S)/p is checked from the definitions of the two filtrations.

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-4-ainf-artin-schreier-condition"></a>

### The condition (As) for Rν_* A_inf,X modulo p^n

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/ainf-artin-schreier-condition` · lemma. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.Syntomic` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/Syntomic/NearbyCycles`.

Setting: A is a p-power-torsion ring in a topos with an automorphism φ, and μ, ξ ∈ A are non-zero-divisors with μ = ξ φ^{−1}(μ) and ξ − p ∈ φ^{−1}(μ)A; put ξ_r = ξ φ^{−1}(ξ) ⋯ φ^{1−r}(ξ), so μ = ξ_r φ^{−r}(μ). Let C ∈ D^{≥0}(A) with H^0(C) μ-torsion-free and a φ-semilinear quasi-isomorphism φ : C ≃ C. Condition (As): 1 − ξ^i φ^{−1} : C/μ^j C → C/μ^j C is a quasi-isomorphism for all i ≥ j ≥ 0. Claim: for a smooth formal scheme 𝔛 over Spf O_C with generic fibre X and ν : X_proét → 𝔛_ét, (As) holds for A = A_inf/p^n and C = Rν_* A_inf,X/p^n. More precisely 1 − ξ^i φ^{−1} is an automorphism of the pro-étale sheaf A_inf,X/(p^n, μ^j) for i ≥ j ≥ 0, and 1 − ξ^i φ^{−1} : A_inf,X/p^n → A_inf,X/p^n is surjective with kernel Z/p^n · μ^i ≅ Z/p^n(i).

**Hypotheses and conventions.** C is a perfectoid field of characteristic 0 containing all p-power roots of unity, μ = [ε] − 1, ξ = μ/φ^{−1}(μ) (the standing notation of BMS2 Section 9). i ≥ j ≥ 0 in (As); for j = 0 the condition is empty. In the printed remark 'g − μ^{i−j}φ^{−1}(g)' reads 'g − ξ^{i−j}φ^{−1}(g)' (register PAPER-BHATT-MORROW-SCHOLZE-19/E10); the node uses the corrected computation.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Reduce to n = 1 by dévissage, where A_inf,X/(p, μ^j) = Ô_X^{♭+}/μ^j.
2. Injectivity: if f ∈ Ô_X^{♭+} and f − ξ^i φ^{−1}(f) ∈ μ^j Ô_X^{♭+}, then g = f/μ^j satisfies g − ξ^{i−j}φ^{−1}(g) ∈ Ô_X^{♭+} because ξ^i φ^{−1}(μ)^j = ξ^{i−j}μ^j; with h = φ^{−1}(g) this says h^p − ξ^{i−j}h ∈ Ô_X^{♭+}, so h is integral over Ô_X^{♭+}, which is integrally closed in Ô_X^♭; hence g ∈ Ô_X^{♭+}.
3. Surjectivity on Ô_X^{♭+}: by integral closedness it reduces to surjectivity of 1 − ξ^i φ^{−1} on Ô_X^♭, i.e. to solving h^p − ξ^i h = f pro-étale locally; ξ is a unit of Ô_X^♭, so this is an Artin–Schreier-type finite étale equation, solvable pro-étale locally by the tilting equivalence (PerfectoidSpaces:P3).
4. Kernel on A_inf,X/p^n: μ^i is fixed by ξ^i φ^{−1} since ξ φ^{−1}(μ) = μ, and the kernel of 1 − φ^{−1} on A_inf,X/p^n[1/μ] = W_n(Ô_X^♭) is Z/p^n.

**Direct prerequisites.** `AInfCohomology:AI.3`; `PerfectoidQuotients:Q0:integral-algebra`; `PerfectoidSpaces:P3`; `ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0`; `ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1:formal-adic-comparison`.

**Acceptance.** i = j = 0: empty; i = j = 1: 1 − ξφ^{−1} is bijective on Ô_X^{♭+}/μ. X = Spa(C, O_C): 1 − ξ^iφ^{−1} is surjective on O_C^♭ with kernel F_p · μ^i modulo p. The kernel Z/p^n · μ^i is identified with Z/p^n(i) by ε^{⊗i} ↦ μ^i for the chosen ε (over C every Tate twist is trivialised by ε); the identification is canonical only after twisting A_inf by {i}.

**Sources.** [BMS2](https://arxiv.org/abs/1802.03261v2), Section 10, the abstract setting before Remark 10.6, and Remark 10.6. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 76. the setting, the condition (As) and its verification for Rν_*A_inf,X/p^n, with the misprinted exponent corrected.

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-4-fixed-points-completed-colimits"></a>

### Frobenius fixed points commute with completed colimits

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/fixed-points-completed-colimits` · lemma. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.Etale` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/Etale/FixedPoints`.

Let B be an F_p-algebra with an element t ∈ B, with its Frobenius σ, and let D_comp(B[F]) ⊂ D(B[F]) be the full subcategory of pairs (M, φ_M) with M derived t-complete. Then the functors D_comp(B[F]) → D(F_p), M ↦ M^{φ=1} and M ↦ (M[1/t])^{φ=1}, commute with colimits. Explicitly, for a diagram (M_i, φ_i) in D_comp(B[F]) with colimit colim M_i in D(B) and derived t-completion (colim M_i)^∧ (the colimit in D_comp(B[F])), the maps colim (M_i)^{φ=1} → ((colim M_i)^∧)^{φ=1} and colim (M_i[1/t])^{φ=1} → ((colim M_i)^∧[1/t])^{φ=1} are isomorphisms. The proof shows N^{φ=1} ≃ (N/t)^{φ=1} for every N ∈ D_comp(B[F]).

**Hypotheses and conventions.** B is an F_p-algebra and φ_M is semilinear over the Frobenius of B, so φ(t) = t^p. t is an arbitrary element; derived t-completeness is required of every M_i and the target colimit is the completed one. The colimits are indexed by arbitrary small diagrams.

**Construction or proof.**

1. The fibre F of colim M_i → (colim M_i)^∧ is uniquely t-divisible, so F ≃ F[1/t] and it suffices to prove F^{φ=1} = 0, that is, the statement for M ↦ M^{φ=1} (Bhatt–Scholze, proof of Lemma 9.2).
2. For N ∈ D(B[F]) the quotient N/t carries an induced φ because φ(t) = t^p ∈ tB. If N is derived t-complete, the fibre of N → N/t is complete for the t-adic filtration and φ is topologically nilpotent on it since φ(t) = t^p ∈ t^2 B; hence its fixed points vanish and N^{φ=1} ≃ (N/t)^{φ=1}.
3. Both functors in D_comp(B[F]) → D(B[F]) → D(F_p), N ↦ N/t ↦ (N/t)^{φ=1}, commute with all colimits (reduction modulo t kills the difference between a colimit and its completion; fixed points are a finite limit in a stable category).

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/frobenius-fixed-points`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-4-frobenius-fixed-points); `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`; `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E5:abstract/stable-infinity-category`.

**Acceptance.** For B = F_p[t] and the completed direct sum of copies of F_p[[t]] indexed by a set J: the fixed points are the direct sum over J of F_p ⊕ F_p[−1]. For a derived p-complete simplicial algebra S over a perfectoid ring: (Δ_{S/A}[1/d]/p)^{φ=1} ≃ (Δ_{S/A,perf}[1/d]/p)^{φ=1}, the step used in Theorem 9.1. Without derived t-completeness of the terms the statement N^{φ=1} ≃ (N/t)^{φ=1} fails: N = B[1/t] has N/t = 0.

**Sources.** [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Lemma 9.2 and its proof. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 71. statement and proof of the lemma, reproduced with all hypotheses.

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-4-perfectoid-artin-schreier-witt"></a>

### The étale comparison for perfectoid rings (Artin–Schreier–Witt and tilting)

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/perfectoid-artin-schreier-witt` · theorem. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.Etale` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/Etale/Perfectoid`.

Let S be a perfectoid ring, (A_inf(S), (d)) its perfect prism and S^♭ its tilt; write d also for the image of d in S^♭ = A_inf(S)/p. For every perfect prism (A, (d)) with a map A/d → S one has Δ_{S/A} = A_inf(S), so Δ_{S/A}[1/d]/p^n = W_n(S^♭[1/d]). For n ≥ 1: (1) (Artin–Schreier–Witt) RΓ_ét(Spec(S^♭[1/d]), Z/p^n) ≃ fib(F − 1 : W_n(S^♭[1/d]) → W_n(S^♭[1/d])) = (Δ_{S/A}[1/d]/p^n)^{φ=1}; (2) (tilting) there is a canonical isomorphism RΓ_ét(Spec(S[1/p]), Z/p^n) ≃ RΓ_ét(Spec(S^♭[1/d]), Z/p^n). Hence RΓ_ét(Spec(S[1/p]), Z/p^n) ≃ (Δ_{S/A}[1/d]/p^n)^{φ=1}, naturally in the perfectoid ring S.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** S is a perfectoid ring in the sense of Bhatt–Morrow–Scholze (integral perfectoid; p-torsion and characteristic p are allowed). If p = 0 in S both sides vanish: S[1/p] = 0 and d maps to 0 in S^♭. Étale cohomology is that of the schemes Spec(S[1/p]) and Spec(S^♭[1/d]), not of adic spectra; the adic spectra enter only through Huber's comparison.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Δ_{S/A} is discrete and equal to the initial prism A_inf(S) of S (PR.2/qrsp-prism applied to the perfectoid ring S, and PR.0/perfect-prisms-perfectoid-rings); reducing modulo p^n and inverting d gives W_n(S^♭)[1/[d]] = W_n(S^♭[1/d]) because S^♭ is perfect.
2. Artin–Schreier–Witt: on the étale site of an F_p-scheme the sequence 0 → Z/p^n → W_n(O) → W_n(O) → 0 with second map F − 1 is exact and W_n(O) has no higher cohomology on affines (requested from SF.2); this gives (1) (Bhatt–Scholze, proof of Theorem 9.1, first approach).
3. Tilting: RΓ_ét(Spec(S[1/p])) ≃ RΓ_ét(Spa(S[1/p], S)) and the same for (S^♭[1/d], S^♭) by Huber's comparison [Huber, Étale cohomology of rigid analytic varieties and adic spaces, Corollary 3.2.2] (H1:henselian), and the two adic spaces have equivalent étale sites by the tilting equivalence [Scholze, Perfectoid spaces, Theorem 1.11] (PerfectoidSpaces:P3).
4. Naturality in S of all three identifications gives a natural isomorphism on the category of perfectoid rings, as needed to finish the proof of Theorem 9.1 arc-locally.
5. For the perfect characteristic-p coefficient ring T=S^♭[1/d], define Frobenius on W_n(T) by the quotient W(T)/p^n≃W_n(T); equivalently it is the coordinatewise map induced by Frobenius of T. No non-existent truncated-Frobenius declaration is imported from Mathlib.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/frobenius-fixed-points`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-4-frobenius-fixed-points); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/perfect-prisms-perfectoid-rings`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-perfect-prisms-perfectoid-rings); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/ainf-prism`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-ainf-prism); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/qrsp-prism`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-qrsp-prism); `PerfectoidQuotients:Q0:integral-algebra`; `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2`; `ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0`; `ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1:henselian`; `PerfectoidSpaces:P3`; [`mathlib:WittVector`](#mathlib-wittvector); [`mathlib:TruncatedWittVector`](#mathlib-truncatedwittvector); [`mathlib:WittVector.frobenius`](#mathlib-wittvector-frobenius).

**Acceptance.** S = O_C, C complete algebraically closed: both sides are Z/p^n in degree 0 (W_n(C^♭)^{F=1} = Z/p^n and F − 1 is surjective). S a perfect F_p-algebra: both sides are 0. S = Z_p^cycl (the p-completion of Z_p[ζ_{p^∞}]): H^1 of the right-hand side is coker(F − 1) on W_n of the tilt of the cyclotomic field, the group Hom_cont(Gal, Z/p^n).

**Sources.** [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Proof of Theorem 9.1, "first approach". Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 71. the perfectoid case of the comparison: identification of Δ_{S/A}[1/d]/p^n with Witt vectors of the tilt, Artin–Schreier–Witt, and the tilting isomorphism via Huber and Scholze.

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-4-syntomic-cohomology-formal-schemes"></a>

### Syntomic cohomology of animated rings and bounded p-adic formal schemes

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/syntomic-cohomology-formal-schemes` · construction. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.Syntomic` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/Syntomic/FormalSchemes`.

For an animated commutative ring R and an integer n let Δ_R{n} be the absolute prismatic complex with Breuil–Kisin twist and Fil^•_N Δ_R{n} its absolute Nygaard filtration (PR.5), with ι : Fil^n_N Δ_R{n} → Δ_R{n} the canonical map and φ{n} : Fil^n_N Δ_R{n} → Δ_R{n} the Frobenius. Define RΓ_syn(Spf R, Z_p(n)) := fib(φ{n} − ι) in the p-complete derived ∞-category D̂(Z_p). Then: (a) R → R^∧_p induces an isomorphism on RΓ_syn(Spf −, Z_p(n)); (b) the map to the Nygaard-completed version fib(φ̂{n} − ι̂ : Fil^n_N Δ̂_R{n} → Δ̂_R{n}) is an isomorphism (Proposition 7.4.6); so for R quasisyntomic RΓ_syn(Spf R, Z_p(n)) = Z_p(n)(R) of PR.4/syntomic-complex; (c) R ↦ RΓ_syn(Spf R, Z_p(n)) satisfies p-complete fpqc descent (7.4.7); (d) it commutes with sifted colimits, hence is left Kan extended from finitely generated polynomial Z-algebras (7.4.8); (e) RΓ_syn(Spf R, Z_p(n)) → Tot RΓ_syn(Spf(R ⊗^L F_p^{⊗•+1}), Z_p(n)) is an isomorphism for n ≥ 0 (7.4.10) and RΓ_syn(Spf R, Z_p(n)) ≃ lim_m RΓ_syn(Spf(R ⊗^L Z/p^m), Z_p(n)) (7.4.11). For a bounded p-adic formal scheme 𝔛, RΓ_syn(𝔛, Z_p(n)) := lim over maps Spec(A) → 𝔛 of RΓ_syn(Spf A, Z_p(n)); it agrees with the affine definition on Spf R, satisfies étale descent, and sits in the fibre sequence RΓ_syn(𝔛, Z_p(n)) → Fil^n_N RΓ_Δ(𝔛){n} → RΓ_Δ(𝔛){n} with second map φ{n} − ι.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** R is any animated commutative ring; p-completeness is not assumed, and is harmless by (a). The construction uses the absolute prismatic cohomology and absolute Nygaard filtration of PR.5 and the twists of PR.3; PR.4 owns only the fibre (ownership fixed by red-team finding RT-AREA-padic-2/28). 𝔛 is a bounded p-adic formal scheme: locally Spf R with R p-complete with bounded p^∞-torsion. n is any integer; the complex vanishes for n < 0 (PR.4/syntomic-low-weights).

**Construction or proof.**

1. Definition and (a): Bhatt–Lurie Construction 7.4.1 and Warning 7.4.2; absolute prismatic complexes and the Nygaard filtration are invariant under p-completion (PR.5).
2. (b): the Frobenius factors as Fil^n_N Δ_R{n} → Fil^n_N Δ̂_R{n} → Δ_R{n} (BL Remark 5.7.10), and the 3 × 3 diagram of BL Proposition 7.4.6 has pullback squares in the upper left and lower right, so the two fibres agree; on quasiregular semiperfectoid rings the absolute filtration is {x : φ(x) ∈ Δ^{[n]}} (BL Corollary 5.6.3) and Theorem 5.6.2 identifies it with the Nygaard filtration over a perfect prism, giving agreement with PR.4/syntomic-complex.
3. (c), (d): descent and sifted colimits for the Nygaard-completed filtered complexes (BL Remark 5.8.6); for (d) reduce modulo p, where for m > n the Frobenius maps F_p ⊗ Δ_R^{[m]}{n} into Δ_R^{[pm−n]}{n} ⊂ Δ_R^{[m+1]}{n}, so φ{n} − 1 is an isomorphism on a deep enough step of a complete filtration and F(R) is the fibre of a map between quotients that commute with sifted colimits (BL Proposition 7.4.8).
4. (e) from the corresponding statements for Fil^m_N Δ_R{n} (BL Proposition 5.5.24, Corollary 5.5.25).
5. Globalisation: BL Variant 7.4.12, using (e) for agreement on affines and (c) for étale descent.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/syntomic-complex`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-4-syntomic-complex); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.5/absolute-prismatic-cohomology`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-5-absolute-prismatic-cohomology); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.5/absolute-nygaard-filtration`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-5-absolute-nygaard-filtration); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.5/absolute-relative-comparison`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-5-absolute-relative-comparison); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/breuil-kisin-twist`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-3-breuil-kisin-twist); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/nygaard-completion`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-3-nygaard-completion); `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E5:animation/animated-commutative-rings`; `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E5:animation/universal-property-of-animation`; `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E3`; `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`.

**Consumers.** Bhatt–Lurie Sections 7.5 and 8: target of the syntomic first Chern class and source of the étale comparison morphism. Bhatt–Lurie Construction 8.4.1: the p-adic corner of the pullback square defining syntomic cohomology of schemes. Bhatt–Mathew Example 1.4 and Section 5: the restriction of Z/p^n(i)_X to the p-adic completion. Colmez–Dospinescu–Nizioł §0.6.1 (routed item in-syntomic): the fibre sequence RΓ_syn → Fil^n_N RΓ_Δ{n} → RΓ_Δ{n} is the syntomic triangle in prismatic form. PrismaticCohomology:PR.7: syntomic cohomology of Spf O_K and its Frobenius-fixed description.

**Planning API.**

- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Syntomic.AbsoluteDatum` (structure): The imported data of an animated ring in weight n: Fil^n_N Δ_R{n} and Δ_R{n} as p-complete complexes with ι and φ{n} (owner PR.5), viewed as a Nygaard datum.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Syntomic.syntomicCohomology` (constructor): RΓ_syn(Spf R, Z_p(n)) = fib(φ{n} − ι).
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Syntomic.syntomicCohomology_completion` (compatibility): The map to the fibre formed with the Nygaard-completed datum is an isomorphism (BL Proposition 7.4.6).
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Syntomic.syntomicCohomology_eq_syntomicComplex` (compatibility): For R quasisyntomic, RΓ_syn(Spf R, Z_p(n)) ≅ Z_p(n)(R).
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Syntomic.syntomicCohomologyFormal` (constructor): RΓ_syn(𝔛, Z_p(n)) for a bounded p-adic formal scheme, the limit over affines mapping to 𝔛.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Syntomic.syntomicTriangle` (relation): The fibre sequence RΓ_syn(𝔛, Z_p(n)) → Fil^n_N RΓ_Δ(𝔛){n} → RΓ_Δ(𝔛){n}.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Syntomic.syntomicCohomologyCup` (structure): Natural pairings Z_p(m)⊗̂^L_ZpZ_p(n)→Z_p(m+n), for all integer weights, and a unit Z_p→Z_p(0) make the direct sum a graded commutative algebra. The pairings are induced by filtered prismatic multiplication and multiplicative divided Frobenius; they respect restriction, base change and the canonical comparison maps.

**Unit tests.**

- `pr4_syntomic_cohomology_trivial_ring` (degenerate): For the zero datum (the ring Z[1/p], whose p-completion vanishes) RΓ_syn = 0.
- `pr4_syntomic_cohomology_qrsp_two_term` (computation): For a datum with both terms discrete, RΓ_syn has cohomology only in degrees 0 and 1.
- `pr4_syntomic_cohomology_completed_agrees` (compatibility): If the completion maps on Fil^n and on Δ{n} are isomorphisms, the completed and uncompleted syntomic complexes are isomorphic.
- `pr4_syntomic_cohomology_not_hodge` (non-example): Replacing the Nygaard filtration by the datum with ι = 0 changes the answer: fib(φ{n}) ≠ fib(φ{n} − ι) already for the perfectoid datum of O_C in weight 0, where the first is 0 and the second has H^0 = Z_p.

**Acceptance.** For R quasiregular semiperfectoid the complex is the two-term complex of PR.4/syntomic-complex. For R a quasiregular semiperfect F_p-algebra it is Fil^n_N A_crys(R) → A_crys(R), x ↦ φ(x)/p^n − x (BL Example 7.4.4). RΓ_syn(Spf Z[1/p], Z_p(n)) = 0, since the p-completion of Z[1/p] is 0. For 𝔛 = Spf R the limit definition returns RΓ_syn(Spf R, Z_p(n)).

**Sources.** [BL22](https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.06120v1), Section 7.4, opening sentence; Construction 7.4.1, Warning 7.4.2, Propositions 7.4.6–7.4.8 and 7.4.10, Corollary 7.4.11. <a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-4-divided-frobenius-contraction"></a>

### The divided Frobenius contracts deep Nygaard levels modulo p

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/divided-frobenius-contraction` · lemma. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.Syntomic` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/Syntomic/Contraction`.

Let C be a perfectoid field of characteristic 0 and A a p-torsion-free quasisyntomic O_C-algebra; fix i ≥ 0. For every integer m ≥ (pi + 1)/(p − 1), both φ_i and the canonical map preserve N^{≥m}Δ̂_A{i}/p functorially in A, and φ_i − 1 : N^{≥m}Δ̂_A{i}/p → N^{≥m}Δ̂_A{i}/p is an equivalence; more precisely φ_i maps N^{≥m}Δ̂_A{i}/p into N^{≥m+1}Δ̂_A{i}/p. Consequently Z/p(i)(A) ≃ fib(φ_i − 1 : (N^{≥i}Δ̂_A{i}/p)/(N^{≥m}Δ̂_A{i}/p) → (Δ̂_A{i}/p)/(N^{≥m}Δ̂_A{i}/p)), and, for quasiregular semiperfectoid O_C-algebras S, Z_p(i)(S) ≃ fib(φ_i − 1 : Fil^i_N Δ_S → Δ_S) computed without Nygaard completion and without twists.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** C is a perfectoid field of characteristic 0; over O_C the Breuil–Kisin twists are trivialised. A is p-torsion-free and quasisyntomic over O_C; by left Kan extension and Nygaard completion the endomorphism φ_i of N^{≥m}Δ̂_A{i}/p and the equivalence extend to every quasisyntomic O_C-algebra. m ≥ (pi + 1)/(p − 1), which is the condition p(m − i) ≥ m + 1.

**Construction or proof.**

1. By quasisyntomic descent assume A quasiregular semiperfectoid and p-torsion-free; then all N^kΔ̂_A/p are discrete, so N^{≥k}Δ̂_A/p is discrete and ξ-torsion-free, and φ_i is induced by ξ̃^{−i}φ on Δ̂_A[1/ξ̃], ξ̃ = φ(ξ) (BMS2 proof of Lemma 7.22).
2. φ_i(N^{≥m}Δ̂_A) ⊂ ξ̃^{m−i}Δ̂_A for m ≥ i; modulo p, ξ̃ ≡ ξ^p, so φ_i(N^{≥m}Δ̂_A/p) ⊂ ξ^{p(m−i)}Δ̂_A/p ⊂ N^{≥p(m−i)}Δ̂_A/p because ξ^kΔ̂_A ⊂ N^{≥k}Δ̂_A.
3. For p(m − i) ≥ m + 1 this gives φ_i(N^{≥m}/p) ⊂ N^{≥m+1}/p: φ_i is topologically nilpotent for the complete Nygaard filtration, so φ_i − 1 is an automorphism.
4. The consequences follow by comparing the fibres of φ_i − 1 on N^{≥i} → Δ̂ and on the quotients by N^{≥m}; for the uncompleted form use that the divided Frobenius of the completion factors through Δ_S (PR.3/nygaard-completion (b)): the cofibres of Fil^i_N Δ_S → N^{≥i}Δ̂_S and of Δ_S → Δ̂_S agree, φ_i induces 0 between them and the canonical map the identity, so the two fibres of φ_i − 1 agree (Bhatt–Lurie Proposition 7.4.6); this holds for every quasiregular semiperfectoid ring.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/syntomic-complex`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-4-syntomic-complex); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/nygaard-filtration-qrsp`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-3-nygaard-filtration-qrsp); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/nygaard-graded-pieces`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-3-nygaard-graded-pieces); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/nygaard-completion`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-3-nygaard-completion); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/divided-frobenius`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-3-divided-frobenius); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/quasisyntomic-descent`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-quasisyntomic-descent); `PerfectoidQuotients:Q0:integral-algebra`.

**Acceptance.** i = 0: every m ≥ 1 works when p ≥ 2, and φ maps N^{≥m}/p into N^{≥pm}/p. i = 1, p = 2: m ≥ 3; i = 1, p odd: m ≥ 2. A = O_C, i = 1: N^{≥m}A_inf/p = ξ^m O_C^♭ and φ_1(ξ^m x) = ξ^{p(m−1)} x^p, which lies in ξ^{m+1}O_C^♭ exactly when p(m − 1) ≥ m + 1.

**Sources.** [BMS2](https://arxiv.org/abs/1802.03261v2), Lemma 7.22 and its proof. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 52. statement and proof; the bound on m is the printed one. [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Proof of Theorem 14.1, first paragraph. <a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-4-leta-frobenius-fixed-points"></a>

### Fixed points of ξ^i φ^{−1} are unchanged under Lη_μ in degrees ≤ i

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/leta-frobenius-fixed-points` · lemma. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.Syntomic` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/Syntomic/NearbyCycles`.

In the abstract setting of PR.4/ainf-artin-schreier-condition assume (As). Write T_ℓ=1−ξ^ℓφ^(−1). BMS2 Lemma 10.7, for i≥0 and j≥1, makes three assertions. On the quotient H^i(C)/μ^jH^i(C), the operator T_(ℓ+j) is injective at ℓ=0 and invertible at positive ℓ. On the μ^j-torsion subgroup of H^i(C), T_ℓ is onto at ℓ=0 and invertible at positive ℓ. On the quotient H^i(C)[μ^j]/H^i(C)[μ], T_ℓ is invertible for every ℓ≥0. (Lemma 10.8) Define ξ^iφ^{−1} on τ^{≤i}Lη_μ C as the composite τ^{≤i}Lη_μ C ≃ τ^{≤i}Lη_{φ^{−1}(μ)} C → τ^{≤i}Lη_ξ Lη_{φ^{−1}(μ)} C = τ^{≤i}Lη_μ C (first map φ^{−1}, second map multiplication by ξ^i). Then the canonical map ι : τ^{≤i}Lη_μ C → C commutes with 1 − ξ^iφ^{−1} and induces a quasi-isomorphism τ^{≤i} hofib(1 − ξ^iφ^{−1} on τ^{≤i}Lη_μ C) → τ^{≤i} hofib(1 − ξ^iφ^{−1} on C).

**Hypotheses and conventions.** A is p-power torsion, so p is nilpotent on C and 1 − p·(anything) is an automorphism of C. (As) holds and ξ − p ∈ φ^{−1}(μ)A (the A_inf congruence used in the proof of Lemma 10.7); H^0(C) is μ-torsion-free; φ : C ≃ C is a φ-semilinear quasi-isomorphism. The décalage functor Lη and the identities H^j(Lη_μ C) ≅ H^j(C)/H^j(C)[μ] and Lη_ξ Lη_{φ^{−1}(μ)} = Lη_μ are owned by AInfCohomology:AI.1.

**Construction or proof.**

1. (1), (2): the fibre sequence C → C → C/μ^jC (first map μ^j) is compatible with 1 − ξ^ℓφ^{−1}, 1 − ξ^{ℓ+j}φ^{−1}, 1 − ξ^{ℓ+j}φ^{−1}; so is the Bockstein sequence 0 → H^i(C)/μ^j → H^i(C/μ^j) → H^{i+1}(C)[μ^j] → 0, whose middle operator is an automorphism by (As). This gives injectivity on the left and surjectivity on the right.
2. For ℓ > 0 it remains to prove injectivity of 1 − ξ^ℓφ^{−1} on H^{i+1}(C)[μ^j]; induct on j through 0 → H[μ] → H[μ^j] → H[μ^{j−1}] to j = 1, where ξ^ℓφ^{−1} is the restriction of pξ^{ℓ−1}φ^{−1} because ξ ≡ p modulo φ^{−1}(μ), and 1 − pξ^{ℓ−1}φ^{−1} is an automorphism.
3. (3): multiplication by μ embeds H^i(C)[μ^j]/H^i(C)[μ] into H^i(C)[μ^{j−1}] compatibly with 1 − ξ^ℓφ^{−1} and 1 − ξ^{ℓ+1}φ^{−1}; injectivity from (2) on the right, surjectivity from (2) on the left.
4. For Lemma 10.8, AI.1 identifies the kernel of H^j(ι) with H^j(C)[μ^j]/H^j(C)[μ] and its cokernel with H^j(C)/μ^jH^j(C), for 0<j≤i. On the kernel the induced operator is T_(i−j); on the cokernel it is T_i. Lemma 10.7 makes the kernel operator invertible for all j≤i, and makes the cokernel operator invertible for j<i and injective for j=i. In degree zero ι is an isomorphism. The long exact sequences of the two homotopy fibres now give the asserted comparison through degree i, including the boundary injectivity needed at degree i.

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-4-crystalline-logarithm-exact-sequence"></a>

### Crystalline logarithmic exact sequence

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/crystalline-logarithm-exact-sequence` · lemma. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/PR4`.

Let R be a quasiregular semiperfect F_p-algebra and J=ker(R^♭→R). There is a natural exact sequence 0→(1+J)^×→^(log[·])Fil^1_NA_crys(R)→^(φ/p−1)A_crys(R)→0. The first map is the crystalline logarithm of the Teichmüller lift, not a logarithm of an arbitrary unit of R.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** Use the canonical PD envelope A_crys(R), its Frobenius, and its Nygaard filtration.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Use p-completeness and p-torsion-freeness of the three groups to reduce exactness modulo p. Isolate the first conjugate-filtration step of A_crys(R)/p and identify its degree-zero quotient with R♭/φ(J).
2. The divided Frobenius on the quotient of Fil_N^1 by p has a degree-zero piece supplied by multiplication by p. Remove that piece; the remaining exactness problem lies in ker(Fil_1^conj(A/p)→R), with target gr_1^conj(A/p).
3. Expand log[1−x] modulo p using terms of degrees at most p. On J/J² this induces the crystalline conjugate identification −[x]^p/p. Reduce the remaining logarithm to a homomorphism (1+J²)/(1+φ(J))→J²/φ(J).
4. For injectivity choose a finitely generated ideal K⊆J with x∈K². Vanishing of the logarithm modulo p improves x modulo φ(J) to successively higher powers of K; K^(pm)⊆φ(K) for m generators finishes the argument.
5. For surjectivity reduce to products uv in J². On their nilpotent principal ideal modulo φ(J), the truncated logarithm has linear coefficient one; its compositional inverse recovers every such product. Lift exactness back p-adically.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/qrsp-char-p-acrys`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-qrsp-char-p-acrys); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/nygaard-filtration-qrsp`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-3-nygaard-filtration-qrsp); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/prismatic-logarithm`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-4-prismatic-logarithm); `CrystallineCohomology:CR.0`; `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.5`; `CrystallineCohomology:CR.4`.

**Acceptance.** For R perfect, J=0 and φ/p−1:pW(R)→W(R) is bijective via multiplication by p followed by 1−pφ^(-1). The nontrivial kernel for a semiperfect quotient consists of lifted units 1+J, not all units of R^♭.

**Sources.** [BL22](https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.06120v1), Theorem 7.1.1 and proof, §7.1. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 167. Theorem 7.1.1 and its proof, pp.167–170. The theorem identifies both the logarithmic kernel and the surjection by divided Frobenius..

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-4-etale-comparison"></a>

### The étale comparison theorem for arbitrary p-adic formal schemes

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/etale-comparison` · theorem. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.Etale` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/Etale/Comparison`.

Let R be a perfectoid ring, (A, (d)) the perfect prism with A/d = R, and X an arbitrary p-adic formal scheme over R. Let Δ_{X/A} ∈ D(X_ét, A) be the derived prismatic cohomology of X relative to A (PR.2; the étale sheafification of S ↦ Δ_{S/A} on affine opens Spf S), with its Frobenius. Let X_η := X ×_{Spf R} Spa(R[1/p], R) be the adic generic fibre and μ : X_{η,ét} → X_ét the nearby-cycles map. Then for every n ≥ 0 there is a canonical identification Rμ_* Z/p^n ≃ (Δ_{X/A}[1/d]/p^n)^{φ=1} in D(X_ét, Z/p^n). In particular, for X = Spf S affine, RΓ_ét(Spec(S[1/p]), Z/p^n) ≃ (Δ_{S/A}[1/d]/p^n)^{φ=1}. The fixed points are the derived ones of PR.4/frobenius-fixed-points. The identification is natural in X and in (R, A), and for X = Spf S with S perfectoid it is the isomorphism of PR.4/perfectoid-artin-schreier-witt.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** R is perfectoid and (A, (d)) is its perfect prism; a generator d of the prism ideal is fixed (it exists, the prism being perfect). X is any p-adic formal scheme over Spf R: no smoothness, no finite-type, flatness or regularity hypothesis, and no restriction on singularities; this corrects the stage text, which restricted the comparison to smooth formal schemes (red-team finding RT-AREA-padic-2/6). Δ_{X/A} is the derived (animated) prismatic cohomology of PR.2, not the cohomology of the prismatic site of a singular X. (−)[1/d] and /p^n are applied before taking fixed points; no completion is applied after inverting d.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Let F(S) = RΓ(Spec S[1/p], Z/p^n) and G(S) = (Δ_{S/A}[1/d]/p^n)^{φ=1} on affine formal schemes over Spf R. F is an arc_p-sheaf [Bhatt–Mathew, The arc-topology, Corollary 6.17] and is arc_p-locally concentrated in degree 0 (products of p-complete rank-one valuation rings with algebraically closed fraction field, BS22 Remark 8.9), so F is the arc_p-sheafification of H^0(F); lifting clopen decompositions through arc_p-equivalences gives H^0(F) → H^0_{arc_p}(−, Z/p^n) and hence F → RΓ_{arc_p}(−, Z/p^n).
2. G(S) → (Δ_{S/A,perf}[1/d]/p^n)^{φ=1} is an isomorphism: reduce to n = 1, where Δ_{S/A,perf}/p is the d-completed colimit of Δ_{S/A}/p along φ_S and each φ_S induces an equivalence on ((−)[1/d])^{φ=1}; apply PR.4/fixed-points-completed-colimits.
3. G is an arc-sheaf because S ↦ S_perfd is (BS22 Corollary 8.11), and an arc_p-sheaf because G(S × S') = G(S) when pS' = 0: Δ_{S'/A,perf} = W(S'_perf) (BS22 Example 8.3) and (d) = (p) there, so W(S'_perf)/p^n[1/d] = 0.
4. The map Z/p^n → G extends uniquely to RΓ_{arc_p}(−, Z/p^n) → G; composing gives F → G, a map of arc_p-sheaves. It is an isomorphism arc-locally, where S may be taken perfectoid and the claim is PR.4/perfectoid-artin-schreier-witt (alternatively on products of absolutely integrally closed valuation rings of rank ≤ 1).
5. Globalise: the étale sheafification of S ↦ RΓ(Spec S[1/p], Z/p^n) on X_ét is Rμ_* Z/p^n by Huber's comparison between Spec(S[1/p]) and Spa(S[1/p], S) (H1:henselian), and that of G is (Δ_{X/A}[1/d]/p^n)^{φ=1}.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/frobenius-fixed-points`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-4-frobenius-fixed-points); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/fixed-points-completed-colimits`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-4-fixed-points-completed-colimits); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/perfectoid-artin-schreier-witt`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-4-perfectoid-artin-schreier-witt); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/derived-prismatic-cohomology`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-derived-prismatic-cohomology); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/perfection-of-prismatic-cohomology`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-perfection-of-prismatic-cohomology); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/frobenius-on-prismatic-cohomology`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-frobenius-on-prismatic-cohomology); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/perfect-prisms-perfectoid-rings`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-perfect-prisms-perfectoid-rings); `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2`; `ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0`; `ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1:henselian`; `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E2`; `ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1:formal-adic-comparison`.

**Acceptance.** X = Spf O_C: both sides are Z/p^n. X = Spf O_C⟨T^{±1}⟩ (formal torus): after a choice of ε, H^1 of both sides is the group of units of C⟨T^{±1}⟩ modulo p^n-th powers (Kummer theory; C⟨T^{±1}⟩ is a principal ideal domain); it contains the class of T, of order p^n, and is not finitely generated, since units 1 + aT with |a| < 1 close to 1 are not p-th powers. A singular input, S = O_C⟨x, y⟩/(xy): the statement holds with the derived Δ_{S/A}; no smoothness is used. X of characteristic p: both sides vanish. For S perfectoid the map is the Artin–Schreier–Witt/tilting isomorphism.

**Sources.** [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Theorem 9.1 and its proof. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 71. the theorem in its full generality, both the nearby-cycle form and the affine form; the proof steps follow the printed proof. [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Section 9, first sentence.  the source states the generality (arbitrary rings) that the stage text had narrowed.

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-4-syntomic-filtered-colimits"></a>

### Z/p^r(i) commutes with filtered colimits

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/syntomic-filtered-colimits` · theorem. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.Syntomic` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/Syntomic/Contraction`.

For all i ≥ 0 and r ≥ 1 the sheaf Z/p^r(i) = Z_p(i)/p^r commutes with filtered colimits in the category QSyn of quasisyntomic rings: for a filtered diagram (A_j) of quasisyntomic rings whose p-completed colimit A is quasisyntomic, colim_j Z/p^r(i)(A_j) → Z/p^r(i)(A) is an isomorphism.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** Colimits of rings are p-completed colimits; the statement is about the reduction modulo p^r, not about Z_p(i) itself. The proof planned is the direct proof of BMS2 through Lemma 7.22; the first printed proof, through K-theory and the theorem of Clausen–Mathew–Morrow, is not used (no trace input may enter PR.4). i ≥ 0; for i < 0 both sides vanish.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Induct on r to reduce to r = 1, using the fibre sequences Z/p^{r−1}(i) → Z/p^r(i) → Z/p(i).
2. Fix C = Q_p^cycl completed; by quasisyntomic descent along A → A ⊗̂ O_C and its Čech nerve (functorial quasisyntomic covers) assume the A_j are O_C-algebras.
3. For p-torsion-free quasisyntomic O_C-algebras, PR.4/divided-frobenius-contraction lets one compute Z/p(i)(A) modulo N^{≥m}Δ̂_A{i}/p for m large, and (N^{≥i}Δ̂_A{i}/p)/(N^{≥m}Δ̂_A{i}/p) is a finite extension of Nygaard graded pieces, which commute with filtered colimits (they are built from wedge powers of the cotangent complex, PR.3/nygaard-graded-pieces).
4. For arbitrary quasisyntomic O_C-algebras define φ_i on N^{≥m}Δ̂_A{i}/p by left Kan extension and Nygaard completion; φ_i − 1 is still an equivalence and the same argument applies (BMS2, direct proof of Proposition 7.21). The statement for all animated rings is BL Proposition 7.4.8.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/syntomic-complex`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-4-syntomic-complex); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/divided-frobenius-contraction`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-4-divided-frobenius-contraction); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/nygaard-graded-pieces`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-3-nygaard-graded-pieces); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/quasisyntomic-descent`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-quasisyntomic-descent); `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.5`.

**Acceptance.** O_C = colim of the rings of integers of finite extensions, p-completed: Z/p^r(i)(O_C) is the colimit of the complexes of the p-completed finite levels. A filtered colimit of perfectoid rings: Z/p^r(i) of the p-completed colimit is the colimit, as used in the proof of Bhatt–Scholze Theorem 9.4. The statement fails for Z_p(i) without reduction: Z_p(0) of a filtered colimit is p-complete, the colimit of Z_p(0) need not be.

**Sources.** [BMS2](https://arxiv.org/abs/1802.03261v2), Proposition 7.21, direct proof. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 52. statement of the proposition and its second (direct) proof, the one planned. [BL22](https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.06120v1), Proposition 7.4.8. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 179. the stronger statement for all animated rings, by the same contraction argument.

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-4-syntomic-complex-char-p"></a>

### Syntomic complexes of quasiregular semiperfect rings

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/syntomic-complex-char-p` · theorem. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.Syntomic` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/Syntomic/CharP`.

Let S be a quasiregular semiperfect F_p-algebra. There is a φ-equivariant isomorphism Δ_S ≅ A_crys(S) identifying the Nygaard filtration of Δ_S with N^{≥•}A_crys(S) = {x : φ(x) ∈ p^• A_crys(S)}, and Z_p(i)(S) is represented by the two-term complex N^{≥i}A_crys(S) → A_crys(S), x ↦ φ(x)/p^i − x (equivalently by its Nygaard-completed version). For i > 0 the complex Z_p(i)(S) is concentrated in degree 0 and equals the p-torsion-free group A_crys(S)^{φ=p^i}. For i = 0, H^0(Z_p(0)(S)) = A_crys(S)^{φ=1} is p-torsion-free and H^1(Z_p(0)(S)) = coker(φ − 1) vanishes after sheafification on quasiregular semiperfect F_p-algebras. In particular Conjecture 7.18 of BMS2 holds in characteristic p. By quasisyntomic descent, for every quasisyntomic F_p-scheme X there is a fibre sequence RΓ_syn(X, Z_p(i)) → Fil^i_N RΓ_crys(X/Z_p) → RΓ_crys(X/Z_p) with second map φ/p^i − 1, and after inverting p, RΓ_syn(X, Z_p(i))[1/p] ≃ fib(φ − p^i on RΓ_crys(X/Z_p)[1/p]).

**Hypotheses and conventions.** S is a quasiregular semiperfect F_p-algebra; X is a quasisyntomic F_p-scheme. Δ̂_S and its Nygaard filtration are identified with Â_crys(S) through the prismatic crystalline comparison and the Nygaard theory of PR.1–PR.3 (Bhatt–Lurie Example 7.4.4; Anschütz–Le Bras Lemma 3.4.2), not through BMS2 Theorem 8.17, which is a statement about TC^− owned by RefinedTraceMethods:RT.6. The printed Proposition 8.20 asserts concentration in degree 0 for all i ≥ 0 and every S; for i = 0 this holds only after sheafification (source issue PrismaticCohomology/E41: Z_p(0)(F_p) has H^1 = Z_p). The statement above is the corrected one. The exact sequence 0 → π_{2i}TC → π_{2i}TC^− → π_{2i}TP → 0 of the same passage belongs to RefinedTraceMethods:RT.6. The filtration on crystalline cohomology is the Nygaard filtration, not the Hodge filtration; after inverting p it becomes trivial.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Identify (Δ_S, φ, Fil_N) with (A_crys(S), φ, N^{≥•}): Δ_S, the initial prism of S, is a crystalline prism, and the crystalline comparison identifies it φ-equivariantly with the p-completed divided power envelope A_crys(S) of W(S^♭) → S (PR.2/qrsp-char-p-acrys (2), PR.2/qrsp-prism, CR.0; Anschütz–Le Bras Lemma 3.4.2); both Nygaard filtrations are defined by divisibility of φ by powers of the generator p (PR.3/nygaard-filtration-qrsp).
2. Surjectivity of φ_i − 1 for i > 0 on the completed complex is PR.4/acrys-divided-frobenius-surjective (1); p-torsion-freeness of N^{≥i}Â_crys(S) follows from that of A_crys(S) (BMS2 Theorem 8.14(1), PR.2/qrsp-char-p-acrys and CR.4) and the definition of the Nygaard filtration.
3. The map α from ker(φ_i − 1) on N^{≥i}A_crys(S) to the kernel on the completion is an isomorphism: the Frobenius of A_crys(S) factors through the Nygaard completion, which gives β : N^{≥i}Â_crys(S) → A_crys(S) with β ∘ α = φ_i and α ∘ β = φ_i; so α(x) = 0 and φ_i(x) = x give x = β(α(x)) = 0, and for y in the completed kernel x = β(y) maps to y and satisfies φ(x) = p^i x. The uncompleted kernel is A_crys(S)^{φ=p^i} by definition of the filtration.
4. i = 0: PR.4/acrys-divided-frobenius-surjective (2). Globalisation: quasisyntomic descent for crystalline cohomology and its Nygaard filtration (BL Theorem 4.6.1, Notation 5.3.2, Proposition 5.3.6) and PR.4/syntomic-cohomology-formal-schemes; Fil^i_N ⊗ Q is everything since p^i lies in Fil^i_N.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/syntomic-complex`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-4-syntomic-complex); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/syntomic-cohomology-formal-schemes`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-4-syntomic-cohomology-formal-schemes); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/acrys-divided-frobenius-surjective`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-4-acrys-divided-frobenius-surjective); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/qrsp-char-p-acrys`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-qrsp-char-p-acrys); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/qrsp-prism`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-qrsp-prism); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/nygaard-filtration-qrsp`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-3-nygaard-filtration-qrsp); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/nygaard-completion`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-3-nygaard-completion); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/quasisyntomic-descent`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-quasisyntomic-descent); `CrystallineCohomology:CR.0`; `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.4`; `CrystallineCohomology:CR.4`.

**Acceptance.** S perfect: Z_p(i)(S) = W(S)^{F=p^i} = 0 for i > 0, and Z_p(0)(S) = fib(F − 1 on W(S)). S = O_C/p: H^0(Z_p(i)(S)) = A_crys^{φ=p^i} contains t^i for t = log[ε], since φ(t) = pt; after inverting p these are the graded pieces of the ring of the Fargues–Fontaine curve. S = F_p, i = 0: H^1 = Z_p ≠ 0, the counterexample to the uncorrected statement. i = 1: A_crys(S)^{φ=p} ≅ T_p(S^×) via x ↦ log[x] (PR.4/syntomic-low-weights).

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-4-syntomic-truncation-ainf"></a>

### Syntomic complexes of smooth formal schemes over O_C vanish above degree i

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/syntomic-truncation-ainf` · theorem. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.Syntomic` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/Syntomic/NearbyCycles`.

Let C be a complete algebraically closed extension of Q_p, A_inf = A_inf(O_C) with ξ a generator of ker θ, ξ̃ = φ(ξ), and 𝔛 a smooth formal scheme over Spf O_C. On 𝔛_ét the syntomic sheaf Z/p^n(i) = Z_p(i)/p^n is identified with hofib(φ_i − 1 : N^{≥i}AΩ_𝔛{i} → AΩ_𝔛{i})/p^n, where AΩ_𝔛 is the A_inf-cohomology sheaf with its Nygaard filtration. Then this complex is concentrated in degrees ≤ i, and the natural map τ^{≤i} hofib(τ^{≤i}N^{≥i}AΩ{i}/p^n → τ^{≤i}AΩ{i}/p^n) → hofib(N^{≥i}AΩ{i} → AΩ{i})/p^n (both fibres of φ_i − 1) is an equivalence of sheaves of complexes on 𝔛_ét. In coordinates: for 𝔛 = Spf A with a framing O_C⟨T_1^{±1}, …, T_d^{±1}⟩ → A (the p-completion of an étale map) and the induced deformation Ã over A_inf, AΩ_A = q-Ω^•_{Ã/A_inf}, N^{≥i}AΩ_A = ξ^{max(i−•,0)} q-Ω^•_{Ã/A_inf}, φ(d_q log T_a) = ξ̃ d_q log T_a and φ_i = ξ̃^{−i}φ.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** C is algebraically closed and complete (the hypothesis of Theorem 1.15(2); Section 10 itself uses the notation μ, ξ of Section 9 and does not restate it). 𝔛 is smooth over Spf O_C; the framing exists étale-locally. The identification of Z/p^n(i) on 𝔛_ét with the AΩ-fibre uses AΩ ≃ φ^*Δ (PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/ainf-omega-comparison) and the match of the Nygaard filtration with the Lη_ξ filtration (PR.3/leta-frobenius-factorisation); the printed text cites BMS2 Theorem 9.6 and Remark 9.11, obtained there through TC, which the plan does not use.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Restrict Z_p(i) to 𝔛_ét (BMS2 Remark 10.4: a quasisyntomic sheaf gives an étale sheaf on 𝔛) and identify N^{≥i}Δ̂{i} → Δ̂{i} with N^{≥i}AΩ{i} → AΩ{i}: PR.6/ainf-omega-comparison, PR.3/relative-nygaard-filtration, PR.3/leta-frobenius-factorisation, and PR.5/absolute-relative-comparison for the perfect prism A_inf.
2. Reduce to n = 1 and to a framed affine; write the complex as ξ̃^{−i}φ − 1 : ξ^{max(i−•,0)} q-Ω^• → q-Ω^• on the basis d_q log T_{a_1} ∧ ⋯ ∧ d_q log T_{a_j}, on which φ acts by ξ̃^j (PR.6/q-de-rham-comparison and AI.4 for the coordinate description).
3. Degree j > i: the map is ξ̃^{j−i}φ − 1 on Ã/p, an automorphism with inverse −Σ_{r≥0} ξ̃_r^{j−i}φ^r, ξ̃_r = ξ̃φ(ξ̃)⋯φ^{r−1}(ξ̃). Degree j = i: the map is φ − 1 on Ã/p, étale-locally surjective by Artin–Schreier covers, the étale sites of 𝔛, Spf Ã/p and Spec A/p being equivalent.
4. Hence the fibre has no cohomology above degree i and is unchanged by truncating source and target at degree i.

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-4-etale-comparison-coefficients"></a>

### Coefficient compatibility and passage to Z_p in the étale comparison

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/etale-comparison-coefficients` · theorem. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.Etale` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/Etale/Comparison`.

In the situation of PR.4/etale-comparison write c_n : Rμ_* Z/p^n ≃ (Δ_{X/A}[1/d]/p^n)^{φ=1}. (1) For n ≥ 1 the square formed by c_n, c_{n−1}, the map Rμ_* Z/p^n → Rμ_* Z/p^{n−1} induced by reduction and the map of fixed points induced by Δ_{X/A}[1/d]/p^n → Δ_{X/A}[1/d]/p^{n−1} commutes; likewise for the maps induced by multiplication p : Z/p^{n−1} → Z/p^n, and c_n ⊗^L_{Z/p^n} Z/p^{n−1} = c_{n−1}. (2) The c_n are maps of commutative algebra objects of D(X_ét, Z/p^n). (3) Passing to derived limits, Rμ_* Z_p := R lim_n Rμ_* Z/p^n ≃ ((Δ_{X/A}[1/d])^∧_p)^{φ=1}, where (−)^∧_p is derived p-completion; for X = Spf S, R lim_n RΓ_ét(Spec(S[1/p]), Z/p^n) ≃ ((Δ_{S/A}[1/d])^∧_p)^{φ=1}. The limit is the derived limit of complexes; its cohomology sits in Milnor sequences with lim and lim^1 of the groups H^i(−, Z/p^n).

**Hypotheses and conventions.** Same hypotheses as PR.4/etale-comparison: R perfectoid, X an arbitrary p-adic formal scheme over R. Z_p-coefficients on the generic fibre mean the derived limit of the Z/p^n-cohomology (equivalently pro-étale cohomology of the constant sheaf lim Z/p^n); they are not étale cohomology of a constant sheaf Z_p. The p-completion in (3) is applied after inverting d; (Δ_{X/A}[1/d])^∧_p is in general not Δ_{X/A}[1/d].

**Construction or proof.**

1. The comparison F_n → G_n of Theorem 9.1 is the unique map of arc_p-sheaves of Z/p^n-modules extending the unit Z/p^n → G_n; functoriality of this characterisation in the coefficient ring gives the commutative squares of (1) (the source states the identification as canonical for each n; the squares follow from the uniqueness in its proof).
2. Δ_{X/A}[1/d]/p^n := Δ_{X/A}[1/d] ⊗^L_Z Z/p^n, so reduction of coefficients is base change and fixed points, a finite limit, commute with it; multiplicativity (2) holds because both sides are sheaves of commutative algebras and the comparison is the unit-preserving map of such (BS22 Theorem 1.8(4) states it for commutative algebras in D(Z/p^n)).
3. (3): R lim_n (M/p^n)^{φ=1} = (R lim_n M/p^n)^{φ=1} = (M^∧_p)^{φ=1} for M = Δ_{X/A}[1/d], since fibres commute with limits and R lim_n M ⊗^L Z/p^n is the derived p-completion (DD.1); Rμ_* commutes with R lim.
4. The identification of R lim_n Rμ_* Z/p^n with pro-étale nearby cycles of the sheaf lim Z/p^n uses repleteness of the pro-étale topos (E2).

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/etale-comparison`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-4-etale-comparison); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/frobenius-fixed-points`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-4-frobenius-fixed-points); `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`; `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E2`; `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2`.

**Acceptance.** X = Spf O_C: Z_p ≃ (W(C^♭))^{φ=1}, and the square for n → n − 1 is reduction Z/p^n → Z/p^{n−1}. Finite level: for the formal torus the Kummer class of T at level n maps to the Kummer class of T at level n − 1 on both sides. For S = Z_p^cycl the lim^1 term vanishes and H^1 = Hom_cont(Gal, Z_p).

**Sources.** [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Theorem 9.1 (the identification is canonical, for each n ≥ 0) and proof of Theorem 9.4 (the sheaves G_n with Z_p-coefficients). Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed pages 71, 73. the compatibility in n is not printed as a statement; it follows from the uniqueness of the comparison map in the proof, and the Z_p-form is the one used in Theorem 9.4. <a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-4-perfectoid-etale-cohomological-dimension"></a>

### Étale cohomological dimension of the generic fibre of a perfectoid ring

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/perfectoid-etale-cohomological-dimension` · theorem. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.Etale` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/Etale/CohomologicalDimension`.

Let R be a perfectoid ring corresponding to a perfect prism (A, I). The F_p-étale cohomological dimension of the scheme X = Spec(R[1/p]) is ≤ 1: for every étale sheaf F of F_p-modules on X one has H^i(X, F) = 0 for i > 1.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** X is the spectrum, not the adic spectrum, of R[1/p]; the statement is false for general sheaves on the adic spectrum. F is an arbitrary étale F_p-sheaf on the scheme X (a filtered colimit of Zariski-constructible sheaves). The bound concerns F_p-coefficients (hence p-power torsion sheaves by dévissage); nothing is claimed for ℓ ≠ p.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Reduce to F = j_! L with j : U → X the inclusion of a quasi-compact open of a constructible closed subset and L an F_p-local system of constant rank; by the method of the trace [Stacks, Tag 03SH] pass to a finite étale cover V → U of degree prime to p on which L is a successive extension of constant sheaves F_p.
2. Lift V → U to a finitely presented finite map Spec(S) → Spec(R), put Y = Spec(S[1/p]) and let J ⊂ S be a finitely generated ideal cutting out the complement of V; dévissage reduces to RΓ(Y, j_! F_p) ∈ D^{≤1}.
3. By the étale comparison (PR.4/etale-comparison) for Spec(S) and Spec(S/J), RΓ(Y, j_! F_p) is (−/p[1/I])^{φ=1} applied to the fibre of Δ_{S/A,perf} → Δ_{(S/J)/A,perf}; fixed points raise the cohomological amplitude by at most one, so it suffices that this fibre is connective, which can be checked after base change to A/I, that is, for S_perfd → (S/J)_perfd.
4. Both S_perfd and (S/J)_perfd are discrete perfectoid rings because R → S is integral (BS22 Theorem 10.11), (S/J)_perfd ≃ (S_perfd/J S_perfd)_perfd by the universal property (PR.2/connective-perfectoidization-perfectoid), and S_perfd/J → (S_perfd/J)_perfd is surjective by BS22 Theorem 7.4 (PerfectoidQuotients:Q4).

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/etale-comparison`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-4-etale-comparison); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/frobenius-fixed-points`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-4-frobenius-fixed-points); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/perfection-of-prismatic-cohomology`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-perfection-of-prismatic-cohomology); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/connective-perfectoidization-perfectoid`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-connective-perfectoidization-perfectoid); `PerfectoidQuotients:Q4`; `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2`.

**Acceptance.** R = O_C: X = Spec C has cohomological dimension 0 ≤ 1. R = Z_p^cycl: X is the spectrum of the completed cyclotomic field, whose absolute Galois group has p-cohomological dimension ≤ 1; H^1_ét(X, F_p) = Hom_cont(Gal, F_p) is non-zero, so the bound 1 is attained. R a perfect F_p-algebra: X is empty and the statement is vacuous.

**Sources.** [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Theorem 11.1 and its proof. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 85. statement with the warning about adic spectra, and the printed proof.

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-4-log-de-rham-witt-comparison"></a>

### Syntomic complexes of smooth algebras in characteristic p are logarithmic de Rham–Witt sheaves

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/log-de-rham-witt-comparison` · theorem. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.Syntomic` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/Syntomic/CharP`.

Let k be a perfect field of characteristic p, A a smooth k-algebra and X = Spec A. Let λ : qSyn_A^op → X_proét be the natural map from the (opposite of the) quasisyntomic site of A to the pro-étale site of X. Then for all i ≥ 0 there is a natural isomorphism Rλ_* Z_p(i) ≃ WΩ^i_{X,log}[−i] of sheaves of complexes on X_proét. Reducing modulo p^r: Rλ_* Z/p^r(i) ≃ W_rΩ^i_{X,log}[−i] on X_ét.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** k is a perfect field of characteristic p and A is smooth over k (Theorem 1.15(1) of BMS2 and Corollary 8.21). The statement is on the pro-étale site of X because the coefficients are p-adic; WΩ^i_log is the inverse limit sheaf. The source deduces it from the description of gr^i TC^− and gr^i TP; the plan uses instead the identification of Rλ_* of the Nygaard-filtered prismatic sheaves with the Nygaard-filtered de Rham–Witt complex, which needs no trace-theoretic input.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Rλ_* of S ↦ (Δ_S, Fil^•_N, φ) on qSyn_A is the étale-local Nygaard-filtered absolute prismatic complex of A, which is (WΩ^•_X, N^{≥•}WΩ^•_X, φ): crystalline comparison (PR.1/crystalline-comparison, BL Theorem 4.6.1), the comparison of crystalline cohomology with the de Rham–Witt complex (CR.4), and the match of filtrations for regular F_p-algebras (BL Proposition 5.3.8; equivalently BMS2 Theorem 8.14(3) with quasisyntomic descent, CR.4).
2. N^{≥i}WΩ^•_X is complete for the Nygaard filtration, so the Nygaard completion changes nothing and Rλ_* Z_p(i) ≃ fib(φ_i − 1 : N^{≥i}WΩ^•_X → WΩ^•_X) as pro-étale sheaves of complexes.
3. PR.4/log-forms-divided-frobenius identifies this fibre with WΩ^i_{X,log}[−i].
4. Use the finite-level logarithmic kernel sequence requested from CR.4 to identify WΩ^i_log/p^r with W_rΩ^i_log. Surjectivity of restriction alone supplies only the surjection; the kernel sequence proves injectivity.
5. The finite-level identification is applied after étale sheafification; it is compatible with the restriction operators and the Nygaard-filtered comparison.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/syntomic-complex`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-4-syntomic-complex); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/syntomic-complex-char-p`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-4-syntomic-complex-char-p); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/log-forms-divided-frobenius`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-4-log-forms-divided-frobenius); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/crystalline-comparison`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-crystalline-comparison); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/quasisyntomic-descent`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-quasisyntomic-descent); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.5/absolute-nygaard-filtration`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-5-absolute-nygaard-filtration); `CrystallineCohomology:CR.4`; `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.4`; `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.5`; `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E2`; [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/qrsp-char-p-acrys`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-qrsp-char-p-acrys); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/nygaard-filtration-qrsp`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-3-nygaard-filtration-qrsp).

**Acceptance.** i = 0: Rλ_* Z_p(0) = Z_p, the constant pro-étale sheaf lim Z/p^r. i = 1: Rλ_* Z_p(1) = WΩ^1_log[−1], matching the classical fact that the pushforward of μ_{p^n} from the flat site is W_nΩ^1_log[−1]. A = k: Z_p(i)(k) = 0 for i ≥ 1. A = k[T^{±1}], i = 1: dlog[T] is a non-zero section of WΩ^1_log.

**Sources.** [BMS2](https://arxiv.org/abs/1802.03261v2), Corollary 8.21 and Remark 8.22; Theorem 1.15(1). Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed pages 8, 66. the statement with its hypotheses; the proof is rerouted through the Nygaard-filtered de Rham–Witt complex and Proposition 8.4. [BM23](https://arxiv.org/abs/2202.04818v2), Example 1.3. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 1. Bhatt–Mathew record the same identification Z/p^n(i)_X ≃ W_nΩ^i_log[−i] for regular F_p-schemes.

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-4-nearby-cycles-comparison"></a>

### Syntomic complexes as truncated p-adic nearby cycles

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/nearby-cycles-comparison` · theorem. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.Syntomic` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/Syntomic/NearbyCycles`.

Let C be a complete algebraically closed extension of Q_p and 𝔛 a smooth formal scheme over Spf O_C with generic fibre X; let ψ : X_ét → 𝔛_ét be the map of sites. Then for all i ≥ 0 and n ≥ 1 there is a natural equivalence Z/p^n(i) ≃ τ^{≤i} Rψ_* Z/p^n(i) of sheaves of complexes on 𝔛_ét, compatible in n; on the left Z/p^n(i) is the syntomic sheaf Z_p(i)/p^n restricted to 𝔛_ét, on the right the usual Tate twist on X. Passing to the inverse limit over n gives Z_p(i) ≃ τ^{≤i} Rψ_* Z_p(i) on the pro-étale site of 𝔛. Consequently the nearby cycle sheaves R^iψ_* Z/p^n are flat over Z/p^n.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** C is algebraically closed and complete over Q_p (BMS2 Theorem 1.15(2)); 𝔛 is smooth over Spf O_C. No properness is assumed. The comparison is with the truncation τ^{≤i}, not with all of Rψ_*: Z/p^n(i) → Rψ_* Z/p^n(i) is an isomorphism exactly when R^jψ_* Z/p^n = 0 for j > i. X is a rigid space, Rψ_* is the nearby-cycles functor of the formal scheme (owner ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology); no theory of nearby cycles beyond the definition is used. The AΩ input is PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/ainf-omega-comparison; no TC enters.

**Construction or proof.**

1. By PR.4/syntomic-truncation-ainf, Z/p^n(i) = τ^{≤i} hofib(φ_i − 1 : τ^{≤i}N^{≥i}AΩ{i}/p^n → τ^{≤i}AΩ{i}/p^n).
2. φ_i identifies τ^{≤i}N^{≥i}AΩ with τ^{≤i}AΩ (the Nygaard filtration is the Lη_ξ-filtration, PR.3/leta-frobenius-factorisation), turning the fibre into τ^{≤i} hofib(1 − ξ^iφ^{−1} on τ^{≤i}AΩ/p^n), with AΩ = Lη_μ Rν_*A_inf,X (AI.3).
3. By PR.4/leta-frobenius-fixed-points and PR.4/ainf-artin-schreier-condition this equals τ^{≤i} hofib(1 − ξ^iφ^{−1} on Rν_*A_inf,X/p^n).
4. On X_proét the map 1 − ξ^iφ^{−1} on A_inf,X/p^n is surjective with kernel Z/p^n · μ^i ≅ Z/p^n(i), so the fibre is τ^{≤i}Rν_*Z/p^n(i) = τ^{≤i}Rψ_*Z/p^n(i). All identifications are compatible with reduction n → n − 1; flatness of R^iψ_*Z/p^n follows from compatibility in n (BMS2 Remark 10.3).

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/syntomic-truncation-ainf`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-4-syntomic-truncation-ainf); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/ainf-artin-schreier-condition`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-4-ainf-artin-schreier-condition); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/leta-frobenius-fixed-points`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-4-leta-frobenius-fixed-points); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/syntomic-complex`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-4-syntomic-complex); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/ainf-omega-comparison`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-6-ainf-omega-comparison); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/leta-frobenius-factorisation`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-3-leta-frobenius-factorisation); `AInfCohomology:AI.3`; `AInfCohomology:AI.4`; `ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0`; `ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1:henselian`; `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E2`; [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/nygaard-filtration-q-de-rham-coordinates`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-6-nygaard-filtration-q-de-rham-coordinates); `ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1:formal-adic-comparison`.

**Acceptance.** 𝔛 = Spf O_C: Z/p^n(i)(O_C) ≃ Z/p^n(i)(C) in degree 0, agreeing with PR.4/tate-twist-perfectoid. 𝔛 = Spf O_C⟨T^{±1}⟩ and i = 1: H^1 of both sides contains the Kummer class of T, which is non-zero in R^1ψ_*μ_{p^n}. i = 0: Z/p^n ≃ τ^{≤0}Rψ_*Z/p^n = ψ_*Z/p^n. Compatibility in n: the squares with Z/p^n(i) → Z/p^{n−1}(i) commute.

**Sources.** [BMS2](https://arxiv.org/abs/1802.03261v2), Theorem 10.1, Remarks 10.2–10.4 and the end of Section 10. <a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-4-etale-comparison-scalar-extension"></a>

### Étale comparison after perfecting the base

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/etale-comparison-scalar-extension` · comparison. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/PR4`.

Let (A,I) be any bounded prism, let f:(A,I)→(A_∞,I_∞) be its completed perfect prism, and let R be a p-completely smooth A/I-algebra. Put R_∞=(R⊗_(A/I)A_∞/I_∞)^∧_p. For n≥1 and a generator d_∞ of I_∞, there is a canonical equivalence RΓ_ét(Spec(R_∞[1/p]),Z/p^n) ≃ ((Δ_(R/A)⊗̂^L_A A_∞)[1/d_∞]/p^n)^(φ=1). This specifies the scalar-extension version for a general base prism. Its étale side is the base-changed algebra R_∞.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** The completion of the prism perfection is essential; its raw Frobenius colimit need not be separated. R is p-completely smooth, so ordinary completed base change gives the derived base-changed algebra. The right side has the Frobenius transported through the canonical base-change equivalence; it is not an arbitrary endomorphism.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Construct the perfect prism A_∞ using PR.0/prism-perfection; it is bounded by perfect-prism-properties and its ideal is principal.
2. Apply PR.2/derived-prismatic-base-change (or the smooth PR.1/prismatic-base-change) to identify Δ_(R_∞/A_∞) with completed scalar extension of Δ_(R/A), respecting Frobenius.
3. Apply PR.4/etale-comparison over the perfect prism A_∞, and substitute the specified equivalence. Localisation at different generators of I_∞ yields the same complex.
4. Functoriality follows from the universal property of prism perfection and functoriality of both comparison maps.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/prism-perfection`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-prism-perfection); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/perfect-prism-properties`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-perfect-prism-properties); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/prismatic-base-change`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-prismatic-base-change); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/derived-prismatic-base-change`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-derived-prismatic-base-change); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/etale-comparison`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-4-etale-comparison).

**Acceptance.** For a perfect base prism, A_∞=A and R_∞=R, giving Theorem 9.1. For a crystalline base the base-changed R_∞ has characteristic p, its generic fibre is empty, and localising Δ at d_∞=p before reducing modulo p^n gives zero. Changing d_∞ by a unit has no effect because only localisation at its ideal occurs.

**Sources.** [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Lemma 3.9; Theorem 1.8(5); Construction 7.6; Theorem 9.1, §§3,7,9,53–55,64–66. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed pages 4, 31, 56, 71. Combines prism perfection, smooth derived base change and the perfect-base étale theorem. The scalar-extension variant is derived here; it is not quoted as a theorem over the original generic fibre..

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-4-crystalline-first-chern-class"></a>

### Crystalline first Chern class as a syntomic fibre

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/crystalline-first-chern-class` · comparison. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/PR4`.

For a quasisyntomic F_p-scheme X there is a natural fibre sequence RΓ_ét(X,G_m)^∧_p[−1]→^(c_1^crys)Fil^1_NRΓ_crys(X)→^(φ/p−1)RΓ_crys(X). The first Chern class gives the canonical weight-one comparison.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** The crystalline complex is the canonical derived crystalline complex; the left side is untruncated étale G_m cohomology.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Construct the crystalline first Chern class on the quasisyntomic site, compatibly with Frobenius, so it lands in the fibre of φ/p−1 on Fil_N^1 crystalline cohomology.
2. Both that fibre and the p-completed étale G_m complex shifted by −1 satisfy descent; use a pro-syntomic cover which is simultaneously pro-fppf and quasisyntomic.
3. On a quasiregular semiperfect F_p-algebra, Proposition 7.2.5 identifies the G_m complex with T_p(R×). Theorem 7.1.1 identifies this with the logarithmic fibre, proving the comparison and its naturality.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/crystalline-logarithm-exact-sequence`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-4-crystalline-logarithm-exact-sequence); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/quasisyntomic-descent`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-quasisyntomic-descent); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/syntomic-complex-char-p`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-4-syntomic-complex-char-p); `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2`; `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.5`.

**Acceptance.** For a perfect affine ring the chartwise kernel is zero. Using Pic alone in place of untruncated RΓ_ét(G_m) loses the Brauer contribution and fails on fields with p-primary Brauer classes.

**Sources.** [BL22](https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.06120v1), Construction 7.3.1, Variant 7.3.3, Theorem 7.3.5 and proof, §7.3. <a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-4-etale-comparison-smooth"></a>

### The étale comparison for smooth formal schemes (Theorem 1.8(4))

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/etale-comparison-smooth` · theorem. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.Etale` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/Etale/Comparison`.

Let (A, I) be a perfect prism and X a quasi-compact quasi-separated smooth p-adic formal scheme over A/I, with generic fibre X_η over Q_p as a (pre-)adic space and RΓ_Δ(X/A) = RΓ((X/A)_Δ, O_Δ) the cohomology of the prismatic site (PR.1). Then for every n ≥ 0 there is a canonical isomorphism RΓ_ét(X_η, Z/p^n) ≅ (RΓ_Δ(X/A)/p^n[1/I])^{φ=1} of commutative algebras in D(Z/p^n). It is the corollary of PR.4/etale-comparison obtained by taking RΓ(X_ét, −) and using that for smooth X the derived prismatic cohomology agrees with site cohomology.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** (A, I) is a perfect prism, so I = (d) is principal and A/I is perfectoid; perfectness is part of the hypothesis of Theorem 1.8(4). X is smooth over A/I; smoothness is needed only to identify the derived Δ_{X/A} with the site-theoretic RΓ_Δ(X/A), not for the comparison itself. X is qcqs for the global statement, so that inverting d and reducing modulo p^n commute with RΓ(X_ét, −).

**Construction or proof.**

1. Apply RΓ(X_ét, −) to Rμ_* Z/p^n ≃ (Δ_{X/A}[1/d]/p^n)^{φ=1} (PR.4/etale-comparison): the left side is RΓ_ét(X_η, Z/p^n) by definition of μ.
2. For smooth X the derived prismatic cohomology agrees with the cohomology of the prismatic site (PR.2/derived-agrees-with-site), so RΓ(X_ét, Δ_{X/A}) = RΓ_Δ(X/A); fixed points, /p^n and (for qcqs X) [1/d] commute with RΓ(X_ét, −).
3. Multiplicativity is PR.4/etale-comparison-coefficients (2).

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/etale-comparison`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-4-etale-comparison); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/etale-comparison-coefficients`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-4-etale-comparison-coefficients); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/derived-agrees-with-site`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-derived-agrees-with-site); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/relative-prismatic-cohomology`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-relative-prismatic-cohomology); `ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0`; `ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1:formal-adic-comparison`.

**Acceptance.** X = Spf O_C⟨T^{±1}⟩ over (A_inf, ker θ): H^1_ét(X_η, μ_{p^n}) is the group of units of C⟨T^{±1}⟩ modulo p^n-th powers, and the class of T corresponds to a φ-fixed class in H^1 of RΓ_Δ(X/A_inf)/p^n[1/d]. X proper smooth over O_C: with PR.1/proper-smooth-perfectness, RΓ_ét(X_C, Z/p^n) is the fixed points of φ on a perfect complex over A_inf/p^n[1/d] = W_n(C^♭). The statement for singular X is PR.4/etale-comparison, not this node.

**Sources.** [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Theorem 1.8 (4). Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 4. the smooth-case statement of the introduction, recorded as the corollary of Theorem 9.1.

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-4-syntomic-low-weights"></a>

### Syntomic complexes in weights n < 0, n = 0 and n = 1

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/syntomic-low-weights` · theorem. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.Syntomic` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/Syntomic/LowWeights`.

Let R be an animated commutative ring. (1) For n > 0, RΓ_syn(Spf R, Z_p(−n)) = 0. (2) There is a canonical map of commutative algebra objects α_R : RΓ_ét(Spec R, Z_p) → RΓ_syn(Spf R, Z_p), characterised by functoriality in R, and it is an isomorphism when R is p-complete; here RΓ_ét(Spec R, Z_p) = lim_k RΓ_ét(Spec R, Z/p^k). If moreover R is a p-complete ring with x ↦ x^p − x surjective on R/pR, then RΓ_syn(Spf R, Z_p) is concentrated in degree 0 and equals the ring of continuous Z_p-valued functions on Spec R. (3) There is a canonical map c_1^syn : RΓ_ét(Spec R, G_m)[−1] → RΓ_syn(Spf R, Z_p(1)), functorial in R and given, for R quasiregular semiperfectoid, in degree 0 by T_p(R^×) → T_p(Δ̄_R^×) → H^0_syn(Spf R, Z_p(1)), the second map being the prismatic logarithm; for R p-complete the induced map RΓ_ét(Spec R, G_m)^∧[−1] → RΓ_syn(Spf R, Z_p(1)) from the p-completion is an isomorphism. (4) Consequently, for a quasisyntomic ring R, Z_p(1)(R) ≃ RΓ_ét(Spec R, G_m)^∧[−1], and the natural map Pic(R)^∧[−2] → Z_p(1)(R), where Pic(R) = (τ^{≤1}RΓ(Spec R, G_m))[1] and (−)^∧ is derived p-completion, is an isomorphism on H^i for i ≤ 1 and injective on H^2; it is an isomorphism if and only if (τ^{≥2}RΓ(Spec R, G_m))^∧ = 0, which holds for perfectoid R and fails for R = F_p(t) (H^2 of the target is T_p Br(R) ≠ 0). This corrects Bhatt–Scholze Lemma 9.6, which asserts the isomorphism for every quasisyntomic ring; Z_p(1) is, locally for the quasisyntomic topology, the sheaf R ↦ T_p(R^×) = lim_n μ_{p^n}(R) in degree 0; and for a quasiregular semiperfect F_p-algebra R the sequence 0 → T_p(R^×) → Fil^1_N A_crys(R) → A_crys(R) → 0 (maps log[·] and φ/p − 1) is exact.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** R is an arbitrary animated commutative ring in (1); p-complete in the isomorphism statements of (2) and (3); quasisyntomic in (4). Étale cohomology with Z_p-coefficients is the derived inverse limit of Z/p^k-cohomology; G_m-cohomology is étale (for (4), flat cohomology gives the same τ^{≤1}). These statements replace BMS2 Propositions 7.16 and 7.17, whose proofs use K-theory and the theorem of Clausen–Mathew–Morrow; the proofs planned here are Bhatt–Lurie's and use no K-theory, TC or trace (requirement of the BMS2 route). In (2) the comparison is with étale cohomology of Spec R (equivalently of Spec R/p), not of the generic fibre Spec R[1/p].

**Construction or proof.**

1. (1) (BL Corollary 7.4.9): by sifted colimits and descent reduce to R quasiregular semiperfectoid, where with a generator e of A{−n}, φ{−n}(e) = λe with λ ∈ I^n, the complex is A → A, x ↦ x − λφ(x), whose differential has the convergent inverse x ↦ x + λφ(x) + λφ(λ)φ^2(x) + ⋯.
2. (2) (BL Proposition 8.1.8, Theorem 8.1.9, Corollary 8.1.10): α_R exists by the universal property of RΓ_ét(Spec −, Z_p) among étale sheaves of algebras; by derived descent modulo p (7.4.10 and Gabber's affine proper base change) reduce to animated F_p-algebras, by sifted colimits to polynomial F_p-algebras, where F_p ⊗ Δ_R ≃ dR_{R/F_p} and φ − 1 is an automorphism of Fil^1_Hodge = (Ω^{≥1}, d) since Frobenius vanishes on it; the remaining map is the Artin–Schreier isomorphism.
3. (3) (BL Theorem 7.1.1, Proposition 7.5.2, Theorem 7.5.6): construct c_1^syn on quasiregular semiperfectoid rings from PR.4/prismatic-logarithm (its image is φ{1}-fixed and lies in Fil^1_N) and extend by descent and Kan extension; to prove the isomorphism reduce modulo p by derived descent to animated F_p-algebras, then to quasisyntomic F_p-algebras, where it is the crystalline first Chern class isomorphism (BL Theorem 7.3.5), proved from the logarithm sequence 0 → (1 + J)^× → Fil^1_N A_crys(R) → A_crys(R) → 0 for quasiregular semiperfect R; surjectivity of φ/p − 1 there is PR.4/acrys-divided-frobenius-surjective with i = 1.
4. (4) (Bhatt–Scholze Lemma 9.6): Pic(−) is a quasisyntomic sheaf locally concentrated in degree −1 (rings without non-trivial line bundles form a basis), units are p-divisible locally, so the sheaf of complexes associated with R ↦ Pic(R)^∧[−2] is locally T_p(R^×), which is Z_p(1) by (3); the presheaf R ↦ Pic(R)^∧[−2] is itself not a sheaf of complexes, and the comparison map has cofibre (τ^{≥2}RΓ(Spec R, G_m))^∧[−1] ∈ D^{≥2}. For perfectoid R this cofibre vanishes because Z_p(1)(R) ∈ D^{[0,1]} (PR.4/syntomic-complex). The exact sequence is BL Example 7.4.5.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/syntomic-cohomology-formal-schemes`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-4-syntomic-cohomology-formal-schemes); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/syntomic-complex`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-4-syntomic-complex); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/prismatic-logarithm`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-4-prismatic-logarithm); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/acrys-divided-frobenius-surjective`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-4-acrys-divided-frobenius-surjective); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.5/absolute-relative-comparison`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-5-absolute-relative-comparison); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/de-rham-comparison-general`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-3-de-rham-comparison-general); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/crystalline-comparison`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-crystalline-comparison); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/quasisyntomic-descent`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-quasisyntomic-descent); `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2`; `CrystallineCohomology:CR.0`; `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.4`; `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.5`; [`mathlib:CommRing.Pic`](#mathlib-commring-pic); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/qrsp-char-p-acrys`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-qrsp-char-p-acrys); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/crystalline-logarithm-exact-sequence`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-4-crystalline-logarithm-exact-sequence); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/crystalline-first-chern-class`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-4-crystalline-first-chern-class); `CrystallineCohomology:CR.4`; [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/nygaard-filtration-qrsp`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-3-nygaard-filtration-qrsp).

**Acceptance.** Z_p(0)(O_C) = Z_p in degree 0; Z_p(0)(F_p) = RΓ_ét(Spec F_p, Z_p) has H^1 = Z_p. Z_p(1)(O_C) = T_p(O_C^×) = Z_p(1) in degree 0, since O_C^× is p-divisible and Pic(O_C) = 0. Z_p(1)(Z_p) has H^1 = (Z_p^×)^∧ = 1 + pZ_p for p odd and H^0 = T_p(Z_p^×) = 0. Z_p(−1)(R) = 0 for every R.

**Sources.** [BL22](https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.06120v1), Corollary 7.4.9.
