<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-4-etale-comparison-without-inverting-d"></a>

### The variant of the étale comparison without inverting p or d

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/etale-comparison-without-inverting-d` · theorem. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.Etale` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/Etale/Comparison`.

Let R be a perfectoid ring with perfect prism (A, (d)) and X a p-adic formal scheme over R. Then for all n ≥ 0 there is a canonical identification Z/p^n ≃ (Δ_{X/A}/p^n)^{φ=1} of objects of D(X_ét, Z/p^n), where Z/p^n is the constant étale sheaf on X. For X = Spf S affine: RΓ_ét(Spf S, Z/p^n) = RΓ_ét(Spec(S/p), Z/p^n) ≃ RΓ_ét(Spec S, Z/p^n) ≃ (Δ_{S/A}/p^n)^{φ=1}, and R lim_n gives RΓ_ét(Spec S, Z_p) ≃ (Δ_{S/A})^{φ=1} = fib(φ − 1 : Δ_{S/A} → Δ_{S/A}). The map Δ_{X/A}/p^n → Δ_{X/A}[1/d]/p^n induces on fixed points the adjunction map Z/p^n → Rμ_* Z/p^n of PR.4/etale-comparison.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** Same generality as Theorem 9.1: X arbitrary over a perfectoid ring R. No element is inverted; the right-hand side is in general not concentrated in degree 0 on global sections, since H^1_ét(Spec S, Z/p^n) can be non-zero. The source leaves the proof to the reader (the remark is quoted in the register as PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22/E17 for a wording slip: read 'a p-adic formal R-scheme'); the proof route below supplies it.

**Construction or proof.**

1. For a p-complete R-algebra S the absolute prismatic complex of S agrees with the relative one, Δ_S ≃ Δ_{S/A}, compatibly with Frobenius (Bhatt–Lurie Proposition 4.4.12; PR.5/absolute-relative-comparison for the perfect prism A).
2. Bhatt–Lurie Theorem 8.1.9 (the weight-0 case of PR.4/syntomic-low-weights) gives RΓ_ét(Spec S, Z_p) ≃ RΓ_syn(Spf S, Z_p) = fib(φ − 1 : Δ_S → Δ_S); its proof reduces modulo p by derived descent to animated F_p-algebras, then by sifted colimits to polynomial F_p-algebras, where F_p ⊗^L Δ is de Rham cohomology and φ − 1 is an automorphism of the Hodge-filtration piece Fil^1 because Frobenius vanishes on differential forms of positive degree.
3. Reduce modulo p^n; Gabber's affine analogue of proper base change for the henselian pair (S, pS) identifies RΓ_ét(Spec S, Z/p^n) with RΓ_ét(Spec S/p, Z/p^n), the étale cohomology of Spf S; sheafify on X_ét.
4. Compatibility with Theorem 9.1: both comparison maps are unit-preserving maps of étale sheaves of commutative algebras, and the square with Δ/p^n → Δ[1/d]/p^n commutes by the uniqueness used in Theorem 9.1 (checked arc_p-locally on O_C, as in Bhatt–Lurie Proposition 8.3.7).

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/frobenius-fixed-points`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-4-frobenius-fixed-points); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/syntomic-low-weights`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-4-syntomic-low-weights); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/etale-comparison`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-4-etale-comparison); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.5/absolute-relative-comparison`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-5-absolute-relative-comparison); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/derived-prismatic-cohomology`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-derived-prismatic-cohomology); `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2`; `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E2`.

**Acceptance.** S = O_C: Z/p^n ≃ (A_inf/p^n)^{φ=1} = W_n(O_C^♭)^{F=1}, and F − 1 is surjective on W_n(O_C^♭). S = Z_p^cycl: H^1 of both sides is H^1_ét(Spec F_p, Z/p^n) = Z/p^n, since the residue field of S is F_p. S an F_p-algebra over a perfect ring R: Δ_{S/A}/p is derived de Rham cohomology up to Frobenius twist and the statement is the Artin–Schreier sequence.

**Sources.** [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Remark 9.3. <a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-4-syntomic-etale-comparison"></a>

### The étale comparison morphism for syntomic cohomology

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/syntomic-etale-comparison` · theorem. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.Syntomic` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/Syntomic/EtaleComparison`.

(1) For every p-complete animated commutative ring R there is a canonical map of graded commutative ring objects of D(Z), ⊕_n γ{n} : ⊕_{n∈Z} RΓ_syn(Spf R, Z_p(n)) → ⊕_{n∈Z} RΓ_ét(Spec(R[1/p]), Z_p(n)), characterised up to homotopy by functoriality in R and by γ{1} ∘ c_1^syn ≃ c_1^ét, where c_1^ét : RΓ_ét(Spec R, G_m)[−1] → RΓ_ét(Spec R[1/p], Z_p(1)) is the étale first Chern class. (2) γ{0} is the composite of α_R^{−1} : RΓ_syn(Spf R, Z_p) ≃ RΓ_ét(Spec R, Z_p) with restriction to Spec R[1/p]. (3) For a perfectoid Z_p^cyc-algebra R with Ext^i_{Z_p^cyc}(F_p, R) = 0 for all i and x ↦ x^p − x surjective on R/pR, the map H^0_ét(Spf R, Z_p)[log_Δ(ε)] → ⊕_n RΓ_syn(Spf R, Z_p(n)) is an isomorphism of graded rings; in particular each RΓ_syn(Spf R, Z_p(n)) is concentrated in degree 0. This applies to O_C for C algebraically closed and spherically complete of mixed characteristic. (4) For a derived p-complete animated Z[ζ_(p^∞)]-algebra R, the class ε of the compatible roots of unity lies in H^0_syn(Spf R,Z_p(1)); inverting it in the graded syntomic algebra gives the graded generic étale algebra after p-completion. In weight zero this is the p-completed colimit along multiplication by ε of the nonnegative syntomic weights. The statement for arbitrary animated R is in syntomic-cohomology-schemes, after that object is constructed.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** R is a p-complete animated ring in (1), (2); a perfectoid algebra over Z_p^cyc, the p-completion of Z[q^{1/p^∞}]/([p]_q), in (3); an animated Z[ζ_{p^∞}]-algebra in (4). γ{n} is in general not an isomorphism, and no range of degrees in which it is one is asserted here: the isomorphism statements are (4) after inverting ε, PR.4/tate-twist-perfectoid for perfectoid rings and PR.4/nearby-cycles-comparison for smooth formal schemes over O_C. Bhatt–Lurie Section 8 proves no range of degrees in which γ{n} is an isomorphism. (4) is a reformulation of Bhatt–Scholze Theorem 9.1 over the perfectoid base Z_p^cyc and depends on it. In the Bhatt–Lurie text the remark after Theorem 8.1.9 cites the wrong theorem and Remark 8.5.4 misprints a target (source issues PrismaticCohomology/E43, E44).

**Construction or proof.**

1. Let 𝒞 be the perfectoid rings admitting a map from Z_p^cyc satisfying the two conditions of (3); 𝒞 contains products of O_{C_i} with C_i algebraically closed and spherically complete, hence is a basis for the arc_p-topology, and R ↦ RΓ_ét(Spec R[1/p], Z_p(n)) is right Kan extended from 𝒞 [Bhatt–Mathew, Corollary 6.17]. So γ and the homotopy with c_1 need only be built on 𝒞.
2. (3): for perfectoid Z_p^cyc-algebras multiplication by log_Δ(ε) : Z_p(n − 1) → Z_p(n) is an isomorphism for n ≥ 2 (its cofibre is 1 − φ^{−1} on (q − 1)^{−n}A/(q − 1)^{1−n}A, where φ^{−1} is divisible by p^{n−1}), and for n = 1 under the Ext-vanishing condition (BL Lemma 8.3.2); with PR.4/syntomic-low-weights (weights ≤ 0) this gives the polynomial ring.
3. (1), (2): on 𝒞 both graded rings are discrete in degree 0 after truncation, and there is a unique graded ring map extending restriction in weight 0 and sending log_Δ(ε) to the Kummer class ρ(ε); it sends log_Δ(u) to ρ(u) for all u ∈ T_p(R^×), checked pointwise on Spec R[1/p] by reduction to O_C, where T_p(O_C^×) is free on ε; hence independence of choices and functoriality (BL proofs of Theorem 8.3.1 and Proposition 8.3.7).
4. (4): reduce to R p-complete over Z_p^cyc = A/I with (A, I) the perfected q-de Rham prism; colim_n Fil^n_N Δ_R{n} → colim_n Δ_R{n} along log_Δ(q^p) is an isomorphism after p-completion (BL Proposition 8.5.3), so colim_n RΓ_syn(Spf R, Z_p(n)) = fib(φ − 1 on A[1/(q − 1)] ⊗̂ Δ_R) = (Δ_{R/A}[1/I]^∧_p)^{φ=1}, which is RΓ_ét(Spec R[1/p], Z_p) by PR.4/etale-comparison and PR.4/etale-comparison-coefficients; the composite with the map from (1) is the identity, checked arc_p-locally.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/syntomic-cohomology-formal-schemes`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-4-syntomic-cohomology-formal-schemes); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/syntomic-low-weights`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-4-syntomic-low-weights); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/prismatic-logarithm`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-4-prismatic-logarithm); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/etale-comparison`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-4-etale-comparison); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/etale-comparison-coefficients`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-4-etale-comparison-coefficients); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.5/absolute-relative-comparison`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-5-absolute-relative-comparison); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.5/absolute-nygaard-filtration`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-5-absolute-nygaard-filtration); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/q-de-rham-prism`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-q-de-rham-prism); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/prism-perfection`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-prism-perfection); `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2`; `PerfectoidQuotients:Q0:integral-algebra`.

**Acceptance.** R = O_C with C algebraically closed and spherically complete: ⊕_n RΓ_syn(Spf O_C, Z_p(n)) = Z_p[log_Δ(ε)] and γ sends log_Δ(ε) to the generator ρ(ε) of Z_p(1)(C); γ{n} is an isomorphism for n ≥ 0 and 0 → Z_p(n)(C) for n < 0. R = Z_p, n = 1: γ{1} on H^1 is the inclusion of the p-completion of Z_p^× into that of Q_p^×, with cokernel Z_p; not an isomorphism. R an F_p-algebra: the target vanishes, and (4) says that ε acts nilpotently up to p-completion: colim along ε of RΓ_syn(Spf R, Z_p(n)) is 0. n = 0: γ{0} is restriction RΓ_ét(Spec R, Z_p) → RΓ_ét(Spec R[1/p], Z_p).

**Sources.** [BL22](https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.06120v1), Theorem 8.3.1, Lemma 8.3.2, Proposition 8.3.3, Example 8.3.4, Proposition 8.3.7 and their proofs. <a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-4-tate-twist-perfectoid"></a>

### p-adic Tate twists of perfectoid rings and étale cohomology of the generic fibre

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/tate-twist-perfectoid` · theorem. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.Syntomic` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/Syntomic/Perfectoid`.

Let R be a perfectoid ring. For every integer n ≥ 1 there is a canonical identification Z_p(n)(R) ≃ RΓ_ét(Spec(R[1/p]), Z_p(n)), where the right-hand side is the derived limit over k of RΓ_ét(Spec(R[1/p]), μ_{p^k}^{⊗n}). For n = 0 there are canonical identifications Z_p(0)(R) ≃ RΓ_ét(Spec R, Z_p) ≃ RΓ_ét(Spec((R/p)_perf), Z_p). The identifications are multiplicative in n, natural in R, and for n = 1 the map is the Kummer map T_p-completion of units: on a p-complete, p-torsion-free rank-one valuation ring V with algebraically closed fraction field C it is T_p(V^×) → T_p(C^×) → H^0(Spec C, Z_p(1)). Moreover, as presheaves on perfectoid rings both sides are, p-completely arc-locally, concentrated in degree 0 and p-torsion-free, and the multiplication Z_p(1)^{⊗̂n} → Z_p(n) exhibits the target as the p-complete arc-sheafification of the source.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** R is an arbitrary perfectoid ring; for n ≥ 1 both sides vanish on rings of characteristic p. For n ≥ 1 the comparison is with the generic fibre Spec R[1/p]; for n = 0 with Spec R, equivalently with the special fibre. The two cases are different statements. The comparison map for n = 1 is constructed from Z_p(1) = lim μ_{p^n} (PR.4/syntomic-low-weights), not from the cyclotomic trace; with this input the proof is purely algebraic (Bhatt–Scholze Remark 9.5). Two slips in the printed proof are in the register as PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22/E18: (∗_b) concerns (G_1/p)^{⊗n} → G_n/p, and 'stacks' reads 'stalks'.

**Construction or proof.**

1. n = 0: PR.4/etale-comparison-without-inverting-d and R lim give Z_p(0)(R) = fib(φ − 1 on A_inf(R)) ≃ RΓ_ét(Spec R, Z_p); Gabber's affine analogue of proper base change passes to R/p and then to its perfection.
2. Over Z_p[ζ_{p^∞}]-algebras, with ε = (1, ζ_p, ζ_{p²}, …), q = [ε^{1/p}], d = [p]_q a generator of ker θ, and μ = q − 1: multiplication by μ^{−n} gives α'_n : F_n(R)/p = (d^{n/p}R^♭ → R^♭, φ/d^n − 1) → G_n(R)/p = (R^♭[1/d] → R^♭[1/d], φ − 1), where G_n/p is identified by PR.4/perfectoid-artin-schreier-witt; α'_n is the colimit of maps homotopic to isomorphisms induced by φ, hence a quasi-isomorphism, and is multiplicative in n.
3. (∗): F_n and G_n are p-complete arc-sheaves on perfectoid rings (arc-descent, BS22 §8.2 and Bhatt–Mathew), arc-locally discrete and p-torsion-free, and F_1^{⊗̂n} → F_n, G_1^{⊗̂n} → G_n are arc-sheafifications: checked for G_n/p on products of p-complete valuation rings with algebraically closed fraction field, using that G_n(−)/p turns p-completed filtered colimits into filtered colimits (Fujiwara–Gabber) and that stalks are absolutely integrally closed valuation rings.
4. Construct α_1 : F_1 → G_1 from Z_p(1) = lim μ_{p^n} and Kummer theory; it is an isomorphism because, arc-locally on V as in the statement, T_p(V^×) → T_p(C^×) is an isomorphism (C^×/V^× is uniquely p-divisible) and T_p(C^×) → H^0(Spec C, Z_p(1)) is an isomorphism (H^1(Spec C, G_m) = 0). By (∗), α_1 induces a multiplicative system of isomorphisms α_n.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/syntomic-complex`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-4-syntomic-complex); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/syntomic-low-weights`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-4-syntomic-low-weights); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/perfectoid-artin-schreier-witt`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-4-perfectoid-artin-schreier-witt); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/etale-comparison`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-4-etale-comparison); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/etale-comparison-without-inverting-d`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-4-etale-comparison-without-inverting-d); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/etale-comparison-coefficients`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-4-etale-comparison-coefficients); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/syntomic-filtered-colimits`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-4-syntomic-filtered-colimits); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/perfect-prisms-perfectoid-rings`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-perfect-prisms-perfectoid-rings); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/q-de-rham-prism`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-q-de-rham-prism); `PerfectoidQuotients:Q0:integral-algebra`; `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2`; `ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1:henselian`.

**Acceptance.** R = O_C: Z_p(n)(O_C) ≃ Z_p(n) in degree 0, a free Z_p-module of rank one, for every n ≥ 0. R perfect of characteristic p and n ≥ 1: Z_p(n)(R) = 0; for n = 0, Z_p(0)(R) = RΓ_ét(Spec R, Z_p) = W(R)^{F=1} derived. R = Z_p^cycl: H^1(Z_p(n)(R)) = H^1(Gal of the completed cyclotomic field, Z_p(n)), non-zero. Finite level: Z/p^k(n)(O_C) = μ_{p^k}^{⊗n}(C), and the maps for k → k − 1 are the reduction maps.

**Sources.** [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Theorem 9.4 and its proof. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 73. statement for n ≥ 1 and n = 0 and the three-step proof, with the comparison map for n = 1 taken from the algebraic description of Z_p(1). [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Remark 9.5. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 75. the source records that with the prismatic logarithm the proof needs no trace-theoretic input.

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-4-syntomic-cohomology-schemes"></a>

### Syntomic cohomology of schemes

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/syntomic-cohomology-schemes` · construction. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.Syntomic` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/Syntomic/Schemes`.

For an animated commutative ring R with p-completion R̂ and an integer n, RΓ_syn(Spec R, Z_p(n)) is the pullback in D̂(Z_p) of RΓ_syn(Spf R̂, Z_p(n)) → RΓ_ét(Spec R̂[1/p], Z_p(n)) ← RΓ_ét(Spec R[1/p], Z_p(n)), the first map being γ{n} of PR.4/syntomic-etale-comparison; the projection to RΓ_ét(Spec R[1/p], Z_p(n)) is again called the étale comparison morphism γ{n}. Properties: (a) if R is p-complete then RΓ_syn(Spec R, Z_p(n)) = RΓ_syn(Spf R, Z_p(n)); (b) if p is invertible in R then γ{n} : RΓ_syn(Spec R, Z_p(n)) ≃ RΓ_ét(Spec R, Z_p(n)); (c) with j : Spec R[1/p] → Spec R there is a fibre sequence RΓ_ét(Spec R, j_!Z_p(n)) → RΓ_syn(Spec R, Z_p(n)) → RΓ_syn(Spf R, Z_p(n)); (d) R ↦ RΓ_syn(Spec R, Z_p(n)) satisfies fpqc descent, hence extends to schemes, formal schemes and algebraic stacks X by RΓ_syn(X, Z_p(n)) = lim over Spec R → X; (e) it is left Kan extended from smooth Z-algebras and commutes with filtered colimits; it does not commute with sifted colimits; (f) RΓ_syn(Spec R, Z_p(0)) ≃ RΓ_ét(Spec R, Z_p) canonically; (g) c_1^syn : RΓ_ét(Spec R, G_m)[−1] → RΓ_syn(Spec R, Z_p(1)) exhibits the target as the p-completion of the source. For a scheme X, Z/p^k(n)_X ∈ D(X_ét, Z/p^k) denotes the restriction of RΓ_syn(−, Z_p(n))/p^k to the small étale site. (h) For every animated Z[ζ_(p^∞)]-algebra R, inverting the compatible-root class ε in ⊕_nRΓ_syn(Spec R,Z_p(n)) and p-completing gives ⊕_nRΓ_ét(Spec R[1/p],Z_p(n)), naturally as graded algebras (BL Theorem 8.5.1).

**Hypotheses and conventions.** R is any animated commutative ring; the étale site and étale cohomology of Spec R[1/p] depend only on π_0(R). The pullback is formed in the p-complete derived ∞-category; all four corners are p-complete. Étale cohomology of Spec R[1/p] with twisted coefficients, j_!, Gabber's affine proper base change and formal glueing for étale cohomology are imported (SF.2 and the arc-descent gap). In the printed proof of Proposition 8.4.10 the last colimit is indexed by ℰ where ℰ' is meant (source issue PrismaticCohomology/E45).

**Construction or proof.**

1. Definition and (a), (b): BL Construction 8.4.1 and Remark 8.4.2; for (a) the right vertical map of the square is an isomorphism, for (b) both lower corners vanish.
2. (c): formal glueing gives a pullback square for RΓ_ét(−, j_!Z_p(n)) along R → R̂ [Bhatt–Mathew, Theorem 6.4], and RΓ_ét(Spec R̂, j_!Z_p(n)) = 0 by Gabber's affine proper base change; so RΓ_ét(Spec R, j_!Z_p(n)) is the fibre of RΓ_ét(Spec R[1/p]) → RΓ_ét(Spec R̂[1/p]) (BL Remark 8.4.4).
3. (d): the first term of (c) satisfies arc-descent [Bhatt–Mathew, Theorem 5.4] and the third p-complete fpqc descent (PR.4/syntomic-cohomology-formal-schemes); (e): the third term commutes with sifted colimits, and F(R) = RΓ_ét(Spec R, j_!Z_p(n)) commutes with filtered colimits and is invariant under henselian surjections (Gabber), which gives left Kan extension from smooth Z-algebras by a cofinality argument (BL Proposition 8.4.10, Corollary 8.4.11, Warning 8.4.12).
4. (f), (g): arithmetic fracture squares for RΓ_ét(−, Z_p) and RΓ_ét(−, G_m)^∧ [Bhatt–Mathew, Theorem 5.13; Česnavičius–Scholze] reduce to the p-complete case (PR.4/syntomic-low-weights) and the case p invertible (BL Propositions 8.4.13, 8.4.14).

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/syntomic-etale-comparison`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-4-syntomic-etale-comparison); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/syntomic-cohomology-formal-schemes`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-4-syntomic-cohomology-formal-schemes); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/syntomic-low-weights`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-4-syntomic-low-weights); `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2`; `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E3`; `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E5:animation/animated-commutative-rings`.

**Consumers.** Bhatt–Lurie Theorem 8.5.1 and Variant 8.5.5: the source of the localisation to the generic fibre: inverting ε gives étale cohomology of Spec R[1/p]. Bhatt–Mathew Notation 1.1, Theorem 1.8: the sheaves Z/p^n(i)_X on the small étale site and their comparison with truncated nearby cycles. PR.4/syntomic-connectivity: the bound Z/p^n(i)_X ∈ D^{[0,i]} is a statement about these sheaves. Bhatt–Lurie Remark 8.4.3 (Selmer K-theory): graded pieces of the motivic filtration; consumed by trace-theoretic roadmaps, not proved here.

**Planning API.**

- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Syntomic.SchemeDatum` (structure): The imported cospan of an animated ring in weight n: RΓ_syn(Spf R̂, Z_p(n)), RΓ_ét(Spec R̂[1/p], Z_p(n)), RΓ_ét(Spec R[1/p], Z_p(n)) with γ{n} and restriction (owners: this stage and SF.2).
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Syntomic.syntomicCohomologyScheme` (constructor): RΓ_syn(Spec R, Z_p(n)), the pullback of the cospan.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Syntomic.etaleComparison` (projection): γ{n} : RΓ_syn(Spec R, Z_p(n)) → RΓ_ét(Spec R[1/p], Z_p(n)).
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Syntomic.toFormal` (projection): The map RΓ_syn(Spec R, Z_p(n)) → RΓ_syn(Spf R̂, Z_p(n)).
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Syntomic.toFormal_isIso_of_complete` (compatibility): If the restriction map of the cospan is an isomorphism (R p-complete), the map to the formal syntomic complex is an isomorphism.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Syntomic.etaleComparison_isIso_of_invertible` (compatibility): If the two p-adic corners vanish (p invertible in R), γ{n} is an isomorphism.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Syntomic.pullback_condition` (relation): The square commutes: γ{n} on Spf R̂ after the map to the formal complex equals restriction after γ{n}.

**Unit tests.**

- `pr4_syntomic_scheme_p_invertible` (degenerate): For a cospan with zero p-adic corners, RΓ_syn(Spec R, Z_p(n)) ≅ RΓ_ét(Spec R[1/p], Z_p(n)).
- `pr4_syntomic_scheme_p_complete` (compatibility): For a cospan whose restriction map is the identity, RΓ_syn(Spec R, Z_p(n)) ≅ RΓ_syn(Spf R, Z_p(n)).
- `pr4_syntomic_scheme_zero` (computation): For the zero cospan (the zero ring) RΓ_syn = 0.
- `pr4_syntomic_scheme_not_product` (non-example): RΓ_syn(Spec R, Z_p(n)) is not the direct sum of the formal and the étale corner: for the cospan with all three objects M ≠ 0 and both maps the identity the pullback is M, not M ⊕ M.

**Acceptance.** RΓ_syn(Spec Q, Z_p(n)) = RΓ_ét(Spec Q, Z_p(n)). RΓ_syn(Spec Z_p, Z_p(1)) = RΓ_syn(Spf Z_p, Z_p(1)) = (Z_p^×)^∧[−1]. RΓ_syn(Spec R, Z_p(n)) = RΓ_ét(Spec R, j_!Z_p(n)) for n < 0. For X proper over a p-henselian ring with bounded p-power torsion, RΓ_syn(X, Z_p(n)) = RΓ_syn of its p-adic completion.

**Sources.** [BL22](https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.06120v1), Construction 8.4.1, Remarks 8.4.2 and 8.4.4, Proposition 8.4.6, Variant 8.4.7. [BL22](https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.06120v1), Proposition 8.4.10, Corollary 8.4.11, Warning 8.4.12, Propositions 8.4.13 and 8.4.14. <a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-4-syntomic-not-generic-fibre-etale"></a>

### Syntomic cohomology is not étale cohomology of the generic fibre in all degrees

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/syntomic-not-generic-fibre-etale` · application. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.Syntomic` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/Syntomic/EtaleComparison`.

The étale comparison morphism γ{n} : RΓ_syn(Spf R, Z_p(n)) → RΓ_ét(Spec R[1/p], Z_p(n)) is not an isomorphism in general, and the φ = 1 statement of PR.4/etale-comparison does not extend to the divided-Frobenius fibres Z_p(n). Instances: (1) R = Z_p, n = 1: H^1 of the source is the p-completion of Z_p^× and H^1 of the target the p-completion of Q_p^×; γ{1} is injective on H^1 with cokernel Z_p, generated by the Kummer class of p. (2) R an F_p-algebra: the target is 0 for every n, while RΓ_syn(Spf R, Z_p) = RΓ_ét(Spec R, Z_p) ≠ 0 for R ≠ 0, and for R = O_C/p the group H^0(Z_p(n)(R)) = A_crys^{φ=p^n} is non-zero for all n ≥ 0. (3) For 𝔛 smooth over Spf O_C the sheaf Z/p^k(n) on 𝔛_ét is the truncation τ^{≤n}Rψ_*Z/p^k(n), so Z/p^k(n) → Rψ_*Z/p^k(n) is an isomorphism if and only if R^jψ_*Z/p^k = 0 for all j > n. (4) For a p-torsion-free F-smooth scheme X (for example regular and flat over Z) with j : X[1/p] → X, Bhatt–Mathew prove that Z/p^k(n)_X → τ^{≤n}Rj_*μ_{p^k}^{⊗n} is an isomorphism on cohomology sheaves in degrees < n and injective in degree n with image generated by symbols from O_X^×; instance (1) is the case X = Spec Z_p, n = 1. For a p-complete Z[ζ_{p^∞}]-algebra R with its specified compatible roots of unity, there is an isomorphism after inverting the resulting class ε and p-completing (PR.4/syntomic-etale-comparison (4)) and, for the fixed points of φ itself, PR.4/etale-comparison.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** The warning concerns the syntomic complexes Z_p(n), built from the Nygaard filtration and the divided Frobenius; it does not concern the φ = 1 statement of Theorem 9.1, which holds for every p-adic formal scheme over a perfectoid ring. (4) is quoted from Bhatt–Mathew Theorem 1.8 as the general shape of the discrepancy; its proof (F-smoothness, Bloch–Kato) is outside this stage and is not a prerequisite of any node. In (1) p is odd for the explicit description 1 + pZ_p of the completed units; the statement about the cokernel holds for all p.

**Construction or proof.**

1. (1): by PR.4/syntomic-low-weights (3), RΓ_syn(Spf Z_p, Z_p(1)) = RΓ_ét(Spec Z_p, G_m)^∧[−1] = (Z_p^×)^∧[−1], and RΓ_ét(Spec Q_p, Z_p(1)) has H^1 = lim Q_p^×/(Q_p^×)^{p^k} by Kummer theory; γ{1} is induced by Z_p^× ⊂ Q_p^× by the characterisation of PR.4/syntomic-etale-comparison, and Q_p^×/Z_p^× = Z.
2. (2): R[1/p] = 0; PR.4/syntomic-low-weights (2) and PR.4/syntomic-complex-char-p give the non-vanishing; t = log[ε] ∈ A_crys(O_C/p) satisfies φ(t) = pt.
3. (3) is a reformulation of PR.4/nearby-cycles-comparison. (4) is the statement of Bhatt–Mathew Theorem 1.8.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/syntomic-etale-comparison`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-4-syntomic-etale-comparison); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/syntomic-low-weights`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-4-syntomic-low-weights); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/syntomic-complex-char-p`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-4-syntomic-complex-char-p); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/nearby-cycles-comparison`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-4-nearby-cycles-comparison); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/etale-comparison`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-4-etale-comparison); `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2`.

**Acceptance.** The cokernel of γ{1} on H^1 for R = Z_p is Z_p, not 0. For R = F_p: RΓ_syn(Spf F_p, Z_p) has H^0 = H^1 = Z_p while Spec F_p[1/p] is empty. For R = O_C: γ{n} is an isomorphism for every n ≥ 0, so the discrepancy is invisible on the basis of the arc_p-topology. A statement 'Z_p(n)(R) ≃ RΓ_ét(Spec R[1/p], Z_p(n)) for every quasisyntomic R' is false by (1).

**Sources.** [BM23](https://arxiv.org/abs/2202.04818v2), Theorem 1.8 and the paragraph after it. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 3. the precise relation between Z/p^n(i)_X and truncated nearby cycles for F-smooth schemes, quoted as the shape of the discrepancy. [BL22](https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.06120v1), Section 8, introduction.  étale cohomology of the generic fibre and syntomic cohomology of the formal completion are different invariants, amalgamated in Construction 8.4.1. [BMS2](https://arxiv.org/abs/1802.03261v2), Theorem 10.1. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 75. only the truncation τ^{≤i} of the nearby cycles is syntomic cohomology.

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-4-picard-perfectoid-uniquely-divisible"></a>

### Picard groups of perfectoid rings are uniquely p-divisible

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/picard-perfectoid-uniquely-divisible` · application. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.Syntomic` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/Syntomic/Perfectoid`.

For a perfectoid ring R the groups Pic(R) and Pic(R[1/p]) are uniquely p-divisible. Moreover the canonical map Pic(R)^∧[−2] → Pic(R[1/p])^∧[−2] of p-completed Picard groupoids is an isomorphism, compatible with Pic(R)^∧[−2] ≃ Z_p(1)(R) (PR.4/syntomic-low-weights), Z_p(1)(R) ≃ RΓ_ét(Spec R[1/p], Z_p(1)) (PR.4/tate-twist-perfectoid) and the Kummer map Pic(R[1/p])^∧[−2] → RΓ_ét(Spec R[1/p], Z_p(1)).

**Hypotheses and conventions.** R is any perfectoid ring. Pic(R) = (τ^{≤1}RΓ(Spec R, G_m))[1] denotes the Picard groupoid as an object of D(Z); Pic(R) with roman type is its H^0, the Picard group. Cohomology of G_m is computed in the flat topology (equivalently étale).

**Construction or proof.**

1. Pic(R) ≅ Pic(A_inf(R)) ≅ Pic(R^♭) by deformation theory along the (p, d)-adically complete ring A_inf(R), and the Picard group of a perfect ring is uniquely p-divisible (Frobenius is an automorphism inducing multiplication by p).
2. In the square with a : Pic(R)^∧[−2] ≃ Z_p(1)(R) (valid for perfectoid R: Z_p(1)(R) = RΓ(Spec R, G_m)^∧[−1] is concentrated in degrees 0 and 1, so (τ^{≥2}RΓ(Spec R, G_m))^∧ = 0), c : Z_p(1)(R) ≃ RΓ(Spec R[1/p], Z_p(1)), b the canonical map and d the Kummer map, commutativity is checked by p-complete arc-descent on R = O_C; d[1] is the p-completion of τ^{≤1}RΓ(Spec R[1/p], G_m) → RΓ(Spec R[1/p], G_m), hence injective on cohomology, so b and d are isomorphisms.
3. Reduce b modulo p: H^0 gives Pic(R[1/p])/p ≅ Pic(R)/p = 0, and H^{−1} with the Bockstein sequences gives a surjection Pic(R)[p] → Pic(R[1/p])[p], whose source is 0.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/syntomic-low-weights`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-4-syntomic-low-weights); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/tate-twist-perfectoid`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-4-tate-twist-perfectoid); `PerfectoidQuotients:Q0:integral-algebra`; `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2`; [`mathlib:CommRing.Pic`](#mathlib-commring-pic).

**Acceptance.** R = O_C: Pic(O_C) = 0 and Pic(C) = 0. R perfect of characteristic p: R[1/p] = 0 and Pic(R) is uniquely p-divisible because Frobenius acts as an automorphism and as multiplication by p. Consequence used in Theorem 14.1: H^1(Z_p(1)(R)) is H^0 of the derived p-completion of R^×.

**Sources.** [BS22-v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.08229v4), Corollary 9.7 and its proof. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 76. statement and proof; the two inputs are Theorem 9.4 and Lemma 9.6.

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-4-syntomic-connectivity"></a>

### Connectivity, rigidity and left Kan extension of syntomic complexes

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/syntomic-connectivity` · theorem. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.Syntomic` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/Syntomic/Connectivity`.

Let i ≥ 0. (1) The functor R ↦ RΓ_syn(Spf R, Z_p(i)) on animated rings commutes with sifted colimits and is left Kan extended from finitely generated polynomial Z-algebras; on quasisyntomic rings Z_p(i) is left Kan extended from finitely generated p-complete polynomial Z_p-algebras. (2) For every quasisyntomic ring R, Z_p(i)(R) ∈ D^{≤ i+1}(Z_p). (3) (Rigidity) For a henselian pair (R, I) with R and R/I p-complete, fib(Z_p(i)(R) → Z_p(i)(R/I)) ∈ D^{≤ i}(Z_p). (4) For a p-complete ring R, H^{i+1}(F_p(i)(R)) ≅ coker(1 − C^{−1} : Ω^i_{R/p} → Ω^i_{R/p}/dΩ^{i−1}_{R/p}); it vanishes when R is w-strictly local, in particular strictly henselian local. (5) Consequently, for every scheme X the étale sheaf of complexes Z/p^n(i)_X obtained by restricting syntomic cohomology (PR.4/syntomic-cohomology-schemes) to the small étale site lies in D^{[0, i]}(X_ét, Z/p^n), and Z/p^n(i)(R) ∈ D^{≤ i} for R strictly henselian local.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** Statements (2)–(4) are Theorems 5.1, 5.2 and Corollary 5.43 of Antieau–Mathew–Morrow–Nikolaus, as used by Bhatt–Mathew (routed item PAPER-BHATT-MATHEW-23/009). In (3) both R and R/I are p-complete and (R, I) is henselian. The printed proofs of (2)–(4) describe Nygaard graded pieces as gr^n THH and use THH of graded rings; no trace-theoretic object may enter PR.4, so the plan replaces each such description by its prismatic counterpart and records the remaining step as a gap. ### Acceptance examples: O_C, the formal torus, finite levels and the maps n → n − 1

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/tate-twists-acceptance-examples` · application. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.Syntomic` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/Syntomic/Examples`.

Let C be a complete algebraically closed extension of Q_p, A_inf = A_inf(O_C), q = [ε^{1/p}] with ε a compatible system of primitive p-power roots of unity, d = [p]_q a generator of ker(A_inf → O_C) and μ = q − 1, so φ(μ) = dμ. (1) For every n ≥ 0, Z_p(n)(O_C) is concentrated in degree 0 and equals Z_p · μ^n ⊂ φ^{−1}(d)^n A_inf, the kernel of φ/d^n − 1; it is identified with H^0(Spec C, Z_p(n)) = T_p(C^×)^{⊗n}. (2) At finite level Z/p^k(n)(O_C) = Z/p^k · μ^n = μ_{p^k}(C)^{⊗n}, and the maps induced by k → k − 1 are the reduction maps, compatible with those of étale cohomology; likewise in PR.4/etale-comparison the isomorphisms Z/p^k ≃ (A_inf[1/d]/p^k)^{φ=1} = W_k(C^♭)^{F=1} commute with reduction. (3) For the formal torus 𝔛 = Spf O_C⟨T^{±1}⟩ with S = O_C⟨T^{±1}⟩: RΓ_ét(Spec S[1/p], Z/p^k) ≃ (Δ_{S/A_inf}[1/d]/p^k)^{φ=1}, and on 𝔛_ét, Z/p^k(0) = Z/p^k and Z/p^k(1) ≃ τ^{≤1}Rψ_*μ_{p^k}, whose H^1 contains the Kummer class of T, a non-zero section of R^1ψ_*μ_{p^k}. (4) For C spherically complete, ⊕_n RΓ_syn(Spf O_C, Z_p(n)) = Z_p[log_Δ(ε)].

**Hypotheses and conventions.** C is complete and algebraically closed; in (4) also spherically complete. The normalisation q = [ε^{1/p}] makes [p]_q a generator of the kernel of θ, as in the proof of Bhatt–Scholze Theorem 9.4. These are instances of earlier nodes, collected as the acceptance tests the stage names; nothing new is proved.

**Construction or proof.**

1. (1): Z_p(n)(O_C) = fib(φ/d^n − 1 : φ^{−1}(d)^n A_inf → A_inf) (PR.4/syntomic-complex); μ^n lies in the kernel because φ(μ^n) = d^nμ^n; by PR.4/tate-twist-perfectoid the complex is RΓ(Spec C, Z_p(n)), free of rank one in degree 0, and multiplication by μ^{−n} is the comparison used in that proof.
2. (2): reduce (1) modulo p^k; compatibility in k is PR.4/etale-comparison-coefficients and the compatibility in n of PR.4/nearby-cycles-comparison.
3. (3): PR.4/etale-comparison for S and PR.4/nearby-cycles-comparison for 𝔛; at the generic point of the special-fibre torus, reduction places T in a separable closure of the characteristic-p function field. T has no p-th root in that separable closure. A hypothetical p-th root after inverting p on an étale neighbourhood is integral over its normal ring and hence lies in it; reduction would give the impossible root. This proves that the Kummer class is a nonzero section. Normality alone would not exclude a root in an arbitrary extension ring.
4. (4): PR.4/syntomic-etale-comparison (3).

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/syntomic-complex`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-4-syntomic-complex); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/tate-twist-perfectoid`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-4-tate-twist-perfectoid); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/etale-comparison`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-4-etale-comparison); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/etale-comparison-coefficients`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-4-etale-comparison-coefficients); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/nearby-cycles-comparison`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-4-nearby-cycles-comparison); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/syntomic-etale-comparison`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-4-syntomic-etale-comparison); `PerfectoidQuotients:Q0:integral-algebra`.

**Acceptance.** φ(μ) = dμ, hence φ(μ^n)/d^n = μ^n. Z/p^k(n)(O_C) → Z/p^{k−1}(n)(O_C) is surjective with kernel p^{k−1}Z/p^k · μ^n. The Kummer class of T in H^1_ét(Spec C⟨T^{±1}⟩, μ_{p^k}) has order p^k. Z_p(n)(O_C) ≠ 0 for every n ≥ 0, whereas Z_p(n)(O_C/p) = A_crys^{φ=p^n} is much larger: reduction modulo p changes syntomic cohomology.

### Z_p(n) is discrete and p-torsion-free

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/tate-twist-discreteness` · theorem. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.Syntomic` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/Syntomic/Discreteness`.

For each n ≥ 0 the sheaf of complexes Z_p(n) on the quasisyntomic site is discrete and p-torsion-free: for every quasisyntomic ring S, H^0(Z_p(n)(−)) is a sheaf of p-torsion-free abelian groups, and every class in H^1(Z_p(n)(S)) vanishes on some quasisyntomic cover S → S' (so the quasisyntomic sheafification of H^1(Z_p(n)(−)) is 0, and H^i(Z_p(n)(−)) = 0 locally for i ≠ 0). Hence Z_p(n)(S) = RΓ(S_qsyn, H^0(Z_p(n))) is the cohomology of a sheaf of p-torsion-free groups. Two lemmas of the proof: (Lemma 14.4) for a perfectoid Z_p[ζ_{p^∞}]^∧-algebra R, R' = R⟨X_1^{1/p^∞}, …, X_r^{1/p^∞}⟩ and S = R'/(X_1, …, X_r), the map Z_p(n)(R') → Z_p(n)(S) is surjective on H^1; (Lemma 14.5) for a perfectoid ring R and a surjection S' → S of quasiregular semiperfectoid R-algebras such that the p-completion of L_{S'/R} → L_{S/R} is surjective on H^{−1}, the map Δ_{S'} → Δ_S is surjective.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** The statement is local: discreteness means vanishing of H^1 after quasisyntomic sheafification; Z_p(n)(S) itself can have H^1 ≠ 0 (already Z_p(0)(F_p)). n ≥ 0; for n < 0 the sheaf is 0. This is Conjecture 7.18 of BMS2. Its K-theoretic consequences, Corollaries 14.2 and 14.3 of Bhatt–Scholze (evenness of K(−; Z_p) locally and for regular quotients), need K(−; Z_p) ≃ τ_{≥0}TC(−; Z_p) on henselian pairs and belong to the proposed roadmap RefinedTraceMethodsPartIIHenselianPairs; they are not planned here. In the printed proof 'C/Q' reads 'C/Q_p complete and algebraically closed' (register PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22/E30).

**Construction or proof.**

1. p-torsion-freeness of H^0: for S quasiregular semiperfectoid, Δ_S is a d-torsion-free δ-ring; if x ∈ H^0 has px = 0 then φ(x) = 0, so d^n x = d^n φ_n(x) = φ(x) = 0 and x = 0 (BMS2 Remark 7.20; by PR.3/nygaard-completion (b) a class of H^0 is the image of an element of Fil^n_N Δ_S, so the argument takes place in the δ-ring Δ_S). It remains to prove (∗)_S: every α ∈ H^1(Z_p(n)(S)) dies on a quasisyntomic cover, for S quasiregular semiperfectoid over O_C, where Z_p(n)(S) = fib(1 − φ_n : Fil^n_N Δ_S → Δ_S) (PR.4/divided-frobenius-contraction).
2. Perfectoid S = R: for n = 0 use PR.4/tate-twist-perfectoid and Artin–Schreier covers; for n > 0 reduce to n = 1 by PR.4/tate-twist-perfectoid, where H^1(Z_p(1)(R)) is H^0 of the derived p-completion of R^× (PR.4/picard-perfectoid-uniquely-divisible), and André's lemma (PerfectoidQuotients:Q3) gives a cover R → R' with (R')^× p-divisible.
3. S_0 = R⟨x_i^{1/p^∞}⟩/(x_i): Lemma 14.4 reduces (∗)_{S_0} to the perfectoid ring R⟨x_i^{1/p^∞}⟩. Proof of 14.4: with A = A_inf(R), D = Δ_{S/A} = A_inf(R'){X_i^p/[p]_q}^∧ has a completed N[1/p]^r-grading with basis X^i/[⌊i⌋]_q!, Fil^n_N D is described termwise by powers of [p]_{q^{1/p}}, φ_n − 1 is surjective on the part of total integral degree ≥ n + 1 (φ_n is contracting there), on the remaining degrees φ_n maps the degree i/p part isomorphically onto the degree i part, so a cokernel class of degree i can be represented in degree i/p; iterate this reduction, and in degrees with all i_j < 1 the map A_inf(R') → D is bijective.
4. General S = R'/I: by André's lemma assume generators x_t of I have compatible p-power roots, map S' = (R'[x_t^{1/p^∞}]/(x_t))^∧ onto S; the map on p-completed cotangent complexes is surjective on H^{−1}, so Δ_{S'} → Δ_S and then H^1(Z_p(n)(S')) → H^1(Z_p(n)(S)) are surjective (Lemma 14.5, from the Hodge–Tate comparison PR.2/derived-hodge-tate-comparison); filter the index set by finite subsets to reduce to S_0.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/syntomic-complex`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-4-syntomic-complex); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/divided-frobenius-contraction`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-4-divided-frobenius-contraction); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/tate-twist-perfectoid`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-4-tate-twist-perfectoid); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/picard-perfectoid-uniquely-divisible`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-4-picard-perfectoid-uniquely-divisible); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/syntomic-low-weights`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-4-syntomic-low-weights); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/nygaard-filtration-qrsp`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-3-nygaard-filtration-qrsp); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/nygaard-completion`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-3-nygaard-completion); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/qrsp-prism`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-qrsp-prism); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/derived-hodge-tate-comparison`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-derived-hodge-tate-comparison); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/quasisyntomic-descent`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-quasisyntomic-descent); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/q-de-rham-prism`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-q-de-rham-prism); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/regular-prismatic-envelopes`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-regular-prismatic-envelopes); `PerfectoidQuotients:Q3`; `PerfectoidQuotients:Q0:integral-algebra`; `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.0`; `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.5`; [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/nygaard-key-case`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-3-nygaard-key-case); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/nygaard-regular-semiperfectoid`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-3-nygaard-regular-semiperfectoid); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/delta-nygaard-continuity`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-3-delta-nygaard-continuity).

**Acceptance.** n = 0: Z_p(0) is the constant sheaf lim Z/p^r, and H^1(Z_p(0)(F_p)) = Z_p dies on the cover F_p → algebraic closure. n = 1: Z_p(1) = T_p G_m, and a class in H^1(Z_p(1)(R)) = (R^×)^∧ dies after adjoining p-power roots of units. S = O_C⟨X^{1/p^∞}⟩/(X): H^1(Z_p(n)(S)) is a quotient of H^1(Z_p(n)(O_C⟨X^{1/p^∞}⟩)) by Lemma 14.4. In characteristic p the statement is PR.4/syntomic-complex-char-p.

## PR.7. Prismatic F-crystals and crystalline lattices

Crystals are finite projective module families with effective base-change maps; F-crystals add Frobenius after inverting the Cartier ideal. Laurent crystals give étale realizations by Artin–Schreier descent and v-descent, with arbitrary-localization and affinoid comparison gaps retained. Fix a complete mixed-characteristic DVR O_K, a perfect residue field and a uniformizer before constructing the geometric realization data. The modification M(D) is defined on all filtered φ-modules. Weak admissibility provides existence of the integral extension, and does not claim uniqueness there. The rank-one twist uses the filtration jump −1. The crystalline-lattice equivalence yields the Breuil–Kisin evaluation theorem; its comparison with Kisin's construction uses the Frobenius-twisted embedding. Full-faithfulness ownership with R07.4 is a recorded reconciliation proposal.

### Prismatic crystals in vector bundles and in perfect complexes

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.7/prismatic-crystal` · definition. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.FCrystal` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/FCrystal/Crystal`.

Let X be a p-adic formal scheme. A prismatic crystal in vector bundles on X is an object of Vect(X_Δ, O_Δ) := lim_{(A,I) ∈ X_Δ} Vect(A): a rule E giving a finite projective A-module E(A) for every bounded prism (A, I) with a map Spf(A/I) → X, and for every map of prisms f: (A, I) → (B, J) over X an isomorphism of B-modules c_f: E(A) ⊗_A B ≅ E(B), with c_id = id and c_{g∘f} = c_g ∘ (c_f ⊗_B C) for (A,I) → (B,J) → (C,K). Equivalently the c_f are given by f-semilinear maps E(A) → E(B), functorial in f, each exhibiting E(B) as the base change of E(A). A morphism E → E′ is a family of A-linear maps E(A) → E′(A) commuting with the transition maps. In the same way D_perf(X_Δ, O_Δ) := lim D_perf(A) (a limit of ∞-categories, transition functors B ⊗^L_A −), and for the two sheaves of O_Δ-algebras O′ = O_Δ[1/p]^∧_{I_Δ} (value A[1/p]^∧_I, the I-adic completion of A[1/p]) and O′ = O_Δ[1/I_Δ]^∧_p (value A[1/I]^∧_p, the p-adic completion of the ring A[1/I] of functions on Spec A ∖ V(I)) one puts Vect(X_Δ, O′) := lim Vect(O′(A)) and D_perf(X_Δ, O′) := lim D_perf(O′(A)). Structure: the unit O_Δ (A ↦ A); tensor product (E ⊗ E′)(A) = E(A) ⊗_A E′(A) and duals E^∨(A) = Hom_A(E(A), A), making Vect(X_Δ, O_Δ) rigid symmetric monoidal; the evaluation functors ev_{(A,I)}: Vect(X_Δ, O_Δ) → Vect(A); the pullback g^*: Vect(X_Δ, O_Δ) → Vect(Y_Δ, O_Δ) along g: Y → X, (g^*E)(A, I, Spf(A/I) → Y) = E(A, I, Spf(A/I) → Y → X); and base change Vect(X_Δ, O_Δ) → Vect(X_Δ, O′), E ↦ (A ↦ E(A) ⊗_A O′(A)).

**Hypotheses and conventions.** p is a fixed prime; a prism is a bounded prism (A, I) in the sense of PR.0, and X_Δ is the absolute prismatic site of PR.5: the opposite of the category of bounded prisms (A, I) with a map Spf(A/I) → X, with the flat topology. A "map of prisms over X" (A, I) → (B, J) is an arrow of the category of prisms, that is an arrow (B, J) → (A, I) of X_Δ. X is an arbitrary p-adic formal scheme; no boundedness or quasi-syntomicity is needed for the definition. In the version read (arXiv v2) the definition is the displayed formula opening §4, the sheaf-theoretic notions are Notation 2.1, and their agreement is Proposition 2.7 (node crystal-descent). Completions: A[1/p]^∧_I is the classical I-adic completion; it agrees with the derived one because I is locally generated by a nonzerodivisor of A[1/p]. A[1/I]^∧_p is the derived p-completion; it is the classical completion whenever A[1/I] has bounded p^∞-torsion (for instance A p-torsion-free: transversal, perfect and Breuil–Kisin prisms), but not for every bounded prism. For Vect the two give the same category lim_n Vect(A[1/I]/p^n); for D_perf the derived completion is meant.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Define the category of compatible families directly, with transition data given as semilinear maps that are base changes; functoriality of the semilinear maps is the cocycle condition (BS23-FCRYS §4, first display).
2. Base change of finite projective modules along A → B is finite projective and commutes with ⊗ and duals (Mathlib TensorProduct, Module.Finite, Module.Projective); this gives the unit, tensor product, duals and their compatibility with the transition maps.
3. Pullback along g: Y → X is restriction of the family along the functor Y_Δ → X_Δ that composes the structure map with g; evaluation is the projection of the limit.
4. For O′ use that a map of prisms (A,I) → (B,J) has IB = J (PR.0/rigidity-prism-ideal), so it induces A[1/I]^∧_p → B[1/J]^∧_p and A[1/p]^∧_I → B[1/p]^∧_J.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.5/absolute-prismatic-site`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-5-absolute-prismatic-site); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/prism`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-prism); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/prism-category`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-prism-category); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/rigidity-prism-ideal`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-rigidity-prism-ideal); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/bounded-prism-complete-flatness`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-bounded-prism-complete-flatness); [`mathlib:Module.Finite`](#mathlib-module-finite); [`mathlib:Module.Projective`](#mathlib-module-projective); [`mathlib:TensorProduct`](#mathlib-tensorproduct); [`mathlib:AdicCompletion`](#mathlib-adiccompletion).

**Consumers.** BS23-FCRYS Definition 4.1 and Definition 3.2: F-crystals and Laurent F-crystals are crystals with a Frobenius structure. BS23-FCRYS Example 2.8, Remark 5.7, §6: a crystal on Spf(O_K) is a module over a covering prism with a descent datum over the self-coproduct. BS23-FCRYS Corollary 7.17: a crystal over O_Δ⟨I_Δ/p⟩[1/p], with no Frobenius, gives a logarithmic connection at the Breuil–Kisin prism. PrismaticCohomology:PR.5/prismatic-crystals-on-wcart: the same limit description, for complete complexes, is the category of quasi-coherent complexes on the Cartier–Witt stack.

**Planning API.**

- `TauCeti.Prismatic.FCrystal.IsBaseChangeAlong` (characterisation): An additive map t: M → N that is semilinear over a ring map g: R → S exhibits N as S ⊗_R M: every g-semilinear map from M to an S-module factors uniquely through t by an S-linear map.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.FCrystal.Crystal` (structure): A crystal in vector bundles over a diagram of rings O: C → CommRing: finite projective O(c)-modules M(c) with functorial semilinear transition maps that are base changes.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.FCrystal.Crystal.Hom` (structure): A morphism of crystals: O(c)-linear maps M(c) → M′(c) commuting with the transition maps.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.FCrystal.Crystal.unit` (constructor): The unit crystal c ↦ O(c), with transition maps the ring maps.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.FCrystal.Crystal.tensor` (functoriality): The tensor product of two crystals, with (E ⊗ E′)(c) ≅ E(c) ⊗_{O(c)} E′(c).
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.FCrystal.Crystal.pullback` (functoriality): Restriction of a crystal along a functor D → C; for D = Y_Δ → C = X_Δ this is g^*.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.FCrystal.Crystal.baseChange` (functoriality): Base change of a crystal along a map of diagrams of rings O → O′, with values O′(c) ⊗_{O(c)} E(c).
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.FCrystal.Crystal.Iso` (structure): An isomorphism of crystals: a pair of mutually inverse morphisms.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.FCrystal.Crystal.dual` (structure): The dual crystal has E^∨(A)=Hom_A(E(A),A); base-change compatibility follows from finite projectivity. Evaluation and coevaluation satisfy the triangle identities, making crystals rigid symmetric monoidal.

**Unit tests.**

- `pr7_crystal_unit_eval` (computation): The unit crystal has value O(c) at every object c.
- `pr7_crystal_base_change_id` (degenerate): The identity of a module exhibits it as its own base change along the identity ring map.
- `pr7_crystal_initial_object_eval` (characterisation): If the diagram C has an initial object c₀ (as the category of prisms over Spf(R) does for R quasiregular semiperfectoid, with c₀ = Δ_R), every O(c₀)-linear map E(c₀) → E′(c₀) extends uniquely to a morphism of crystals.
- `pr7_crystal_hodge_tate_quotient_not_projective` (non-example): For a prism (A, I) with I ≠ A the A-module A/I is not projective, so A ↦ A/I, although compatible with base change, is not a crystal in vector bundles.

**Acceptance.** The unit crystal evaluates to A on every prism. For X = Spf(R) with R quasiregular semiperfectoid, evaluation at Δ_R is an equivalence Vect(X_Δ, O_Δ) ≃ Vect(Δ_R) (node f-crystals-over-qrsp). The rule A ↦ A/I is compatible with base change but is not a crystal in vector bundles.

**Sources.** [BS23-FCRYS](https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.14735v2), Section 4, opening display.  the definition of Vect(X_Δ, O_Δ) as the limit of Vect(A) over the site. <a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-7-f-crystal-over-prism"></a>

### F-crystals over a single prism

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.7/f-crystal-over-prism` · definition. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.FCrystal` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/FCrystal/OverPrism`.

Let (A, I) be a prism with Frobenius φ, and let A[1/I] be the ring of functions on Spec A ∖ V(I): the initial A-algebra L with IL = L (it is A[1/d] when I = (d)). The category Vect^φ(A) of F-crystals over (A, I) has objects the pairs (M, φ_M) with M a finite projective A-module and φ_M: (φ^*M)[1/I] ≅ M[1/I] an isomorphism of A[1/I]-modules, where φ^*M = A ⊗_{φ,A} M and N[1/I] = A[1/I] ⊗_A N; equivalently φ_M is a φ-semilinear map M → M[1/I] whose A[1/I]-linearisation is bijective. Morphisms are A-linear maps f: M → M′ with φ_{M′} ∘ φ^*f = f ∘ φ_M after inverting I. (M, φ_M) is effective when φ_M carries φ^*M into M. Tensor product and duals are those of the underlying modules with φ_M ⊗ φ_{M′} and (φ_M^∨)^{-1}; the unit is (A, φ). A map of prisms (A, I) → (B, J) induces the base change Vect^φ(A) → Vect^φ(B), M ↦ M ⊗_A B. For an A-algebra A′ with a compatible Frobenius (such as A[1/I]^∧_p, A[1/p], A⟨I/p⟩[1/p]) the category Vect^φ(A′) is defined in the same way.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** (A, I) is a prism (PR.0/prism); boundedness is not needed for the definition. Objects of Vect^φ(𝔖) for the Breuil–Kisin prism (𝔖, (E(u))) are Breuil–Kisin modules; the effective ones with finite free M are the modules of finite E-height Mod^φ_{/𝔖} of FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory:R07.4/kisin-modules. Objects of Vect^φ(A_inf) are the finite free Breuil–Kisin–Fargues modules of AInfCohomology:AI.2 (node bkf-modules-comparison). No bound on the poles or zeros of φ_M along I is part of the data; this is why the notion is adequate only for finite locally free coefficients (node mod-p-full-faithfulness-fails).

**Construction or proof.**

1. Define A[1/I] by its universal property and show it is A[1/d] for an orientation d (Mathlib Localization.Away); in general it is the filtered colimit of the invertible modules I^{-n}.
2. Record φ_M as a semilinear map M → A[1/I] ⊗_A M that is a base change along A → A → A[1/I] (first map φ); this is equivalent to the isomorphism (φ^*M)[1/I] ≅ M[1/I].
3. Base change along a map of prisms uses φ_B ∘ f = f ∘ φ_A and IB = J (PR.0/rigidity-prism-ideal), which give φ_B^*(M ⊗_A B) = (φ_A^*M) ⊗_A B and B[1/J] = A[1/I] ⊗_A B.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/prism`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-prism); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/prism-category`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-prism-category); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/rigidity-prism-ideal`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-rigidity-prism-ideal); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/breuil-kisin-prism`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-breuil-kisin-prism); [`mathlib:Module.Finite`](#mathlib-module-finite); [`mathlib:Module.Projective`](#mathlib-module-projective); [`mathlib:TensorProduct`](#mathlib-tensorproduct); [`mathlib:Localization.Away`](#mathlib-localization-away); [`mathlib:LinearMap.lTensor`](#mathlib-linearmap-ltensor).

**Consumers.** BS23-FCRYS Example 4.10, Theorem 5.2: over a quasiregular semiperfectoid ring R the F-crystals on Spf(R) are Vect^φ(Δ_R); for R = O_C these are Breuil–Kisin–Fargues modules. BS23-FCRYS Theorems 7.2 and 7.9: Vect^φ(𝔖) is the target of evaluation at the Breuil–Kisin prism. BS23-FCRYS Construction 6.2 and §6.2: the same definition over the period sheaves Δ_•{I/p}, Δ_•⟨I/p⟩[1/p], Δ_•[1/p]. FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory:R07.4/kisin-modules: the comparison node kisin-functor-comparison identifies effective objects over 𝔖 with modules of finite E-height.

**Planning API.**

- `TauCeti.Prismatic.FCrystal.IsAwayIdeal` (characterisation): An A-algebra L is A[1/I]: IL = L and L is initial among A-algebras with this property.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.FCrystal.OverPrism` (structure): An F-crystal over a prism: a finite projective module M with a φ-semilinear map M → L ⊗_A M that is a base change along A → A → L.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.FCrystal.OverPrism.Hom` (structure): A morphism of F-crystals over a prism: an A-linear map commuting with the Frobenius structures.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.FCrystal.OverPrism.IsEffective` (characterisation): The Frobenius carries M into the image of M in L ⊗_A M.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.FCrystal.OverPrism.unit` (constructor): The unit F-crystal (A, φ).
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.FCrystal.OverPrism.baseChange` (functoriality): Base change of an F-crystal along a map of prisms, with underlying module B ⊗_A M. The source and target coefficient algebras are required to satisfy IsAwayIdeal for I and J; their universal properties give the coefficient map.

**Unit tests.**

- `pr7_over_prism_away_principal` (compatibility): If I = (d) then Mathlib's Localization.Away d is A[1/I].
- `pr7_over_prism_unit_effective` (computation): The unit F-crystal is effective.
- `pr7_over_prism_rank_one_scaling` (computation): On the free module of rank one, x ↦ u ⊗ φ(x) is a Frobenius structure for every unit u of A[1/I] (over the Breuil–Kisin prism, u = c·E(u)^n); it is effective when u is the image of an element of A.
- `pr7_over_prism_frob_ne_zero` (non-example): If A[1/I] ⊗_A M is nonzero, the Frobenius of an F-crystal is not the zero map.

**Acceptance.** Over the Breuil–Kisin prism the rank one objects (𝔖, c·E(u)^n·φ), c ∈ W(k)^×, n ∈ Z, are F-crystals, effective exactly for n ≥ 0. Over a crystalline prism (A, (p)) an F-crystal is a finite projective A-module with an isomorphism φ^*M[1/p] ≅ M[1/p]. The zero map is not a Frobenius structure on a module with M[1/I] ≠ 0.

**Sources.** [BS23-FCRYS](https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.14735v2), Definition 4.1. <a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-7-artin-schreier-riemann-hilbert"></a>

### Riemann–Hilbert for F_p-local systems and invariance under completed perfection

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.7/artin-schreier-riemann-hilbert` · theorem. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.FCrystal` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/FCrystal/Laurent`.

(1) Let S be a commutative F_p-algebra. Extension of scalars along F_p → O_{Spec(S),ét} and Frobenius fixed points are mutually inverse equivalences D^b_lisse(Spec(S), F_p) ≃ D_perf(S)^{φ=1}, where D_perf(S)^{φ=1} is the ∞-category of pairs (E, α) with E a perfect complex of S-modules and α: φ^*E ≃ E, and D^b_lisse is the bounded derived category of étale F_p-sheaves with locally constant cohomology sheaves of finite rank; on hearts of vector bundles it is Katz's equivalence between F_p-local systems on Spec(S) and finite projective S-modules M with φ^*M ≅ M. Each cohomology module of such an (E, α) is finite projective. (2) Let R be an F_p-algebra with an element t such that R is derived t-complete, and S = (R_perf)^∧_t the t-completed perfection. Then the base change functors D_perf(R[1/t])^{φ=1} → D_perf(R_perf[1/t])^{φ=1} → D_perf(S[1/t])^{φ=1} are equivalences.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** In (1) S is an arbitrary commutative F_p-algebra (no noetherian, normality or reducedness hypothesis). In (2) R is derived t-complete, hence henselian along t; R_perf = colim_φ R. Étale sheaves, lisse complexes, the Artin–Schreier sequence and topological invariance of the étale site are requested from SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Full faithfulness in (1): by finite étale descent on both sides reduce to endomorphisms of the constant sheaf, i.e. to RΓ(Spec(S)_ét, F_p) ≃ fib(φ − 1: S → S), the Artin–Schreier sequence.
2. Each H^i(E) is a vector bundle: by descending induction treat the top cohomology H^n(E), which is finitely presented with φ^*H^n ≅ H^n; by noetherian approximation and localisation S is noetherian local, any Fitting ideal J satisfies J = φ(J)S, so J ∈ {0, S} by Krull's intersection theorem.
3. Essential surjectivity in (1): by the previous step and full faithfulness reduce to a vector bundle (M, α); the functor of α-fixed bases is a finite étale GL_n(F_p)-torsor over Spec(S) (Katz, p-adic properties of modular schemes and modular forms, Proposition 4.1.1; Kedlaya–Liu, Relative p-adic Hodge theory: foundations, Proposition 3.2.7), which gives the local system.
4. (2): the first functor is an equivalence by (1) and topological invariance of the étale site (R[1/t] → R_perf[1/t] is a universal homeomorphism). Full faithfulness of the composite is BS22 Lemma 9.2 (φ-fixed points commute with t-completed filtered colimits; PR.4), perfect complexes over R being derived t-complete. Essential surjectivity: by (1) for S[1/t] it suffices that every lisse F_p-sheaf on Spec(S[1/t]) comes from Spec(R[1/t]), which holds because finite étale algebras over R_perf[1/t] and over S[1/t] agree (Gabber–Ramero, Foundations for almost ring theory, Proposition 5.4.54; PerfectoidSpaces:P3/henselian-finite-etale-approximation).

**Direct prerequisites.** `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2`; [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/frobenius-fixed-points`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-4-frobenius-fixed-points); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/etale-comparison`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-4-etale-comparison); `PerfectoidSpaces:P3/henselian-finite-etale-approximation`; `PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-etale-under-completed-perfection`; `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`; [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/fixed-points-completed-colimits`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-4-fixed-points-completed-colimits).

**Acceptance.** S = F_p: the right side is perfect F_p-complexes equipped with an automorphism, matching bounded lisse complexes on Spec(F_p) and their continuous Frobenius action. The automorphism data cannot be omitted. S = k a separably closed field: every (M, α) is trivial, M ≅ M^{φ=1} ⊗_{F_p} k (Lang). S = F_p[x]: on the rank-two free module take Φ(e₁) = e₁ and Φ(e₂) = e₂ + x e₁. Its linearisation is invertible. A fixed basis requires a solution of a^p − a = −x, giving a nontrivial Artin–Schreier cover. The multiplier 1 + x would not define an invertible rank-one Frobenius. The statement fails for finitely generated modules that are not projective if the isomorphism α is replaced by an arbitrary map.

**Sources.** [BS23-FCRYS](https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.14735v2), Proposition 3.4 and its proof. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 9. statement (1); the proof planned is the source's. [BS23-FCRYS](https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.14735v2), Proposition 3.4, proof. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 9. the full faithfulness step. [BS23-FCRYS](https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.14735v2), Proposition 3.6 and its proof. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 10. statement (2) and its proof.

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-7-crystal-descent"></a>

### Descent for prismatic crystals

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.7/crystal-descent` · theorem. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.FCrystal` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/FCrystal/Descent`.

Let X be a p-adic formal scheme. (1) The assignment (A, I) ↦ Vect(A) on X_Δ is a sheaf of categories for the flat topology, and the natural functor lim_{(A,I) ∈ X_Δ} Vect(A) → Vect(X_Δ, O_Δ) to vector bundles on the ringed topos (Shv(X_Δ), O_Δ) (locally of the form P ⊗ O for P finite projective) is an equivalence; the same holds with D_perf in place of Vect. (2) The same two statements hold for O_Δ[1/p]^∧_{I_Δ} and O_Δ[1/I_Δ]^∧_p. (3) Čech form: if (B, J) ∈ X_Δ covers the final object of Shv(X_Δ) and (B^•, J^•) is its Čech nerve (the cosimplicial prism of iterated coproducts in the category of prisms over X), then Vect(X_Δ, O_Δ) ≃ lim(Vect(B^0) ⇉ Vect(B^1) ⇶ Vect(B^2)): a crystal is a finite projective B-module M with an isomorphism p_1^*M ≅ p_2^*M over B^1 satisfying the cocycle condition over B^2; likewise for the two completed sheaves and for D_perf (with the full cosimplicial limit).

**Hypotheses and conventions.** p is a fixed prime; a prism is a bounded prism (A, I) in the sense of PR.0, and X_Δ is the absolute prismatic site of PR.5: the opposite of the category of bounded prisms (A, I) with a map Spf(A/I) → X, with the flat topology. A "map of prisms over X" (A, I) → (B, J) is an arrow of the category of prisms, that is an arrow (B, J) → (A, I) of X_Δ. In (3) the Čech nerve exists whenever the iterated coproducts exist in the category of bounded prisms over X; this is checked for the two covers of Spf(O_K) in node breuil-kisin-and-ainf-covers. The input for (2) is the Drinfeld–Mathew theorem (the source's Theorem 2.2, Mathew, Faithfully flat descent of almost perfect complexes in rigid geometry, Theorem 5.8): for a connective E_∞-ring R and a finitely generated ideal I ⊂ π_0 R the functors S ↦ D_perf, D^-_coh, Vect of Spec(S^∧_I) ∖ V(IS) are sheaves for the I-completely flat topology. It is requested from SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.1.

**Construction or proof.**

1. (1): a (p, I)-completely faithfully flat map of bounded prisms A → B induces faithfully flat maps A/(p, I)^n → B ⊗_A A/(p, I)^n; Vect(A) = lim_n Vect(A/(p,I)^n) since A is classically (p, I)-complete (PR.0/bounded-prism-complete-flatness), and ordinary faithfully flat descent applies at each level (BS23-FCRYS, lines after Theorem 2.2; Anschütz–Le Bras Proposition A.3).
2. Since the prestack is a sheaf, its global sections over the topos are the limit over the site; this is the equivalence with the sheaf-theoretic category (proof of Proposition 2.7, first paragraph). The same argument gives D_perf.
3. (2) for D_perf: devissage modulo powers of I_Δ reduces to lim D_perf(A/I[1/p]) ≃ D_perf(X_Δ, O_Δ/I_Δ[1/p]), which is Drinfeld–Mathew (1) for the ring A/I and the ideal (p); the case of O_Δ[1/I_Δ]^∧_p is the same with the roles of p and I exchanged. For Vect use: over a ring R derived J-complete for a finitely generated ideal J, E ∈ D_perf(R) is a vector bundle if and only if E ⊗^L_R R/J is one.
4. (3): Čech theory in the topos Shv(X_Δ) for a cover of the final object, applied to the sheaf of categories of (1) and (2); for 1-categories of vector bundles the limit over the cosimplicial diagram is computed by its 2-truncation (BS23-FCRYS Example 2.8).

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.7/prismatic-crystal`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-7-prismatic-crystal); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/finite-projective-descent-prisms`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-finite-projective-descent-prisms); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.5/absolute-prismatic-site`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-5-absolute-prismatic-site); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/prismatic-structure-sheaf`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-prismatic-structure-sheaf); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/bounded-prism-complete-flatness`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-bounded-prism-complete-flatness); `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.1`; `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`; `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E3`.

**Acceptance.** For X = Spf(O_K) and the Breuil–Kisin prism: a crystal is a finite free 𝔖-module with a descent isomorphism over 𝔖^(1) and the cocycle condition over 𝔖^(2). For a faithfully flat map of bounded prisms A → B the sequence Vect(A) → Vect(B) ⇉ Vect(B ⊗̂_A B) is an equaliser of categories. The statement for O_Δ[1/I_Δ]^∧_p does not follow from flat descent of modules alone: A[1/I]^∧_p → B[1/I]^∧_p is not flat in general, and Drinfeld–Mathew is used.

**Sources.** [BS23-FCRYS](https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.14735v2), Proposition 2.7 and its proof. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 6. statement (1) and (2); the proof is the one planned. [BS23-FCRYS](https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.14735v2), Theorem 2.2. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 5. the Drinfeld–Mathew descent theorem imported for (2). [BS23-FCRYS](https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.14735v2), Example 2.8. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 7. the Čech form (3) for the Breuil–Kisin cover of Spf(O_K).

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-7-prismatic-f-crystal"></a>

### Prismatic F-crystals on a p-adic formal scheme

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.7/prismatic-f-crystal` · definition. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.FCrystal` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/FCrystal/Basic`.

Let X be a p-adic formal scheme. A prismatic F-crystal (of vector bundles) on X is a pair (E, φ_E) with E ∈ Vect(X_Δ, O_Δ) and φ_E: (φ^*E)[1/I_Δ] ≅ E[1/I_Δ] an isomorphism of crystals over O_Δ[1/I_Δ]; that is, an F-crystal structure φ_{E(A)} on each E(A) (node f-crystal-over-prism) such that the transition isomorphisms E(A) ⊗_A B ≅ E(B) are isomorphisms in Vect^φ(B). Morphisms are morphisms of crystals commuting with φ_E. The category is Vect^φ(X_Δ, O_Δ) = lim_{(A,I) ∈ X_Δ} Vect^φ(A). (E, φ_E) is effective when φ_E carries φ^*E into E. Tensor products make Vect^φ(X_Δ, O_Δ) rigid symmetric monoidal with unit (O_Δ, φ); g: Y → X induces g^*: Vect^φ(X_Δ, O_Δ) → Vect^φ(Y_Δ, O_Δ). For a sheaf O′ of O_Δ-algebras with a compatible Frobenius, Vect^φ(X_Δ, O′) is defined in the same way, and a prismatic F-crystal of perfect complexes is E ∈ D_perf(X_Δ, O_Δ) with φ^*E[1/I_Δ] ≃ E[1/I_Δ]. Example: the Breuil–Kisin twist O_Δ{1} of PR.3 is an invertible prismatic F-crystal on Spf(Z_p), hence by pullback on every bounded X, with φ^*O_Δ{1} ≅ I_Δ^{-1} ⊗ O_Δ{1}; O_Δ{n} = O_Δ{1}^{⊗n} for n ∈ Z.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** p is a fixed prime; a prism is a bounded prism (A, I) in the sense of PR.0, and X_Δ is the absolute prismatic site of PR.5: the opposite of the category of bounded prisms (A, I) with a map Spf(A/I) → X, with the flat topology. A "map of prisms over X" (A, I) → (B, J) is an arrow of the category of prisms, that is an arrow (B, J) → (A, I) of X_Δ. X is an arbitrary p-adic formal scheme for the definition; the twist O_Δ{1} is used on bounded X. Finite locally free F-crystals do not classify torsion or derived Galois representations: the source states that with Z/p^n-coefficients or in the derived category the correct objects should also bound the zeros and poles of φ_E along I_Δ (perfect complexes on Drinfeld's stack Σ″, F-gauges). No statement about F-gauges is planned here.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Add to a crystal (node prismatic-crystal) the Frobenius structures of node f-crystal-over-prism on its values, compatible with the transition maps; φ^*E is the crystal A ↦ φ_A^*E(A), well defined because maps of prisms commute with φ.
2. The limit description, tensor products, duals and pullback are inherited from prismatic-crystal and f-crystal-over-prism.
3. The twist: O_Δ{1}(A) = A{1} with the isomorphism φ^*A{1} ≅ I^{-1} ⊗ A{1} of PR.3/breuil-kisin-twist, natural in the prism (BS23-FCRYS Example 4.5).

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.7/prismatic-crystal`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-7-prismatic-crystal); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.7/f-crystal-over-prism`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-7-f-crystal-over-prism); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.5/absolute-prismatic-site`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-5-absolute-prismatic-site); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/breuil-kisin-twist`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-3-breuil-kisin-twist).

**Consumers.** BS23-FCRYS Theorem 5.6: the source category of the equivalence with crystalline lattices. BS23-FCRYS Constructions 4.8 and 4.12: the source of the étale, crystalline and de Rham realisation functors. BS23-FCRYS Example 4.6: R f_* O_Δ of a proper smooth map is an effective F-crystal in perfect complexes. BS23-FCRYS Proposition 6.8, Remark 5.8: the twists O_Δ{n} enter the Tate-twist calculation and the mod p counterexample.

**Planning API.**

- `TauCeti.Prismatic.FCrystal.SiteData` (data): The category of bounded prisms over X with the diagrams of rings O_Δ, O_Δ[1/I_Δ] and O_Δ[1/I_Δ]^∧_p and the Frobenius of the last.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.FCrystal.SiteData.restrict` (functoriality): Restriction of the data along a functor, as for Y_Δ → X_Δ.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.FCrystal.PrismaticFCrystal` (structure): A prismatic F-crystal: a crystal over O_Δ with a Frobenius structure on every value, compatible with the transition maps.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.FCrystal.PrismaticFCrystal.Hom` (structure): A morphism of prismatic F-crystals.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.FCrystal.PrismaticFCrystal.eval` (projection): Evaluation at an object (A, I): an F-crystal over that prism.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.FCrystal.PrismaticFCrystal.IsEffective` (characterisation): Every evaluation is effective.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.FCrystal.PrismaticFCrystal.unit` (constructor): The unit F-crystal (O_Δ, φ).
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.FCrystal.PrismaticFCrystal.tensor` (functoriality): Tensor product of prismatic F-crystals.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.FCrystal.PrismaticFCrystal.pullback` (functoriality): Pullback along a functor of sites, as for g: Y → X.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.FCrystal.breuilKisinTwist` (example): The invertible F-crystal O_Δ{n}.

**Unit tests.**

- `pr7_fcrystal_eval_effective` (compatibility): A prismatic F-crystal is effective if and only if each of its evaluations is.
- `pr7_fcrystal_twist_invertible` (computation): Every value of O_Δ{n} is an invertible module.
- `pr7_fcrystal_twist_not_effective` (non-example): If some prism of the site has I ≠ A, then O_Δ{1} is not effective.
- `pr7_fcrystal_unit_effective` (degenerate): The unit F-crystal is effective.

**Acceptance.** The unit (O_Δ, φ) is effective; O_Δ{−1} is effective and O_Δ{1} is not. On a quasi-syntomic F_p-scheme the notion is that of an F-crystal on the crystalline site (node crystalline-realization). For X = Spf(R), R quasiregular semiperfectoid, Vect^φ(X_Δ, O_Δ) = Vect^φ(Δ_R).

**Sources.** [BS23-FCRYS](https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.14735v2), Definition 4.1.
