<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-7-quasisyntomic-crystal-comparison"></a>

### Crystals on the prismatic site and on the quasi-syntomic site

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.7/quasisyntomic-crystal-comparison` · theorem. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.FCrystal` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/FCrystal/Descent`.

Let X be a quasi-syntomic p-adic formal scheme, X_qsyn its quasi-syntomic site and X_qrsp ⊂ X_qsyn the full subcategory of Spf(R) → X with R quasiregular semiperfectoid; Δ_• is the sheaf of rings R ↦ Δ_R on X_qsyn (defined on X_qrsp) and I ⊂ Δ_• its ideal sheaf. (1) lim_{R ∈ X_qrsp} Vect(Δ_R) ≃ Vect(X_qsyn, Δ_•). (2) There is a natural equivalence Vect(X_Δ, O_Δ) ≃ Vect(X_qsyn, Δ_•), induced by pullback along the map of ringed topoi ν: (Shv(X_Δ), O_Δ) → (Shv(X_qsyn), Δ_•) determined by R ↦ Δ_R. (3) Both statements hold with D_perf in place of Vect, and with (O_Δ[1/p]^∧_{I_Δ}, Δ_•[1/p]^∧_I) or (O_Δ[1/I_Δ]^∧_p, Δ_•[1/I]^∧_p) in place of (O_Δ, Δ_•). (4) Concretely, for X = Spf(R) affine and R → S a quasi-syntomic cover with S quasiregular semiperfectoid, with p-completed Čech nerve S^•, both sides are lim Vect(Δ_{S^•}).

**Hypotheses and conventions.** p is a fixed prime; a prism is a bounded prism (A, I) in the sense of PR.0, and X_Δ is the absolute prismatic site of PR.5: the opposite of the category of bounded prisms (A, I) with a map Spf(A/I) → X, with the flat topology. A "map of prisms over X" (A, I) → (B, J) is an arrow of the category of prisms, that is an arrow (B, J) → (A, I) of X_Δ. X is quasi-syntomic (DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.5). For R in X_qrsp the prism Δ_R is bounded. The topos Shv(X_qsyn) equals Shv(X_qrsp) (BMS2 Proposition 4.31, Variant 4.35; DD.5).

**Construction or proof.**

1. Reduce to X_qrsp and, by Zariski descent on both sides, to X = Spf(R) affine (proof of Proposition 2.14).
2. The functor Δ(−): R_qrsp → R_Δ, S ↦ Δ_S, satisfies Hom_{R-alg}(S, A/I) = Hom_{R_Δ}(Δ_S, (A, I)) because Δ_S is the initial prism over S (PR.2/qrsp-prism); hence it commutes with finite non-empty coproducts.
3. If S ∈ R_qrsp is a quasi-syntomic cover of R then Δ_S covers the final object of Shv(X_Δ) (BS22 Proposition 7.11, PR.2/quasisyntomic-descent).
4. Choose such an S with Čech nerve S^•: Čech theory in R_qsyn gives Vect(R_qsyn, Δ_•) ≃ lim Vect(Δ_{S^•}), and Čech theory in R_Δ (node crystal-descent (3)) identifies the same limit with Vect(R_Δ, O_Δ). Independence of S: the category of such covers has finite non-empty coproducts, so it is sifted; or use ν^*.
5. (1) is proved as crystal-descent (1)–(2), on the site X_qrsp.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.7/crystal-descent`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-7-crystal-descent); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.7/prismatic-crystal`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-7-prismatic-crystal); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/qrsp-prism`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-qrsp-prism); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/quasisyntomic-descent`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-quasisyntomic-descent); `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.5`; `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.4`.

**Acceptance.** For X = Spf(O_K): Vect(X_Δ, O_Δ) ≃ lim(Vect(A_inf) ⇉ Vect(Δ_{O_C ⊗̂ O_C}) ⇶ Vect(Δ_{O_C ⊗̂ O_C ⊗̂ O_C})), completed tensor products over O_K. For X = Spf(R) with R quasiregular semiperfectoid both sides are Vect(Δ_R).

**Sources.** [BS23-FCRYS](https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.14735v2), Proposition 2.14 and its proof. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 8. statements (2)–(4) and the proof planned. [BS23-FCRYS](https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.14735v2), Proposition 2.13. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 7. statement (1). [BS23-FCRYS](https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.14735v2), Definition 2.9. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 7. the quasi-syntomic site, the subcategory of quasiregular semiperfectoid objects and the sheaf Δ_•.

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-7-laurent-f-crystal"></a>

### Laurent F-crystals

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.7/laurent-f-crystal` · definition. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.FCrystal` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/FCrystal/Laurent`.

Let X be a bounded p-adic formal scheme. For a prism (A, I) the Frobenius φ of A induces a Frobenius on the p-adic completion A[1/I]^∧_p, because φ(I) ≡ I^p modulo p. A Laurent F-crystal in vector bundles on X is an object of Vect(X_Δ, O_Δ[1/I_Δ]^∧_p)^{φ=1} := lim_{(A,I) ∈ X_Δ} Vect(A[1/I]^∧_p)^{φ=1}: a crystal E of vector bundles over O_Δ[1/I_Δ]^∧_p with an isomorphism φ_E: φ^*E ≅ E. In perfect complexes: D_perf(X_Δ, O_Δ[1/I_Δ]^∧_p)^{φ=1} := lim D_perf(A[1/I]^∧_p)^{φ=1}, the ∞-category of pairs (E, φ_E: φ^*E ≃ E). Since I_Δ is invertible in O_Δ[1/I_Δ]^∧_p this category is Vect^φ(X_Δ, O_Δ[1/I_Δ]^∧_p) in the sense of node prismatic-f-crystal. The Z_p-module of Frobenius-fixed sections of E over (A, I) is E(A)^{φ=1} = {x : φ_E(x) = x}.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** p is a fixed prime; a prism is a bounded prism (A, I) in the sense of PR.0, and X_Δ is the absolute prismatic site of PR.5: the opposite of the category of bounded prisms (A, I) with a map Spf(A/I) → X, with the flat topology. A "map of prisms over X" (A, I) → (B, J) is an arrow of the category of prisms, that is an arrow (B, J) → (A, I) of X_Δ. X is bounded: locally Spf(R) with R[p^∞] of bounded exponent (the source's Notation 3.1). The definition itself makes sense for every X; boundedness is used to speak of the generic fibre. If X has characteristic p then every prism of X_Δ has I = (p), A[1/I]^∧_p = 0, and the category is zero (the source's Remark 3.3).

**Construction or proof.**

1. Construct the Frobenius of A[1/I]^∧_p: modulo p^n the element φ(d) of a local generator d of I differs from d^p by a multiple of p, so φ(d) is a unit of A[1/I]/p^n; pass to the limit.
2. Define the category as a limit, using crystal-descent (2) to identify crystals over O_Δ[1/I_Δ]^∧_p with compatible families.
3. The Frobenius structure is recorded as a φ-semilinear endomorphism of each value whose linearisation is bijective, commuting with the transition maps.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.7/prismatic-crystal`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-7-prismatic-crystal); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.7/crystal-descent`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-7-crystal-descent); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.5/absolute-prismatic-site`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-5-absolute-prismatic-site); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/prism`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-prism); [`mathlib:AdicCompletion`](#mathlib-adiccompletion); [`mathlib:Localization.Away`](#mathlib-localization-away).

**Consumers.** BS23-FCRYS Corollaries 3.7 and 3.8: equivalent to lisse Z_p-sheaves, resp. Z_p-local systems, on the generic fibre. BS23-FCRYS Construction 4.8: target of the étale realisation. BS23-FCRYS Theorem 7.2, Corollary 7.10: over the Breuil–Kisin prism: étale φ-modules over the p-adic completion of 𝔖[1/u], i.e. representations of G_{K_∞}.

**Planning API.**

- `TauCeti.Prismatic.FCrystal.LaurentRing` (constructor): The p-adic completion of A[1/I].
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.FCrystal.laurentFrobenius` (constructor): The Frobenius of the p-adic completion of A[1/I] induced by φ.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.FCrystal.LaurentFCrystal` (structure): A crystal over O_Δ[1/I_Δ]^∧_p with a φ-semilinear endomorphism of each value, bijective after linearisation and compatible with the transition maps.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.FCrystal.LaurentFCrystal.Hom` (structure): A morphism of Laurent F-crystals.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.FCrystal.LaurentFCrystal.fixedPoints` (projection): The additive group of Frobenius-fixed elements of a value.

**Unit tests.**

- `pr7_laurent_char_p_zero` (degenerate): If p ∈ I then the p-adic completion of A[1/I] is the zero ring.
- `pr7_laurent_frobenius_extends` (compatibility): The Frobenius of the completion restricts to φ on the image of A.
- `pr7_laurent_fixed_points_res` (computation): The transition maps of a Laurent F-crystal carry Frobenius-fixed elements to Frobenius-fixed elements (over Spf(O_C) the fixed elements of the unit object are Z_p ⊂ W(C^♭)).
- `pr7_laurent_p_frobenius_non_example` (non-example): If p is not a unit of A[1/I]^∧_p, the semilinear map p·φ on the free module of rank one is not a Frobenius structure: its linearisation is multiplication by p, which is not bijective (over O_C this is the F-isocrystal of slope 1, which has no unit-root lattice).

**Acceptance.** For X = Spf(O_C), with C complete and algebraically closed of characteristic 0, the category is Vect(W(C^♭))^{φ=1}, equivalent to Vect(Z_p) by taking φ-fixed points. For X of characteristic p the category is zero. A crystal over O_Δ[1/I_Δ]^∧_p[1/p] with φ^*E ≅ E is in general not a Laurent F-crystal up to isogeny: over O_C these are all F-isocrystals over C^♭, of which only those of slope 0 arise (the source's Remark 3.9).

**Sources.** [BS23-FCRYS](https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.14735v2), Definition 3.2. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 9. the definition, in vector bundles and in perfect complexes. [BS23-FCRYS](https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.14735v2), Remark 3.9. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 11. the non-example: inverting p in the coefficients gives a strictly larger category.

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-7-laurent-f-crystals-local-systems"></a>

### Laurent F-crystals are Z_p-local systems on the generic fibre

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.7/laurent-f-crystals-local-systems` · theorem. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.FCrystal` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/FCrystal/Laurent`.

Let X be a bounded p-adic formal scheme with generic fibre X_η, regarded as a locally spatial diamond. (1) For every bounded prism (A, I) with perfection (B, J), base change is an equivalence D_perf(A[1/I]^∧_p)^{φ=1} ≃ D_perf(B[1/J]^∧_p)^{φ=1}; hence extension of scalars is an equivalence D_perf(X_Δ, O_Δ[1/I_Δ]^∧_p)^{φ=1} ≃ D_perf(X_Δ, O_{Δ,perf}[1/I_Δ]^∧_p)^{φ=1}, the right side being the limit over perfect prisms. (2) The right side is equivalent to D^{(b)}_lisse(X_η, Z_p): the full subcategory of D(X_{η,proét}, Z_p) of locally bounded, derived p-complete objects whose reduction modulo p has locally constant cohomology sheaves with finitely generated stalks. (3) On vector bundles: Vect(X_Δ, O_Δ[1/I_Δ]^∧_p)^{φ=1} ≃ Loc_{Z_p}(X_η), and after inverting p in the Hom groups, Vect(X_Δ, O_Δ[1/I_Δ]^∧_p)^{φ=1} ⊗ Q_p ≃ Loc_{Z_p}(X_η) ⊗ Q_p. (4) For X = Spf(R) with R perfectoid, Δ_R[1/I]^∧_p = W(R^♭[1/I]) and the equivalence is M ↦ the local system of φ-fixed points on Spa(R[1/p], R). (5) For X = Spf(O_K) as in node crystalline-lattices-theorem: Vect(X_Δ, O_Δ[1/I_Δ]^∧_p)^{φ=1} ≃ Rep_{Z_p}(G_K), finite free Z_p-modules with continuous G_K-action, the representation being the φ-fixed points of the value on A_inf with the action induced by that of G_K on the object (A_inf, ker θ̃).

**Hypotheses and conventions.** p is a fixed prime; a prism is a bounded prism (A, I) in the sense of PR.0, and X_Δ is the absolute prismatic site of PR.5: the opposite of the category of bounded prisms (A, I) with a map Spf(A/I) → X, with the flat topology. A "map of prisms over X" (A, I) → (B, J) is an arrow of the category of prisms, that is an arrow (B, J) → (A, I) of X_Δ. X is bounded. In the source this is Corollary 3.7 (derived) and Corollary 3.8 (vector bundles); item 3.9 of the source is the remark on the two enlargements recorded in the last hypothesis. The identification (2) uses that X ↦ D^{(b)}_lisse(X_η, Z_p) is a sheaf of ∞-categories for the quasi-syntomic topology, by v-descent on the diamond X_η; this is requested from DiamondEtaleCohomology:C2 (red-team finding RT-AREA-padic-2/30 (a)). Loc_{Z_p}(X_η) ⊗ Q_p is in general smaller than the category of pro-étale Q_p-local systems, and Vect(…)^{φ=1} ⊗ Q_p smaller than Vect(X_Δ, O_Δ[1/I_Δ]^∧_p[1/p])^{φ=1}; no equivalence between the enlargements is claimed (the source's Remark 3.9).

**Construction or proof.**

1. (1): by the definition of both sides as limits it is enough to treat one prism; by devissage along powers of p reduce to coefficients modulo p, where A/p[1/I] → B/p[1/I] is the passage from R = A/p (derived t-complete for a local generator t of I) to the t-completed perfection, and node artin-schreier-riemann-hilbert (2) applies.
2. (4): for R perfectoid, Δ_R = A_inf(R) (PR.0/perfect-prisms-perfectoid-rings) and A_inf(R)[1/I]^∧_p = W(R^♭[1/I]); modulo p apply artin-schreier-riemann-hilbert (1) to S = R^♭[1/I], then the tilting equivalence of finite étale sites of Spa(R[1/p], R) and its tilt (PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-etale-tilting-equivalence) and the algebraisation of finite étale covers of affinoid perfectoid spaces; pass to Z_p-coefficients by devissage and derived p-completeness (the source's Example 3.5).
3. (2): the limit over perfect prisms in X_Δ is the limit over perfectoid rings R with Spf(R) → X; these give a basis of affinoid perfectoid objects over the diamond X_η, so v-descent for D^{(b)}_lisse (DiamondEtaleCohomology:C2) and (4) identify the limit with D^{(b)}_lisse(X_η, Z_p).
4. (3) follows by the same argument on hearts; the second statement by inverting p. (5): X_η = Spa(K, O_K), whose Z_p-local systems are continuous G_K-representations on finite free Z_p-modules; the Čech nerve of Spa(C, O_C) → Spa(K, O_K) is G_K^n × Spa(C, O_C), so descent data are continuous semilinear actions.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.7/laurent-f-crystal`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-7-laurent-f-crystal); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.7/artin-schreier-riemann-hilbert`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-7-artin-schreier-riemann-hilbert); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.7/crystal-descent`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-7-crystal-descent); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/prism-perfection`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-prism-perfection); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/perfect-prisms-perfectoid-rings`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-perfect-prisms-perfectoid-rings); `PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-etale-tilting-equivalence`; `PerfectoidQuotients:Q0:integral-algebra`; `DiamondEtaleCohomology:C2`; `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`; `PerfectoidSpaces:P3`; `DiamondsAndVStacks:D0`.

**Acceptance.** X = Spf(O_C), with C complete and algebraically closed of characteristic 0: the category of Laurent F-crystals is Vect(Z_p) (taking φ-fixed points of modules over W(C^♭)). X of characteristic p: both sides are zero. X = the p-completion of P^1 over Z_p: de Jong's Q_p-local system with monodromy SL_2(Q_p) is not in Loc_{Z_p}(X_η) ⊗ Q_p. Analogue on the special fibre (the source's Remark 3.11): D_perf(X_Δ, O_Δ)^{φ=1} ≃ D^b_lisse(X_{p=0}, Z_p).

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-7-crystalline-realization"></a>

### The crystalline and de Rham realisations

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.7/crystalline-realization` · construction. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.FCrystal` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/FCrystal/Realization`.

Let X be a quasi-syntomic p-adic formal scheme, flat over Z_p, with special fibre X_{p=0}. (1) For a quasi-syntomic F_p-scheme Z every prism of Z_Δ is crystalline, I = (p), and crystals of vector bundles on Z_Δ and on the crystalline site Z_crys are identified compatibly with Frobenius; hence Vect^φ(Z_Δ, O_Δ) is the category Vect^φ(Z_crys) of F-crystals on Z_crys (finite locally free crystals E with φ^*E[1/p] ≅ E[1/p]). (2) Pullback along X_{p=0} → X gives the crystalline realisation D_crys: Vect^φ(X_Δ, O_Δ) → Vect^φ(X_{p=0,crys}). (3) Forgetting the Frobenius and using that crystals on X_crys and on X_{p=0,crys} agree gives the de Rham realisation D_dR: Vect^φ(X_Δ, O_Δ) → Vect(X_crys); for X formally smooth over a base Y it gives D_{dR,Y} with values in Vect((X/Y)_crys) ≃ vector bundles on X with a topologically quasi-nilpotent flat connection relative to Y. For X = Spf(O_K): the value of D_crys(E) on the prism (W(k), (p)) of Spec(k) is the φ-module E(W(k)); it determines D_crys(E) up to isogeny only (Dwork's trick, node crystalline-representation-of-f-crystal), and D_crys(T(E)[1/p]) = E(W(k))[1/p].

**Hypotheses and conventions.** p is a fixed prime; a prism is a bounded prism (A, I) in the sense of PR.0, and X_Δ is the absolute prismatic site of PR.5: the opposite of the category of bounded prisms (A, I) with a map Spf(A/I) → X, with the flat topology. A "map of prisms over X" (A, I) → (B, J) is an arrow of the category of prisms, that is an arrow (B, J) → (A, I) of X_Δ. X is quasi-syntomic and Z_p-flat (the source assumes flatness for simplicity). Part (1) needs only that Z is a quasi-syntomic F_p-scheme. The crystalline site, crystals on it and their description by connections belong to CrystallineCohomology:CR.1 (requested).

**Construction or proof.**

1. (1): by quasi-syntomic descent on both sides (node quasisyntomic-crystal-comparison) reduce to Z = Spec(R) with R quasiregular semiperfect, where Δ_R ≅ A_crys(R) compatibly with φ (crystalline comparison for prismatic cohomology, PR.2/qrsp-char-p-acrys, with the derived crystalline comparison supplied by CR.4; the smooth comparison PR.1 alone does not cover this case) and both categories are modules over this ring.
2. I = (p) on Z_Δ: p ∈ I because p = 0 in A/I, and the irreducibility lemma for distinguished elements (PR.0/distinguished-factor-rigidity) gives I = (p).
3. (2) is pullback of prismatic F-crystals (node prismatic-f-crystal) along the closed immersion, followed by (1).
4. (3): X_{p=0} ⊂ X is a pro-PD thickening, so crystals on X_crys and X_{p=0,crys} agree (CrystallineCohomology:CR.1).

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.7/prismatic-f-crystal`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-7-prismatic-f-crystal); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.7/quasisyntomic-crystal-comparison`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-7-quasisyntomic-crystal-comparison); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/crystalline-comparison`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-crystalline-comparison); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/qrsp-prism`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-qrsp-prism); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/distinguished-factor-rigidity`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-distinguished-factor-rigidity); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/crystalline-prism`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-crystalline-prism); `CrystallineCohomology:CR.1`; [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/qrsp-char-p-acrys`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-qrsp-char-p-acrys); `CrystallineCohomology:CR.4`.

**Consumers.** BS23-FCRYS Proposition 5.3: the pullback of E to O_C/p and to k gives the comparison T(E) ⊗ B_crys ≅ E(W(k)) ⊗ B_crys. BS23-FCRYS Construction 6.5: the φ-module D over K_0 is regarded as an F-crystal on Spec(k) and pulled back to Δ_•{I/p}. BS23-FCRYS Introduction, after Definition 1.1: the special-fibre realisation of a prismatic F-crystal, of the same rank.

**Planning API.**

- `TauCeti.Prismatic.FCrystal.ideal_eq_span_p_of_mem` (characterisation): For a prism (A, I) with p ∈ I, and p and I in the Jacobson radical, I = (p).
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.FCrystal.crystallineRealization` (constructor): Pullback of a prismatic F-crystal to the site of the special fibre.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.FCrystal.deRhamRealization` (constructor): The underlying crystal of the crystalline realisation, with the Frobenius forgotten.

**Unit tests.**

- `pr7_crys_real_site_crystalline` (characterisation): On the restricted site of a formal scheme of characteristic p every prism is crystalline.
- `pr7_crys_real_eval` (compatibility): The value of D_crys(E) on a prism of the special fibre is the value of E on the same prism regarded over X.
- `pr7_crys_real_twist_value` (computation): The Frobenius of the Breuil–Kisin twist on a crystalline prism (A, (p)) is p^{-1}φ on a free module of rank one: its linearisation carries a generator of φ^*A{1} to p^{-1} times a generator of A{1}.
- `pr7_crys_real_not_effective` (non-example): D_crys(O_Δ{1}) is not effective on a crystalline prism in which p is not a unit.

**Acceptance.** D_crys(O_Δ) is the unit F-crystal; D_crys preserves ranks and tensor products. For X = Spf(O_K): D_crys(O_Δ{n}) is W(k) with Frobenius p^{-n}φ. On Spec(F_p): prismatic F-crystals are finite free Z_p-modules M with an automorphism of M[1/p].

**Sources.** [BS23-FCRYS](https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.14735v2), Construction 4.12. <a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-7-breuil-kisin-and-ainf-covers"></a>

### The Breuil–Kisin and A_inf prisms as covers of Spf(O_K), and their Čech nerves

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.7/breuil-kisin-and-ainf-covers` · construction. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.FCrystal` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/FCrystal/OK`.

Notation as in OK. (1) Breuil–Kisin prism: for a uniformizer π ∈ O_K with Eisenstein polynomial E(u) ∈ W[u], the prism (𝔖, (E(u))) = (W[[u]], (E(u))) with φ(u) = u^p and 𝔖/E(u) ≅ O_K, u ↦ π, is an object of X_Δ which covers the final object of Shv(X_Δ). For every (B, J) ∈ X_Δ and every lift v ∈ B of the image of π, the prismatic envelope C = B[u]{(u − v)/J}^∧_{(p,J)} is a (p, J)-completely flat δ-B-algebra, E(u)C = JC, and (C, JC) is the coproduct of (𝔖, (E)) and (B, J) in the category of prisms over X. (2) A_inf-prism: (A_inf, ker θ̃) = Δ_{O_C} with O_K → O_C is an object of X_Δ covering the final object, because O_K → O_C is a quasi-syntomic cover. (3) Čech nerves: 𝔖^{(•)}, with 𝔖^{(0)} = 𝔖 and 𝔖^{(1)} = W[[u, v]]{(u − v)/E(u)}^∧_{(p,E(u))}, in which E(v)/E(u) is a unit; each 𝔖^{(i)} is a transversal prism. The Čech nerve of A_inf is Δ_{Y^{•/X}}: its terms are Δ_R for R = O_C ⊗̂_{O_K} … ⊗̂_{O_K} O_C, which are quasiregular semiperfectoid and p-torsion-free. (4) A compatible system π̃ = (π, π^{1/p}, …) ∈ O_C^♭ of p-power roots of π (so θ([π̃]) = π and θ̃([π̃]^p) = π) gives the map of prisms over X (𝔖, (E)) → (A_inf, ker θ̃), u ↦ [π̃]^p, which on W(k) is the Frobenius of the Witt-functorial inclusion W(k) ⊂ A_inf (BMS1 §4; this is the W-algebra structure of A_inf compatible with θ̃, as in the source's Notation 5.1). It is the composite of Kisin's embedding u ↦ [π̃] with the Frobenius of A_inf (missed source issue on Notation 7.1), and G_K acts on the object (A_inf, ker θ̃) of X_Δ. (5) Evaluation: for a crystal E on X_Δ (over any of the sheaves of node prismatic-crystal) one has E(𝔖) ⊗_𝔖 A_inf ≅ E(A_inf), E(A_inf) carries a semilinear G_K-action, and E is equivalent to E(𝔖) with a descent datum over 𝔖^{(1)}, and to E(A_inf) with a descent datum over Δ_{O_C ⊗̂ O_C}, each with the cocycle condition over the third term.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** K is a complete discretely valued field of characteristic 0 with perfect residue field k of characteristic p, O_K its ring of integers, W = W(k), K_0 = W[1/p], C a completed algebraic closure of K, G_K = Gal(K̄/K); X = Spf(O_K), Y = Spf(O_C). O_K and O_C are W-algebras through the unique Frobenius-equivariant section k → O_K/p (the source's Notation 5.1). π is a uniformizer; 𝔖 depends on π, A_inf does not. The δ-W-algebra map 𝔖 → A_inf depends on the choice of π^♭. The prisms themselves are PR.0/breuil-kisin-prism and PR.0/ainf-prism; this node adds their structure as objects of X_Δ, the covering property and the Čech nerves.

**Construction or proof.**

1. (1), covering: by (4) the Breuil–Kisin prism maps to the A_inf-prism in X_Δ, and the latter covers the final object by (2); hence so does the former (the first argument indicated in the source's Example 2.6 (1)). (1), coproduct: C exists and is (p, J)-completely flat over B by the existence theorem for prismatic envelopes of regular ideals (BS22 Proposition 3.13, PR.0/regular-prismatic-envelopes) applied to B[u] and the ideal (J, u − v). Since u ≡ v modulo JC, E(u) ≡ E(v) ∈ JC; the irreducibility lemma (BS22 Lemma 2.24, PR.0/distinguished-factor-rigidity) gives E(u)C = JC. The two maps O_K → C/JC agree on π, hence are equal, and the universal property of the envelope gives the coproduct property. The source's direct argument for the covering property also needs B → C to be faithfully flat, which it reads off from Proposition 3.13 although that proposition states complete flatness only (source issue PrismaticCohomology/E79); the plan does not use it.
2. (2): O_K → O_C is a quasi-syntomic cover and O_C is perfectoid; BS22 Proposition 7.11 (PR.2/quasisyntomic-descent) shows Δ_{O_C} covers the final object (compare node quasisyntomic-crystal-comparison).
3. (3): iterate (1) for 𝔖^{(•)}; transversality follows from complete flatness over 𝔖. For A_inf use that Δ(−) commutes with finite non-empty coproducts on quasiregular semiperfectoid algebras.
4. (4): first use the δ-map ι_K : W[[u]] → A_inf with u ↦ [π̃] and the Witt-functorial inclusion on W(k). The map over X for ker θ̃ is ι = φ ∘ ι_K: it sends u to [π̃]^p and acts by Frobenius on W(k). Since θ̃ ∘ φ = θ, its composite with θ̃ sends u to π and agrees with 𝔖 → O_K → O_C. This is the shifted convention required in Notation 7.1. (5) is node crystal-descent (3) for the two covers.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.7/crystal-descent`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-7-crystal-descent); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.7/quasisyntomic-crystal-comparison`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-7-quasisyntomic-crystal-comparison); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/breuil-kisin-prism`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-breuil-kisin-prism); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/ainf-prism`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-ainf-prism); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/regular-prismatic-envelopes`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-regular-prismatic-envelopes); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/distinguished-factor-rigidity`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-distinguished-factor-rigidity); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/qrsp-prism`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-qrsp-prism); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/quasisyntomic-descent`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-quasisyntomic-descent); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.5/absolute-prismatic-site`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-5-absolute-prismatic-site); `PerfectoidQuotients:Q0:integral-algebra`; [`mathlib:PowerSeries`](#mathlib-powerseries); [`mathlib:WittVector`](#mathlib-wittvector); [`mathlib:Polynomial.IsEisensteinAt`](#mathlib-polynomial-iseisensteinat).

**Consumers.** BS23-FCRYS §5 and §6: the main theorem is proved by descent along Spf(O_C) → Spf(O_K), using the first three terms of the Čech nerve. BS23-FCRYS Theorem 7.9, Remark 7.12: evaluation at 𝔖 defines D_𝔖; the map 𝔖 → A_inf and the crystal property give independence of the uniformizer. BS23-FCRYS Remark 5.7: descent along 𝔖^{(•)} gives a second proof of full faithfulness. BS23-FCRYS Corollary 7.17: the descent datum over 𝔖^{(1)} induces the logarithmic connection.

**Planning API.**

- `TauCeti.Prismatic.FCrystal.OKData` (data): The data attached to O_K: the site Spf(O_K)_Δ, the group G_K, the objects 𝔖 and A_inf with the map 𝔖 → A_inf, the crystalline lattices and the weakly admissible filtered φ-modules.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.FCrystal.bk_covers` (characterisation): Every object of the site maps to an object that also receives a map from the Breuil–Kisin prism.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.FCrystal.ainf_covers` (characterisation): Every object of the site maps to an object that also receives a map from the A_inf-prism.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.FCrystal.evalBK` (projection): Evaluation of a prismatic F-crystal at the Breuil–Kisin prism: a Breuil–Kisin module.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.FCrystal.evalAinf` (projection): Evaluation at the A_inf-prism: a Breuil–Kisin–Fargues module.

**Unit tests.**

- `pr7_ok_bk_to_ainf_base_change` (compatibility): For a crystal E the transition map E(𝔖) → E(A_inf) exhibits E(A_inf) as E(𝔖) ⊗_𝔖 A_inf.
- `pr7_ok_ainf_perfect` (computation): The A_inf-prism is perfect and orientable (I is generated by [p]_q).
- `pr7_ok_bk_not_perfect` (non-example): The Breuil–Kisin prism is not perfect: u is not in the image of φ.
- `pr7_ok_bk_orientable` (degenerate): The Breuil–Kisin prism is orientable, with I generated by E(u).

**Acceptance.** K = Q_p, π = p: 𝔖 = Z_p[[u]], E = u − p; 𝔖^{(1)} = Z_p[[u, v]]{(u − v)/(u − p)}^∧. K = Q_p(p^{1/p}), π = p^{1/p}: E = u^p − p, and 𝔖 → A_inf carries u − p to a unit multiple of [p]_{q^{1/p}} (the source's Example 7.8). The Breuil–Kisin prism is not perfect; the A_inf-prism is its image under a map to a perfect prism, not its perfection (the perfection is A_inf of the completion of K(π^{1/p^∞})).

**Sources.** [BS23-FCRYS](https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.14735v2), Example 2.6. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 6. statements (1) and (2) with the proof of the covering property. [BS23-FCRYS](https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.14735v2), Construction 7.13. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 34. statement (3): the Čech nerve of the Breuil–Kisin prism. <a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-7-etale-realization"></a>

### The étale realisation functor

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.7/etale-realization` · construction. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.FCrystal` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/FCrystal/Realization`.

For every p-adic formal scheme X the p-completed base change E ↦ E ⊗_{O_Δ} O_Δ[1/I_Δ]^∧_p, with the induced Frobenius, is a symmetric monoidal functor T: Vect^φ(X_Δ, O_Δ) → Vect(X_Δ, O_Δ[1/I_Δ]^∧_p)^{φ=1}: on a prism (A, I) it sends (M, φ_M) to M ⊗_A A[1/I]^∧_p with φ_M ⊗ φ, which is an isomorphism because I is invertible in the target. For X bounded, composing with the equivalence of node laurent-f-crystals-local-systems gives T: Vect^φ(X_Δ, O_Δ) → Loc_{Z_p}(X_η), the étale realisation; it preserves ranks, tensor products and duals and commutes with pullback along maps of bounded p-adic formal schemes. For F-crystals of perfect complexes the same formula gives T with values in D^{(b)}_lisse(X_η, Z_p). For X = Spf(O_K), T(E) is the G_K-representation (E(A_inf) ⊗_{A_inf} W(C^♭))^{φ=1}. On twists, T(O_Δ{i}) = Z_p(i) for all i and all bounded X.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** p is a fixed prime; a prism is a bounded prism (A, I) in the sense of PR.0, and X_Δ is the absolute prismatic site of PR.5: the opposite of the category of bounded prisms (A, I) with a map Spf(A/I) → X, with the flat topology. A "map of prisms over X" (A, I) → (B, J) is an arrow of the category of prisms, that is an arrow (B, J) → (A, I) of X_Δ. The functor to Laurent F-crystals exists for every p-adic formal scheme X; the identification of its target with Loc_{Z_p}(X_η) requires X bounded. The source's Construction 4.8 says "for any p-adic formal scheme" for both and refers to Corollary 3.7; the hypothesis and the reference (Corollary 3.8 for vector bundles) are corrected here (source issue PrismaticCohomology/E72). T(O_Δ{1}) = Z_p(1) is stated in the source's Example 4.9 without proof, with a pointer to the q-logarithm of Anschütz–Le Bras and the prismatic logarithm of Bhatt–Lurie. The plan uses, for perfectoid R, the identification of the φ-fixed elements of Fil^1_N Δ_R{1} with the Tate module T_p(R^×) (BS22 Theorem 9.4 and Remark 9.5, PR.4/tate-twist-perfectoid), which is natural in R and therefore Galois-equivariant.

**Construction or proof.**

1. On each prism: base change M ↦ M ⊗_A A[1/I]^∧_p with the Frobenius of node laurent-f-crystal; φ_M becomes an isomorphism φ^*(M ⊗ A[1/I]^∧_p) ≅ M ⊗ A[1/I]^∧_p. Naturality in the prism gives a functor on the limits.
2. Symmetric monoidality: base change commutes with tensor products of finite projective modules.
3. Compose with laurent-f-crystals-local-systems (3) for bounded X; compatibility with pullback follows from the naturality of that equivalence in X.
4. Twists: by pullback from Spf(Z_p) and descent it suffices to treat perfectoid R containing all p-power roots of unity; there T_p(R^×) → Δ_R{1}^{φ=1} → (Δ_R{1}[1/I]^∧_p)^{φ=1} identifies the local system T(O_Δ{1}) with Z_p(1), by PR.4/tate-twist-perfectoid and naturality in R; tensor powers give all i.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.7/prismatic-f-crystal`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-7-prismatic-f-crystal); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.7/laurent-f-crystal`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-7-laurent-f-crystal); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.7/laurent-f-crystals-local-systems`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-7-laurent-f-crystals-local-systems); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/breuil-kisin-twist`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-3-breuil-kisin-twist); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/tate-twist-perfectoid`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-4-tate-twist-perfectoid); `DiamondsAndVStacks:D0`.

**Consumers.** BS23-FCRYS Theorem 5.6: the main theorem says T is an equivalence onto crystalline lattices for X = Spf(O_K). BS23-FCRYS Example 4.10, Lemma 4.11: T is faithful over p-torsion-free quasiregular semiperfectoid rings. BS23-FCRYS Theorem 7.2: the same functor at the single prism 𝔖 is fully faithful. BS23-FCRYS Remark 5.8: with mod p coefficients T is not fully faithful.

**Planning API.**

- `TauCeti.Prismatic.FCrystal.etaleRealization` (constructor): The Laurent F-crystal E ⊗ O_Δ[1/I_Δ]^∧_p attached to a prismatic F-crystal E.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.FCrystal.etaleRealizationMap` (functoriality): The action of the étale realisation on morphisms.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.FCrystal.etaleRealization_eval` (compatibility): The value of T(E) on a prism is the completed base change of E(A).
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.FCrystal.galoisRep` (constructor): For X = Spf(O_K): the G_K-representation on the φ-fixed points of the value of a Laurent F-crystal on A_inf.

**Unit tests.**

- `pr7_etale_real_unit` (computation): T of the unit F-crystal has value O_Δ[1/I_Δ]^∧_p(A) on every prism, with Frobenius the Frobenius of that ring.
- `pr7_etale_real_char_p_zero` (degenerate): If p ∈ I for a prism (A, I) of the site, the value of T(E) on it is zero.
- `pr7_etale_real_map_injective_transversal` (compatibility): If A → A[1/I]^∧_p is injective for every prism of the site, then T is injective on morphisms.
- `pr7_etale_real_not_full` (non-example): The étale realisation is not full in general: there are a site and F-crystals E, E′ with a morphism T(E) → T(E′) not of the form T(f) (over Spf(O_C): E = O_Δ{1}, E′ = O_Δ).

**Acceptance.** T(O_Δ) is the constant local system Z_p; T(O_Δ{1}) = Z_p(1). For X of characteristic p, T = 0; in particular T is not faithful there. Over Spf(O_C), T is faithful but not full: Hom(O_Δ{1}, O_Δ) = (μA_inf)^{φ=1} = 0, while the realisations Z_p(1) and Z_p are isomorphic Z_p-modules (there is no Galois action over O_C). In the other direction the inclusion A_inf ⊂ μ^{-1}A_inf = A_inf{1} is a morphism whose realisation is an isomorphism although it is not one. T commutes with proper smooth pushforward of the structure sheaf (the source's Example 4.9), through the Artin–Schreier sequence on X_{η,proét}; this is the étale comparison PR.4/etale-comparison with coefficients and is recorded as a consistency check, not planned as a node.

**Sources.** [BS23-FCRYS](https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.14735v2), Construction 4.8. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 13. the construction; the boundedness hypothesis for the second identification is added. [BS23-FCRYS](https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.14735v2), Example 4.9. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 13. the value on Breuil–Kisin twists.

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-7-f-crystals-over-qrsp"></a>

### F-crystals over a quasiregular semiperfectoid ring; faithfulness of the étale realisation

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.7/f-crystals-over-qrsp` · theorem. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.FCrystal` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/FCrystal/Realization`.

Let R be a quasiregular semiperfectoid ring with prism (Δ_R, I) and X = Spf(R). (1) (Δ_R, I) is the final object of X_Δ (the initial prism over R), so evaluation at Δ_R gives equivalences Vect^φ(X_Δ, O_Δ) ≃ Vect^φ(Δ_R) and D_perf(X_Δ, O_Δ[1/I_Δ]^∧_p)^{φ=1} ≃ D_perf(Δ_R[1/I]^∧_p)^{φ=1}, and similarly for every sheaf of node prismatic-crystal. (2) If R is p-torsion-free then (Δ_R, I) is transversal ((p, d) is a regular sequence for a generator d of I), the map Δ_R → Δ_R[1/I]^∧_p is injective, and so is M → M ⊗_{Δ_R} Δ_R[1/I]^∧_p for every finite projective Δ_R-module M. (3) Consequently the étale realisation T: Vect^φ(X_Δ, O_Δ) → Vect(X_Δ, O_Δ[1/I_Δ]^∧_p)^{φ=1} is faithful when R is p-torsion-free.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** p is a fixed prime; a prism is a bounded prism (A, I) in the sense of PR.0, and X_Δ is the absolute prismatic site of PR.5: the opposite of the category of bounded prisms (A, I) with a map Spf(A/I) → X, with the flat topology. A "map of prisms over X" (A, I) → (B, J) is an arrow of the category of prisms, that is an arrow (B, J) → (A, I) of X_Δ. The universal prism is final in X_Δ, since Definition 2.3 reverses prism arrows. Examples 3.5 and 4.10 use the other direction, inconsistent with Example 2.5 (PrismaticCohomology/E71). Part (2) assumes R p-torsion-free; for R of characteristic p the target ring is zero.

**Construction or proof.**

1. (1): Δ_R is the initial prism over R (BS22 Proposition 7.10, PR.2/qrsp-prism); a limit over a category with an initial object is the value there.
2. (2): Δ̄_R is p-torsion-free because it has an exhaustive filtration with graded pieces p-completely flat over the p-torsion-free ring R (Hodge–Tate comparison, PR.2/derived-hodge-tate-comparison); hence (p, d) is regular. The cofibre of Δ_R → Δ_R[1/I]^∧_p is derived p-complete, so by derived Nakayama injectivity follows from injectivity of Δ_R/p → Δ_R/p[1/I], which holds because d is a nonzerodivisor modulo p.
3. (3): a morphism of F-crystals over Δ_R that vanishes after base change to Δ_R[1/I]^∧_p vanishes, by (2) applied to the internal Hom module.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.7/prismatic-f-crystal`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-7-prismatic-f-crystal); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.7/etale-realization`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-7-etale-realization); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/qrsp-prism`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-qrsp-prism); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/derived-hodge-tate-comparison`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-derived-hodge-tate-comparison); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/transversal-prism-regular-sequences`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-transversal-prism-regular-sequences); `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`.

**Acceptance.** R = O_C: A_inf → W(C^♭) is injective. R = O_C ⊗̂_{O_K} O_C and its triple analogue: T is faithful on every term of the Čech nerve of Spf(O_C) → Spf(O_K). R = O_C/p: Δ_R = A_crys, I = (p), and the étale realisation is zero, so faithfulness fails without p-torsion-freeness.

**Sources.** [BS23-FCRYS](https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.14735v2), Lemma 4.11 and its proof. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 14. statement (2). [BS23-FCRYS](https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.14735v2), Example 4.10. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 13. statements (1) and (3).

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-7-bkf-modules-comparison"></a>

### F-crystals over O_C are Breuil–Kisin–Fargues modules; the functor of Fargues' theorem

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.7/bkf-modules-comparison` · comparison. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.FCrystal` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/FCrystal/OK`.

Notation as in OK and PER. (1) Evaluation at A_inf identifies Vect^φ(Y_Δ, O_Δ) = Vect^φ(A_inf) with the category of finite free Breuil–Kisin–Fargues modules of AInfCohomology:AI.2: finite free A_inf-modules M with φ_M: φ^*M[1/ξ̃] ≅ M[1/ξ̃]. (2) For such M the étale realisation is T = (M ⊗_{A_inf} W(C^♭))^{φ=1}, a finite free Z_p-module with M ⊗ W(C^♭) ≅ T ⊗_{Z_p} W(C^♭), and this isomorphism restricts to M[1/μ] ≅ T ⊗_{Z_p} A_inf[1/μ] (BMS1 Lemma 4.26); since μ is invertible at the Hodge–Tate point, M ⊗ B_dR^+ ≅ T ⊗ B_dR^+, and F := φ^*M ⊗_{A_inf} B_dR^+ is a B_dR^+-lattice in T ⊗_{Z_p} B_dR. (3) The functor M ↦ (T, F) from Vect^φ(A_inf) to pairs (T a finite free Z_p-module, F a B_dR^+-lattice in T ⊗ B_dR) is an equivalence (Fargues); PR.7 uses only that it is fully faithful. (4) Vector bundles on Spec(A_inf) ∖ {x_k}, x_k the closed point, extend uniquely to Spec(A_inf).

**Hypotheses and conventions.** K is a complete discretely valued field of characteristic 0 with perfect residue field k of characteristic p, O_K its ring of integers, W = W(k), K_0 = W[1/p], C a completed algebraic closure of K, G_K = Gal(K̄/K); X = Spf(O_K), Y = Spf(O_C). O_K and O_C are W-algebras through the unique Frobenius-equivariant section k → O_K/p (the source's Notation 5.1). Period rings, normalised as in the source's Notation 5.1: A_inf = A_inf(O_C) = Δ_{O_C} with q = [ε], μ = q − 1, ξ̃ = [p]_q, θ̃: A_inf → O_C with kernel (ξ̃), and θ = θ̃ ∘ φ; A_crys = A_inf{[p]_q/p} = Δ_{O_C/p}, the p-completed PD envelope of ker θ; B_crys^+ = A_crys[1/p], B_crys = A_crys[1/μ]; B_dR^+ the completion of A_inf[1/p] at ker θ̃, B_dR = B_dR^+[1/[p]_q]; the map φ^*B_crys → B_dR is A_inf-linear for the Frobenius-twisted structure on B_crys. These are the rings of PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1 with θ replaced by θ̃ = θ ∘ φ^{-1}; the dictionary is part of the request to R06.1. C is algebraically closed and complete. Fargues' equivalence, BMS1 Lemma 4.26, the elementary proof of full faithfulness (BMS1 Remark 4.29) and the extension statement (Kedlaya; BMS1 Lemma 4.6) are owned by AInfCohomology:AI.2 and requested there; they are not planned again. AI.2 states Breuil–Kisin–Fargues modules with φ_M: M[1/ξ] → M[1/ξ̃] semilinear; the linearised form used here is the same datum.

**Construction or proof.**

1. (1): node f-crystals-over-qrsp (1) for R = O_C, and Δ_{O_C} = A_inf with I = ker θ̃ (PR.0/ainf-prism); finite projective A_inf-modules are free because A_inf is local.
2. (2): laurent-f-crystals-local-systems (4) for R = O_C gives T and the trivialisation over W(C^♭) = A_inf[1/I]^∧_p; BMS1 Lemma 4.26 (AI.2) descends it to A_inf[1/μ]; θ̃(μ) = ε_p − 1 ≠ 0 gives the statement over B_dR^+.
3. (3) and (4) are imported from AI.2.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.7/f-crystals-over-qrsp`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-7-f-crystals-over-qrsp); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.7/laurent-f-crystals-local-systems`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-7-laurent-f-crystals-local-systems); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.7/f-crystal-over-prism`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-7-f-crystal-over-prism); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/ainf-prism`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-ainf-prism); `AInfCohomology:AI.2`; `PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/de-rham-period-ring`; `PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/bdr-plus-complete-dvr`; `PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/tilt-of-cp-and-special-elements`.

**Acceptance.** M = A_inf with φ: (T, F) = (Z_p, B_dR^+). M = A_inf{1} ≅ μ^{-1}A_inf: T = Z_p(1) and F = ξ̃^{-1}·(T ⊗ B_dR^+), a lattice different from T ⊗ B_dR^+; so A_inf and A_inf{1} are not isomorphic although their realisations are. The equivalence is not asserted for finitely presented torsion Breuil–Kisin–Fargues modules.

**Sources.** [BS23-FCRYS](https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.14735v2), Theorem 5.2 and the construction after it. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 15. the statement imported and the construction of (T, F) from a prismatic F-crystal on Spf(O_C).

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-7-period-sheaves-qrsp"></a>

### Period sheaves on the quasi-syntomic site of O_K

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.7/period-sheaves-qrsp` · construction. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.FCrystal` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/FCrystal/Period`.

Notation as in OK. On X_qrsp (quasiregular semiperfectoid O_K-algebras R, quasi-syntomic over O_K; each Δ_R is a transversal bounded prism with ideal I) define the presheaves of rings: Δ_• (R ↦ Δ_R); A_crys = Δ_•{I/p} (R ↦ Δ_R{I/p} = Δ_{R/p} = A_crys(R)); the rational localisation Δ_•⟨I/p⟩ (R ↦ Δ_R[I/p]^∧_p, equal to Δ_R[x]/(px − d)^∧_p for a generator d of I); Δ_•{φ(I)/p} (R ↦ Δ_R{φ(I)/p}, the φ-pullback of A_crys); Δ_•[1/I]^∧_p; and the de Rham period sheaves B_dR^+ = (Δ_•[1/p])^∧_I, B_dR = B_dR^+[1/I]. They are related by natural maps Δ_•[1/I]^∧_p ← Δ_• → Δ_•{φ(I)/p} → Δ_•⟨I/p⟩ → Δ_•{I/p}. The Frobenius of Δ_• carries I to φ(I) and induces φ̃: Δ_•{I/p} → Δ_•{φ(I)/p}, linear over φ; composing with the maps above gives Frobenius endomorphisms of Δ_•, Δ_•{I/p}, Δ_•⟨I/p⟩, Δ_•{φ(I)/p} and Δ_•[1/I]^∧_p. This assertion concerns the five presheaves of Construction 6.2; it does not extend Frobenius to the I-adic completions B_dR^+ or B_dR of Construction 6.4. More generally Δ_•⟨φ^n(I)/p⟩ is defined for n ≥ 0, with maps Δ_•⟨φ^{n+1}(I)/p⟩ → Δ_•⟨φ^n(I)/p⟩ and φ̃: Δ_•⟨φ^n(I)/p⟩ → Δ_•⟨φ^{n+1}(I)/p⟩. For each of the five Frobenius-equipped rings an F-crystal is a vector bundle M with φ_M: (φ^*M)[1/I] ≅ M[1/I]. Lemma (the source's Lemma 6.7): for every transversal prism (A, I) and n ≥ 0 the natural map A[1/p]^∧_I → A⟨φ^n(I)/p⟩[1/p]^∧_I is an isomorphism; so B_dR^+ ≅ Δ_•⟨φ^n(I)/p⟩[1/p]^∧_I for all n ≥ 0.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** K is a complete discretely valued field of characteristic 0 with perfect residue field k of characteristic p, O_K its ring of integers, W = W(k), K_0 = W[1/p], C a completed algebraic closure of K, G_K = Gal(K̄/K); X = Spf(O_K), Y = Spf(O_C). O_K and O_C are W-algebras through the unique Frobenius-equivariant section k → O_K/p (the source's Notation 5.1). Every R in X_qrsp is p-torsion-free, so Δ_R is transversal: (p, d) is a regular sequence (node f-crystals-over-qrsp (2)). The endomorphism φ of Δ_•⟨I/p⟩ is not a Frobenius lift: it need not be congruent to the p-th power map modulo p; forcing the congruence gives Δ_•{I/p} (the source's footnote to Construction 6.2). Δ_R{I/p} and Δ_R{φ(I)/p} are δ-envelopes, constructed in PR.0 (PR.0/pd-envelope-as-delta-envelope: A{φ(f)/p} is the p-completed PD envelope of (f)); Δ_R{I/p} = Δ_{R/p} is PR.2/qrsp-prism for R/p. For the complete algebraically closed field C of this node, B_dR^+(O_C) is the usual discrete valuation ring (PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/de-rham-period-ring with θ̃ in place of θ). For a general perfectoid R the same completion defines a period algebra, without a discrete valuation ring assertion; for example a product of two copies of O_C gives a product of period rings.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Define each presheaf objectwise from Δ_R with its orientation-independent ideal I; functoriality in R follows from that of Δ_R (PR.2/qrsp-prism) and IΔ_{R′} = I′ (PR.0/rigidity-prism-ideal).
2. The maps: φ(d) = d^p + pδ(d) gives φ(d)/p = p^{p−1}(d/p)^p + δ(d) ∈ Δ_R[d/p], whence Δ_R{φ(I)/p} → Δ_R⟨I/p⟩ (the divided powers of d exist in Δ_R⟨I/p⟩ because d^n/n! = (p^n/n!)(d/p)^n); Δ_R⟨I/p⟩ → Δ_R{I/p} is the universal map out of the ring obtained by adjoining d/p.
3. Lemma 6.7: with I = (d) and A⟨φ^n(d)/p⟩ = A[x]/(px − φ^n(d))^∧_p it suffices that A[1/p]/d → Kos(A[x]; px − φ^n(d), d)^∧_p[1/p] is an isomorphism. Write φ^n(d) = d^{p^n} + ph and y = x − h: the target is Kos(A[y]; py, d)^∧_p[1/p] ≃ Kos(A[y]; y, d)^∧_p[1/p] ≃ A/d[1/p], because py is a nonzerodivisor on A/d[y] (transversality) and the kernel of A[y]/py → A[y]/y is killed by p.
4. For the five rings of Construction 6.2, the Frobenius endomorphisms are the composites of φ̃ with the structure maps. The later I-adic completion defining B_dR^+ is not a Frobenius-continuous completion and supplies no such endomorphism.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.7/f-crystals-over-qrsp`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-7-f-crystals-over-qrsp); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.7/quasisyntomic-crystal-comparison`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-7-quasisyntomic-crystal-comparison); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/qrsp-prism`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-qrsp-prism); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/pd-envelope-as-delta-envelope`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-pd-envelope-as-delta-envelope); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/rigidity-prism-ideal`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-rigidity-prism-ideal); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/transversal-prism-regular-sequences`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-transversal-prism-regular-sequences); `PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/de-rham-period-ring`; `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`; [`mathlib:AdicCompletion`](#mathlib-adiccompletion); [`mathlib:Localization.Away`](#mathlib-localization-away).

**Consumers.** BS23-FCRYS Construction 6.5 and Remark 6.6: a filtered φ-module gives an F-crystal over Δ_•⟨I/p⟩[1/p], modified along I = 0 through B_dR^+ and continued to Δ_•⟨φ^n(I)/p⟩[1/p]. BS23-FCRYS Propositions 6.8 and 6.10: φ-fixed elements of Δ_R⟨I/p⟩{n}[1/p] and descent data over Δ_R⟨I/p⟩[1/p] are compared with those over Δ_R[1/p]. BS23-FCRYS Theorem 7.9, Corollary 7.17: the same rings for the Breuil–Kisin prism: 𝔖⟨I/p⟩[1/p] and its completion at E(u).

**Planning API.**

- `TauCeti.Prismatic.FCrystal.Period.Rational` (constructor): The ring A⟨d/p⟩: the p-adic completion of A[x]/(px − d).
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.FCrystal.Period.toRational` (data): The structure map A → A⟨d/p⟩.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.FCrystal.Period.rationalFrobenius` (constructor): The endomorphism φ of A⟨d/p⟩ extending φ of A, for d a generator of the ideal of a prism.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.FCrystal.Period.BdRPlus` (constructor): The ring A[1/p]^∧_d, the d-adic completion of A[1/p].
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.FCrystal.Period.bdRPlus_equiv_rational` (compatibility): For a transversal oriented prism (A, (d)) and n ≥ 0: A[1/p]^∧_d ≅ A⟨φ^n(d)/p⟩[1/p]^∧_d.

**Unit tests.**

- `pr7_period_rational_p_dvd` (computation): In A⟨d/p⟩ the image of d is divisible by p.
- `pr7_period_bdr_plus_p_unit` (compatibility): p is a unit of A[1/p]^∧_d.
- `pr7_period_rational_frobenius_extends` (compatibility): The Frobenius of A⟨d/p⟩ restricts to φ on the image of A.
- `pr7_period_frobenius_not_lift` (non-example): It is not true that for every oriented prism the endomorphism φ of A⟨d/p⟩ is congruent to the p-th power map modulo p (A = Z_p[[u]], d = u − p, x = u/p).

**Acceptance.** R = O_C: Δ_•{I/p} = A_crys, B_dR^+ the usual ring, Δ_•[1/I]^∧_p = W(C^♭). In Δ_R⟨I/p⟩ every element of I is divisible by p; in B_dR^+(R) the element p is a unit. For A = Z_p[[u]], d = u − p: A⟨d/p⟩ = Z_p⟨u/p⟩ and φ(u/p) = p^{p−1}(u/p)^p ≡ 0 modulo p, while (u/p)^p is not; so φ is not a Frobenius lift on A⟨d/p⟩.

**Sources.** [BS23-FCRYS](https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.14735v2), Construction 6.2. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 19. the five sheaves, the maps between them and their Frobenius endomorphisms. [BS23-FCRYS](https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.14735v2), Construction 6.4. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 20. the de Rham period sheaves. [BS23-FCRYS](https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.14735v2), Lemma 6.7 and its proof. <a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-7-crystalline-representation-of-f-crystal"></a>

### Prismatic F-crystals on O_K give crystalline Galois representations

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.7/crystalline-representation-of-f-crystal` · theorem. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.FCrystal` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/FCrystal/OK`.

Notation as in OK and PER. Let E ∈ Vect^φ(X_Δ, O_Δ). (1) There is a canonical G_K-equivariant, Frobenius-compatible isomorphism T(E) ⊗_{Z_p} B_crys ≅ E(W(k)) ⊗_{W(k)} B_crys, where E(W(k)) is the value of E on the crystalline prism (W(k), (p)) over Spec(k) ⊂ Spec(O_K/p); hence T(E)[1/p] is a crystalline representation of G_K, of dimension rk(E), and D_crys(T(E)[1/p]) ≅ E(W(k))[1/p] as φ-modules over K_0. Thus T takes values in Rep^crys_{Z_p}(G_K), the category of finite free Z_p-modules with continuous G_K-action whose rationalisation is crystalline. (2) Compatibility of lattices: base change of (1) along φ^*B_crys → B_dR gives T(E) ⊗ B_dR ≅ φ^*E(W(k)) ⊗_{W(k)} B_dR, and the B_dR^+-lattice F′ = φ^*E(W(k)) ⊗_{W(k)} B_dR^+ equals the lattice F = φ^*E(A_inf) ⊗_{A_inf} B_dR^+ of node bkf-modules-comparison. (3) Under T(E)[1/p] = V, F = D_dR(V) ⊗_K B_dR^+.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** K is a complete discretely valued field of characteristic 0 with perfect residue field k of characteristic p, O_K its ring of integers, W = W(k), K_0 = W[1/p], C a completed algebraic closure of K, G_K = Gal(K̄/K); X = Spf(O_K), Y = Spf(O_C). O_K and O_C are W-algebras through the unique Frobenius-equivariant section k → O_K/p (the source's Notation 5.1). Period rings, normalised as in the source's Notation 5.1: A_inf = A_inf(O_C) = Δ_{O_C} with q = [ε], μ = q − 1, ξ̃ = [p]_q, θ̃: A_inf → O_C with kernel (ξ̃), and θ = θ̃ ∘ φ; A_crys = A_inf{[p]_q/p} = Δ_{O_C/p}, the p-completed PD envelope of ker θ; B_crys^+ = A_crys[1/p], B_crys = A_crys[1/μ]; B_dR^+ the completion of A_inf[1/p] at ker θ̃, B_dR = B_dR^+[1/[p]_q]; the map φ^*B_crys → B_dR is A_inf-linear for the Frobenius-twisted structure on B_crys. These are the rings of PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1 with θ replaced by θ̃ = θ ∘ φ^{-1}; the dictionary is part of the request to R06.1. Crystalline representations, D_crys and D_dR are those of PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2 (period-functors, admissible-representations). The Frobenius twist: the filtered φ-module attached to E has underlying K_0-space D = E(W(k))[1/p] and filtration on D ⊗_{W(k),φ} K, the convention of the source's Construction 6.5.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Crystal property for A_inf = Δ_{O_C} → A_crys = Δ_{O_C/p}: E(A_inf) ⊗_{A_inf} A_crys ≅ E(A_crys). Invert μ and use M[1/μ] ≅ T ⊗ A_inf[1/μ] (node bkf-modules-comparison (2)): T(E) ⊗ B_crys ≅ E(A_crys)[1/μ].
2. Dwork's Frobenius trick: O_K/p → k is a nilpotent thickening in characteristic p, so φ^n of O_K/p factors through k for n large; for a crystal E′ on Spec(O_K/p), (φ^n)^*E′ is the pullback of E′|_{Spec(k)} along φ_n: k → O_K/p. Pull back to O_C/p and use the F-crystal structure to remove the Frobenius pullback after inverting p: E(A_crys)[1/μ] ≅ E(W(k)) ⊗_{W(k)} B_crys.
3. The composite isomorphism is G_K-equivariant (G_K acts on the objects A_inf, A_crys of the site and trivially on E(W(k))), so dim_{K_0}(T(E)[1/p] ⊗ B_crys)^{G_K} = rk(E) and T(E)[1/p] is crystalline (R06.2).
4. (2) and (3): unwind the constructions of F and F′; the filtration on D_dR is induced by B_dR^+ ⊂ B_dR.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.7/etale-realization`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-7-etale-realization); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.7/bkf-modules-comparison`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-7-bkf-modules-comparison); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.7/crystalline-realization`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-7-crystalline-realization); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.7/breuil-kisin-and-ainf-covers`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-7-breuil-kisin-and-ainf-covers); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/pd-envelope-as-delta-envelope`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-pd-envelope-as-delta-envelope); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/qrsp-prism`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-qrsp-prism); `PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/crystalline-period-ring`; `PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/frobenius-on-acris`; `PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/acris-embedding-into-bdr-plus`; `PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/period-functors`; `PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/admissible-representations`; `PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1`; `PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2`.

**Acceptance.** E = O_Δ: T = Z_p, D_crys = K_0 with φ. E = O_Δ{1}: T = Z_p(1), E(W(k)) = W(k) with p^{-1}φ; this fixes the normalisation of D_crys relative to R06.2. A ramified character of finite order is de Rham but not crystalline, so by (1) its lattice is not the realisation of a prismatic F-crystal on Spf(O_K).

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-7-filtered-phi-module-to-crystal"></a>

### From filtered φ-modules to F-crystals over the open unit disc

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.7/filtered-phi-module-to-crystal` · construction. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.FCrystal` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/FCrystal/Inverse`.

Notation as in OK. Let (D, φ_D, Fil^•) be a filtered φ-module over K: D a finite-dimensional K_0-vector space, φ_D: φ^*D ≅ D, and Fil^• a finite, exhaustive, separated filtration on D_K = D ⊗_{W(k),φ} K (the Frobenius twist is the prismatic normalisation). Then there is an F-crystal M(D)_{⟨I/p⟩} ∈ Vect^φ(X_qrsp, Δ_•⟨I/p⟩[1/p]), functorial in D, constructed as follows. (a) M_1 = D ⊗_{W(k)} Δ_•{I/p}, a unit F-crystal over Δ_•{I/p}[1/p] with φ induced by φ_D. (b) M_2 = M_1 ⊗_{Δ_•{I/p}, φ̃} Δ_•⟨I/p⟩, a unit F-crystal over Δ_•⟨I/p⟩[1/p]. (c) M_3 = M(D)_{⟨I/p⟩} is the Beauville–Laszlo glueing along the Cartier divisor I = 0 of M_2[1/I] and Fil^0(D_K ⊗_K B_dR) ∈ Vect(X_qrsp, B_dR^+) along M_2[1/I] ⊗ B_dR ≅ D ⊗_{W(k),φ} B_dR ≅ Fil^0(D_K ⊗_K B_dR)[1/I], with φ_{M_3} = φ_{M_2}[1/I]. (d) Analytic continuation: every F-crystal (M, φ_M) over Δ_•⟨I/p⟩[1/p] on X_qrsp extends uniquely to F-crystals over Δ_•⟨φ^n(I)/p⟩[1/p] for all n ≥ 1, compatibly in n; for n = 1 the extension N is glued from φ̃^*M over Δ_•⟨φ(I)/p⟩[1/p, 1/I] and M^∧_I over B_dR^+. The compatible system M(D) = {M(D)_{⟨φ^n(I)/p⟩}}_{n ≥ 1} has value M(D)(Y) on Y = Spf(O_C) an F-crystal on Spa(A_inf) ∖ {p = 0}.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** K is a complete discretely valued field of characteristic 0 with perfect residue field k of characteristic p, O_K its ring of integers, W = W(k), K_0 = W[1/p], C a completed algebraic closure of K, G_K = Gal(K̄/K); X = Spf(O_K), Y = Spf(O_C). O_K and O_C are W-algebras through the unique Frobenius-equivariant section k → O_K/p (the source's Notation 5.1). Filtered φ-modules are those of PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/filtered-phi-n-modules with N = 0, with the filtration placed on the Frobenius twist D ⊗_{W(k),φ} K; no admissibility is assumed in this node. K acts on B_dR^+(R) for R in X_qrsp: K_0 ⊂ Δ_R[1/p] and K/K_0 is finite étale, so K lifts uniquely along B_dR^+(R) → (Δ_R/I)[1/p] ⊃ K by Hensel's lemma. Beauville–Laszlo glueing of vector bundles along a nonzerodivisor is requested from SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.1.

**Construction or proof.**

1. (a): regard (D, φ_D) as an F-crystal of O_Δ[1/p]-modules on Spec(k) and pull back along W(k) → Δ_•{I/p}, a diagram of prisms over k (node crystalline-realization (1)).
2. (b): base change along φ̃: Δ_•{I/p} → Δ_•{φ(I)/p} → Δ_•⟨I/p⟩ (node period-sheaves-qrsp).
3. (c): identify B_dR^+ with Δ_•⟨I/p⟩[1/p]^∧_I (Lemma 6.7, node period-sheaves-qrsp) and glue; the result is a vector bundle over Δ_•⟨I/p⟩[1/p] with M_3[1/I] ≅ M_2[1/I] and (M_3)^∧_I ≅ Fil^0(D_K ⊗_K B_dR).
4. (d): the contracting property of φ: φ̃ maps Δ_•⟨φ^n(I)/p⟩ to Δ_•⟨φ^{n+1}(I)/p⟩, φ^*N = φ̃^*M, and both sides of φ_N: (φ^*N)[1/I] ≅ N[1/I] are identified with (φ̃^*M)[1/I] (the source's Remark 6.6).
5. A partial inverse over the Breuil–Kisin prism is the functor 𝒟 of node breuil-kisin-evaluation.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.7/period-sheaves-qrsp`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-7-period-sheaves-qrsp); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.7/crystalline-realization`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-7-crystalline-realization); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.7/prismatic-f-crystal`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-7-prismatic-f-crystal); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.7/quasisyntomic-crystal-comparison`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-7-quasisyntomic-crystal-comparison); `PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/filtered-phi-n-modules`; `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.1`.

**Consumers.** BS23-FCRYS §6.4: for D weakly admissible the system M(D) is the input of the construction of the F-crystal of a crystalline lattice. BS23-FCRYS Theorem 7.9: the functor 𝒟 on Vect^φ(𝔖⟨I/p⟩[1/p]) is a left inverse of D ↦ M(D)_{⟨I/p⟩}(𝔖). FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory:R07.4/phi-n-nabla-modules: Kisin's module 𝓜(D) over the open unit disc is the analogue over 𝔖, with a connection in place of descent data.

**Planning API.**

- `TauCeti.Prismatic.FCrystal.filteredCrystal` (constructor): The crystal over Δ_•⟨φ^n(I)/p⟩[1/p] underlying M(D).
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.FCrystal.filteredCrystal_rank` (characterisation): Each value of M(D) has constant rank dim_{K_0} D.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.FCrystal.filteredCrystal_restrict` (compatibility): The members of the system M(D) are compatible under Δ_•⟨φ^{n+1}(I)/p⟩ → Δ_•⟨φ^n(I)/p⟩.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.FCrystal.filteredCrystal_frobenius` (structure): The Frobenius on M(D) is φ_(M_2)[1/I] on the generic chart; after Beauville–Laszlo glueing it is an isomorphism (φ^*M_3)[1/I]≃M_3[1/I]. The analytically continued members inherit it, and all restriction maps commute with it.

**Unit tests.**

- `pr7_filtered_crystal_rank_zero` (degenerate): If dim D = 0 then every value of M(D) is the zero module.
- `pr7_filtered_crystal_finite_projective` (compatibility): Every value of M(D) is finite projective.
- `pr7_filtered_crystal_twist` (computation): For D of dimension one every value of M(D) is an invertible module (for φ_D = p^{-1}φ and the filtration jumping at −1 it is the Breuil–Kisin twist).
- `pr7_filtered_crystal_not_integral` (non-example): The construction does not produce a module over Δ_•: the system M(D) lives over the rings Δ_•⟨φ^n(I)/p⟩[1/p], in which p is a unit.
- `pr7_filtered_crystal_jump_minus_one` (computation): For (D,φ_D)=(K_0,p^(-1)φ) with filtration jumping at −1, M_3=I·M_2 and φ(d e)=(φ(d)/(pd))·d e. This gives φ^*M_3≃I^(-1)⊗M_3, the twist {1}; a jump at 0 produces a different modification.

**Acceptance.** D = K_0 with φ and Fil^0 = D_K, Fil^1 = 0: M(D)_{⟨I/p⟩} = Δ_•⟨I/p⟩[1/p]. D = K_0 with φ_D = p^{-1}φ and Fil^{-1} = D_K, Fil^0 = 0: M(D)_{⟨I/p⟩} = Δ_•⟨I/p⟩{1}[1/p], the Breuil–Kisin twist. The rank of M(D) is dim_{K_0} D, and M(D ⊗ D′) = M(D) ⊗ M(D′).

**Prototype boundary.** `pr7_filtered_crystal_jump_minus_one` needs its supplier carrier: R06 supplies the specific one-dimensional filtered φ-module over K_0 with its jump at −1 and φ=p^(-1)φ_K0. The abstract category MF in the fixed geometric adapter does not yet expose this concrete constructor.

**Sources.** [BS23-FCRYS](https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.14735v2), Construction 6.5. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 20. steps (a)–(c). [BS23-FCRYS](https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.14735v2), Remark 6.6. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 21. step (d), the analytic continuation.

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-7-tate-twist-analytic-continuation"></a>

### Analytic continuation for p-adic Tate twists

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.7/tate-twist-analytic-continuation` · theorem. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.FCrystal` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/FCrystal/Inverse`.

Let R be a quasiregular semiperfectoid p-torsion-free O_C-algebra, and n ≥ 0. The natural map Δ_R{n}^{φ=1}[1/p] → Δ_R⟨I/p⟩{n}^{φ=1}[1/p] is an isomorphism. Here (−)^{φ=1} denotes fixed points in the ordinary (non-derived) sense: the elements x of Δ_R{n} (resp. of Δ_R⟨I/p⟩{n}) with φ(x) = x in Δ_R{n}[1/I] (resp. in Δ_R⟨I/p⟩{n}[1/I]).

**Hypotheses and conventions.** R is a p-torsion-free quasiregular semiperfectoid O_C-algebra; the O_C-structure trivialises the twists, Δ_{O_C}{1} ≅ (q − 1)^{-1}Δ_{O_C}. The source states the proposition without a range for n; its proof and its use (the source's Lemma 6.9 (1)) concern n ≥ 0, the range of the Beilinson fibre square, and that range is stated here. The source recalls Q_p(n)(R) with the uncompleted Nygaard-filtered Δ_R; by Bhatt–Lurie Proposition 7.4.6 the fibre of φ_n − 1 is unchanged by Nygaard completion, so this is the complex of PR.4/syntomic-complex. Input from RefinedTraceMethods:RT.3b (Antieau–Mathew–Morrow–Nikolaus, Theorem 6.17 and 6.18–6.21): for p-torsion-free quasisyntomic R, a functorial pullback square in D(Q_p) with top row Q_p(n)(R) → Q_p(n)(R/p) and bottom row (LΩ_R^{≥n})_{Q_p} → (LΩ_R)_{Q_p}, equivalently a fibre sequence Q_p(n)(R) → Q_p(n)(R/p) → (LΩ_R/Fil^n_H LΩ_R)[1/p]; and for R quasiregular semiperfectoid and n > 0 the right vertical map χ_n is injective (for n = 0 the third term of the fibre sequence vanishes and steps 3-5 are not needed) with image the φ = p^n eigenspace of A_crys(R/p)[1/p] = LΩ_R[1/p], so that up to a nonzero scalar it is the forgetful map. Here LΩ_R is p-completed derived de Rham cohomology over Z_p with its Hodge filtration, and the subscript Q_p means p-completion followed by inversion of p. Suspension dictionary: the square comes from the pullback square TC(R; Q_p) → TC(R/p; Q_p), HC^-(R; Q_p) → HP(R; Q_p) by applying τ_{[2n−1, 2n]}; in cyclic-homology terms the cofibre of TC(R; Q_p) → TC(R/p; Q_p) is Σ^2 HC(R; Q_p), and π_{2n} of it is HC_{2n−2} = (LΩ_R/Fil^n_H)[1/p] for these R. The source's introduction writes the third term as HC(R) with the double suspension suppressed (source issue PrismaticCohomology/E76).

**Construction or proof.**

1. H^0(Q_p(n)(R)) → Δ_R{n}^{φ=1}[1/p] is an isomorphism: a φ-fixed element lies in Fil^n_N because the Nygaard filtration of a quasiregular semiperfectoid ring is the φ-preimage of the I-adic filtration (BS22 Definition 12.1, PR.3/nygaard-filtration-qrsp).
2. Δ_{R/p} = Δ_R{I/p}, and H^0(Q_p(n)(R/p)) = (Δ_R{I/p}{n})^{φ=1}[1/p] since inverting p kills the Nygaard graded quotients of Δ_{R/p}. The map b: H^0(Q_p(n)(R)) → H^0(Q_p(n)(R/p)) factors as c ∘ a through Δ_R⟨I/p⟩{n}^{φ=1}[1/p], and a, b, c are injective; so it suffices that d ∘ c = 0, where d is the map to H^0((LΩ_R/Fil^n_H LΩ_R){n}[1/p]) in the exact sequence of the Beilinson fibre square (RT.3b).
3. By the description of χ_n (RT.3b), d is up to a nonzero scalar the forgetful map Q_p(n)(R/p) → Δ_{R/p}[1/p] ≅ LΩ_R[1/p] followed by the projection; so one must show that ((q − 1)^{-n}Δ_R⟨I/p⟩)^{φ=1}[1/p] maps into (q − 1)^{-n}Fil^n_H LΩ_R[1/p].
4. Frobenius induces an injection (LΩ_R/Fil^n_H LΩ_R)[1/p] → B_dR^+(R)/I^n: φ gives Δ_R/Fil^n_N → Δ_R/I^n injective, and (Δ_R/Fil^n_N)[1/p] ≅ (LΩ_R/Fil^n_H)[1/p] by the filtered absolute de Rham comparison (Bhatt–Lurie §5.4, Proposition 5.5.12; PR.5/absolute-nygaard-filtration). Dividing by (q − 1)^n, whose image under φ generates I·B_dR^+(R), gives an injection into I^{-n}B_dR^+(R)/B_dR^+(R).
5. On φ-fixed elements this injection is induced by the natural map (q − 1)^{-n}Δ_R⟨I/p⟩[1/p] → I^{-n}B_dR^+(R) (node period-sheaves-qrsp, Lemma 6.7), which lands in B_dR^+(R) because q − 1 is a unit there; so the composite is zero.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.7/period-sheaves-qrsp`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-7-period-sheaves-qrsp); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.7/f-crystals-over-qrsp`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-7-f-crystals-over-qrsp); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/syntomic-complex`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-4-syntomic-complex); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/nygaard-filtration-qrsp`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-3-nygaard-filtration-qrsp); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/nygaard-graded-pieces`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-3-nygaard-graded-pieces); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/breuil-kisin-twist`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-3-breuil-kisin-twist); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/qrsp-prism`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-2-qrsp-prism); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/pd-envelope-as-delta-envelope`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-pd-envelope-as-delta-envelope); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.5/absolute-nygaard-filtration`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-5-absolute-nygaard-filtration); `RefinedTraceMethods:RT.3b`; `RefinedTraceMethods:RT.6`; `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.4`.

**Acceptance.** R = O_C: both sides are one-dimensional over Q_p, equal to Q_p(n) as G_K-modules. R = O_C: the sequence 0 → Q_p(n) → (B_crys^+)^{φ=p^n} → B_dR^+/Fil^n → 0 is the fundamental exact sequence (PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/fundamental-exact-sequence), which checks the suspension dictionary. For R = O_C and n ≥ 1 the map c is not surjective: its cokernel is B_dR^+/Fil^n.

**Sources.** [BS23-FCRYS](https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.14735v2), Proposition 6.8. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 22. the statement, with the range n ≥ 0 made explicit. [BS23-FCRYS](https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.14735v2), Proposition 6.8, proof. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 22. where the Beilinson fibre square enters. [BS23-FCRYS](https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.14735v2), Proposition 6.8, proof. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 22. the description of the boundary map taken from Antieau–Mathew–Morrow–Nikolaus 6.18–6.21.

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-7-etale-realization-over-breuil-kisin-prism"></a>

### Full faithfulness of the étale realisation over the Breuil–Kisin prism

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.7/etale-realization-over-breuil-kisin-prism` · theorem. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.FCrystal` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/FCrystal/BreuilKisin`.

Notation as in OK, with a uniformizer π, the Breuil–Kisin prism (𝔖, (E(u))) and a compatible system π^♭ of p-power roots of π, K_∞ = K(π^{1/p^∞}). (1) 𝔖[1/E(u)]^∧_p = 𝔖[1/u]^∧_p, a complete discrete valuation ring with uniformizer p and residue field k((u)). (2) The étale realisation T: Vect^φ(𝔖) → Vect^φ(𝔖[1/E(u)]^∧_p), M ↦ M ⊗_𝔖 𝔖[1/E(u)]^∧_p, is fully faithful. (3) Vect^φ(𝔖[1/E(u)]^∧_p) ≃ Rep_{Z_p}(G_{K_∞}): by node laurent-f-crystals-local-systems (1) the category is unchanged by passing to the perfection of (𝔖, (E)), which is A_inf of the completion of O_{K_∞}, and Laurent F-crystals over that perfectoid ring are Z_p-representations of the absolute Galois group of the completion of K_∞, which is G_{K_∞}.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** K is a complete discretely valued field of characteristic 0 with perfect residue field k of characteristic p, O_K its ring of integers, W = W(k), K_0 = W[1/p], C a completed algebraic closure of K, G_K = Gal(K̄/K); X = Spf(O_K), Y = Spf(O_C). O_K and O_C are W-algebras through the unique Frobenius-equivariant section k → O_K/p (the source's Notation 5.1). On effective objects (2) is Kisin's Proposition 2.1.12, which the packet of FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory states as R07.4/kisin-etale-full-faithfulness with Kisin's proof (as repaired in his erratum); (3) is there Fontaine's equivalence R07.4/kummer-etale-phi-modules through the field of norms. This node plans the source's independent proof, which uses neither; the two formulations are identified in node kisin-functor-comparison, and the overlap is reported in the restructure record of the stage. The points and adic spaces used: 𝒴 = Spa(A_inf)^an ∖ {y_crys}, 𝒳 = Spa(𝔖)^an ∖ {x_crys}, π: 𝒴 → 𝒳, y_n = φ^n(y_C) with y_C the Hodge–Tate point, x_n = π(y_n), B = {x_n : n ≥ 1}. For n ≥ 0 the point x_n is 𝔖 → 𝔖 → O_K ⊂ K (first map φ^n); for n < 0 it is 𝔖 → 𝔖/φ^{-n}(E(u))[1/p] (the source prints φ^n; source issue PrismaticCohomology/E74).

**Construction or proof.**

1. Reduction: by internal Hom it suffices that M^{φ=1} → (M[1/E]^∧_p)^{φ=1} is bijective for M ∈ Vect^φ(𝔖); injectivity holds because M is finite free and 𝔖 → 𝔖[1/E]^∧_p is injective.
2. For α in the target, its image in M ⊗_𝔖 W(C^♭) lies in M ⊗_𝔖 A_inf[1/(q−1)] (BMS1 Lemma 4.26, node bkf-modules-comparison (2), applied to M ⊗_𝔖 A_inf).
3. Meromorphy (the source's Lemma 7.7): every f ∈ 𝔖[1/u]^∧_p ∩ A_inf[1/(q−1)] ⊂ W(C^♭) is meromorphic over 𝔖 with poles in a finite subset B′ ⊂ B. Ingredients: the classification of points of Spa(A_inf) (Lemma 7.3); finiteness of B′ = {x_m ∈ B : π^{-1}(x_m) is a single point} by a ramification count (Lemma 7.5); if h ∈ A_inf[1/(q−1)] is entire near every y_n, n ≥ 1, then h ∈ A_inf, because ker(A_inf → W(O_C)) = (q−1) (Lemma 7.6; BMS1 Lemma 3.23); Kedlaya's criterion that a function on 𝒳 which is analytic on 𝒴 is analytic (Kedlaya, Slope filtrations revisited, Definition 2.2.13, Lemma 2.3.5, Remark 2.3.8); and 𝔖 = 𝔖[1/u]^∧_p ∩ A_inf, checked modulo p as k[[u]] = k((u)) ∩ O_{C^♭}.
4. Conclusion: as 𝔖 is a unique factorisation domain, α = β/g with β ∈ M and g ∈ 𝔖 vanishing only at points of B. Iterating the Frobenius, φ_M^r(β ⊗ 1) = (φ^r(g)/g)·β in M[1/I_r], I_r = I·φ(I)⋯φ^{r−1}(I); the ideals I_r are invertible at every x_m, m ≥ 1, and φ^r(g) is invertible at x_m for r large (φ moves a zero at x_k to x_{k−1}); hence α ∈ M^∧_{x_m} for all m ≥ 1 and α ∈ M.
5. (3): the perfection of (𝔖, (E)) is (A_inf(O), ker θ̃) for O the p-completion of O_K[π^{1/p^∞}] (PR.0/prism-perfection, PR.0/perfect-prisms-perfectoid-rings); apply laurent-f-crystals-local-systems (1), (4), Fontaine–Wintenberger for the perfectoid field (PerfectoidSpaces:P3/fontaine-wintenberger) and the equality of the Galois groups of K_∞ and its completion (Krasner; PerfectoidSpaces:P3/henselian-finite-etale-approximation).

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.7/f-crystal-over-prism`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-7-f-crystal-over-prism); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.7/breuil-kisin-and-ainf-covers`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-7-breuil-kisin-and-ainf-covers); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.7/bkf-modules-comparison`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-7-bkf-modules-comparison); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.7/laurent-f-crystals-local-systems`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-7-laurent-f-crystals-local-systems); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/breuil-kisin-prism`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-breuil-kisin-prism); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/prism-perfection`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-prism-perfection); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/perfect-prisms-perfectoid-rings`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-perfect-prisms-perfectoid-rings); `AInfCohomology:AI.2`; `PadicHodgeTheory:P7:annulus-foundations`; `PerfectoidSpaces:P3/fontaine-wintenberger`; [`mathlib:PowerSeries`](#mathlib-powerseries); `PerfectoidSpaces:P3/henselian-finite-etale-approximation`; `PerfectoidSpaces:P3`.

**Acceptance.** M = 𝔖: 𝔖^{φ=1} = Z_p = (𝔖[1/u]^∧_p)^{φ=1}. K = Q_p(p^{1/p}), π = p^{1/p}: f = 1/(u − p) lies in 𝔖⟨p/u^2⟩[1/u] ∩ A_inf[1/(q−1)] and has a simple pole at x_1, so the set B′ is nonempty (the source's Example 7.8); B′ is empty when e(K/K_0) < p. The analogous statement for A_inf fails: Hom(A_inf{1}, A_inf) = (μA_inf)^{φ=1} = 0 although both realisations are free of rank one over Z_p. Over 𝔖 the realisations of 𝔖{1} and 𝔖 are Z_p(1) and Z_p restricted to G_{K_∞}, with no nonzero map between them; the proof uses that u does not divide a power of q − 1 in A_inf.

**Sources.** [BS23-FCRYS](https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.14735v2), Theorem 7.2 and its proof. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 28. statement (2) and the proof planned.
