[BS23-FCRYS](https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.14735v2), Corollary 7.10, proof. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 33. statement (3) is the equivalence used there.

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-7-etale-realization-fully-faithful"></a>

### Full faithfulness of the étale realisation over O_K

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.7/etale-realization-fully-faithful` · theorem. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.FCrystal` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/FCrystal/MainTheorem`.

Notation as in OK. The étale realisation T: Vect^φ(X_Δ, O_Δ) → Vect(X_Δ, O_Δ[1/I_Δ]^∧_p)^{φ=1} ≃ Rep_{Z_p}(G_K) is fully faithful. More precisely: (1) T is faithful over X, over Y = Spf(O_C) and over every term of the Čech nerve Y^{•/X}. (2) For a lattice T_0 in a de Rham representation V of G_K the assignment T_0 ↦ (T_0, D_dR(V) ⊗_K B_dR^+) is compatible, through the functor of Fargues' theorem, with restriction of F-crystals from X to Y and of Laurent F-crystals from X to Y. (3) For M, N ∈ Vect^φ(X_Δ, O_Δ) and a morphism g: T(M) → T(N) there is a unique f: M → N with T(f) = g.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** K is a complete discretely valued field of characteristic 0 with perfect residue field k of characteristic p, O_K its ring of integers, W = W(k), K_0 = W[1/p], C a completed algebraic closure of K, G_K = Gal(K̄/K); X = Spf(O_K), Y = Spf(O_C). O_K and O_C are W-algebras through the unique Frobenius-equivariant section k → O_K/p (the source's Notation 5.1). The proof uses only the full faithfulness part of Fargues' theorem (node bkf-modules-comparison (3)). A second proof, through the Breuil–Kisin prism, is in the source's Remark 5.7: descent along 𝔖^{(•)}, full faithfulness in cosimplicial degree 0 by node etale-realization-over-breuil-kisin-prism, and faithfulness in every degree because 𝔖^{(i)} → 𝔖^{(i)}[1/I]^∧_p is injective.

**Construction or proof.**

1. (1): node f-crystals-over-qrsp (2)–(3) for the p-torsion-free quasiregular semiperfectoid rings O_C ⊗̂_{O_K} … ⊗̂_{O_K} O_C; faithfulness over X follows from that over Y since A_inf covers the final object.
2. (2): the commutative diagram of the source's Construction 5.5, using node crystalline-representation-of-f-crystal (2)–(3) to identify the lattice of M|_Y with D_dR ⊗ B_dR^+.
3. Fullness over Y: g|_Y is a map of finite free Z_p-modules which is G_K-equivariant, hence respects the lattices D_dR(·) ⊗ B_dR^+; by full faithfulness in Fargues' theorem it comes from a unique f_Y: M|_Y → N|_Y.
4. Descent: the two pullbacks a, b of f_Y to Y ×_X Y satisfy T(a) = T(b), both being the pullback of g; by (1) over Y ×_X Y, a = b, and node crystal-descent (3) gives f with f|_Y = f_Y.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.7/f-crystals-over-qrsp`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-7-f-crystals-over-qrsp); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.7/bkf-modules-comparison`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-7-bkf-modules-comparison); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.7/crystalline-representation-of-f-crystal`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-7-crystalline-representation-of-f-crystal); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.7/breuil-kisin-and-ainf-covers`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-7-breuil-kisin-and-ainf-covers); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.7/crystal-descent`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-7-crystal-descent); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.7/etale-realization`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-7-etale-realization); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.7/laurent-f-crystals-local-systems`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-7-laurent-f-crystals-local-systems); `PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/period-functors`; `PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/crystalline-semistable-de-rham-implications`.

**Acceptance.** Hom(O_Δ, O_Δ{n}) = 0 for n ≠ 0, matching Hom_{G_K}(Z_p, Z_p(n)) = 0. End(O_Δ) = Z_p. The statement fails with O_Δ/p-coefficients (node mod-p-full-faithfulness-fails).

**Sources.** [BS23-FCRYS](https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.14735v2), Theorem 5.6, proof of full faithfulness. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 17. the theorem and the proof planned. [BS23-FCRYS](https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.14735v2), Construction 5.5. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 17. step (2) and fullness over Spf(O_C). [BS23-FCRYS](https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.14735v2), Remark 5.7. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 17. the second proof through the Breuil–Kisin prism.

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-7-descent-data-boundedness"></a>

### Boundedness of descent data at the boundary of the open unit disc

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.7/descent-data-boundedness` · theorem. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.FCrystal` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/FCrystal/Inverse`.

Notation as in OK; R = O_C ⊗̂_{O_K} O_C, and q_1, q_2 ∈ Δ_R are the images of q ∈ A_inf under the two structure maps. (A) (the source's Lemma 6.9) (1) Δ_R[1/(p(q_1−1)(q_2−1))]^{φ=1} → Δ_R⟨I/p⟩[1/(p(q_1−1)(q_2−1))]^{φ=1} is an isomorphism on H^0. (2) (q_1−1)(q_2−1) is invertible in Δ_R⟨p/(q_1−1)^p⟩[1/p]. (3) 0 → Δ_R → Δ_R⟨(q_1−1)^p/p⟩ ⊕ Δ_R⟨p/(q_1−1)^p⟩ → Δ_R⟨p/(q_1−1)^p, (q_1−1)^p/p⟩ → 0 is exact. (B) (the source's Proposition 6.10) Let M ∈ Vect^φ(A_inf) and suppose M⟨I/p⟩[1/p] ∈ Vect^φ(A_inf⟨I/p⟩[1/p]) is given a descent datum with respect to Y → X, that is a lift to Vect^φ(X_qrsp, Δ_•⟨I/p⟩[1/p]). Then the descent datum extends uniquely to M[1/p] ∈ Vect^φ(A_inf[1/p]): the isomorphism α_{⟨I/p⟩}: p_1^*M⟨I/p⟩[1/p] ≅ p_2^*M⟨I/p⟩[1/p] over Δ_R⟨I/p⟩[1/p] is the base change of a unique isomorphism α: p_1^*M[1/p] ≅ p_2^*M[1/p] over Δ_R[1/p], and α is φ-equivariant and satisfies the cocycle condition.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** K is a complete discretely valued field of characteristic 0 with perfect residue field k of characteristic p, O_K its ring of integers, W = W(k), K_0 = W[1/p], C a completed algebraic closure of K, G_K = Gal(K̄/K); X = Spf(O_K), Y = Spf(O_C). O_K and O_C are W-algebras through the unique Frobenius-equivariant section k → O_K/p (the source's Notation 5.1). M is an F-crystal over A_inf = Δ_{O_C} (a finite free Breuil–Kisin–Fargues module); the descent datum is given only over the rational localisation with p inverted. The rings Δ_R⟨f/g⟩ are p-completed (resp. (q_1−1)-completed) rational localisations as in the source: Δ_R⟨p/(q_1−1)^p⟩ = (Δ_R[z]/(z(q_1−1)^p − p))^∧_{(q_1−1)}.

**Construction or proof.**

1. (A1): Δ_R{2n} ≅ (q_1−1)^{-n}(q_2−1)^{-n}Δ_R by base change of Δ_{O_C}{n} ≅ (q−1)^{-n}Δ_{O_C} along the two maps; pass to the colimit over n and apply node tate-twist-analytic-continuation to the twists.
2. (A2): q_1 − 1 is invertible because (q_1−1)^p divides p. For q_2 − 1 show A = Δ_R⟨p/(q_1−1)^p⟩/(q_2−1) is an F_p-algebra: [p]_{q_1} = u·[p]_{q_2} for a unit u (Δ_R is a prismatic envelope of A_inf ⊗ A_inf), and [p]_{q_i} ≡ (q_i−1)^{p−1} modulo p, so (q_1−1)^p = p(q_1−1)x modulo (q_2−1); then z(q_1−1)^p − p = p(ε − 1) with ε = z(q_1−1)x topologically nilpotent, so p = 0 in A.
3. (A3): for Z_p[u] the Mayer–Vietoris sequence of the blow-up at (p, u) is 0 → Z_p[u] → Z_p[u][u/p] ⊕ Z_p[u][p/u] → Z_p[u][p/u, u/p] → 0; base change it (p, u)-completely along the (p, u)-completely flat map Z_p[u] → A_inf → Δ_R, u ↦ (q_1−1)^p; the terms stay discrete.
4. (B): it suffices to show α_{⟨I/p⟩} carries p_1^*M[1/p] into p_2^*M[1/p] (apply the same to the inverse); φ-equivariance and the cocycle condition follow because Δ_•[1/p] → Δ_•⟨I/p⟩[1/p] is injective on X_qrsp. By analytic continuation (node filtered-phi-module-to-crystal (d)) the datum extends over Δ_R⟨φ(I)/p⟩[1/p], hence, since φ(I) ⊂ pΔ_R⟨(q_1−1)^p/p⟩, to a φ-equivariant map α_1 over Δ_R⟨(q_1−1)^p/p⟩[1/p].
5. Trivialise M[1/(q−1)] ≅ T ⊗_{Z_p} A_inf[1/(q−1)] φ-equivariantly (node bkf-modules-comparison (2)); in a basis of T the matrix of α_{⟨I/p⟩} has φ-fixed entries in Δ_R⟨I/p⟩[1/(p(q_1−1)(q_2−1))], which lie in Δ_R[1/(p(q_1−1)(q_2−1))] by (A1) and so in Δ_R⟨p/(q_1−1)^p⟩[1/p] by (A2); this defines α_2 there, compatible with α_1 on the overlap. Tensor the sequence (A3)[1/p] with the finite projective module Hom(p_1^*M[1/p], p_2^*M[1/p]) to glue α_1 and α_2 to α.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.7/tate-twist-analytic-continuation`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-7-tate-twist-analytic-continuation); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.7/filtered-phi-module-to-crystal`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-7-filtered-phi-module-to-crystal); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.7/period-sheaves-qrsp`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-7-period-sheaves-qrsp); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.7/bkf-modules-comparison`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-7-bkf-modules-comparison); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.7/breuil-kisin-and-ainf-covers`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-7-breuil-kisin-and-ainf-covers); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.7/quasisyntomic-crystal-comparison`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-7-quasisyntomic-crystal-comparison); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/breuil-kisin-twist`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-3-breuil-kisin-twist); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/regular-prismatic-envelopes`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-regular-prismatic-envelopes); `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`.

**Acceptance.** M = A_inf: the descent datum is multiplication by a φ-fixed unit of Δ_R⟨I/p⟩[1/p], which lies in Δ_R[1/p]. M = A_inf{1}: in the bases (q_i − 1)^{-1} the datum of the crystal O_Δ{1} is a unit c of Δ_R with φ(c) = c·[p]_{q_2}/[p]_{q_1}. Without a Frobenius structure the extension fails: a general element of Δ_R⟨I/p⟩[1/p] is not in Δ_R[1/p].

**Sources.** [BS23-FCRYS](https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.14735v2), Proposition 6.10 and its proof. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 25. statement (B) and its proof. [BS23-FCRYS](https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.14735v2), Lemma 6.9 and its proof. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 24. statement (A).

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-7-weakly-admissible-extension-over-ainf"></a>

### Weak admissibility gives a Breuil–Kisin–Fargues module

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.7/weakly-admissible-extension-over-ainf` · theorem. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.FCrystal` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/FCrystal/Inverse`.

Notation as in OK. Let (D, φ_D, Fil^•) be a weakly admissible filtered φ-module over K and M(D)(Y) the F-crystal on Spa(A_inf) ∖ {p = 0} of node filtered-phi-module-to-crystal. Then: (1) the base change M(D)(Y)_ℛ to the Robba ring ℛ of A_inf (Fargues–Fontaine, Definition 1.8.1; the extended Robba ring R̃ of Scholze–Weinstein, Berkeley lectures, Definition 13.4.3) is a trivial φ-module; (2) hence it extends, as a φ-module, to the integral Robba ring ℛ^int (R̃^int of Berkeley Definition 12.3.1); (3) hence M(D)(Y) extends to an F-crystal M′ over A_inf, i.e. a finite free Breuil–Kisin–Fargues module M′ with M′⟨φ^n(I)/p⟩[1/p] ≅ M(D)_{⟨φ^n(I)/p⟩}(Y) compatibly with φ for all n ≥ 1. The argument gives existence; it does not establish uniqueness of an integral extension. The prescribed restriction away from p=0 is fixed.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** K is a complete discretely valued field of characteristic 0 with perfect residue field k of characteristic p, O_K its ring of integers, W = W(k), K_0 = W[1/p], C a completed algebraic closure of K, G_K = Gal(K̄/K); X = Spf(O_K), Y = Spf(O_C). O_K and O_C are W-algebras through the unique Frobenius-equivariant section k → O_K/p (the source's Notation 5.1). Weak admissibility is that of PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/weak-admissibility for the filtered φ-module with filtration on D ⊗_{W(k),φ} K. Inputs from VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB2:classification (red-team finding RT-AREA-padic-2/30 (b)), cited as the source prints them: Fargues–Fontaine, Courbes et fibrés vectoriels en théorie de Hodge p-adique, Corollary 11.2.22 (φ-modules over ℛ are vector bundles on the Fargues–Fontaine curve X_FF), Proposition 10.5.6 (weakly admissible implies semistable of slope 0 for the associated bundle), Theorem 8.2.10 (1) (semistable bundles of slope 0 are trivial). Inputs from AInfCohomology:AI.2: Berkeley lectures Theorem 14.2.1 (F-crystals on Spec(A_inf) and on Spa(A_inf) ∖ {x_k} agree) and the passage from a φ-module over ℛ^int to a φ-bundle near p = 0. The argument is the A_inf-variant of Kisin's (FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory:R07.4/weakly-admissible-slope-zero), which works over the Robba ring of 𝔖 with Kedlaya's slope filtration; that node is not used here.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Identify φ-modules over ℛ with vector bundles on X_FF (Fargues–Fontaine Corollary 11.2.22) and check that the bundle attached to M(D)(Y)_ℛ is the modification of the bundle E(D, φ_D) at the point ∞ by the lattice Fil^0(D_K ⊗_K B_dR), i.e. the bundle Fargues–Fontaine attach to (D, φ_D, Fil^•): this is the matching of constructions, read off from step (c) of node filtered-phi-module-to-crystal.
2. By weak admissibility and Fargues–Fontaine Proposition 10.5.6 this bundle is semistable of slope 0; by Theorem 8.2.10 (1) (VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB2:classification/dieudonne-manin-classification-of-bundles) it is trivial. Hence (1).
3. A trivial φ-module over ℛ has the φ-stable lattice spanned by a φ-fixed basis over ℛ^int; this gives (2).
4. Glue M(D)(Y) on Spa(A_inf) ∖ {p = 0} with the φ-module over ℛ^int near p = 0 to an F-crystal on Spa(A_inf) ∖ {x_k}, and extend over the closed point by Berkeley Theorem 14.2.1. This gives (3).

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.7/filtered-phi-module-to-crystal`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-7-filtered-phi-module-to-crystal); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.7/period-sheaves-qrsp`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-7-period-sheaves-qrsp); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.7/bkf-modules-comparison`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-7-bkf-modules-comparison); `VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB2:classification`; `VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB2:classification/dieudonne-manin-classification-of-bundles`; `AInfCohomology:AI.2`; `PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/weak-admissibility`; `PadicHodgeTheory:P7/extended-robba-ring-with-galois-action`.

**Acceptance.** D = K_0 with φ and trivial filtration: M′ = A_inf. D of dimension one with φ_D = p^{-1}φ and filtration jumping at −1 (weakly admissible): M′ = A_inf{1}. D of dimension one with φ_D = p^{-1}φ and filtration jumping at 0 (not weakly admissible): the bundle on X_FF has degree ±1, so it is not trivial, and M(D)(Y) does not extend over A_inf.

**Sources.** [BS23-FCRYS](https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.14735v2), Section 6.4, proof of essential surjectivity, second paragraph.  the statement and the argument planned; the references to Fargues–Fontaine are those printed there. [BS23-FCRYS](https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.14735v2), Section 6.4, proof of essential surjectivity, second paragraph.  where weak admissibility is used.

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-7-crystalline-lattice-to-f-crystal"></a>

### The prismatic F-crystal of a crystalline lattice

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.7/crystalline-lattice-to-f-crystal` · construction. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.FCrystal` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/FCrystal/Inverse`.

Notation as in OK. For L ∈ Rep^crys_{Z_p}(G_K) let (D, φ_D, Fil^•) be the weakly admissible filtered φ-module attached to L[1/p] (Fontaine's D_crys, in the Frobenius-twisted normalisation of node crystalline-representation-of-f-crystal). There is a prismatic F-crystal 𝔐(L) = M(D)_int ∈ Vect^φ(X_qrsp, Δ_•) ≃ Vect^φ(X_Δ, O_Δ) such that: (a) 𝔐(L)(A_inf) = M′ is a Breuil–Kisin–Fargues module with M′⟨φ^n(I)/p⟩[1/p] ≅ M(D)_{⟨φ^n(I)/p⟩}(Y) for n ≥ 1; (b) the descent datum of 𝔐(L) over Δ_{O_C ⊗̂ O_C} restricts, after inverting p and passing to Δ_•⟨I/p⟩, to that of M(D)_{⟨I/p⟩}; (c) T(𝔐(L)) ≅ L as G_K-representations. The assignment L ↦ 𝔐(L) is functorial and quasi-inverse to the étale realisation.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** K is a complete discretely valued field of characteristic 0 with perfect residue field k of characteristic p, O_K its ring of integers, W = W(k), K_0 = W[1/p], C a completed algebraic closure of K, G_K = Gal(K̄/K); X = Spf(O_K), Y = Spf(O_C). O_K and O_C are W-algebras through the unique Frobenius-equivariant section k → O_K/p (the source's Notation 5.1). L is a finite free Z_p-module with continuous G_K-action and L[1/p] crystalline; D_crys(L[1/p]) is weakly admissible (PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/admissible-implies-weakly-admissible); the converse direction of Colmez–Fontaine is not used. Step 3 below uses, for R = O_C ⊗̂_{O_K} O_C, that Δ_{R,perf} is almost isomorphic to Cont(G_K, A_inf); the source asserts this without proof or reference (source issue PrismaticCohomology/E78), and it is recorded as a gap of this stage.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Step 1 (bounded crystal): M(D) (node filtered-phi-module-to-crystal) has value on Y extending to M′ over A_inf (node weakly-admissible-extension-over-ainf); by node descent-data-boundedness the descent datum of M(D)_{⟨I/p⟩} extends to M′[1/p], giving M(D)_bdd ∈ Vect^φ(X_qrsp, Δ_•[1/p]) with M(D)_bdd(Y) = M′[1/p].
2. Step 2 (Galois-stable lattice): M′[1/I]^∧_p = T ⊗_{Z_p} A_inf[1/I]^∧_p with T finite free over Z_p (node laurent-f-crystals-local-systems (4)); after inverting p the left side is the value on Y of a crystal on X, so T[1/p] is a G_K-representation. Choose a G_K-stable lattice L′ ⊂ T[1/p] and modify M′ along {p = 0} ⊂ Spec(A_inf) ∖ {x_k} by Beauville–Laszlo glueing, extending over x_k by node bkf-modules-comparison (4), so that T = L′; then M′ carries a G_K-equivariant structure extending that of M′[1/p].
3. Step 3 (integrality of the descent datum): α: p_1^*M′[1/p] ≅ p_2^*M′[1/p] carries p_1^*M′ onto p_2^*M′. As (p, I) is a regular sequence in Δ_R (R = O_C ⊗̂_{O_K} O_C), sections of vector bundles extend over V(p, I); the claim is clear after inverting p, and by Beauville–Laszlo glueing it remains to check it over Δ_R[1/I]^∧_p. There Vect^φ(Δ_R[1/I]^∧_p) → Vect^φ(Δ_{R,perf}[1/I]^∧_p) is fully faithful, also after inverting p (node artin-schreier-riemann-hilbert (2)), and Δ_{R,perf} is almost isomorphic to Cont(G_K, A_inf); inverting I and p-completing turns almost isomorphisms into isomorphisms, and the claim becomes the G_K-stability of the lattice M′[1/I]^∧_p.
4. Step 4 (the lattice is L): steps 1–3 give M(D)_int ∈ Vect^φ(X_qrsp, Δ_•) with T(M(D)_int) = L′. By the argument of node crystalline-representation-of-f-crystal and (b), T(M(D)_int)[1/p] ≅ L[1/p]; repeat step 2 with L′ = L.
5. Functoriality and the quasi-inverse property follow from full faithfulness (node etale-realization-fully-faithful).

- `TauCeti.Prismatic.FCrystal.latticeFCrystal` (constructor): The prismatic F-crystal 𝔐(L) of a crystalline lattice L.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.FCrystal.latticeFCrystal_realization` (characterisation): The étale realisation of 𝔐(L) is isomorphic to L as a representation of G_K.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.FCrystal.latticeFCrystal_unique` (universal-property): A prismatic F-crystal whose étale realisation is isomorphic to L is isomorphic to 𝔐(L).

**Unit tests.**

- `pr7_lattice_rank` (compatibility): The value of 𝔐(L) on the Breuil–Kisin prism is free of rank rk_{Z_p} L.
- `pr7_lattice_twist` (computation): If L is isomorphic to the étale realisation of O_Δ{n} (that is, L ≅ Z_p(n)), then 𝔐(L) is isomorphic to O_Δ{n}.
- `pr7_lattice_hom` (characterisation): Morphisms 𝔐(L) → 𝔐(L′) correspond bijectively to G_K-equivariant maps L → L′.
- `pr7_lattice_not_all_representations` (non-example): Not every Z_p-representation of G_K is the étale realisation of a prismatic F-crystal: the lattice of a ramified character of finite order is not.

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-7-crystalline-lattices-theorem"></a>

### Prismatic F-crystals on O_K are lattices in crystalline representations

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.7/crystalline-lattices-theorem` · theorem. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.FCrystal` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/FCrystal/MainTheorem`.

Let K be a complete discretely valued field of mixed characteristic (0, p) with perfect residue field, X = Spf(O_K), and Rep^crys_{Z_p}(G_K) the category of finite free Z_p-modules T with a continuous G_K-action such that T[1/p] is crystalline. The étale realisation functor T: Vect^φ(X_Δ, O_Δ) → Rep^crys_{Z_p}(G_K) is an equivalence of symmetric monoidal categories, with quasi-inverse L ↦ 𝔐(L). Under it rank corresponds to rank, O_Δ{n} to Z_p(n), and D_crys(T(E)[1/p]) ≅ E(W(k))[1/p].

**Hypotheses and conventions.** K is complete, discretely valued, of characteristic 0 with perfect residue field of characteristic p; the residue field need not be finite. Coefficients are finite locally free over O_Δ and lattices are finite free over Z_p. The analogue with O_Δ/p-coefficients is false (node mod-p-full-faithfulness-fails), and no classification of torsion or derived Galois representations is claimed; a statement about F-gauges needs a separate source theorem. In the source this is Theorem 5.6 (Theorem 1.2 of the introduction); the atlas stage text cites the same number.

**Construction or proof.**

1. T takes values in crystalline lattices: node crystalline-representation-of-f-crystal.
2. T is fully faithful: node etale-realization-fully-faithful (descent along Spf(O_C) → Spf(O_K) and the full faithfulness part of Fargues' theorem).
3. T is essentially surjective, with explicit quasi-inverse: node crystalline-lattice-to-f-crystal, which uses the filtered φ-module construction, the Fargues–Fontaine classification (node weakly-admissible-extension-over-ainf) and the boundedness of descent data (node descent-data-boundedness, resting on the Beilinson fibre square).
4. Symmetric monoidality is that of node etale-realization.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.7/crystalline-representation-of-f-crystal`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-7-crystalline-representation-of-f-crystal); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.7/etale-realization-fully-faithful`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-7-etale-realization-fully-faithful); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.7/crystalline-lattice-to-f-crystal`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-7-crystalline-lattice-to-f-crystal); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.7/etale-realization`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-7-etale-realization); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.7/prismatic-f-crystal`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-7-prismatic-f-crystal); `PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/admissible-representations`.

**Acceptance.** Rank one: invertible prismatic F-crystals on Spf(O_K) correspond to crystalline characters G_K → Z_p^×; O_Δ{n} ↔ χ_cyc^n. For a proper smooth formal scheme over O_K whose special fibre has torsion-free crystalline cohomology, the F-crystal H^i(R f_* O_Δ) corresponds to the lattice H^i_ét(X_C, Z_p) (the source's Example 4.6 with BMS1 Theorem 14.5). K = Q_p: End of the unit object is Z_p on both sides.

**Sources.** [BS23-FCRYS](https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.14735v2), Theorem 5.6. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 17. the main theorem. [BS23-FCRYS](https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.14735v2), Introduction, proof strategy after Theorem 1.2. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 2. the route of the proof planned in the three prerequisite nodes.

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-7-breuil-kisin-evaluation"></a>

### Evaluation at the Breuil–Kisin prism: Kisin's full faithfulness theorems

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.7/breuil-kisin-evaluation` · theorem. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.FCrystal` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/FCrystal/BreuilKisin`.

Notation as in node etale-realization-over-breuil-kisin-prism. Let D_𝔖: Rep^crys_{Z_p}(G_K) → Vect^φ(𝔖) be the composite of the quasi-inverse 𝔐 of the étale realisation (node crystalline-lattices-theorem) with evaluation at (𝔖, (E(u))) ∈ X_Δ. (1) D_𝔖 is fully faithful. (2) The composite of D_𝔖 with Vect^φ(𝔖) → Vect^φ(𝔖[1/E(u)]^∧_p) ≃ Rep_{Z_p}(G_{K_∞}) is restriction along G_{K_∞} ⊂ G_K; hence the restriction functor Rep^crys_{Z_p}(G_K) → Rep_{Z_p}(G_{K_∞}) is fully faithful (Breuil's conjecture, proved by Kisin). (3) Rationally, the composite Rep^crys_{Z_p}(G_K)[1/p] → Vect^φ(𝔖)[1/p] → Vect^φ(𝔖⟨I/p⟩[1/p]) → MF^φ(K), the last functor being the functor 𝒟 below, is Fontaine's D_crys in the Frobenius-twisted normalisation. (4) Dependence on the uniformizer: for uniformizers π, π′ with compatible systems of p-power roots, the maps of prisms (𝔖_π, (E)) → (A_inf, ker θ̃) ← (𝔖_{π′}, (E′)) give D_{𝔖_π}(L) ⊗_{𝔖_π} A_inf ≅ 𝔐(L)(A_inf) ≅ D_{𝔖_{π′}}(L) ⊗_{𝔖_{π′}} A_inf, equivariantly for φ and G_K (Liu's compatibility).

**Hypotheses and conventions.** K is a complete discretely valued field of characteristic 0 with perfect residue field k of characteristic p, O_K its ring of integers, W = W(k), K_0 = W[1/p], C a completed algebraic closure of K, G_K = Gal(K̄/K); X = Spf(O_K), Y = Spf(O_C). O_K and O_C are W-algebras through the unique Frobenius-equivariant section k → O_K/p (the source's Notation 5.1). The target Vect^φ(𝔖) depends on π; the equivalence of node crystalline-lattices-theorem does not. The proof of (1) uses the main theorem, Fontaine's full faithfulness of D_crys and two elementary lemmas of Kisin on Frobenius modules over a disc (Kisin, Crystalline representations and F-crystals, Lemma 1.2.6 and Proposition 1.2.8), which are proved here over 𝔖⟨I/p⟩[1/p]; it does not use Kisin's connection N_∇, Kedlaya's slope filtration or the field of norms. In the version read this statement is Theorem 7.9 (with Corollary 7.10 and Remark 7.12); Theorem 7.2 is node etale-realization-over-breuil-kisin-prism.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Faithfulness: (𝔖, (E)) covers the final object of Shv(X_Δ) (node breuil-kisin-and-ainf-covers).
2. The functor 𝒟: Vect^φ(𝔖⟨I/p⟩[1/p]) → MF^φ(K). For (𝔐, φ_𝔐) put D(𝔐) = 𝔐 ⊗ K_0 along u ↦ 0, an F-isocrystal. Since φ^*𝔐 is a unit φ-module over 𝔖⟨I/p⟩[1/p] (φ(E) is invertible there), Dwork's trick gives a unique φ-equivariant isomorphism φ^*D(𝔐) ⊗_{K_0} 𝔖⟨I/p⟩[1/p] ≅ φ^*𝔐 lifting the identity modulo u; base change to 𝔖[1/p]^∧_I[1/I], compose with φ_𝔐 and transport the I-adic filtration of 𝔐 ⊗ 𝔖[1/p]^∧_I to a filtration on D(𝔐) ⊗_{K_0,φ} K. 𝒟 is faithful because it recovers φ^*𝔐, and it is a left inverse of D ↦ M(D)_{⟨I/p⟩}(𝔖) (node filtered-phi-module-to-crystal).
3. Rational full faithfulness: by the previous step and the construction of 𝔐(L) the composite in (3) is D_crys, which is fully faithful (PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/dst-exact-tensor-fully-faithful); every functor in the composite is faithful (𝔖 → 𝔖⟨I/p⟩[1/p] is injective), so D_𝔖[1/p] is fully faithful.
4. Integrality: for α: D_𝔖(L) → D_𝔖(L′) some p^nα = D_𝔖(a); the forgetful functor to Z_p-modules factors through D_𝔖 followed by the étale realisation over 𝔖 (statement (2), which holds by the crystal property for 𝔖 → A_inf and node laurent-f-crystals-local-systems), so a is divisible by p^n as a map of Z_p-modules, hence of representations. This proves (1).
5. (2): the restriction functor is the composite of D_𝔖, the fully faithful functor of node etale-realization-over-breuil-kisin-prism (2) and the equivalence (3) there. (4): the crystal property of 𝔐(L) for the two maps of prisms, and the G_K-action on the object (A_inf, ker θ̃).

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.7/crystalline-lattices-theorem`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-7-crystalline-lattices-theorem); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.7/crystalline-lattice-to-f-crystal`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-7-crystalline-lattice-to-f-crystal); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.7/breuil-kisin-and-ainf-covers`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-7-breuil-kisin-and-ainf-covers); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.7/filtered-phi-module-to-crystal`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-7-filtered-phi-module-to-crystal); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.7/period-sheaves-qrsp`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-7-period-sheaves-qrsp); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.7/etale-realization-over-breuil-kisin-prism`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-7-etale-realization-over-breuil-kisin-prism); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.7/laurent-f-crystals-local-systems`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-7-laurent-f-crystals-local-systems); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.7/f-crystal-over-prism`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-7-f-crystal-over-prism); `PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/dst-exact-tensor-fully-faithful`; `PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/period-functors`; `PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/filtered-phi-n-modules`.

**Acceptance.** D_𝔖(Z_p) = (𝔖, φ); D_𝔖(Z_p(1)) = 𝔖{1}, free of rank one with Frobenius a unit multiple of E(u)^{-1}φ. D_𝔖 is not essentially surjective: an object of Vect^φ(𝔖) is in the image exactly when it carries a descent datum over 𝔖^{(1)}. For K = Q_p and π = p versus π′ = −p the modules D_𝔖(L) differ, but their base changes to A_inf agree.

**Sources.** [BS23-FCRYS](https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.14735v2), Theorem 7.9 and its proof. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 31. statement (1) and the proof planned. [BS23-FCRYS](https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.14735v2), Theorem 7.9, remark before the proof. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 31. the inputs of the proof. <a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-7-mod-p-full-faithfulness-fails"></a>

### Failure of full faithfulness with mod p coefficients

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.7/mod-p-full-faithfulness-fails` · application. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.FCrystal` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/FCrystal/MainTheorem`.

Let K = Q_p and X = Spf(Z_p). The invertible F-crystal E = O_Δ{p−1}/p ∈ Vect^φ(X_Δ, O_Δ/p) has étale realisation T(E) = Z/p(p−1) ≅ Z/p, the trivial local system, but E is not isomorphic to the unit object O_Δ/p; in fact E ≅ I_Δ^{-1}/p as O_Δ/p-modules, and I_Δ/p is a non-trivial invertible O_Δ/p-module. Hence the étale realisation Vect^φ(X_Δ, O_Δ/p) → Vect(X_Δ, O_Δ[1/I_Δ]/p)^{φ=1} is not fully faithful, and the analogue of node crystalline-lattices-theorem with mod p coefficients is false. More generally the stage makes no claim that finite locally free prismatic F-crystals with torsion or derived coefficients classify torsion or derived Galois representations.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** X = Spf(Z_p); any prime p. The source attributes the failure to the fact that sections of vector bundles on Spec(A_inf/p) change when the closed point is removed, unlike on Spec(A_inf) (Kedlaya), which is what full faithfulness in Fargues' theorem uses. The source refers the Sen-operator computation to Bhatt–Lurie §3.5; this plan imports the corresponding calculation from PR.5/hodge-tate-divisor.

**Construction or proof.**

1. T is symmetric monoidal and T(O_Δ{1}) = Z_p(1) (node etale-realization), so T(E) = Z/p(p−1), which is trivial because χ_cyc^{p−1} ≡ 1 modulo p.
2. O_Δ{p}/p ≅ φ^*O_Δ{1}/p because the Frobenius pullback of an invertible module over an F_p-algebra is its p-th tensor power, and φ^*O_Δ{1} ≅ I_Δ^{-1} ⊗ O_Δ{1} (PR.3/breuil-kisin-twist); hence E = O_Δ{p}/p ⊗ O_Δ{−1}/p ≅ I_Δ^{-1}/p.
3. I_Δ/p is not trivial: restrict to the Hodge–Tate locus; I_Δ/p ⊗ Ō_Δ/p = Ō_Δ{1}/p carries the Sen operator with weight 1 and Ō_Δ/p with weight 0 (Bhatt–Lurie §3.5; PR.5/hodge-tate-divisor, PR.5/prismatic-crystals-on-wcart), and 1 ≠ 0 in F_p.

**Direct prerequisites.** [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.7/prismatic-f-crystal`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-7-prismatic-f-crystal); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.7/etale-realization`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-7-etale-realization); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.7/crystalline-lattices-theorem`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-7-crystalline-lattices-theorem); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/breuil-kisin-twist`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-3-breuil-kisin-twist); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.5/hodge-tate-divisor`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-5-hodge-tate-divisor); [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.5/prismatic-crystals-on-wcart`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-5-prismatic-crystals-on-wcart).

**Acceptance.** p = 2: E = O_Δ{1}/2 has trivial realisation Z/2(1) ≅ Z/2 and is not trivial. With Z_p-coefficients the same twist O_Δ{p−1} is distinguished from O_Δ by its realisation Z_p(p−1). The correct torsion and derived objects are expected to be perfect complexes on Drinfeld's stack Σ″ (F-gauges), which also record the Nygaard filtration; none is planned in this stage.

**Sources.** [BS23-FCRYS](https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.14735v2), Remark 5.8. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 18. the counterexample and its proof. [BS23-FCRYS](https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.14735v2), Introduction, footnote to Theorem 1.2. Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 2. the non-claim about torsion and derived coefficients.

<a id="prismaticcohomology-pr-7-kisin-functor-comparison"></a>

### Comparison with Kisin's modules of finite E-height

`PrismaticCohomology:PR.7/kisin-functor-comparison` · comparison. Proposed namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.FCrystal` in `TauCeti/Prismatic/FCrystal/BreuilKisin`.

Notation as in node breuil-kisin-evaluation; Kisin's objects are those of the packet of FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory (stage R07.4), with Hodge–Tate weights normalised by HT(χ_cyc) = +1. (1) Rings: 𝔖, φ, E(u) are those of R07.4/bk-coefficient-rings, and the ring 𝒪_ℰ there is 𝔖[1/E(u)]^∧_p. Embeddings: R07.4 uses ι_K: 𝔖 → A_inf, u ↦ [π̃], compatible with θ; the map of prisms (𝔖, (E)) → (A_inf, ker θ̃) of node breuil-kisin-and-ainf-covers is ι = φ ∘ ι_K = ι_K ∘ φ_𝔖 (u ↦ [π̃]^p, Frobenius on W(k)). For M ∈ Vect^φ(𝔖), M ⊗_{𝔖,ι} W(C^♭) = φ^*(M ⊗_{𝔖,ι_K} W(C^♭)), and φ_M is a φ- and G_{K_∞}-equivariant isomorphism from it to M ⊗_{𝔖,ι_K} W(C^♭); the étale realisation of PR.7 is identified with Fontaine's functor through this isomorphism. (2) Modules: the effective objects of Vect^φ(𝔖) are the objects of Mod^φ_{/𝔖} (finite free, finite E-height) of R07.4/kisin-modules; every object of Vect^φ(𝔖) becomes effective after replacing φ_M by E(u)^h φ_M, which changes no Hom group. Vect^φ(𝔖[1/E]^∧_p) is the category of finite free étale φ-modules over 𝒪_ℰ, and the equivalence with Rep_{Z_p}(G_{K_∞}) of node etale-realization-over-breuil-kisin-prism (3) is Fontaine's covariant functor of R07.4/kummer-etale-phi-modules; Kisin's contravariant V_𝔖(𝔐) = Hom_{𝔖,φ}(𝔐, 𝔖^ur) is the dual of the étale realisation of 𝔐. Under this dictionary statement (2) of node etale-realization-over-breuil-kisin-prism, on effective objects, is R07.4/kisin-etale-full-faithfulness. (3) Lattices: for L ∈ Rep^crys_{Z_p}(G_K), D_𝔖(L) is effective exactly when the Hodge–Tate weights of L[1/p] are ≤ 0; in that case D_𝔖(L) is the 𝔖-lattice of finite E-height in the étale φ-module of L|_{G_{K_∞}}, unique by R07.4/finite-height-lattices (1), so D_𝔖(L) is Kisin's module 𝔐 with V_𝔖(𝔐) ≅ L^∨|_{G_{K_∞}} (R07.4/semistable-finite-height (b) for the lattice L^∨, of weights ≥ 0). For general L twist by O_Δ{n}. (4) Consequently node breuil-kisin-evaluation (1) and (2) are integral forms, for all Hodge–Tate weights, of R07.4/kisin-crystalline-embedding restricted to N = 0 and of R07.4/crystalline-restriction-full-faithfulness.

**Hypotheses and conventions.** K is a complete discretely valued field of characteristic 0 with perfect residue field k of characteristic p, O_K its ring of integers, W = W(k), K_0 = W[1/p], C a completed algebraic closure of K, G_K = Gal(K̄/K); X = Spf(O_K), Y = Spf(O_C). O_K and O_C are W-algebras through the unique Frobenius-equivariant section k → O_K/p (the source's Notation 5.1). Red-team findings RT-AREA-padic-2/4 and RT-AREA-padic-2/30 (c): the comparison rests on four targets of R07.4, which its packet now states as nodes: the Kummer-tower field of norms and Fontaine's étale φ-module equivalence for G_{K_∞} (kummer-etale-phi-modules), modules of finite E-height (kisin-modules, phi-n-nabla-modules), the slope-zero characterisation of weak admissibility (weakly-admissible-slope-zero), and the lattice functor with full faithfulness of restriction to G_{K_∞} (finite-height-lattices, semistable-finite-height, crystalline-restriction-full-faithfulness). What is still requested from the stage is listed in the requests of this stage. The source's Remark 7.11 deduces the comparison from "Corollary 7.10"; what the argument uses is the full faithfulness of Vect^φ(𝔖) → Rep_{Z_p}(G_{K_∞}), i.e. Theorem 7.2 (source issue PrismaticCohomology/E75). R07.4 is not upstream of PR.7 in the atlas; the edge R07.4 → PR.7 is acyclic and is requested.

**Construction or proof.**

1. (1)–(2): E(u) ≡ u^e modulo p, so inverting E(u) and completing p-adically is the same as inverting u and completing. Compare the two descriptions of étale φ-modules: the perfection of 𝔖[1/u]^∧_p is W of the completed perfection of k((u)), which is the tilt of the completion of K_∞, and Fontaine's 𝒪̂_{ℰ^ur} embeds in W(C^♭) compatibly with φ and G_{K_∞}; so (W(C^♭) ⊗ M)^{φ=1} = (𝒪̂_{ℰ^ur} ⊗ M)^{φ=1}.
2. Effectivity in (3): by node crystalline-representation-of-f-crystal (3) the lattice φ^*M ⊗ B_dR^+ at the Hodge–Tate point is D_dR(L[1/p]) ⊗_K B_dR^+, which lies in L ⊗ B_dR^+ exactly when Fil^0 D_dR = D_dR, i.e. when the weights are ≤ 0; an effective object has finite E-height because φ_M is an isomorphism after inverting E(u).
3. (i) For every p-torsion-free quasisyntomic ring R and n ≥ 0: a natural map χ_n: Q_p(n)(R/p) → (LΩ_R)_{Q_p} and a functorial pullback square in D(Q_p) with top row Q_p(n)(R) → Q_p(n)(R/p), left column Q_p(n)(R) → (LΩ_R^{≥n})_{Q_p}, right column χ_n and bottom row (LΩ_R^{≥n})_{Q_p} → (LΩ_R)_{Q_p}; equivalently a fibre sequence Q_p(n)(R) → Q_p(n)(R/p) → (LΩ_R/LΩ_R^{≥n})_{Q_p}. Here Q_p(n)(−) = Z_p(n)(−)[1/p] with Z_p(n) the syntomic complex of PR.4, LΩ_R is p-completed derived de Rham cohomology over Z_p with its Hodge filtration (not Hodge-completed), and the subscript Q_p means p-completion followed by inversion of p, in this order. (ii) For R quasiregular semiperfectoid and p-torsion-free and n > 0: χ_n is injective on H^0 with image the φ = p^n eigenspace of A_crys(R/p)[1/p] = LΩ_R[1/p]; so, up to a nonzero scalar depending only on n, χ_n is the forgetful map Q_p(n)(R/p) → Δ_{R/p}[1/p] composed with Δ_{R/p} = A_crys(R/p) ≅ LΩ_R. (iii) The suspension dictionary: the square is τ_{[2n−1,2n]} of the pullback square TC(R;Q_p) → TC(R/p;Q_p) over HC^-(R;Q_p) → HP(R;Q_p) (AMMN Corollary 3.9 in the atlas numbering), shifted by −2n; the fibre of TC(R;Q_p) → TC(R/p;Q_p) is ΣHC(R;Q_p), the cofibre is Σ^2HC(R;Q_p), and for R quasiregular semiperfectoid π_{2n}Σ^2HC(R;Q_p) = HC_{2n−2}(R;Q_p) = (LΩ_R/LΩ_R^{≥n})_{Q_p}. The sequence TC → TC(R/p) → HC printed in the introduction of the F-crystals paper is this one with the double suspension suppressed. (iv) Check for R = O_C: the sequence is 0 → Q_p(n) → (B_crys^+)^{φ=p^n} → B_dR^+/Fil^n → 0.

## Gaps and exact completion work


### Gap 1: Joyal's theorem: Witt vectors are the cofree δ-ring

Bhatt–Scholze Remark 2.7 cites Joyal for the statement that the right adjoint of the forgetful functor from δ-rings to rings is the p-typical Witt vector functor. Mathlib has Witt vectors with Frobenius and ghost components but not this universal property, and no layer of the atlas plans its proof. The node states the adjunction and the unit w_A; a lemma-level proof (construction of the δ-structure on W(R) for R with p-torsion, and of the counit) is still to be planned in this layer.

Needed by [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-ring-category`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-delta-ring-category).

### Gap 2: Remark 2.5: derived Frobenius lifts

The source's characterisation of δ-structures on a Z_(p)-algebra as derived Frobenius lifts (a lift of Frobenius together with a homotopy on R ⊗^L F_p) is not planned: no target of PR.0–PR.7 uses it. The pullback square for W_2 of a simplicial commutative ring, which the same remark states and which the proof of BS22 Lemma 7.7 (1) does use, is planned as PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/witt2-derived-pullback-square. The gap is recorded so that the ordinary Frobenius congruence is never mistaken for the derived datum.

Needed by [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-frobenius-dictionary`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-0-delta-frobenius-dictionary).

### Gap 3: p-torsion-freeness of completely flat modules over a general p-torsion-free bounded prism

Needed: for a bounded prism (A,I) with A p-torsion-free and a derived (p,I)-complete, (p,I)-completely flat A-module B, B is p-torsion-free. Established here: B[p] ≅ lim_n B ⊗_A (A/I^n)[p], which vanishes when the pro-system ((A/I^n)[p])_n is pro-zero, in particular for crystalline prisms and for prisms in which (p,d) is a regular sequence. Not established for arbitrary p-torsion-free bounded prisms; Anschütz–Le Bras Lemma 5.1.6 asserts it by calling the first term of the Čech–Alexander complex p-completely flat over A, which Bhatt–Scholze Proposition 3.13 does not state. A proof, or the restriction of the lemma to prisms with A/p of bounded I^∞-torsion, closes the gap; the application in Anschütz–Le Bras (A = A_inf) is covered.

Needed by [`PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/p-torsion-free-h0-syntomic`](#prismaticcohomology-pr-1-p-torsion-free-h0-syntomic).

Missing input of BS22 Lemma 8.4: for an E_∞-algebra over F_p the operation P^0 on homotopy groups (Lurie, Rational and p-adic homotopy theory, §2.2), with two properties: (i) for the realisation of a simplicial cosimplicial commutative F_p-algebra, P^0 is induced by the levelwise Frobenius; (ii) P^0 annihilates every homotopy class of positive degree (Remark 2.2.7 there). No atlas stage plans power operations on E_∞-F_p-algebras; the natural owner is the E_∞-algebra layer EnhancedDerivedSheaves E5:abstract or the stable homotopy roadmap that supplies concrete spectra. Until it is supplied, node perfectoidization-coconnective and its consumer rest on this gap.

### Gap 25: Arbitrary naturality of the AΩ comparison

The all-unit-subsets construction of BS22 §17 compares framed Koszul complexes only for maps injective on coordinates. A ring map can identify two units; the associated coordinate-merging map does not commute with the q-derivatives (PR.6/framed-q-pd-datum). To obtain the arbitrary naturality asserted by Theorem 17.2 and used in the Hodge–Tate check, replace subsets by finite indexed families with a coherent comparison, or supply an intrinsic descent construction. Proposed owner: PR.6/ainf-omega-comparison-map, using AI.3/AI.4 and the generalized QW.6 prefix. This extension is not supplied by the existing subset-indexed proof.

## Ownership decisions and structural proposals


Q3's description says that it proves Bhatt–Scholze Proposition 7.11 (lifting quasisyntomic covers to bounded prisms). Its proof is the first half of Proposition 7.10 and uses only PR.2; it is planned as PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/quasisyntomic-covers-lift-to-prisms, and Q3 should import it. Bhatt–Scholze Lemma 4.8 (maps out of a perfect prism are determined by their reduction), which Q0:animated-application holds as an inherited aggregate, is planned as PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/perfect-prism-initial.

No stage text states the definition of a quasiregular semiperfectoid ring (BMS2 Definition 4.20). DD.5 speaks of "the semiperfectoid covers used by BMS2", and the PerfectoidQuotients packet records DD.0/DD.5 as its owners. PR.2–PR.4 follow that decision and request the definition from DD.5; DD.5's description should name it.

A stage edge PerfectoidQuotients:Q3 → PrismaticCohomology:PR.3 is needed: André's flatness lemma (Bhatt–Scholze Theorem 7.14) is used in the proof of Proposition 12.8 (PR.3/nygaard-regular-semiperfectoid). The roadmap lists only AI.1 and PR.2 as requirements of PR.3.

Export to RT.6, with no prerequisite in the other direction: Bhatt–Scholze Theorem 13.1 and Proposition 15.7 identify π_0 TC^-(S; Z_p), respectively π_0 TP(S/S[u]; Z_p), with the Nygaard completion of Δ_S, respectively of Δ^{(1)}_{S/𝔖}. PR.3 supplies the prismatic half (PR.3/bms2-comparison, nygaard-completion, nygaard-graded-pieces, nygaard-key-case, nygaard-regular-semiperfectoid); RT.6 owns the non-completed theory of BMS2 Construction 7.12, BMS2 Theorem 8.17 and the identification itself.

Bhatt–Scholze Corollaries 14.2 and 14.3 (K(−; Z_p) is concentrated in even degrees locally on the quasisyntomic site; surjectivity of π_*K(R; Z_p) → π_*K(R/(f_1, …, f_r); Z_p) in odd degrees) follow from PR.4/tate-twist-discreteness and Lemmas 14.4–14.5 together with K(−; Z_p) ≃ τ_{≥0}TC(−; Z_p) on henselian pairs and the motivic filtration on TC. They are left to the proposed Part II of RefinedTraceMethods on henselian pairs and are not nodes of PR.4. The identification gr^n TC(S; Z_p)[−2n] ≃ Z_p(n)(S) (BMS2 Theorem 1.12(5)) and the exact sequence before BMS2 Proposition 8.20 belong to RT.6, which consumes PR.4/syntomic-complex; no PR.4 node has a RefinedTraceMethods prerequisite.

Routed item PAPER-COLMEZ-DOSPINESCU-NIZIOL-20-B/in-syntomic: PR.4 exports the syntomic complex with its defining fibre sequence (PR.4/syntomic-cohomology-formal-schemes), its crystalline form in characteristic p (PR.4/syntomic-complex-char-p), the integral comparison map with étale cohomology and its isomorphism after inverting ε (PR.4/syntomic-etale-comparison), and the identification with τ^{≤n}Rψ_* for smooth formal schemes over O_C (PR.4/nearby-cycles-comparison). The Fontaine–Messing form with the Hodge filtration in mixed characteristic and its comparison with Z_p(n) (Antieau–Mathew–Morrow–Nikolaus Theorem F) rests on the Beilinson fibre square and needs an owner downstream of PR.4 and RT.3b; see the structure proposals.

RT-AREA-etale/28. The framed q-de Rham machinery has one owner, QWittVectors:QW.6. QW.6 requires QW.5, but the framing prefix that PR.6 needs (framings, the automorphisms γ_i, q-derivatives, the framed q-de Rham complex, reduction modulo q − 1, the framed Frobenius) uses none of QW.5 and should be a stage of its own, stated for a base ring D with an element q and not only for A[[q−1]] over a Λ-ring A; the edge to PrismaticCohomology:PR.6 then starts at that stage. QWittVectors depends on PrismaticCohomology only through QW.1 → PR.0, so the edge closes no cycle. HabiroCohomologyFoundations:HQ.1 should import the framed q-difference complex, the q-integers and the twisted Leibniz rule from the same owner, and from PR.6 only the q-crystalline site, the comparison of the framed complex with q-crystalline cohomology (Bhatt–Scholze Theorem 16.22), change of framing and the comparison with prismatic cohomology over (Z_p[[q−1]], ([p]_q)).

The acceptance check of AI.7 ("agreement of all prior comparison maps through the uniqueness and polynomial/torus tests of BS22 §18") can cite PR.6/comparison-uniqueness. The agreement of the de Rham specialisation of AΩ built in AI.4 with the one transported from PR.3 through PR.6/ainf-omega-comparison is AI.7's statement; it is not proved in Bhatt–Scholze §§16–18.

The stage text of PR.7 cites "Corollary 3.9 supplies an underlying pullback-square input": this is Corollary 3.9 of Antieau–Mathew–Morrow–Nikolaus in the numbering of the RT.3b stage text, not a statement of the F-crystals paper, where 3.9 is a remark.

The comparison needs the Beilinson fibre square, which is trace-theoretic and may not enter PR.4, while PR.4 owns the prismatic complexes it compares. Give the comparison of the prismatic syntomic complexes Z_p(n) with Fontaine–Messing syntomic cohomology (Antieau–Mathew–Morrow–Nikolaus Section 6, Theorem F) an owner downstream of PrismaticCohomology:PR.4 and RefinedTraceMethods:RT.3b, for instance CohomologyComparisons:CP.6 or a sub-stage of RefinedTraceMethods:RT.3b, with edges PR.4 → owner and RT.3b → owner; consumers of the syntomic route of Colmez–Dospinescu–Nizioł §0.6.1 import it from there.

RT-AREA-etale/28: one owner for the framed q-de Rham machinery; the prefix must not depend on QW.5. Split QWittVectors:QW.6 into a framing prefix (framed algebras over a base ring D with an element q, I-completely étale or toric framings for I = (q−1) or (p, q−1), the automorphisms γ_i, q-derivatives, twisted Leibniz rule, framed q-de Rham and q-Hodge Koszul complexes, reduction modulo q − 1, framed Frobenius), requiring only DD.1 and AI.1, and the remainder of QW.6 requiring QW.5. PrismaticCohomology:PR.6 and HabiroCohomologyFoundations:HQ.1 import the prefix.

Two statements have a node on each side, with different proofs. (1) Full faithfulness of 𝔐 ↦ 𝒪_ℰ ⊗_𝔖 𝔐: R07.4/kisin-etale-full-faithfulness (Kisin 2.1.12 with the erratum proof, through Fontaine's field-of-norms equivalence and Kisin's embedding) and PR.7/etale-realization-over-breuil-kisin-prism (Bhatt–Scholze Theorem 7.2, for all objects of Vect^φ(𝔖), through A_inf, with no field of norms and no slope filtration). (2) Full faithfulness of restriction from G_K to G_{K_∞} on crystalline representations: R07.4/crystalline-restriction-full-faithfulness (Q_p-coefficients) and part (2) of PR.7/breuil-kisin-evaluation (Z_p-lattices, from the main theorem). PR.7 keeps its nodes because the stage must prove the Breuil–Kisin statements from the main theorem as the source does, and the comparison node PR.7/kisin-functor-comparison identifies the two formulations. one owner per statement. Either R07.4 keeps both statements and the two PR.7 nodes are recorded as second proofs linked through the comparison node, or the statement (1) moves to PR.7 (its proof there has lighter prerequisites) and R07.4/kisin-etale-full-faithfulness cites it; the second choice needs R07.4 split so that the stage-level edges stay acyclic (PR.7 → the part of R07.4 using it, and the rest of R07.4 → PR.7 for the comparison).

Sub-layers of PR.7 for the atlas (PROTOCOL section 14). For the atlas the stage divides naturally into three sub-layers: PR.7:crystals (prismatic-crystal, crystal-descent, quasisyntomic-crystal-comparison, f-crystal-over-prism, prismatic-f-crystal, laurent-f-crystal, artin-schreier-riemann-hilbert, laurent-f-crystals-local-systems, etale-realization, crystalline-realization, f-crystals-over-qrsp), which needs only PR.0–PR.5, SF, DD and C2; PR.7:crystalline-lattices (the nodes for Spf(O_K) up to crystalline-lattices-theorem and mod-p-full-faithfulness-fails), which adds AI.2, R06, VB2:classification, RT.3b and RT.6; and PR.7:breuil-kisin (etale-realization-over-breuil-kisin-prism, breuil-kisin-evaluation, kisin-functor-comparison), the only part that touches R07.4.

## Source correction register

This review checked all 81 entries in the public PDFs: 80 confirmed and E33 rejected. Historical line numbers refer to earlier workers’ TeX navigation; the current verdicts come from rendered PDFs. Each statement below is in original words. The public metadata and correction screen is recorded in the packet; it establishes no exhaustive novelty claim. The public [2025 ALB erratum](https://lebras.perso.math.cnrs.fr/Erratum_PDT.pdf) addresses a separate Proposition 5.23 proof.

### PrismaticCohomology/E1 — confirmed

**Locator.** Remark 2.5, the sentence after the first square (TeX l. 513), printed p.14, description of the right arrow in the first square; arXiv:1905.08229v4 only; rendered-PDF statement-heading page 14.

**Issue.** The explanatory sentence has a missing letter in the verb describing the quotient projection.

**Correction.** Insert the missing s: the right map is the canonical projection.

**Independent check.** The right arrow is the projection R → R/p; the adjacent verb has a missing letter. The diagram and its mathematical interpretation agree.

### PrismaticCohomology/E11 — confirmed

**Locator.** Proof of Lemma 5.4, first displayed decomposition, p. 47 (TeX l. 1572) (arXiv:1905.08229v4); rendered-PDF statement-heading page 48.

**Issue.** The disjoint decomposition is indexed by every monoid element, rather than by the previously chosen representatives.

**Correction.** ⊔_{s ∈ S} (pM) + s ≃ M, the union over the set S = {0,…,p−1}^r of coset representatives.

**Independent check.** The translates are disjoint only when indexed by the chosen representatives S of M^gp/pM^gp. Indexing by all of M repeats translates; the following multivariate display uses S correctly.

### PrismaticCohomology/E12 — confirmed

**Locator.** Construction 4.17 and Construction 4.18, pp. 41–42 (TeX ll. 1422, 1436), against Proposition 3.13 and Example 3.14 (arXiv:1905.08229v4); rendered-PDF statement-heading pages 33, 35, 41, 42, 108, 111.

**Issue.** The finite-presentation envelope results are applied to a presentation with one polynomial variable for each element of the target ring.

**Correction.** For a presentation in infinitely many variables write the ideal as a filtered union of ideals (I, x_1,…,x_r) with completely regular sequences, and obtain the envelope as the (p,I)-completed filtered colimit of the envelopes of Proposition 3.13; it has the universal property and is (p,I)-completely flat over A.

**Independent check.** Proposition 3.13 assumes a finite completely regular sequence locally, whereas the canonical presentation in Construction 4.17 can have arbitrarily many variables. Completed filtered colimits of finite envelopes supply the missing extension, with closed ideal and universal property; ALB23 Remark 3.1.8(2) gives this broader form.

### PrismaticCohomology/E13 — confirmed

**Locator.** Theorem 1.8 (5) (and the global forms of (1) and (3)), p. 4 (TeX ll. 203–237), in arXiv:1905.08229v4, the only text read; rendered-PDF statement-heading page 4.

**Issue.** Global completed base change is asserted for smooth formal schemes without a quasi-compactness or separation restriction.

**Correction.** Assume X quasi-compact and quasi-separated. The sheaf statement, Corollary 4.12, holds for every smooth X.

**Independent check.** For X = ⨿ Spf F_p over (Z_p,(p)), base change to Z_p⟨t⟩ compares (∏ Z_p)⟨t⟩ with ∏ Z_p⟨t⟩. Modulo p, the sequence (t^n) has no preimage, since every image has uniformly bounded polynomial degree. The packet restricts global base change to qcqs X and uses the QCoh projection formula, rather than a finite-hypercover shortcut for unbounded complexes.

### PrismaticCohomology/E14 — confirmed

**Locator.** Proof of Lemma 5.1.6, second sentence (arXiv:1907.10525v4); rendered-PDF statement-heading page 76.

**Issue.** The first Čech–Alexander term is described as complete and completely flat only for the p-adic ideal.

**Correction.** Use the joint (p,I)-complete-flatness statement. For the p-torsion argument add bounded I-power torsion of A/p, which makes ((A/I^n)[p]) pro-zero; perfect prisms satisfy this condition. The arbitrary p-torsion-free bounded-prism case remains unproved here.

**Independent check.** The envelope theorem provides (p,I)-complete flatness, not p-complete flatness. With p injective in A, the latter would already imply the desired absence of p-torsion in B. The I-adic pro-zero calculation repairs the argument when A/p has bounded I-power torsion, in particular for perfect prisms; regularity of (p,ξ) is not asserted for every A_inf. The general step remains an explicit gap.

### PrismaticCohomology/E21 — confirmed

**Locator.** Proof of Lemma 8.6, p. 66 (TeX l. 2038) (arXiv:1905.08229v4); rendered-PDF statement-heading page 66.

**Issue.** The reduction argument replaces an arbitrary semiperfect base by a perfect characteristic-p base without justifying that replacement.

**Correction.** Replace the perfect coefficient ring by k=A/(p,φ⁻¹(d))≅R/p, an arbitrary F_p-algebra. The polynomial Cartier calculation and k[X^(1/p∞)] extension suffice; no perfection identification is needed.

**Independent check.** After the indicated base change the coefficient ring is A/(p,φ⁻¹(d)) ≅ R/p, which need only be semiperfect. For O_C/p it is not reduced. The polynomial Cartier calculation and the free extension adjoining all p-power roots work over any F_p-algebra, so perfectness of this coefficient ring is unnecessary.

### PrismaticCohomology/E22 — confirmed

**Locator.** Proof of Proposition 3.5.1 (arXiv:1907.10525v4); rendered-PDF statement-heading page 25.

**Issue.** The unit computation is described categorically as preservation of a final object.

**Correction.** Use the initial algebra objects when checking preservation of the empty coproduct.

**Independent check.** The map on unit objects is the empty-coproduct case: the base algebra is initial in the category of algebras. Its terminal object is the zero algebra. Reversing to the geometric category would reverse these words, but that is not the category used here.

### PrismaticCohomology/E23 — confirmed

**Locator.** Appendix A, before Proposition A.3, printed p.94, arXiv:1907.10525v4 PDF; rendered-PDF statement-heading page 94.

**Independent check.** Complete flatness alone does not imply faithfulness, as a localization shows. The following descent proof uses faithful flatness of the reduced quotient maps. The rendered arXiv PDF numbers the proposition A.3; no assertion about publisher numbering is needed.

**Correction.** Lemma 12.7 treats R = Z_p[ζ_{p^∞}]^∧ only. For a general perfectoid R one must first pass, by André's lemma and properties (3), (4), to a perfectoid R-algebra containing compatible p-power roots of unity, as is done in the proof of Theorem 13.1 (l. 2977).

**Independent check.** Lemma 12.7 treats the cyclotomic perfectoid base. The fixed base in Proposition 12.8 is arbitrary perfectoid and need not receive that cyclotomic algebra. André’s lemma first adjoins compatible p-power roots of unity; complete faithful flat descent then supplies the reduction.

### PrismaticCohomology/E98 — confirmed

**Locator.** Lemma 9.6 and its proof (arXiv:1905.08229v4, TeX ll. 2345-2353); rendered-PDF statement-heading page 76.

**Issue.** The Picard comparison is stated pointwise using a complex that only yields the desired result after quasisyntomic sheafification.

**Correction.** Z_p(1)(R) ≃ RΓ_fl(Spec R, G_m)^∧[−1] (Bhatt–Lurie Theorem 7.5.6); the map Pic(R)^∧[−2] → Z_p(1)(R) is an isomorphism on H^i for i ≤ 1, injective on H^2, and an isomorphism if and only if (τ^{≥2}RΓ(Spec R, G_m))^∧ = 0, for instance for perfectoid R.

**Independent check.** For k=F_p(t), the truncated Picard complex modulo p has no H², whereas fppf μ_p cohomology has H²=Br(k)[p]≠0. Thus the pointwise derived-category assertion fails. The full completed fppf G_m complex supplies weight one; the truncated formula remains valid in the perfectoid applications.

**Correction.** The formula holds for a generator d adapted to a trivialisation of the Breuil–Kisin twist (a generator e of A{1} with φ(e) = d^{−1}e; d = [p]_q over Z_p^cycl, d = p in characteristic p); adapted generators differ by factors v/φ(v), v ∈ A^×. At the cyclotomic base the usual generator admits μ as a nonzero weight-one solution; the altered generator would require y^(p−1)=ū in the fraction field of the perfected power-series ring, impossible because its algebraic constants lie in F_p. Adapted twist generators remove this ambiguity.
